title: Discovery test matrix over synthetic trees (M1 checkpoint 2)
description:
## Background

M1 checkpoint 2 (vision §7 M1 Checkpoints) requires that synthetic trees resolve correctly:
- every product in §4.1, including `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_` at 1.60.x;
- every legacy `ClientRules` row;
- a game on a mapped drive letter outside `drive_c`;
- a custom client outside any prefix;
- each launcher config;
- an unknown `_xyz_` folder (yields a usable `unknown` target).

Each discovery bead tests its own piece; this bead is the end-to-end matrix that proves the pieces compose through `discover()` + registry reconciliation, and that discovery never writes (vision defect R10, §5.2 step 7). It is also the Forever launch guard: WoW: Forever launches 2026-11-04, and both the beta layout (`wow_classic_beta` in `_classic_beta_`, 1.60.1.70374) and the launch layout (`wowf` in `_forever_`, 1.60.1.70245) must resolve as family `forever`.

Expected values (vision §4.1; interface = major×10000 + minor×100 + patch for Battle.net, patch omitted for legacy):

| Folder / client | Family | Interface | Kind | Default id |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_retail_` 12.1.5 | mainline | 120105 | live | retail |
| `_ptr_` 12.1.0 | mainline | 120100 | test | ptr |
| `_xptr_` 12.1.5 | mainline | 120105 | test | xptr |
| `_beta_` 12.0.1 | mainline | 120001 | test | beta |
| `_classic_` 5.5.4 | mists | 50504 | live | classic |
| `_classic_ptr_` 5.5.4 | mists | 50504 | test | classic-ptr |
| `_classic_beta_` 1.60.1 | forever | 16001 | test | classic-beta |
| `_classic_era_` 1.15.9 | vanilla | 11509 | live | era |
| `_classic_era_ptr_` 2.5.6 | tbc | 20506 | test | era-ptr |
| `_anniversary_` 2.5.6 | tbc | 20506 | live | anniversary |
| `_classic_titan_` 3.80.2 | titan | 38002 | live | titan |
| `_forever_` 1.60.1 | forever | 16001 | live | forever |
| custom 1.12.1 | vanilla-legacy | 11200 | live | vanilla |
| custom 2.4.3 | tbc-legacy | 20400 | live | tbc |
| custom 3.3.5a (12340) | wrath-legacy | 30300 | live | wotlk |
| custom 4.3.4 | cata-legacy | 40300 | live | cata |
| custom 5.4.8 | mists-legacy | 50400 | live | mists |

## Technical Approach

- New integration test crate `tests/discover_matrix.rs` using `tests/common/` (test-trees bead) and the DEC-6 `TestEnv`.
- Drive it through the library (`omaddons::discover::discover` + `registry::reconcile`) for precise assertions, plus one binary-level smoke per scenario once a read command that lists targets exists (if `cmd-targets`/`cmd-status` have not landed when this bead is worked, keep the binary checks out and note it in the close comment; the E7 contract suite covers the binary later).
- Table-driven: one `Case { name, build: fn(&TestEnv), expect: Vec<Expected> }` per scenario; `Expected { id, family, interface, kind, product, flavor_dir, exe_name_lowercase, label }`. Assertions compare the full serialized target (minus paths) so a field regression is visible in the diff.
- Scenarios:
  1. **All Battle.net products** in one root under `<home>/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft` (the table above).
  2. **Forever layouts side by side**: one root with only `_classic_beta_` (beta layout), another with only `_forever_` (launch layout); both `forever`.
  3. **Legacy rows**: five custom roots (one per version) inside prefixes at `<prefix>/drive_c/WoW`, each with a realmlist; the 3.3.5a root has 23 `Blizzard_*` folders and `set realmlist 127.0.0.1` → label "localhost" (mirrors the development machine).
  4. **Mapped drive outside drive_c**: a prefix whose `dosdevices/d:` points at a directory outside the prefix, with the WoW root there and a product.db naming `D:/Games/World of Warcraft`; found only via product.db.
  5. **Custom client outside any prefix**: `<home>/Games/turtle/Wow.exe` (1.12.1).
  6. **Launcher configs**: one prefix per launcher (Lutris native, Heroic native + Flatpak, Steam native + Flatpak with a second library, Bottles native + Flatpak), each containing a WoW root placed outside `<home>/Games` so only the launcher hint can find it; assert each target's qualifier.
  7. **Unknown flavor**: `_xyz_` with no `.flavor.info` product mapping and no version → family `unknown`, id `xyz`, usable (has `client_dir`), warning `unknown_flavor`; and `_xyz_` with `.flavor.info` `wowz` + `.build.info` row 13.0.0 → `mainline`.
  8. **Disagreement → warning, not failure**: `_retail_` with `WTF/Config.wtf` `lastAddonVersion "120100"` → interface 120105 kept + `client_not_launched_since_patch`; discovery still returns all targets.
  9. **Broken and partial installs**: a flavor folder without exe or `Interface/`; a `.build.info` that is garbage; an unreadable directory → targets still returned where possible, no panic, no error.
  10. **Collisions**: two retail installs (Battle.net prefix + Steam prefix) → `retail` and `retail@steam`.
- **Never writes**: for every scenario compute `tree_hash` of the whole `TestEnv` home and of `<state>` before and after `discover()` + `reconcile()`; they must be equal. The discovery cache (if the discover-cache bead has landed) lives in `<cache>`, which is excluded from this assertion.
- Determinism: run each scenario twice; serialized results identical.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every row of the expected-values table is asserted and passes.
- Both Forever layouts resolve as family `forever`, interface 16001, with kinds `test` (beta) and `live` (launch).
- The mapped-drive root is found only through product.db + dosdevices, and the custom client outside any prefix is found by the `<home>/Games` scan.
- Every launcher scenario resolves its root with the right qualifier.
- The unknown folder yields a usable `unknown` target with `unknown_flavor`; the version/interface disagreement yields `client_not_launched_since_patch` and no failure.
- Broken and partial installs never panic or fail discovery.
- Tree hashes of home and `<state>` are unchanged by discovery and reconciliation in every scenario.
- Results are deterministic across two runs.

## Test Plan

- This bead is itself the test plan for checkpoint 2: `cargo test --test discover_matrix`.
- On failure, print the scenario name, the built tree listing and a JSON diff of expected vs actual targets (log test inputs and outputs).
- Record in the close comment which scenarios were also exercised through the binary.

## Considerations

- Expected interfaces for `_ptr_` (120100) and `_beta_` (120001) follow mechanically from the formula and the table's versions; if the rules-tables bead encodes a different formula for any row, this matrix must fail loudly rather than be edited to match.
- `_classic_era_ptr_` running TBC 2.5.6 is the canonical "product code does not determine family" case; keep it in the table.
- The real-machine half of the checkpoint (retail and the 3.3.5a client on the development machine) belongs to the E7 `m1-checkpoint` bead.
- If a launcher location turns out wrong on a real install, fix it in discover-launchers and test-trees together; this matrix only consumes them.
acceptance_criteria: Every row of the expected-values table (12 Battle.net products, 5 legacy clients) passes with the right family, interface, kind and default id; both Forever layouts resolve as forever with interface 16001, kinds test (beta) and live (launch); the mapped-drive root is found only via product.db and dosdevices and the custom client outside any prefix via the <home>/Games scan; every launcher scenario resolves with the right qualifier; the unknown folder yields a usable unknown target with unknown_flavor and the lastAddonVersion disagreement yields client_not_launched_since_patch without failure; broken and partial installs never panic or fail discovery; home and <state> tree hashes are unchanged in every scenario; results are deterministic across two runs
close_reason: M1 checkpoint 2: the discovery matrix passes over synthetic trees, through the library and the binary

title: Bounded discovery scan and hint aggregation
description:
## Background

Discovery must find every WoW root on the machine with zero configuration (vision G2, §5.2 steps 1–2) and stay cheap enough to run on every non-cached command. This bead owns the entry point `discover()`: it collects hints, picks candidate prefixes, runs a bounded scan, classifies each root as Battle.net or custom (via the discover-battlenet and discover-custom beads), de-duplicates, and returns targets in a deterministic order. Discovery never writes to game directories (vision defect R10).

Placeholders: `<home>` = the user's home directory; `<prefix>` = a Wine prefix (a directory with `drive_c/`).

Hints, in order (vision §5.2 step 1):
- (a) Battle.net `product.db` per prefix at `<prefix>/drive_c/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db`, parsed by the product-db bead; install paths mapped through `<prefix>/dosdevices/<letter>:` symlinks. A parse failure falls through to scanning.
- (b) Launcher configs (Lutris, Heroic, Steam, Bottles) — added by the discover-launchers bead; this bead provides the input slot.
- (c) Running processes (`WINEPREFIX` and exe paths) — computed by the running-detection bead; the caller passes them in.
- (d) `extra_roots` from `config.toml` — passed in by the caller.

Bounded scan (vision §5.2 step 2, constants from `src/politeness.rs`, vision §5.13):

| Constant | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `DISCOVERY_MAX_DEPTH` | 4 | Under each `drive_c` and under `<home>/Games` |
| `DISCOVERY_SKIP_DIRS` | `windows`, `users`, `ProgramData` | Under `drive_c`. `ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db` is read directly as a hint |
| `DISCOVERY_MAX_DIRS` | 50 000 | Directories visited per scan before stopping with a warning |

Candidate prefixes: `<home>/Games/*`, `<home>/.wine`, Steam compatdata `*/pfx` in every library, and prefixes from (b). The scan runs under each prefix's `drive_c` and under `<home>/Games` itself (for custom clients outside prefixes), looking for `World of Warcraft/` or any directory containing a `Wow*.exe` (case-insensitive).

## Technical Approach

- New file `src/discover/scan.rs`; `discover()` lives in `src/discover/mod.rs`.
- Input/output types (in `src/discover/mod.rs`, `Serialize` + `JsonSchema` per DEC-3 where they reach output):
  ```rust
  pub struct DiscoveryInput {
      pub home: PathBuf,
      pub extra_roots: Vec<PathBuf>,          // config extra_roots + registry manual roots
      pub extra_prefixes: Vec<ExtraPrefix>,   // running processes, etc.
      pub launcher_hints: Vec<LauncherHint>,  // filled by discover-launchers; empty here
  }
  pub struct ExtraPrefix { pub path: PathBuf, pub qualifier: String, pub source: DiscoverySource }
  pub struct LauncherHint { pub launcher: String, pub flatpak: bool, pub prefix: Option<PathBuf>, pub exe: Option<PathBuf> }
  pub struct Discovery { pub targets: Vec<DiscoveredTarget>, pub warnings: Vec<Warning>, pub diagnostics: Vec<String> }
  pub fn discover(input: &DiscoveryInput) -> Discovery
  ```
  `diagnostics` are debug notes (unreadable files, skipped hints) rendered as stderr `log` events at `-v`; they are not warnings.
- **Prefix collection** (`scan.rs`): `<home>/Games/*` entries that contain `drive_c/`; `<home>/.wine` if it has `drive_c/`; `<home>/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/*/pfx` (default library only — discover-launchers adds every library from `libraryfolders.vdf`); `extra_prefixes`; prefixes from `launcher_hints`. Each prefix carries a qualifier: the launcher name for launcher/Steam prefixes (`steam`, `lutris`, `heroic`, `bottles`), otherwise the prefix directory's basename lowercased with non `[a-z0-9-]` characters replaced by `-` (e.g. `battlenet`, `wow-335`).
- **Hint (a)**: for each prefix, `product_db::read_product_db(prefix)`; map each `install_path` with `dosdevices::map_windows_path`; mapped directories become root candidates with source `ProductDb`; collect `flavor_folder → product` and `product → version` pairs into the `BattlenetHints` passed to `battlenet::discover_root` for that root.
- **Scan** — one bounded breadth-first walk per base directory, sharing one visited-directory budget:
  - bases: each prefix's `drive_c` (with `DISCOVERY_SKIP_DIRS` applied to its direct children, matched case-insensitively), `<home>/Games` itself, and each `extra_roots` entry;
  - depth is counted from the base (`drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft` is depth 2); stop descending past `DISCOVERY_MAX_DEPTH`;
  - when walking `<home>/Games`, do not descend into directories that are Wine prefixes (contain `drive_c/`), because their `drive_c` is scanned as its own base (decided: avoids walking every prefix twice and walking `drive_c/windows` without the skip list);
  - at each directory, list entries once (read-only) and classify:
    - contains `.build.info` → Battle.net root (`battlenet::is_battlenet_root`); record it and do not descend further;
    - is a custom root (`custom::is_custom_root`: exe matching `wow*.exe`, an `Interface/` dir, no `.build.info`) → record, do not descend;
    - contains a `wow*.exe` and its parent contains `.build.info` → it is a flavor folder; record the parent as a Battle.net root (covers roots not named `World of Warcraft`);
  - directory symlinks are followed, with a visited set of `(dev, ino)` pairs as the loop guard; each directory counts once against `DISCOVERY_MAX_DIRS`;
  - reaching `DISCOVERY_MAX_DIRS` stops the scan and adds warning `discovery_truncated` (message: how many directories were visited and the base being scanned; fix: display "add the client with: omaddons targets add <path>", argv null). Add `discovery_truncated` to `WarningCode` in `src/error.rs` (contract addition before the M4 freeze).
- **Classification and de-duplication**: canonicalize every root (`std::fs::canonicalize`, read-only) and keep the first occurrence in hint order (product.db, launchers, processes, extra roots, scan), which decides `DiscoverySource` and qualifier. Battle.net roots → `battlenet::discover_root`; custom roots → `custom::discover_custom_root`. For custom roots found under `<home>/Games` outside any prefix, the qualifier is the root's basename.
- **Order**: sort targets by `(install_root, flavor_dir)` as byte strings; sort warnings by code then message. Same filesystem → identical output.
- Never writes: no fsx, no `std::fs` mutation; the whole module is read-only. Errors reading a directory (permission denied, vanished) become diagnostics, never failures.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With `HOME` pointed at a synthetic home, `discover()` finds: a Battle.net root in `<home>/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft`; a root reached only through `product.db` + a `d:` drive mapping outside `drive_c`; a custom 3.3.5a client at `<prefix>/drive_c/WoW`; a custom client directly under `<home>/Games/<name>/` outside any prefix; a root listed in `extra_roots`.
- A root reachable by two routes (product.db hint and scan, or a symlinked path) appears once, with the product.db source.
- `drive_c/windows`, `drive_c/users` and `drive_c/ProgramData` (any case) are never descended into; directories deeper than depth 4 are not visited.
- A symlink loop under `<home>/Games` terminates.
- Setting the directory budget to a small value in a test hook stops the scan and yields `discovery_truncated`.
- Running `discover()` twice on the same tree returns byte-identical serialized output.
- The scanned trees are unchanged afterwards (tree hash before == after).

## Test Plan

- Unit (`scan.rs`): depth counting, skip-list matching (case-insensitive), prefix detection, qualifier normalization, root classification on synthetic listings.
- Integration (`tests/discover_scan.rs`, using `tests/common/` builders from the test-trees bead): the trees in the acceptance criteria; a symlink loop; a permission-denied directory (chmod 000 in the tempdir; skipped with a diagnostic); a budget-limited run via a `#[cfg(test)]`/debug-only override of the directory budget (decided: the constant stays in `src/politeness.rs`; tests use an internal `ScanLimits` struct defaulting to the constants).
- Determinism: run twice, compare serialized `Discovery`.
- Log the visited-directory count and the target list on failure.

## Considerations

- Discovery cost matters for every command; budget it at tens of milliseconds on the development machine (two prefixes). The discovery cache (discover-cache bead) removes the per-root parsing cost, and `status --cached` skips the scan entirely.
- A game installed on a drive letter outside `drive_c` is found only through product.db or launcher hints or `extra_roots`; the scan does not follow `dosdevices`.
- Steam libraries beyond the default one come from the discover-launchers bead.
- Out of scope: launcher readers (discover-launchers), caching (discover-cache), keys and ids (registry), running detection (running-detection; the caller converts running prefixes into `extra_prefixes`).
acceptance_criteria: discover() finds a Battle.net root under <home>/Games/battlenet/drive_c, a root reached only through product.db and a d: mapping outside drive_c, a custom client at <prefix>/drive_c/WoW, a custom client under <home>/Games outside any prefix, and an extra_roots entry; a root reachable two ways appears once with the product.db source; windows, users and ProgramData under drive_c are skipped case-insensitively and nothing deeper than depth 4 is visited; a symlink loop terminates; exhausting the directory budget yields warning discovery_truncated; two runs give byte-identical output; scanned trees are unchanged
close_reason: discover() finds every WoW root with zero configuration: product.db hints mapped through dosdevices, launcher and process hints, extra roots, then a bounded breadth-first scan with skip dirs, depth, a shared directory budget and a symlink loop guard; roots are de-duplicated by canonical path in route order and output is deterministic; reads only

title: Tolerant product.db protobuf reader and dosdevices drive mapping
description:
## Background

The Battle.net Agent keeps a protobuf database of installed products at `<prefix>/drive_c/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db` (vision §4.1, §5.2 step 1a). `<prefix>` is a Wine prefix such as Omarchy's `<home>/Games/battlenet` (`<home>` = the user's home directory). It is discovery's first and best hint: it names install paths directly, including installs on another drive letter that a scan of `drive_c` would never reach.

Facts:
- On the development machine product.db contains the install path `C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft`, the flavor folder `_retail_` and the version `12.1.0.69933`.
- The field layout follows WowUp's reader and is **UNVERIFIED**. A tolerant wire-format reader is sufficient; a parse failure falls through to scanning.
- Install paths are Windows paths. They map to Linux paths through `<prefix>/dosdevices/<letter>:` symlinks. The development machine has `c: → ../drive_c`, `s: → /home`, `w: → /mnt`, `x: → <home>`, `z: → /`. A game installed on another letter lives outside `drive_c`.
- `DISCOVERY_SKIP_DIRS` skips `ProgramData` during the scan precisely because product.db is read directly as a hint.

No protobuf crate is used (vision §5.12: the protobuf wire reader is implemented inline, ~100 lines).

## Technical Approach

- New files `src/discover/product_db.rs` and `src/discover/dosdevices.rs`; declare both in `src/discover/mod.rs`.
- **Wire reader** (`product_db.rs`, private module section):
  - Decode varints (max 10 bytes; overflow → stop), tags (`field << 3 | wire_type`), and wire types 0 (varint), 1 (fixed64), 2 (length-delimited), 5 (fixed32). Wire types 3/4 (groups) and anything else end parsing of that message.
  - Every read is bounds-checked; a truncated or malformed message returns what was decoded so far. No `unwrap`, no indexing that can panic, no recursion deeper than 16 levels.
  - `fn fields(buf: &[u8]) -> Vec<Field>` where `Field { number: u32, value: Value::{Varint(u64), Bytes(&[u8]), Fixed32, Fixed64} }`.
- **Shape-based extraction** (layout-agnostic, because the layout is UNVERIFIED):
  - Treat each top-level length-delimited field as one candidate "product install" entry (in WowUp's layout these are the repeated `product_installs`).
  - Within an entry, walk length-delimited values recursively: try to decode as a nested message (accept it if it decodes cleanly to at least one field and consumes the whole buffer); otherwise, if it is valid UTF-8, collect it as a string.
  - Classify the entry's strings:
    - install path: matches `^[A-Za-z]:[/\\]` (e.g. `C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft`);
    - product code: matches `^wow[a-z0-9_]*$` (all WoW product codes start with `wow`);
    - version: matches `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`;
    - flavor folder: matches `^_[a-z0-9_]+_$`.
  - Keep only entries that have an install path and either a `wow*` product code or an install path containing `World of Warcraft` (case-insensitive); product.db also lists the Agent and other Blizzard games.
  - Output: `pub struct ProductDbEntry { pub product: Option<String>, pub install_path: String, pub flavor_folder: Option<String>, pub version: Option<String> }` and `pub fn parse_product_db(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<ProductDbEntry>` (empty on any failure; never errors).
  - `pub fn read_product_db(prefix: &Path) -> Vec<ProductDbEntry>` reads `drive_c/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db` (read-only, size-capped by refusing files over 16 MiB; decided: a product.db is a few KiB, and the cap keeps a corrupt file from being slurped — it is a parse guard, not a §5.13 safety limit).
- **dosdevices mapping** (`dosdevices.rs`):
  - `pub fn map_windows_path(prefix: &Path, win: &str) -> Option<PathBuf>`:
    1. Normalize `\` to `/`; split `X:` drive letter (case-insensitive) from the rest.
    2. Read the symlink `<prefix>/dosdevices/<x>:` (lowercase letter). Resolve a relative target (`../drive_c`) against `<prefix>/dosdevices/`; absolute targets are used as-is.
    3. Join the remaining components. Wine resolves names case-insensitively, so when an exact component is missing, match it case-insensitively against the directory listing (read-only). If several entries differ only in case, pick the exact match if present, else the lexicographically first, and continue.
    4. Return `None` when the letter has no mapping or a component cannot be found.
  - `pub fn drive_map(prefix: &Path) -> BTreeMap<char, PathBuf>` for diagnostics and for `running-detection`, which maps process exe paths the same way.
- Discovery integration is done by `discover-scan`: for each candidate prefix it calls `read_product_db`, maps each `install_path` with `map_windows_path`, and treats the result as a Battle.net root hint; the `flavor_folder` → `product` pairs become the product.db fallback that `discover-battlenet` uses when a flavor folder lacks `.flavor.info`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A synthetic product.db encoding WowUp's layout (entries with uid/product code, a nested settings message holding the install path, a nested state message holding the version) parses into `ProductDbEntry { product: Some("wow"), install_path: "C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft", flavor_folder: Some("_retail_"), version: Some("12.1.0.69933") }`.
- The same strings placed at different field numbers and nesting depths are still extracted (layout-agnostic).
- Non-WoW entries (e.g. product code `agent` with a non-WoW path) are dropped.
- Truncated, random and empty inputs return an empty or partial list and never panic (proptest, 10 000 cases).
- `map_windows_path` resolves `C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft` through `c: → ../drive_c`, resolves a `D:/Games/WoW` path through `d: → <some dir outside drive_c>`, matches components case-insensitively, accepts backslashes, and returns `None` for an unmapped letter.
- Neither module writes anything (no `std::fs` write calls; read-only APIs only).

## Test Plan

- Unit (`product_db.rs`): a small `#[cfg(test)]` encoder (varint + length-delimited helpers, ~30 lines) builds:
  - the WowUp-shaped database with `wow` and `wow_classic_era` installs plus an `agent` entry;
  - a shuffled-field-number variant;
  - a database with a truncated final entry.
- Property: arbitrary bytes and arbitrary mutations of the valid fixture never panic; decoding a valid fixture is deterministic.
- Unit (`dosdevices.rs`): tempdir prefix with `dosdevices/c:` → `../drive_c`, `dosdevices/d:` → an absolute tempdir path outside `drive_c`, `dosdevices/z:` → `/`; directories created with different case (`program files (x86)`); assert mapping results.
- Fixture: if the development machine's product.db contains no personal data (only product codes, paths and versions), copy its bytes to `tests/fixtures/product_db/retail.db` and assert the retail entry. If it contains anything personal (account names, emails), do not copy it; keep only the synthetic fixture and say so in the close comment.
- Log the decoded field tree on assertion failure.

## Considerations

- WowUp's exact field numbers are UNVERIFIED; do not hard-code them as the only path. The shape-based classifier is the contract; field numbers may be used as a tie-breaker only.
- A string field that happens to decode as a valid nested message (short ASCII strings sometimes do) can be misclassified; the "consumes the whole buffer and every field is well-formed" rule plus checking both interpretations (collect the string too when it is valid UTF-8) keeps paths from being lost.
- Multiple installs of the same product in one prefix are possible; return all entries, de-duplication happens in `discover-scan` by canonical root path.
- Out of scope: turning entries into targets (`discover-battlenet`), choosing which prefixes to read (`discover-scan`), the fuzz target (E7 `fuzz-targets`).
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic WowUp-shaped product.db yields product wow, install path C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft, flavor folder _retail_ and version 12.1.0.69933; the same strings at different field numbers and nesting depths are still extracted; non-WoW entries are dropped; truncated, random and empty inputs never panic (proptest); map_windows_path resolves C: through a relative ../drive_c link and D: through an absolute link outside drive_c, matches components case-insensitively, accepts backslashes and returns None for an unmapped letter; neither module writes to the filesystem
close_reason: Tolerant inline protobuf reader for product.db, with shape-based extraction of WoW installs (path, product, flavor folder, version), and dosdevices mapping of Windows paths into the prefix; reads only, bounded

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/discover/{product_db,dosdevices}.rs).**
(1) Size guard: `read_product_db` reuses limits::DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES (1 MiB) through a new `discover::read_bytes`, which refuses an oversized file rather than truncating it. This replaces the bead's separate 16 MiB guard: constants live in limits.rs, and a product.db is ~1 KiB.
(2) Only printable UTF-8 (no control characters) counts as a string. This keeps a nested message whose bytes happen to be ASCII from being classified as a path. Each class takes its first match in depth-first order.
(3) An entry without a `wow*` code is kept only when its path contains 'World of Warcraft' (product None).
(4) **Layout verified** against this machine's product.db: install path at settings(3).1, flavor folder at settings(3).13, version at cached_state(4).base_state(1).7. That matches WowUp's layout. Field numbers are recorded here only; the code stays shape-based.
(5) Fixture `tests/fixtures/product_db/retail.db` is that file (1259 bytes). It contains product codes (agent, bna, wow), Windows install paths under C:/, versions, public build-config hashes and region/locale tags (us/USA/US, enUS). It has no account names, emails, usernames or home paths (checked with strings and grep). It parses to exactly the expected retail entry.
(6) `map_windows_path`: a relative dosdevices link is resolved lexically, so `c:` maps to `<prefix>/drive_c` (clean paths for dedup). A `..` component in the Windows path returns None; empty and `.` components are skipped; a non-Windows path returns None. Case-insensitive components use `discover::find_child` (exact match first, else the sorted first).
(7) The decoder function is `decode_message`: ubs flags any function named `decode` as a JWT risk.

Plus read_bytes. ubs 0 critical. Layout verified and fixture contents listed in the comment above · found: none

title: Target registry: ULID keys, aliases, markers, registration under the lock, and -t resolution
description:
## Background

Discovery produces targets; the registry gives them a stable identity (vision §5.1, §5.2 steps 5 and 7, §5.6). State files are keyed by the identity, so it must survive moves, renames and copies, and it must never be written by a read command.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory); `<client dir>` = the directory holding a client's `Interface/` and `WTF/`.

Identity rules (vision §5.1):
- **`key`** is an immutable ULID. It is assigned under the global lock at registration: by the first mutating command that touches the target, or by `targets add|rename|default`.
  - It is stored in the registry and mirrored in `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json`. State files are keyed by it.
  - A moved install is re-linked by its marker.
  - A copied install (two live markers with one key) keeps the key at the original path; the copy gets a new key (doctor finding `target-key-duplicate` in M4; a warning in M1).
  - Read commands report unregistered targets with `key: null` and a deterministic provisional id, and never write markers.
- **`id`** is a human alias. Defaults: `retail`, `classic`, `era`, `anniversary`, `forever`, `ptr`, `xptr`, `beta`, `classic-ptr`, `classic-beta`, `era-ptr`, `titan`. Legacy clients take their family name (`vanilla`, `tbc`, `wotlk`, `cata`, `mists`) unless named. The defaults come from the rules-tables product table's `default_id` column (and its legacy-family ids), carried on each discovered target as `default_id`; the registry keeps no list of its own.
  - The first-discovered target keeps the bare id permanently. Later collisions are qualified (`retail@steam`).
  - `targets rename <id> <new>` exists. `-t` also accepts keys.
- `-t` accepts a target id, key, family name, product code (`wow_classic_era`), flavor folder name (`_retail_`), install root, or AddOns path (vision §5.9 Target defaults). `--flavor` is an alias of `-t` (the CLI bead declares the flag; this bead resolves the value).
- Errors: `target_not_found` (exit 3, not retryable), `target_ambiguous` (exit 3, not retryable; `details.candidates`, `fix` + `alternatives` with exact commands).
- Registration writes keys, ids and markers only under the lock (vision §5.2 step 7). Discovery itself never writes to game directories.

## Technical Approach

- Storage in `src/state/registry.rs`; logic in `src/discover/registry.rs` (decided: the vision layout lists "registry" under both modules; the persisted format belongs with the other state files, reconciliation with discovery output belongs with discovery).
- **`<state>/omaddons/registry.json`** via `StateFile<Registry>` (state-store bead; own `schema_version` "1.0"):
  ```rust
  pub struct Registry { pub schema_version: String, pub targets: Vec<RegistryEntry>, pub default: Option<TargetKey> }
  pub struct RegistryEntry {
      pub key: TargetKey, pub id: String,
      pub install_root: PathBuf, pub client_dir: PathBuf, pub flavor_dir: Option<String>, pub product: Option<String>,
      pub qualifier: String, pub origin: Origin /* discovered | manual */, pub registered_at: jiff::Timestamp,
  }
  ```
  Decided: one `id` per entry instead of the plan's `ids[]`, because no M1 command creates extra aliases; aliases can be added additively later. Entries sorted by key on write.
- **Marker** `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json` = `{"schema_version":"1.0","key":"<ulid>"}`, read tolerantly; written only through fsx (`Op::CreateDir` for `Interface/.omaddons` if missing, then `Op::WriteFile`). The `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/` scope is writable by the install engine per the fsx write-scope table.
- **Reconcile (read-only)** — `pub fn reconcile(reg: &Registry, found: &Discovery) -> Resolved { targets: Vec<Target>, warnings: Vec<Warning> }`:
  1. For each discovered target, read its marker (read-only). Match order: registry entry with the same `client_dir` → that key/id; else marker key present in the registry (moved install) → that key/id, with the new paths (persisted at the next registration); else unregistered (`key: None`).
  2. Copy detection: two discovered targets carrying the same marker key → the one at the registry's recorded `client_dir` keeps it; the other is treated as unregistered and gets warning `target_key_duplicate` (message names both ids; fix: display "it gets a new key on its first mutation", argv null). Add `target_key_duplicate` to `WarningCode` in `src/error.rs` (contract addition before the M4 freeze).
  3. Provisional ids for unregistered targets: start from `default_id`; if it is taken by a registered target or an earlier unregistered one (order: sorted by `(install_root, flavor_dir)`), qualify as `<id>@<qualifier>`; if that is also taken, append `-2`, `-3`, … Deterministic for the same filesystem and registry.
  4. Registered targets keep their stored id, even if discovery would now suggest another.
  5. Registry entries whose `client_dir` no longer exists and whose key is not found on any marker are kept in the registry (history refers to them) and reported by `status` as missing; they are not targets in the result.
- **Registration (writes)** — all take `&GlobalLockGuard` (fsx-lock bead) as type-level proof the lock is held, and `&mut WriteSession`:
  - `ensure_registered(&mut self, lock, session, target: &Target) -> Result<TargetKey>`: reuse the marker key when the marker is valid and not a duplicate, else mint `Ulid::new()`; write the marker; insert/update the entry (paths refreshed for moved installs); save `registry.json`. Idempotent. Decided: within a transaction the caller passes its transaction session; `targets add|rename|default|rm` use an untracked session (DEC-10), because those are not undoable transaction kinds.
  - `add_manual(path, name: Option<String>)`: normalize — an AddOns path (`…/Interface/AddOns`) → its client dir; a flavor folder whose parent has `.build.info` → that root and folder; a root → as-is; then discover just that root (`battlenet::discover_root` / `custom::discover_custom_root`), register each resulting target with `origin: manual`, applying `--name` as the id when exactly one target results (several → `usage` error suggesting a flavor folder path). Manual roots are fed back into `DiscoveryInput.extra_roots` by the caller on later runs.
  - `remove(id)`: drop the entry, clear `default` if it pointed there; leave the client dir and marker untouched (decided in the plan: a later `add` re-links the same key).
  - `rename(id, new)`: validate `new` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9@._-]*$`, unique, not a ULID, not a family name or product code, to keep `-t` unambiguous) else `usage` (exit 2).
  - `set_default(id)`. Decided (shared with the config and cmd-targets beads): a `default_target` set in `config.toml` wins over the registry's `default`; `default_target()` resolution reads config first and the registry second, and `targets default` reports `overridden_by_config: true` when config names a different target.
  - Read-modify-write of `registry.json` happens only under the lock (no lost updates between widget, terminal and agent).
- **Selector resolution** — `pub fn resolve(selector: &str, targets: &[Target], argv: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Target>>` and `resolve_one(...) -> Result<Target>`; precedence, first match wins:
  1. exact key (ULID string, case-insensitive);
  2. exact id (including qualified ids);
  3. product code (`wow_classic_era`);
  4. flavor folder name (`_retail_`, case-insensitive);
  5. family name (`forever`, `wrath-legacy`, `mainline`);
  6. path: an install root, client dir, or AddOns path (canonicalized; `~` is not expanded here — the shell does that).
  - No match → `target_not_found` with `fix` = `omaddons targets` (argv `["omaddons","targets"]`) and `details.selector`.
  - `resolve_one` with several matches → `target_ambiguous`: `details.candidates` = ids; `fix` = the original argv with the `-t`/`--target`/`--flavor` value replaced by the first candidate id (or `-t <id>` appended when the selector came from a default), `alternatives` = the same for each other candidate. Example: `omaddons install weakauras -t forever` matching `forever` (id) wins at step 2, while `-t vanilla-legacy` with two such clients is ambiguous.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Reconciling a fresh discovery with an empty registry returns every target with `key: null` and ids from the default table; two retail clients yield `retail` and `retail@<qualifier>`; the result is identical across runs.
- `ensure_registered` refuses to compile without a `GlobalLockGuard`, writes `registry.json` and `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json` through fsx, and is idempotent.
- Moving a registered client dir to a new path re-links it by marker (same key and id); after the next registration the registry holds the new path.
- Copying a registered client dir yields `target_key_duplicate`; the original keeps the key; the copy gets a new key at its first registration.
- A registered target keeps its id even when an earlier-sorted new target would now take the bare id.
- `rename` rejects duplicates, ULIDs, family names and product codes with `usage` (exit 2).
- `resolve` accepts each of the seven selector forms; unknown selectors fail `target_not_found` (exit 3); ambiguous ones fail `target_ambiguous` (exit 3) with candidates, a `fix` whose `argv` is the original command with `-t <first candidate>`, and one alternative per other candidate.
- Read paths (`reconcile`, `resolve`) never write (asserted by hashing `<state>` and the trees before and after).

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/discover/registry.rs`): provisional id assignment table (collisions, qualifiers, `-2` suffixes), selector precedence table, ambiguity fix construction from argv (with `-t x`, `--target=x`, `--flavor x`, and no `-t`).
- Integration (`tests/registry.rs`, DEC-6 env isolation, `tests/common/` trees): register under a real `GlobalLock`; move and copy scenarios; concurrent registration from two threads (second waits on the lock, no lost entries); markers survive `remove` and re-link on `add_manual`.
- Log the registry JSON and reconcile output on failure.

## Considerations

- A copy detected only by marker can also be a restored backup of the same disk; the original-path rule decides deterministically, and both remain usable.
- The provisional id of an unregistered target can change when another target registers first; once registered, ids are permanent. Document this in the `targets` output (E7).
- Ids appear in `fix` argv; keep them shell-safe (the id grammar above guarantees it) even though display strings are quoted with shell-words anyway.
- Out of scope: the `targets` command (E7 `cmd-targets`), install's "single compatible target" default (E7 `cmd-install`), doctor auto-fix for duplicates (M4).
acceptance_criteria: Reconciling a fresh discovery with an empty registry yields key null and default-table ids, with collisions qualified as retail@<qualifier>, identically across runs; ensure_registered requires a GlobalLockGuard, writes registry.json and Interface/.omaddons/target.json through fsx and is idempotent; a moved client dir re-links by marker with the same key and id; a copied client dir yields target_key_duplicate, the original keeps its key and the copy gets a new one at first registration; registered targets keep their ids; rename rejects duplicates, ULIDs, family names and product codes with usage (exit 2); resolve accepts id, key, family, product code, flavor folder, install root and AddOns path, fails target_not_found (exit 3) for unknown selectors and target_ambiguous (exit 3) with candidates, a fix argv using the first candidate and one alternative per other candidate; reconcile and resolve never write
close_reason: Targets get stable identity: reconcile assigns registered keys and ids (by client dir, then marker for moved installs), detects copies, and gives unregistered targets deterministic provisional ids. **Implementation decisions (src/state/registry.rs, src/discover/registry.rs, tests/registry.rs).**
(1) Storage: `Registry { targets: Vec<RegistryEntry>, default }` and `TargetMarker { key }` are `Versioned` (kinds 'registry' and 'target_marker', 1.0, both listed in store::KINDS). schema_version comes from the store's encode, not from a struct field. Entries are sorted by key on save. There is one id per entry (no ids[]), as the bead decided.
(2) **Resolution works over `DiscoveredTarget`, not `Target`.** `resolve(selector, &[DiscoveredTarget]) -> Result<Vec<&DiscoveredTarget>>` and `resolve_one(selector, targets, argv)` keep the qualifier, which registration needs. `reconcile(&Registry, &[DiscoveredTarget]) -> Resolved { targets, warnings, missing }` returns DiscoveredTargets with key and id filled.
(3) Lock proof: `LockedRegistry::load(&GlobalLockGuard, &Paths)` is the only way to register, rename, remove, set_default or add_manual, and a `compile_fail` doctest shows the call without a guard. Each change saves at once, and the loaded version status is checked, so a newer registry refuses with state_too_new.
(4) The session's ScopeTable must already contain the target's client dir: WriteSession borrows the table immutably, so `ensure_registered` cannot add it. Callers build `ScopeTable::new(paths, &client_dirs, None)` from the targets they may register.
(5) Reconcile: match by client dir first, then by marker key (a moved install). A marker key already taken by an earlier match is a copy: `target_key_duplicate` ('<copy id> carries the key of <owner> (a copied install); <owner> keeps it', fix text 'it gets a new key on its first mutation'). Provisional ids reserve every registry id, missing entries included, then go in discovery order: default → default@qualifier → default@qualifier-2, …. Unassigned registry entries come back in `missing`.
(6) Registration: an entry already at this client dir means only the marker is repaired if needed; nothing is written otherwise, so it is idempotent. A marker key whose registered dir no longer carries it means a move: the entry's paths are refreshed. A marker key that is free is reused, so `remove` followed by `add` re-links. Otherwise a new key is minted. The id is the provisional id when it is still free in the registry, else the free_id sequence. The marker is written before the registry, so a crash between the two leaves a marker key that the next registration reuses.
(7) The marker path follows the on-disk case of `Interface` (`marker_path`). `read_marker` is tolerant: only the 'key' field matters, so a newer marker version still reads.
(8) Ids: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9@._-]*$`, and not a ULID, family name or product code (`id_problem`). Discovery defaults are made id-safe (`client` when nothing is left). rename and add_manual with a name return usage (exit 2) on any violation or duplicate.
(9) add_manual normalizes: an AddOns path becomes its client dir, a flavor folder becomes its Battle.net root plus that folder, a custom root stays as-is. Anything else is target_not_found with details.path. A name with several resulting targets is usage, with one fix or alternative per flavor folder.
(10) Selectors: key (case-insensitive ULID), id (ASCII case-insensitive), product, flavor folder, family, then a canonical path (install root, client dir or AddOns dir). The first step with a match wins. Ambiguity rewrites argv: -t/--target/--flavor values, --target=/--flavor=, -tX, or '-t <id>' appended before '--'; presentation flags are dropped via cli::fix_argv.
(11) Config's default_target vs the registry default is left to the config bead (2.1). The registry only stores `default`.

title: Epic: M1 ClientRules, TOC engine and folder inventory
description:
## Background

The reference addon manager (vision §3, defects R5 and R6) picked files by upstream metadata and copied archive folders verbatim, so it installed alpha builds by default and could install a build the client never loads. omaddons treats the client's own load rules as ground truth (D5): every candidate archive and every installed folder is checked against the rules of the client that will load it.

Those rules differ by client. Modern Battle.net clients load one of several suffixed TOC files by a fixed precedence and accept comma-separated `## Interface` lists. Private-server clients (1.12.1, 2.4.3, 3.3.5a, 4.3.4, 5.4.8) read only `Folder/Folder.toc` with one Interface value. A WoW: Forever client loads a retail-only `_Mainline.toc`, so the suffix alone cannot decide compatibility. Wine resolves names case-insensitively, so folder identity and TOC lookup must be case-insensitive too.

Vision D15 and D29 require all of this to be data: a product table, a version-to-family table, an interface formula and a `ClientRules` table keyed by version range and install kind. No client version is special-cased in code. New flavors (WoW: Forever launches 2026-11-04; its final layout is UNVERIFIED) must work by adding or overriding table rows.

This epic delivers the data tables, the TOC parser, `loaded_toc` with the compatibility verdict, the M1 checkpoint test matrix, and the folder inventory that classifies `AddOns/` entries as protected, managed, linked or unmanaged.

## Goals

- `src/rules.rs`: the product table, version-to-family table, interface formula, family interface ranges, release.json flavor names, TOC suffix sets and `ClientRules` rows for modern retail, every Classic family, Forever and the five legacy generations, all overridable from config.
- `src/toc.rs`: a TOC parser that never panics, honors the 1024-character line limit and recognizes every directive the vision lists.
- `loaded_toc` and the compatibility verdict over a `FolderView` trait (DEC-14), shared by installed folders and archive contents.
- The M1 TOC checkpoint: every suffix, the Forever-loads-`_Mainline` guard, comma Interface lists and every legacy row are covered by table-driven tests.
- `src/inventory.rs`: read-only classification of every `AddOns/` entry by case-folded key, with TOC metadata and a verdict against the target.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:
- Interface vectors come from the tables: 12.1.5 → 120105, 1.60.1 → 16001, 3.80.2 → 38002, 3.3.5 → 30300, 1.12.1 → 11200, 2.4.3 → 20400, 4.3.4 → 40300, 5.4.8 → 50400.
- A Forever target never verifies a retail-only `_Mainline.toc` (Interface 120105), and a modern classic-flavor build never verifies against a 1.12.1 client.
- Every builtin `ClientRules` row has fixtures, and the toc-matrix suite passes in `argc gate`.
- `inventory` classifies the development machine's 3.3.5a client (23 `Blizzard_*` folders) as 23 protected folders and nothing else, without writing anything.
- `grep` finds no interface number or client version literal in `src/toc.rs` or `src/inventory.rs`; every such value lives in `src/rules.rs`.

## Non-Goals

- Dependency resolution from `Dependencies`/`OptionalDeps` (M2). This epic parses the directives only.
- Drift detection against the per-file index (M2).
- CurseForge and Wago folder fingerprints, which use the TOC-derived file set (M5).
- Adoption tiers that read TOC `X-` ids (M2). This epic exposes the fields.
- Evaluating directive conditionals or path variables beyond recognizing them.
- Archive reading. The archive `FolderView` implementation belongs to the archive-inspect bead (E6).

## Considerations

- Several client facts are UNVERIFIED in the vision and must stay marked: the exact classic builds that gained multi-TOC (1.13.7 / 2.5.1 region) and comma Interface lists, how legacy clients treat a comma list (assumed: leading integer), the syntax of directive conditionals, Titan's game-specific TOC suffix, and the final Forever layout. Each must be a table value that config can override, never a code branch.
- Family interface ranges are derived from the version-to-family table. They are deliberately conservative for legacy clients (3.3.x → exactly the 30300 generation); config can widen them.
- `status --cached` has a 5 ms budget, so the inventory needs a classification-only mode that reads no TOC files.
- The inventory and verdict feed the ownership checks (E6) and the `list` and `status` commands (E7). Wire names in their output are pinned later by the M4 golden test, so pick them carefully now (DEC-3).
acceptance_criteria: interface vectors 12.1.5→120105, 1.60.1→16001, 3.80.2→38002, 3.3.5→30300, 1.12.1→11200, 2.4.3→20400, 4.3.4→40300, 5.4.8→50400 come from src/rules.rs tables; a Forever target never verifies a retail-only _Mainline.toc and a modern classic-flavor build never verifies against a 1.12.1 client; every builtin ClientRules row has fixtures and the toc-matrix suite passes in argc gate; inventory classifies a 3.3.5a client with 23 Blizzard_* folders as 23 protected folders without writing anything; no interface number or client version literal appears in src/toc.rs or src/inventory.rs

title: Folder inventory: classify AddOns folders and read TOC metadata
description:
## Background

The reference implementation only listed unmanaged addons and exposed custom clients' `Blizzard_*` folders as if they were mutable (vision §3, R9). omaddons classifies every entry in a target's `AddOns/` folder by its case-folded key, because Wine resolves names case-insensitively (D27), and protects `Blizzard_*` folders at the type level (D14). The inventory is the read-only view that ownership checks (E6 ownership bead), `list` and `status` (E7) are built on.

Folder classes (vision §5.1; protection, ownership, collision and duplicate checks all use the key):
- `protected`: key starts with `blizzard_`. Private-server client packs ship extracted `Blizzard_*` addons inside `Interface/AddOns`; they must never be modified. The development machine's 3.3.5a client has 23 of them and nothing else.
- `managed`: owned by exactly one managed addon record.
- `linked`: a symlink, for example a developer's working copy. Listed, never mutated, never followed outside AddOns.
- `unmanaged`: everything else.

Rules from the vision: read commands never write to game directories (§3 R10), and discovery never creates `AddOns/`.

Placeholders: `<client dir>` is the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/` (a flavor folder such as `<root>/_retail_/`, or a custom client root).

## Technical Approach

Module `src/inventory.rs` (currently a doc comment). All output types derive `Serialize` and `JsonSchema` with snake_case wire names (DEC-3); field order is wire order.

```rust
pub enum Depth { Classes, Full }
pub fn inventory(client: &ClientPaths, target: &Target, record: Option<&TargetRecord>,
                 table: &RulesTable, depth: Depth) -> Result<Inventory>
```
- `ClientPaths` comes from `src/state/paths.rs` (`addons()` = `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns`). `TargetRecord` (state-records bead) supplies managed ownership: each `AddonRecord.folders` entry maps folder key → addon name.
- `Depth::Classes` does a `read_dir` plus `symlink_metadata` per entry and reads no TOC files. `status --cached` uses it to stay inside its 5 ms budget. `Depth::Full` adds TOC metadata and a verdict per folder.

Algorithm:
1. If `AddOns/` does not exist, return an empty inventory with `addons_dir_missing: true`. Never create it.
2. If `AddOns/` cannot be listed, return error `io` (exit 1) with a fix naming the path's permissions. Per-entry failures do not fail the whole call.
3. Entries: directories and symlinks only. Regular files are counted in `stray_files` and otherwise ignored.
4. For each entry, `FolderName::new(name)` (model bead). A failure (for example a leading `.`, a control character, over 255 bytes) gives class `invalid`, never mutated, listed with its lossy name.
5. Class precedence: `invalid` > `protected` (`is_protected()`, even when the entry is a symlink) > `linked` (`symlink_metadata().file_type().is_symlink()`) > `managed` (key present in the record's folder map) > `unmanaged`. Decided: `linked` beats `managed`. A managed folder replaced by a symlink is reported as linked with its `owners` still filled in, so `list` can say which addon's folder became a link, and nothing ever mutates it.
6. `owners: Vec<String>`: every record claiming the key, sorted. More than one owner means corrupt state; set `ownership_conflict: true`. Detecting it is in scope; the doctor finding is M4.
7. Case duplicates: group entries by key. Groups larger than one set `case_duplicate: true` on every member. The ownership bead turns this into a refusal (`case_collision`). The inventory only reports it.
8. Missing managed folders: record folders with no entry on disk go into `missing: Vec<MissingFolder { addon, folder }>`. Drift and the doctor finding `record-folder-missing` come later.
9. With `Depth::Full`, for non-linked, non-invalid directories: `loaded_toc(&DiskFolder::new(path), &target.rules)` and `verdict(...)` (toc-loaded bead). Store `toc: Option<TocSummary { file, title, version, author, interfaces, x_ids: BTreeMap<String,String> }>`, `verdict: Option<VerdictReport>`. A read error sets `unreadable: true` and leaves `toc` empty. Linked folders are not read. Their link target is reported only in verbose output (`link_target`, skipped when `None`), because it may point anywhere on the user's disk.
10. Sort entries by key, then by on-disk name, so output is deterministic.

```rust
pub struct Inventory { addons_dir_missing: bool, folders: Vec<FolderEntry>, missing: Vec<MissingFolder>,
                       counts: Counts, stray_files: u32 }
pub struct FolderEntry { name: String, key: String, class: FolderClass, owners: Vec<String>,
                         case_duplicate: bool, ownership_conflict: bool, unreadable: bool,
                         toc: Option<TocSummary>, verdict: Option<VerdictReport>, link_target: Option<String> }
pub enum FolderClass { Protected, Managed, Linked, Unmanaged, Invalid }
pub struct Counts { protected: u32, managed: u32, linked: u32, unmanaged: u32, invalid: u32 }
```

Read-only guarantee: the module performs no writes, so it needs no fsx session. The single-writer test (fsx-prune-guard bead) already forbids `std::fs` mutation calls outside `src/fsx/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A synthetic 3.3.5a client with 23 `Blizzard_*` folders gives 23 `protected` entries, zero others, and `counts.protected == 23`. A before/after hash of the tree is identical.
- `blizzard_auctionui` (lowercase), `BLIZZARD_x` and a symlink named `Blizzard_Foo` all classify as `protected`.
- A folder listed in a `TargetRecord` is `managed` with its owner. The same folder replaced by a symlink is `linked` with `owners` still set. A record folder absent on disk appears in `missing`.
- `WeakAuras` and `weakauras` side by side are both flagged `case_duplicate`. Two records claiming one key set `ownership_conflict`.
- `.git` and a name with a control character are `invalid`. A stray `foo.zip` file counts in `stray_files` only.
- With `Depth::Full`, entries carry the loaded TOC file name, Title, Version and Interface list, plus a verdict against the target (a retail-only addon in a Forever target shows `wrong_flavor`). With `Depth::Classes`, no TOC file is opened (asserted with a `FolderView` read counter or by making TOC files unreadable).
- A missing `AddOns/` returns `addons_dir_missing: true` and does not create the directory. An unlistable `AddOns/` returns error `io`.
- Output order is deterministic, and an insta JSON snapshot of a mixed inventory is committed.

## Test Plan

- Unit: class precedence table (each combination of protected name, symlink, record ownership); key grouping for case duplicates; missing-folder detection; counts.
- Integration (`tests/inventory.rs`, using `tests/common/trees.rs`): the 3.3.5a 23-folder client; a retail client with managed, unmanaged, linked (symlink to a dir outside the tree; assert it is never read) and invalid entries; a Forever client holding a retail-only addon (`wrong_flavor` verdict); an unreadable folder (chmod 000; skip when running as root); a missing AddOns dir.
- Performance: `Depth::Classes` on 500 synthetic folders completes in under 5 ms warm (debug-build assertion with generous slack, or a `#[ignore]` benchmark run at checkpoints).
- Snapshot: insta JSON of a mixed inventory.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (tree listing and the inventory JSON).

## Considerations

- The inventory never decides whether a mutation is allowed. Refusals (`protected_folder`, `unmanaged_folder`, `ownership_conflict`, `case_collision`, all exit 4) are the ownership bead's job, re-checked under the lock by the engine.
- Hidden entries such as `.git` are reported as `invalid` rather than silently skipped, so the user can see them. They are never touched.
- Large UIs (ElvUI, WeakAuras plus companions) can have hundreds of folders. `Depth::Full` reads one TOC per folder with bounded line reads (toc-loaded), so expect tens of milliseconds, not seconds.
- Account, realm and character names never appear here; the inventory does not look inside `WTF/`.
- Adoption tiers (M2) will consume `toc.x_ids` and the unmanaged list. Keep those fields stable.
acceptance_criteria: a synthetic 3.3.5a client with 23 Blizzard_* folders gives 23 protected entries and nothing else, and the tree hash is unchanged; blizzard_auctionui, BLIZZARD_x and a symlink named Blizzard_Foo classify as protected; a record-listed folder is managed with its owner, the same folder replaced by a symlink is linked with owners still set, and a record folder absent on disk appears in missing; WeakAuras and weakauras side by side are both case_duplicate and two records claiming one key set ownership_conflict; .git and control-character names are invalid and a stray foo.zip only counts in stray_files; Depth::Full entries carry loaded TOC file, Title, Version, Interface list and a verdict (retail-only addon in a Forever target shows wrong_flavor) while Depth::Classes opens no TOC file; a missing AddOns returns addons_dir_missing true without creating it and an unlistable AddOns returns error io; output order is deterministic and an insta JSON snapshot is committed
close_reason: The folder inventory classifies every AddOns entry (protected, managed, linked, unmanaged, invalid) by case-folded key, reports owners, ownership conflicts, case duplicates, missing record folders and stray files, and at full depth adds each folder's loaded TOC summary and verdict; it never writes or follows links

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **loaded_toc/verdict landed (src/toc/loaded.rs).** For each AddOns folder: `let view = toc::DiskFolder::new(path)?`; `toc::loaded_toc(&view, &target.rules)?` gives `Option<LoadedToc { file, level, suffix, case_ambiguous, toc }>`; `toc::verify_target(&view, &target, &table)?` gives `VerdictReport { loaded (summary), verdict: Compatible{out_of_date} | WrongFlavor{reason} | NoToc, warnings }`. DiskFolder never follows symlinks or opens FIFOs, and TOC reads are bounded per line.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: claim: src/inventory.rs, src/toc/loaded.rs (judge split), tests/inventory.rs.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/inventory.rs; tests/inventory.rs; src/toc/loaded.rs gained `judge`).**
(1) Signature `inventory(&Target, Option<&TargetRecord>, &RulesTable, Depth) -> Result<Inventory>`, with no ClientPaths parameter: Target already carries client_dir, and AddOns is found with `discover::find_path(client_dir, [Interface, AddOns])`, ignoring case. When it is missing, `addons_dir_missing` is set and nothing is created.
(2) Each TOC is read once: `toc::judge(folder, Option<&LoadedToc>, rules, family, interface, table)` judges an already-loaded TOC, and `toc::verdict` now calls it.
(3) Non-folders (regular files, FIFOs, sockets) all count in `stray_files`. Folder classes follow the bead's precedence, invalid > protected > linked > managed > unmanaged, so a symlink named Blizzard_* is protected.
(4) `x_ids` holds the X- fields whose key ends in 'id' (case-insensitive): X-Curse-Project-ID, X-WoWI-ID, X-Wago-ID, X-Tukui-ProjectID. Other X- fields stay in the TOC.
(5) `link_target` is filled only at Depth::Full (the 'verbose' view) and omitted from JSON when None. Links are never opened or followed.
(6) `missing` is sorted and de-duplicated. `owners` lists the names of every record addon claiming the key, sorted; more than one means `ownership_conflict`.
(7) An unlistable AddOns is error io (exit 1) with the fix 'check the permissions of <path>'. An entry whose TOC or folder cannot be read gets `unreadable: true`.
(8) Performance: 500 folders at Depth::Classes take under 5 ms in release, asserted with 50 ms of slack in debug.

title: Product, version-to-family, interface and ClientRules tables in src/rules.rs
description:
## Background

Vision D15 and D29: client detection and client capabilities are data, never code. New flavors appear with little notice (WoW: Forever's product `wowf` / folder `_forever_` first appeared in Blizzard's productconfig on 2026-10-13; launch is 2026-11-04 and the final layout is UNVERIFIED), and private-server clients from 1.12.1 to 5.4.8 need correct rules without a code change. The product code does not determine the game family: `wow_classic_era_ptr` runs TBC 2.5.x and `wow_classic_beta` runs Forever 1.60.x. Family is derived from the version; the product is a label and a fallback.

This bead fills `src/rules.rs` (currently a doc comment) with every table the rest of M1 reads. Per DEC-13 it depends on nothing: `Family`, `InstallKind`, `TargetKind`, `ClientVersion` and `ClientRules` are defined here, and `src/model.rs` (model bead) builds `Target` on top of them. Discovery, the TOC engine, candidate selection and the inventory all consume these tables.

## Technical Approach

All types derive `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema` (DEC-3); field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.

**Core types**
- `ClientVersion { major: u32, minor: u32, patch: u32, build: Option<u32> }`. `FromStr` accepts 2–4 dot-separated numeric parts and ignores trailing letters on the last numeric part (`"3.3.5a"` → 3.3.5). Displays and serializes as `major.minor.patch[.build]`. `Ord` compares the numeric tuple. Model's `Target.version` uses this type.
- `Family`, serialized kebab-case: `vanilla`, `forever`, `tbc`, `wrath`, `titan`, `cata`, `mists`, `mainline`, `vanilla-legacy`, `tbc-legacy`, `wrath-legacy`, `cata-legacy`, `mists-legacy`, `unknown`. `Family::is_legacy()`.
- `InstallKind { Battlenet, Custom }` → `battlenet|custom`. `TargetKind { Live, Test }` → `live|test`.

**Product table** (vision §4.1; exe names vary in case, so match case-insensitively; folder names are not derivable by pattern):

| product | folder | exe | kind | default_id |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wow | `_retail_` | WoW.exe | live | retail |
| wowt | `_ptr_` | WoWT.exe | test | ptr |
| wowxptr | `_xptr_` | WoWT.exe | test | xptr |
| wow_beta | `_beta_` | WoWB.exe | test | beta |
| wow_classic | `_classic_` | WoWClassic.exe | live | classic |
| wow_classic_ptr | `_classic_ptr_` | WoWClassicT.exe | test | classic-ptr |
| wow_classic_beta | `_classic_beta_` | WowB.exe | test | classic-beta |
| wow_classic_era | `_classic_era_` | WoWClassic.exe | live | era |
| wow_classic_era_ptr | `_classic_era_ptr_` | WowClassicT.exe | test | era-ptr |
| wow_anniversary | `_anniversary_` | WoWClassic.exe | live | anniversary |
| wow_classic_titan | `_classic_titan_` | WoWClassic.exe | live | titan |
| wowf | `_forever_` | Wow.exe | live | forever |

Lookups: `product_by_code`, `product_by_folder` (case-insensitive), `product_by_exe`. Legacy default ids by family: vanilla-legacy → `vanilla`, tbc-legacy → `tbc`, wrath-legacy → `wotlk`, cata-legacy → `cata`, mists-legacy → `mists`. Decided: the default ids live in this table so discovery and the registry consume one source rather than each defining its own list.

**Version → family table**, ordered rows, first match wins (vision §4.1):
1. custom 1.12.x → vanilla-legacy; custom 2.4.x → tbc-legacy; custom 3.3.x → wrath-legacy; custom 4.3.x → cata-legacy; custom 5.4.x → mists-legacy.
2. any kind: major 1 and minor < 50 → vanilla (Era); major 1 and minor ≥ 50 → forever; 2.5 → tbc; 3.4 → wrath; 3.80 → titan; 4.4 → cata; 5.5 → mists; major ≥ 6 → mainline.
3. no match → unknown.

Decided: custom clients whose version is not in a legacy range fall through to the general rows, so a custom 3.4.x client is `wrath`.

**Interface formula**: `major*10000 + minor*100`, plus `patch` when the row's `interface_includes_patch` is true. Vectors: 12.1.5 → 120105; 1.60.1 → 16001; 3.80.2 → 38002; legacy rows omit the patch: 3.3.5 → 30300, 1.12.1 → 11200, 2.4.3 → 20400, 4.3.4 → 40300, 5.4.8 → 50400. Current interfaces (warcraft.wiki.gg TOC format, Oct 2026): retail 120105, Mists Classic 50504, Classic Era 11509, Anniversary/TBC 20506, Titan 38002, Cata 40402, Forever 16001.

**Family interface ranges** (inclusive), used by the verdict as the family floor and ceiling. They are derived from the version table:
mainline 60000..; forever 15000–19999; vanilla 11300–14999; tbc 20500–20599; wrath 30400–30499; titan 38000–38099; cata 40400–40499; mists 50500–50599; vanilla-legacy 11200–11299; tbc-legacy 20400–20499; wrath-legacy 30300–30399; cata-legacy 40300–40399; mists-legacy 50400–50499; unknown has no range.
Decided: the vanilla floor is 11300, not 10000, because Battle.net Classic Era clients start at 1.13. Interfaces 11200–11299 are the 1.12 private-server generation, which has a different API and belongs to `vanilla-legacy`. Ranges separate families, not expansions: an older-expansion retail TOC is `out_of_date`, not wrong flavor.

**TOC suffixes** (vision §4.3; the separator may be `-` or `_`):
- game-specific: `Standard` (retail, since 12.1.5), `Forever`/`Camelot` (internal game type `camelot`), `Mists`, `Cata`, `Wrath`, `TBC` (also Anniversary), `Vanilla`, `Plunderstorm`/`WoWLabs`, `WoWHack`;
- family: `Mainline` (standard, forever, plunderstorm, wowhack), `Classic` (vanilla through mists);
- legacy: `BCC`, `WOTLKC`, which current clients no longer load but which appear in the wild.
Export `KNOWN_TOC_SUFFIXES` (all of the above) for archive root detection.

**ClientRules row**: `{ name, family, install_kind: Option<InstallKind>, version_min, version_max: Option, game, game_types: Vec<String>, multi_toc, comma_interface, game_suffixes, family_suffixes, legacy_suffixes, directive_conditionals, path_variables, interface_includes_patch, legacy }`. Decided: `game` (the row's game type) and `game_types` (every name `AllowLoadGameType` may use for it) are row fields, so `loaded_toc` takes `(folder, &ClientRules)` and needs no separate game argument.

Builtin rows (`rules_for(version, kind)` = the version's family, then the first row of that family whose range contains the version, else `fallback`):

| name | versions | game_suffixes | family | multi | comma | dir.cond | patch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mainline | ≥ 12.1.5 | Standard | Mainline | y | y | y | y |
| mainline-12.0.7 | 12.0.7–12.1.4 | — | Mainline | y | y | y | y |
| mainline-10.2.7 | 10.2.7–12.0.6 | — | Mainline | y | y | n | y |
| mainline-9.1 | 9.1.0–10.2.6 | — | Mainline | y | n | n | y |
| forever | 1.50+ | Forever, Camelot | Mainline | y | y | n | y |
| vanilla | 1.13–1.49 | Vanilla | Classic | y | y | n | y |
| tbc / wrath / cata / mists | 2.5 / 3.4 / 4.4 / 5.5 | TBC / Wrath / Cata / Mists | Classic | y | y | n | y |
| titan | 3.80 | — (UNVERIFIED) | Classic | y | y | n | y |
| vanilla-legacy … mists-legacy | 1.12 / 2.4 / 3.3 / 4.3 / 5.4, custom | — | — | n | n | n | n |
| fallback | anything else | — | — | n | n | n | n |

Legacy rows and `fallback` set `legacy: true`. `legacy_suffixes` is empty in every builtin row, because current clients dropped `_BCC`/`_WOTLKC`. The field exists for overrides. `path_variables` is true on multi-TOC rows and false elsewhere; the introducing build is UNVERIFIED, and the M1 verdict does not use it. game/game_types: standard/[standard] for mainline rows; camelot/[camelot, forever]; vanilla, tbc, wrath, cata and mists each list their own name. Titan's game type and suffix are UNVERIFIED: empty game_types, `game = "titan"`.

**release.json flavor names** per family: mainline→`mainline`, vanilla→`classic`, tbc→`bcc`, wrath→`wrath`, titan→`titan`, cata→`cata`, mists→`mists`, forever→`forever`; legacy families and unknown → none. `family_for_release_flavor(name)` also accepts the packager aliases tbc→bcc, vanilla→classic, wotlkc→wrath and camelot→forever.

**Overrides**: `RulesTable::builtin()` and `RulesTable::with_overrides(&self, RulesOverrides) -> Result<RulesTable, RulesError>`. `RulesOverrides` (deserializable from a config `[rules]` section; the config bead wires loading) can add or replace product rows by code, prepend version-family rows, add or replace ClientRules rows by name, and replace family ranges. Validation rejects empty suffixes, suffixes with characters other than ASCII letters and digits, duplicate product folders, and inverted ranges. Methods: `family_for(&ClientVersion, InstallKind)`, `rules_for(..) -> &ClientRules`, `interface_for(&ClientVersion, &ClientRules) -> u32`, `family_range(Family)`, `release_flavor(Family)`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The interface vectors 12.1.5→120105, 1.60.1→16001, 3.80.2→38002, 3.3.5→30300 (custom), 1.12.1→11200 (custom), 2.4.3→20400, 4.3.4→40300 and 5.4.8→50400 come out of `rules_for` + `interface_for`, not literals in code.
- `family_for` maps 1.15.9→vanilla, 1.60.1→forever (both `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_`), 2.5.6→tbc (including product `wow_classic_era_ptr`), 3.80.2→titan, custom 3.3.5→wrath-legacy, custom 3.4.3→wrath, Battle.net 2.6.0→unknown.
- `rules_for(12.1.5)` lists `Standard`; `rules_for(12.1.0)` (PTR) does not; `rules_for(12.0.1)` (beta) has `directive_conditionals: false`.
- Product lookups by folder and by exe are case-insensitive (`wowclassic.exe` matches), and unknown folders return None.
- Overrides can add a `_newflavor_` product and replace Titan's suffixes; invalid overrides return `RulesError`.
- All types serialize with the wire names above, and an insta snapshot of `RulesTable::builtin()` is committed.

## Test Plan

- Unit (in `src/rules.rs`): table-driven vectors for `family_for`, `rules_for` and `interface_for` across every product in §4.1 and every legacy row; product lookups; release flavor names and aliases.
- Unit: table invariants. Product codes, folders and default ids are unique; every family except unknown has a range; ranges do not overlap; every builtin row's family matches its version range; suffix strings are valid.
- Unit: `ClientVersion` parsing (`12.1.5.70391`, `3.3.5a`, `1.60.1`, two-part `2.5`), ordering, display round-trip; proptest: parse(display(v)) == v.
- Unit: overrides merge and validation.
- Snapshot: `insta::assert_json_snapshot!(RulesTable::builtin())`.

## Considerations

- UNVERIFIED, so each is a table value only: Titan's game suffix and type; the first classic builds with multi-TOC and comma lists (the rows cover current clients only); directive conditional support outside retail ≥ 12.0.7; the build that introduced path variables; the final Forever layout (`_forever_` vs `_classic_beta_`). Both Forever layouts map to `forever` through the version.
- Pre-9.1 retail private-server clients (e.g. 7.x) get the conservative `fallback` row. Proper rows are out of scope for M1; users can add them through overrides.
- Legacy families are exactly one minor generation wide (3.3.x → 30300), so a 3.2-era addon is wrong flavor for a 3.3.5a client. This is conservative on purpose; overrides can widen a range.
- CurseForge gameVersionTypeIds and Wago `game_version` names are M5 and do not belong in this bead.
- No I/O in this module.

comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/rules.rs).** Each one keeps a dependent bead's expectation or closes a gap in this bead's spec.

- **Two fallback rows, chosen by install kind**, instead of a single `fallback`:
  - `fallback-custom` is the bead's conservative row: legacy, a single plain TOC, no patch digit. Custom clients with no matching row get it, e.g. pre-9.1 retail private servers (7.3.5 → 70300) and custom 1.11.
  - `fallback-battlenet` is a permissive modern row: multi-TOC, comma lists, path variables, patch digit, family suffixes `Mainline` then `Classic`, empty game types, not legacy.
  - Why: discover-battlenet step 8 expects "the most permissive modern row" for unknown Battle.net flavors, and every Battle.net client is multi-TOC. The verdict's exact-interface rule for `unknown` is what guards installs.
  - `RulesTable::fallback(kind)` returns the row directly, for targets with no usable version.
  - Both rows are struct fields, so a fallback always exists by type. Overrides can patch them by name.
- **`rules_for`** = the version's family, then the first row of that family whose `install_kind` and version range match, else `fallback(kind)`. Range bounds ignore build numbers (12.1.4.99999 is inside `..=12.1.4`).
- **Range encoding.**
  - Version → family rows are `{install_kind, major: NumRange, minor: NumRange, family}`, with `NumRange {min, max: Option}` inclusive.
  - Family interface ranges use the same `NumRange`.
  - Classic-family `ClientRules` rows have no `version_max`, because their family already bounds them.
- **Lookups are `RulesTable` methods**, not free functions, so config overrides apply. The one exception is `rules::interface_for(&ClientVersion, &ClientRules)`, which needs no table.
- **`products_by_exe`** returns an iterator instead of a single `product_by_exe`. `WoWClassic.exe` and `WoWT.exe` are shared by several products, and `Wow.exe` by `wowf`.
- **`Family::release_flavor()` / `Family::from_release_flavor()`** are on `Family`, as the select bead expects, because `select(set, target, channel)` has no table. Families are a closed enum, so the mapping stays next to it.
- **`default_id_for_family`** also covers non-legacy families (the family name), so discover-custom reads one table. `unknown` → `None` (the id then comes from the root basename).
- **`toc_suffixes()`** returns `KNOWN_TOC_SUFFIXES` plus any other row suffix, override rows included, de-duplicated ignoring case. This is the union archive-inspect asks for.
- **Overrides** come from the config `[rules]` table as `RulesOverrides { products, version_families, family_ranges, client_rules }`.
  - `client_rules.<name>` is a `ClientRulesOverride` field subset, which patches an existing row.
  - A new name adds a row before the builtin rows. A new row requires `family`, `version_min`, `game`, `multi_toc`, `comma_interface`, `interface_includes_patch` and `legacy`; every other field defaults to empty, false or `None`.
  - A patch cannot reset `install_kind`/`version_max` to `None`.
  - Validation also rejects empty product fields and a range on `unknown`.
  - No `deny_unknown_fields`: config's `config_unknown_key` warning should cover typos without failing the load.
- **`RulesTable`** derives `Serialize` + `JsonSchema` but not `Deserialize`, and its fields are private. The only way in is `builtin()`/`with_overrides()`, both validated.
- **Legacy `game` values** are the base game name (`wrath` for `wrath-legacy`). The fallbacks use `unknown`. Legacy rows ignore game-type directives, so the value is descriptive only.
