Unit: zips and directories (ids stable, .git ignored, changes detected, bad and missing paths), same-zip identity, allowlisted hosts and host_blocked fix. tests/plan.rs: fetch_once over file:, file: dir and url: makes zero requests; a file: dir install takes its version from the TOC · found: none

title: Http trait, ureq client, per-hop host allowlist, offline mode and net.log
description:
## Background

Every network request omaddons makes must go through one HTTP client, so the privacy promise can be checked rather than taken on trust (vision goal G5, decisions D9 and D13). This bead builds that client and the guard around it: an `Http` trait, a ureq 3 implementation on rustls with the ring provider, a hard host allowlist checked on every request and on every redirect hop, https only, an offline switch, size and time limits, and a local `net.log` that records every request with credentials and query secrets stripped.

The reference project passed API URLs around unchecked (vision §3, R11) and had no request log. Here a request to a host outside the allowlist fails with `host_blocked` before any bytes reach that host, and the user can read every request omaddons ever made with `omaddons net-log` (that command lands in cmd-info-netlog).

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/net/mod.rs` (trait, request/response types, stack constructor), `src/net/client.rs` (ureq transport), `src/net/guard.rs` (allowlist, https, offline, size cap, logging layer), `src/net/allowlist.rs`, `src/net/log.rs` (net.log writer and reader).

**Types.**
- `trait Http: Send + Sync { fn send(&self, req: Request) -> Result<Response>; }` (`Result` is `crate::error::Result`).
- `Request { method: Method, url: String, headers: Vec<(String, String)>, purpose: Purpose, timeout: TimeoutKind /* Api | Download */, redirect: RedirectMode /* Follow | Manual */, validators: bool }`. `purpose` is a short static label written to net.log (`"release-latest"`, `"release-json"`, `"asset"`, `"commits-atom"`, `"rest-releases"`, `"download"`, …). `validators` is consumed by net-resilience; net-core ignores it.
- `Response { status: u16, headers: Vec<(String, String)>, final_url: String, body: Body }` with `Body` readable either fully into bytes (API calls) or as a streaming reader (`Response::into_reader()` for downloads, DEC-11). Helpers: `header(name)` (case-insensitive), `location()`, `error_for_status(context) -> Result<Response>` mapping non-success statuses to `http_status` (exit 1; retryable only for 5xx).
- Layering, outermost first: `Redirecting<Guarded<T>>` where `T` is a transport (`UreqTransport` here; `ReplayTransport`/`RecordTransport` come from net-fixtures). net-resilience wraps this stack further. `net::stack(&NetConfig) -> Box<dyn Http>` builds it; it exposes a hook for net-fixtures to swap the transport in debug builds (DEC-7).

**Guard layer (`Guarded`).** Every request that reaches the wire passes through it, including each redirect hop:
1. If offline (`NetConfig.offline`, set from `--offline` or `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`), fail immediately with `offline` (exit 1, not retryable). Nothing is logged because nothing was sent.
2. Parse the URL. Scheme must be `https`; anything else is `host_blocked`.
3. Host must be on the allowlist (exact, case-insensitive host match; no implicit subdomains). Otherwise `host_blocked` (exit 4, not retryable). `details` names the host, and the message says whether it was the first request or a redirect hop.
4. Send through the transport, measure duration, and write one net.log line. Downloads log when the body is fully read or dropped (a counting reader), so `bytes` is the real byte count.
5. Enforce `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (512 MiB): reject up front on a larger `Content-Length`, and abort the counting reader when the stream passes the cap. Both fail with `archive_too_large` (exit 4).

**Allowlist (vision §5.7).**
- Always: `api.github.com`, `github.com`, `codeload.github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com`, `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, `api.mmoui.com`, `cdn.wowinterface.com`, `api.tukui.org`.
- Only when the CurseForge source is enabled: `api.curseforge.com`, `edge.forgecdn.net`, `mediafilez.forgecdn.net`. Only when Wago is enabled: `addons.wago.io`. Neither is ever enabled in M1, but `NetConfig` carries the flags so M5 adds no new mechanism.
- Plus the git hosts the user configures (`NetConfig.git_hosts`). Those hosts are allowed for git subprocesses (source-git-hosts), which use the same allowlist check through `Allowlist::permits(host)`.
- `NetConfig` is built by the command layer from config and flags. net-core does not read `config.toml` itself.

**Redirects (`Redirecting`).** ureq is configured with zero redirects (`max_redirects(0)`) and `http_status_as_error(false)`. With `RedirectMode::Manual` the 3xx response is returned as is: the GitHub source reads the tag from `releases/latest`'s `Location`. With `Follow`, 301/302/303/307/308 are followed up to `MAX_REDIRECTS` hops. Each hop is a fresh request through `Guarded`, so it is allowlist-checked and logged. A relative `Location` resolves against the current URL. Exceeding the hop limit gives `network` (retryable: false). Decided: add `MAX_REDIRECTS = 5` to `src/politeness.rs` (no other place may hold it). Recording the new constant on the vision bead is part of this bead's close-out, because §5.13 requires every politeness value to appear there.

**Transport (`UreqTransport`).** One `ureq::Agent` built once per process:
- user agent `USER_AGENT` (`omaddons/<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>`);
- `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` 10 s;
- a whole-call timeout of `API_READ_TIMEOUT` (30 s) for `TimeoutKind::Api` and `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` (300 s) for `Download`;
- rustls with the ring provider (the crate's `rustls` feature) and webpki roots;
- no proxy. Decided: proxies are not supported in M1, because the vision does not call for them and CurseForge's terms forbid proxy access.

Transport errors map to `network` (exit 1, retryable): DNS, connect, TLS, timeout, reset.

**net.log (`src/net/log.rs`).** Path `<state>/omaddons/net.log`. Each request appends one JSON line through an fsx untracked session (`Op::AppendFile`, DEC-10), in this field order: `{"time": RFC 3339 UTC, "method", "host", "path", "status": u16|null, "bytes": u64|null, "duration_ms", "purpose", "via": "http"|"git", "error": code|null}`.
- Decided: the query string is never logged, only the path. This strips tokens, `api-key`/`key`/`access_token` parameters and the signed parameters on GitHub release-asset redirect URLs in one rule.
- Request headers are never logged, so `Authorization` and `x-api-key` cannot leak.
- `status` is null and `error` holds the error code when no response arrived.
- Rotation: before appending, if the file is larger than `NET_LOG_MAX_BYTES` (10 MiB), rename it to `net.log.1` with `Op::Rename{mode: Replace}`, keeping exactly one previous file.
- `NetLog::record_git(GitLogEntry)` lets source-git-hosts log subprocesses: `via: "git"`, `method: "GIT"`, `status` = exit code, `purpose` = `"ls-remote"`/`"clone"`/`"fetch"`.
- A reader `NetLog::read(since: Option<Timestamp>) -> Vec<NetLogEntry>` covers `net.log.1` and `net.log` in order and skips a torn last line. It serves `net-log` and the test helpers.

**Credentials.** Never placed in a child process's argv and never logged. Headers carrying credentials are set by the caller (source-github-rest adds `Authorization` for `api.github.com` only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Http` trait, `Request`/`Response`, `Guarded`, `Redirecting`, `UreqTransport` and `net::stack()` exist in `src/net/`. ureq runs on rustls with ring and no redirects of its own.
- Requests to a non-allowlisted host fail with `host_blocked` (exit 4) before any connection to that host. A redirect hop to a non-allowlisted host fails the same way, and the hops before it are logged.
- Non-https URLs fail with `host_blocked`.
- With offline set, every request fails with `offline` (exit 1) and net.log is unchanged.
- Every request that reaches the transport produces exactly one net.log line with the documented fields. The query string and all request headers are absent from the line.
- Downloads larger than `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` fail with `archive_too_large`, whether announced by Content-Length or discovered while streaming.
- `MAX_REDIRECTS` exists only in `src/politeness.rs`, and `Follow` stops after that many hops.
- net.log rotates to `net.log.1` above `NET_LOG_MAX_BYTES`, keeping one previous file.
- `NetLog::record_git` and `NetLog::read` exist, and the reader tolerates a torn last line.
- All writes go through fsx; the single-writer test stays green.

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - allowlist matching: case-insensitive; `evil-github.com` and `github.com.evil` rejected; CF/Wago hosts rejected unless their flags are set; configured git hosts accepted.
  - Redirect resolution of relative and absolute `Location`.
  - Hop counting.
  - net.log line serialization: field order; query stripped from `/x?token=abc&sig=def`; no header text present.
  - Rotation threshold.
  - Reader skips a torn last line.
- Integration (a scripted in-process fake transport that returns canned responses; no network):
  - 302 from github.com to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` is followed and both hops are logged.
  - 302 to `example.org` yields `host_blocked`, with one logged hop.
  - Offline yields `offline` with zero lines.
  - The size cap applies via Content-Length and via a streaming body.
  - Manual mode returns the 302 with its `Location`.
- Live (`#[ignore]`, `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`): one GET to `https://github.com/` succeeds through `UreqTransport` and is logged. This proves rustls/ring works on the machine.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (request URL, response status, the net.log line).

## Considerations

- Concurrent processes append to the same net.log. Each line is a single `write` on an `O_APPEND` descriptor, so lines do not interleave on local filesystems. Rotation is best-effort, and a process still holding the old descriptor writes into `net.log.1`; that is acceptable because no line is lost.
- Host matching is exact. If GitHub moves release assets to a new host, downloads fail with `host_blocked` until the allowlist is updated. That is the intended trade-off.
- Retries, validators and the concurrency limits are net-resilience. Fixture replay, record mode and the live-probe harness are net-fixtures. This bead only provides the transport-swap hook.
- `api.mmoui.com`, `cdn.wowinterface.com` and `api.tukui.org` are on the always-list now, but no M1 source contacts them.
- Adding `MAX_REDIRECTS` changes the §5.13 politeness table. Post the updated row as a comment on omad-vision-8qa when closing this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Http trait, Request/Response, Guarded, Redirecting, UreqTransport and net::stack() exist in src/net/ with ureq on rustls+ring and no internal redirects; requests and redirect hops to non-allowlisted hosts fail with host_blocked (exit 4) before connecting, earlier hops logged; non-https URLs fail with host_blocked; offline makes every request fail with offline (exit 1) and leaves net.log unchanged; every wire request writes exactly one net.log line with the documented fields and no query string or headers; downloads over DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES fail with archive_too_large via Content-Length or streaming; MAX_REDIRECTS lives only in src/politeness.rs and Follow stops at it; net.log rotates to net.log.1 above NET_LOG_MAX_BYTES keeping one previous; NetLog::record_git and NetLog::read exist and the reader tolerates a torn last line; all writes go through fsx and the single-writer test stays green
close_reason: src/net provides the Http trait, Request/Response, the Guarded layer (offline, https+allowlist per hop, size cap, one net.log line per wire request), the Redirecting layer (MAX_REDIRECTS, credential stripping across hosts), UreqTransport on rustls+ring with no redirects or proxy, net::stack/stack_with, and NetLog with rotation, record_git and a torn-line-tolerant reader

title: HTTP fixture replay, record mode and live-probe harness
description:
## Background

Tests must never touch the network (vision §5.12 testing strategy), yet the sources have to be exercised against real upstream responses: GitHub's 302 `Location` headers, atom feeds with ETags, `release.json` files with their real quirks, and zip downloads. This bead provides three pieces:

- A **replay** transport that serves recorded responses.
- A **record** mode that captures real responses into fixture files with credentials and query secrets stripped.
- A **live-probe** harness, run only at milestone checkpoints, that hits each keyless endpoint once.

It also provides the test helpers that read `net.log`, so tests can assert facts such as "zero GitHub REST requests" (vision M1 checkpoint).

All three hooks are debug-only (DEC-7): compiled in, active only when `cfg!(debug_assertions)`, and ignored by release builds.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/net/replay.rs`, `src/net/record.rs`, the selection hook in `net::stack()` (`src/net/mod.rs`), `tests/common/netlog.rs`, and `tests/live_probes.rs`.

**Transport selection (DEC-7).** `net::stack()` picks the bottom transport through `select_transport(env, debug: bool)`:
- `debug && OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES=<dir> && OMADDONS_RECORD != "1"` → `ReplayTransport::load(dir)`.
- `debug && OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES=<dir> && OMADDONS_RECORD == "1"` → `RecordTransport::new(dir, UreqTransport)`.
- Otherwise, including every release build → `UreqTransport`.

The transport always sits under net-core's `Guarded` layer. Replayed and recorded runs therefore still enforce the allowlist and https-only rule, honor offline mode, and write normal `net.log` lines. This is what lets fixture tests assert REST counts from `net.log`.

**Fixture layout.** `tests/fixtures/http/<scenario>/<host>/<method>-<path-slug>-<hash8>.json`, plus an optional sibling `.body` file. `<hash8>` is the first 8 hex digits of the sha256 of the normalized request key. File shape:

```json
{"schema_version":"1.0",
 "request":{"method":"GET","url":"https://github.com/WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/releases/latest"},
 "responses":[{"status":302,"headers":[["location","https://github.com/WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/releases/tag/5.19.0"]],"body_file":null}]}
```

The tag value above is illustrative, not a fact. `responses` is consumed in order and the last entry repeats, which lets one scenario express "first 200 with ETag, then 304". Header names are stored lowercase. A scenario is a directory, and one test points `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` at one scenario.

**Request normalization (shared by record and replay).** The key is `METHOD scheme://host/path?query`, where:
- secret query parameters are removed: `token`, `api-key`, `api_key`, `key`, `access_token`, `jwt`, `sig`, `signature`, `se`, `sp`, `sv`, `sr`, `skoid`, `sktid`, `skt`, `ske`, `sks`, `skv`, `hmac`, and every `X-Amz-*` parameter;
- the remaining parameters are sorted.

Record applies the same stripping to every stored URL and to stored `location` headers. A replayed redirect therefore points at the normalized URL, which replay can then match.

**ReplayTransport.**
- Loads every `*.json` in the scenario directory tree at construction. Two files with the same key are a load error.
- `send` normalizes the request and serves the next response for its key, with the body streamed from the `.body` file when present.
- An unmatched request returns `internal` with the message `replay: no fixture for <METHOD> <normalized url>` (DEC-5 fix). A distinct code prevents an error-path test from passing by accident.
- `ReplayTransport::unmatched()` returns the misses for in-process tests.
- Never opens a socket.

**RecordTransport.**
- Wraps `UreqTransport` and forwards every request.
- Writes or overwrites the fixture for the normalized key, with the response body saved verbatim to `.body`.
- Never writes request headers, so `Authorization` and `x-api-key` cannot reach a fixture.
- Strips `set-cookie` from stored response headers.
- Writes go through fsx. Decided: in debug builds only, while `OMADDONS_RECORD=1`, the fsx write-scope table gains one entry, "the directory named by `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`", writable by `RecordTransport` alone. This bead adds that row to the scope table built by fsx-mutate. It keeps record mode inside the single-writer rule instead of letting `src/net/` call `std::fs`.

**net.log helpers (`tests/common/netlog.rs`, DEC-8).**
- `read_net_log(state_dir) -> Vec<NetLogEntry>` (wraps `omaddons::net::log::NetLog::read`).
- `count_host(&entries, host)`.
- `assert_no_github_rest(&entries)`: fails, listing the offending lines, if any entry has host `api.github.com`.
- `assert_each_url_once(&entries)`, which feeds the fetch-once checks.

**Live probes (`tests/live_probes.rs`).**
- Every test is `#[ignore]` and also returns early unless `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`.
- One request per keyless M1 endpoint, against `gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2` (the vision's example ref):
  1. `https://github.com/WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/releases/latest` returns 302 with a `Location` containing `/releases/tag/`.
  2. `releases.atom` returns 200 with an `ETag`. A conditional re-request returns 304.
  3. `releases/download/<tag>/release.json` redirects to an allowlisted host and decodes as JSON with a `releases` array.
  4. `commits/<default branch>.atom` returns 200 atom.
  5. `https://codeload.github.com/WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/zip/<sha>` returns 200 with a zip signature (`PK\x03\x04`).
- These probes check raw shape only. Each source bead adds its own decoder-level probe to this file (source-github-stable decodes `release.json`, source-git-github decodes commits atom), because the decoders live in those beads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In debug builds, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` selects replay, and adding `OMADDONS_RECORD=1` selects record. `select_transport` ignores both when `debug == false` (unit-tested).
- Replay serves recorded status, headers and body for a normalized request key, consumes `responses` in order with the last repeating, never opens a socket, and returns `internal` naming the URL for an unmatched request.
- Record writes fixtures in the documented layout with secret query parameters stripped from URLs and `location` headers, never stores request headers, and drops `set-cookie`.
- Record writes go through fsx under the debug-only fixture scope, and the single-writer test stays green.
- Replayed requests still pass through `Guarded`: allowlist enforced, offline honored, `net.log` lines written.
- `tests/common/netlog.rs` provides `read_net_log`, `count_host`, `assert_no_github_rest` and `assert_each_url_once`.
- `tests/live_probes.rs` exists with the five probes. They are skipped unless run with `--ignored` and `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`, and they pass against live GitHub at the checkpoint.

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - normalization strips each secret parameter, sorts the rest, and is idempotent;
  - fixture JSON round trip;
  - duplicate keys rejected at load;
  - `responses` sequencing;
  - `select_transport` truth table, including `debug=false`.
- Integration:
  - a scenario with a 302 chain (github.com → release-assets) replays through the full `net::stack()`, and `net.log` shows both hops;
  - a scenario hop to a non-allowlisted host still yields `host_blocked`;
  - an unmatched request yields `internal` with the URL;
  - record mode against a fake inner transport (not ureq) writes the expected files into a tempdir scenario, with `token=` and `X-Amz-Signature=` stripped and no request headers.
- Live (`#[ignore]`, `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`): the five probes above.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (normalized key, the fixture path looked up).

## Considerations

- Record runs real commands against the network. Use it only with throwaway `HOME`/`XDG_*` directories (DEC-6), and review the diff of `tests/fixtures/http/` before committing: fixtures are tracked and may become public. They must contain no tokens, cookies or personal data.
- Fixture bodies for large zips bloat the repository. Prefer the smallest real release that exercises a case, or build synthetic zips in `tests/common/archives.rs` (archive-inspect) for structural cases.
- Signed asset URLs change on every request. Stripping their query makes replay deterministic, at the cost of the fixtures no longer holding the exact signed URL. That is intended.
- Fixture files under `tests/fixtures/**` count as code changes for the local gate (D16).
- Out of scope: source-specific fixtures (recorded by each source bead), and the decoder-level live probes (added by the source beads).
acceptance_criteria: In debug builds OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES selects replay and OMADDONS_RECORD=1 selects record, and select_transport ignores both when debug is false; replay serves recorded status, headers and body for a normalized request key, sequences responses with the last repeating, never opens a socket, and returns internal naming the URL for unmatched requests; record writes fixtures in the documented layout with secret query parameters stripped from URLs and location headers, never stores request headers and drops set-cookie; record writes go through fsx under the debug-only fixture scope and the single-writer test stays green; replayed requests still pass through Guarded (allowlist, offline, net.log); tests/common/netlog.rs provides read_net_log, count_host, assert_no_github_rest and assert_each_url_once; tests/live_probes.rs holds the five probes, skipped unless --ignored with OMADDONS_LIVE=1, and they pass live at the checkpoint
close_reason: Debug builds replay recorded HTTP fixtures (or record new ones with secrets stripped, through fsx) underneath the full guarded stack, tests have net.log assertion helpers, and live probes of the five keyless GitHub endpoints exist and pass

The replay/record transports implement `net::Http` and get the same Redirecting+Guarded layers, so allowlist and logging behave as in production. Set `req.validators = true` on feed and list GETs to get 304 revalidation (`resp.cache == CacheState::Revalidated`). `net::run_bounded(items, MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS, |item| …)` fetches many refs in input order. comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/net/{replay,record}.rs, transport selection in src/net/mod.rs, tests/common/netlog.rs, tests/net_replay.rs, tests/live_probes.rs).**
(1) `net::choose_transport(env, debug) -> TransportChoice { Real, Replay(dir), Record(dir) }` is the pure truth table. `select_transport(env, debug, paths)` builds it, and `stack(config, log, paths)` uses it with the process env and cfg!(debug_assertions). title: Retry with backoff, HTTP validators cache and bounded parallelism
description:
## Background

Upstream hosts throttle, time out and fail. omaddons has to be polite to them (vision §5.13, D22) and dependable for the user: retry transient failures with backoff, honor `Retry-After`, avoid re-downloading unchanged feeds through ETag/Last-Modified validators, and cap concurrency both globally and per host. github.com's web endpoints, which the GitHub source relies on for its no-REST path, have undocumented secondary limits, and `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST` exists partly to stay under them (vision §8).

This bead adds three `Http` decorators on top of net-core's stack, plus a bounded worker helper that sources use to fetch many refs in parallel.

Placeholders: `<cache>` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `.cache` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/net/retry.rs`, `src/net/validators.rs`, `src/net/limit.rs`, `src/net/pool.rs`. The decorators wrap net-core's stack in this order (outermost first): `Limited<Retrying<Validating<Redirecting<Guarded<Transport>>>>>`. `net::stack()` (net-core) gains the three layers here.

**Constants used (all from `src/politeness.rs`, never literals):**

| Constant | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` | 6 | global in-flight request cap and worker-pool size |
| `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST` | 3 | per-host in-flight cap |
| `MAX_RETRIES` | 3 | retries after the first attempt, idempotent GET/HEAD only |
| `BACKOFF_BASE` / `BACKOFF_MAX` | 500 ms / 8 s | exponential ×2 with full jitter |
| `RETRY_AFTER_CAP` | 60 s | a longer `Retry-After` fails with `rate_limited` and the reset time |

**Retrying.**
- Only `GET` and `HEAD` are retried. Retryable outcomes:
  - HTTP 429;
  - any 5xx;
  - transport `network` errors (timeout, connection reset, connect failure).
- Delay before retry *n* (n = 0, 1, 2) is `random(0, min(BACKOFF_MAX, BACKOFF_BASE × 2^n))` (full jitter).
- If the response carries `Retry-After` (seconds or an HTTP-date, parsed with `jiff`):
  - a value ≤ `RETRY_AFTER_CAP` replaces the computed delay;
  - a longer value fails at once with `rate_limited` (exit 1, retryable). `details.reset_at` holds an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- Primary rate limits: a 403 or 429 carrying `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` fails at once with `rate_limited`. `reset_at` comes from `X-RateLimit-Reset` (epoch seconds). These responses are never retried.
- When retries are exhausted, the last outcome maps to its error:
  - 429 → `rate_limited`;
  - 5xx → `http_status` (retryable: true);
  - transport → `network` (retryable: true).
- Each attempt is a separate wire request, so each appears as its own net.log line (net-core logs them).
- Only failures that happen before the response is handed to the caller are retried. A body-read failure on a streamed download surfaces as `download_failed` (exit 1, retryable); the downloader (E6 blob-cache) may retry the whole download once.
- Randomness: a small inline xorshift64* generator seeded from the system time and pid. Decided: no new crate, because jitter needs no cryptographic quality.
- `Sleeper`, `Rng` and `Clock` are injectable traits, so tests run instantly and deterministically.

**Validating (ETag / Last-Modified).**
- Only requests with `Request.validators == true` take part: atom feeds and, later, the WoWI file list and REST release lists. Downloads never do.
- Cache directory: `<cache>/omaddons/http/`, two files per URL keyed by the sha256 of the full URL:
  - `<sha>.json` = `{"schema_version": "1.0", "url", "etag": str|null, "last_modified": str|null, "status": 200, "headers": [[k, v], …], "stored_at"}`;
  - `<sha>.body`.
- Before sending, add `If-None-Match` and/or `If-Modified-Since` when cached values exist.
- On `304`, return the cached response (status 200 and the cached body) with `Response.cache = CacheState::Revalidated`.
- On `200` with an `ETag` or `Last-Modified`, store body and metadata.
- Writes go through an fsx untracked session (DEC-10). The cache is derived data and safe to delete. A corrupt or missing cache entry means "no validators", never an error.
- net.log records the real 304, so revalidations are visible.

**Limited (concurrency).**
- A global counting semaphore of `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` permits plus one semaphore per host of `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST`, built from `Mutex` + `Condvar`.
- A permit is held for the duration of `send` and, for streamed downloads, until the body reader is dropped.
- The host comes from the request URL. Redirect hops run inside the same permit, because redirects are followed below this layer.

**Pool (`run_bounded`).** `pub fn run_bounded<T, R>(items: Vec<T>, max_workers: usize, f: impl Fn(T) -> R + Sync) -> Vec<R>` uses `std::thread::scope` with at most `max_workers` threads pulling from a shared queue, and returns results in input order (determinism, DEC-3). Sources call it with `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`. The per-host cap is still enforced by `Limited`, so a pool of 6 hitting github.com never has more than 3 requests in flight there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Retrying` retries GET/HEAD on 429, 5xx and transport errors, up to `MAX_RETRIES` times, with full-jitter exponential delays between 0 and min(`BACKOFF_MAX`, `BACKOFF_BASE`×2^n). It never retries POST.
- `Retry-After` ≤ 60 s is honored as the delay. A longer value returns `rate_limited` with `details.reset_at` and no retry.
- A 403 or 429 with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` returns `rate_limited` with `reset_at` from `X-RateLimit-Reset` and is not retried.
- Exhausted retries map to `rate_limited`, `http_status` (retryable) or `network` (retryable), as appropriate.
- `Validating` sends `If-None-Match`/`If-Modified-Since` for opted-in requests, turns a 304 into the cached 200 body with `CacheState::Revalidated`, stores validators under `<cache>/omaddons/http/` through fsx, and treats a corrupt cache entry as absent.
- `Limited` never has more than 6 requests in flight in total, or more than 3 to one host (asserted with a blocking fake transport and counters).
- `run_bounded` preserves input order and never runs more than `max_workers` closures at once.
- All delays use the injected `Sleeper`; no test sleeps in real time.
- Every value comes from `src/politeness.rs`.

## Test Plan

- Unit (fake transport plus a recording sleeper):
  - 500 → 500 → 200 succeeds on the third attempt with two recorded delays inside the jitter bounds;
  - four 503s → `http_status` retryable after exactly 4 attempts;
  - 429 with `Retry-After: 2` → one 2 s sleep, then success;
  - `Retry-After: 120` → immediate `rate_limited` with `reset_at` = now + 120 s (injected clock);
  - HTTP-date `Retry-After` parsing;
  - 403 with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` → `rate_limited`, no retry;
  - POST never retried;
  - a transport timeout is retried.
- Validators:
  - first fetch stores the ETag;
  - second fetch sends `If-None-Match`, fake returns 304, caller sees the cached body and `Revalidated`;
  - `Last-Modified`-only path;
  - corrupt `<sha>.json` → plain GET;
  - downloads never send validators.
- Limits: a transport that blocks until released, 20 parallel requests to 2 hosts; assert max global in flight = 6 and max per host = 3.
- Pool: order preserved; concurrency bound respected (atomic counter high-water mark).
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (attempt count, delays, statuses).

## Considerations

- Body-read retries for large downloads are deliberately left to the downloader, because the layer cannot replay a half-consumed stream into the caller's writer.
- The validator cache is not size-capped in M1. Atom feeds are small, and the WoWI file list (about 5.6 MB) arrives in M2, which may add a cap. Deleting `<cache>/omaddons/http/` is always safe.
- GitHub REST conditional requests return free 304s only when authenticated (vision §4.5). Unauthenticated, a 304 still costs a request against the 60/hour budget. source-github-rest accounts for that.
- `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` (15 min) applies to `outdated` and belongs to M2, not here.
- Out of scope: the fixture transports (net-fixtures) and the `GITHUB_REST_RESERVE` budget logic (source-github-rest).
acceptance_criteria: Retrying retries GET/HEAD on 429, 5xx and transport errors up to MAX_RETRIES with full-jitter exponential delays bounded by BACKOFF_BASE/BACKOFF_MAX and never retries POST; Retry-After <= 60 s is honored and longer values return rate_limited with details.reset_at without retrying; 403/429 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 returns rate_limited with reset_at from X-RateLimit-Reset and is not retried; exhausted retries map to rate_limited, http_status (retryable) or network (retryable); Validating sends If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since for opted-in requests, maps 304 to the cached 200 body with CacheState::Revalidated, stores validators under <cache>/omaddons/http/ through fsx, and treats corrupt entries as absent; Limited never exceeds 6 in-flight requests globally or 3 per host; run_bounded preserves input order and bounds concurrency; all delays go through the injected Sleeper; every value comes from src/politeness.rs
close_reason: The net stack now retries transient failures with full-jitter backoff and Retry-After, fails fast on rate limits with the reset time, revalidates opted-in feeds with ETag/Last-Modified from an fsx-written cache, caps requests at 6 in flight overall and 3 per host, and offers run_bounded for ordered parallel fetches; all values from politeness.rs

comments.author: BoldKettle

title: Ref parsing, the Source trait, ReleaseSet and the fetch-once orchestrator
description:
## Background

Users and agents name addons many ways: a canonical ref (`gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2`), a URL pasted from a browser, a git URL with a branch, a local zip, the name of an installed addon, or a catalog name such as `weakauras`. The vision (§5.4) requires all of these to work, and an ambiguous input to fail with the candidates rather than a guess. Every source also shares one contract. `fetch` does all the network work for a batch of refs. Selection and verification are pure and live elsewhere. A run fetches each distinct ref exactly once, however many targets want it (D28: "requests no longer multiply by target count").

This bead provides the user-facing ref parser, the `Source` trait, the source registry, and the fetch-once orchestrator. The model bead owns the canonical `Ref` type and its `source:id` round trip; this bead builds on it.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/sources/mod.rs` (trait, `SourceId`, registry, `fetch_once`), `src/sources/refs.rs` (user-input parsing).

**Canonical forms (owned by the model bead, restated here):** `gh:<owner>/<repo>`, `wowi:<id>`, `tukui:<slug>`, `cf:<id>`, `wago:<id>`, `git:<url>[#<rev>]`, `url:<https-url>`, `file:<path>`.

**Parsing, `parse_user_ref(input: &str, ctx: &RefContext) -> Result<ParsedRef>`.** `ParsedRef { r#ref: Ref, version_hint: Option<String>, asset_hint: Option<String>, matched_by: MatchKind }`, where `MatchKind` is one of `Canonical | Url | Path | Installed | Catalog | Shorthand`. Steps, in order:

1. **Canonical prefix** (`gh:`, `wowi:`, `tukui:`, `cf:`, `wago:`, `git:`, `url:`, `file:`): delegate to the model's `FromStr`, then validate:
   - `gh` owner/repo use GitHub's charset (`[A-Za-z0-9-]` for owner; `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` for repo, which is never `.` or `..`);
   - `wowi`/`cf` ids are numeric;
   - `tukui` slugs are `[a-z0-9-]+`;
   - `git:` URLs are https, with an optional `#rev` that may not be empty;
   - `url:` is https (no extension requirement; the engine verifies the content is a zip);
   - `file:` paths are made absolute against the current directory.

   Violations are `ref_invalid` (exit 2).
2. **https URL:**
   - `github.com/<o>/<r>` (with or without a trailing `/` or `.git`) → `gh:<o>/<r>`.
   - `…/releases/tag/<tag>` → `gh:<o>/<r>` with `version_hint = tag`.
   - `…/releases/download/<tag>/<file>` → `gh:<o>/<r>` with `version_hint = tag` and `asset_hint = file`.
   - `…/tree/<branch>` → `git:https://github.com/<o>/<r>#<branch>`.
   - `wowinterface.com/downloads/info<id>-<slug>.html` or `download<id>-…` → `wowi:<id>`.
   - `tukui.org` addon pages → `tukui:<slug>`.
   - `curseforge.com/wow/addons/<slug>` and `addons.wago.io/addons/<slug>` → fail at once with `source_disabled` (exit 1), saying CurseForge/Wago arrive in M5, with fix `omaddons help install`. Decided: these URLs carry a slug, not the id a `cf:`/`wago:` ref needs, so they cannot become a canonical ref. Failing at parse time gives the same observable result as DEC-12.
   - A URL whose host is a configured git host (`RefContext.git_hosts`), or whose path ends in `.git` → `git:<url>`.
   - Any other https URL → `url:<url>`.
   - `http://` URLs → `ref_invalid` with the https form as the fix.
3. **Local path** (starts with `/`, `./` or `../`, or names an existing file or directory): an existing `.zip` file or a directory → `file:<absolute path>`. A missing path that starts with `/`, `./` or `../` → `not_found` (exit 3).
4. **`<owner>/<repo>` shorthand** (exactly one `/`, both halves valid GitHub names):
   - → `gh:<owner>/<repo>`;
   - if a relative path of that name also exists on disk → `ref_ambiguous` (exit 3), with candidates `./<owner>/<repo>` and `gh:<owner>/<repo>`, each with an exact `omaddons install …` fix argv.
5. **Bare name:**
   - Look up installed addons via the injected `RefContext.installed(name) -> Vec<InstalledMatch { name, r#ref, target_id }>`. It is case-insensitive on record name and folder key and is fed from state records by the caller.
   - Look up the catalog via the injected `RefContext.catalog(name) -> Option<CatalogMatch { name, r#ref }>`. It is case-insensitive on name and aliases and is fed by the catalog bead.
   - If every match resolves to one ref, use it.
   - If matches resolve to different refs → `ref_ambiguous` (exit 3). `details.candidates` lists each canonical ref and where it came from, and `alternatives` carries one `omaddons install <canonical ref>` argv per candidate.
   - No match → `not_found` (exit 3), with fix `omaddons help install`.

Injected lookups keep this bead free of dependencies on state-records and catalog. The command layer wires them.

**Source trait (vision §5.4):**

```rust
pub trait Source: Send + Sync {
    fn id(&self) -> SourceId;
    /// Network; batched; called once per run with every distinct ref of this source.
    fn fetch(&self, refs: &[Ref], http: &dyn Http) -> Vec<Result<ReleaseSet>>;
}
```

`SourceId` is one of `Github | Git | Url | Local | Wowi | Tukui | Curseforge | Wago`, with wire names `github, git, url, local, wowi, tukui, curseforge, wago`. Results are positional: result *i* belongs to `refs[i]`. Decided: `search` is left out of the M1 trait. M2's search bead adds it with a default implementation, so M1 sources carry no stub.

**Registry and fetch-once.**
- `SourceRegistry` maps `SourceId → Box<dyn Source>`. The M1 registry holds `local`, `url` and `github`; `git` is added when source-git-github lands. Refs whose source is not registered (`wowi`, `tukui`, `cf`, `wago`) yield `source_disabled` per ref (DEC-12). The message names the milestone (WoWI/Tukui: M2; CurseForge/Wago: M5), and the fix is `omaddons help install`.
- `fetch_once(refs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Ref>, registry: &SourceRegistry, http: &dyn Http) -> BTreeMap<Ref, Result<ReleaseSet>>`:
  1. deduplicate by canonical ref (`Ref: Ord`);
  2. group by `SourceId`;
  3. call each source's `fetch` exactly once with its group;
  4. run the groups concurrently with `net::pool::run_bounded` (net-resilience) capped at `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`.

  Sources that fetch many refs parallelize inside `fetch` with the same helper. The per-host limit is enforced in the `Http` stack.
- Errors are per ref, so one bad ref never fails the others. Partial success becomes `partial: true` in the command layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `parse_user_ref` handles every input class above, with the documented results and error codes: `ref_invalid` (2), `ref_ambiguous` (3), `not_found` (3), `source_disabled` (1).
- GitHub repo, release-tag, release-download and tree URLs map to the documented refs and hints. WoWI `info<id>-…` URLs map to `wowi:<id>`.
- CurseForge/Wago project URLs fail with `source_disabled`, naming M5.
- Every ambiguity error carries `details.candidates` and one executable `alternatives[].argv` per candidate.
- `Source` and `SourceId` exist as specified, with no `search` method.
- `fetch_once` calls each registered source's `fetch` exactly once per run with deduplicated refs, returns one result per distinct ref, and yields `source_disabled` for unregistered sources without touching the network.
- Per-ref failures do not affect other refs.
- No network or filesystem writes in the parser. Its only filesystem access is reading whether a path exists and what kind it is.

## Test Plan

- Unit, table-driven over about 60 inputs with expected `ParsedRef` or error code:
  - canonical forms of every source;
  - GitHub URLs with and without `www`, trailing slash, `.git`, `/releases/tag/v1.2`, `/releases/download/v1.2/Foo.zip`, `/tree/main`;
  - WoWI URLs;
  - CurseForge/Wago URLs;
  - `http://` URLs;
  - configured git host URLs;
  - arbitrary https zip URLs;
  - existing and missing local paths (tempdir);
  - `owner/repo` with and without a colliding local directory;
  - bare names hitting installed only, catalog only, both agreeing, both disagreeing, neither.
- Proptest: `parse_user_ref` never panics on arbitrary strings, and every canonical ref it returns round-trips through `Display`/`FromStr`.
- fetch-once:
  - a counting fake source receiving the same ref from three "targets" is called once with one ref;
  - two sources run concurrently (fake sources with barriers);
  - an unregistered `wowi:` ref yields `source_disabled` and the fake `Http` records zero requests;
  - one failing ref leaves the others `Ok`.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (input string, parsed result).

## Considerations

- The parser reads the filesystem to decide whether a path exists. That is the only side effect, and it never follows symlinks out of an explicit path the user gave.
- Version and asset hints from URLs are hints. The install command turns `version_hint` into the equivalent of `--version` and fails if it conflicts with an explicit `--version`.
- Branch names that look like versions (`#v2`) are handled by the git sources, not here. The parser only splits on the first `#`.
- Catalog and installed-name lookups are injected, so this bead can land before catalog and state-records. The fuzz bead (fuzz-targets) adds a fuzz target for `parse_user_ref`.
- Out of scope: the GitHub, git, url and local sources themselves; candidate selection (select); WoWI/Tukui fetching (M2).
- Dependency added beyond the plan: `net-resilience`, because `fetch_once` runs source groups through `net::pool::run_bounded`.
acceptance_criteria: parse_user_ref handles canonical refs, https URLs, local paths, owner/repo shorthand and bare names with the documented results and codes ref_invalid (2), ref_ambiguous (3), not_found (3), source_disabled (1); GitHub repo, release-tag, release-download and tree URLs map to the documented refs and hints and WoWI info<id> URLs map to wowi:<id>; CurseForge/Wago project URLs fail with source_disabled naming M5; ambiguity errors carry details.candidates and one executable alternatives[].argv per candidate; Source and SourceId exist without a search method; fetch_once calls each registered source's fetch exactly once per run with deduplicated refs, returns one result per distinct ref, and yields source_disabled for unregistered sources without network; per-ref failures do not affect other refs; the parser performs no network access or writes
close_reason: User refs parse from canonical forms, GitHub/WoWI/Tukui/git/https URLs, local paths, owner/repo shorthand and installed or catalog names, with ambiguity reported as exact candidate commands; the Source trait, SourceId, registry and fetch_once give every source one batched fetch per run with per-ref errors and source_disabled for later milestones

Canonical refs already reject non-https git:/url:, git revs starting with '-' (argv injection) and unsafe tukui/wago ids. Pasted-URL and name resolution stay with this bead.

Set `req.validators = true` on feed and list GETs to get 304 revalidation (`resp.cache == CacheState::Revalidated`). `net::run_bounded(items, MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS, |item| …)` fetches many refs in input order. Retry errors: rate_limited (details.reset_at), http_status (retryable for 5xx), network. A body-read failure on a download is the downloader's to retry once.

comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/sources/{mod,refs}.rs).**
(1) **A bare name that is also an existing local file or dir is matched against installed and catalog too**, and disagreement is ref_ambiguous. The bead's step 3 would take any existing path first, but `omaddons install WeakAuras` run inside an AddOns folder must not silently install the local copy. A lone local match is still a Path.
(2) Agreement uses Ref identity, so the installed gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2 and the catalog's gh:weakauras/weakauras2 are one candidate; the first found (installed) keeps its spelling and MatchKind.
(3) Paths: an explicit /, ./ or ../ path that is missing is not_found. An existing path must be a .zip file or a directory, else ref_invalid. An input with two or more slashes that is not owner/repo shorthand is a path (missing means not_found). file: canonical refs become absolute against RefContext.cwd. The parser only stats; it never reads or writes.
(4) URLs: hosts lose 'www.', userinfo and port. github.com/<o>/<r> with any extra path (issues, etc.) maps to gh:o/r, except releases/tag, releases/download (version and asset hints) and tree/<branch…> (git:…#branch, slashes kept). github.com/<owner> alone is url:. WoWI accepts info<id>… and download<id>… pages. **Tukui (unverified upstream)** accepts ?ui=<slug>, /addon/<slug>, /addons/<slug> and /<slug>, lowercased. CurseForge and Wago links are source_disabled naming M5. Configured git hosts or a .git path give git: (a #fragment becomes the rev); any other https URL gives url:. http:// is ref_invalid, with the https form as an `omaddons install <https>` fix.
(5) Ambiguity errors carry details {input, candidates: [{ref, from}]}; the fix is `omaddons install <first>` and there is one alternative per other candidate.
(6) Source registry: `SourceRegistry::new()` starts empty, and each source bead registers itself (github: 5.10, local/url: 5.11, git: 5.7). `sources::disabled(&ref)` names the milestone (WoWI and Tukui M2; CurseForge and Wago M5) with fix `omaddons help install`.
(7) fetch_once dedupes by Ref identity within each source group (GitHub case-insensitively), runs groups through net::run_bounded, and fills a missing positional result with an internal error. Results are a BTreeMap<Ref, Result<ReleaseSet>>.

title: Pure candidate selection per target
description:
## Background

One fetch of a ref produces a `ReleaseSet`. Each target then needs its own ordered list of candidate assets to try. The vision (§5.4, D28) makes this a pure function, `fn select(set: &ReleaseSet, t: &Target, ch: Channel) -> Vec<Candidate>`, with no I/O, so it can be table-tested for every family. Fetching stays once per ref while selection runs once per target.

Selection only orders. The engine downloads each candidate in order, inspects it, and verifies its TOCs against the target's `ClientRules`. The first compatible candidate wins, and a failing one falls back to the next. Metadata is a hint, never a verdict (D5): WeakAuras' current `release.json` has no `mainline` entry, yet its zip contains a Mainline TOC and works on retail. Legacy clients have no metadata at all.

Facts used here:
- BigWigs packager flavor names: `mainline, classic, bcc, wrath, cata, mists, titan, forever`. The packager maps tbc→bcc, vanilla→classic, wotlkc→wrath, camelot→forever.
- Family to `release.json` flavor comes from the rules-tables bead (`Family::release_flavor() -> Option<&str>`):

  | Family | Flavor |
  |---|---|
  | mainline | mainline |
  | vanilla (Classic Era) | classic |
  | tbc (incl. Anniversary and the 2.5.x era PTR) | bcc |
  | wrath | wrath |
  | titan | titan |
  | cata | cata |
  | mists | mists |
  | forever (incl. the `_classic_beta_` 1.60.x client) | forever |
  | every `-legacy` family and `unknown` | none |

- Channels: `stable` (default) | `beta` | `alpha`. A GitHub prerelease is beta.

## Technical Approach

File: `src/resolve/select.rs`. Public API:

```rust
pub fn select(set: &ReleaseSet, target: &Target, channel: Channel, pin: Option<&str>) -> Selection;
pub struct Selection { pub candidates: Vec<Candidate>, pub empty_reason: Option<EmptyReason> }
pub enum EmptyReason { NoEligibleRelease, PinnedVersionNotFound, NoAssets }
```

`Candidate` (model bead) carries `release_id`, `version`, `channel`, the `Asset`, and a `rank: RankReason` enum used by `--verbose` output and tests. The vision's three-argument signature gains `pin`. Decided: a pinned version is part of selection, so the "which release" logic lives in one pure place.

**Step 1: choose the release.**
- With `pin`: the release whose `version` or tag equals `pin`, also matching after stripping a leading `v` from either side. If none matches, return no candidates with `PinnedVersionNotFound`.
- Without `pin`: filter by channel (`stable` = stable releases only; `beta` = stable + beta; `alpha` = all), then take the newest by `published_at`, falling back to set order (sources emit newest first). None left → `NoEligibleRelease`.
- Decided: candidates come only from that one release. Older releases are never tried automatically, because silently installing an old version would mask a broken release. The user can pin with `--version`.

**Step 2: rank that release's assets, best first.** Tiers, stable sort within each tier by original asset order:
1. **Metadata match.** The asset's `release.json` metadata has `flavor == target family's release flavor`. Within the tier, exact `interface == target.interface` first, then same major/minor family digits, then the rest.
2. **Name-hint match.** No metadata, but `name_flavors` (from source-github-rest) contains the target family, or `ClassicAny` for any classic family.
3. **Unannotated.** No metadata and no name hints. Every asset for `file:`, `url:` and `git:` refs falls here.
4. **Name-hint mismatch.** Hints present, none matching.
5. **Metadata mismatch.** Metadata present, none matching. Decided: kept as last-resort candidates rather than dropped, because metadata is wrong in practice (WeakAuras has no `mainline` entry). TOC verification decides.

Within every tier, `nolib: false` comes before `nolib: true`. Non-zip assets never reach select; sources filter them.

**Legacy and unknown targets.** `release_flavor()` is `None`, so nothing can be a metadata match. A modern `classic` metadata entry is a mismatch (tier 5) for a `vanilla-legacy` target. It stays a candidate only so verification can reject it with a precise reason, and it is ranked after everything unannotated. A modern Classic Era build (Interface 11509) never verifies against a 1.12.1 client (Interface 11200); that guarantee belongs to toc-loaded and is tested in toc-matrix.

**Purity.** No filesystem, network, clock or environment access. Deterministic output for identical inputs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `select` is pure and deterministic, with no I/O. A test asserts that it compiles without any `std::fs`/`net` imports in the module.
- Release choice follows the channel rules: stable excludes beta/alpha, beta includes stable, alpha includes all. Candidates come only from the newest eligible release.
- A pin selects the matching release (with `v` prefix tolerance) or returns `PinnedVersionNotFound`.
- Assets rank in the five documented tiers, with `nolib: false` first inside each tier.
- Metadata mismatches are kept last, not dropped.
- Table tests cover every family:
  - mainline, vanilla, tbc, wrath, titan, cata, mists and forever, including a `_classic_beta_` 1.60.x target as forever;
  - each legacy family: vanilla-legacy, tbc-legacy, wrath-legacy, cata-legacy, mists-legacy;
  - unknown.
- A WeakAuras-shaped release set (metadata without `mainline`) still yields its zip as a candidate for a mainline target.

## Test Plan

- Unit, table-driven (`tests` module in `src/resolve/select.rs`, built from synthetic `ReleaseSet`s):
  - multi-flavor BigWigs-style set (one zip per flavor plus nolib variants) × every family → expected first candidate;
  - single multi-flavor zip with metadata listing several flavors;
  - WeakAuras-shaped set for mainline;
  - interface tie-break (two `mainline` entries, 120100 vs 120105, target 120105);
  - name-hint-only REST set (`Foo-classic.zip`, `Foo-mainline.zip`, `Foo-3.3.5.zip`) for wrath-legacy, mainline and vanilla;
  - `git:`/`url:`/`file:` single unannotated asset for every family;
  - channel matrix over a set with stable 1.0, beta 1.1-beta and alpha 1.2-alpha;
  - pin hits `1.0`, `v1.0` and misses;
  - empty asset list → `NoAssets`.
- Proptest: output is a permutation of the chosen release's assets, so no asset is invented or lost.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (family, channel, candidate order with rank reasons).

## Considerations

- Fallback across candidates, downloading and verifying are the planner's job (E6 plan). This bead never decides compatibility.
- `published_at` is missing for no-REST GitHub releases, which yield a single release anyway, so set order is the fallback.
- If the packager adds a flavor name (as it did with `forever`), only the rules table needs a new mapping (D15). Unknown flavors in metadata simply never match.
- Out of scope: dependency candidates (M2) and CurseForge `gameVersionTypeId`/`releaseType` mapping (M5).
acceptance_criteria: select is pure and deterministic with no I/O; release choice follows the channel rules (stable excludes beta/alpha, beta includes stable, alpha includes all) and candidates come only from the newest eligible release; a pin selects the matching release with v-prefix tolerance or returns PinnedVersionNotFound; assets rank in the five documented tiers with nolib false first inside each tier and metadata mismatches kept last, not dropped; table tests cover mainline, vanilla, tbc, wrath, titan, cata, mists, forever (including a _classic_beta_ 1.60.x target), every legacy family and unknown; a WeakAuras-shaped release set without mainline metadata still yields its zip as a mainline candidate
close_reason: Candidate selection is a pure, deterministic per-target ordering of one release's assets (pinned or newest on the channel) in five documented tiers, never dropping metadata mismatches, table-tested for every modern, legacy and unknown family

Both live on Family rather than RulesTable because select() receives no table.

Register in `SourceRegistry::builtin()`. Test helpers: tests/common/http.rs (`fixture`, `replay`, `record`, `scenario`).

comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/resolve/select.rs).**
(1) API as specified: `select(&ReleaseSet, &Target, Channel, pin: Option<&str>) -> Selection { candidates, empty_reason: Option<EmptyReason::{NoEligibleRelease, PinnedVersionNotFound, NoAssets}> }`. EmptyReason serializes snake_case.
(2) Pin: matches the release version or the tag after the last '@' of release_id, with a leading v/V stripped on both sides. **A pin ignores the channel** (it is explicit). Without a pin, the newest eligible release is chosen by published_at when every eligible release has one (ties go to set order), else the first in set order.
(3) **Metadata flavors compare through `Family::from_release_flavor`**, so packager aliases (tbc, vanilla, wotlkc, camelot) match; unknown flavors match nothing. Tier 1 closeness: an exact target.interface gives MetadataInterface; otherwise MetadataFlavor ordered same interface/100, then other (and None interfaces). For a legacy or unknown target, any metadata is a tier-5 mismatch.
(4) **Name hints:** FlavorHint maps to the release-flavor names (Classic→classic, Bcc→bcc, …). ClassicAny fits every modern non-mainline family. Hints never match legacy or unknown targets. FlavorHint has no legacy variants (e.g. 3.3.5): a legacy-named zip without hints is Unannotated (tier 3), which ranks it ahead of mismatched hints for a 3.3.5 target.
(5) Sort key: (tier, nolib, closeness, original index). nolib false comes first within a tier, before interface closeness, as the bead orders it.
(6) Purity: a test scans the non-test part of the file for std::fs, std::net, crate::net, std::env, SystemTime and Timestamp::now.
(7) Tests: every modern family takes its BigWigs flavor first with the nolib twin second and the 14 others kept as MetadataMismatch; every legacy family and unknown has no metadata match; WeakAuras-shaped mainline; interface tie-break; name hints for retail, era and 3.3.5; unannotated git asset for every family; channel matrix and pins (v-prefix, tag vs version); published_at; a proptest that candidates are a permutation of the release's assets.

title: git refs for GitHub-hosted repos via commits atom and codeload
description:
## Background

Many legacy private-server addons have no releases at all: the repository is the addon, and users track a branch. The vision (§5.4) adds `git:` refs, `git:<url>[#<tag|branch|sha>]`. For GitHub-hosted repositories it avoids both the `git` binary and REST:
- branch heads come from `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/commits/<branch>.atom`, an in-process request that is allowlisted and logged;
- archives come from `codeload.github.com`.

The M1 checkpoint requires "a legacy addon installs into the 3.3.5a target from a git repo".

## Technical Approach

File: `src/sources/git_github.rs`, registering `SourceId::Git` in the M1 `SourceRegistry` and handling refs whose URL host is `github.com`. source-git-hosts later adds non-GitHub hosts to the same `SourceId::Git` implementation through a dispatch on host. This bead creates `src/sources/git.rs` as that dispatcher and routes `github.com` here.

**Accepted refs.** `git:https://github.com/<o>/<r>[.git][#<rev>]`. Owner and repo are validated (the refs bead already checked the charset), and a trailing `.git` is stripped.

**Rev resolution (in-process, purpose `commits-atom`).**
1. `rev` is 40 hex characters → treat it as a commit sha. No request is needed to resolve it.
2. `rev` is present otherwise → try it as a branch first: `GET https://github.com/<o>/<r>/commits/<rev>.atom`.
   - 200 with at least one entry → head sha = the newest entry's commit sha, taken from the entry `id` (`tag:github.com,2008:Grit::Commit/<sha>`) or the link `…/commit/<sha>`.
   - 404 → treat `rev` as a tag. No resolution request is made; the archive is fetched by tag name.
   - Decided: branch first, then tag, because tracking a branch is the main reason to use a git ref over a release. Document that a branch and a tag sharing a name resolve to the branch.
3. No `rev` → the default branch. Decided, per the plan: the implementer verifies with one live probe, recorded as a fixture, whether `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/commits.atom` with no branch tracks the default branch. If it does, use it. Otherwise try `commits/main.atom`, then `commits/master.atom`. Record which behavior was confirmed in this bead's close comment and in the code comment.

The Atom decoder is the shared `src/sources/atom.rs` from source-github-stable.

**Release set.** One `Release`:
- **Branch or default**: `release_id = "git:<url>@<sha>"`, `version` = the first 7 characters of the sha, `version_confidence: release`, `channel: Stable`.
- **Tag**: `release_id = "git:<url>@<tag>"`, `version` = tag.
- **Sha**: `release_id = "git:<url>@<sha>"`, `version` = short sha.
- One `Asset { name: "<repo>-<rev>.zip", location: Url("https://codeload.github.com/<o>/<r>/zip/<resolved>"), flavors: [], nolib: false }`, where `<resolved>` is the resolved sha for branches and default, the tag name for tags (`zip/refs/tags/<tag>`), or the sha itself.

Pinning the archive URL to the resolved sha guarantees the plan installs exactly what was resolved, even if the branch moves before download.

**Archive layout.** codeload zips wrap everything in `<repo>-<rev>/`. The repository may be the addon itself (`<repo>-<sha>/<Addon>.toc`) or contain addon folders (`<repo>-<sha>/<Addon>/<Addon>.toc`). archive-inspect normalizes both by TOC name, and this bead does nothing special. If the repository root is the addon, its folder name comes from the TOC name, not the `-<sha>` suffix.

**Updates.** Re-running install resolves the branch again. A new head sha gives a new `release_id`, so the planner records `kind: update`. The same sha means "already current".

**Channels and versions.** Git refs have no channels, so `--channel` is ignored for them. An explicit `--version` on a git ref is treated as a rev, identical to `#<rev>`. A conflicting `#rev` plus `--version` is `usage` (exit 2).

**Zero REST.** Nothing here touches `api.github.com`. The tests assert it through `assert_no_github_rest`.

**Fixtures.** Record into `tests/fixtures/http/git-github/`:
- the commits atom and a small codeload zip for one real legacy 3.3.5a addon repository with no releases (implementer picks and confirms it; do not guess);
- the default-branch probe result;
- a tag-resolution scenario (branch atom 404).

Add a decoder-level live probe for commits atom to `tests/live_probes.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `git:https://github.com/<o>/<r>[#rev]` refs fetch through `commits/<branch>.atom` and codeload only, with no REST and no git subprocess.
- Branch revs resolve to the newest commit sha, and the archive URL is pinned to it. Tags resolve after a branch-atom 404. 40-hex revs are used without a resolution request.
- The default-branch behavior is verified live once, recorded as a fixture, and implemented as confirmed.
- The release set has the documented `release_id`, `version` (short sha or tag) and a single codeload asset.
- Re-fetching after the branch moves yields a new `release_id`; an unchanged branch yields the same one.
- `--version` on a git ref acts as a rev, and conflicting with `#rev` is `usage`.
- Replay tests for the recorded legacy repository pass with `assert_no_github_rest`.
- `src/sources/git.rs` dispatches `github.com` URLs here and rejects other hosts with `source_disabled` until source-git-hosts lands.

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - commit sha extraction from atom entry `id` and `link` forms;
  - rev classification (40-hex vs other);
  - codeload URL construction for branch, tag (`refs/tags/…`) and sha, including a tag containing `/`;
  - `release_id` and version formatting.
- Integration (replay):
  - default branch;
  - explicit branch;
  - tag fallback after 404;
  - explicit sha;
  - branch moved (two scenarios with different heads → different release ids);
  - `net.log` shows only `github.com` and `codeload.github.com` lines.
- E2E (in m1-checkpoint / engine-tests): installing the recorded legacy repository into a synthetic 3.3.5a target verifies by TOC (`## Interface: 30300`).
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (ref, atom URL, resolved sha, asset URL).

## Considerations

- GitHub could stop serving commits atom for some repositories (very large ones, or archived ones). The live probe at the checkpoint watches for it, and the fallback is a `gh:` ref or a `url:` codeload link.
- Short shas as versions can collide in display only; identity uses the full sha in `release_id`.
- Private repositories return 404 on atom, so they are treated as "branch not found" and then fail at archive download with `http_status` 404. The error message says private repositories are not supported in M1.
- Out of scope: non-GitHub hosts and the `git` binary (source-git-hosts).
acceptance_criteria: git:https://github.com/<o>/<r>[#rev] refs fetch through commits/<branch>.atom and codeload only, with no REST and no git subprocess; branch revs resolve to the newest commit sha and the archive URL is pinned to it, tags resolve after a branch-atom 404, and 40-hex revs need no resolution request; default-branch behavior is verified live once, recorded as a fixture, and implemented as confirmed; the release set has the documented release_id, version (short sha or tag) and a single codeload asset; a moved branch yields a new release_id and an unchanged branch the same one; --version on a git ref acts as a rev and conflicting with #rev is usage; replay tests for a recorded legacy repository pass with assert_no_github_rest; src/sources/git.rs dispatches github.com URLs here and rejects other hosts with source_disabled until source-git-hosts lands
close_reason: git: refs for GitHub repositories through the commits feed and codeload, zero REST; the legacy catalog entries resolve and GroupBulletinBoard installs into a 3.3.5a client

(2) GitHub serves commits/<tag>.atom too: GroupBulletinBoard's commits/v1.2.3.atom answers 200 headed by the tag's own commit (95653f8, not main's fbf8ed2). So the plan's 'tags resolve after a branch-atom 404' does not match GitHub. **Decided:** every non-sha rev goes through commits/<rev>.atom and resolves to a commit (Resolved::Head), release_id git:<url>@<sha>, version the short sha, archive pinned to codeload zip/<sha>, for branches and tags alike; a branch and a tag sharing a name resolve as GitHub picks. (3) A missing branch answers 404. **Also needed:** archive inspection did not recognize codeload's <repo>-<40-hex sha>/ wrapper (only -main/-master/-<version>), so GroupBulletinBoard was bad_archive; wrapped_names now accepts a full commit sha suffix (not a short one: Foo-cafe stays a name). title: git refs for non-GitHub hosts through the git binary
description:
## Background

Some legacy addons live on git hosts other than GitHub: Codeberg, a self-hosted Gitea or GitLab. The vision (§5.4) handles them with the `git` binary: "Other hosts use `git ls-remote` with https only, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `-c http.followRedirects=false`, logged as a `via: git` entry in `net.log`", and archives come from `git clone --depth 1 --branch` of the working tree.

Two privacy rules from §5.7 apply:
- Git subprocesses are restricted to allowlisted https hosts with redirects disabled.
- Every git subprocess is logged.

A git subprocess is the one place where bytes reach the disk without passing through fsx, so this bead also defines exactly where git may write.

Placeholders: `<cache>` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `.cache` under the home directory), `<config>` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (default `.config`).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/sources/git_hosts.rs`, plus dispatch in `src/sources/git.rs` (created by source-git-github) for non-GitHub hosts.

**Configured hosts.** Add the config key `git_hosts`, a list of hostnames (e.g. `git_hosts = ["codeberg.org"]`), to the config schema (config bead): typed, validated as bare hostnames without scheme or path, and settable with `config set`. The command layer passes the list into `NetConfig.git_hosts` (net-core), which adds the hosts to the allowlist. A `git:` URL whose host is neither `github.com` nor in `git_hosts` fails with `host_blocked` (exit 4). The fix is `omaddons config set git_hosts <host>` as display, with `argv: null` because the value must be merged into the existing list by the user. Only `https://` URLs are accepted; anything else is `ref_invalid` (2).

**Subprocess hygiene.** Every invocation goes through one helper, `run_git(args, purpose, timeout) -> Result<Output>`:
- `std::process::Command::new("git")` with argv only, never a shell.
- `env_clear()`, then set only:
  - `PATH` and `HOME`;
  - `LC_ALL=C`, so output parsing is stable;
  - `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`;
  - `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, so the user's `url.<x>.insteadOf`, proxy or credential settings cannot redirect a fetch to a non-allowlisted host;
  - `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https`.
- Always pass `-c http.followRedirects=false -c credential.helper= -c core.askPass= -c protocol.allow=never -c protocol.https.allow=always`.
- Credentials are never placed in argv. Repositories that need authentication fail fast because prompts are disabled, giving `download_failed` (exit 1, not retryable) with a message saying private repositories are not supported.
- Timeouts: `API_READ_TIMEOUT` (30 s) for `ls-remote`, `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` (300 s) for clone/fetch. On expiry the child is killed and the result is `network` (retryable).
- Before running, the URL host is checked with `Allowlist::permits`.
- After running, one net.log line via `NetLog::record_git`: `via: "git"`, `method: "GIT"`, host, path (no query), `status` = exit code, `bytes: null`, `duration_ms`, `purpose` ∈ `ls-remote|clone|fetch`.
- `--offline` makes `run_git` fail with `offline` before spawning anything.
- A missing `git` binary (spawn `NotFound`) gives `source_disabled` (exit 1) with fix display `install git (pacman -S git)` and `argv: null`.

**fetch (resolution only).** `git ls-remote --symref <url> [<rev>]`:
- No rev → read `ref: refs/heads/<b>\tHEAD` for the default branch and the HEAD sha.
- Branch → the sha of `refs/heads/<rev>`.
- Tag → the sha of `refs/tags/<rev>^{}` when peeled, else `refs/tags/<rev>`.
- 40-hex rev → used as-is.
- Nothing matches → `not_found` (3).

Branch is checked before tag, matching source-git-github. The release set has one release, `release_id = "git:<url>@<sha>"` and `version` = short sha (or the tag for tags), with one `Asset { location: GitCheckout { url, rev, sha } }`. `fetch` writes nothing.

**Materialize (download step).** `pub fn materialize(asset: &GitCheckout, dest: &Path) -> Result<()>` is called by the engine's planner/download step (E6 plan), which knows the transaction id. Decided, per the plan: git writes only into a fresh directory `<cache>/omaddons/tmp/<tx>/git/` that the caller creates through fsx. That directory is the one sanctioned subprocess write, and it is pruned with `prune(PostCommitCleanup)` after commit or by orphan cleanup when the transaction's in-flight lock is free. Steps:
- branch or tag: `git clone --depth 1 --branch <rev> --single-branch --no-tags <url> <dest>`;
- sha: `git init <dest>`, then `git -C <dest> fetch --depth 1 <url> <sha>`, then `git -C <dest> checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD`. Servers that refuse fetching by sha produce `download_failed` with a message suggesting a branch or tag;
- after checkout, verify `git -C <dest> rev-parse HEAD` equals the resolved sha, else `plan_stale` (1, retryable), meaning the branch moved between resolution and clone.

The engine reads `<dest>` through `FolderView` as a directory input, with `.git/` excluded, so the tree is never re-zipped.

**Asset shape.** Add the `GitCheckout { url, rev, sha }` variant to `AssetLocation` (introduced by source-local-url) if it is missing. The E6 plan bead must route this variant to `materialize`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `git_hosts` config key exists, is validated, and feeds the allowlist. `git:` URLs to unlisted non-GitHub hosts fail with `host_blocked`, and non-https URLs with `ref_invalid`.
- Every git invocation runs through `run_git` with the cleared environment, the listed `-c` options and env vars, no shell and no credentials in argv, and writes exactly one `via: "git"` net.log line.
- `ls-remote` resolution handles the default branch, branch, peeled tag and sha, branch before tag. Unknown revs give `not_found`.
- `materialize` clones branch/tag shallowly, or fetches a sha, into a caller-provided fsx-created directory under `<cache>/omaddons/tmp/<tx>/`, and verifies HEAD matches the resolved sha (`plan_stale` otherwise).
- Missing git gives `source_disabled` with the package fix. Offline gives `offline` without spawning. Timeouts kill the child and return `network`.
- `src/sources/git.rs` routes non-GitHub hosts here.
- No git subprocess can follow redirects or read the user's global or system git config (asserted by inspecting the constructed `Command`).

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - `ls-remote --symref` output parsing over recorded samples: default branch, branches, peeled and unpeeled tags, empty output;
  - host validation for `git_hosts` values;
  - the `Command` builder has the exact env and `-c` set, with no `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GIT_*` leakage from the parent (set junk vars in the test and assert they are absent).
- Integration (local, no network). Production refuses every protocol except https, so decided: test against a local bare repository through a test-only seam. `run_git` takes a `ProtocolPolicy`; `ProtocolPolicy::FileForTests` exists only under `cfg(test)`, so these are in-crate tests in `src/sources/git_hosts.rs`. They cover resolution, clone into a tempdir, sha fetch, branch moved → `plan_stale`, and timeout via a fake `git` script on `PATH` that sleeps. The production path never allows `file://`.
- Live (`#[ignore]`, `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`): `ls-remote` and a shallow clone of one real public repository on a non-GitHub host (implementer picks one), logged in net.log with `via: "git"`.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (argv, env keys, stdout/stderr of git, resolved sha).

## Considerations

- `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` needs git 2.32 or later (2021). The minimum supported git version is checked at first use (`git --version`); older versions give `source_disabled` with an upgrade fix.
- git's own HTTPS stack does not go through omaddons' `Http` trait, so retries and per-host limits do not apply to it. Each subprocess is still bounded by its timeout and logged.
- `git clone --depth 1` downloads the whole tree at that commit. Large repositories are bounded only by `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT`; the inspection limits still apply to what is installed.
- Out of scope: GitHub-hosted git refs (source-git-github), SSH URLs (not supported, since https is mandatory), and submodules (not fetched).
- Dependency added beyond the plan: `config`, because this bead adds the `git_hosts` key to the config schema.
acceptance_criteria: A git_hosts config key exists, is validated and feeds the allowlist; git: URLs to unlisted non-GitHub hosts fail with host_blocked and non-https URLs with ref_invalid; every git invocation runs through run_git with the cleared environment, the listed -c options and env vars, no shell and no credentials in argv, and writes exactly one via: git net.log line; ls-remote resolution handles default branch, branch, peeled tag and sha with branch before tag and unknown revs give not_found; materialize clones branch/tag shallowly or fetches a sha into a caller-provided fsx-created directory under <cache>/omaddons/tmp/<tx>/ and verifies HEAD equals the resolved sha (plan_stale otherwise); missing git gives source_disabled with the package fix, offline gives offline without spawning, and timeouts kill the child and return network; src/sources/git.rs routes non-GitHub hosts here; no git subprocess can follow redirects or read the user's global or system git config
close_reason: git refs to configured non-GitHub hosts through a hygienic git runner, with checkouts materialized by the engine

comments.text: **net-core landed.** Check git hosts with `NetConfig::allowlist().permits(host)`; the user's configured hosts come from `NetConfig.git_hosts`. Log each subprocess with `NetLog::record_git(GitLogEntry { host, path, exit_code, duration_ms, purpose: "ls-remote"|"clone"|"fetch", error })`. Never put credentials in the path.

comments.text: **Source trait note (from 5.10):** `Source::fetch(&self, wanted: &[sources::Wanted], http)`. `Wanted { ref, channel, version }` is what fetch_once dedupes on, and results are keyed by Wanted. Register in `SourceRegistry::builtin()`. Test helpers: tests/common/http.rs (`fixture`, `replay`, `record`, `scenario`).

GitRunner::command: argv only, env_clear then PATH, HOME, LC_ALL=C, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https; -c http.followRedirects=false, credential.helper=, core.askPass=, protocol.allow=never, protocol.https.allow=always; stdin null; its own process group, so a timeout kills git-remote-https too (rustix gained its 'process' feature for kill_process_group; no new crate, cargo deny clean).
