title: Implement the targets command: list, add, rm, rename, default and --rescan
description:
## Background

A target is one WoW client directory (the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`) plus its identity: an immutable ULID `key`, a human `id` alias, family, kind, version, interface and `ClientRules` (vision §5.1). Discovery finds targets with no setup (§5.2); the registry (`<state>/omaddons/registry.json`) remembers registered ones, and a marker at `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json` lets a moved install be re-linked. `omaddons targets` is the user-facing surface over all of that: list what exists, add a client discovery cannot find, remove, rename, choose a default, and force a rescan.

The registry bead (E3) owns keys, aliases, markers, registration under the lock and `-t` resolution; the discover-cache bead owns the cache that `--rescan` bypasses. This bead is the command layer.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory); `<config>` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (default `.config`); `<client dir>` as above; `<root>` = a WoW install root.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/targets.rs`, a `Targets` subcommand with `add`, `rm`, `rename`, `default` sub-subcommands in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

Synopsis (vision §5.9): `omaddons targets [add <path> [--name N] | rm <id> | rename <id> <new> | default <id>] [--rescan]`.

Decided: the envelope `command` for sub-subcommands is the space-joined path (`"targets add"`, `"targets rm"`, `"targets rename"`, `"targets default"`); bare listing is `"targets"` (why: one string per distinct `data` schema keeps envelopes self-describing; coordinate with the output-envelope bead so every command family follows it).

### targets (list)

- Runs discovery (using the discovery cache when valid; `--rescan` bypasses and refreshes it) and merges registered targets. Read-only apart from the derived discovery cache.
- Each target reports: `id`, `key` (null when unregistered), `registered`, `default`, `family`, `kind` (`live` | `test`), `install_kind` (`battlenet` | `custom`), `product` (null for custom), `version`, `interface`, `label`, `client_dir`, `missing` (registered but the directory is gone), `found_by` (`product_db` | `scan` | `launcher:<lutris|heroic|steam|bottles>` | `extra_root` | `manual`).
- Decided: `client_dir` is always included, unlike other commands where paths are verbose-only (why: a target is its client dir; a target list without it is useless). `-v` adds `install_root`, `flavor_dir`, `exe_name`, the `ClientRules` row name, and the alias list.
- Discovery warnings (unknown flavor folders, version/interface disagreement, `client_not_launched_since_patch`, `DISCOVERY_MAX_DIRS` reached) pass through as warnings.

### targets add <path> [--name N]

- Accepts a Battle.net root, a flavor folder (`<root>/_retail_`), a custom client root, an `Interface` directory or an `Interface/AddOns` directory, and normalizes to client dir(s) by running the discovery recognizers on that path.
- Decided: a Battle.net root registers every flavor folder under it (one target each); `--name` is then allowed only when exactly one target results, otherwise `usage` (exit 2) with fix naming the flavor-folder form (why: one name cannot label several clients).
- A path that does not exist, or contains no recognizable client → `target_not_found` (exit 3), message saying what was looked for (`.build.info`, `Wow*.exe` + `Interface/`), fix `omaddons targets` (argv form).
- The path is stored in the registry as a manual root so later discovery includes it even outside the bounded scan.
- `--name N`: Decided: ids match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,31}$`, must not parse as a ULID, must not contain `@` (reserved for qualified collisions such as `retail@steam`), and must not already be taken; violations → `usage` (exit 2) naming the target that holds the id and suggesting `omaddons targets rename`.
- Already registered → idempotent, `changed: false`, exit 0.
- Registration (key assignment, registry write, marker write) happens under the global lock via the registry API.

### targets rm <id>

- Decided: removes the registry entry and leaves the client dir untouched, marker included, so a later `add` (or the next mutation touching it) re-links the same key. State files `targets/<key>.json` and `.files.json` are kept for the same reason.
- If it was the default target, the default is cleared.
- Data reports how many managed addons the target had (`managed_addons`) so a caller notices it unregistered a target with content. No warning code.
- Unknown id → `target_not_found` (3).

### targets rename <id> <new>

- Gives the target a new primary id; the old id is released. Same validation as `--name`. Renaming an unregistered target registers it first (vision §5.1: keys are assigned by the first mutating command or by `targets add|rename|default`).

### targets default <id>

- Sets the default target in the registry (registering it if needed). The default is used by `install` when `-t` is absent.
- Decided: config `default_target` in `<config>/omaddons/config.toml`, when set, overrides the registry default (explicit configuration wins); `targets default` still writes the registry and reports `overridden_by_config: true` so the caller knows why nothing changed in behavior. Flagged to the plan owner as a two-sources-of-truth problem worth revisiting.

Mutating sub-subcommands take the global lock (`LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` 5 s → `locked`, exit 5) and write through fsx via the registry API. They are not transactions (they are not in the transaction kind list) and are not undoable; they are idempotent and cheap to reverse by hand. `--dry-run` reports what would change and writes nothing.

`--json` `data` schemas:

```
targets:          {"targets": [Target], "default": string | null, "rescanned": bool}
targets add:      {"changed": bool, "targets": [Target]}
targets rm:       {"id": string, "key": string, "managed_addons": int, "was_default": bool}
targets rename:   {"key": string, "from": string, "to": string}
targets default:  {"id": string, "key": string, "overridden_by_config": bool}

Target = {"id": string, "key": string | null, "registered": bool, "default": bool, "family": string,
          "kind": "live" | "test", "install_kind": "battlenet" | "custom", "product": string | null,
          "version": string, "interface": int, "label": string | null, "client_dir": string,
          "missing": bool, "found_by": string}
```

Human output (list):

```
* retail   01JB…  mainline      12.1.0.69933  live  <client dir>
  wotlk    01JC…  wrath-legacy  3.3.5.12340   live  localhost  <client dir>
  ptr      -      mainline      12.1.0        test  (unregistered)  <client dir>
```

(`*` marks the default; in real output `<client dir>` is the actual path.)

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 3, 5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a synthetic machine, bare `omaddons targets --json` lists every discovered target with `client_dir`, `found_by`, `registered: false` and `key: null` before any mutation.
- `targets add <custom root> --name pserver` registers it with a ULID key, writes `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json` containing that key, and a second identical call returns `changed: false`.
- `targets add <Battle.net root>` with two flavor folders registers both; adding `--name` there exits 2.
- `targets add` on a directory with no client exits 3 `target_not_found` with a fix.
- `targets rename retail main` makes `-t main` resolve and `-t retail` fail; invalid ids (`Main`, a ULID, `a@b`, a taken id) exit 2.
- `targets rm <id>` removes the registry entry, leaves the marker and state files in place; `targets add` of the same path restores the same key.
- `targets default <id>` makes `install` without `-t` use that target; with config `default_target` set to another id, the output reports `overridden_by_config: true`.
- `--rescan` ignores the discovery cache: with a cache entry whose stored target data was edited in place by the test (stat keys left valid), bare `targets` shows the cached data, `targets --rescan` shows the on-disk truth with `rescanned: true` and rewrites the cache.
- A mutating sub-subcommand with the lock held by another process for longer than 5 s exits 5 `locked` with `retryable: true`.
- `--dry-run` on add/rm/rename/default writes nothing.

## Test Plan

- Unit: path normalization (root, flavor folder, custom root, `Interface`, `Interface/AddOns`); id validation; default precedence (config vs registry).
- Integration (`tests/targets.rs`, synthetic trees, HOME/XDG_* tempdirs per DEC-6): the cases above; lock contention using a second process holding the lock via `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.swapped=sleep:<ms>` (or the fsx-lock test helper); marker contents checked as JSON.
- E2E contract: one stdout envelope per sub-subcommand, success and failure, with the documented `command` string.

## Considerations

- Two live markers with one key (a copied install) are handled by the registry: the original path keeps the key, the copy gets a new one; `targets` surfaces the registry's warning.
- `extra_roots` in config and `targets add` overlap: config is declarative (dotfiles), `add` is imperative and recorded in the registry. Both feed discovery.
- Family names, product codes and flavor folder names are also accepted by `-t`; an id equal to one of those could be confusing. The registry bead defines resolution precedence; this bead only rejects ids that are already taken.
- Removing a target never deletes anything in the client dir.
acceptance_criteria: Bare targets --json lists every discovered target with client_dir, found_by, registered false and key null before any mutation; targets add <custom root> --name pserver registers a ULID key, writes Interface/.omaddons/target.json with that key, and repeating it returns changed false; add on a Battle.net root with two flavor folders registers both and --name there exits 2; add on a directory with no client exits 3 target_not_found with a fix; rename makes the new id resolve and the old fail, and invalid ids (uppercase, ULID-shaped, containing @, taken) exit 2; rm removes the registry entry but leaves marker and state files, and re-adding the path restores the same key; default <id> makes install without -t use it and reports overridden_by_config true when config default_target differs; --rescan ignores the discovery cache (an in-place edited cache entry is shown by bare targets, while --rescan shows on-disk truth with rescanned true and rewrites the cache); a mutating sub-subcommand with the lock held past 5 s exits 5 locked retryable; --dry-run on add/rm/rename/default writes nothing
close_reason: omaddons targets lists every client (registered or provisional, with found_by, missing and default) and adds, removes, renames and chooses targets under the global lock; --rescan bypasses the discovery cache; --dry-run writes nothing; nested help and usage errors work for its subcommands

title: Implement the undo and history commands
description:
## Background

Undo is what makes agent autonomy safe (vision D6, D31): every mutation is a snapshotted transaction attributed to an actor, and `omaddons undo` reverts it. `history` is how humans and agents see what happened and who did it, and it feeds the canonical intent "undo what the agent did today" (`history --actor agent --since 1d`, then `undo --last-by agent`).

The undo engine (E6 `undo` bead) implements reverting, conflict detection and the SavedVariables policy. The records bead (E2 `state-records`) implements `history.jsonl` reading with filters. This bead is the command layer for both: argument parsing, transaction selection, `data` schemas and human output.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/undo.rs`, `src/app/history.rs`, `Undo` and `History` subcommands in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

### undo

Synopsis (vision §5.9): `omaddons undo [<tx> | --last-by <actor>] [--saved-variables auto|restore|keep]`, plus global `--dry-run`, `--actor`, `--reason`, `--while-running`, `-t`, `--json`.

Selection:
- No argument: the most recent transaction in `history.jsonl` across all targets. Decided: a global `-t T` narrows "most recent" to that target (why: `-t` is a global flag, and "undo my last change to retail" is a natural request).
- `<tx>`: a full ULID, or a unique prefix of at least 8 characters. Unknown → `not_found` (exit 3, fix `omaddons history`); an ambiguous prefix → `not_found` with the matching ids in `details.candidates` (the general dictionary maps "not found or ambiguous" to 3).
- `--last-by <actor>`: the most recent transaction whose `actor` is `human`, `agent` or `widget`. Another value → `usage` (exit 2). None found → `not_found` (exit 3).
- `<tx>` and `--last-by` together → `usage`.
- Empty history → `not_found`, message "nothing to undo", fix `omaddons history`.

Rules the engine enforces (restated so the command maps them correctly):
- `undo <tx>` reverts an older transaction only if no later transaction of any kind (including `adopt` and `repair` in later milestones) touched the same folders; otherwise `undo_conflict` (exit 4) naming the later transaction(s) in `details`, with fix `omaddons undo <later tx>`.
- Undo is itself a transaction (kind `undo`), snapshotted and undoable. The output always names the reverted transaction.
- `--saved-variables` (default `auto`), per SavedVariables file of the touched folders:
  - `auto`: unchanged since the transaction → nothing to do; changed → the current file is cloned into the undo transaction, then restored; the target's client running → the SavedVariables part is skipped and reported as warning `saved_variables_deferred` with fix `omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables restore` (argv form) to run once the client exits. Folders still follow the running policy.
  - `restore`: like `auto`, but while the client runs it is refused with `game_running` (exit 4) instead of deferred.
  - `keep`: SavedVariables are never touched.
  - SavedVariables are never written while the target's client runs, under any policy or flag.
- `--dry-run`: reports what would be restored and the SavedVariables decisions per file count; takes no lock and writes nothing (DEC-16).

After a commit, `commands` holds the undo-the-undo hint `{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo <undo tx>","argv":[...],"destructive":false}`, and a `reload_required` warning when needed.

`--json` `data` schema (`UndoData`):

```
{
  "dry_run": bool,
  "reverted": {"tx": string, "kind": string, "at": string, "target": {"id": string, "key": string}, "actor": "human"|"agent"|"widget", "argv": [string]},
  "tx": string | null,                          // the new undo transaction
  "folders": {"restored": [string], "removed": [string]},   // removed = folders the reverted tx had added
  "saved_variables": {"policy": "auto"|"restore"|"keep", "restored": int, "unchanged": int, "deferred": int, "kept": int},
  "reload_required": "none" | "reload" | "restart",
  "atomic_swap": bool | null
}
```

Counts only: account, realm and character names never appear in output (vision §4.4). `-v` adds the reverted transaction's `reason` and the folder paths.

Human output:

```
reverted 01JB… (install by agent, 2026-10-20 14:02) on retail
restored 3 folders, removed 1 · SavedVariables: 2 restored, 4 unchanged
tx 01JC… · /reload in game · undo this: omaddons undo 01JC…
```

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

### history

Synopsis: `omaddons history [-t T] [--limit N] [--actor A] [--since D]`. Read-only; never takes the lock; never writes.

- Newest first. Decided: default `--limit 20` (token-frugal; agents can raise it). `--limit 0` → `usage`.
- `--actor human|agent|widget`; another value → `usage`.
- `--since D`: a duration (`30m`, `12h`, `1d`, `2w`) relative to now, or an RFC 3339 timestamp, parsed with `jiff`. Anything else → `usage` (exit 2) with fix `omaddons history --since 1d`.
- `-t T`: resolve with the registry resolver; unknown → `target_not_found` (3).
- A torn last line in `history.jsonl` is skipped by the records reader; the command emits one stderr `log` event about it and no warning code (the doctor finding `history-torn-line` arrives in M4).

`--json` `data` schema (`HistoryData`):

```
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "tx": string,
      "kind": "install"|"update"|"remove"|"undo"|"adopt"|"sync"|"restore"|"repair",
      "at": string,                                   // RFC 3339 UTC
      "target": {"id": string, "key": string},
      "actor": "human" | "agent" | "widget",
      "reason": string | null,
      "argv": [string],
      "changes": {"added": int, "replaced": int, "removed": int},
      "result": string                                // as stored by the engine
    }
  ],
  "truncated": bool                                   // more entries matched than --limit
}
```

`-v` replaces the `changes` counts with the stored `ops[]`. Target ids are resolved from the registry at render time; a key no longer registered shows `id` = the key.

Human output: one line per entry, `01JB…  2026-10-20 14:02  agent  install  retail  +3 ~0 -0  "reason"`.

Exit codes: 0, 2, 3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After an install, `omaddons undo --json` reverts it, names the reverted tx in `data.reverted`, creates a new `kind: undo` transaction, and the folders are byte-identical to before the install.
- `omaddons undo` on the undo transaction re-applies the install (undo is undoable).
- `undo <tx>` with a later transaction touching the same folders exits 4 `undo_conflict`, naming the later transaction; with disjoint folders it succeeds.
- `undo --last-by agent` reverts only the most recent `actor: agent` transaction even when a newer human transaction exists.
- Unique 8-character prefixes resolve; unknown ids and ambiguous prefixes exit 3 with a fix.
- `--saved-variables` policies behave as specified; while the client runs (fake /proc), `auto` defers with warning `saved_variables_deferred` whose fix argv is `["omaddons","undo","<tx>","--saved-variables","restore"]`, and `restore` exits 4 `game_running`.
- No output, JSON or human, contains account, realm or character names from the synthetic `WTF/` tree.
- `omaddons history --actor agent --since 1d --json` lists only matching entries newest first, with `truncated` correct for `--limit`.
- `history` with an invalid `--since` or `--actor` exits 2 with a fix.

## Test Plan

- Unit: tx selection (latest, latest with `-t`, prefix resolution, ambiguous prefix, `--last-by`, conflicting arguments), `--since` parsing (durations, RFC 3339, invalid), history filtering and `truncated`.
- Integration (`tests/undo_history.rs`, synthetic trees with a `WTF/Account/<ACCT>/…` layout using fake account/realm/character names, `file:` installs, fake /proc for the running client): install → undo → byte comparison; undo of undo; conflict across install then remove of the same folder; `--last-by agent` with `OMADDONS_ACTOR=agent` and `--actor human` transactions interleaved; SavedVariables matrix (unchanged, changed, running × auto/restore/keep); grep all outputs for the fake names (must not appear).
- E2E contract: one stdout envelope per case; exit codes as documented.
- Log argv, env and full outputs on failure.

## Considerations

- Undo after retention pruned the reverted transaction's snapshot cannot restore folders; the undo engine reports that case and this command passes its error through unchanged.
- `history` reads the whole `history.jsonl`; it grows by one line per transaction, so this is fine for M1. If it ever becomes slow, read from the end.
- Verb aliases (`revert`, `rollback` → undo; `log` → history) are M4.
- `doctor undo <run>` resolving to `omaddons undo <tx>` is M4.
acceptance_criteria: undo --json after an install reverts it, names the reverted tx in data.reverted, creates a kind undo transaction and leaves folders byte-identical to before the install; undoing the undo re-applies the install; undo <tx> with a later transaction touching the same folders exits 4 undo_conflict naming it, and succeeds for disjoint folders; undo --last-by agent reverts only the latest agent transaction even when a newer human one exists; unique 8-character prefixes resolve and unknown or ambiguous ids exit 3 with a fix; --saved-variables auto defers with saved_variables_deferred and fix argv omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables restore while the client runs, and restore exits 4 game_running; no output contains account, realm or character names; history --actor agent --since 1d --json lists only matching entries newest first with truncated correct for --limit; invalid --since or --actor exits 2 with a fix
close_reason: undo and history commands over the engine undo and the history reader

comments.text: **state-records landed.** history and undo read with `history::read(&paths, &HistoryFilter { target, actor, kind, since, limit })` → HistoryRead { entries (oldest first), torn_tail, skipped_lines }; `history::last(&paths, &filter)` gives the most recent match for `undo --last-by`. HistoryEntry.reverts names the transaction an undo reverted. Default `--limit 20` is this command's to apply.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **cli-skeleton landed: how to add this command (DEC-1).** (1) Add a variant to `cli::Command`; its doc comment becomes the 'about' in bare help, which lists commands automatically, ordered by `app::help::COMMON_VERBS`. (2) Add its canonical name to `app::COMMANDS`, so usage errors name it. (3) Add arms to `app::command_name` and `app::dispatch` that call `src/app/<cmd>.rs`, returning `Result<impl output::Outcome, Error>`; dispatch renders it with `output::emit`. `Context` provides: output, actor, reason, argv (argv[0] = omaddons, for history and fix_argv), offline (flag or OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1), dry_run (read-only commands ignore it), while_running, target (raw -t value), started. Command-specific flags go on the variant. Global flags are already accepted before or after the subcommand. tests/cli_skeleton.rs has an isolated-HOME runner (`support::run_env`) that checks every stderr line is NDJSON.

comments.text: **registry landed (src/discover/registry.rs, src/state/registry.rs).** Pipeline for a command: `discover(&input, &table)`, then `reconcile(&load_registry(&paths)?.value, &found.targets)` gives `Resolved { targets (key and id filled, key None when unregistered), warnings, missing }`. Then `resolve_one(selector, &resolved.targets, &ctx.argv)` gives target_not_found / target_ambiguous with argv fixes. To register (mutating commands, inside the transaction): `GlobalLock::acquire`, then `LockedRegistry::load(&guard, &paths)?`, then `.ensure_registered(&mut session, &target)?`. The session's ScopeTable must include the target's client dir. Read paths never write.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Engine undo landed (6.12):** call `engine::undo(&UndoRequest { selector: UndoSelector::{Latest, Tx(id), LastBy(actor)}, sv_policy: SvPolicy::{Auto, Restore, Keep}, dry_run, while_running, reason, targets: world.resolved.targets.clone() }, &EngineCtx { command: "undo", .. })` → `UndoOutcome { undoes, outcome: TxOutcome (flattened: target, key, tx, kind, dry_run, changes, atomic_swap, reload_required, warnings, lock_held_ms), sv: { restored, deferred, unchanged, kept } }`; it serializes directly as the data core. The engine needs no network; build EngineCtx like install's private Engine (src/app/install.rs). Errors already carry fixes: undo_conflict (fix: undo the newest conflicting tx; after a deferred undo: `undo <tx> --saved-variables restore`), not_found (fix: omaddons history), game_running. history.jsonl entries now have `reverts` and `sv_deferred`. The 7.2 test plan's '--force over an unmanaged folder, then undo restores it' E2E belongs here: tests/install.rs has the harness and the refusals test sets that scene up.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Implementation decisions (src/app/undo.rs, src/app/history.rs, src/app/engine.rs).** (1) The command resolves the transaction itself and calls the engine with UndoSelector::Tx: no argument = newest undoable entry (on the -t target's key when -t is given; an unregistered -t target has nothing to undo); <tx> = full ULID or unique prefix of 8+ characters, any case (shorter → usage; unknown → not_found fix 'omaddons history'; ambiguous → not_found with details.candidates); --last-by conflicts with <tx> at the parser (usage). (2) data.folders: restored = added + replaced folders of the undo's changes, removed = folders it removed, each sorted by key; saved_variables carries the policy plus restored/unchanged/deferred/kept; -v adds reverted.reason and client_dir. commands carry the undo-the-undo hint. (3) history's --actor is the global attribution flag read as a filter (it takes the same three values; OMADDONS_ACTOR never filters), because a subcommand flag cannot share a global flag's name. -v replaces changes with ops; undo entries also carry reverts. --since accepts Nm/Nh/Nd/Nw and RFC 3339. -t resolves discovered targets first, then registry entries whose client is gone. A torn tail is one info log on stderr. (4) install's Engine moved to src/app/engine.rs (Engine::new(ctx, world, command), run, undo) for remove to reuse; tests/common/home.rs now holds the Home/Run end-to-end harness. (5) The 7.2 leftover '--force over an unmanaged folder, then undo restores it byte for byte' is covered in tests/undo_history.rs.

title: Build the M1 CLI contract conformance suite and the exit-site test
description:
## Background

The CLI contract is the product (vision D2, D17): agents drive `omaddons` directly, so every command must behave the same way at the edges. Individual command beads test their own cases; this bead is the cross-command conformance suite that proves the M1 contract-core checkpoint (vision §7 M1):

- bare `omaddons` prints help;
- every M1 command accepts `--json` and emits exactly one stdout envelope on success and on failure (`cmd --json | jq -e .ok` distinguishes failure);
- every error has a non-empty `fix` and a `fix_argv`;
- stderr is NDJSON when it is not a TTY;
- exit sites match the general dictionary.

It also implements the vision's "a test asserts that every exit site in the source maps to a published code" (§5.9 publication rules).

Placeholders: `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` = the XDG state, cache and config dirs, which tests point at tempdirs (DEC-6).

## Technical Approach

Location: `tests/contract/` as one integration-test crate (`tests/contract/main.rs` with modules), using `assert_cmd`, `insta` (json feature), synthetic trees from `tests/common/trees.rs`, archives from `tests/common/archives.rs`, and HTTP replay via `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` (DEC-7). No network: a test fails if the replay layer sees an unknown URL.

Contract facts the suite asserts (restated from vision §5.9 so the suite is self-contained):

- Envelope (stdout under `--json`), one shape for success and failure, keys in this order: `ok`, `schema_version` (`"1.0"`), `tool_version`, `command`, `exit_code`, `partial`, `data` (success) or `error` (failure), `warnings`, `commands`, `meta` (`elapsed_ms`, `offline`). Under `--check`/`--strict` failures (exit 6) both `error` (`code: "check_failed"`) and `data` are present.
- `error` = `{code, message, fix, fix_argv, alternatives: [{display, argv}], retryable, details}`. `fix` is never empty. `fix_argv` is an array, or null only for non-CLI fixes (for example "/reload in game", "upgrade omaddons"). When `fix_argv` is an array its first element is `omaddons` and `shell_words::join(fix_argv) == fix`.
- Every `warnings[]` entry has `code`, `message`, and when it has a `fix`, a `fix_argv` (array or null) following the same rule. Every `commands[]` entry has `action`, `command`, `argv`, `destructive`.
- `--json`, `--format json`, `--robot` and `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json` are equivalent.
- stderr is NDJSON when stderr is not a TTY, or `CI` is set, or `TERM=dumb`: every line parses as a JSON object with `event` ∈ `progress|log|warning|error`. Every error is mirrored to stderr as exactly one `{"event":"error",…}` line.
- Human mode (no JSON flag): stdout is empty on error.
- General exit dictionary: 0 `ok` (including partial success), 1 `failed`, 2 `usage`, 3 `not_found`, 4 `refused`, 5 `locked`, 6 `check_failed`. `exit_code` in the envelope equals the process exit code, and equals the error code's registered exit.
- Determinism: running the same command twice on the same state produces byte-identical stdout once `meta` is removed.

Command matrix (each row is at least one success and one failure case, all run under `--json`):

| Command | Success case | Failure case |
|---|---|---|
| (bare) | `omaddons` → help on stdout, exit 0; `omaddons --json` → envelope with `command: "help"` | `omaddons --bogus` → `usage` (2) |
| `help` | `help install` | `help nosuch` → `usage` (2) with closest-command fix |
| `status` | two-target synthetic machine | `-t nosuch` → `target_not_found` (3); leftover journal + `--check` → 6 |
| `targets` | list; `targets add <root>` | `targets add <empty dir>` → `target_not_found` (3); `targets rename x Bad` → `usage` (2) |
| `list` | after a `file:` install | `-t nosuch` → 3 |
| `info` | catalog name with replay fixtures | `info nosuchaddon` → `not_found` (3) |
| `install` | `file:` zip; `gh:` with fixtures | `ref_invalid` (2); `target_ambiguous` (3); `protected_folder` (4); partial + `--strict` → 6 |
| `remove` | installed addon | `not_managed` (3) |
| `undo` | after install | empty history → `not_found` (3); `undo_conflict` (4) |
| `history` | after install | `--since nonsense` → `usage` (2) |
| `config` | `config get`, `config set`, `config path` | `config set nosuch.key 1` → `usage` (2) |
| `net-log` | after install | `--since nonsense` → 2 |

Additional cases:
- `locked` (5): hold the global lock in a second process (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.swapped=sleep:<ms>` on a concurrent install) past `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` and run a mutating command; assert exit 5, `retryable: true`.
- Panic: `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=cli.panic=panic` (DEC-7) → stdout holds one envelope with `error.code == "internal"`, exit 1, fix `omaddons status` (DEC-5), and one stderr error line.
- `--offline` on a command that needs the network (`install gh:…`) → `offline` (1).
- `CI=1` and `TERM=dumb` each force NDJSON stderr even when stderr would otherwise be human (simulate by setting them; the suite cannot allocate a TTY, so the TTY-human path stays covered by the output bead's unit tests).

Snapshots: `insta::assert_json_snapshot!` of each envelope with `meta` removed and ULIDs/timestamps redacted (`insta` redactions on `.data.tx`, `.data..at`, etc.), stored under `tests/contract/snapshots/`.

Exit-site test (`tests/contract/exit_sites.rs`):
- Scan `src/` for every `ErrorCode::<Variant>` construction and assert each variant appears in the registry's published table (the registry exposes an iterator over all codes with `wire()`, `exit()`, `retryable()`).
- Assert every registry entry's exit is in the general dictionary (0–6), and every wire name is unique snake_case.
- Assert `std::process::exit` appears nowhere in `src/`, and `ExitCode::from` appears only in `src/main.rs`/`src/cli.rs`, where the value is derived from `Exit` (why: one exit path means every exit maps to a published code).
- The doctor dictionary (64/66/73/74 etc.) does not exist in M1; the test is written so M4 can add the second dictionary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/contract/` covers every row of the command matrix plus the locked, panic, offline and CI/TERM cases, and passes in `argc gate`.
- For every case: stdout is exactly one JSON document (parsing stdout as a stream yields one value), `.ok` matches success/failure, the process exit code equals `exit_code` and the registered exit of `error.code`.
- Every error and every warning with a fix has a non-empty `fix`; `fix_argv` is null only for the documented non-CLI fixes, otherwise starts with `omaddons` and round-trips through shell-words to `fix`.
- Every stderr line in non-TTY runs parses as JSON with a valid `event`; each failing run has exactly one `error` event.
- Human-mode failures leave stdout empty.
- `--json`, `--format json`, `--robot` and `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json` produce identical stdout (meta removed).
- Repeated runs produce identical stdout (meta removed).
- The exit-site test fails if a new `ErrorCode` variant is used without a registry entry, or if `std::process::exit` is added anywhere in `src/`.
- Envelope snapshots are committed and reviewed.

## Test Plan

- This bead is itself the test plan for the contract. Structure: `tests/contract/main.rs` (shared harness: env setup per DEC-6, run helper returning parsed stdout/stderr/exit, assertion helpers `assert_envelope`, `assert_ndjson_stderr`, `assert_fix_argv`), one module per command, `exit_sites.rs`, `snapshots/`.
- Self-test the harness: feed it a known-bad stdout (two JSON documents; empty fix) and assert the helpers fail.
- On failure, log argv, env, full stdout and stderr.

## Considerations

- The suite depends on every M1 command bead; command beads should already have per-command e2e tests, so this suite focuses on uniformity, not behavior depth.
- `fix_argv` placeholders: fixes that need user input (for example `omaddons targets add <path>`) carry `argv: null`; the suite's allowlist of null-argv fixes must stay small and explicit, listed in the harness.
- M4 extends this suite with `capabilities`, the wire-name golden (`tests/contract/wire_names.txt`), the doctor dictionary, intent inference and `robot-docs schema` validation of every snapshot.
- TTY behavior (human stderr lines, colors, progress bars) cannot be exercised without a pseudo-terminal; it is covered by unit tests in the output bead.

title: Add cargo-fuzz targets for every M1 parser and archive inspection
description:
## Background

Every parser in M1 reads bytes omaddons does not control: `.build.info` and `.flavor.info` (BPSV), Battle.net's `product.db` (protobuf, layout UNVERIFIED), launcher configs (Lutris YAML, Heroic JSON, Steam VDF, Bottles YAML, all read by small tolerant hand-written readers), TOC files, addon archives from the internet, and user-typed refs. The vision's goal G3 says upstream drift yields typed errors, never crashes; the testing strategy (§5.12) lists property tests and fuzz targets for exactly these inputs, and the M1 checkpoint requires each fuzz target to run for at least 10 minutes without a crash.

Property tests live in each parser's own bead. This bead adds the cargo-fuzz harness, the targets, seed corpora and the recipe, and runs nothing in the per-commit gate (fuzz runs happen at milestone checkpoints, vision §5.12 "Not in the per-commit gate").

## Technical Approach

- `fuzz/` is its own cargo-fuzz crate (`fuzz/Cargo.toml` with `[package.metadata] cargo-fuzz = true`, its own `[workspace]` table so the main package's build, clippy and tests never include it, `libfuzzer-sys`, and a path dependency on `omaddons`).
- Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` pins stable 1.97.1; cargo-fuzz needs nightly sanitizer flags, so targets run with `cargo +nightly fuzz run <target>` (a nightly toolchain is installed on the development machine). Decided: no nightly pin in the repository (why: nightly is only for fuzzing; the product builds on stable).
- Targets (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/<name>.rs`), each calling the production entry point on arbitrary bytes and asserting only "returns, never panics, never allocates without bound":
  - `bpsv` → the BPSV parser (`src/discover/bpsv.rs`).
  - `product_db` → the protobuf wire reader (`src/discover/product_db.rs`).
  - `lutris`, `heroic`, `steam_vdf`, `bottles` → the launcher-config readers (discover-launchers bead).
  - `toc` → the TOC parser (`src/toc.rs`), with lossy UTF-8 input.
  - `archive` → archive inspection on in-memory zip bytes (`std::io::Cursor`); the inspection API must accept `Read + Seek` so no file is needed. Limits (`ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES`, `ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED`, `ARCHIVE_MAX_RATIO`) must keep memory bounded.
  - `ref_parse` → the user-ref parser (`src/sources/refs.rs`), with lossy UTF-8 input.
- Entry points must be reachable from outside the crate. If a parser is private, expose it through a `#[doc(hidden)] pub mod fuzzing` re-export in `src/lib.rs` rather than widening module visibility.
- Seed corpora: decided — committed under `fuzz/seeds/<target>/` (why: `fuzz/corpus/` is gitignored for generated inputs). Seeds come from the existing test fixtures (`tests/fixtures/…`, the hostile archives from `tests/common/archives.rs` written out once, the `.build.info` example header from vision §4.1). Each target gets at least three seeds, including one malformed.
- Recipe in `Argcfile.sh`: `argc fuzz <target> [--time <seconds>]` (default 600) running `cargo +nightly fuzz run <target> fuzz/corpus/<target> fuzz/seeds/<target> -- -max_total_time=<seconds> -rss_limit_mb=2048`, plus `argc fuzz-all [--time]` looping over every target. Use the argc DSL correctly (`@cmd`, `@arg target![...]` with a `_choice_target` function listing `fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs`, `@option --time`), shellcheck-clean, `@meta require-tools cargo-fuzz` on those recipes.
- Crash triage: a crash writes an artifact under `fuzz/artifacts/<target>/`; the fix is a regression test in the owning parser's unit tests using that input, then the fuzz run is repeated.
- Gate interaction: files under `fuzz/` count as code changes (vision §5.12), so commits touching them run `argc gate`; the gate itself does not build the fuzz crate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fuzz/` exists as a separate cargo-fuzz crate excluded from the main package; `cargo build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` in the repository root do not compile it.
- Nine targets exist: `bpsv`, `product_db`, `lutris`, `heroic`, `steam_vdf`, `bottles`, `toc`, `archive`, `ref_parse`, each with at least three committed seeds under `fuzz/seeds/<target>/`.
- `argc fuzz <target> --time 30` runs each target for 30 seconds without a crash on the development machine (smoke run recorded in the close reason).
- `argc fuzz` and `argc fuzz-all` are shellcheck-clean and pass `argc --argc-export Argcfile.sh`.
- Any crash found while building the targets is fixed in the owning parser with a regression unit test.
- The 10-minute-per-target run is left to the m1-checkpoint bead (documented in the recipe help).

## Test Plan

- Smoke: 30-second run per target (above).
- Regression: every crash input becomes a unit test in the owning module.
- Check that the main package is unaffected: `argc gate` passes with `fuzz/` present.

## Considerations

- The `archive` target can find slow inputs rather than crashes (decompression of near-limit entries); `-timeout` defaults are fine, but report slow units if libFuzzer flags them.
- The Lua SavedVariables parser (M3) and the WoWI/Tukui decoders (M2) add their own targets later.
- If `cargo +nightly fuzz` is unavailable on a machine, the recipe must fail with a message naming `cargo install cargo-fuzz` and a nightly toolchain, not a cryptic error.
acceptance_criteria: fuzz/ is a separate cargo-fuzz crate that cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test in the repository root do not compile; nine targets exist (bpsv, product_db, lutris, heroic, steam_vdf, bottles, toc, archive, ref_parse), each with at least three committed seeds under fuzz/seeds/<target>/; argc fuzz <target> --time 30 runs each target 30 seconds without a crash, recorded in the close reason; argc fuzz and argc fuzz-all are shellcheck-clean and pass argc --argc-export; any crash found is fixed in the owning parser with a regression unit test; the 10-minute-per-target run is documented as the m1-checkpoint's job
close_reason: cargo-fuzz crate with nine targets, committed seeds and argc fuzz / fuzz-all recipes; 30 s smoke per target clean

Nine targets call the production entry points: bpsv (Bpsv::parse + rows, build_info_rows, flavor_product), product_db (parse_product_db), lutris (lutris::parse + Game::client_exe), heroic (wine_prefixes), steam_vdf (library_paths), bottles (custom_path), toc (parse_toc), archive (inspect_zip on a Cursor with default ArchiveLimits, asserting accepted rel_paths never escape) and ref_parse (Ref::from_str round trip + parse_user_ref with a nonexistent cwd and empty lookups). Every entry point was already public, so no fuzzing re-export module was needed. **Seeds:** 32 under fuzz/seeds/<target>/ (3 to 5 per target, each with a malformed one), written by the ignored generator tests/fuzz_seeds.rs (OMADDONS_WRITE_SEEDS=1) from the test builders and fixtures; its normal test keeps every target with a source, a [[bin]] and three seeds. **Toolchain decision:** argc fuzz/fuzz-all take --toolchain (default nightly) and first check that cargo-fuzz exists and that the toolchain's rustc is at least the crate's rust-version, failing with a message naming cargo install cargo-fuzz or rustup update nightly / --toolchain nightly-<date>. This replaces @meta require-tools, whose generic message would not name the install commands. On the development machine the undated nightly is 1.96 (too old for rust-version 1.97), so the smoke run used nightly-2026-08-31. No crash was found, so no regression tests were needed.

title: Epic: Post-M2 audit fixes (gaps in milestones 1 and 2)
description:
## Background

On 2026-10-16, right after milestone 2 closed, an independent audit compared the vision bead (`omad-vision-8qa`), README.md and the code at `53b54e6`. Seven read-only investigations covered discovery and rules, the transaction engine, sources and the network layer, the CLI contract, the gate and test suite, the beads-versus-vision coverage, and a read-only smoke test on the development machine.

The result: M1 and M2 are real. The gate passes 1,288 tests with 0 failures, and every M1/M2 command works on the development machine's six clients. But the audit found defects inside that "done" work, and none of them was tracked:

- correctness bugs in the engine's failure paths: recovery, the journal, SavedVariables;
- contract holes an agent will hit, e.g. a usage-error fix that turns `uninstall` into `install`;
- integrity and privacy statements the code does not fully keep;
- discovery and rules fields that do nothing;
- test-suite blind spots;
- README statements that no longer match the code;
- real-world facts that have only ever been checked against synthetic fixtures.

On 2026-10-18 the owner decided these gaps are fixed before any milestone 3 work is planned. This epic holds them. Each leaf bead was re-verified against `53b54e6` before filing, with exact file:line anchors and, where possible, a reproduction in an isolated HOME.

## Goals

- Every defect the audit found in M1/M2 code is fixed, with a regression test.
- Every promise in README.md is true of the code, or the README says exactly what the code does.
- The real-world assumptions the safety model rests on are observed on real clients, not only on fixtures: running detection under Proton, in-game loading, legacy client behaviour.

## Success Criteria

- Every child area epic is closed (`br epic close-eligible`).
- `argc gate` passes at the closing commit.
- The pinned vision bead has comments recording every contract addition these fixes made (DEC-4, before the M4 freeze).
- README.md's numbers and claims match the code at the closing commit.

## Non-Goals

- No milestone 3, 4 or 5 work: no Omarchy widget, `errors`, `backup`, `doctor`, `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, skill, stored plans/`apply`, completions, full intent inference, wire-name golden file, CurseForge, Wago, GraphQL or packaging. Where a fix touches one of those areas, the leaf bead scopes itself to what M1/M2 promised and names the boundary.
- No refactors beyond what each fix needs.

## Considerations

- Several engine fixes touch the same recovery code (`src/engine/journal.rs`, `src/engine/tx.rs`, `src/engine/undo.rs`). Their `blocks` edges order them so they do not collide.
- Contract additions (new warning or error codes, data keys) are allowed until the M4 freeze, but each must be registered in `src/error.rs`, documented in README.md and recorded on the vision bead.
- The real-world verification beads wait on external events or on owner-supplied clients and sessions. They are deferred with the exact ask, so they do not hold up the code fixes.
acceptance_criteria: every child area epic is closed (br epic close-eligible); argc gate passes at the closing commit; the vision bead has a comment for every contract addition these fixes made; README.md's numbers and claims match the code

title: A failed in-process recovery deletes the journal and the stage dir holding the old folders
description:
## Background

The journal exists so that "at every instant, each AddOns folder is either the complete old version or the complete new version ... across crashes via the journal" (vision §5.5 Invariant, D25) and so that "the next command that commits a change ... recovers under the lock first" (README, Safety model, Interrupted runs). Neither holds when a commit fails and recovering it in the same process fails too: the code then deletes the very journal and staged folders the next lock holder needs.

How it happens (verified at HEAD 53b54e6, found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit):

1. `src/engine/tx.rs:767-807` runs the commit in a closure. On any error, `src/engine/tx.rs:808-815` calls `recover_tx(&guard, paths, scopes, tx)?` (line 810). The `?` propagates a recovery error out of `locked()`.
2. `commit_target()` calls `cleanup(ctx.paths, scopes, inflight, &tx, Some(&staged.stage_dir))` unconditionally right after `locked(...)` returns (`src/engine/tx.rs:465-468`). `cleanup()` (`src/engine/tx.rs:1130-1156`) prunes `paths.journal(tx)`, both in-flight lock files, the cache tmp dir and the stage dir under the transaction's own in-flight lock.
3. `fsx::prune` never checks a journal's phase: `Kind::Journal` is simply a `PostCommitCleanup` kind (`src/fsx/prune.rs:264-276`, location rule at `src/fsx/prune.rs:306`), although its own doc says "committed journals" (`src/fsx/prune.rs:28`).
4. `recover_parsed()` itself is careful: when `roll_forward`/`roll_back` fail it returns before its own prune (`src/engine/journal.rs:523-561`). The caller's cleanup undoes that care.

The undo commit has the identical pattern: `src/engine/undo.rs:336-342` (`recover_tx(...)?` at line 338) and the unconditional `cleanup(...)` at `src/engine/undo.rs:192-193`.

Why it loses data: after a `RENAME_EXCHANGE` the stage dir holds the OLD live folder (`src/engine/swap.rs:294-300`; it moves to the snapshot only in phase 2, `src/engine/swap.rs:314-320`). If the commit fails after the exchange and the rollback rename fails as well (EIO, a filesystem that turned read-only after an error, ENOSPC on the state disk while the journal append of a later step fails, ...), cleanup prunes the stage dir: the only copy of the old version is deleted. That old version can hold the user's local edits (README: "the transaction snapshot keeps them, so `omaddons undo` brings them back") or an unmanaged folder replaced with `--force` (README: "the snapshot keeps the original for undo"). The journal that would let the next lock holder finish the job is deleted too, so nothing reports `journal_pending`, the record still describes the old version, and multi-folder addons can be left half-swapped. When the AddOns filesystem itself refuses writes, the stage-dir prune fails but the journal prune (state filesystem) succeeds, and retention later sweeps the then-"orphaned" stage dir after `ORPHAN_MIN_AGE` (`src/engine/retention.rs:214-251`), so the loss is only delayed.

User-visible consequence: silent, permanent loss of local edits or of a replaced unmanaged folder; AddOns contents that disagree with the records (`status` reports the addon modified, a new folder unmanaged); no journal, no warning, no way to undo.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (fresh `HOME`, `XDG_*` under it, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<empty dir>`), with a synthetic retail Battle.net root under `$HOME/Games/WoW` (`.build.info` with one `wow` row, `_retail_/.flavor.info`, `_retail_/WoW.exe`, `_retail_/Interface/AddOns`, `_retail_/WTF`). Addon sources are plain folders: `<src>/pkg/Foo/Foo.toc` (`## Interface: 120105`) and `core.lua`.

Data loss (old folder with a local edit deleted):

1. `omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail` installs Foo 1.
2. `echo '-- MY LOCAL EDIT' >> <client>/Interface/AddOns/Foo/core.lua`
3. Make `<src>/pkg` hold Foo 2 and a new folder Bar.
4. `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS='engine.swap.after_exchange=error,fsx.rename_with.before=error@3' omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail` (rename 1 = Bar NOREPLACE, rename 2 = Foo EXCHANGE, then the commit fails; rename 3 = the rollback's exchange back, which fails).
5. Expected: the command fails, the journal is kept and reported (`journal_pending`), the old Foo with the edit is in the stage dir, and the next change command rolls back to Foo 1 with the edit.
6. Actual (reproduced 2026-10-18): exit 1 `io`; AddOns holds Foo 2 and Bar 2; `<state>/omaddons/journal/` is empty; the stage dir and trash are empty; `grep -r 'MY LOCAL EDIT'` over the whole isolated tree finds nothing; `status` shows `journal.pending: 0`, Foo `modified`, one unmanaged folder; `list` still says Foo 1; history has no line for the failed transaction.

Half-applied multi-folder addon with existing engine failpoints only:

- Same steps 1 and 3, then `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS='engine.swap.after_exchange=error,engine.recover.step=error' omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail`.
- Actual: rollback undid the Foo exchange, then failed; AddOns is Foo 1 plus Bar 2, the journal is gone, `status` lists Bar as unmanaged and no pending journal.

## Technical Approach

Decided fix: a transaction's leftovers are pruned only when its journal is finished; when recovery fails, everything recovery needs stays for the next lock holder.

1. `cleanup()` (`src/engine/tx.rs:1130-1156`) decides from the journal itself, not from the caller's control flow: read `paths.journal(tx)` with the journal module's reader (`journal::read`, `src/engine/journal.rs:381-386`; expose a `pub(crate) fn phase_of(paths, tx) -> Option<Phase>` or similar). If the journal exists and its phase is `Prepared` or `Swapped` (`src/engine/journal.rs:287-293`), the victims are only the cache scratch (`paths.cache_inflight_lock(tx)`, `paths.cache_tmp(tx)`); the journal, the state in-flight lock file and the stage dir stay. Phases `Unprepared`/`Committed`, a missing journal, or an unreadable journal whose prepared line is absent keep today's victim list. Dropping the `InflightLock` still releases the flock, so the next lock holder sees a free lock and recovers (`src/engine/journal.rs:466-471`), and retention never sweeps the stage dir because a journal exists (`src/engine/retention.rs:225-227`).
2. The client-side snapshot `snapshots/<tx>/` is never pruned by cleanup today; keep it that way (roll-forward and rollback both need it).
3. In `locked()` (`src/engine/tx.rs:808-815`) and the undo `commit()` (`src/engine/undo.rs:336-342`), replace `recover_tx(...)?` with an explicit match: on `Err(recovery)` return the ORIGINAL commit error, annotated: message suffix `"; recovering it failed too ({recovery.message}), so its journal is kept and the next omaddons command that commits a change finishes it"`, `retryable: false`, fix `omaddons status`, and `details.journal_pending = "<tx>"` plus `details.recovery_error = {"code": ..., "message": ...}` merged into the existing details. Do not swallow the recovery error and do not report success.
4. `fsx::prune` gains a defence-in-depth check for `Kind::Journal` victims under `LockUse::Own`: refuse (scope_denied, "refusing to prune an unfinished journal") a journal file whose last complete line is not `{"type":"committed"}` and whose first line is a valid `prepared`. fsx must not depend on `engine::journal`, so implement a tiny tail check in `src/fsx/prune.rs` (read the file, split lines, look for a final `"type":"committed"` line or an absent/torn `prepared` first line). Recovery's own prune (`LockUse::Held`, `src/engine/journal.rs:554-559`) deletes journals it just finished or rolled back, so the check applies to `LockUse::Own` only.
5. Correct the prune doc (`src/fsx/prune.rs:28`) and the cleanup doc ("Best effort: recovery and retention sweep anything left", `src/engine/tx.rs:1127-1129`) to describe the rule.

Rejected alternatives:
- Passing a "keep" flag from `locked()` to `cleanup()`: works for this path but leaves every other early return (a panic unwinding past `locked`, a future code path) able to delete an unfinished journal. Reading the phase in cleanup makes the rule structural.
- Retrying recovery in a loop in process: a read-only or failing disk will not recover in milliseconds; the next command (or M4 doctor) is the right retry point.
- Moving the old folder into the snapshot before the exchange: would cost an extra rename and break the single-exchange atomic swap (D25).

Contract (DEC-4, allowed before the M4 freeze): the failure envelope of install/update/sync/pin/adopt/copy/remove/undo may carry `error.details.journal_pending` (tx id string) and `error.details.recovery_error` ({code, message}); no new codes. Register nothing new in `src/error.rs`; document the two details keys in README (Safety model, Interrupted runs: "If recovering a failed commit fails too, for example because the disk turned read-only, the journal and the staged folders are kept, the command fails naming the transaction, and the next command that commits a change finishes it"; and the troubleshooting entry "journal_pending that does not clear"). Record the change as a comment on omad-vision-8qa (§5.5 Steps 9 / Journal phases and recovery: "cleanup prunes a journal only once it is committed or rolled back").

## Acceptance Criteria

- With `engine.swap.after_exchange=error,fsx.rename_with.before=error@3` the install fails with its original `io` error carrying `details.journal_pending` and `details.recovery_error`; the journal, the stage dir (holding the old Foo with the local edit) and `snapshots/<tx>/` still exist; `status` reports `journal_pending` for that tx.
- The next `install`/`remove`/`undo` without failpoints rolls the transaction back, reports `journal_recovered`, and AddOns is byte-identical to before the failed install (tree digest), the local edit included; Bar is gone; the journal and stage dir are pruned.
- Same for a failure in phase `swapped` whose roll-forward fails (see Test Plan): the journal is kept and the next command rolls it forward exactly once (one history line).
- `cleanup()` never prunes a journal in phase `prepared` or `swapped`; `fsx::prune` under `LockUse::Own` refuses one.
- The undo commit behaves the same.
- README Safety model and troubleshooting describe the behaviour; vision comment recorded.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/tx.rs` tests, `TxScene`): `with_spec("engine.swap.after_exchange=error,engine.recover.step=error", ...)` on an install that replaces Foo and adds Bar: the error carries `details.journal_pending`; the journal and stage dir exist; then `recover_all` under a fresh lock restores the old trees (compare `TreeDigest`) and prunes them.
- Unit (`src/fsx/prune.rs` tests): `LockUse::Own` refuses a journal whose lines are `prepared` + `step`; deletes one ending in `committed`; deletes one with a torn first line.
- Add a recovery failpoint `engine.recover.forward` at the top of `roll_forward` (`src/engine/journal.rs:564`) and list it in `FAILPOINTS` (`src/engine/tx.rs:62-87`; the DEC-7 test checks the list against the source) so the swapped-phase double fault is reproducible: `engine.record.written=error,engine.recover.forward=error`. README Safety model, Crash testing counts them ("All 24 engine failpoints"): update the number.
- Integration (`tests/engine_crash.rs`): a double-fault scenario through the binary, as in Steps to Reproduce, for install-over-local-edits and for `--force` over an unmanaged folder; assert the second command restores the original bytes.
- Undo (`tests/undo_history.rs` or `tests/engine_undo.rs`): an undo whose commit fails after the exchange with `engine.recover.step=error` keeps its journal and is finished by the next command.
- Crash matrix (`tests/engine_crash.rs`) must stay green: abort-based crashes never reach cleanup, so their behaviour is unchanged.

## Considerations

- Interaction with omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.2 and omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3: once failed recoveries keep their journals, a recovery that fails deterministically (today: a SavedVariables restore refused by the scope table, omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.2) would be retried and fail on every later command. omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3 makes roll-forward defer the SavedVariables restore instead of failing, and omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.2 stops planning out-of-scope restores; omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3 is therefore a dependency. omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9 limits any remaining stuck journal to its own target instead of blocking every target.
- Interaction with omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.11: both edit the `match committed` arms in `tx.rs`/`undo.rs`; omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.11 changes what `RolledForward` carries. Coordinate or land one after the other.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2 (removing snapshot dirs of transactions that never committed) relies on this bead: omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2 leaves both halves alone while a journal remains, which after this fix is exactly the case where recovery still needs them. omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.5 extends the crash matrices to failed recoveries; the double-fault tests of this bead's Test Plan can live in its matrices.
- Multi-target commands continue with the next target after one fails (`src/engine/tx.rs:357-386`); that next target's `recover_all` will try the kept journal again. With omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9 a failure there becomes a warning for the other target, not a second failure.
- Performance: reading the journal in cleanup is one small file read per transaction.
- Must not regress: own-transaction cleanup without the global lock (vision comment 282, `LockUse::Own`), dry runs and planning never taking the global lock, crash-matrix expectations.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.2`: Undo half-applies when WTF, Account or SavedVariables is symlinked out of the client
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3`: Recovery rolls an undo forward and writes SavedVariables while the game client runs
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2`: Snapshot dirs of rolled-back and failed transactions are never removed
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.11`: An in-process roll-forward reports atomic_swap true and drops atomic_swap_unavailable
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.5`: Close the crash-matrix gaps: Nth rename, undo, SavedVariables, failed recovery, snapshots
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9`: A leftover journal of one client makes changes on other clients fail with scope_denied
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.5`: Transaction journal: phases, step records and recovery under the lock
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.3`: Lock, revalidate and commit: the transaction driver

title: Lock holders outside the engine and no-op change commands never recover pending journals
description:
## Background

Vision §5.5: "Mutating commands recover right after acquiring the lock and report `journal_recovered`." README, Safety model, Interrupted runs: "The next command that commits a change (install, remove or undo) recovers under the lock first." The `journal_pending` warning: "the next command that changes addons recovers it" (`src/engine/journal.rs:433-439`). The code recovers in exactly two places, the engine's commit window (`src/engine/tx.rs:573-575`) and undo's (`src/engine/undo.rs:221-223`).

Verified at HEAD 53b54e6 (found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit):

- These take the global lock for a mutation and never recover: `config set` (`src/app/config.rs:286-297`), every `targets` change through `locked()` (`src/app/targets.rs:337-354`: add, rm at 427, rename, default), `auth github set|--from-gh|clear` (`src/app/auth.rs:278-289`), `export --write` (`src/app/export.rs:398-407`).
- A change command whose plan has no ops (everything already current, a pinned addon, a no-op sync) never takes the lock, so never recovers: `if req.dry_run || !plan.has_ops()` (`src/engine/tx.rs:341-346`; `has_ops` at `src/engine/plan.rs:431-435`). Undo dry runs return before the lock (`src/engine/undo.rs:174-176`).
- README's list "(install, remove or undo)" is also incomplete for the commands that do recover: `update`, `sync`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` and `copy` commit through the same engine.

Dry runs never recovering is by design (vision comment 282: planning and `--dry-run` never take the global lock) and stays.

User-visible consequence: an agent that sees `journal_pending` and runs an install of something already current, or changes a setting, leaves the journal pending although the warning said the next change would recover it; the documentation names the wrong set of commands.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (fresh `HOME` and `XDG_*`, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<empty dir>`), synthetic retail root, addon source folders `<src>/barpkg/Bar` and `<src>/pkg/Foo`.

1. `omaddons install file:<src>/barpkg -t retail` (Bar installed and current).
2. `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS='engine.swapped=abort' omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail` (Foo's journal is left in phase `swapped`).
3. `omaddons config set running_policy refuse` (takes the global lock).
4. `omaddons targets rename retail main` (takes the global lock).
5. `omaddons install file:<src>/barpkg -t main` (Bar unchanged: the plan is empty).
6. Expected: the first of steps 3-5 reports `journal_recovered` and the journal is gone.
7. Actual (reproduced 2026-10-18): step 3 prints `set running_policy = "refuse"`, step 4 `renamed retail to main`, step 5 `main: Bar unchanged (2)` with a `journal_pending` warning that says "the next command that changes addons recovers it"; after each, `<state>/omaddons/journal/` still holds the journal.

## Technical Approach

Decided: every global-lock acquisition made for a mutation recovers first; a change command that ends up with nothing to commit takes the lock only when there is something to recover; documentation states the rule exactly.

1. One entry point. With omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9's `RecoveryEnv`, expose `engine::journal::recover_under(guard, paths, own: &[TargetKey], sv_writable)` returning `(Vec<Warning>, Vec<Warning>)` (recovered, still pending). Non-engine callers pass `own = &[]` and `sv_writable = |_| false` (they run no discovery, so SavedVariables are always deferred, omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3).
2. Call it right after the lock in `config set` (`src/app/config.rs:290`), `targets` `locked()` (`src/app/targets.rs:345`), `auth` `write()` (`src/app/auth.rs:283`) and `export --write` (`src/app/export.rs:401`), and add its warnings to each outcome. A recovery failure there is a warning, never the command's failure: these commands touch neither AddOns nor target records, and omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9 already turns other targets' failures into `journal_pending`.
3. No-op change commands. In `run()` (`src/engine/tx.rs:341-346`), when `!req.dry_run && !plan.has_ops()` and `journal::pending(paths)` lists a journal whose in-flight lock is free, take the lock, recover (own = the request's targets), release, and put the warnings in `TxOutcomes.warnings`. D24 holds: the lock is still taken only for a commit window (here: recovery's), and only when something is pending.
4. `retain()` and `BlobCache::evict` take the lock only to prune; they do not recover (they run right after a commit that already did).
5. Texts:
   - `journal_pending` message (`src/engine/journal.rs:433-439`): "transaction {tx} on target {key} did not finish; the next omaddons command that changes addons, settings or targets recovers it (dry runs never do)".
   - README Safety model, Interrupted runs: "The next command that changes something recovers under the global lock first: install, update, sync, pin, unpin, adopt, copy, remove and undo (also when they turn out to change nothing), `config set`, `targets add`, `rm`, `rename` and `default`, `auth github set` and `clear`, and `export --write`. Dry runs and read commands never recover." Concurrency bullet: the lock is also held briefly by `auth github` and `export --write`.
   - README "`journal_pending` that does not clear": the same list.
6. Record on omad-vision-8qa (§5.5 Journal phases and recovery: the exact set of recovering commands).

Rejected alternatives:
- Narrowing the documentation to the engine commands only: leaves journals pending through `config`/`targets` use for no reason; recovery under those locks is cheap and safe once scopes come from the journal (omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9).
- Taking the lock on every no-op change command: costs a lock wait on every repeat install; doing it only when a journal is pending keeps the common case lock-free.
- A dedicated `recover` command: doctor (M4) owns repairs; this bead stays within M1/M2.

Contract: changed behaviour and texts; no new codes. `journal_recovered` can now appear on `config set`, `targets`, `auth` and `export --write`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of steps 3, 4 and 5, run as the first command after step 2 (a fresh scenario each), reports `journal_recovered` and leaves `journal/` empty; step 5 still reports Bar unchanged.
- `config set` under a journal that cannot be recovered succeeds with a `journal_pending` warning naming the reason.
- `--dry-run` of any of these commands leaves the journal and takes no lock.
- README and the warning text list exactly the recovering commands; vision comment recorded.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Integration (`tests/journal.rs` or a new section in `tests/cli_config.rs`, `tests/targets.rs`, `tests/auth.rs`, `tests/export.rs`): leave a journal with `engine.swapped=abort`, run each command, assert `journal_recovered` and an empty `journal/`.
- Integration (`tests/install.rs`): a no-op install recovers a pending journal; a no-op install without journals takes no lock (hold the lock from the test with `GlobalLock::acquire` and assert the no-op still returns at once).
- `tests/engine_concurrency.rs::recovery_happens_only_under_the_lock` stays green.

## Considerations

- Depends on omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9: without per-journal scopes, recovery under `config set` (whose scope table has no client dirs) would fail with `scope_denied` for every journal.
- Depends on omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3: recovery here cannot detect running clients, so it must defer SavedVariables.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.12 makes the same outputs drop the stale `journal_pending` of a journal they just recovered.
- `targets rm` of a target with a pending journal: recovery runs first; if it cannot recover, the journal stays and is still recoverable later through the client's marker (omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9), even with the registry entry gone.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1`: A failed in-process recovery deletes the journal and the stage dir holding the old folders
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.12`: Change commands report journal_pending for the journal they just recovered
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.5`: Transaction journal: phases, step records and recovery under the lock
acceptance_criteria: config set, targets add/rm/rename/default, auth github set/--from-gh/clear and export --write recover pending journals right after taking the global lock and report journal_recovered (a recovery failure there is a journal_pending warning, not a failure); a change command whose plan is empty takes the lock to recover only when a recoverable journal is pending; dry runs never recover; README and the journal_pending text name exactly which commands recover; argc gate passes
close_reason: Every command that takes the global lock to change something recovers pending journals first, a change command with nothing to commit recovers when a journal waits, and README and the journal_pending text name exactly those commands.

Non-engine callers can pass own: &[] and their own scope table (no client dirs): every journal they meet is then foreign, so a failure only warns.

title: An in-process roll-forward reports atomic_swap true and drops atomic_swap_unavailable
description:
## Background

README, Safety model: "On filesystems without `renameat2` exchange (NTFS through ntfs-3g, some FUSE mounts), omaddons falls back to two journaled renames per folder and reports `atomic_swap: false` with an `atomic_swap_unavailable` warning." Vision D25: "`atomic_swap: false` keeps the claim honest where unsupported." The swap computes this in `SwapReport` (`src/engine/swap.rs:341-345`, warning at `src/engine/swap.rs:420-431`).

Verified at HEAD 53b54e6 (found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit):

- When the commit fails after `swapped` and the in-process recovery rolls it forward, the outcome is built from a constant: `Some(RecoveryAction::RolledForward) => (true, Vec::new())` (`src/engine/tx.rs:808-815`, line 812) and the same in undo (`src/engine/undo.rs:336-342`, line 339). The real report is lost with the closure's error.

User-visible consequence: on exactly the filesystems where the swap was not atomic, an update that hit a late error (and was completed by recovery) claims `atomic_swap: true` and omits `atomic_swap_unavailable`, so an agent believes the "wholly old or wholly new at every instant" invariant held.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (fresh `HOME` and `XDG_*`, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<empty dir>`), synthetic retail root, addon source folder `<src>/pkg/Foo`.

1. `omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail`, then put Foo 2 in `<src>/pkg`.
2. Control: in a second identical environment, `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS='fsx.renameat2.einval' omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail --json` → `data.atomic_swap: false`, warnings `["atomic_swap_unavailable"]`.
3. `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS='fsx.renameat2.einval,engine.record.written=error' omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail --json` (the swap used two renames per folder; the commit fails after `swapped`; recovery rolls it forward in process).
4. Expected: `ok: true`, `atomic_swap: false`, `atomic_swap_unavailable`.
5. Actual (reproduced 2026-10-18): `ok: true`, item `updated`, `data.atomic_swap: true`, `warnings: []`; Foo 2 is live and history has the update.

## Technical Approach

Decided fix: derive the report from the journal, which is authoritative for what the swap did.

1. `recover_tx` (`src/engine/journal.rs:478-491`) returns, with `RolledForward`, whether the transaction's steps include a plain rename: `atomic_swap = !parsed.steps.iter().any(|s| s.op == StepOp::Rename)` (`StepOp::Rename` is recorded only by the fallback, `src/engine/swap.rs:440-452`; a flagged attempt that hit `EINVAL` is journaled as `noreplace`/`exchange` and then a `rename`). Shape: `RecoveryAction::RolledForward { atomic_swap: bool }`, or a small `Recovered { action, atomic_swap }` struct; `recover_one`'s message is unchanged.
2. In `locked()` (`src/engine/tx.rs:808-815`) and the undo `commit()` (`src/engine/undo.rs:336-342`), build `(atomic_swap, warnings)` from it: when `atomic_swap` is false, push the same `atomic_swap_unavailable` warning the swap emits. Move that warning's construction into one function in `src/engine/swap.rs` (e.g. `pub(super) fn atomic_swap_unavailable() -> Warning`) used by both the swap and this path, so the text cannot drift.
3. Rejected: capturing the `SwapReport` in a variable outside the closure. It is lost when the error happens inside `swap()` after `mark_swapped` (the `engine.swapped` failpoint, `src/engine/swap.rs:339-340`), while the journal always knows.

Contract: none (the outcome becomes truthful; fields and codes unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Steps to Reproduce step 3 reports `atomic_swap: false` and `atomic_swap_unavailable`.
- With flags supported, an in-process roll-forward still reports `atomic_swap: true` and no warning.
- An undo rolled forward in process on a fallback filesystem reports the same as the install.
- The warning text exists once in the code.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/tx.rs` tests, `TxScene`): `with_spec("fsx.renameat2.einval,engine.record.written=error", ...)` on an update → `atomic_swap == false`, one `AtomicSwapUnavailable`; `with_spec("engine.record.written=error", ...)` → `true`, none; also `engine.swapped=error` with fallback (report lost inside `swap()`).
- Unit (`src/engine/undo.rs` tests): the undo equivalent.
- Integration (`tests/engine_fallbacks.rs`): the Steps to Reproduce through the binary.

## Considerations

- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1 rewrites the error arm of the same `match` (keep the journal when recovery fails); land the two together or rebase one on the other.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3 makes roll-forward return warnings (`saved_variables_deferred`); this bead's return value should carry them in the same struct.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1`: A failed in-process recovery deletes the journal and the stage dir holding the old folders
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3`: Recovery rolls an undo forward and writes SavedVariables while the game client runs
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.11`: Per-folder atomic swaps with snapshots, SavedVariables reflink snapshots and fallback
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.3`: Lock, revalidate and commit: the transaction driver
acceptance_criteria: after an in-process roll-forward the outcome's atomic_swap is false and atomic_swap_unavailable is present whenever the journal recorded a plain rename, true otherwise; same for undo; argc gate passes
close_reason: A transaction completed by the in-process roll-forward reports atomic_swap from its journal and keeps atomic_swap_unavailable on fallback filesystems.

title: Change commands report journal_pending for the journal they just recovered
description:
## Background

Vision §5.5: "Read commands never recover. They list `journal/` ... and add the warning `journal_pending` ... Mutating commands recover right after acquiring the lock and report `journal_recovered`." `World::load` says the same in its comment: "Unfinished transactions, reported without recovering (D23). A mutating command recovers them under the lock and reports `journal_recovered` instead." (`src/app/world.rs:105-107`). "Instead" does not hold.

Found while reproducing omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3 for the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit; verified at HEAD 53b54e6:

- `World::load` adds `journal::pending_warnings(&paths)` to `world.warnings` before the command does anything (`src/app/world.rs:107`).
- The mutating commands start their outcome warnings from `world.warnings.clone()` (`src/app/install.rs:414`, `src/app/update.rs:131`, `src/app/sync.rs:585`, `src/app/pin.rs:133`, `src/app/adopt.rs:470`, `src/app/copy.rs:172`, `src/app/remove.rs:255`) and then add the engine's `journal_recovered` (`TxOutcomes.warnings`, `src/engine/tx.rs:376`).

User-visible consequence: one envelope says both "transaction X ... did not finish; the next command that changes addons recovers it" (`journal_pending`) and "transaction X ... was interrupted; recovery completed it" (`journal_recovered`). An agent following the warnings cannot tell whether X is still pending and may run another command, or `status`, to "recover" it.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (fresh `HOME` and `XDG_*`, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<empty dir>`), synthetic retail root, addon source folders `<src>/pkg/Foo` and `<src>/barpkg/Bar`.

1. `omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail`
2. Change Foo in `<src>/pkg`; `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS='engine.swapped=abort' omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail` (journal left).
3. `omaddons install file:<src>/barpkg -t retail --json`
4. Expected: `warnings` holds `journal_recovered` for the tx, and no `journal_pending`.
5. Actual (reproduced 2026-10-18): `warnings` holds `journal_pending` for the tx (and the same stderr event) followed by `journal_recovered` for the same tx.

## Technical Approach

Decided: a mutating command's journal warnings describe the state when it finishes.

1. Add one helper beside the World (e.g. `World::settle_journal_warnings(&self, warnings: &mut Vec<Warning>) -> Result<()>` in `src/app/world.rs`): remove every `JournalPending` and `TxInProgress` warning, then append a fresh `journal::pending_warnings(&self.paths)?` (a directory listing plus a non-blocking lock probe, `src/engine/journal.rs:416-443`).
2. Call it in each mutating command after its engine runs and before building the outcome: install, update, sync, pin/unpin, adopt, copy, remove (the call sites above). `undo` builds its warnings without `world.warnings` (`src/app/undo.rs:442-536`) and needs nothing; read commands are unchanged.
3. The stderr NDJSON stream: if world warnings are emitted as events when the World loads, keep that (it was true at that moment); the final envelope is what this bead corrects. If the renderer emits warnings only from the envelope, nothing else changes.

Rejected alternatives:
- Filtering by matching the tx id inside messages: warnings carry no structured tx field, and parsing messages is brittle.
- Skipping `pending_warnings` in `World::load` for mutating commands: a dry run or a no-op run would then hide pending journals it does not recover.

Contract: behaviour change only (fewer contradictory warnings); no codes or keys change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Steps to Reproduce: the envelope has `journal_recovered` and no `journal_pending` for that tx.
- A journal that the run could not recover (another target's, omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9) is still reported as `journal_pending`.
- A dry run with a pending journal still reports `journal_pending`.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Integration (`tests/journal.rs` or `tests/install.rs`): the Steps to Reproduce through the binary; assert the warning codes per tx.
- Integration: the same for `remove` and `update` (one case each), and a `--dry-run` case keeping `journal_pending`.

## Considerations

- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10 adds recovery to `config set`, `targets`, `auth` and `export --write`; those outcomes do not start from `world.warnings` today, but if omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10 adds world warnings to them, call the same helper.
- The extra `pending_warnings` call costs a `read_dir` of `journal/` and a lock probe per mutating command.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10`: Lock holders outside the engine and no-op change commands never recover pending journals
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9`: A leftover journal of one client makes changes on other clients fail with scope_denied
