title: Undo half-applies when WTF, Account or SavedVariables is symlinked out of the client
description:
## Background

README (Safety model, Undo): "Only the touched addons' own files (`WTF/…/SavedVariables/<Folder>.lua` and `.lua.bak`, account-wide and per character) are snapshotted ... On undo, a file that is unchanged since is left alone, a changed one is restored". The write-scope table (vision §5.5) admits the `Undo` writer only on `<client dir>/WTF/Account/**/SavedVariables/<owned folder>.lua[.bak]`. Players do keep `WTF/` (or one account's folder) in a sync folder and symlink it into the client. omaddons then snapshots those files but can never restore them, and the failure lands in the worst place.

Verified at HEAD 53b54e6 (found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit):

- Snapshot reads through the symlink: `sv_candidates()` (`src/engine/swap.rs:169-214`) uses `read_dir` on `wtf.join("Account")` and on each `SavedVariables` dir, which follows a symlinked `WTF`, `Account` or `SavedVariables` directory; `CloneFile { from }` only scope-checks the destination (`src/engine/swap.rs:134-148`). (An `Account/<acct>`, realm or character directory that is itself a symlink is silently skipped instead, because `dirs()` keeps only real directories: `src/engine/swap.rs:516-540`.)
- Restore writes the canonical path: `restore_one()` renames a staged clone onto `client.wtf().join(rel)` (`src/engine/undo.rs:1176-1211`). `mutate()` normalizes both paths by canonicalizing the parent (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:249-262`, `normalize` at `src/fsx/mutate.rs:442-466`), so the destination becomes `<sync folder>/WTF/Account/...`. The scope table matches canonical paths against canonical client dirs only (`client_components`, `src/fsx/scope.rs:405-446` and `505-509`), so the path is "outside every write scope" (`src/fsx/scope.rs:323-328`): `scope_denied`.
- The restore runs after the journal reached `swapped`: `swap()` ends with `mark_swapped` (`src/engine/swap.rs:339`), then `restore_saved_variables` (`src/engine/undo.rs:300-303`). The in-process recovery rolls forward, and roll-forward retries the SavedVariables restore first (`src/engine/journal.rs:573-578`), which fails identically; with omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1 the journal is then deleted.
- The error text is false: "a SavedVariables file could not be restored; the next omaddons command that changes addons finishes the undo" (`src/engine/undo.rs:1163-1169`).

User-visible consequence: `undo` exits 4 `scope_denied`; the addon folders are already reverted on disk, but the record, files index and history line are never written (`list` shows the addon as installed with its folder missing, history has no undo line), the undo's own snapshot (holding the folders it swapped out and a clone of the current SavedVariables) is orphaned, and repeating `undo` fails the same way forever.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (fresh `HOME` and `XDG_*`, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<empty dir>`), synthetic retail Battle.net root under `$HOME/Games/WoW`; addon source folder `<src>/pkg/Foo/Foo.toc`.

1. Move `<client>/WTF` to `<sync>/WTF` and `ln -s <sync>/WTF <client>/WTF`.
2. `echo 'FooDB = { v = 0 }' > <client>/WTF/Account/<acct>/SavedVariables/Foo.lua`
3. `omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail` (the snapshot holds `Foo.lua`, read through the symlink).
4. `echo 'FooDB = { v = 1 }' > <client>/WTF/Account/<acct>/SavedVariables/Foo.lua` (the game wrote it).
5. `omaddons undo --json`
6. Expected: Foo is removed and `Foo.lua` is either restored or explicitly left alone with a warning; history gains the undo line.
7. Actual (reproduced 2026-10-18): exit 4 `scope_denied`, message "...the next omaddons command that changes addons finishes the undo"; `Interface/AddOns` is empty; `Foo.lua` still says `v = 1`; `<state>/omaddons/journal/` is empty; `list` shows `Foo 1 ... missing Foo`; `history` shows only the install; `Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<undo tx>/` holds `AddOns/Foo`, a `WTF/` clone and two `sv-restore/<attempt>/` clones that nothing references.

## Technical Approach

Decided policy: SavedVariables are protected only inside the client's own directory tree. A SavedVariables directory that resolves outside the canonical client dir is out of scope up front: no snapshot, no restore attempt, and a warning that counts (never names) the affected files. The fsx scope table is not widened.

1. In `src/engine/swap.rs`, replace the walk in `sv_candidates()` with a resolver (e.g. `sv_dirs(client) -> SvDirs { dirs: Vec<(rel, path)>, out_of_scope_files: usize }`) that:
   - enumerates `WTF/Account/<acct>/` and `WTF/Account/<acct>/<realm>/<char>/` following symlinks (so a symlinked account or character directory is no longer skipped silently);
   - for each candidate `SavedVariables` directory, canonicalizes it and keeps it only if it starts with the canonicalized client dir (`std::fs::canonicalize(client.client_dir())`); this single test catches a symlink at any level, `WTF` itself included, and lets a symlink that stays inside the client (one character's folder pointing at another's) keep working because fsx accepts its canonical path;
   - de-duplicates kept directories by canonical path (two names for one directory are snapshotted once);
   - counts, for each excluded directory, the existing files that would have been candidates (`<Folder>.lua`, `<Folder>.lua.bak` of the touched folders, case-insensitive as today).
   `sv_candidates()` keeps its signature for callers but works from the kept directories only. Manifest paths stay relative to `WTF/` exactly as today.
2. `snapshot_saved_variables()` (`src/engine/swap.rs:112-164`) returns the out-of-scope count in `SvReport` (new field `sv_files_out_of_scope: usize`, serialized like the others: counts only). `locked()` (`src/engine/tx.rs:773-774`) and the undo commit (`src/engine/undo.rs:298`) turn a non-zero count into the warning below. Snapshot runs under the lock after `prepared`, so the warning joins the outcome's warnings after commit.
3. Undo planning (`plan_saved_variables`, `src/engine/undo.rs:1086-1140`) applies the same test to each manifest entry of an existing snapshot (snapshots taken before this fix can contain entries read through a symlink): an entry whose live parent directory does not canonicalize inside the client dir is neither compared nor restored, and is counted for the warning. This guarantees the post-`swapped` restore only ever sees in-scope paths, so the omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.2 failure cannot recur from old snapshots.
4. Warning: new code `saved_variables_out_of_scope` (`src/error.rs` WarningCode registry, beside `saved_variables_deferred` at `src/error.rs:246`). Message, never naming a file or directory: `"{n} SavedVariables files of {target id}'s changed addons are in a WTF folder reached through a symlink outside the client directory, so they were not snapshotted and undo will not restore them"` (undo variant: `"...so undo left them as they are"`). Fix: `Suggestion::text("omaddons protects SavedVariables only inside the client's own WTF folder; keep WTF/ there (not a symlink to a sync folder) for undo to restore them")`. Emitted only when the count is non-zero, so a new addon without SavedVariables yet does not warn on every install.
5. Replace the false message at `src/engine/undo.rs:1166` with one that is true whatever happens next: `"a SavedVariables file could not be restored"`, fix `omaddons status`. (With omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3, roll-forward defers a failing restore rather than failing, and omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1 keeps the journal, so the user then gets `saved_variables_deferred` with the follow-up command.)

Rejected alternatives:
- Widening the fsx scope through symlinks (matching the non-canonical path, or adding the symlink target as a scope root): the scope table's guarantee is "anything else is refused" on canonical paths; following a user-controlled symlink would let the Undo writer write wherever a link points (another client's WTF, a sync folder shared with other machines, anywhere).
- Snapshotting through the symlink and refusing only at undo time: the snapshot is useless and the user learns at undo time; deciding up front is cheaper and honest.
- Refusing installs on such clients: SavedVariables snapshots are a safety net for undo, not a precondition for changing addons.

Contract (DEC-4, allowed before the M4 freeze): new warning code `saved_variables_out_of_scope`; `SvReport` gains `sv_files_out_of_scope` (internal report, counts only). README: add the warning row to the "Every warning code" table in the README Exit codes section (beside `saved_variables_deferred`, and bump the count in its summary), and extend Safety model, Undo, SavedVariables: "SavedVariables directories that lead outside the client directory through a symlink (a `WTF/` kept in a sync folder) are never snapshotted or written; `saved_variables_out_of_scope` counts the files undo cannot restore." Record on omad-vision-8qa as a comment (§5.5 Undo and write-scope table: "SavedVariables are snapshotted and restored only where their canonical path is inside the client dir").

## Acceptance Criteria

- With `WTF/` symlinked outside the client: install and update snapshot no SavedVariables from it, and warn `saved_variables_out_of_scope` with the file count when the touched addons have files there; no file or account/realm/character name appears in any output.
- Undo of such a transaction succeeds (exit 0), reverts the folders, writes record, index and history, leaves the SavedVariables untouched, and warns `saved_variables_out_of_scope`.
- Undo of a snapshot taken before the fix (manifest entries read through the symlink) also succeeds and skips those entries at plan time; nothing fails after `swapped`.
- A symlink that stays inside the client (a character's `SavedVariables/` pointing at another character's) is still snapshotted and restored, once.
- A symlinked `Account/<acct>` directory leading outside counts toward the warning instead of being skipped silently.
- The restore error message no longer claims the next command finishes the undo.
- README and vision comment updated; `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/swap.rs` tests, `Scene`): the resolver keeps in-client directories, drops a `WTF` symlinked to a sibling temp dir, drops a symlinked account dir, de-duplicates an in-client character symlink, counts out-of-scope files; `SvReport` serialization contains no private names.
- Unit (`src/engine/undo.rs` tests, `TxScene`): a manifest entry whose live parent resolves outside is skipped by `plan_saved_variables` and counted.
- Integration (`tests/undo_history.rs`, its `Session` helper): install, symlink-move `WTF`, play, undo: exit 0, `saved_variables_out_of_scope` present, history has the undo line, `list` shows the addon gone. A second scenario symlinks `WTF` after the install (old-style manifest) and asserts the same.
- `tests/fsx_scope.rs`: unchanged expectations (the scope table is not widened); add a case that a canonical path outside the client is still refused for `Writer::Undo`.

## Considerations

- omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1 moves the SavedVariables snapshot before the lock (`prestage_saved_variables` / `finish_saved_variables`, both enumerating `sv_candidates`) and makes undo restore by exchange. Put this bead's in-scope test inside the shared enumeration so both phases apply it; whichever lands second adapts to the other.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.8 (case-insensitive WTF/Account/SavedVariables) changes the same resolver; it depends on this bead and reuses `saved_variables_out_of_scope` for the "two spellings" case.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3 makes roll-forward defer a SavedVariables restore that fails for any other reason (for example a symlink created between planning and restore), so the journal can always finish the folder and record part.
- Canonicalizing each SavedVariables directory costs a few `realpath` calls per account and character; negligible beside hashing the files.
- The client dir itself may be reached through `dosdevices` symlinks; compare canonical with canonical (as `ScopeTable::new` does, `src/fsx/scope.rs:217-247`), never the raw path.
- Must not regress: SavedVariables snapshot/restore on ordinary clients (`tests/engine_fallbacks.rs::without_reflinks_saved_variables_are_byte_copied_and_undo_restores_them`, `tests/undo_history.rs::saved_variables_while_the_client_runs_and_after`), and the rule that SavedVariables errors never name files.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1`: A failed in-process recovery deletes the journal and the stage dir holding the old folders
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3`: Recovery rolls an undo forward and writes SavedVariables while the game client runs
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1`: The global lock is held for seconds when SavedVariables or undone folders are large
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.8`: SavedVariables under a lowercase wtf/ or account/ are never snapshotted or restored
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.12`: Undo: revert transactions with conflict detection and the SavedVariables policy
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.11`: Per-folder atomic swaps with snapshots, SavedVariables reflink snapshots and fallback
acceptance_criteria: SavedVariables directories whose canonical path is outside the canonical client dir are never snapshotted and never restored; a saved_variables_out_of_scope warning counts the affected files without naming any; undo of a snapshot taken before the fix skips such entries at plan time and never fails after swapped; the restore error text no longer promises a recovery that cannot happen; README and the warning table document it; argc gate passes
close_reason: SavedVariables dirs resolving outside the client are never snapshotted or written; saved_variables_out_of_scope counts the files; undo skips such manifest entries at plan time and succeeds

title: Recovery rolls an undo forward and writes SavedVariables while the game client runs
description:
## Background

README, Safety model, Running clients: "**SavedVariables are never written while the client runs**, under any policy or flag, because the game rewrites them on logout." Vision §5.5 Undo: "SavedVariables are never written while the target's client runs, under any policy or flag." A live undo honours this (`plan_saved_variables`, `src/engine/undo.rs:1116-1138`: `auto` defers, `restore` refuses with `game_running`). Recovery does not.

Verified at HEAD 53b54e6 (found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit):

- An undo's journal payload carries `sv_restore` (`src/engine/undo.rs:260-279`), planned while the client was not running.
- If the undo is interrupted after `swapped` and before its SavedVariables restore (crash between `src/engine/swap.rs:339` and `src/engine/undo.rs:301-303`), the journal stays in phase `swapped`.
- The next lock holder recovers it: `recover_all` runs right after the global lock in every engine commit (`src/engine/tx.rs:573-575`, `src/engine/undo.rs:221-223`), for any change on that client, including adding an unrelated addon, which the default `safe` running policy allows while the game runs.
- `roll_forward()` restores the SavedVariables unconditionally, first thing (`src/engine/journal.rs:573-578`); recovery has no notion of a running client at all (`recover_all`/`recover_parsed`, `src/engine/journal.rs:460-561`).
- It then appends the payload's prebuilt history line, whose `sv_deferred` is `false` (`src/engine/undo.rs:244-259`), so nothing remembers that the files were written under a running client.

User-visible consequence: the game overwrites the restored files on logout, so the restore silently does not take effect; the undo's history line says it was complete (no `sv_deferred`), so the follow-up `undo <tx> --saved-variables restore` is refused as "already undone" and the user never gets the command that would bring the pre-transaction settings back. The README's "never, under any policy or flag" promise is broken.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (fresh `HOME` and `XDG_*`, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<proc>` an empty dir), synthetic retail Battle.net root under `$HOME/Games/WoW`; addon sources `<src>/pkg/Foo` and `<src>/barpkg/Bar`.

1. `echo 'FooDB = { v = 0 }' > <client>/WTF/Account/<acct>/SavedVariables/Foo.lua`
2. `omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail`
3. `echo 'FooDB = { v = 1, played = true }' > .../Foo.lua` (the game wrote it).
4. `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS='engine.swapped=abort' omaddons undo` (crash after `swapped`, before the restore; the game is not running, so the restore was planned). Foo is gone from AddOns, `Foo.lua` still `v = 1`, one journal left.
5. Start the "game": `mkdir <proc>/4242; printf 'WoW.exe\n' > <proc>/4242/comm; printf '%s\0' <client>/WoW.exe > <proc>/4242/cmdline; : > <proc>/4242/environ`. `omaddons status` now shows retail `running`.
6. `omaddons install file:<src>/barpkg -t retail` (adding a folder is allowed under `safe`).
7. Expected: the undo is finished for folders and records, `Foo.lua` is left as it is, history marks the undo `sv_deferred`, and a `saved_variables_deferred` warning carries `omaddons undo <install tx> --saved-variables restore`.
8. Actual (reproduced 2026-10-18): `journal_recovered ... recovery completed it (rolled forward)`, `reload_required` (the client is running), and `Foo.lua` is back to `FooDB = { v = 0 }` while the client runs; no `saved_variables_deferred`.

## Technical Approach

Decided fix: recovery writes SavedVariables only when it can show the client is not running; otherwise it defers them exactly as a live `--saved-variables auto` undo does. A restore that fails for any reason is also deferred, never a recovery failure.

1. Recovery input. Give `recover_all` and `recover_tx` (`src/engine/journal.rs:460-491`) a predicate `sv_writable: &dyn Fn(&Path) -> bool` (or a small `RecoveryEnv` struct carrying it; omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9 adds per-journal scopes to the same struct). It answers, for a journal's `prepared.client_dir`, "SavedVariables may be written now". Callers:
   - `locked()` (`src/engine/tx.rs:575`) and the undo `commit()` (`src/engine/undo.rs:223`): `|dir| known.contains(dir) && !running.contains(dir)` where `running = running_now(ctx, &known)` (`src/engine/tx.rs:424-429`) is computed once under the lock over `known`, the targets this command discovered. Add `known_targets: &'a [Target]` to `EngineCtx` (`src/engine/tx.rs:119-149`), filled in `app/engine.rs` (`Engine::new`, `src/app/engine.rs:52-87`) from `World::resolved` (every discovered target), and from `req.targets` in tests. Compare client dirs canonically. A client dir that matches no discovered target answers `false` (deferred): a false "running" only defers; a false "not running" would break the promise.
   - In-process `recover_tx` in `locked()`/`commit()` uses the same predicate.
   - Callers without discovery (omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10's `config set`, `auth`, ...): `|_| false`.
2. `roll_forward()` (`src/engine/journal.rs:564-620`): when `commit.sv_restore` is `Some(sv)`:
   - if `sv_writable(&prepared.client_dir)` is true, run `restore_saved_variables` as today; if it returns an error, treat it like a running client (step below) instead of returning the error, and keep the error's message (it never names files) for the warning;
   - otherwise skip the restore.
   When skipped or failed, append a copy of `commit.history` with `sv_deferred = true` instead of the prebuilt line, and return a `saved_variables_deferred` warning: message `"transaction {tx} on target {key} was recovered while its game client was running (or its SavedVariables could not be written), so {n} SavedVariables files were left as they are"`, fix `omaddons undo <sv.from> --saved-variables restore` (the same argv shape as `src/engine/undo.rs:463-480`). Make roll-forward return its warnings (`Result<Vec<Warning>>`) and have `recover_one` (`src/engine/journal.rs:494-520`) append them after `journal_recovered`; the in-process path in `commit()` adds them to the undo outcome.
3. Idempotence: the history presence check (`src/engine/journal.rs:608-618`) stays keyed on the tx id, so a roll-forward that crashes after appending the deferred line does not append again; a partially restored set of files is fine because the follow-up restore skips files already back (`src/engine/undo.rs:1156-1161`).
4. The follow-up works unchanged: `plan()` finds the deferred undo by `sv_deferred` (`src/engine/undo.rs:417-425`) and runs a SavedVariables-only undo.
5. Documentation: README Safety model, Interrupted runs: add "An interrupted undo whose SavedVariables restore had not run yet restores them during recovery only when the client is not running; otherwise recovery leaves them and warns `saved_variables_deferred` with the command to run after quitting." Record on omad-vision-8qa (§5.5 Journal phases and recovery and comment 289's "re-applied idempotently by roll-forward": "only when the client is not running; otherwise deferred with sv_deferred").

Rejected alternatives:
- Refusing recovery (`game_running`) while the client runs: every change command on that client would fail until the game exits, and the folder half of the undo would stay unfinished; deferring finishes everything except the part that must wait.
- Detecting running clients inside `journal.rs` itself from the registry: the registry has no exe names or prefixes (`src/state/registry.rs:33-47`); detection needs discovered `Target`s, which the command already has.
- Writing the restore anyway and adding a warning: still breaks "never written while the client runs".

Contract (DEC-4, allowed before the M4 freeze): `journal_recovered` may now be accompanied by `saved_variables_deferred` from recovery; a recovered undo's history line may carry `sv_deferred: true`. No new codes. `EngineCtx` gains `known_targets` (internal).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Steps to Reproduce end with `Foo.lua` unchanged (`v = 1`), the undo's history line carrying `sv_deferred: true`, and a `saved_variables_deferred` warning whose `fix_argv` is `["omaddons","undo","<install tx>","--saved-variables","restore"]`.
- After the fake process is removed, that follow-up restores `Foo.lua` to `v = 0`.
- With the client not running, recovery restores the SavedVariables as today (no `sv_deferred`).
- A recovery whose SavedVariables restore fails (a new engine failpoint `engine.recover.sv`, hit right before roll-forward restores SavedVariables and listed in `FAILPOINTS`, `src/engine/tx.rs:62-87`, armed `=error`; update the "All 24 engine failpoints" count in README Crash testing) still finishes folders, record, index and history with `sv_deferred: true` and the warning; the journal is pruned.
- Recovery of a journal whose client the command did not discover defers the SavedVariables.
- README and vision comment updated; `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/journal.rs` tests): a prepared+swapped undo journal with `sv_restore`; `recover_all` with `sv_writable = |_| false` leaves the live file, appends one history line with `sv_deferred`, returns `journal_recovered` and `saved_variables_deferred`; with `|_| true` it restores; with `engine.recover.sv=error` it defers.
- Integration (`tests/undo_history.rs`, `Session` with `home.retail_running()`): the Steps to Reproduce through the binary, then the follow-up after the client stops.
- Crash suite (`tests/engine_crash.rs`): the undo crash points after `swapped` with a running client recover to the deferred state.
- Concurrency: none new.

## Considerations

- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.5 (running detection that fails open on an unreadable `/proc`) decides what `running_now` returns; this bead's predicate trusts it, so when omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.5 makes detection fail closed, recovery defers in exactly those cases too.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1 changes how the restore itself works (prestaged copies, exchange under the lock); the running check and the defer-on-failure rule here wrap whichever `restore_saved_variables` exists, so the two compose.
- With omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1 (failed recoveries keep their journals) a deterministic restore failure would otherwise block every later command; deferring on failure makes roll-forward unable to get stuck on SavedVariables, so land this with or before omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.7 must pin the reverted transaction's snapshot while a deferred restore is pending; recovery-created `sv_deferred` lines are pending restores like live ones.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10 adds recovery to `config set`, `targets` and `auth`, which have no discovery: they pass `|_| false`, so SavedVariables are always deferred there.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9 changes the same `recover_all` signature (per-journal scopes); implement both through one `RecoveryEnv` to avoid two signature churns.
- Running detection costs one `/proc` scan per lock window, already done for the command's own targets (`src/engine/tx.rs:595`); reuse it.
- Must not regress: the live undo's `auto`/`restore`/`keep` behaviour and messages, roll-forward idempotence (`tests/journal.rs::a_roll_forward_interrupted_after_writing_state_does_not_repeat_it`).

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1`: A failed in-process recovery deletes the journal and the stage dir holding the old folders
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.2`: Undo half-applies when WTF, Account or SavedVariables is symlinked out of the client
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1`: The global lock is held for seconds when SavedVariables or undone folders are large
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10`: Lock holders outside the engine and no-op change commands never recover pending journals
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.5`: Running detection fails open: an unreadable /proc makes every client look not running
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.7`: Retention can prune the snapshot a deferred SavedVariables restore still needs
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9`: A leftover journal of one client makes changes on other clients fail with scope_denied
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.12`: Undo: revert transactions with conflict detection and the SavedVariables policy
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.5`: Transaction journal: phases, step records and recovery under the lock

title: Recovery after a reboot stops: journal steps compare st_dev, which btrfs and FUSE renumber
description:
## Background

The journal exists for crashes, and the commonest crash is a power loss followed by a reboot. README, Safety model, Interrupted runs: "Each step records the device and inode of both paths, so rollback reverses a rename only if it actually happened." Vision comment 225 (from 6.5): "Journal step lines carry `from_id`/`to_id` ({dev, ino} or null) ... Recovery decides whether a step ran from them." The device number is not stable across mounts on the filesystems omaddons targets first.

Verified at HEAD 53b54e6 (found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit):

- `FileId { dev, ino }` from `symlink_metadata` (`src/engine/journal.rs:159-174`), recorded before each rename by `Journal::step` (`src/engine/journal.rs:238-251`).
- `ran()` compares the whole `(Option<FileId>, Option<FileId>)` pair, dev included, against the before and after states; anything else is `internal` "matches neither its before nor its after state; leaving it for manual repair" (`src/engine/journal.rs:637-656`).
- That error aborts `recover_all` (`src/engine/journal.rs:460-473`), which every engine commit runs right after taking the lock (`src/engine/tx.rs:575`, `src/engine/undo.rs:223`), so every change command fails (on every target until omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9 isolates targets). README "journal_pending that does not clear" documents the dead end: "Every later change command then fails until it is fixed. `doctor`, which will automate this repair, is planned for milestone 4."

Why st_dev changes (authoritative references):
- btrfs reports a per-subvolume anonymous device as `st_dev`: `btrfs_getattr()` sets `stat->dev = BTRFS_I(inode)->root->anon_dev` (fs/btrfs/inode.c), and `btrfs_init_fs_root()` allocates it with `get_anon_bdev(&root->anon_dev)` when the subvolume root is first read (fs/btrfs/disk-io.c). `get_anon_bdev()` (fs/super.c) takes the lowest free minor from a global IDA (`ida_alloc_range(&unnamed_dev_ida, 1, ...)`, `MKDEV(0, dev)`), shared with every other anonymous-device filesystem (tmpfs, proc, overlay, FUSE, ...). The number therefore depends on mount order, which systemd parallelizes, and can differ after every reboot or remount. The btrfs documentation says inode numbers are not filesystem-wide identifiers and to "use the subvolumeid:inodenumber pair" (btrfs.readthedocs.io, Subvolumes, Inode numbers); LWN "The Btrfs inode-number epic" (lwn.net/Articles/866582) describes the per-subvolume device numbers that do not appear in mountinfo.
- FUSE: plain `fuse` mounts get an anonymous device per mount (`get_tree_nodev`, fs/fuse/inode.c `fuse_get_tree`); `fuseblk` (ntfs-3g on a partition) reports the block device's number, which can change when disks enumerate in another order (a USB or second drive). FUSE filesystems such as ntfs-3g are exactly where omaddons falls back to two plain renames per folder.
- Even block-device filesystems on device-mapper (LUKS, LVM) report the dm minor, assigned in activation order, which can differ between boots when several volumes are opened.
- Illustration on the development machine (game, state and config directories on btrfs): `stat -c %d` on a path in the home subvolume reports an anonymous major-0 device, and `/proc/self/mountinfo` lists the filesystem under a different anonymous major-0 number: both are mount-time allocations, not on-disk identities.

What is stable: the inode number of a directory on btrfs, ext4, xfs and tmpfs is preserved by `rename`/`RENAME_EXCHANGE` and by reboots; the birth time (`statx` `STATX_BTIME`, Rust `Metadata::created()`) is an inode attribute that rename keeps and a re-created inode does not share. Each step's two paths are always on one filesystem and one subvolume: the stage dir is checked to share AddOns' device at staging (`same_filesystem`, `src/engine/stage.rs:376-400`), and a cross-device rename is an error, never a fallback (`src/fsx/sys.rs:182-201`). So within one step the device adds no information that the inode lacks.

User-visible consequence: after a crash and a reboot that renumbered the device, recovery refuses every journal step, every change command fails with `internal`, and in fallback mode (ntfs-3g) a folder that was between its two renames stays missing from AddOns, so the addon does not load, with no automated repair until M4.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (fresh `HOME` and `XDG_*`, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<empty dir>`), synthetic retail root; addon source folders `<src>/pkg/Foo` and `<src>/barpkg/Bar`.

1. `omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail` (Foo 1), then put Foo 2 in `<src>/pkg`.
2. `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS='fsx.renameat2.einval,engine.swap.before_rename=abort@3' omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail`: the fallback's first rename moved live Foo to the snapshot, the process aborted before the second. `Interface/AddOns` is empty; one journal is left.
3. Simulate the reboot's device renumbering: in `<state>/omaddons/journal/<tx>.jsonl` replace every `"dev":<n>` with another number (inode numbers untouched).
4. `omaddons install file:<src>/barpkg -t retail` (or `remove Foo`, or `undo`).
5. Expected: recovery rolls back (Foo 1 is live again), `journal_recovered`, and the command proceeds.
6. Actual (reproduced 2026-10-18): every one of these commands fails with exit 1 `internal`: "journal step 3 (...) matches neither its before nor its after state; leaving it for manual repair"; Foo stays missing. Restoring the original `dev` values makes the same command recover and roll back at once.

## Technical Approach

Decided identity: inode number, plus birth time when the filesystem reports one; the device number is recorded for diagnosis only and never compared.

1. `FileId` (`src/engine/journal.rs:159-174`) gains `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] born_ns: Option<i64>` (nanoseconds since the epoch, which fits an i64 until 2262; avoid i128 here because the journal line goes through `serde_json::Value`, `src/engine/journal.rs:50-77`) from `Metadata::created()` (statx `STATX_BTIME`; `None` where the filesystem has no birth time, e.g. most FUSE servers). Keep `dev` in the line (diagnostics, and so older binaries still parse it).
2. Replace the tuple equality in `ran()` (`src/engine/journal.rs:637-656`) with `same(a: Option<FileId>, b: Option<FileId>) -> bool`: both `None`, or both `Some` with equal `ino` and, when both carry `born_ns`, equal `born_ns`. `dev` is ignored. The before/after logic and the "neither" error stay as they are.
3. Journals written by older binaries have no `born_ns`, so they compare by inode alone and recover after a renumbering reboot too. A journal written by this build and read by an older binary still parses (unknown field ignored) and behaves as today.
4. The journal line format stays `schema_version` 1.0 (an optional, additive field; `parse` ignores schema versions, `src/engine/journal.rs:308-351`).
5. Documentation: README Safety model, Interrupted runs: "Each step records the inode (and, where the filesystem keeps one, the birth time) of both paths, so rollback reverses a rename only if it actually happened, also after a reboot." Record on omad-vision-8qa, superseding comment 225 (a): "`from_id`/`to_id` are {dev, ino, born_ns?}; recovery compares ino and born_ns, never dev, because btrfs, FUSE and device-mapper renumber st_dev across mounts."

Rejected alternatives:
- `statx` `STATX_SUBVOL` (Linux 6.10+, btrfs and bcachefs) or `statfs` `f_fsid` as a stable filesystem identity: f_fsid is derived from the device number on xfs and is zero for FUSE, STATX_SUBVOL exists only on two filesystems, and neither adds information within one step, whose paths share a filesystem by construction. Birth time is portable through std and also detects a re-created inode that reused the number.
- Keeping dev and falling back to ino-only only when dev mismatches: two code paths for the same question, and the dev comparison never protects anything the inode and birth time do not.
- Path existence heuristics: the module rejects them on purpose (an exchange leaves both paths in place either way).

Contract: journal line field addition (internal state file); README wording; vision comment. No error or warning codes change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `ran()` ignores `dev`; a step whose recorded devices differ from today's but whose inodes (and birth times) match is judged correctly as ran or not ran.
- Steps to Reproduce end with Foo 1 live again, `journal_recovered`, and the second command succeeding.
- A legacy step line without `born_ns` is judged by inode.
- A re-created directory at `from` with a different birth time (same inode number reused) is still "neither" when the filesystem reports birth times.
- README and the vision comment updated; `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/journal.rs` tests, beside `step_identity_decides_whether_it_ran`): a recorded step with a bumped `dev` still decides correctly for exchange and noreplace; a legacy JSON step line without `born_ns` round-trips and decides by inode; `born_ns` mismatch with equal inode is "neither" (construct the `StepRecord` by hand).
- Integration (`tests/journal.rs`, the six-step scene): rewrite every recorded `dev` in the journal file before recovery and assert the same outcome as without rewriting, at every interrupted prefix (`every_interrupted_prefix_rolls_back_to_the_old_trees`).
- Fallback (`tests/engine_fallbacks.rs::crashes_in_fallback_mode_still_recover_to_one_side`): repeat with rewritten `dev` values.

## Considerations

- Inode numbers on FUSE are only as stable as the server makes them (UNVERIFIED for ntfs-3g across remounts; it is expected to report NTFS file record numbers). If a server renumbers inodes per mount, recovery still stops with the existing "manual repair" error, which is the safe failure; this bead removes the false positives caused by st_dev only.
- A btrfs snapshot rollback restores inode numbers and birth times exactly as they were when the snapshot was taken, so steps then read as "not ran", which matches the restored on-disk state.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9 keeps a journal that still needs manual repair from blocking other targets.
- `born_ns` adds a statx call per recorded path (two per step); negligible.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1`: A failed in-process recovery deletes the journal and the stage dir holding the old folders
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.9`: A leftover journal of one client makes changes on other clients fail with scope_denied
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.5`: Transaction journal: phases, step records and recovery under the lock
acceptance_criteria: journal steps are judged by inode number plus birth time where the filesystem reports one, never by st_dev; a journal whose recorded st_dev no longer matches (after a reboot) rolls back or forward correctly; journals written by older binaries (dev and ino only) recover by inode; README and the vision record say so; argc gate passes
close_reason: Journal steps are judged by inode plus birth time, never st_dev, so recovery works after a reboot that renumbered btrfs/FUSE/dm devices

title: Running detection fails open: an unreadable /proc makes every client look not running
description:
## Background

Two promises depend on knowing whether a client runs:
- README "Running clients": "Removing a folder the client loads, or an update that deletes or renames the TOC it loads, is refused with `game_running` until it exits. On legacy and unrecognized custom clients, every change is refused". Vision D30 (running policy `safe`).
- README "Running clients", vision §5.5 and D33: "**SavedVariables are never written while the client runs**, under any policy or flag, because the game rewrites them on logout".

`src/discover/running.rs:47-57` (`detect_running`) returns an empty map, meaning "nothing runs", when `std::fs::metadata("/proc/self")` fails (`:48-50`). `processes()` (`:216-225`) turns a failed `read_dir(proc_root)` into an empty iterator (`.into_iter().flatten()`), with the same result. Nothing warns. Every caller trusts the empty answer:
- the engine's `running_now` (`src/engine/tx.rs:424-429`), used for planning (`tx.rs:281`) and again under the lock (`tx.rs:595`);
- undo (`src/engine/undo.rs:172`, `:229`), which then restores SavedVariables as if the game were closed;
- `status` (`src/app/status.rs:384`, `:505`), which reports `running: false`.

The module's own doc (`running.rs:10-11`) argues that "a false negative degrades to a warning, never data loss". That holds for folder swaps, which stay atomic. It does not hold for SavedVariables: undo would write them while the game runs, and the game overwrites them on logout, discarding the play session's settings or the restored ones.

When does detection fail? `/proc` is not mounted or not visible: chroots, some containers and toolbox setups, a `/proc` bind-mounted from another PID namespace, or an empty directory where `/proc` should be. Rare, but the failure is silent and lands exactly on the safety rule the README highlights in bold. Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (`HOME` and XDG dirs under a scratch dir, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`), a synthetic retail client in `$HOME/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/_retail_` with a managed addon `Foo` (installed with `install gh:o/foo --file <dir>/Foo -t retail`). `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<scratch>/proc` holds one fake process `4242/` with `comm` = `Wow.exe`, `cmdline` = `C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_retail_\Wow.exe`, `environ` = `WINEPREFIX=<the prefix>`.

1. `omaddons status --json` → `running: true`.
2. `omaddons remove foo -t retail --dry-run --json` → `game_running` (correct).
3. `chmod 000 <scratch>/proc` (the proc root can no longer be listed: the same code path as an unreadable real `/proc`).
4. `omaddons status --json` → `running: false`, `warnings: []`. Expected: `running: null` and a warning naming the cause.
5. `omaddons remove foo -t retail --json` → `ok: true`, `reload_required: "none"`, no warning. The loaded addon was removed while the client "runs". Expected: `game_running` and a `running_unknown` warning.

## Technical Approach

Decided: **fail closed for decisions, report unknown for reads.**

1. **`src/discover/running.rs`.**
   - `detect_running` returns `RunningScan { clients: BTreeMap<PathBuf, Vec<RunningInfo>>, unavailable: Option<String> }`. `unavailable` carries a cause such as "/proc could not be listed: permission denied" or "/proc does not list this process (not mounted, or another PID namespace)". The cause never contains environment values or a home path.
   - The own uid comes from `rustix::process::getuid()` (the `process` feature is already enabled, `Cargo.toml:23`), not from `/proc/self`.
   - Unavailable when `read_dir(proc_root)` fails. For the real `/proc` only (not a debug `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` tree), it is also unavailable when the listing has no entry for `std::process::id()`: an unmounted `/proc` is an empty directory, and a foreign namespace does not list us.
   - A per-process read failure (`comm`, `cmdline`, `environ`) stays a silent skip. Those are other users' or exited processes.
   - `detect_running_in` keeps its signature for `tests/running.rs` and gains an `unavailable`-reporting twin used by `detect_running`.
2. **Engine.**
   - `running_now` (`src/engine/tx.rs:424`) returns the set plus the cause. When unavailable, every target passed is in the running set (fail closed), and one `running_unknown` warning joins the command's warnings.
   - Planning, the re-check under the lock, and undo then behave exactly as for a running client. `safe` lets adds and TOC-keeping replacements through with `reload_required: "reload"`, refuses removes and drops of a loaded TOC, and refuses everything on legacy clients. `refuse` refuses. `--while-running` lifts the folder rules. SavedVariables: `auto` defers (`saved_variables_deferred`), `restore` refuses (`game_running`).
   - `game_running` raised in this state says "may be running" and names the cause in its message. Its `details` gain `"running": "unknown"` (additive; absent when detection worked).
   - `EngineCtx.running = Some(..)` (tests) bypasses detection as today.
3. **`status`.** `StatusTarget.running` (`src/app/status.rs:93`) becomes `Option<bool>`, serialized `null` when unknown, with the `running_unknown` warning. Human output shows `running?` where it shows `running` (`status.rs:235`). Agents testing truthiness read `null` as falsy, which is today's behaviour, while the warning and the null tell careful readers the truth.
4. **Contract (DEC-4, before the M4 freeze).**
   - New warning code `running_unknown` in `src/error.rs` `WarningCode` (`= "running_unknown"`). Its fix is a text suggestion: "omaddons could not read /proc, so it treats every client as running: quit the game and add --while-running to change folders; SavedVariables restores wait until /proc is readable".
   - Type change: `status` `targets[].running` goes from `bool` to `bool | null`.
   - New `details.running: "unknown"` on `game_running` raised while detection is unavailable.
   - Document all three in README (warning table near `saved_variables_deferred`, `status` reference, "Running clients": "If omaddons cannot read `/proc`, it treats every client as running and says so (`running_unknown`)"). Record them as a vision comment on `omad-vision-8qa`, next to the M2 contract list.
5. Update the module docs of `src/discover/running.rs` and `src/engine/running.rs`: a false negative can no longer come from an unreadable process table.

Rejected alternatives:
- Fail open with a warning only. It keeps writing SavedVariables while the game may run, against D33.
- Failing every mutation with a new error. Too blunt: adds and TOC-keeping replacements are safe under a running client (D30), and `--while-running` already expresses the user's override.
- Reporting `running: true` in `status`. The widget would show every client running, a false positive presented as a fact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With the proc root unreadable or not listing this process (real `/proc` case unit-tested through an injectable root and pid), mutating commands treat every selected target as running and carry exactly one `running_unknown` warning. `remove` of a loaded addon fails `game_running` with `details.running == "unknown"`. `--while-running` lets it through. `undo` defers (`auto`) or refuses (`restore`) SavedVariables.
- `status --json` reports `running: null` and `running_unknown`. A readable empty proc root still reports `running: false` and no warning (the test harness's `no-proc` dir keeps working).
- No read of `/proc/self` remains in `src/discover/running.rs`.
- Registry, README and vision comment updated; contract snapshots updated for the status type.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/discover/running.rs`):
  - unreadable root gives `unavailable` with a cause;
  - a real-root mode with an injectable "own pid" absent from the listing gives `unavailable`;
  - a fake root without our pid is still available (the debug seam);
  - per-process unreadable files are skipped silently;
  - the cause string has no home path.
- Unit (`src/engine/running.rs`, `tx.rs`): `running_now` with unavailable marks every target running and yields one warning.
- Integration (`tests/running.rs` or `tests/remove.rs`): the reproduction above with `chmod 000` on the fake proc root (skip when running as root, like `common::procfs::running_as_root`). Covers `remove` refused with `details.running: "unknown"`, `--while-running` allowed, and `status` null plus the warning.
- Integration (`tests/undo_history.rs`): undo with changed SavedVariables and an unreadable proc root gives `saved_variables_deferred` plus `running_unknown`. `--saved-variables restore` gives `game_running`.
- Contract (`tests/contract/`): status envelope snapshot with `running: null`; warning code registered.

## Considerations

- Running inside a sandbox that has its own readable `/proc` but cannot see the host's processes (a Flatpak'd omaddons, say) still lists our own pid, so it remains a silent false negative. README "Running clients" should say detection sees only processes in omaddons' own PID namespace. Not fixable from inside the sandbox; out of scope.
- `process_prefixes` (`running.rs:87-112`, a discovery hint) may keep failing open: a missed hint only means a nested prefix is not discovered while running.
- The warning must appear once per command, not once per target. Multi-target commands (`update`, `sync`, `copy`) share one detection.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.7 adds `game_running` tests for sync and copy. Add one fail-closed case there once both land.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3 makes recovery check whether the client runs before rolling an undo's SavedVariables restore forward. It must use the same fail-closed `RunningScan`, so an unreadable `/proc` defers the restore instead of writing.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3`: Recovery rolls an undo forward and writes SavedVariables while the game client runs
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.7`: Add game_running and reload_required tests for sync and copy
acceptance_criteria: when running detection cannot read the process table, mutations treat every affected client as running (running policy applies, SavedVariables writes deferred or refused) and carry a new running_unknown warning naming the cause; status reports running: null with the same warning; own uid comes from getuid, not /proc/self; the real /proc must list this process to count as readable; README, error registry and vision comment updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: Running detection fails closed: an unreadable or foreign /proc treats every client as running, warns running_unknown once, refusals carry details.running unknown, status reports running null

title: A torn history line swallows the next transaction; roll-forward re-appends onto it
description:
## Background

`history.jsonl` is what undo selection, undo conflict checks and retention read (vision §5.6; README Files and state: "One line per committed transaction"). Its module promises: "A crash mid-append leaves at most a torn last line; the reader skips it and never fails on a bad line" (`src/state/history.rs:5-6`). The writer does not keep the "last line" part of that promise.

Verified at HEAD 53b54e6 (found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit):

- `history::append()` serializes the entry, adds `\n` and appends it with one `Op::AppendFile` (`src/state/history.rs:123-138`). It never checks whether the file already ends with `\n`.
- After a power loss mid-append the file ends with a fragment. The next append is written right after it, producing one line `<fragment><complete line>`. The reader (`src/state/history.rs:174-212`) cannot parse it; since it is no longer the last line it is counted in `skipped_lines` (line 204), which nothing surfaces: only `torn_tail` reaches the user, as an info log of `history` (`src/app/mod.rs:380-389`, `src/app/history.rs:110-124`).
- The transaction being appended when the power went is exactly the one whose journal is still in phase `swapped` (history is appended before `committed`: `src/engine/tx.rs:802-805`, `src/engine/undo.rs:330-333`). Its roll-forward checks whether its line is present by parsing the history (the fragment does not parse), then appends right after the fragment (`src/engine/journal.rs:608-618`). So recovery itself merges the line it is trying to restore with its own fragment.
- If the crash cut only the final `\n`, the reader treats the complete-but-unterminated last line as torn (`src/state/history.rs:198`), roll-forward appends a second copy after it, and the two merge the same way.

User-visible consequence: a committed transaction disappears from `history`; `undo` cannot select it (bare `undo` reverts the previous one instead, `undo <tx>` says it does not exist); undo conflict checks no longer see its folders (`src/engine/undo.rs:533-592`), so an older transaction touching the same folders can be undone over it; retention never considers its snapshot (`src/engine/retention.rs:138-155`), which leaks. Nothing tells the user a line was lost.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (fresh `HOME` and `XDG_*`, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<empty dir>`), synthetic retail root; addon source folders `<src>/pkg/Foo`, `<src>/barpkg/Bar`, `<src>/bazpkg/Baz`.

1. `omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail`
2. `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS='engine.history.appended=abort' omaddons install file:<src>/barpkg -t retail` (the line is written, the journal stays at `swapped`).
3. Simulate the power loss mid-append: `truncate -s -40 <state>/omaddons/history.jsonl` (the file now ends in the middle of Bar's line).
4. `omaddons install file:<src>/bazpkg -t retail`: recovery reports `journal_recovered ... rolled forward` for Bar's transaction.
5. `omaddons history`; `omaddons undo --dry-run`
6. Expected: three transactions (Foo, Bar, Baz); undo would revert Baz, then Bar.
7. Actual (reproduced 2026-10-18): `history` lists only Foo and Baz. The file has three lines; line 2 is Bar's fragment immediately followed by Bar's complete line (two `"tx"` keys for Bar's id). Bar is installed and managed but its transaction cannot be undone or seen. No warning anywhere.

## Technical Approach

Decided fix: the writer always starts on a fresh line, roll-forward is idempotent against its own fragment, the reader salvages what older binaries merged, and unreadable lines are surfaced.

1. Writer. In `history::append()` (`src/state/history.rs:123-138`), before serializing, check whether `history.jsonl` exists, is non-empty and does not end with `\n` (open it read-only and read the last byte; history appends run under the global lock, so this cannot race another writer). If so, prepend `\n` to the content of the same single `Op::AppendFile` write, so the fragment is closed and the new line starts clean in one fsync'd append (no new fsx op; every write still goes through `mutate`).
2. Roll-forward. In `roll_forward()` (`src/engine/journal.rs:608-618`), call a new `history::close_torn_tail(s, paths)` first (an `AppendFile` of `"\n"` when the file does not end with one), then re-read and check presence. A line that was complete except for its newline is now a valid line and is found, so it is not appended twice; a truncated fragment stays unparseable and the complete line is appended after it.
3. Reader (`src/state/history.rs:174-212`):
   - Salvage: every line starts with `{"schema_version":` (its documented first key, `src/state/history.rs:5`, `HistoryEntry` field order). For a line that does not parse, try the substring starting at the last `{"schema_version":` at an offset greater than 0; if that parses as a `HistoryEntry`, use it. This recovers transactions that older binaries merged onto a fragment.
   - Classify the rest: a line whose parse error is `serde_json::error::Category::Eof` (input ended inside the value) is a closed fragment of an interrupted write: count it in a new `HistoryRead::torn_lines` and do not warn. Any other unreadable line (syntax or data errors: a hand edit, a line from a newer schema) counts in `skipped_lines`.
   - The unterminated last line keeps today's handling (`torn_tail`).
4. Surface `skipped_lines`: new warning code `history_lines_skipped`, message `"{n} lines of history.jsonl could not be read and were skipped; the transactions on them are not listed and cannot be undone"`, fix `Suggestion::text("a line was damaged by a crash or a hand edit; omaddons never rewrites history.jsonl")`. Emitted by `history` (`src/app/history.rs:260-285`) and by `undo` (its selection reads the history at `src/engine/undo.rs:154` and discards the counts today; carry the warning into `UndoOutcome`), only when `skipped_lines > 0`.
5. README: Files and state row for `history.jsonl`: add "A line cut short by a crash is closed off by the next write; unreadable lines are skipped and counted in a `history_lines_skipped` warning on `history` and `undo`." Add the warning row to the "Every warning code" table.

Rejected alternatives:
- Truncating the fragment before appending: there is no truncate op in fsx and history is append-only by design (vision §5.6); rewriting the whole file to drop a fragment would turn every append into a whole-file write.
- Warning on every skipped line including closed fragments: after this fix a closed fragment never hides a transaction (its journal re-appends the complete line), so warning forever about one old power loss would be noise.
- Surfacing skipped lines in every command's output: only `history` and `undo` depend on the lost lines; `status` stays quiet.

Contract (DEC-4, allowed before the M4 freeze): new warning code `history_lines_skipped` (register in `src/error.rs`, README table); `HistoryRead` gains `torn_lines` (internal). Record on omad-vision-8qa (§5.6 history.jsonl: "appends start on a fresh line; readers salvage merged lines").

## Acceptance Criteria

- Steps to Reproduce: `history` lists Foo, Bar and Baz; the file's Bar fragment is on its own line; no warning (the fragment is a closed truncation).
- A history file merged by an older binary (fragment + complete line on one line) reads back with the complete entry salvaged.
- A complete line missing only its final newline, with its journal at `swapped`, is recovered to exactly one line for that tx.
- A garbage line (`not json`) in the middle of the file yields `history_lines_skipped` with n = 1 on `history` and `undo`.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/state/history.rs` tests): append after an unterminated fragment writes `\n` first (one `AppendFile`); reader cases: closed fragment (torn_lines), merged line (salvaged), garbage (skipped_lines), complete unterminated last line (torn_tail), empty file.
- Unit (`src/engine/journal.rs` tests): roll-forward with a complete-but-unterminated own line appends nothing new; with a truncated own fragment appends one complete line.
- Integration (`tests/undo_history.rs` or `tests/journal.rs`): the Steps to Reproduce scenario through the binary, then `undo` reverts Baz and then Bar.
- Fuzz seeds (`tests/fuzz_seeds.rs`), if the history reader has a target: add a merged line.

## Considerations

- Salvage looks for the last `{"schema_version":` only when the whole line fails to parse, so a valid line containing that text inside a `--reason` string is never split.
- The extra last-byte read costs one small read per commit under the lock; keep the lock-hold budget (`tests/engine_concurrency.rs::every_commit_holds_the_lock_under_50_ms`).
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1 keeps journals whose recovery failed; a history append that fails mid-write is then retried by the next roll-forward, which this bead makes safe.
- Must not regress: history filters and ordering (`tests/undo_history.rs::history_filters_orders_and_truncates`), the existing `torn_tail` info log.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1`: A failed in-process recovery deletes the journal and the stage dir holding the old folders
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.2.7`: Target records, per-file index, history.jsonl and monotonic status.json
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.5`: Transaction journal: phases, step records and recovery under the lock
acceptance_criteria: history::append closes an unterminated last line before appending; roll-forward finds a complete-but-unterminated line of its own tx and never duplicates it; the reader salvages a line merged by older binaries and counts truncated fragments apart from unreadable lines; unreadable lines surface as a history_lines_skipped warning on history and undo; README documents it; argc gate passes
close_reason: history::append closes an unterminated last line in the same write; roll-forward closes it before looking for its own line, so it neither misses nor duplicates it; the reader salvages lines merged by older binaries and counts closed fragments (torn_lines) apart from unreadable lines (skipped_lines); history and undo warn history_lines_skipped. README Files and state and the warning table updated; vision comment added.

title: Retention can prune the snapshot a deferred SavedVariables restore still needs
description:
## Background

README, Safety model, Undo: "With `--saved-variables auto` and the game running, folders revert ..., and the SavedVariables restore is deferred. You get a `saved_variables_deferred` warning carrying the command to run after quitting: `omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables restore`." Vision comment 289 (undo 6.12): history lines gain `sv_deferred: true` on such an undo. The follow-up reads the reverted transaction's SavedVariables manifest and copies from `<client>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/WTF/` (`plan_saved_variables`, `src/engine/undo.rs:1086-1140`; `restore_one`, `src/engine/undo.rs:1186-1193`), and it refuses unless both snapshot halves exist (`src/engine/undo.rs:430-432`, error `not_found` "snapshot for <tx> was pruned by retention").

Verified at HEAD 53b54e6 (found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit):

- Retention protects only by age, count and recency: `select()` keeps a snapshot when it is the target's most recent transaction or younger than `TX_RETENTION.min_age` (24 h), then the newest `keep_last` (10) within `window` (7 days), then prunes oldest-first to `SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES` (`src/engine/retention.rs:95-125`). `run()` builds the candidates from history without looking at `sv_deferred` (`src/engine/retention.rs:138-155`).
- After a deferred undo D of transaction T, the target's most recent transaction is D, so T's snapshot is protected only for its first 24 hours, and only among the newest 10 within 7 days after that.
- No code pins a pending deferred restore (`grep sv_deferred src/engine/retention.rs` finds nothing).

User-visible consequence: a player who undoes an update while the game runs, keeps playing for more than a day while agents or the widget run other transactions (or simply returns after a week), and then runs the offered `omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables restore`, gets `not_found` "snapshot ... was pruned by retention": the pre-update SavedVariables (often irreplaceable addon profiles that the new version migrated) are gone, although the command was offered as the way to get them back.

## Steps to Reproduce

Not reproducible through the binary without waiting a day: the 24-hour floor is not configurable (`TX_RETENTION.min_age`, `src/limits.rs:39-40`) and the binary uses the real clock. Code-level reproduction (needs a new unit test, described in the Test Plan):

1. History for one target: T (install, 8 days old, both snapshot halves present), D (undo of T, `sv_deferred: true`, 8 days old), then one more transaction X (most recent).
2. `retention::run` at now: T is not most recent, older than 24 h and outside the 7-day window, so `select()` puts it in `prune` (`src/engine/retention.rs:104-110`) and both halves are deleted (`src/engine/retention.rs:163-171`).
3. `undo T --saved-variables restore` then fails at `src/engine/undo.rs:430-432` with `not_found`.

## Technical Approach

Decided: a snapshot that a pending deferred restore needs is protected like the most recent transaction, until the restore is done or can no longer run.

1. Definition of "pending" (also the definition of "abandoned"): for each history entry D with `kind == undo`, `sv_deferred == true` and `reverts == Some(T)` on the target, the restore of T is pending exactly when the follow-up `undo T --saved-variables restore` would pass its conflict check now, i.e. `check_conflicts(entries, at_T, Some(at_D))` (`src/engine/undo.rs:533-592`) returns `Ok`. That check already fails when:
   - the follow-up ran (a later undo of T without `sv_deferred` reads as "already undone");
   - D itself was undone (that undo touches T's folders);
   - a later transaction of any kind touched T's folders (a reinstall or update of the addon), after which restoring the old SavedVariables is no longer offered.
   Using the same function keeps "pinned" and "restorable" identical by construction. Expose it from `src/engine/undo.rs` as `pub(super) fn pending_sv_restores(entries: &[HistoryEntry]) -> BTreeSet<TxId>` (the set of T).
2. In `retention::run()` (`src/engine/retention.rs:129-200`), compute the set from the target's entries it already reads (it reads them filtered by target; read unfiltered or filter the result, since the conflict check compares targets itself) and mark those `SnapshotTx` as protected: add `pinned: bool` to `SnapshotTx` (`src/engine/retention.rs:63-71`) and treat `pinned` like `most_recent` in `select()`'s `protected` closure (`src/engine/retention.rs:98`). Protected snapshots keep beating the size cap; if they alone exceed it, the existing `snapshot_cap_exceeded` warning applies.
3. No new limit and no expiry: SavedVariables hold player settings that cannot be re-downloaded, and the pin ends by itself when any later change touches those addons.
4. README, Safety model, Retention: add "A snapshot that a deferred SavedVariables restore still needs (`saved_variables_deferred`) is kept until that restore runs, the undo is undone, or a later transaction changes those addons." Record on omad-vision-8qa (§5.5 Retention).

Rejected alternatives:
- Pinning only the `WTF/` part of T's snapshot: retention prunes whole transaction dirs (`Kind::ClientSnapshot`, `src/fsx/prune.rs:293-296`); a partial prune would need a new prunable kind, and the follow-up also requires the state half (`src/engine/undo.rs:430`).
- A maximum pin age (a new limits.rs constant): would reintroduce the loss on a schedule; the size-cap warning already reports when protected snapshots grow large.
- Relaxing the follow-up to work without the state half: does not help, the SavedVariables copies are in the client half.

Contract: behaviour change only (retention keeps more); no new codes or keys.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In the scenario above, T's snapshot survives retention while D's restore is pending, and the follow-up restores the files.
- After the follow-up runs, or after a later transaction touches T's folders, or after D is undone, the next retention run may prune T's snapshot under the normal rules.
- Pinned snapshots are listed as kept and count toward `snapshot_cap_exceeded`.
- README Retention updated; vision comment recorded; `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/retention.rs` tests, `Fixture`): extend `Fixture::commit` to write undo entries with `reverts` and `sv_deferred`; cases: pending (kept), follow-up done (pruned), later touching transaction (pruned), deferred undo undone (pruned); `select()` treats `pinned` like `most_recent` over the cap.
- Unit (`src/engine/undo.rs` tests): `pending_sv_restores` agrees with `check_conflicts` on the same histories as `tests/undo_history.rs::saved_variables_while_the_client_runs_and_after`.
- Library-level end to end (`src/engine/undo.rs` or `src/engine/retention.rs` tests with `TxScene`): install, deferred undo (running client), two more transactions, then `retention::run` with `now` eight days later (it takes `now` as a parameter, `src/engine/retention.rs:129-137`); T's snapshot halves survive and the SavedVariables follow-up restores the files. A binary-level test is not practical because the 24-hour floor is fixed and the binary uses the real clock.

## Considerations

- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3 makes recovery produce `sv_deferred` undo lines too; they are pending restores like live ones and are covered by the same rule.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2 sweeps snapshots of transactions without history lines only, so it never competes with this pin. omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.4 warns about retention bounding the undo of folders that exist nowhere else and leaves retention unchanged; it is independent of this pin.
- Cost: one pass over the target's history per retention run, which `run()` already reads.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3`: Recovery rolls an undo forward and writes SavedVariables while the game client runs
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2`: Snapshot dirs of rolled-back and failed transactions are never removed
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.4`: Undo of a folder that exists nowhere else silently ends when retention prunes it
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.8`: Snapshot retention and blob eviction via prune()
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.12`: Undo: revert transactions with conflict detection and the SavedVariables policy
acceptance_criteria: retention never prunes either snapshot half of a transaction whose undo deferred its SavedVariables while that follow-up restore is still possible; the pin ends when the follow-up ran, the deferred undo was undone, or a later transaction touched the reverted folders; pinned snapshots count toward the size cap like other protected ones; README Retention says so; argc gate passes
close_reason: retention::run pins the snapshots engine::undo::pending_sv_restores names (the follow-up would still pass check_conflicts); select() protects pinned like most_recent, over the cap too. The pin ends when the follow-up runs, the deferred undo is undone, or a later transaction touches those folders. README Retention and FAQ updated; vision comment added.

title: SavedVariables under a lowercase wtf/ or account/ are never snapshotted or restored
description:
## Background

README, Safety model, Undo: "Only the touched addons' own files (`WTF/…/SavedVariables/<Folder>.lua` and `.lua.bak`, account-wide and per character) are snapshotted ... a changed one is restored". Wine resolves names ignoring case, so a client whose folders are `wtf/` or `account/` (common in private-server packs copied from Windows or unpacked from archives) is an ordinary, working client. omaddons already treats case variants as the client's own folder for `Interface` and `AddOns` (vision comment 350, xud.2 (d): "ClientPaths::interface()/addons() ... resolve an existing case variant"; `src/state/paths.rs:339-369`), and discovery reads `WTF/Config.wtf` the same way (`find_path`, `src/discover/config_wtf.rs:15-17`, `src/discover/mod.rs:589-621`). SavedVariables do not.

Verified at HEAD 53b54e6 (found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit):

- `ClientPaths::wtf()` is the literal `client_dir.join("WTF")` (`src/state/paths.rs:400-403`).
- `sv_candidates()` joins the literals `"Account"` and `"SavedVariables"` (`src/engine/swap.rs:169-214`, lines 171-191) and records manifest paths with the literal `Account/` prefix. Only the realm-level skip of `SavedVariables` and the file names are case-insensitive (lines 177, 192-202).
- Undo reads and writes `client.wtf().join(rel)` (`src/engine/undo.rs:1102-1106`, `1153-1158`, `1185`).
- The fsx scope row is already case-insensitive (`eq_ci` on `WTF`, `Account` and `SavedVariables`, `src/fsx/scope.rs:420-432` and `478-499`), so no scope change is needed.

User-visible consequence: on such a client every transaction's SavedVariables manifest is empty, silently; undo reports `saved_variables: 0 restored, 0 unchanged` and leaves files the new version rewrote, although README promises they are snapshotted and restored.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (fresh `HOME` and `XDG_*`, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<empty dir>`), synthetic retail root, addon source folder `<src>/pkg/Foo`.

1. Rename `<client>/WTF` to `wtf` and `wtf/Account` to `account`.
2. `echo 'FooDB = { v = 0 }' > <client>/wtf/account/<acct>/SavedVariables/Foo.lua`
3. `omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail`; `cat <client>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/WTF.manifest.json`
4. `echo 'FooDB = { v = 1 }' > .../Foo.lua`; `omaddons undo --json`
5. Expected: the manifest lists `Foo.lua` (and the absent `.bak`, character files); undo restores `v = 0` (`saved_variables.restored: 1`).
6. Actual (reproduced 2026-10-18): the manifest is `"entries": []`; undo succeeds with `saved_variables: {restored: 0, unchanged: 0, deferred: 0, kept: 0}` and `Foo.lua` stays `v = 1`, no warning. The same steps with the canonical spelling restore `v = 0` (`restored: 1, unchanged: 3`).

## Technical Approach

Decided: resolve each SavedVariables path component on disk ignoring ASCII case, exactly like `Interface`/`AddOns`, and never guess between two spellings.

1. `ClientPaths::wtf()` (`src/state/paths.rs:400-403`) resolves through `find_child(&client_dir, "WTF")` like `interface()` (exact spelling first, else a case variant; `WTF` when none exists). Add `wtf_case_variants()` mirroring `addons_case_variants()` (`src/state/paths.rs:355-369`).
2. The resolver introduced by omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.2 in `src/engine/swap.rs` walks `<wtf>/<Account>/<acct>/[<realm>/<char>/]<SavedVariables>` resolving `Account` and each `SavedVariables` with `find_children` (`src/discover/mod.rs:599-616`, already imported by `src/state/paths.rs:15`): exactly one match is used whatever its case; two or more spellings of `WTF`, of `Account`, or of one directory's `SavedVariables` make that subtree ambiguous.
3. Manifest paths are relative to the resolved WTF dir and use the on-disk spelling of every component (`account/<acct>/savedvariables/Foo.lua`), so restore writes the very file the snapshot read. Absent candidates keep the on-disk directory spelling and `<Folder>.lua`. Old manifests (written with `Account/...` literals) were produced only where those spellings existed on disk, so they stay valid.
4. Undo planning and restore (`src/engine/undo.rs:1102-1106`, `1153-1158`, `1185-1188`) use the resolved `wtf()`; `restore_one` keeps renaming onto the manifest path, now spelled as on disk.
5. Ambiguous subtrees: files there are not snapshotted and not restored, and are counted into omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.2's `saved_variables_out_of_scope` warning; the message distinguishes the reason ("in a WTF folder reached through a symlink outside the client directory" vs "in a WTF, Account or SavedVariables folder spelled two ways, which the game reads only one of"), never naming paths.
6. README, Safety model, Undo, SavedVariables: "Folder names under `WTF/` are matched ignoring case, as Wine does; a folder spelled two ways (`WTF` and `wtf`) is left alone and counted in `saved_variables_out_of_scope`." Record on omad-vision-8qa beside the xud.2 (d) note ("WTF, Account and SavedVariables resolve case variants like Interface/AddOns; two spellings are skipped, not refused").

Rejected alternatives:
- Refusing the transaction with `case_collision` when two spellings exist, as for `Interface`/`AddOns`: that refusal protects the folder the transaction writes; here omaddons only reads WTF for an undo safety net, so blocking installs and updates would be out of proportion, and the user would have to edit WTF by hand.
- Emulating Wine's exact-match-first lookup to pick one of two spellings: depends on Wine internals and differs on case-folding mounts; guessing could snapshot one copy and restore into the copy the game does not read.

Contract (DEC-4, allowed before the M4 freeze): manifest paths may use non-canonical spellings (local file only); `saved_variables_out_of_scope` gains the "two spellings" reason in its message. No new code beyond omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.2's.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Steps to Reproduce: the manifest lists the files under their on-disk spelling, and undo restores `v = 0` (`restored: 1`).
- Mixed spellings (`wtf/Account/<acct>/savedvariables/`) work the same.
- With both `WTF/` and `wtf/` present, no SavedVariables are snapshotted or restored, `saved_variables_out_of_scope` reports the count, and nothing under either is written.
- A character directory with both `SavedVariables/` and `savedvariables/` is skipped alone; other directories still work.
- No path, account, realm or character name appears in any output.
- README and vision comment updated; `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/state/paths.rs` tests): `wtf()` resolution (exact, lowercase, absent) and `wtf_case_variants()`.
- Unit (`src/engine/swap.rs` tests, `Scene`): snapshot under `wtf/account/<acct>/savedvariables/` lists entries with on-disk spellings; two spellings at each level are skipped and counted.
- Integration (`tests/undo_history.rs` `Session`, or `tests/engine_fallbacks.rs`): the Steps to Reproduce through the binary, and the two-spellings case.
- Existing SavedVariables tests stay green (canonical spelling unchanged).

## Considerations

- omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1 splits the snapshot into a pre-lock prestage and an under-lock finish that both enumerate `sv_candidates`; the case resolution belongs in that shared enumeration, so the two phases agree on spellings.
- Depends on omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.2, which introduces the resolver and the `saved_variables_out_of_scope` warning; implement both in the same resolver so symlink and case rules are applied in one walk.
- `addons_case_variants()` style checks stay where they are for AddOns; do not route SavedVariables ambiguity into `case_collision`.
- Discovery's own `WTF/` reads (Config.wtf, realmlist) already resolve case; no change there.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.2`: Undo half-applies when WTF, Account or SavedVariables is symlinked out of the client
