title: A leftover journal of one client makes changes on other clients fail with scope_denied
description:
## Background

Vision §5.5: "Mutating commands recover right after acquiring the lock and report `journal_recovered`." The `journal_pending` warning tells the user "the next command that changes addons recovers it" (`src/engine/journal.rs:433-439`), and README Safety model, Interrupted runs: "The next command that commits a change ... recovers under the lock first." That only works when the next change is on the same client.

Found while verifying omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3/omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10 for the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit; verified at HEAD 53b54e6:

- The engine builds its write-scope table from the command's own targets only: `ScopeTable::new(ctx.paths, &client_dirs, None)` with `client_dirs` = the request's targets (`src/engine/tx.rs:263-269`); undo uses only the undone target (`src/engine/undo.rs:178`).
- `recover_all` (`src/engine/journal.rs:460-473`) recovers every journal in `journal/`, whatever its target, with that table: roll-forward's state writes succeed (`<state>/omaddons` is in scope), but its SavedVariables restore, every rollback rename (`src/engine/journal.rs:658-687`) and the final prune of the other client's stage dir (`src/engine/journal.rs:544-559`; `fsx::prune` finds no client dir for it, `src/fsx/prune.rs:280-301`, and refuses "it is not a prunable location") are refused.
- Any error from `recover_all` aborts the commit (`src/engine/tx.rs:575`, `src/engine/undo.rs:223`).

User-visible consequence: after any interrupted transaction on client A (a crash, a power loss), every install, update, remove or undo on client B fails with exit 4 `scope_denied` ("refusing to prune <A's stage dir>: it is not a prunable location", not retryable, fix `omaddons status`) until the user happens to change something on A. Worse, a swapped-phase journal is rolled forward far enough to write A's record and mark the journal `committed` before the prune fails, so from then on `status` reports nothing pending while B keeps failing. With omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.4 or any journal that needs manual repair, one bad journal blocks every client.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (fresh `HOME` and `XDG_*`, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<empty dir>`), one synthetic Battle.net root with two products (`wow` → `_retail_`, `wow_classic` → `_classic_`); addon source folders `<src>/pkg/Foo` (interface 120105) and `<src>/cpkg/Baz` (interface 50504).

1. `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS='engine.swapped=abort' omaddons install file:<src>/pkg -t retail` (one journal left for retail).
2. `omaddons install file:<src>/cpkg -t classic --json`
3. Expected: retail's transaction is recovered (`journal_recovered`) and Baz installs on classic.
4. Actual (reproduced 2026-10-18): exit 4 `scope_denied`, "refusing to prune <client>/Interface/.omaddons/stage/<tx>: it is not a prunable location". The journal now ends with `{"type":"committed"}` (retail's record and history were written). Repeating step 2 fails identically; `status` no longer reports a pending journal; only a change on retail (`omaddons remove Foo -t retail`) clears it.

## Technical Approach

Decided fix: recovery derives each journal's scope from the journal, validates it, and isolates failures per target.

1. Per-journal scope. In `recover_parsed()` (`src/engine/journal.rs:523-561`), when the journal has a `prepared` line, take `prepared.client_dir` and accept it only if that directory's target marker (`<client>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json`, read with `crate::discover::registry::read_marker`) holds `prepared.target_key`. Registration writes the marker under the lock before any journal is created (`src/engine/tx.rs:578-588`), and only omaddons writes markers, so a journal cannot point recovery at an arbitrary directory. Then clone the caller's `ScopeTable` and `add_client_dir(&prepared.client_dir)` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:240-247`; `ScopeTable` is `Clone`) for that journal's roll-forward, rollback and prune.
2. Unvalidated journals (marker missing or naming another key, client dir gone): do not touch the client side. A `committed` or unprepared journal is still pruned (state-side victims only: the journal and its in-flight lock); a `prepared`/`swapped` one is left and reported.
3. Isolation. `recover_all` takes the keys of the targets the caller is about to commit (`own: &[TargetKey]`; the engine passes the target being committed; omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10's non-engine callers pass none). A journal of an `own` target that fails to recover returns the error as today (the commit must not proceed over it). A journal of any other target that fails (or is unvalidated) becomes a `journal_pending` warning naming its tx and target and the reason (`"... could not be recovered: {error.message}"`, fix `omaddons status`) and recovery continues with the next journal.
4. Introduce a `RecoveryEnv { lock, paths, scopes, own, sv_writable }` struct (omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3 adds `sv_writable`) so `recover_all`/`recover_tx` change signature once; in-process `recover_tx` passes the transaction's own target.
5. README: Safety model, Interrupted runs: "Recovery handles every client's journals, whichever client the command changes." Troubleshooting, "`journal_pending` that does not clear": replace "Every later change command then fails until it is fixed" with "Every later change on that client then fails until it is fixed; other clients are not affected and keep reporting it as `journal_pending`."

Rejected alternatives:
- Adding every registered client dir to the engine's scope table up front: widens every command's writable area to all clients for the whole run, not just for recovery of a validated journal.
- Trusting `prepared.client_dir` without the marker check: a damaged or hand-edited journal could then direct renames and prunes into any directory with an `Interface/AddOns` shape.
- Skipping other targets' journals entirely: they would wait for a change on their own client, contradicting §5.5 and the `journal_pending` text.

Contract (DEC-4, allowed before the M4 freeze): `journal_pending` can now also appear in mutating commands' outputs for a journal recovery could not finish (with the reason in the message); behaviour change only, no new codes. Record on omad-vision-8qa (§5.5 Journal phases and recovery: "recovery scopes each journal to its own client dir, validated by the target marker; a failure on another target is reported, not fatal").

## Acceptance Criteria

- Steps to Reproduce: step 2 succeeds, reports `journal_recovered` for retail's tx, and installs Baz on classic; retail's record, files index and history are rolled forward exactly once; the journal and retail's stage dir are pruned.
- A rollback-phase journal of retail is rolled back by a classic command (folders back, `journal_recovered`).
- A retail journal that needs manual repair (see omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.4's reproduction) makes classic commands succeed with a `journal_pending` warning naming it, while retail commands still fail.
- A journal whose `client_dir` has no matching marker is never used to write that directory.
- README updated, vision comment recorded; `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/journal.rs` tests): two client dirs, a swapped journal for one, `recover_all` with a scope table built for the other recovers it; marker mismatch leaves the client untouched; `own` isolation returns the error only for an own target.
- Integration (`tests/engine_multi_target.rs` or `tests/journal.rs`): the two-client scenario through the binary, for roll-forward and rollback; a third case where the other target's journal is unrecoverable.
- Crash suite: unchanged expectations for single-client crashes.

## Considerations

- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10 (recovery under `config set`, `targets`, `auth`, `export --write`) needs this: those commands have no client dirs in their scope tables at all.
- Depends on omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3: its running predicate decides the SavedVariables part of another target's roll-forward. Without it, recovering another target's undo would write its SavedVariables without a running check, extending omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3's bug to every client's commands.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1 keeps journals whose in-process recovery failed; with this bead such a journal blocks only its own target.
- Marker reads add one small file read per leftover journal; there are normally none.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1`: A failed in-process recovery deletes the journal and the stage dir holding the old folders
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3`: Recovery rolls an undo forward and writes SavedVariables while the game client runs
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.4`: Recovery after a reboot stops: journal steps compare st_dev, which btrfs and FUSE renumber
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10`: Lock holders outside the engine and no-op change commands never recover pending journals
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.5`: Transaction journal: phases, step records and recovery under the lock
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.3`: Lock, revalidate and commit: the transaction driver
acceptance_criteria: recovery builds each journal's write scope from the journal's own client dir, validated by that client's target marker; a change command on client B recovers client A's leftover journal (journal_recovered) instead of failing; a journal that cannot be recovered blocks only commits on its own target and is reported as journal_pending on the others; README journal troubleshooting updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: Recovery scopes each journal to its own client (validated by the target marker) and reports another target's unrecoverable journal as journal_pending instead of failing the command

Add the own: &[TargetKey] field there and derive per-journal scopes inside recover_parsed. title: Epic: Engine performance, retention, undo semantics and engine tests
description:
## Background

Beyond the recovery bugs, the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found engine defects in performance, retention and undo semantics, plus test-suite gaps that let them through:
- the global lock is held for seconds (17 s measured in a debug build) when SavedVariables are large, so a concurrent command fails `locked`;
- snapshot dirs of failed and rolled-back transactions are never removed;
- undo of an older transaction strands a dependency's later requesters without `still_required`;
- undo of a folder that exists nowhere else silently ends when retention prunes it;
- undo resets restored directory modes, and the tests' digest cannot see it;
- the crash matrix has no mid-swap, undo, SavedVariables or failed-recovery scenes;
- sync and copy have no running-client tests;
- the single-writer scanner stops at the first `#[cfg(test)]` and misses several write APIs.

## Goals

- The lock is held for milliseconds whatever the size of SavedVariables or folders (vision D24).
- Undo is honest about what it can and cannot bring back, and keeps `required_by` consistent.
- The tests that guard the engine's invariants actually cover the paths those invariants depend on.

## Success Criteria

- Every child bead is closed with its regression or coverage test.
- A lock-hold test with large SavedVariables on a filesystem without reflinks passes.
- `argc gate` passes; README and the vision bead record each behaviour change.

## Non-Goals

- No new retention policy beyond sweeping orphans and stating the existing bound.
- No `doctor` findings (M4).

## Considerations

- The crash-matrix bead depends on the recovery fixes in the engine-safety epic (its failed-recovery scenes fail until those land).
- The lock-hold fix rewrites the SavedVariables snapshot and restore that several engine-safety beads also touch. Coordinate through their `related` edges.

title: The global lock is held for seconds when SavedVariables or undone folders are large
description:
## Background

Vision D24 and §5.5 say the global lock is "held only for revalidate → journal → swap → commit (milliseconds), never across network I/O", and goal G3 says "widget, terminal and agent can mutate concurrently, because the lock is held only for milliseconds". README "Safety model → Concurrency" says: "Tests assert each commit holds it under 50 ms, and the M1 checkpoint measured at most 2 ms. A second run waits up to 5 seconds, then fails with `locked`". `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` is 5 s (`src/limits.rs:36`).

The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found that the commit window does work proportional to the size of the touched addons' SavedVariables, and undo also does work proportional to the size of the folders it reverts. All of it runs while the global flock is held (install: `src/engine/tx.rs:573` acquire → `:838` drop; undo: `src/engine/undo.rs:221` → `:344`):

1. **Install/update/remove SavedVariables snapshot** (`src/engine/tx.rs:774` → `src/engine/swap.rs:112` `snapshot_saved_variables`). For every account and per-character `SavedVariables/<Folder>.lua` and `.lua.bak` of every touched folder:
   - `mutate(.., Op::CloneFile)` (`src/engine/swap.rs:141`): a reflink on btrfs/xfs, a **full byte copy with fsync** on ext4, tmpfs, NTFS and most FUSE (`src/fsx/sys.rs` `clone_file`);
   - the fsx after-digest hashes the new copy in full (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:340` → `digest_after` → `hash_file`);
   - `swap.rs:145` then hashes the source file in full a second time (`sha256_file(path)`) for the manifest.
2. **Undo** does more, all under the lock:
   - `commit()` re-runs `plan()` under the lock (`src/engine/undo.rs:230`), whose `plan_saved_variables` hashes every manifest file (`undo.rs:1106` `present_hash`);
   - `snapshot_saved_variables` for the undo's own snapshot (`undo.rs:298`): copy + two hashes per file, as above;
   - `restore_saved_variables` hashes each file again (`undo.rs:1159`), then `restore_one` clones the reverted snapshot's copy into `sv-restore/` (`undo.rs:1193`: byte copy + after-digest hash) and renames it over the live file with `RenameMode::Replace` (`undo.rs:1198`), whose fsx before-digest hashes the staged file and whose verbatim backup hashes the live file, byte-copies it into the backup dir and hashes the copy (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:596-631` `backup`). That is about 8 full hashes and 3 byte copies per changed SavedVariables file.
   - Folder ops are built with `old_tree: None` (`undo.rs:728`, `undo.rs:740`), so the fsx before-digest of every folder undo removes or replaces is `TreeDigest::compute` (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:586`): every file of the live folder is read and hashed under the lock. The install planner takes these digests from the files index instead (`src/engine/plan.rs:3684-3703`).
3. `install --force` over an unmanaged folder has no index digest either, so the same `TreeDigest::compute` runs under the lock for that folder.

Every existing lock-hold test (`tests/engine_concurrency.rs:491` `multi_addon_commits_hold_the_lock_under_50_ms`, `:531` `every_commit_holds_the_lock_under_50_ms`) uses scenes without any `WTF/` tree (`tests/common/engine.rs` writes none) and never measures undo, so none of this is caught.

User-visible consequence: SavedVariables of 5–50 MB per addon are common (WeakAuras, Details!, TSM, AllTheThings, each with a `.lua.bak` beside it, per account, and some per character), so `update --all` over a heavy profile or an `undo` after a play session holds the lock for seconds. A widget, agent or second terminal command that commits meanwhile waits 5 s and fails `locked` (exit 5), which D24 says is "practically unreachable".

## Steps to Reproduce

Measured on the development machine (tmpfs, so every clone is a byte copy; a fast CPU with SHA extensions; release binary, `-v` prints `lock released: tx …, lock_held_ms N`). Isolated environment as in the audit rules (`HOME`, XDG dirs, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` an empty dir) with a synthetic Battle.net retail client and a local addon directory `Foo/` (one TOC, one Lua file):

1. `omaddons install gh:o/foo --file <dir>/Foo -t retail --json -v` twice: `lock_held_ms 1`.
2. Create `<client>/WTF/Account/ACCT1/SavedVariables/Foo.lua` (40 MiB) and `Foo.lua.bak` (40 MiB), and 10 characters with `Foo.lua` and `Foo.lua.bak` of 2 MiB each (120 MiB in total).
3. The same install again: `lock_held_ms 129` and `131` (expected: a few ms).
4. Append a line to every one of those files (a play session), then `omaddons undo --json -v`: `lock_held_ms 504`.
5. A 100 MiB addon folder (20 files of 5 MiB): install twice → `lock_held_ms 1`; `undo` (a replace with `old_tree: None`) → `lock_held_ms 93`.
6. With the debug binary (what the test suite runs), step 3 holds the lock 4351 ms. With the debug binary, starting `undo` (after step 4) and 2.5 s later `omaddons install gh:o/bar --file <dir>/Bar -t retail --json` in a second process: the second command fails with `locked`, "omaddons undo (pid N) held the lock for more than 5000 ms", exit 5; the undo reported `lock_held_ms 17429`.

Release builds scale at about 1.1 ms per MiB of SavedVariables for a commit and 4.2 ms per MiB for an undo on this fast machine; slower CPUs without SHA extensions and real disks (fsync of every copy) are several times slower, so a heavy profile crosses the 5 s timeout in production too.

## Technical Approach

Decided: under the lock, a SavedVariables file or folder is only `stat`ed and renamed. Hashing and copying happen before the lock, and the commit window re-verifies them with a stat stamp. Steps:

1. **A stat stamp.** Add `fsx::FileStamp { dev, ino, size, mtime_ns, ctime_ns }`, read with `symlink_metadata`, and a `TreeStamp` (the sorted `(relative path, kind, FileStamp)` list of a directory, symlinks not followed). `ctime` changes on every write and cannot be set from user space, so an equal stamp means the bytes did not change. Put both in `src/fsx/` next to `TreeDigest` (they are read-only, but they belong with the digests they guard).
2. **SavedVariables snapshot before the lock.** Split `snapshot_saved_variables` (`src/engine/swap.rs:112`) into:
   - `prestage_saved_variables(s, tx, client, folders) -> SvPrestage`, called after staging and before `GlobalLock::acquire` (`src/engine/tx.rs:573`, and in `undo()` before `commit()`). It enumerates `sv_candidates`, takes each present file's stamp, clones it into `snapshots/<tx>/WTF/<rel>` through fsx (a tracked `WriteSession::tx` for this tx; the session needs no global lock, as staging does not), takes the stamp again, and accepts the entry only if both stamps are equal. The SHA-256 comes from the clone's after-digest in the returned `ActionRecord.after_hash`, so each file is hashed once. Drop the second hash at `swap.rs:145`. A source that changed during the copy is retried once and otherwise left for the lock.
   - `finish_saved_variables(s, prestage, ...)` under the lock, in place of the call at `tx.rs:774`. It enumerates `sv_candidates` again (directory listings only). For each candidate whose current stamp equals the prestaged one, it keeps the entry. For anything new, changed or vanished since (rare: a client wrote on logout in between), it redoes that one entry under the lock exactly as today, removing the stale clone first. Then it writes `WTF.manifest.json` (small). The manifest format does not change.
   - The snapshot dir for `<tx>` now exists before the journal. A crash or error between the prestage and `prepared` leaves `snapshots/<tx>/` with no journal and no history. omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2 makes cleanup, recovery and retention remove exactly that (in-flight lock free, no journal, no history line), hence the dependency.
3. **Undo SavedVariables.**
   - Pre-lock `plan()` (`undo.rs:173`) already hashes the manifest files. Keep their stamps in `SvPlan`, and under the lock compare stamps instead of hashing again (`undo.rs:1106`, `:1159`). A changed stamp means re-hash that one file under the lock.
   - Prestage the undo's own snapshot (step 2).
   - Prestage each restore copy: before the lock, clone `snapshots/<reverted>/WTF/<rel>` into `snapshots/<undo>/sv-restore/<attempt>/<rel>` and verify its hash against the manifest's `sha256`. This also catches a corrupted snapshot before anything moves. Under the lock, restore with `Rename { mode: Exchange }` staged ⇄ live, then a `NoReplace` rename of the displaced live file to `snapshots/<undo>/sv-replaced/<rel>`. An exchange is not a `Replace`, so fsx takes no verbatim backup copy. The displaced inode itself is preserved, and the undo's own `WTF/<rel>` clone already holds the same bytes.
   - Where `RENAME_EXCHANGE` is `Unsupported`, fall back to today's `Replace` path for that file. It is slower but correct, like the swap's `atomic_swap: false`.
   - Roll-forward (`src/engine/journal.rs` `roll_forward` → `restore_saved_variables`) must finish both renames idempotently. It skips a file whose live hash already matches, then moves a displaced file still at the staged path into `sv-replaced/`. Recovery is rare, so hashing there is fine.
4. **Folder digests for undo.** In `FolderPlan::inverse` (`undo.rs:686`), take `old_tree` for `SwapOp::Remove`/`Replace` from the current files index of the live folder (load `FilesIndex` once in `plan()`), exactly as `TargetPlanner::swap_ops` does (`src/engine/plan.rs:3684-3689`).
   - For a folder without an index entry (an unmanaged folder under `install --force`, or an index-less record), compute `TreeDigest` plus `TreeStamp` before the lock (planning already walks it).
   - Under the lock, re-check the `TreeStamp`. If equal, pass the digest as `tree_before`. If not, fall back to computing it there.
   - The digest is audit data for `actions.jsonl`, but it must not lie, hence the stamp.
5. **Test** (see Test Plan) with large SavedVariables on a byte-copy path: the `fsx.reflink.unsupported` failpoint forces byte copies even on btrfs (`src/fsx/sys.rs:218`).
6. **Docs and contract.** No error or warning code and no JSON key changes. README "Safety model → Transactions": move "snapshot touched SavedVariables" to the stage column (the commit window re-checks them). Keep the "Concurrency" bullet's 50 ms claim and add that it holds with large SavedVariables. Add a vision comment on `omad-vision-8qa`: §5.5 step 7 now snapshots SavedVariables before the lock and re-verifies by stat stamp under it, and undo restores SavedVariables by exchange.

Rejected alternatives:
- Raising `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT`. It hides the symptom, and D24's promise is about the hold time.
- Snapshotting SavedVariables without the manifest hash. Undo's "unchanged since" test needs the hash.
- A per-target lock for SavedVariables. It is a second lock, against D23's single-lock model.
- Skipping the SavedVariables snapshot when the client is not running. The game can start between the snapshot and the commit, and undo still needs the old bytes.
- Trusting mtime and size alone. Both can be preserved by tools; `ctime` plus inode cannot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No `hash_file`/`sha256_file`/`TreeDigest::compute` and no `CloneFile` of an unchanged SavedVariables file or indexed folder runs between `GlobalLock::acquire` and the guard's drop, in `tx::locked` and `undo::commit`. A file or folder whose stamp changed after the prestage is handled correctly under the lock.
- The manifest, undo semantics (unchanged/changed/created, `auto`/`restore`/`keep`, deferral) and every existing undo test are unchanged.
- New test: 16 MiB of SavedVariables (account `.lua` and `.lua.bak`, plus 4 characters), byte-copy path forced. Install, update, remove and undo (with every file changed after the update) each hold the lock under 50 ms in a debug build.
- Undo of a replace of an indexed 64 MiB folder holds the lock under 50 ms.
- A SavedVariables file rewritten between the prestage and the lock (the `pause` failpoint from omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.4 on `engine.stage.synced`, or `engine.stage.synced=sleep:…` until that lands, plus a write from the test) is snapshotted with its new bytes and its new hash.
- The crash matrices pass, including omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.5's SavedVariables scenes once they exist.
- README Transactions and Concurrency updated; vision comment recorded.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/fsx/`): `FileStamp` equality changes on content rewrite, on touch with a preserved mtime (`ctime` moves), and on replace-by-rename; `TreeStamp` sees add, remove, rename and mode change.
- Unit (`src/engine/swap.rs`): prestage then finish with nothing changed gives the same manifest as today's `snapshot_saved_variables`. A candidate created, changed or deleted between the two is redone under the lock. Each file is hashed once, checked by counting hashes behind a test-only counter.
- Unit (`src/engine/undo.rs`): extend `saved_variables_unchanged_changed_created_and_kept` and `an_error_at_any_failpoint_leaves_the_undo_wholly_done_or_not_done` for the exchange-based restore. Add an `Unsupported` exchange (the `fsx.renameat2.einval` failpoint) that falls back to `Replace`. Roll-forward finishes a restore interrupted between the exchange and the `sv-replaced` rename.
- Integration (`tests/engine_concurrency.rs`): `large_saved_variables_hold_the_lock_under_50_ms`, with `fsx.reflink.unsupported` armed (a list of failpoints is accepted, comma-separated). Install v1, update to v2, append to every SavedVariables file, `undo`; parse `lock_held_ms` from `-v` as the existing tests do. A second case undoes a replace of a 64 MiB indexed folder.
- Crash: the cross-process matrix with SavedVariables comes from omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.5; this change must keep it green.

## Considerations

- Size: this is at the top of size-M. If it grows, split it into E6a (install-path prestage plus the lock-hold test, steps 1, 2 and 5) and E6b (undo: steps 3 and 4), with E6b depending on E6a.
- The pre-lock snapshot dir appears before `prepared`, which is why omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2 (sweep of snapshot dirs without history, journal or live in-flight lock) matters here. `cleanup()` (`src/engine/tx.rs:1130`) must prune the tx's snapshot halves when the tx did not commit (omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2 decides how).
- Running clients: SavedVariables are never written by install, and undo writes them only when the client is not running (D33), so the window between the prestage and the lock sees a writer only if the client starts or logs out in that window. The stamp re-check covers it.
- `snapshot_state` (record, files index and registry clones, `swap.rs:218`) stays under the lock. Those files are small, and they must be the state the commit replaces.
- Disk use is unchanged: the same copies are made, only earlier. On btrfs/xfs the clones stay reflinks.
- Do not regress the 2 ms typical hold: the extra stat pass costs one `symlink_metadata` per candidate.
- Interaction with omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.5: undo planning uses the running state. Keep the pre-lock and under-lock decisions on the same detection call as today.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.8 (case variants of `wtf/`/`account/` in `sv_candidates`) and omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3 (roll-forward of an undo's SavedVariables restore while the client runs) touch the same functions. The prestage and finish split must keep omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.8's candidate rules, and the exchange-based roll-forward must keep omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3's running check.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.3`: Recovery rolls an undo forward and writes SavedVariables while the game client runs
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.5`: Running detection fails open: an unreadable /proc makes every client look not running
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.8`: SavedVariables under a lowercase wtf/ or account/ are never snapshotted or restored
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.5`: Close the crash-matrix gaps: Nth rename, undo, SavedVariables, failed recovery, snapshots
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.4`: Race tests order processes with fixed sleeps; add a pause failpoint and sync explicitly
acceptance_criteria: a commit or undo holds the global lock for a time independent of SavedVariables size and folder size (no full-file hash or byte copy of an unchanged file under the lock); a new lock-hold test with 16 MiB of SavedVariables on a byte-copy path holds the lock under 50 ms for install, update and undo (changed files restored); the existing 50 ms tests still pass; the crash and undo suites still pass; README Concurrency and the vision record the change; argc gate passes
close_reason: The global lock no longer reads or copies an unchanged SavedVariables file or indexed folder. SavedVariables are cloned and hashed before it and re-checked by stat stamp under it; undo prestages its own snapshot and its checked restore copies, re-plans through a stamp-keyed hash memo, and restores by RENAME_EXCHANGE with known digests; folder digests come from the files index, or are taken before the lock with a TreeStamp.

title: Snapshot dirs of rolled-back and failed transactions are never removed
description:
## Background

README "Retention" bounds what omaddons keeps on disk: snapshots are pruned by age, count and the 2 GiB per-target cap, and "Orphaned stage directories and in-flight locks older than an hour are swept". Vision §5.5 "Retention" bounds snapshots the same way. Nothing removes the snapshot dirs of a transaction that never committed, so they grow without bound, outside every cap. Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit.

Where the dirs come from:
- A transaction writes `<client>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/` (the SavedVariables clones under `WTF/`, `WTF.manifest.json`, and folders moved into `AddOns/` during the swap) and `<state>/omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/` (record, files index and registry clones, `actions.jsonl`, fsx backups). The first write is `Journal::create` (`src/engine/tx.rs:765`, `src/engine/undo.rs:294`), whose actions line creates the state half.
- After omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1, the client half is created before the lock as well.

Why nothing removes them:
- Recovery: `recover_parsed` (`src/engine/journal.rs:523-561`) rolls back or forward, then prunes only the stage dir, the journal and the in-flight lock (`:543-560`).
- In-process failure: `locked` (`src/engine/tx.rs:808-815`) and `undo::commit` (`src/engine/undo.rs:336-342`) call `recover_tx`, which is the same `recover_parsed`.
- Cleanup: `cleanup` (`src/engine/tx.rs:1130-1155`) prunes the journal, both in-flight locks, the cache tmp dir and the stage dir.
- Retention: `retention::run` (`src/engine/retention.rs:129-200`) builds its candidate list only from `history.jsonl` entries of the target (`:140-156`), so a transaction without a history line is never a candidate. Its orphan sweep (`orphans`, `:212-252`) lists only stage dirs and in-flight lock files.
- The tests miss it: the leftover checks (`src/engine/tx.rs:1230-1243`, `src/engine/undo.rs:1318-1331`, and the crash matrices' journal and AddOns checks in `tests/engine_crash.rs`) never look at snapshot dirs.

User-visible consequence: every `plan_stale` at the rename, I/O error, failpoint, crash or interrupted run after `prepared` leaves a full SavedVariables copy behind. On ext4 and tmpfs these are byte copies, often tens of MB per run (omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1), under `<client>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/` and `<state>/omaddons/snapshots/`, forever. `status` never mentions them.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (`HOME`/XDG under a scratch dir, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, empty `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`). A synthetic retail client with `WTF/Account/ACCT1/SavedVariables/Foo.lua` and `.lua.bak` (1 MiB each) and two characters (1 MiB each, plus `.bak`). A local addon dir `Foo/`.

1. `omaddons install gh:o/foo --file <dir>/Foo -t retail --json`: one snapshot dir in each half (the committed tx).
2. `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.swap.after_exchange=error omaddons install gh:o/foo --file <dir>/Foo -t retail --json` fails with `io` (rolled back in process).
3. `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.swap.before_rename=abort omaddons install …` crashes (exit 134).
4. `omaddons install gh:o/bar --file <dir>/Bar -t retail --json` → `journal_recovered` ("recovery undid it (rolled back)").
5. `omaddons history --json` lists 2 transactions. `ls <client>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/` and `ls <state>/omaddons/snapshots/` list 4 each. The two extra ones (steps 2 and 3) each hold 6.1 MB of SavedVariables copies.
6. Age both orphan dirs (`touch -h -d '3 hours ago'` on every entry), then commit another install. Retention runs and both orphans are still there. Expected: gone after step 4 (crash) and step 2 (in-process), or at the latest swept once older than `ORPHAN_MIN_AGE`.

## Technical Approach

Decided: remove them at the earliest point that has proof the transaction will never commit, and sweep the rest by age.

1. **Recovery (`src/engine/journal.rs` `recover_parsed`).**
   - After `roll_back` (phase `Prepared`), and for `(None, _) | (_, Phase::Unprepared)` (a torn or empty journal), prune both snapshot halves: `ClientPaths::new(&prepared.client_dir).snapshots(tx)` when `prepared` parsed, and `paths.state_snapshot(tx)` always.
   - `fsx::prune` admits snapshot dirs only for `PruneReason::Retention` (`src/fsx/prune.rs:251-272`, `Kind::ClientSnapshot`/`StateSnapshot`). Prune them in a second `fsx::prune(scopes, PruneReason::Retention, &snapshots, LockUse::Held(lock))` call, next to the existing `PostCommitCleanup` one, rather than widening the reason table. A dead transaction's snapshot is retention's garbage. `src/engine/journal.rs` is already in `tests/single_writer.rs` `PRUNE_CALLERS`.
   - Only after a successful `roll_back`: if it fails, the error returns before any prune and everything stays for the next lock holder (omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1).
   - Safety guard: prune the client half only if `snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/` is absent or empty after the rollback. If a folder is still in there, rollback did not bring it back (a recovery bug like omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1–omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.4 elsewhere). Keep the whole dir and append "its snapshot is kept: N folders are still in it" to the `journal_recovered` message. That is message text only; no new code.
   - Rolled forward and committed: keep, as today.
2. **In-process failure.** `recover_tx` uses the same path, so the in-process rollbacks in `tx::locked` and `undo::commit` get the same behaviour for free.
3. **`cleanup` (`src/engine/tx.rs:1130`)** gains a `committed: bool` argument (callers know: `commit_target` and `undo()` pass whether a history line was written).
   - When `false` and no journal for the tx remains (it never existed, or recovery finished and removed it), also prune both snapshot halves if they exist (with the same `AddOns/` guard). Do it under the transaction's own in-flight lock (`LockUse::Own`), as the other victims are, in a separate `PruneReason::Retention` call.
   - When a journal remains (omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1 keeps an unfinished journal when in-process recovery fails), leave both halves: the next recovery needs them.
   - This covers failures before `prepared`: `locked` acquire timeout, `plan_stale` at revalidation, and after omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1 the pre-lock SavedVariables snapshot.
   - Check that `fsx::prune` accepts snapshot victims under `LockUse::Own` (every victim must be named for the caller's own tx). The single-writer allowlist (`tests/single_writer.rs` `PRUNE_CALLERS`) needs no new file.
4. **Retention sweep (`src/engine/retention.rs` `orphans`).** Also list `client.meta_dir().join("snapshots")` and `paths.state_snapshots_dir()` entries whose name parses as a `TxId` and that meet all of these:
   - no history line for that tx in the whole `history.jsonl`, not filtered by target: two targets can share one client dir, see `6d68415`. Test this on the raw file text (the tx id string occurs nowhere in it), not only on the parsed entries, so a committed transaction whose line is torn or merged (omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.6) never loses its snapshot;
   - no live in-flight lock (`InflightLock::is_live`, which checks both lock places);
   - no journal;
   - older than `ORPHAN_MIN_AGE`, by the dir's mtime;
   - for the client half, an empty or absent `AddOns/`.
   They go to `fsx::prune(.., PruneReason::Retention, ..)`, since snapshot kinds take only that reason. Count them in `RetentionReport.orphans_swept`. Read the history once per run (it is already read for the target; read it unfiltered and filter in memory).
5. **Tests' leftover checks.** `leftovers()` in `src/engine/tx.rs:1230` and `src/engine/undo.rs:1318`, and the crash matrices (`tests/engine_crash.rs` `matrix`, `shape_matrix`, `record_matrix`), assert that every dir under both snapshot roots belongs to a transaction with a history line.
6. **Docs.**
   - README "Retention": "Orphaned stage directories, in-flight locks and the snapshots of transactions that never committed are swept (immediately on rollback, otherwise once older than an hour)."
   - README "Interrupted runs": rollback also removes the transaction's snapshot.
   - Vision comment on `omad-vision-8qa` (§5.5 Retention orphan sweep, extends the 6.8 comment). No code, key or warning changes.

Rejected alternatives:
- Sweeping only by age in retention. Leaves big copies around for an hour after every failure, and retention runs only for the target just changed.
- Counting orphan snapshots against the 2 GiB cap. They are garbage, not history, and the cap would then prune real undo snapshots first.
- Deleting a snapshot whose `AddOns/` still holds folders. That could destroy the only copy of a user's addon if a recovery bug left it there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After an in-process rollback and after a crash plus recovery, neither snapshot root has a dir for the rolled-back tx.
- A snapshot whose `AddOns/` still has an entry after rollback is kept, and the `journal_recovered` message says so.
- `cleanup` of a transaction that failed before `prepared` leaves no snapshot dir for it. A committed transaction's snapshot is untouched.
- Retention removes an aged snapshot dir with no history line, lock or journal, in both roots. It keeps one with a live in-flight lock, one with a journal, one younger than `ORPHAN_MIN_AGE`, and one with `AddOns/` content.
- All leftover checks include snapshot dirs and pass.
- README and vision comment updated.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/journal.rs`):
  - `recover_parsed` after a rollback with an empty `AddOns/` prunes both halves;
  - a rollback that leaves a folder in `AddOns/` keeps the dir and the warning says so;
  - an `Unprepared` journal prunes the state half.
- Unit (`src/engine/retention.rs`): extend the orphan tests (next to `dead_orphans…`) with snapshot dirs in each of the keep/sweep states above, plus a dir belonging to another target's committed transaction in a shared client dir (kept).
- Unit (`src/engine/tx.rs`, `undo.rs`): `an_error_at_any_failpoint_leaves_folders_wholly_old_or_wholly_new` and `an_error_at_any_failpoint_leaves_the_undo_wholly_done_or_not_done` with the stricter `leftovers()`.
- Integration (`tests/engine_crash.rs`): the matrices assert no snapshot dir without a history line after the recovering command (omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.5 builds on this).
- Integration (`tests/fsx_prune.rs`): a snapshot dir is prunable under `LockUse::Own` and `Held`.

## Considerations

- Ordering with omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1: once omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1 snapshots SavedVariables before the lock, step 3 (cleanup of a non-committed tx) is what removes them after a `locked` timeout or a `plan_stale`. Land omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2 first or together with omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1 (keep an unfinished journal, stage dir and snapshot when in-process recovery fails) also edits `cleanup()` and `recover_parsed`. This bead's rule is compatible: prune snapshots only once no journal remains. Whichever lands second rebases onto the other.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1–omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.4 may change `recover_parsed` further. Keep the `AddOns/` guard whatever they do, so a recovery bug can never escalate into deleting a folder.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.7 pins the snapshots a deferred SavedVariables restore needs. Those transactions have history lines, so this sweep never touches them.
- History reads: `history.jsonl` is append-only and read whole. Reading it unfiltered once per retention run is fine at M2 sizes, and it is already read once per run.
- Do not sweep a tx dir whose name does not parse as a `TxId`. Unknown entries are left alone (doctor, M4, can report them).
- The state half is global (`<state>/omaddons/snapshots/`), so the sweep may remove orphans of any target. That is correct, since the conditions are per tx.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1`: A failed in-process recovery deletes the journal and the stage dir holding the old folders
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.6`: A torn history line swallows the next transaction; roll-forward re-appends onto it
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1`: The global lock is held for seconds when SavedVariables or undone folders are large
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.7`: Retention can prune the snapshot a deferred SavedVariables restore still needs
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.5`: Close the crash-matrix gaps: Nth rename, undo, SavedVariables, failed recovery, snapshots
- `omad-gfoq`: install --dry-run creates inflight/ and trash/ in the state directory
acceptance_criteria: recovery and in-process rollback prune the rolled-back transaction's client and state snapshot dirs (kept only if AddOns/ still holds an entry); cleanup prunes the snapshot dirs of a transaction that did not commit; retention sweeps snapshot dirs whose tx has no history line, no live in-flight lock and no journal, older than ORPHAN_MIN_AGE; every leftover check in tx.rs, undo.rs and the crash matrices includes snapshot dirs; README Retention says so; argc gate passes
close_reason: Snapshot dirs of transactions that never commit are removed: by recovery after a rollback or an unprepared journal, by cleanup when the caller did not see the commit and history does not name the tx, and by retention's orphan sweep (no history mention, lock, or journal; older than ORPHAN_MIN_AGE). A client half whose AddOns/ holds an entry is kept, and journal_recovered says so. README Retention and Interrupted runs updated; vision comment added.

So 'a journal remains' is now exactly the case where recovery still needs both halves; prune snapshot/stage leftovers only when no journal names the tx.

title: Undo of an older transaction strands a dependency's later requesters without a warning
description:
## Background

README `remove` → **Dependencies**: "Removing an addon others still require goes ahead, with `still_required` naming them: they will not load without it … `undo` restores `required_by` exactly, even if the dependency was updated in between." M2-D35 (vision comment, M2 decomposition record): "`required_by` edits are history ops with an `edit` field; undo reverses them in place, and conflict detection ignores them."

Because conflict detection ignores in-place edits (`src/engine/undo.rs:533-596` `check_conflicts` filters `o.edit.is_none()`), `undo <older tx>` can revert a transaction that installed or updated a dependency after a later transaction made another addon depend on it. Two defects follow, both found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit and reproduced:

- **A. No `still_required`.** `restored_state` (`undo.rs:879-998`) drops the dependency's record when the reverted transaction installed it, and `FolderPlan::inverse` (`undo.rs:686-810`) removes its folders. Nothing checks who still requires it. `WarningCode::StillRequired` is raised only by `plan::bookkeeping_warnings` (`src/engine/plan.rs:707-761`), which undo never calls. The later requester stays installed and silently stops loading. `status` shows no attention either.
- **B. `required_by` loses later requesters.** When the reverted transaction updated the dependency, `restored_state` puts back the record from the snapshot taken before it (`undo.rs:944-951`, `record.addons.insert(addon_key.clone(), then.clone())`). That record predates the later transaction's in-place `required_by_add`, so the later requester disappears from `required_by`. Two consequences: removing the original requester later raises a false `orphaned_dependency`, whose fix (`omaddons remove BigWigs`) breaks the later requester, and removing the dependency raises no `still_required`. This contradicts the README sentence quoted above.

## Steps to Reproduce

Integration tests over replayed GitHub releases (the `tests/deps.rs` `graph` helper). Nodes: LittleWigs requires BigWigs, Other requires BigWigs, BigWigs. The catalog names all three.

A:
1. `install littlewigs` → tx1 installs LittleWigs and BigWigs (`required_by: [LittleWigs]`).
2. `install other` → tx2 installs Other. History op on BigWigs: `record` with `edit: {"required_by_add":"Other"}`. BigWigs `required_by: [LittleWigs, Other]`.
3. `undo <tx1>` → exit 0, `warnings: []`, `folders.removed: [BigWigs, LittleWigs]`. Other is still installed and requires BigWigs, which is gone. `status` lists no attention. Expected: a `still_required` warning "On retail, BigWigs is required by Other, which will not load without it", fix `omaddons undo <undo tx>`.

B:
1. `install littlewigs` (BigWigs v1 as a dependency).
2. Publish BigWigs v2, then `update bigwigs --refresh` → tx1 (BigWigs replaced).
3. `install other` → BigWigs `required_by: [LittleWigs, Other]`.
4. `undo <tx1>` → BigWigs back to v1, `required_by: [LittleWigs]` (Other lost), no warning. Expected: `[LittleWigs, Other]`.
5. `remove littlewigs` → `orphaned_dependency`: "BigWigs was installed as a dependency, and nothing requires it any more", fix `omaddons remove BigWigs -t retail`. Expected: no warning (Other requires it).
6. `remove bigwigs` → no warning. Expected: `still_required` naming Other.

(Reproduced on the development machine with scratch copies of these tests at HEAD 53b54e6.)

## Technical Approach

Decided: undo goes ahead, warns `still_required` exactly as `remove` does, and keeps `required_by` consistent by replaying later in-place edits.

1. **Replay later in-place edits onto restored records** (`src/engine/undo.rs` `restored_state`).
   - For every addon whose record is restored from the snapshot (`restored`), collect the later transactions' in-place edits on that addon: entries after the reverted one in `entries[at+1..]`, same target, not in `cancelled_after(..)` (reuse `undo.rs:598`), ops with `edit: Some(..)` whose `addon` key matches. Apply them in history order (`RequiredByAdd` adds, `RequiredByRemove` removes) after the restore and before the existing "forget requesters that are no longer recorded" filter (`undo.rs:976-984`).
   - Pass `entries` and `at` into `restored_state` (it gets only `reverted` today).
   - The undo writes no extra history op for this. The record simply keeps what later transactions did, as M2-D35 intends ("conflict detection ignores them" is only sound if undo preserves them).
2. **`still_required` on undo.**
   - After `restored_state`, compute the addons the undo removes from the record (in `current`, absent from the new `record`). For each, its dependents are the names in its **current** `required_by` (`current.addons[key].required_by`, which includes later in-place edits) that are still recorded after the undo.
   - Generalize `plan::bookkeeping_warnings` (`src/engine/plan.rs:713`) into a helper that takes `(before: &TargetRecord, after: &TargetRecord, target, tx)` and yields `still_required` and `orphaned_dependency` the same way, then call it from both the planner path and undo.
   - Message as remove's: "On {target}, {name} is required by {dependents}, which will not load without it".
   - Fix: `omaddons undo <this undo's tx>` (re-applies the reverted transaction, bringing the dependency back). Under `--dry-run`: the text suggestion remove uses.
   - Push it into `Planned.warnings` (`undo.rs` `plan()`), so `--dry-run` and the real run both report it, and `undo --run` reports it per transaction.
   - `orphaned_dependency` from an undo: raise it too, when the undo leaves a dependency required by nothing (e.g. undoing Other's install in scenario A, after tx1). Same helper, same fix as remove's.
3. **Rejected alternatives.**
   - Refusing with `undo_conflict`. It would make an older install impossible to undo until every later requester is removed, and README says a still-required remove goes ahead.
   - Keeping BigWigs installed automatically. Undo would no longer be the inverse of the transaction the user named.
   - Recomputing `required_by` from TOC dependencies. That is the planner's job; undo restores records and must stay offline and exact.
4. **Contract (DEC-4, before the M4 freeze).** No new code or key: `undo` can now emit `still_required` and `orphaned_dependency`. README:
   - in `undo [TX]`, add "Undoing a transaction that installed or updated a dependency still required by an addon installed later goes ahead with `still_required`, as `remove` does";
   - fix the `remove` paragraph's last sentences to match;
   - `still_required` row in the warning table: "a removed addon (by `remove` or `undo`) …".
   Record a vision comment on `omad-vision-8qa` refining M2-D35: undo replays later in-place `required_by` edits onto restored records and warns `still_required`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Scenario A: `undo <tx1>` and `undo <tx1> --dry-run` each carry exactly one `still_required` naming BigWigs and Other. Its fix argv is `omaddons undo <undo tx>` (dry-run: the text suggestion). Folders and records otherwise exactly as today.
- Scenario B: after `undo <tx1>`, BigWigs `required_by == [LittleWigs, Other]`. `remove littlewigs` raises no `orphaned_dependency`. `remove bigwigs` raises `still_required` naming Other.
- Existing undo tests unchanged, notably `an_install_is_undone_after_its_dependency_updates`, `a_remove_that_dropped_a_requirement_is_undone_exactly` and `conflicts_ignore_in_place_edits_on_both_sides` (`src/engine/undo.rs:1980-2085`).
- Undoing the undo restores the state before it exactly, `required_by` included.
- README and vision comment updated.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/undo.rs`, the `required_by` test module near `scene_with_requirement`):
  - replay of a later `RequiredByAdd`, and of an add then a remove;
  - a later edit by a transaction since undone is not replayed;
  - `still_required` for a removed dependency with a staying requester, none when the requester goes too (both in the reverted transaction);
  - `orphaned_dependency` when the undo leaves a dependency unrequired.
- Unit (`src/engine/plan.rs`): the generalized bookkeeping helper keeps `bookkeeping_warns_once_per_still_required_removal_and_once_for_every_orphan` green.
- Integration (`tests/deps.rs`): `undo_of_an_older_dependency_install_warns_still_required` (scenario A) and `undo_of_an_older_dependency_update_keeps_a_later_requester` (scenario B, steps 1–6).
- Integration (`tests/undo_history.rs`): `undo --run` over a multi-target run that includes such an undo reports the warning per transaction.

## Considerations

- History replay must use the same cancellation rule as conflict detection (`cancelled_after`), or undo-of-undo chains will diverge.
- Requesters named only by the reverted transaction's own direct ops (e.g. tx1 installed both LittleWigs and BigWigs) leave with it: LittleWigs is not recorded after the undo, so the existing filter drops it.
- `status` does not report "an installed addon's required dependency is missing" as attention. That is a doctor finding (M4); this bead only makes undo say it at the time.
- Performance: the replay walks history after the reverted entry once, which is already read for conflict checks.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.4`: Undo of a folder that exists nowhere else silently ends when retention prunes it
acceptance_criteria: undo (and undo --dry-run) that removes an addon still required by an addon that stays raises still_required with remove's message shape; an undo that restores a record from its snapshot keeps the requesters later transactions added in place (replaying their required_by edits); the two reproduction scenarios are integration tests; README undo/remove text and vision comment updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: Undo of an older transaction keeps later requesters in restored records (later in-place required_by edits replayed) and warns still_required / orphaned_dependency as remove does.

title: Undo of a folder that exists nowhere else silently ends when retention prunes it
description:
## Background

README promises undo without a bound for content that exists only in the transaction's snapshot:
- FAQ "Will it touch the addons I already have?": "Replacing one requires `--force`, and even that is undoable."
- `install` flags: "`--force` … replace an unmanaged folder (both undoable)".
- "Ownership and protected folders": "`--force` … replaces it, and the snapshot keeps the original for undo".
- The `unmanaged_folder` error section: "Replacing it instead is undoable".
- "Why use omaddons?" row: "Undo any change".
- `remove`: "Remove managed addons from one target, as an undoable transaction".

Only `update` says "(at least 24 hours)" (README `update`, for local changes).

Retention (`src/engine/retention.rs:95-127` `select`, limits `src/limits.rs:39-45`) deletes a snapshot for good once:
- it is older than 24 h, is not the target's most recent transaction, and either is outside the 7-day window or has 10 newer kept snapshots on that target;
- or the kept set passes 2 GiB.

After that, `undo <tx>` fails `not_found` ("snapshot for <tx> was pruned by retention", `src/engine/undo.rs:641-650`).

For most transactions that is fine: the old release can be installed again from its source. These folders exist nowhere else:
1. an unmanaged folder replaced by `install --force` (the user's own addon, or one from another manager);
2. `remove` of an addon adopted as it is: adopt records `release_id: None` when the files are not exactly a release (`src/app/adopt.rs:1071-1081`), and `blob_sha256` is absent;
3. `remove` or replacement of an addon installed from a local archive or directory (`--file`, `file:`): `release_id` `…@sha256:`/`…@dir:`, no blob (`src/model.rs:564-567`; `resolve::updates::is_static`, `src/resolve/updates.rs:151-157`), and the source file may be gone;
4. local edits replaced by an update or reinstall (`local_changes_replaced`, which already names the snapshot under `-v`).

None of these warn at commit time. Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit and reproduced.

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (`HOME`/XDG under a scratch dir, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, empty `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`), synthetic retail client.

1. Create an unmanaged `<client>/Interface/AddOns/Hand/` (`Hand.toc`, `Hand.lua` with the user's code).
2. `omaddons install gh:o/hand --file <dir>/Hand -t retail --force --json` → `ok: true`, `warnings: []` (tx A).
3. Age tx A: set its `at` in `<state>/omaddons/history.jsonl` to 9 days ago (stands in for a week of normal use).
4. Any other commit, e.g. `omaddons install gh:o/bar --file <dir>/Bar -t retail --json`. Retention runs and tx A's snapshot is pruned.
5. `omaddons undo <tx A> --json` → `not_found`, "snapshot for <tx A> was pruned by retention". The hand-made `Hand/` is gone for good. Nothing at step 2 said that undo had a deadline.

## Technical Approach

Decided: warn at commit time with a new warning code, and state the bound in README wherever undo of such content is promised. Retention behaviour does not change.

1. **Predicate** (a pure helper next to `plan::local_changes_warning`, `src/engine/plan.rs:686`): `only_copy(folder, owner_before: Option<&AddonRecord>) -> bool` is true for a folder the transaction moves into `snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/` (`SwapOp::Replace` of the live folder, `SwapOp::Remove`) when either holds:
   - `owner_before` is `None` (an unmanaged folder replaced under `--force`);
   - the owner has `blob_sha256: None` and (`release_id: None` or `resolve::updates::is_static(owner)`).
   It is false for a folder whose recorded digest equals the incoming staged folder's digest with no local changes (a byte-identical reinstall), because the new live folder holds the same bytes. Folders with local changes are covered by `local_changes_replaced` (step 3), so they do not get this warning too.
2. **New warning `snapshot_only_copy`**, raised in `tx::locked` after the commit next to the `local_changes_replaced` loop (`src/engine/tx.rs:822-836`), and by the planner for `--dry-run`. One warning per transaction, listing up to 10 folders and counting the rest, as `local_changes_replaced` does.
   - Message: "On {target}, {tx}'s snapshot holds the only copy of {folders}: `omaddons undo {tx}` brings them back until retention prunes it (kept at least {min_age}; then pruned once {keep_last} newer transactions on this client exist, after {window}, or past the {cap} snapshot cap)". The values come from `ctx.retention` (the effective `[limits]`), not hard-coded.
   - Fix: `omaddons undo <tx>`. Under `--dry-run`: the text "nothing is moved under --dry-run; after the run, its snapshot holds the only copy until retention prunes it".
   - `-v` notes name the snapshot folder of each listed folder (as `tx.rs:827-834` does for local changes), so the user can copy it elsewhere.
   - `remove` and `sync --prune` go through the same engine path.
   - `undo` (`src/engine/undo.rs` `commit`) applies the same predicate to the folders it moves out, judged against the record before the undo. For example, undoing a `--file` install moves that folder into the undo's snapshot, its only copy if the source file is gone. Undo never prunes the reverted transaction's snapshot.
3. **`local_changes_replaced`**: append the same retention clause to its message (message text only).
4. **Contract (DEC-4, before the M4 freeze).**
   - New warning code `snapshot_only_copy` in `src/error.rs` `WarningCode`.
   - README warning table row: "a transaction moved folders that exist nowhere else into its snapshot; undo can restore them only until retention prunes it".
   - README text, with the bound stated where undo is promised:
     - FAQ: "…and even that is undoable for as long as the snapshot is kept (at least 24 hours; `snapshot_only_copy` says when a snapshot holds the only copy)". Also fix that answer's stale "Adopting existing addons into management is milestone 2": `adopt` shipped in M2.
     - the `--force` row; the Ownership table row; the `unmanaged_folder` section; the `remove` intro; the "Undo any change" row ("until retention prunes its snapshot").
     - Retention: "Undo of a pruned transaction fails `not_found`; for folders with no other copy, the commit says so with `snapshot_only_copy`".
   - Vision comment on `omad-vision-8qa` (§5.5 Undo and Retention).

Rejected alternatives:
- Pinning such snapshots forever. That breaks the 2 GiB cap and retention's purpose; a hand-made addon can be gigabytes of media.
- Refusing `--force` over unmanaged folders. It is documented and wanted, with `adopt` as the gentler fix.
- Copying the folder into a permanent backup area. That is backup work (M3 `backup` covers `WTF/`, not AddOns), so out of scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `install --force` over an unmanaged folder warns `snapshot_only_copy` naming it and the tx, with fix argv `["omaddons","undo","<tx>"]`; `--dry-run` warns with the text fix.
- `remove` of an addon adopted as it is (`release_id: null`) warns. `remove` of a `--file` install warns. `remove` of an addon from a GitHub release with `blob_sha256` does not. `update` of a GitHub-release addon does not.
- A byte-identical reinstall of a local directory install does not warn.
- `local_changes_replaced` messages state the bound.
- The bound in the message follows `[limits] tx_retention_count`/`tx_retention_days` and `snapshot_max_bytes` from config.
- README updated in every place listed; registry and vision comment updated.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/plan.rs`): `only_copy` table test (unmanaged; adopted with `release_id` None; `--file` zip; `--file` dir; GitHub release with blob; GitHub release whose blob was evicted, which has a `release_id` and so is false; byte-identical reinstall).
- Unit (`src/engine/tx.rs`): a forced replace in `TxScene` yields one `snapshot_only_copy` with the configured limits in its message and a `-v` note.
- Integration (`tests/install.rs`): `--force` over an unmanaged folder, real run and `--dry-run`, JSON and human output.
- Integration (`tests/remove.rs`): remove of an adopted-as-is addon (adopt first, as `tests/adopt.rs` does) warns; remove of a catalog GitHub addon does not.
- Contract (`tests/contract/`): the new code is registered and appears in the warning registry snapshot.

## Considerations

- Wording must not name account or character data. Folder names and the tx id are fine; snapshot paths only in `-v` notes, as today.
- `copy` installs onto another target from releases. Never an only copy unless forced over an unmanaged folder, which the predicate covers.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.6 makes the restore faithful (directory modes); omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2 keeps orphan snapshots from piling up. Neither changes this bound.
- Retention keeps the target's most recent transaction forever, so a `remove` that is the last change on a client stays undoable until the next change there. The message says "until retention prunes it", which stays true.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2`: Snapshot dirs of rolled-back and failed transactions are never removed
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.6`: Undo resets restored directories to 0755; the undo tests' digest is blind to it
acceptance_criteria: a commit (and its --dry-run) that moves into its snapshot a folder with no other copy (unmanaged under --force, or owned by a record with no blob and no upstream release) carries a new snapshot_only_copy warning naming the folders, the tx and the retention bound, with fix omaddons undo <tx> and a -v note naming the snapshot folder; local_changes_replaced states the same bound; README states the bound wherever it promises undo of such folders; error registry and vision comment updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: A transaction that moves a folder with no other copy into its snapshot warns snapshot_only_copy with the configured retention bounds, and README states the bound wherever undo of such content is promised.

title: Close the crash-matrix gaps: Nth rename, undo, SavedVariables, failed recovery, snapshots
description:
## Background

README "Safety model → Crash testing": "All 24 engine failpoints are armed as a real `abort` in a child process for first installs, installs, updates and removes. The state afterwards must be wholly old or wholly new". Vision §5.12 testing strategy: "Engine failure injection (failpoint hook) at every step of §5.5, asserting the invariant and journal recovery". Vision §5.5 "Invariant": "Multi-folder addons are consistent across crashes via the journal".

The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found five holes in that matrix (`tests/engine_crash.rs`; the failpoint list is `src/engine/tx.rs:62-87` `FAILPOINTS`):

- **(a) Only the first rename is ever crashed.** The matrices arm `<name>=abort` (`tests/engine_crash.rs:98`, `:309`, `:467`), which fires on the first hit. `engine.swap.before_rename` is hit once per journaled rename (`src/engine/swap.rs:462`), so a crash between the 1st and the Nth rename of a multi-folder swap (UpdateMany, Handover, an update that also drops a folder) never happens cross-process. The `@N` form (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs:3-5`) is used nowhere on it; the only `@N` in tests is `engine.lock.acquired=error@2` (`tests/engine_multi_target.rs:338`).
  - In the two-rename fallback mode (`fsx.renameat2.einval`), `tests/engine_fallbacks.rs:42-70` also crashes only the first hit. That hit comes before any rename, so the window where a live folder sits in the snapshot and its replacement is not yet in AddOns is never crashed.
  - `tests/journal.rs:255` simulates every executed prefix in process, which is the journal logic only, not the engine.
- **(b) Undo is not in the cross-process abort matrix.** Its only failpoint test is in-process `=error` (`src/engine/undo.rs:1756-1820`), which exercises the in-process `recover_tx`, not a crashed process recovered by the next one. Its list skips `engine.swap.before_rename` and `engine.recover.step`.
- **(c) No crash scene has SavedVariables.** `tests/common/engine.rs` writes no `WTF/` tree, so `engine.snapshot.sv`, a crash between the swap and the SavedVariables restore of an undo, and roll-forward of `sv_restore` are never crashed cross-process.
- **(d) No failed-recovery or torn-write scenes.**
  - `engine.recover.step` is in `FAILPOINTS` but the matrices arm failpoints only on the crashing command; the recovering command runs clean (`tests/engine_crash.rs:148`, `:354`, `:511`). A crash during recovery is untested.
  - Torn tails of append-only files (journal, `history.jsonl`, `actions.jsonl`) are tested only as journal parsing (`src/engine/journal.rs:793` `phases_torn_lines_and_unknown_types`), never as a scene the next command must recover.
- **(e) Leftover checks ignore snapshot dirs** (`src/engine/tx.rs:1230-1243`, `src/engine/undo.rs:1318-1331`, the matrices' journal and AddOns checks). Orphaned snapshot dirs (omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2) pass unnoticed.

## Technical Approach

Test-only work in `tests/engine_crash.rs` (and helpers in `tests/common/engine.rs`), with small production changes only if a scene finds a bug, each filed separately with `discovered-from` this bead.

1. **Nth rename, atomic and fallback (a).**
   - For each multi-folder scene (`Op::Update`, which replaces Foo and removes FooOld, plus `Shape::UpdateMany` and `Shape::Handover`), first count the reference run's rename steps: the journal's step records, or `actions.jsonl` rename lines.
   - Then for N in 1..=steps run `engine.swap.before_rename=abort@N`, and the same with `fsx.renameat2.einval=error,engine.swap.before_rename=abort@N`.
   - Assert the existing oracle: each folder wholly old or wholly new at the crash; after the recovering command all on one side, generation and history consistent, no stray AddOns entries, lock inode unchanged.
   - Assert that at least one N > 1 crashes a scene whose folders are mixed until recovery, which proves the window is reached.
2. **Undo matrix (b).**
   - `Op::Undo`: install v1, update to v2 (the reverted transaction), change the SavedVariables (a "play"), then `undo --json`.
   - Every `FAILPOINTS` name as `=abort`, plus `engine.swap.before_rename=abort@N` for every rename.
   - Oracle: folders wholly v1 or wholly v2; SavedVariables wholly the played version or wholly the restored one (an `sv_restore` past `swapped` must be completed by roll-forward); at most one `undo` history line, present iff the folders are v1.
   - Also an undo with `--saved-variables keep`, and with a running client (fake `/proc`) where SavedVariables are deferred.
3. **SavedVariables in every scene (c).**
   - `Scene::new()` gains a `WTF/Account/ACCT/SavedVariables/Foo.lua` and `.lua.bak`, plus one character's, so `engine.snapshot.sv` is on every path.
   - The oracle compares the SavedVariables bytes: install, update and remove never change them; undo changes them only as in step 2.
   - Add the debug byte-copy seam (`fsx.reflink.unsupported`) to one matrix run, so the copy path, not a reflink, is what crashes.
4. **Failed recovery and torn tails (d).**
   - For every crash point of the install and update matrices, run the recovering command with `engine.recover.step=abort@K` for K in 1..=its rollback or roll-forward steps, then a third clean command. Assert the oracle after the third.
   - Torn tails: after a clean commit, append half a JSON line (no newline) to `history.jsonl`; after a crash, truncate the journal mid-line, and separately truncate `actions.jsonl` mid-line. The next mutating command recovers to one side, and a read command reports without writing.
   - These scenes exercise the recovery bugs filed as omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1–omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.4 and the journal issue omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.6. They are expected to fail until those land, which is why this bead depends on omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.1 and omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.6. Do not mark them `#[ignore]`.
5. **Snapshot leftovers (e).** After every recovering command, assert that each dir under `<client>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/` and `<state>/omaddons/snapshots/` belongs to a transaction with a history line. That is omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.2's invariant, hence the dependency.
6. **Runtime.**
   - The matrices already spawn about 24 children per scene. The Nth-rename and recovery loops multiply that.
   - Keep each scene small (tiny folders, 1 KiB SavedVariables) and run each matrix in its own `#[test]`, so the harness parallelizes them.
   - If `argc gate` time grows past about 60 s for this binary, gate the K-loop of step 4 to K ∈ {1, last} in the gate and the full loop at milestone checkpoints via an env var. Document that in README "Milestone checkpoints".
7. **Docs.** README "Crash testing": add Nth-rename crashes in both swap modes, undo with SavedVariables, crashes during recovery, torn tails, and the snapshot leftover check. Update the Tests table row for `tests/engine_crash.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every scene's Nth-rename crash recovers to one side, in atomic and fallback mode; some N > 1 is shown to cross a mixed state.
- The undo matrix passes for every failpoint and every rename index, with SavedVariables wholly on one side.
- Every matrix scene has SavedVariables and asserts them.

title: Undo resets restored directories to 0755; the undo tests' digest is blind to it
description:
## Background

README "Safety model → Undo": "Folders come back byte for byte from `<client>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/`; tests compare tree digests." README "What works today" says the same: "`undo` restores folders byte for byte". The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit asked what that holds for.

How undo restores today:
- **By copy, not by rename.** `stage_trees` (`src/engine/stage.rs:197-238`) clones the snapshot folder into the undo's stage dir (`copy_tree`, `stage.rs:240-293`), so the snapshot stays intact, and the swap then renames the copy in.
- What `copy_tree` keeps:
  - file bytes and file modes (`CloneFile`; both `reflink_copy::reflink` and the byte-copy fallback in `src/fsx/sys.rs` `clone_file` keep the mode);
  - symlink targets (`SymlinkAtomic`);
  - empty directories (created before recursing).
- What it changes:
  - every directory gets `DIR_MODE` 0755 (`stage.rs:295-299` `create_dir`, `stage.rs:37`), whatever it was;
  - every file gets a new mtime.
  - Special files are refused with an error, which is fine.

The digests the tests use:
- The integration helper `tests/common/trees.rs:439` `tree_hash` covers entry kinds, empty dirs, symlink targets and file bytes, but not permission bits.
- The engine's unit tests compare `TreeDigest::compute` (`src/engine/undo.rs:1285` `tree()`; also `src/engine/tx.rs` scenes). `TreeDigest` hashes regular files only: "Symlinks and empty directories do not contribute" (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:106-110`, `compute` at `:146-168`). Those tests cannot see a lost empty dir, a lost symlink or a mode change.

Archive installs never contain symlinks and always stage 0644/0755, so the gap only bites folders that came from the user: `install --force` over an unmanaged folder, `remove` of an adopted hand-made addon, and local changes replaced by an update. Those are exactly the folders whose only copy is the snapshot (omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.4).

## Steps to Reproduce

Debug build, isolated environment (`HOME`/XDG under a scratch dir, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, empty `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`), synthetic retail client.

1. Put an unmanaged folder `<client>/Interface/AddOns/Hand/` there with:
   - `Hand.toc`;
   - `empty/` (an empty dir);
   - `libs/` (mode 0775) holding `lib.lua`;
   - `link.lua`, a symlink to `libs/lib.lua`;
   - `private/` (mode 0700) holding `p.lua` (mode 0600).
2. `omaddons install gh:o/hand --file <dir>/Hand -t retail --force --json`, then `omaddons undo --json`.
3. `find Hand -printf '%y %m %p -> %l\n' | sort`, before and after. `empty/`, `link.lua -> libs/lib.lua`, `p.lua` 0600 and every file's bytes match. `libs/` and `private/` come back 0755 (they were 0775 and 0700). Expected: identical.

## Technical Approach

Decided: restore directory modes, strengthen the tests' comparison, and state the claim exactly. The recorded `TreeDigest` stays as it is.

1. **`copy_tree` keeps directory modes** (`src/engine/stage.rs:240`). After a directory's children are copied, `Chmod` it to `(source mode & 0o777) | 0o700` through `mutate` (`Op::Chmod`). Owner rwx stays forced, because swaps, retention and prune must be able to move and delete inside it.
   - Order: chmod after recursion, so a 0500 source does not block its own children.
   - Archive staging (`stage()`) keeps its fixed 0644/0755 (README "Hostile archives").
   - The chmod runs in the untracked staging session, outside the lock.
2. **One tree comparison for engine tests.** Add `tree_snapshot(dir) -> Vec<(PathBuf, Kind, mode & 0o7777, Option<link target>, Option<sha256>)>` to `src/engine/testing.rs`: sorted, symlinks not followed. Use it where the undo and tx unit tests compare restored folders (`undo.rs:1285` `tree()`, the failpoint matrices). Extend `tests/common/trees.rs:439` `tree_hash` to hash permission bits too, after checking which callers compare across a staging boundary that legitimately changes modes: archive installs compare with archive-staged trees, so modes are equal there.
3. **Leave `TreeDigest` alone.** It is derived from files-index entries (`TreeDigest::from_entries`), which list regular files only. Making `compute` include symlinks and empty dirs would make it disagree with the index-derived digest. It is audit data for `actions.jsonl`, not the comparison undo correctness rests on.
4. **README "Undo"**: "Folders come back as they were from `<client>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/`: every file's bytes and mode, directory modes, symlinks and empty directories (restored files get new timestamps); tests compare all of these." Apply the same wording to the "What works today" row. Record a vision comment on `omad-vision-8qa` (§5.5 Undo: what "byte for byte" covers). No contract key changes.

Rejected alternatives:
- Only narrowing the README to "file contents". Directory modes are cheap to keep, and the folders affected are the user's own.
- Restoring by renaming the snapshot back instead of copying. The snapshot must survive, because undo of the undo needs it.
- Preserving mtimes. The client does not read them, and the files index is stamped at the restore (`undo_index`, `undo.rs:843`, after `wait_out_racy_slack`), so drift detection already works with the new mtimes. Old mtimes would gain nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After `install --force` over the folder above and `undo`, and after adopting it, `remove` and `undo`, `tree_snapshot` before equals after.
- Undo unit tests use `tree_snapshot` (or the extended `tree_hash`) for folder equality. A regression that drops empty dirs, symlinks or directory modes fails them.
- Archive installs still stage 0644 files and 0755 dirs.
- README Undo and the "What works today" row updated; vision comment recorded.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/stage.rs`): `stage_trees` of a source with an empty dir, a symlink, a 0600 file and 0700/0775/0500 dirs yields the same `tree_snapshot`, except 0500 → 0700.
- Unit (`src/engine/undo.rs`): a forced transfer (`a_forced_transfer_is_undone_for_both_owners`) and a new test that undoes a remove of a hand-made folder with that shape.
- Integration (`tests/engine_undo.rs`): `undoing_a_forced_replace_restores_modes_links_and_empty_dirs`, through the CLI, comparing with the extended `tree_hash`.

## Considerations

- `tree_hash` is used widely (`tests/deps.rs`, `tests/copy.rs`, real-machine tests). Hashing modes there could expose umask differences in fixtures built with `fs::create_dir_all`. Run the full suite; fixture dirs made by tests are 0755 under the default umask 022, the same as staging.
- Real-machine tests compare AddOns trees before and after undo. Directory modes of real addons are 0755, so they are unaffected.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.4 makes the snapshot the explicit only copy of such folders; this bead makes sure what comes back from it is faithful.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.4`: Undo of a folder that exists nowhere else silently ends when retention prunes it
acceptance_criteria: undo restores directory permission bits as they were (owner rwx kept); undo unit tests compare folders with a helper that covers kinds, empty dirs, symlink targets, file bytes and permission bits; a test undoes a forced replace and a remove of folders holding an empty dir, a symlink, a 0600 file and 0700/0775 dirs and finds them identical; README Undo states exactly what comes back (not timestamps); argc gate passes
close_reason: Undo restores directory modes along with file bytes, file modes, symlinks and empty directories, and the engine and CLI tests compare all of them.
