Evidence: unit stage staged_trees_keep_modes_links_and_empty_dirs (0775/0700 dirs, 0600 file, symlink, empty dir kept; 0500 → 0700; top-level 0750 kept; index lists regular files only), undo undoing_a_forced_replace_restores_a_hand_made_folder_as_it_was and undoing_a_remove_restores_an_adopted_hand_made_folder_as_it_was, tests/engine_undo.rs undoing_a_forced_replace_restores_modes_links_and_empty_dirs (CLI install --file --force, undo, tree_hash equal); all three fail with stage.rs stashed and pass with it; archive staging modes still pinned by tests/stage.rs. argc gate passes. decided: the adopt+remove path is tested without the symlink, because files_index refuses a folder with an inner symlink, so adoption never holds one. · found: none

title: Add game_running and reload_required tests for sync and copy
description:
## Background

README "Running clients": under `safe`, "Adds and replacements that keep the loaded TOC go through, with `reload_required: "reload"` … Removing a folder the client loads, or an update that deletes or renames the TOC it loads, is refused with `game_running` until it exits. On legacy and unrecognized custom clients, every change is refused". "`--while-running` lifts these folder rules for one command". Vision D30 and §5.5 "Running policy": "Every mutation outcome carries `reload_required: none|reload|restart` per target."

`sync` and `copy` mutate through `engine::run` (`src/app/sync.rs:663`, `src/app/copy.rs:270` pass `while_running`). They therefore go through the planner's policy check (`src/engine/plan.rs:3626-3637`, `running::evaluate`) and the re-check under the lock (`src/engine/tx.rs:595`). But neither `tests/sync.rs` nor `tests/copy.rs` contains a single running-client case: no fake `/proc`, no `game_running`, no `reload_required` assertion. `install`, `update`, `remove`, `adopt` and `undo` have them (`tests/install.rs`, `tests/update.rs:478-505`, `tests/remove.rs`, `tests/adopt.rs`, `tests/undo_history.rs`). Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit.

Behaviour today is right: on the development machine, in an isolated environment with a fake running process, `sync <file> --prune` returned `partial: true` with the pruned Foo `failed` `game_running`, and both folders stayed. So this is a test gap, not a bug. It matters because both commands fan out over several targets and fold per-item failures into a partial run (M2-D24, M2-D30), a path the existing running tests do not exercise.

## Technical Approach

Tests only. Use the fake process table as `tests/update.rs:478-490` does: `common::procfs::FakeProc` with a `Wow.exe` whose `cmdline` is the retail client's Windows exe path and whose `environ` has `WINEPREFIX`, assigned to `home.proc`. For a legacy client use `/usr/bin/wine <client>/Wow.exe`.

1. **`tests/sync.rs`** (reuse `prune_home()`, `tests/sync.rs:32`):
   - `sync_prune_of_a_loaded_addon_is_refused_while_the_client_runs`: the client runs; `sync --prune` with a file that drops an installed addon. Assert `partial: true`, the item `failed` with `error.code == "game_running"` and `details.reason == "loaded_toc"`, the folder still there, no `tx` for that target when nothing else changed, and `warnings` mirroring the failure.
   - Same with `--while-running`: removed, `reload_required` is `"restart"` (a dropped loaded TOC is `Restart`, `src/engine/running.rs:169-178`), with a `reload_required` warning, and `undo` brings it back once the client "exits" (clear `home.proc`).
   - `sync_install_of_a_new_addon_while_running_needs_reload`: a file adding an addon → installed, `reload_required: "reload"`, a `reload_required` warning.
2. **`tests/copy.rs`** (reuse `era_and_anniversary()` and `publish`):
   - `copy_while_the_destination_runs_reloads`: the destination (anniversary) client runs; copying a new addon installs it with `reload_required: "reload"`.
   - `copy_that_drops_the_loaded_toc_is_refused`: the destination has the addon at a release whose loaded TOC is `<Name>.toc`; the source's release ships only `<Name>_TBC.toc`. With the destination running, `game_running` (`loaded_toc`) is a failed item and the run is partial. With `--while-running`, it goes through.
   - Running source, idle destination: copy proceeds with `reload_required: "none"`. Only the destination's client matters.
3. **Legacy destination**: one `copy` or `sync` case onto a custom 3.3.5a client (`common::trees::CustomRoot`, as in `tests/update.rs`) while it runs. Every change is refused with `details.reason == "legacy_client"`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The tests above exist and pass. Each asserts the exit code, `partial`, the item status and error code, `details.reason`, `reload_required`, and the AddOns tree (`tree_hash`) where nothing may change.
- No production change. If a test exposes wrong behaviour, file a bug with `--deps discovered-from:<this bead>` rather than widening this task.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Integration: `tests/sync.rs` (three cases), `tests/copy.rs` (three cases), plus one legacy case in either file.
- Run with the default parallel harness; each case builds its own `Home`.

## Considerations

- `copy` resolves the destination's builds from release fixtures. The TOC-rename case needs a second published release for the source family. Follow `publish()` in `tests/copy.rs`.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.5 (fail closed on unreadable `/proc`) will add a variant where the fake proc root is unreadable. Add it to these files when omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.5 lands.
- Keep fixture names public-safe (fake account and realm names are not needed here).

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.5`: Running detection fails open: an unreadable /proc makes every client look not running
acceptance_criteria: tests/sync.rs and tests/copy.rs each cover a refusal under the safe policy (a prune of a loaded folder for sync; a copy that drops the destination's loaded TOC) with game_running per item and the run partial, the same with --while-running going through, an allowed replace reporting reload_required reload, and a legacy destination refusing everything; argc gate passes
close_reason: sync and copy now have running-client tests: safe-policy refusal and --while-running for a loaded prune, reload for adds, a legacy client refusing every change, and an unreadable /proc failing closed; copy shows only --to's client matters.

Add one such fail-closed case for sync and copy here (see tests/remove.rs::an_unreadable_process_table_fails_closed for the pattern).

No production change. decided: copy cannot drop a loaded TOC (it skips any addon --to has by ref, and without --force a same-name unmanaged folder is ownership_conflict), so its refusal coverage is the legacy and unreadable-/proc paths, with the legacy refusal in sync as the bead allows; the reason is asserted from the message because item errors drop details.reason/running (filed omad-7dee). argc gate passes. · found: omad-7dee

title: The single-writer scanner skips production code after #[cfg(test)] and misses write APIs
description:
## Background

CLAUDE.md and README "Invariants the build enforces": "Only `src/fsx/` writes to the filesystem (`tests/single_writer.rs` scans the source)". Vision §5.5: "a test fails if `std::fs` write/rename/remove/create calls appear anywhere else", and D26 (one writer). The scanner is a text matcher (`tests/single_writer.rs:10-171`). The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found blind spots. Each one below was confirmed by running the real `scan_source` on probe inputs (a scratch copy of the test file at HEAD 53b54e6); the flagged count is shown:

1. **It stops at the first column-0 `#[cfg(test)]`** (`tests/single_writer.rs:104-106`, `break`; the same `break` in `prune_is_called_only_from_its_allowlist`, `:269-271`). It assumes the attribute marks a trailing `mod tests { … }`.
   - `src/net/mod.rs:20-21` is `#[cfg(test)]` / `mod tests;` followed by 380 lines of production code (`:22-401`: the `Http` trait, the request stack, the guard wiring), which is never scanned. A sweep of every `src/**/*.rs` outside `src/fsx/` found no other file where production code follows the first column-0 `#[cfg(test)]`.
   - Probes: `#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests;\nfn f() { std::fs::write(..) }` → 0; `#[cfg(test)]\nfn helper() {}\nfn f() { std::fs::write(..) }` → 0.
2. **Write APIs not in `PATTERNS`** (`:15-35`), each probe → 0:
   - `std::fs::File::options().write(true).create(true).open(p)`;
   - `std::fs::DirBuilder::new().create(p)`;
   - `file.set_permissions(perms)`: only `fs::set_permissions(` is listed;
   - `file.set_modified(t)` / `set_times`;
   - `std::os::unix::fs::chown(..)` (also `lchown`, `fchown`);
   - `t.persist_noclobber(p)` on a `NamedTempFile` that came from elsewhere: `.persist(` does not match `.persist_noclobber(`.
3. **rustix** (`RUSTIX_WRITES`, `:38-45`, matched only on a line containing `rustix::fs::`):
   - a multi-line `use rustix::fs::{\n renameat,\n CWD,\n};` then a bare `renameat(..)` → 0;
   - `rustix::fs::open(p, OFlags::WRONLY | OFlags::CREATE, ..)` → 0;
   - `rustix::fs::unlink`, `mkdir`, `chmod`, `ftruncate` → 0 each (`rename` is caught only because it also matches `fs::rename(`).
4. **Imports**: `use std::{fs::write, io};` then `write(p, b)` → 0. Only `use std::fs::…` is parsed (`:121-141`).
5. **Strings across lines**: `code_of` (`:64-95`) keeps no state between lines. After a string literal that spans lines, the rest of its closing line is treated as string, and a write on that line is missed: `let s = "a\nb"; std::fs::write(..)?;` → 0.
6. **Subprocesses**: `std::process::Command::new("rm")` → 0. Production spawns today are git (`src/sources/git_hosts.rs:122`, which writes checkouts under `<cache>/omaddons/tmp/<tx>/git/`, accepted in the vision's git comment) and the credential command (`src/state/config.rs:812`, stdout only). A new spawn would go unnoticed.

No real violation exists today. Grepping production regions for every pattern above finds only reads (`src/toc/loaded.rs:94` `rustix::fs::open` with `RDONLY`) and the two allowed spawns. The `File::options`/`set_modified` (`src/drift.rs:422-426`), `mkfifo` and `renameat_with` hits are all inside test modules. The scanner's stated rule (`:5-8`: "Test code is not production code (DEC-8): scanning stops at a top-level `#[cfg(test)]`") is what lets `src/net/mod.rs` slip.

## Steps to Reproduce

The scanner is test code, so the reproduction is a probe row in its own self-test, run in a scratch copy of the repository (never commit the probe):

1. In the copy, add rows to the table in `the_scanner_flags_writes_and_ignores_reads_comments_and_strings` (`tests/single_writer.rs`), each expecting 1 violation:
   - `("#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests;\nfn f() { std::fs::write(\"a\", \"b\").unwrap(); }", 1)`
   - `("fn f() { std::fs::File::options().write(true).create(true).open(\"p\").unwrap(); }", 1)`
   - `("use rustix::fs::{\n    renameat,\n    CWD,\n};\nfn f() { renameat(CWD, \"a\", CWD, \"b\").unwrap(); }", 1)`
   - `("use std::{fs::write, io};\nfn f() { write(\"p\", b\"x\").unwrap(); }", 1)`
   - `("let s = \"a\nb\"; std::fs::write(\"p\", s).unwrap();", 1)`
2. `cargo test --locked --test single_writer`.
3. Expected: the self-test passes (each probe is flagged). Actual (reproduced 2026-10-18 at HEAD 53b54e6): each of these rows reports 0 violations, so the assertion fails for every row.
4. On the real tree, no probe is needed for the first blind spot: `tests/single_writer.rs:104-106` stops at `src/net/mod.rs:20` (`#[cfg(test)]` before `mod tests;`), so `src/net/mod.rs:22-401` is never scanned. Adding `std::fs::write("x", "y").ok();` to any production function in that range (in the scratch copy) leaves `only_fsx_writes_to_the_filesystem` green.

## Technical Approach

Decided: keep the text scanner (fast, no new dependency), make it item-precise and stateful, and add the missing patterns.

1. **A small lexer state across lines.** Replace `code_of(line)` with a `Lexer` that walks the whole file and yields each line's code with comments and literal contents blanked. It carries across lines: inside a `"…"` string (escapes), a raw string `r#"…"#` (any number of `#`), a block comment `/* … */` (nested), a char literal. Lifetimes like `'a` must not open a char literal: treat `'x'`, `'\n'` and `'\u{..}'` as chars and anything else as a lifetime.
2. **Skip exactly the `#[cfg(test)]` items**, at any indentation.
   - When a line's code is `#[cfg(test)]` (also `#[cfg(all(test, …))]`, any form whose predicate requires `test`), skip following attribute lines, then skip the item: up to its terminating `;` at depth 0 (`mod tests;`, `use …;`), or from its first `{` to the matching `}` using the lexer's blanked code.
   - Resume scanning after the item.
   - Keep `#![cfg(test)]` (whole file) as today.
   - Apply the same item skipping in `prune_is_called_only_from_its_allowlist` through one shared iterator `production_lines(text) -> impl Iterator<Item = (line_no, code)>`.
3. **Patterns.**
   - Add to `PATTERNS`: `File::options(`, `DirBuilder`, `.set_permissions(`, `.set_modified(`, `.set_times(`, `os::unix::fs::chown(`, `os::unix::fs::lchown(`, `os::unix::fs::fchown(`, `.persist_noclobber(`, `NamedTempFile`, `TempPath`, `.extract(` (zip's tree extraction).
   - Extend `RUSTIX_WRITES` to `rename`, `unlink`, `mkdir`, `rmdir`, `chmod`, `chown`, `symlink`, `link`, `ftruncate`, `fallocate`, `copy_file_range`, `ioctl_ficlone`, `utimensat`, `futimens`, `mknodat`, `setxattr`, `fsetxattr`, `removexattr`. Match each as a whole identifier after `rustix::fs::`, or as a bare call `name(` when it was imported from `rustix::fs`.
   - Flag `OFlags::CREATE`, `OFlags::TRUNC`, `OFlags::WRONLY`, `OFlags::RDWR`, `OFlags::APPEND`, `OFlags::TMPFILE` anywhere outside fsx, since a write-mode open is a write.
4. **Imports.**
   - Parse every `use` statement across lines (brace groups, nested paths such as `use std::{fs::{self, write}, io}`) into full paths.
   - Flag any imported `std::fs::<FS_IMPORTS>` or `rustix::fs::<RUSTIX_WRITES>`, plus `use std::fs as …` (kept).
   - Record bare imported write names so a later bare `write(` is not needed for detection: the import itself is the violation, as today.
5. **Subprocess allowlist.** Flag `Command::new(` (and `process::Command`) outside an explicit allowlist with reasons, like `PRUNE_CALLERS`: `src/sources/git_hosts.rs` ("git checkouts in <cache>/omaddons/tmp/<tx>/git, removed with the tx's temp dir") and `src/state/config.rs` ("credential_command: reads its stdout, writes nothing"). The vision comment records the allowlist.
6. **Self-tests.**
   - Extend `the_scanner_flags_writes_and_ignores_reads_comments_and_strings` with one row per probe above, expected ≥ 1.
   - Add negatives: a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { const S: &str = "}"; fn t() { std::fs::write(..) } }` followed by clean code → 0; a block comment and a raw string containing a write → 0; `rustix::fs::open(p, OFlags::RDONLY …)` → 0; a lifetime `fn f<'a>(x: &'a str)` does not open a char literal.
   - Add a coverage self-check: `production_lines` over `src/net/mod.rs` includes line 22 and the last line.
7. **Doc comment** (`:1-8`): "scanning skips items marked `#[cfg(test)]`". Record the extended pattern set and the subprocess allowlist as a vision comment on `omad-vision-8qa` (D26 enforcement). No product contract change.

Rejected alternatives:
- A `syn`-based scanner. It would add a parse dependency (even if `syn` is already in the tree, a dev-dependency means `cargo deny`). Path resolution would still be needed for `use` aliases. And the text scanner, once stateful, covers the same ground.
- Moving `src/net/mod.rs`'s `mod tests;` to the end of the file. That fixes one file, not the rule.
- Exempting spawns entirely. A spawn that writes is a writer, which D26 forbids outside fsx unless named.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every probe input listed in Background is flagged. The negatives in step 6 are not.
- `only_fsx_writes_to_the_filesystem` and `prune_is_called_only_from_its_allowlist` scan `src/net/mod.rs:22-401` and every other production line. They pass on today's `src` with no new exemption except the two-entry subprocess allowlist.
- README "Invariants the build enforces" mentions the subprocess allowlist. Vision comment recorded.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit-style self-tests in `tests/single_writer.rs` (the file is its own test binary): the probe table, the negatives, the `production_lines` coverage check, and a lexer test over raw strings with `#`, nested block comments, escaped quotes and lifetimes.
- Integration: `cargo test --test single_writer` over the real tree.

## Considerations

- False positives are fixed by moving code into `src/fsx/`, never by weakening a pattern (the file's own rule). `.extract(` and `NamedTempFile` are specific enough. If `.set_times(` collides with an unrelated method name later, prefer a narrower pattern plus a self-test.
- Keep the scanner fast. It reads about 100 files once, so a per-file lexer pass is negligible.
- Subprocess writes cannot be proven absent by scanning. The allowlist only makes a new spawn a reviewed decision.
- The `git` checkouts under `<cache>` are outside fsx today by design. If a later bead routes git through fsx (e.g. clone into a stage dir created by fsx), drop it from the allowlist.

title: WoWInterface and Tukui downloads without a usable MD5 install unverified and silently
description:
## Background

README promises an MD5 check on every WoWInterface and Tukui download:

- "What works today": "WoWInterface: `wowi:` refs and links, keyless, every download checked against its MD5" and "Tukui (ElvUI and Tukui): … every download checked against its `ETag` MD5".
- Sources table, WoWInterface row: "then the file from `cdn.wowinterface.com`, checked against the MD5 the API publishes". Tukui row: "The download must match the MD5 in its `ETag`."
- Vision M2-D11 (WoWInterface release identity is `wowi:<id>@<md5>`) and M2-D13 ("the `ETag` MD5 is verified").

The code skips the check when the hash is missing and tells nobody:

- WoWInterface: `src/sources/wowi.rs:204-248` (`release`). `ExpectedHash::md5(details.md5.trim())` (`src/model.rs:1023`) returns `None` for an absent or malformed `UIMD5`. The asset then has `expected_hash: None`, so `BlobCache::download` checks nothing, and the release id falls back to `wowi:<id>@d<UIDate>`, or to `@d0` when `UIDate` is missing too (`wowi.rs:208-211`). No note is written, not even under `-v`.
- Tukui: `src/engine/blobs.rs:248-258` (`download_resolving`). When `etag_md5` (`blobs.rs:504-516`) rejects the header (absent, weak, unquoted or not 32 hex), the download is stored unchecked. The only trace is a `-v` debug line: "`…: no ETag; its MD5 is not checked`".
- The release memo's `CandidateFact` (`src/state/memo.rs:93-103`) records the download's SHA-256 with no mark that it was never checked. `TargetPlanner::fetch_blob` (`src/engine/plan.rs:3966-3972`) then reuses that blob on later runs with no download and no check.
- Existing tests pin the silent behaviour: `wowi.rs` `missing_fields_degrade_without_failing` asserts `wowi:1@d1700000000000` "no usable MD5", and `blobs.rs` `a_strong_etag_md5_is_checked_and_an_unusable_one_is_noted` asserts success plus one `-v` note. No integration test covers what a user sees.

Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit. The consequence: a user or an agent reading the output cannot tell an unverified install from a verified one, and the README claims a check that did not happen.

## Steps to Reproduce

Reproduced in an isolated environment with recorded-HTTP replay (`OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES=<fx>`, debug build) and a synthetic retail client (12.1.5, `.build.info` plus `_retail_/.flavor.info`, shaped as `tests/common/trees.rs` `BattlenetRoot` writes them).

1. Build a zip `Bar.zip` holding `Bar/Bar.toc` (`## Interface: 120105`) and `Bar/Bar.lua`.
2. Tukui fixtures:
   - `GET https://api.tukui.org/v1/addons`: a list with one entry, slug `bar`, `patch: ["12.1.5"]`, `directories: ["Bar"]`.
   - `GET https://api.tukui.org/v1/addon/bar`: the same entry, with `url` `https://api.tukui.org/v1/download/bar/TOKEN1`.
   - `GET https://api.tukui.org/v1/download/bar/TOKEN1`: 200, the zip, **no `etag` header**.
3. WoWInterface fixtures:
   - `GET https://api.mmoui.com/v3/game/WOW/filedetails/123.json`: `[{"UID":"123","UIName":"Bar","UIVersion":"1.0","UIDate":1791824100000,"UIFileName":"Bar.zip","UIDownload":"https://cdn.wowinterface.com/downloads/getfile.php?id=123&d=1&minion"}]`, with **no `UIMD5`**.
   - That `UIDownload` URL: 200, the zip.
4. `omaddons install tukui:bar -t retail --dry-run` and `omaddons install wowi:123 -t retail --dry-run`, each with and without `--json`.

Expected: each item warns that its download was not checked.
Actual: `retail: would be installed Bar 1.0 (1 folder)`. With `--json`, `"warnings":[]` and the item carries no warnings. Under `-v`, Tukui alone prints `{"event":"log","level":"debug","message":"https://api.tukui.org/v1/download/bar/…: no ETag; its MD5 is not checked"}`; WoWInterface prints nothing. `<cache>/omaddons/releases.json` `candidates` holds `{"release_id":"wowi:123@d1791824100000",…,"sha256":"…"}` and `{"release_id":"tukui:bar@1.0",…}`, neither marked unverified.

## Technical Approach

**Decision: warn, do not refuse.** A missing or unusable source hash installs with a new warning, `download_unverified`, in default output and in JSON.

- TLS to an allowlisted host still protects the transfer.
- The MD5 here is a corruption check, not a security boundary: `src/model.rs:1044-1046` says so for `HashFromHeader`, and the same source publishes both the hash and the file.
- A truncated or corrupt zip is still refused by the archive reader.
- Tukui's ETag-is-MD5 convention is undocumented. If it fails closed, one CDN change on Tukui's side would make every ElvUI install fail with no workaround but `--file`.
- `UIMD5` is normally always present, so on WoWInterface the warning should be rare. Refusing would gain little and would leave a file with a metadata gap uninstallable.

Steps:

1. **Warning code.** Add `DownloadUnverified = "download_unverified"` to `warning_codes!` in `src/error.rs` (after `TargetAddonsShared`), with a doc comment: "A download installed without the hash its source normally publishes; TLS protected the transfer, and the TOCs were verified."
2. **Carry the reason out of the download.**
   - `BlobCache::download` and `download_resolving` (`src/engine/blobs.rs:208-264`) return the reason alongside the `BlobRef`, for example `Downloaded { blob, unverified: Option<String> }`, instead of pushing it into `notes`.
   - `notes` stays for genuinely `-v` detail.
   - The reason is `"<source> published no usable MD5 for it"` or the existing `etag_md5` wording (`no ETag`, `a weak ETag (…)`, …), always redacted through `crate::net::redact`.
3. **WoWInterface.** An asset whose source normally publishes an MD5 but did not must be distinguishable from one that never has a hash (GitHub release assets, `url:`).
   - Add the expectation to the asset. Simplest: a new `ExpectedHash`-adjacent marker on `Asset`, e.g. `hash_missing: Option<String>` (serde default, skipped when `None`), which `wowi::release` sets to `"WoWInterface published no usable MD5 for it"` when `ExpectedHash::md5` returns `None`.
   - Tukui's `HashFromHeader::EtagMd5` path already knows.
   - Rejected: warning for every hashless download. GitHub release assets have no published hash at all, so that would be noise on every GitHub install.
4. **Planner.** `TargetPlanner::fetch_blob`/`download` (`src/engine/plan.rs:3923-4022`) puts the reason into `Downloaded` (the per-command `ctx.downloads` memo keeps it, so every target and engine run of the command sees it). `Winner` construction (`plan.rs:3862-3875`) then pushes `Warning::new(WarningCode::DownloadUnverified, format!("{name} {version}: its download was not checked: {reason}"))` into the winner's `warnings`, with no fix. These flow into the item's and the envelope's `warnings` exactly like `out_of_date`.
5. **Memo.** Add `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")] pub unverified: bool` to `CandidateFact` (`src/state/memo.rs:93`). This is additive and optional: no `schema_version` bump (M2-D36).
   - `TargetPlanner::learn` (`plan.rs:3896-3920`) sets it from the download. `merge_fact` keeps `unverified` true once set for the same release and asset.
   - The fact fast path (`plan.rs:3966-3972`) returns the reason again when the fact is unverified, so a reuse from the cache warns as the first install did.
   - A fact never claims a verified hash it did not check.
6. **WoWInterface release id.** In `wowi::release` (`wowi.rs:207-211`), when there is no usable MD5 use `@d<UIDate>` if `UIDate` is present, else `@v<UIVersion>`. Never `@d0`: two different files with neither field would otherwise share one release id, and an update would never be seen.
7. **README** (product contract):
   - "What works today" rows 143-144: "every download checked against its MD5 (a file published without one installs with a `download_unverified` warning)", and the same for Tukui's `ETag`.
   - Sources table, WoWInterface row: "checked against the MD5 the API publishes; when the API publishes none, the file installs with a `download_unverified` warning". Tukui row: "The download is checked against the MD5 in its `ETag`; a download without a usable one installs with a `download_unverified` warning."
   - Warning table: add the row and change "Every warning code (26)" to the true count (omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.5 owns the warning table; whichever lands second updates the count in the same commit).
8. **Vision bead.** Record a comment on `omad-vision-8qa`: "Post-M2 audit: a WoWInterface file without a usable `UIMD5` or a Tukui download without a usable `ETag` MD5 installs with the new warning `download_unverified` (DEC-4, before the M4 freeze); M2-D11's identity falls back to `@d<UIDate>`, then `@v<UIVersion>`; M2-D13's check stays fail-open, by decision."

This is a contract change allowed before the M4 freeze (DEC-4): a new warning code and a new optional memo field.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Fail closed on both.** Rejected for the availability reasons above.
- **Fail closed on WoWInterface only.** It is inconsistent, it gains nothing over TLS, and it would refuse a file the user can only install with `--file`.
- **Keep the `-v` note.** A user cannot see it, and the README claim stays false.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `install wowi:<id>` whose `filedetails` entry has no `UIMD5`, or a malformed one, installs, and the item and envelope carry `download_unverified`. The human output shows it without `-v`.
- `install tukui:<slug>` whose token download has no ETag, or a weak, unquoted or non-MD5 one, behaves the same way.
- A matching hash still gives no warning, and a mismatching one still fails `hash_mismatch` after one retry.
- The memo's candidate fact for an unverified download has `"unverified": true`. A later run that reuses the cached blob warns `download_unverified` again, with no request.
- A WoWInterface entry with neither `UIMD5` nor `UIDate` gets release id `wowi:<id>@v<UIVersion>`.
- README and the warning table describe exactly this, and a vision-bead comment records it.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit, `src/sources/wowi.rs`: update `missing_fields_degrade_without_failing` to assert the `hash_missing` marker and the `@v` fallback when `UIDate` is absent.
- Unit, `src/engine/blobs.rs`: change `a_strong_etag_md5_is_checked_and_an_unusable_one_is_noted` to assert the returned unverified reason, not `notes`. Keep the four bad-ETag cases.
- Unit, `src/state/memo.rs`: `merge_fact` keeps `unverified`. A memo without the field loads as `false`.
- Integration, `tests/sources_wowi.rs` and `tests/sources_tukui.rs`: replay scenarios with a missing hash.
  - Assert the warning in `--json` and in human output.
  - Assert the memo fact is marked.
  - Run a second `install --reinstall` and assert it warns again with zero new `net.log` lines.
- Contract: the warning-code list test (if one enumerates `WarningCode::ALL` against README) gains the row.

## Considerations

- `adopt` verification and `outdated --verify` download through the same `fetch_blob`. Their reports should carry the warning too, or at least must not report `exact` from an unverified blob without saying so. Check `src/app/adopt/apply.rs` and `src/app/outdated.rs` when wiring `Downloaded`.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.9 changes how a download's mid-body errors are classified in `store_checked`. Both touch `blobs.rs`, so land them in either order but rebase carefully.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.11 adds restarts to `download_resolving`. The unverified reason belongs to the attempt that succeeded.
- Do not regress M2-D28 (download each archive once per command). The reason must ride in the per-command download memo, not trigger another download.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.8 also adds a field to `Asset` (`flavor_source`). There are about 21 `Asset { … }` literals in `src/` and `tests/`; when both beads are in flight, update them by hand in one pass (no scripted edits, CLAUDE.md). Both fields are serde-defaulted, so memo files written before still load.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.9`: A download that fails mid-body is reported as an io error on the cache temp file
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.11`: A connection that fails while a body is read is never retried (API calls and downloads)
acceptance_criteria: a WoWInterface file without a usable UIMD5 and a Tukui download without a usable ETag MD5 install with a download_unverified warning in default and JSON output; the memo marks such a candidate fact unverified and a reuse warns again; a WoWInterface release id never falls back to @d0; README and the warning table say exactly this; argc gate passes
close_reason: A WoWInterface file without a usable UIMD5, or a Tukui download without a usable ETag MD5, installs with a download_unverified warning, in JSON and human output, recorded in the release memo so a cached reuse warns again.

title: A github.com link without a repository becomes a url: ref that downloads an HTML page
description:
## Background

README, Sources table: `https://github.com/o/r` becomes `gh:o/r`, and "any other `https://` link" becomes `url:`, "refused at plan time unless its host is allowlisted". `github.com` is always allowlisted, so a link to a GitHub *profile* passes that check.

In `src/sources/refs.rs` `url()`, the GitHub arm only matches `"github.com" if segments.len() >= 2` (`refs.rs:215`). `https://github.com/WeakAuras` (one segment) falls through to `format!("url:https://{rest}")` (`refs.rs:313`). The unit table even pins it: `("https://github.com/WeakAuras", "url:https://github.com/WeakAuras", …)` in `refs.rs` `CASES`.

What install then does (code trace, `src/sources/url.rs:43-91`, `src/engine/plan.rs:3723-3733`):

1. `UrlSource` accepts the host (`url.rs:58`) and makes one release whose asset is the profile URL, named `WeakAuras`.
2. The engine downloads the HTML page, one `asset` request of a few hundred KB.
3. The page is stored in the content-addressed blob cache, where it stays until LRU eviction.
4. Inspection fails with `bad_archive`, "the download is not a readable zip: invalid Zip archive: Could not find EOCD". The fix it gives is "nothing was installed; the archive holds no installable addon, so report it to the addon's author", which is misleading: there is no addon and no author.

Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit.

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment with `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1` and a synthetic retail client:

1. `omaddons info https://github.com/WeakAuras --json`
   - Actual: `"ref":"url:https://github.com/WeakAuras"`.
2. `omaddons install https://github.com/WeakAuras -t retail --dry-run --json`
   - Expected: `ref_invalid` (exit 2), no request.
   - Actual: `offline: not requesting https://github.com/WeakAuras`. Online it is one HTML download, then `bad_archive` (the not-a-zip message was observed with a replayed non-zip body).

## Technical Approach

1. In `refs.rs` `url()`, add an arm before the generic fall-through: `"github.com"` with fewer than two segments is `invalid(input, "a GitHub link names a repository: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>")`. That gives `ref_invalid`, exit 2, with fix `omaddons help install` (the house fix for `ref_invalid`).
2. Update the `CASES` row for `https://github.com/WeakAuras` to expect `ref_invalid`. Add `https://github.com/` and `https://www.github.com/WeakAuras/` (one segment after trimming).
3. README, Sources table `https://github.com/o/r` row: append "a github.com link that names no repository (`https://github.com/o`) is `ref_invalid`".

This is a behaviour change allowed before the M4 freeze (DEC-4). It refuses earlier, with a better code; no new error code is introduced.

Rejected:

- Turning an owner link into a search (`omaddons search <owner>`). That guesses at intent and sends the owner name to GitHub's search, while a ref parser should have no side effects.
- Leaving `url:` and improving the `bad_archive` message. That still spends a request and stores an HTML blob.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `https://github.com/<owner>` and `https://github.com/` parse to `ref_invalid` (exit 2), and `install`, `info` and `sync` make no request for them.
- `https://github.com/o/r` and every longer form behave as before.
- The README row says so.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `src/sources/refs.rs` `every_input_class` rows as above.
- Integration: `tests/install.rs` (or `tests/info_netlog.rs`). `install https://github.com/WeakAuras -t <id> --json` fails `ref_invalid`, and `net.log` stays empty.

## Considerations

- GitHub's non-repository namespaces (`orgs/<org>`, `users/<u>`, `settings`, `sponsors/<u>`, `topics/<t>`, `marketplace`, `apps/<a>`) parse today as `gh:orgs/<org>` and so on, and fail `not_found` after one `releases/latest` request. That is not a download of HTML, so it is out of this bead's scope. If it is ever tightened, reuse the same `ref_invalid` message.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.2 edits the same match. Coordinate.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.2`: Pasted GitHub release links lose their pin: tags are not decoded, slash tags are dropped
acceptance_criteria: https://github.com/<owner> and https://github.com/ are ref_invalid with the help install fix, never a url: ref, and send no request; the parser test row is updated; README says so; argc gate passes
close_reason: A github.com link that names no repository is ref_invalid (exit 2, fix omaddons help install) before any request, instead of a url: ref that downloads an HTML page.

title: A connection that fails while a body is read is never retried (API calls and downloads)
description:
## Background

Vision §5.13, `MAX_RETRIES` = 3: "Idempotent GET only; 429, 5xx, timeout or connection reset". README Network and privacy: "Retries cover 429, 5xx and network errors, up to 3 times with full-jitter backoff (0.5 s base, 8 s cap)".

`Retrying::send` (`src/net/retry.rs:128-171`) retries only what happens before the response headers arrive. It retries a 429/5xx status, or a transport `Err` with code `network`. The body is read after `send` returns, by the caller, so a reset or timeout during the body is never retried:

- **API calls.** Callers do `http.send(req)?.error_for_status(…)?.bytes()?`, for example `src/sources/wowi.rs:115`, `src/sources/tukui.rs:93-96` and `src/sources/github.rs:371`. `Response::bytes` maps the failure to `network` (`src/net/mod.rs:207-212`, `body_error`), but nothing sends the request again. The exception is requests with `validators: true` (feeds, the WoWInterface file list). `Validating` reads their 200 body inside `send` (`src/net/validators.rs:144`), so a mid-body error there surfaces from `send` and `Retrying` does retry it. The behaviour is inconsistent by accident.
- **Downloads.** `BlobCache::download_resolving` (`src/engine/blobs.rs:230-264`) streams the body into the blob store once. A mid-body failure ends the download. Today it even surfaces as `io`, not `network` (omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.9). The loop retries only a hash mismatch (once) and a dead Tukui token (403/404, once).

Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit. Consequence: on a flaky connection, one reset in the middle of a 50 MB archive fails the item (the run becomes partial) instead of being retried as documented. The `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` whole-call timeout (300 s) is a mid-body failure too.

## Steps to Reproduce

Code trace (the replay transport cannot inject a mid-body reset; a test needs a canned transport whose body reader errors after N bytes, as `src/net/tests.rs` `harness` builds):

1. Build a stack over a transport whose first response's body yields 100 bytes and then `Err(io::ErrorKind::ConnectionReset)`, and whose second response is a full 200.
2. API: `stack.send(Request::get("https://api.mmoui.com/…", "wowi-details"))?.bytes()`.
   - Expected: success after two transport requests.
   - Actual: `Err(network)` after one.
3. Download: `BlobCache::download(…)` over the same transport.
   - Expected: success after two requests.
   - Actual: an error after one (code `io` today; `network` once omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.9 lands).

## Technical Approach

**Decision: yes, a mid-body network failure starts the GET over from the first byte**, without `Range`, within the `MAX_RETRIES` budget and with the same backoff. Each attempt is already its own `net.log` line, because `LoggingReader` logs the failed one with `error: "network"` (`src/net/guard.rs:217-224`).

1. **API requests, in `Retrying`.** For `TimeoutKind::Api` requests, in the success branch of `Retrying::send` (`retry.rs:139-141`), read the whole body before returning:
   - `let mut body = resp.take_body(); let mut buf = Vec::new();`, then `body.read_to_end(&mut buf)`.
   - On `Err(e)` map through `super::body_error(e)`. If the code is `Network` and `attempt < MAX_RETRIES`, sleep `self.backoff(attempt)`, drop the response, increment and `continue`. Otherwise return the mapped error, which keeps `archive_too_large` and the log's own error as they are, unretried.
   - On success, `resp.set_body(Box::new(Cursor::new(buf)))` and return it.
   - API bodies are already read whole by every caller and capped at `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` (64 MiB), so buffering adds no memory. `take_body`/`set_body` are `pub(crate)` in `net` already.
   - `Limited` sits above `Retrying`, so the request keeps its permits across the retry, as header-phase retries already do.
2. **Downloads, in `BlobCache::download_resolving`.** Keep streaming (archives can be 512 MiB, so no buffering).
   - When `store_checked` fails with `ErrorCode::Network` (classified by omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.9) and `restarts < MAX_RETRIES`, increment `restarts`, sleep a full-jitter backoff (`BACKOFF_BASE × 2^restarts`, capped at `BACKOFF_MAX`), and loop.
   - The loop calls `resolve()` again, so a Tukui token is fresh for the restart. The atomic write already aborted, so nothing partial is left.
   - The hash-mismatch retry (once) and the dead-token retry (once) keep their own counters.
   - Expose the backoff computation from `net::retry` (e.g. `pub fn backoff_delay(attempt: u32, random: u64) -> Duration`) so both layers share it. Give `BlobCache` an injectable sleeper (`with_sleeper(Box<dyn Sleeper>)`, defaulting to `RealSleeper`) so tests do not sleep.
3. **Budget.** An API request makes at most `1 + MAX_RETRIES` attempts across header-phase and body-phase failures together. A download makes at most `1 + MAX_RETRIES` body attempts, and each attempt's `send` keeps its own header-phase retries.
4. **README**, Network and privacy: "Retries cover 429, 5xx and network errors, including a connection that fails while a response or download is being read (it is requested again from the start), up to 3 times with full-jitter backoff". Record a vision comment that §5.13's `MAX_RETRIES` now explicitly includes mid-body failures, with downloads restarting from byte 0.

Rejected:

- **Resuming with `Range`.** Not every allowlisted host honours it, and Tukui token URLs die within seconds. It is also not needed for correctness, since the hash and size checks run on the whole new body.
- **A transparent "re-GET and skip the bytes already delivered" reader inside `Retrying`.** A changed entity (WoWInterface `getfile.php` serves the *current* file) would splice two files, and only an MD5 source would notice.
- **Buffering downloads in memory.** Too large.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An API GET whose body resets after some bytes, then succeeds, returns the full body. `net.log` shows two lines, the first with `error: "network"`.
- Four consecutive mid-body resets on an API GET fail `network` after 4 attempts.
- A download that resets mid-body, then succeeds, stores the right blob after two requests. With a Tukui deferred asset, `resolve` runs twice.
- A download that resets 4 times fails `network` (retryable).
- A streamed body past the size cap, a hash mismatch, and a `net.log` failure are not restarted by this rule.
- README and a vision comment say so.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit, `src/net/retry.rs` tests: a `Script` transport whose body reader errors after N bytes (a small `Read` impl). Cover a retry and success, budget exhaustion, a size-cap error not retried (through `Guarded`), and a validators request still retried once only (no double counting).
- Unit, `src/engine/blobs.rs`: a `Serve`-like `Http` whose first body resets. Cover success after a restart, 4 resets failing, and a `download_resolving` restart that resolves again. The sleeper is a no-op recorder.
- Integration, `tests/net_replay.rs` is not possible (replay cannot reset), so the unit tests carry this.

## Considerations

- Worst case for a download that keeps timing out: 4 × `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` = 20 minutes. That is the vision's rule ("timeout" is retryable). If it proves painful, cap restarts after a timeout separately in a later bead.
- Priority 3, not 2: the failure is reported honestly (once omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.9 lands) and a rerun fixes it. No integrity or privacy is at stake.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.1 changes the shape of what `download_resolving` returns (the unverified reason). Keep the reason of the attempt that succeeded.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.1`: WoWInterface and Tukui downloads without a usable MD5 install unverified and silently
acceptance_criteria: an API GET whose body fails mid-stream with a network error is sent again within the same MAX_RETRIES budget; a download whose body fails mid-stream restarts from the first byte (deferred assets re-resolved) up to MAX_RETRIES times with the politeness backoff; each attempt is its own net.log line; size caps, hash mismatches and log failures are not retried this way; README says so; argc gate passes
close_reason: A connection that fails mid-body is retried as documented: API bodies are read inside Retrying within its budget, and downloads restart from the first byte (resolving again) up to MAX_RETRIES times.

comments.author: JaggedThistle
comments.text: omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.9 landed, so downloads now classify mid-body failures. What: engine::blobs Guard::read maps an inner read error through net::body_error (Interrupted passes through), so a reset or timeout while the body streams fails network (retryable) instead of io on the cache temp file. Why it matters here: this bead can now restart exactly the failures classified network, for downloads as well as Response::bytes. How: retry around BlobCache::store_checked in download_resolving when the error is network, honouring politeness.rs retry limits and starting the GET over (the temp write already aborts cleanly). Risk: never retry archive_too_large or a net.log io error, which body_error also returns. Done when a fixture body that resets once then succeeds installs, with two net.log lines for the asset.

title: search: a failed WoWInterface index fetch never makes the run partial
description:
## Background

README `search`: "A source not consulted is listed in `sources_skipped` (`offline`, `rate_limited` with `reset_at`, `disabled`, `no_index`). A spent GitHub search is not a failure; any other source failure makes the run `partial`. `--offline` searches the catalog, the stored index and the remembered Tukui list."

`WowiIndex::load_or_refresh_at` (`src/sources/wowi/index.rs:162-197`) never returns `Err`. A failed fetch becomes a `-v` diagnostic (`index.rs:188-195`) plus, when a stored index exists, a `stale_check` warning. Without one, the load just has `index: None`.

In `src/app/search.rs:343-381`, `Ok(load)` then only does `load.skipped()` (`index.rs:108-114`), always `no_index`. So the run is never partial, and the `Err(error)` branch at `search.rs:377-380` is dead code.

The Tukui list is handled differently (`search.rs:385-399`). Any error whose `skip_reason` (`search.rs:262-268`) is `no_index` makes the run partial with an item warning. `offline` and `rate_limited` do not. A rate-limited Tukui is therefore not partial either, although README exempts only a spent *GitHub* search.

The offline case is inconsistent too. With no stored WoWInterface index, `--offline` reports `wowi: no_index`, while Tukui reports `offline`.

Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit. Consequence: an agent reading `partial: false` believes WoWInterface was searched, when its index could not be fetched and no results came from it.

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment with a synthetic retail client and an empty replay fixture directory (`OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES=<empty dir>`, so every request fails):

1. `omaddons search bugsack --source wowi --json`
   - Actual: `{"ok":true,"partial":false,"sources_skipped":[{"source":"wowi","reason":"no_index"}],"warnings":[]}`. Under `-v`: `WoWInterface file list: replay: no fixture for GET https://api.mmoui.com/v3/game/WOW/filelist.json`.
2. `omaddons search bugsack --source tukui --json`
   - Actual: `"partial":true` with warning `the Tukui list: replay: no fixture for GET https://api.tukui.org/v1/addons`.
3. `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 omaddons search bugsack --source wowi --source tukui --json` (fresh cache)
   - Actual: `sources_skipped: [{wowi, no_index}, {tukui, offline}]`.

Expected per README: (1) is partial with a warning; (3) reports `wowi: offline`.

## Technical Approach

1. **Say what happened, in `IndexLoad`.** Add `pub failure: Option<Error>`, set when a fetch was attempted and failed (`index.rs:187-196`), and a private `policy: IndexPolicy`.
   - `IndexLoad::skipped()` returns `None` when an index is used.
   - With no index, it returns `Offline` under `IndexPolicy::Offline`; otherwise `rate_limited` (with `reset_at` from the error's details) when the failure is `rate_limited`; otherwise `NoIndex`.
2. **Stale fallback.** When a fetch failed but a stored index is used, extend the `stale_check` message: "the WoWInterface index is from {fetched_at}; refreshing it failed: {failure.message}". It is not partial, because results came from the stored copy, which `stale_check` already discloses.
3. **One rule in `search.rs`, for WoWInterface and Tukui alike.**
   - Not a failure: `offline` (the user asked) and `disabled` (config).
   - A failure: anything else that leaves the source contributing nothing, `rate_limited` included. Set `partial = true`, push `Warning::item(&error)` with the message prefixed by the source ("the WoWInterface index: …", "the Tukui list: …"), and list the source in `sources_skipped` with its reason (`rate_limited` with `reset_at`, else `no_index`).
   - GitHub keeps its README exemption: `rate_limited` is not a failure (`search.rs:426-430`).
   - Remove the dead `Err` branch, or keep `load_or_refresh` returning `Err` only for truly unexpected errors and route them the same way.
4. **README `search`**: keep the sentence and make it exact: "A spent GitHub search is not a failure; any other source that could not be read (its fetch failed, or it is rate limited) makes the run `partial`, with a warning naming the failure. A stored WoWInterface index used because a refresh failed is not a failure: its `stale_check` warning says so."

This is a behaviour change allowed before the M4 freeze (DEC-4). It uses no new codes. Record a short vision comment.

Rejected: making a stale fallback partial. Results were produced, and `stale_check` is the established signal for "answered from stored data".

## Acceptance Criteria

- An online search whose WoWInterface fetch fails with nothing stored is `partial: true`, with an item warning "the WoWInterface index: …" and `sources_skipped: [{wowi, no_index}]`.
- The same with a stored stale index returns its results, is not partial, and `stale_check` names the failed refresh.
- Offline with no stored index gives `sources_skipped: [{wowi, offline}]`, not partial.
- A rate-limited WoWInterface or Tukui is partial and listed `rate_limited` with `reset_at`.
- A rate-limited GitHub search is still not partial.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit, `src/sources/wowi/index.rs`: `load_or_refresh_at` with a failing `Http` sets `failure`. `skipped()` gives `Offline` under the offline policy and `NoIndex` otherwise. The stale message includes the failure.
- Integration, `tests/search.rs` (replay):
  1. An empty fixture dir with `--source wowi` is partial.
  2. A stored index older than its window plus an empty fixture dir is not partial, and the warning text names the failure.
  3. Offline with a fresh cache gives `wowi: offline`.
  4. A Tukui 429 with a long `Retry-After` is partial and `rate_limited`.

## Considerations

- `adopt` also uses `IndexLoad::skipped()` (`src/app/adopt.rs:528`). It gains the more accurate `offline` reason for free. Its partial semantics are not promised by README and stay unchanged.
- Dependency resolution (`src/engine/indexes.rs:122`) already names unconsulted sources in `missing_dependency`. Using `load.failure` for a better "could not consult: fetch failed" note there is optional.
acceptance_criteria: search with a failed WoWInterface fetch and no stored index is partial with a warning naming the failure; a stale stored index used after a failed refresh is not partial but its stale_check says the refresh failed; offline without a stored index skips wowi as offline, not no_index; Tukui and WoWInterface follow one rule (only offline, disabled and a spent GitHub search are not failures); argc gate passes
close_reason: search: a WoWInterface index or Tukui list that could not be read makes the run partial with a warning (rate limits included); offline and disabled stay states, a stale stored index used after a failed refresh says so in stale_check, and GitHub keeps its spent-search exemption.

title: Catalog families filter dependencies and adoption, though documented to restrict nothing
description:
## Background

README, The built-in catalog: "The last column is the families the publisher declares (in `release.json`, or the TOCs' interfaces). It is shown by `info` and does not restrict anything: TOC verification decides every install. … RaiderIO declares only mainline but its TOCs also load on vanilla and mists." `src/resolve/catalog.rs:8-11` says the same: "no target choice reads it and TOC verification alone decides an install".

Vision D5: "Verify TOCs inside the archive. Upstream metadata is wrong in practice."

In practice the families are a hard filter in two places:

- **Dependencies.** `src/resolve/deps.rs:285-290` (`resolve`, step 2) keeps only catalog entries whose `families` contain the target's family (or are empty). Otherwise the chain goes on to Tukui, then WoWInterface, then `missing_dependency`.
- **Adoption.** `src/resolve/adopt.rs:224-233` (`evidence`, row 1) emits `CatalogFolder` evidence only for entries declaring the target's family.

So on Classic Era (vanilla), a dependency on `RaiderIO` is not resolved from the catalog, although its TOCs load there, and adopting an installed `RaiderIO` folder on vanilla or mists loses its catalog evidence. `search` (`src/app/search.rs:338`, `CompatBasis::Catalog`) also shows `no` from families. That use is documented ("`yes` or `no`: the catalog's families") and stays.

What the filter protects: the five legacy git entries (pfUI, PlateBuffer, GroupBulletinBoard, MikScrollingBattleText, InFlight) must never answer a modern client's folder lookup. A modern addon requiring `InFlight` should reach WoWInterface's modern InFlight, not a 5.4.8 git branch. TOC verification would mark that branch out of date on retail (README: an older interface "gets an `out_of_date` warning"), and the dependency engine then reports `missing_dependency` (out of date, `src/engine/plan.rs:1690-1692`) instead of trying WoWInterface. That costs a download and loses the right answer.

Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit.

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment (`OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`) with synthetic retail (12.1.5) and Classic Era (1.15.9, `_classic_era_`) clients:

1. A zip `needsrio.zip` with `NeedsRio/NeedsRio.toc`: `## Interface: 120105, 11509`, `## Dependencies: RaiderIO`.
2. `omaddons install ./needsrio.zip -t retail --dry-run --json`: the dependency resolves to `gh:RaiderIO/raiderio-addon` (it then fails `offline`, as expected offline).
3. `omaddons install ./needsrio.zip -t era --dry-run --json`
   - Actual: `missing_dependency`: "NeedsRio on era requires RaiderIO, which was not installed: no keyless source consulted ships it (…)", with `unresolved: [{folder: RaiderIO, reason: no_source}]`.
   - Expected: the catalog's RaiderIO is tried, and its TOCs decide.

## Technical Approach

**Decision: families rank, they do not filter, within a client generation (modern or legacy, `Family::is_legacy`, `src/rules.rs:221`).** This keeps every outcome that resolves today and adds the TOC-decided ones.

1. **Dependencies** (`src/resolve/deps.rs` `resolve`):
   - Step 2 stays as is for *declared* entries (families contain the target's family, or are empty).
   - Steps 3-4 (Tukui, WoWInterface) are unchanged.
   - New last step, before returning anything other than `Resolved` from the WoWInterface step (none, ambiguous or abandoned): catalog entries for the folder whose families are all of the target's generation but do not name its family. One such entry (or one named like the folder) resolves with a new `DepVia::CatalogUndeclared`. Several are `Ambiguous` (`SeveralCatalogEntries`). None falls through to today's result.
   - Entries of the other generation never resolve.
   - Placing it last means no currently-resolving case changes.
2. **A refusal of an undeclared resolution is a warning, not a failure.** In the dependency planner (`src/engine/plan.rs` `plan_dependency`, `:1663-1705`), when the dependency came via `CatalogUndeclared` and its install fails `no_compatible_release` (or `wrong_flavor`), return `Err(UnresolvedReason::NotShipped)` ("The resolved project's archive does not ship the folder for this client"). The requester then gets `missing_dependency` with that candidate, instead of the run going partial.
   - Declared resolutions keep M2-D9: a failed install makes the run partial.
   - `RoundDep` needs to carry `via` for this.
3. **Adoption** (`src/resolve/adopt.rs` row 1): emit `CatalogFolder` claims for declared entries first, then for undeclared same-generation entries. Adoption already verifies by downloading and checking TOCs before `exact`/`identified`, so a wrong guess is caught. Never emit for the other generation.
4. **Wire.** `DepVia` is serialized in `unresolved[].candidates`/`DepCandidate.via` (`deps.rs:212-228`). Adding `catalog_undeclared` is a contract addition. Alternatively, keep `via: catalog` on the wire and carry the distinction internally. **Choose the internal flag**: the user-facing fact is "from the catalog", so the wire stays unchanged.
5. **Docs:**
   - README catalog paragraph: "It is shown by `info`, gives `search`'s `yes`/`no`, and orders lookups: a dependency or an adopted folder is matched first to entries declaring the client's family, and to other entries of the same generation (never a legacy entry on a modern client, or the reverse) only after Tukui and WoWInterface. It never refuses an install: TOC verification decides."
   - README install **Dependencies**: "the catalog (entries declaring this client first, …)".
   - `src/resolve/catalog.rs:8-11`: the same.
   - Vision comment: "M2-D8 refined: catalog families rank, not filter, within a generation (D5)."

Behaviour change allowed before the M4 freeze (DEC-4), with no new wire value.

Rejected:

- **Docs-only** ("families restrict dependency and adoption lookups"). It keeps a metadata filter D5 warns against, and RaiderIO-on-vanilla stays unresolvable.
- **Dropping the filter outright.** Legacy entries would shadow WoWInterface's modern projects (see Background).
- **Ranking undeclared entries before Tukui and WoWInterface.** A mainline-only entry that truly does not load would then hide a Classic port on WoWInterface. The engine tries one resolution per folder, with no fall-through after a refusal.
- **Fixing RaiderIO's families in `catalog/catalog.toml`.** The column is documented as what the publisher declares, and the live catalog probe checks it against `release.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a vanilla client, a required `RaiderIO` with no Tukui or WoWInterface answer resolves to `gh:RaiderIO/raiderio-addon` from the catalog. If its TOCs refuse, the requester warns `missing_dependency` (`not_shipped`, candidate listed) and the run is not partial.
- On retail, a required `InFlight` (legacy-only in the catalog) never resolves to the 5.4.8 git entry.
- On a 3.3.5a client, a modern-only entry's folder never resolves to it.
- Adopting a `RaiderIO` folder on vanilla gets catalog evidence, ranked after any declared entry.
- Every case that resolves today resolves the same way.
- README and docs updated, plus a vision comment.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit, `src/resolve/deps.rs` tests (helper `entry(name, ref, folders, families)` at `deps.rs:480`):
  1. A declared entry wins.
  2. An undeclared same-generation entry is used only after Tukui and WoWInterface miss.
  3. WoWInterface resolving uniquely beats an undeclared entry.
  4. A legacy entry is never used on a modern target, and the reverse.
  5. Two undeclared entries give `Ambiguous`.
- Unit, `src/resolve/adopt.rs`: claim order for declared vs undeclared, and no cross-generation claim.
- Integration, `tests/deps.rs`: the reproduction (era client, local requester, replayed RaiderIO release). An undeclared resolution whose archive does not load gives `missing_dependency` (`not_shipped`) and `partial: false`.

## Considerations

- `search`'s `yes`/`no` from families is unchanged. Showing `unlikely` instead of `no` for undeclared same-generation entries would be more D5-faithful, but it changes `commands` hints; leave it.
- Dependency limits (4 rounds, 32 dependencies) count undeclared attempts like any other.
- Only RaiderIO, MythicDungeonTools and Tukui declare few families today. The change is small in effect but removes a metadata filter.
acceptance_criteria: catalog families rank instead of filter in dependency resolution (declared entries first; then Tukui and WoWInterface; then same-generation undeclared entries, whose refusal is a missing_dependency warning, not a failure) and in adoption evidence (undeclared same-generation entries kept, after declared ones); legacy and modern entries never cross; README catalog, install Dependencies and catalog.rs docs say exactly this; argc gate passes
close_reason: Catalog families rank, not filter, within a generation: a dependency is matched to an undeclared same-generation entry after Tukui and WoWInterface (its TOCs decide, a refusal is not_shipped), adoption claims such an entry when none declares the family, and no entry ever crosses between legacy and modern clients.

title: Pasted GitHub release links lose their pin: tags are not decoded, slash tags are dropped
description:
## Background

README, Sources table, `https://github.com/o/r` row: "`/releases/tag/T` pins tag `T`, `/releases/download/T/F` pins tag `T` and installs exactly the asset `F` (or nothing: `not_found` naming the release's assets, or refused when it does not load)". The Pinning paragraph adds: "A pasted release link pins its tag the same way."

Two defects in `src/sources/refs.rs` `url()` break this. Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit.

1. **No percent-decoding.**
   - The tag and file are taken verbatim from the URL path (`refs.rs:226-234`) into `ParsedRef.version_hint` and `asset_hint`. `src/app/install.rs:464` makes the hint the install's `version` (pinned).
   - `src/sources/github.rs:366` and `:377` encode the tag again (`encode_tag`, `github.rs:473-478`), so `%2B` goes on the wire as `%252B`. The release is never found: the web path 404s, and the REST fallback (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:202`, `encode_path`) asks for the doubly-encoded tag, giving `not_found` after up to two web requests and one REST request.
   - The asset hint is compared byte for byte with release.json's `filename` (`src/engine/plan.rs:3013-3014`), so an encoded file name never matches either.
2. **Exact-length match arms.**
   - `["releases", "tag", tag]` (`refs.rs:226`) and `["releases", "download", tag, file]` (`refs.rs:230`) only accept a one-segment tag. A tag containing `/` falls through to `_ => with_url(gh())` (`refs.rs:243`), a plain `gh:` ref: the latest release, no pin and no asset.
   - GitHub writes slash tags with literal slashes. Questie's catalog tags look like `bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6`. GitHub's REST `html_url` for its latest release is `https://github.com/Questie/Questie/releases/tag/bundle/v12.1.0%2Bv1.0.6` (checked 2026-10-18). The recorded `releases/latest` redirect in `tests/fixtures/http/github-stable/github.com/get-Questie-Questie-releases-latest-5d9f1ab1.json` is `Location: …/releases/tag/bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6`.
   - For download links the tag spans every segment but the last, which is the file. omaddons itself requests `…/releases/download/bundle/v12.1.0%2Bv1.0.6/release.json` and GitHub answers it (the recorded `…-release.json-2e144701.json` fixture).

The same missing decode affects `/tree/<branch>` (`refs.rs:235-242`): the joined segments go into the `git:` rev still encoded, and `src/sources/git_github.rs:200` encodes them again.

User-visible consequence: pasting the link of the very release you want installs a different (latest) release, unpinned, and silently drops the named asset. Or it fails `not_found` for a tag that exists.

## Steps to Reproduce

In an isolated environment (HOME, XDG dirs and `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` on a scratch tree, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`) with a synthetic retail client:

1. `omaddons install 'https://github.com/Questie/Questie/releases/tag/bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6' -t retail --dry-run --json`
   - Expected: an offline error naming the pinned tag's `release.json` (`…/releases/download/bundle/v12.1.0%2Bv1.0.6/release.json`).
   - Actual: `"offline: not requesting https://github.com/Questie/Questie/releases/latest"`, which is the unpinned latest path.
2. `omaddons install 'https://github.com/Questie/Questie/releases/download/bundle/v12.1.0%2Bv1.0.6/Questie-v12.1.0.zip' -t retail --dry-run --json`
   - Actual: the same `releases/latest` request. Pin and asset are both lost.
3. `omaddons install 'https://github.com/o/r/releases/tag/v1.0%2Bbuild' -t retail --dry-run --json`
   - Expected: `…/releases/download/v1.0%2Bbuild/release.json`.
   - Actual: `"offline: not requesting https://github.com/o/r/releases/download/v1.0%252Bbuild/release.json"`, which is double-encoded.

Unit view: `parse_user_ref("https://github.com/Questie/Questie/releases/tag/bundle/v12.1.0%2Bv1.0.6", ctx)` returns `version_hint: None`.

## Technical Approach

In `src/sources/refs.rs` `url()`, GitHub arm (`refs.rs:215-244`):

1. Percent-decode each path segment after `owner/repo` with `crate::sources::github::percent_unescape` (`github.rs:436`, already used for `releases/latest` Location headers). Do it after splitting on `/`, so an encoded `%2F` inside one segment stays a literal `/` in the tag, which is what GitHub means by it. Decode owner and repo too before validating them with `is_github_owner`/`is_github_repo`. An encoded owner or repo is invalid anyway.
2. Replace the exact-length arms:
   - `["releases", "tag", rest @ ..] if !rest.is_empty()`: the tag is `rest.join("/")`.
   - `["releases", "download", rest @ ..] if rest.len() >= 2`: the file is the last segment, the tag is the others joined with `/`.
   - `["releases", "download", _]` (a tag and no file) is `ref_invalid`: "a release download link names a tag and a file".
3. Validate the decoded tag with the same rule the GitHub source uses (`github::valid_tag`, `github.rs:427`: no empty, `.` or `..` segment, no control characters). Make it `pub(crate)`. A bad tag is `ref_invalid`, never a request.
4. Validate the decoded file name: no `/` (it is one segment by construction), not empty, no control characters. Otherwise `ref_invalid`.
5. `/tree/<branch…>`: decode each segment before `join("/")`.
6. README: no wording change is needed. The table already promises this, and slash tags are simply tags. Optionally add "(GitHub's own links work as pasted, `+` and `/` in tags included)" to the Pinning paragraph.

No contract change: this makes shipped behaviour match the README.

Rejected:

- Decoding in `install.rs` instead of the parser. `info`, `sync` and anything else using `ParsedRef` would still see encoded hints.
- Treating the download link's second segment as the whole tag. That is wrong for every slash tag.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `https://github.com/Questie/Questie/releases/tag/bundle/v12.1.0%2Bv1.0.6` parses to `gh:Questie/Questie` with `version_hint: "bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6"`. The `+` form of the same link gives the same result.
- `…/releases/download/bundle/v12.1.0%2Bv1.0.6/Questie-v12.1.0.zip` parses with that tag and `asset_hint: "Questie-v12.1.0.zip"`. An encoded file name (`My%20Addon.zip`) decodes.
- `…/releases/tag/v1.0%2Bbuild` makes the install request `…/releases/download/v1.0%2Bbuild/release.json` (encoded once).
- `…/releases/download/v1` and a tag with a `..` segment are `ref_invalid`.
- `…/tree/feature%2Bx` becomes `git:https://github.com/o/r#feature+x`.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit, `src/sources/refs.rs` `CASES` table: add rows for the slash tag (encoded and literal `+`), the download link with a slash tag, an encoded asset name, the double-encoding case, `releases/download/<tag>` without a file, a `..` tag, and an encoded tree branch.
- Integration, `tests/sources_github.rs` (replay): reuse the `github-stable` Questie fixtures. Pasting the release link installs pinned at `bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6`, with no `releases/latest` request in `net.log`. Pasting the download link installs exactly that asset.

## Considerations

- `install.rs:451-458` compares `--version` with the hint after trimming `v`. With decoding, `--version bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6` plus the pasted link agree, as they should.
- Pinned versions also try a `v` prefix (`github.rs:213-219`). That fallback is unaffected.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.10 touches the same function (`github.com` with fewer than two segments). Land them together or rebase.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.10`: A github.com link without a repository becomes a url: ref that downloads an HTML page
acceptance_criteria: /releases/tag/<tag> and /releases/download/<tag>/<file> links percent-decode every segment, a tag spans every remaining segment (download links: all but the last); Questie's bundle/v12.1.0%2Bv1.0.6 link pins tag bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6; a %2B tag is requested once-encoded; /tree/<branch> decodes too; argc gate passes
close_reason: Pasted GitHub release links keep their pin: path segments are percent-decoded once, slash tags span every segment (the download link's last segment is the file), and bad tags or file names are ref_invalid.

Evidence: refs every_input_class rows (Questie slash tag encoded and literal +, download link with slash tag, My%20Addon.zip, v1.0%2Bbuild decoded once and %252B once, download without file, .. segment literal and encoded, control char, encoded / in file, tree feature%2Bx, encoded owner); tests/sources_github.rs a_pasted_release_link_pins_its_slash_tag_and_names_its_asset (github-stable replay: pinned bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6 fetched via …/bundle/v12.1.0%2Bv1.0.6/release.json, asset Questie-v12.1.0+v1.0.6.zip listed, no releases/latest, no %25, no REST). argc gate passes; argc fuzz ref_parse --time 180: 4351482 runs, no crash. title: git clone and fetch for git_hosts repositories have no byte cap and can fill the disk
description:
## Background

Vision §5.13: `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (512 MiB, config `limits.download_max_bytes`) is the safety limit on what a download may store. README Hostile archives and the `archive_too_large` row ("over the entry, uncompressed-size or download limit") present it as the guard against a source that sends too much.

The HTTP path enforces it twice: `src/net/guard.rs:139-147` and `:228-235`, and `src/engine/blobs.rs:477-491`. The git binary path for `git_hosts` repositories enforces nothing:

- `GitRunner::materialize` (`src/sources/git_hosts.rs:266-353`) runs `git clone --depth 1 --branch=<rev> --single-branch --no-tags -- <url> <dest>` (`git_hosts.rs:307-326`), or for a sha `git init` + `git fetch --depth 1 -- <url> <sha>` + `git checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD` (`git_hosts.rs:272-305`).
- `finish` (`git_hosts.rs:586-651`) waits only for exit or for the timeout (`DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT`, 300 s), polling every 10 ms. Nothing measures what git wrote.
- The working tree is measured only afterwards, by `inspect_dir` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:504-570`, entries and uncompressed size). That walk skips `.git` (`inspect.rs:553`). By then the pack and the checkout are already on disk.
- `finish`'s pipe readers (`git_hosts.rs:600-609`) `read_to_end` stdout and stderr without a bound, so a hostile server's sideband chatter is also buffered whole in memory.

Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit. Consequence: a hostile, compromised or simply huge repository on a listed host can stream data for up to 300 s into `<cache>/omaddons/tmp/<tx>/git/…`. At typical link speeds that is tens of GiB, enough to fill the filesystem that also holds the user's home.

## Steps to Reproduce

Code trace. A reproduction needs a git server that streams an oversized pack, which needs new test code (a local `file://` repository through `GitRunner::for_tests` with a large blob works; see `materialize_branch_tag_and_sha_and_a_moved_branch` in `git_hosts.rs` tests for the harness):

1. Create a local repository with a 2 MB file committed on `main`.
2. Set a cap of 1 MB (the runner's new cap field).
3. `materialize(url, "main", sha, dest)`.
   - Expected: `archive_too_large`, the process group killed, nothing above the cap left in `dest` after cleanup.
   - Actual today: success, with 2 MB in `dest`, and no cap consulted anywhere.

## Technical Approach

Reuse `limits.download_max_bytes`, not a new limit. A git checkout is a download, and the config key users already raise for big archives should cover it.

1. **Plumb the cap.**
   - `GitRunner::new(config: &NetConfig, log)` (`git_hosts.rs:94-104`) stores `config.download_max_bytes` (already in `NetConfig`, `src/net/mod.rs:259`, filled from the effective limits in `src/app/engine.rs:62-67`). `src/app/info.rs:343-350` builds its `NetConfig` with the default; that is harmless because `info` never checks out.
   - Tests build runners directly (`git_hosts.rs:672-685`): give them a field default of `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` and let a test set a small one.
2. **Watchdog.** Give `finish` an optional `watch: Option<(&Path, u64)>`.
   - Every 500 ms of the wait loop (not every 10 ms poll), sum `symlink_metadata().len()` over every entry under the watched directory, `.git` included, without following symlinks.
   - Past the cap, kill the process group exactly as the timeout path does (`git_hosts.rs:627-635`).
   - Return `Error::new(ErrorCode::ArchiveTooLarge, format!("the git checkout of {host}{path} grew past the {cap}-byte download limit"), Suggestion::text("if the repository is genuine, raise the limit: omaddons config set limits.download_max_bytes <value>")).details(json!({"limit": cap, "config_key": "limits.download_max_bytes"}))`. That is the same message family and details as `blobs.rs:481-490`, not retryable.
   - `run` (`git_hosts.rs:185-238`) passes the watch for the `clone`, `fetch` and `checkout` runs of `materialize`. `init`, `rev-parse` and `ls-remote` write nothing (or nothing of size) and get none.
3. **Check before staging.** After `materialize`'s last run succeeds, measure `dest` once more (a fast clone can finish between two watchdog ticks) and fail the same way past the cap. `TargetPlanner::checkout` (`src/engine/plan.rs:3874-3893`) then never hands an oversized tree to `inspect_dir`.
4. **Bounded output.** In `finish`'s pipe readers, keep at most `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` (`src/limits.rs:85`, 64 MiB) of each stream. Keep reading and discarding the rest so git never blocks on a full pipe. `ls-remote` output is parsed from stdout; anything past the bound is not a real ref listing, so a truncated listing that fails to resolve gives `not_found`, as today.
5. **net.log.** The killed run's `record_git` line carries `error: "archive_too_large"` and `status: null`, as the timeout line carries `network`.
6. **README.** In Network and privacy, the git subprocess paragraph gains: "A checkout is held to the download limit (`limits.download_max_bytes`): git is stopped, with its process group, once the checkout grows past it (`archive_too_large`)." In the Configuration table, the `limits.download_max_bytes` description gains "and git checkouts". Record a vision comment: "§5.13 `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` also bounds `git_hosts` checkouts (post-M2 audit)."

Rejected:

- **A new `GIT_CHECKOUT_MAX_BYTES` limit.** It adds a knob users would have to discover, and the downloaded-bytes semantics are the same.
- **`git clone --filter=blob:limit=…`.** That caps single blobs, not the total. It needs server support for partial clone and changes what is checked out.
- **Relying on `inspect_dir` alone.** It runs after the disk is already full and ignores `.git`.
- **`RLIMIT_FSIZE` on the child.** It caps a single file, not the total, and setting it needs `pre_exec` (unsafe is denied).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `materialize` whose checkout grows past the runner's cap fails `archive_too_large` (exit 4) with `details.limit` and `details.config_key`. The git process group is killed. The planner treats it as that candidate's failure, and the transaction's tmp dir cleanup removes the partial checkout.
- A checkout that finishes under the cap still passes, and one that finishes over it (between ticks) is refused by the post-exit check.
- Raising `limits.download_max_bytes` in config.toml raises the git cap.
- Captured stdout and stderr are each bounded at `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES`.
- README and a vision comment record the rule.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit, `src/sources/git_hosts.rs` tests:
  - A local `file://` repository (existing `Local` helper) with a 2 MB file and a 1 MB cap, for both the clone path (branch) and the init+fetch path (sha). Assert `archive_too_large` and the details.
  - The same with a 4 MB cap succeeds.
  - A stand-in `git` script that writes a growing file into the watched dir and sleeps proves the watchdog kills it before it exits, with its children (pattern: `a_slow_git_is_killed_with_its_children`).
  - A stand-in that prints more than the output bound to stderr and exits proves the capture is bounded and git is not blocked.
- Integration, `tests/engine_fallbacks.rs` or a new git-hosts scenario: an install whose checkout is over a lowered `limits.download_max_bytes` reports the item failed with `archive_too_large`, and nothing is left under `<cache>/omaddons/tmp/` after the run.

## Considerations

- Measuring a 20 000-entry tree takes a few tens of ms. At a 500 ms interval this is negligible next to the clone.
- Apparent size (`len`) over-counts sparse files. That is conservative and fine.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.6 (git's HOME) and omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.7 (the git net.log line) change the same `command`/`run`/`finish` functions, so sequence or rebase them. omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.4 changes `run`'s allowlist check.
- This bead is M2 scope: it bounds what M1/M2's `git_hosts` path already does. No new source.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.6`: git gets the real HOME, so libcurl can send $HOME/.netrc credentials to git hosts
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.7`: A git run succeeds when its net.log line cannot be written; HTTP fails in the same case
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.4`: The git and HTTP allowlists leak: git may reach any API host, HTTP may reach git_hosts
acceptance_criteria: a git run that writes into a checkout directory is killed with its process group once the directory passes limits.download_max_bytes and fails archive_too_large (exit 4, details.config_key) with a net.log line; the size is checked again after git exits; captured git output is bounded; README says the download limit covers git checkouts; argc gate passes
