title: A family override on a client with no readable version picks the fallback rules
description:
## Background

README promises two things about family overrides: "An unknown flavor folder still becomes a target. If its version cannot be read, it can receive installs only after you set its family" (`README.md:402`), and in "Per-target overrides" (`README.md:1517-1522`): `family = "wrath-legacy"  # a misdetected or unreadable client: re-picks its load rules`. Vision §5.3 and D29 make the rules row the single source of what a client loads.

The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found that the override re-picks the wrong row when the version is unreadable:

- A Battle.net flavor folder with no readable version gets version `0.0.0`, family `unknown` and the `fallback-battlenet` row (`src/discover/battlenet.rs:58-73`); a custom client likewise gets `fallback-custom` (`src/discover/custom.rs:70-86`).
- `apply_target_overrides` (`src/app/world.rs:221-241`) sets `target.family` and calls `Target::refresh_rules` (`src/model.rs:529-533`), which calls `RulesTable::rules_for_family(family, &version, kind)` (`src/rules.rs:640-650`). That function requires `row.covers(version)`; no versioned row covers `0.0.0`, so it returns the fallback again.
- `fallback-battlenet` (`src/rules.rs:1309-1323`) has no game suffixes, no game types and family suffixes `Mainline` before `Classic`. A `family = "vanilla"` or `"forever"` override therefore loads `_Mainline.toc` before `_Vanilla.toc`/`_Classic.toc`/`_Forever.toc`, never loads a game-suffix TOC, and refuses every `AllowLoadGameType` folder (`game_type_excluded`, `src/toc/loaded.rs:456-461`, sees only `mainline`/`classic`). Legacy overrides on custom clients happen to work because `fallback-custom` behaves like a legacy row.

Found while verifying (NEW, folded in here because it is the same function): the override never recomputes the **interface**. `apply_target_overrides` leaves `target.interface` as discovery computed it for the original row, and the legacy `lastAddonVersion` rule (`src/discover/custom.rs:87-92`, applied only when the *discovered* row is legacy) is skipped. Reproduced with a synthetic custom client whose exe reports 1.18.1 (see omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5): discovery gives family `vanilla` and interface 11801; `[targets.vanilla] family = "vanilla-legacy"` re-picks the `vanilla-legacy` row but keeps 11801, so every 1.12 addon (Interface 11200) installs with a false `out_of_date` warning ("older than the client's 11801"), and the client's own `WTF/Config.wtf` `lastAddonVersion "11200"` is ignored. Also, `unknown_flavor` keeps firing after the override, with the fix "set its family with a [targets.<id>] override", which the user already did (`src/discover/battlenet.rs:92-110`, `src/discover/custom.rs:93-107`: discovery emits it before overrides apply).

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment; a Classic Era folder whose `.build.info` has no row for its product (version unreadable):

```bash
ISO=<scratch>/iso-d4; mkdir -p $ISO/home/.config/omaddons $ISO/proc
run() { env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=$ISO/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$ISO/home/.config \
  XDG_STATE_HOME=$ISO/home/.local/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=$ISO/home/.cache \
  OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=$ISO/proc target/debug/omaddons "$@"; }
R="$ISO/home/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft"
mkdir -p "$R/_classic_era_/Interface/AddOns"; touch "$R/_classic_era_/WowClassic.exe"
printf 'Product Flavor!STRING:0\nwow_classic_era\n' > "$R/_classic_era_/.flavor.info"
printf 'Branch!STRING:0|Active!DEC:1|Build Key!HEX:16|Tags!STRING:0|Version!STRING:0|KeyRing!HEX:16|Product!STRING:0\n' > "$R/.build.info"
A=<scratch>/addons; mkdir -p $A/Multi $A/Gated $A/Fv
printf '## Interface: 120105\nm.lua\n' > $A/Multi/Multi_Mainline.toc
printf '## Interface: 11509\nm.lua\n'  > $A/Multi/Multi_Vanilla.toc
printf '## Interface: 11509\n## AllowLoadGameType: vanilla\ng.lua\n' > $A/Gated/Gated.toc
printf '## Interface: 16001\nf.lua\n'  > $A/Fv/Fv_Forever.toc
printf '## Interface: 120105\nf.lua\n' > $A/Fv/Fv_Mainline.toc
printf '[targets.era]\nfamily = "vanilla"\n' > $ISO/home/.config/omaddons/config.toml
run targets -v --json | jq -c '.data.targets[] | {id, family, rules: .details.rules}'
run install $A/Multi -t era --dry-run --json | jq -c '[.error.details.tried[]?.reason]'
run install $A/Gated -t era --dry-run --json | jq -c '[.error.details.tried[]?.reason]'
run targets --json | jq -c '[.warnings[]?.code]'
printf '[targets.era]\nfamily = "forever"\n' > $ISO/home/.config/omaddons/config.toml
run install $A/Fv -t era --dry-run --json | jq -c '[.error.details.tried[]?.reason]'
```

Expected: rules `vanilla`; Multi installs from `Multi_Vanilla.toc`; Gated installs; no `unknown_flavor`; with `forever`, Fv installs from `Fv_Forever.toc`.

Actual (HEAD 53b54e6): `{"id":"era","family":"vanilla","rules":"fallback-battlenet"}`; Multi `interface_not_in_family` with `interfaces: [120105]` (the `_Mainline` TOC was loaded); Gated `game_type_excluded`; `unknown_flavor` still reported; Fv `interface_not_in_family` with `[120105]`.

Interface part: a custom root `<home>/Games/turtle` with `Interface/`, `WTF/Config.wtf` containing `SET lastAddonVersion "11200"`, and a `WoW.exe` whose `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` is 1.18.1.7272 (build it with `tests/common/pe.rs::pe_stub(1, 18, 1, 7272)` or a port of it); `[targets.vanilla] family = "vanilla-legacy"`; `targets -v --json` shows `interface: 11801`, and installing a folder with `## Interface: 11200` warns `out_of_date` "older than the client's 11801". Expected: interface 11200, no warning.

## Technical Approach

1. **Row choice without a version** (`src/rules.rs:640-650`): when `version` is `0.0.0` (the "unreadable" value both discoverers use), `rules_for_family` returns the **first** row of that family whose install kind applies, ignoring version bounds. Rows of one family are ordered newest first (`mainline` 12.1.5+, then 12.0.7, 10.2.7, 9.1; one row for every other family), so this is the current client's row. Only when no row of the family applies to the kind (e.g. a `*-legacy` family on a Battle.net folder) does it fall back. Document it on the function and on `Target::refresh_rules`.
   - Rejected: a separate `version` override key (more config surface; the family is what users know); taking the oldest row (would deny comma lists and multi-TOC to a current client); leaving the fallback and documenting it (README promises the override works).
2. **Recompute the interface on override** (`src/app/world.rs:221-241`): after re-picking the row, set `interface` the way discovery does, through one shared helper (move the logic out of `src/discover/battlenet.rs:70-74` and `src/discover/custom.rs:83-92`, e.g. `discover::client_interface(&Target, &RulesTable) -> u32`): `interface_for(version, rules)` when the version is readable; on a legacy row, `WTF/Config.wtf` `lastAddonVersion` wins when present (`config_wtf::last_addon_version`); with no readable version, `lastAddonVersion` when present and inside the family's interface range, else 0 (the verdict then judges by the family range alone, `src/toc/loaded.rs:368-430`, and `out_of_date` cannot fire; say so in README's override paragraph).
3. **`unknown_flavor` after overrides:** emit it from `World::load_with` after `apply_target_overrides`, for every resolved target whose family is still `unknown`, instead of from the two discoverers. Keep one constructor (messages unchanged: "has no readable version" when the version is `0.0.0`, "runs version X, which no family covers" otherwise; "permissive modern rules" for Battle.net, "conservative legacy rules" for custom). Cached roots then carry no `unknown_flavor` (the cache is derived; it re-parses once anyway on the next basis change). Discovery-level tests that assert the warning move to the World/CLI level (`tests/discover_matrix.rs`, `tests/discover_custom.rs`: check which assert it).
4. **Tests:**
   - Unit (`src/rules.rs`): `rules_for_family` with `0.0.0` for every family and both kinds: `mainline`, `forever`, `vanilla`, `tbc`, `titan`, `mists` on Battle.net give their rows; `vanilla-legacy` on custom gives `vanilla-legacy`; `vanilla-legacy` on Battle.net falls back. Extend `rules_for_family_honors_a_decided_family` (`src/rules.rs:1673-1700`).
   - Unit (`src/app/world.rs` tests): `apply_target_overrides` recomputes the interface (1.18.1 custom → `vanilla-legacy` with Config.wtf 11200 → 11200; without Config.wtf → 11800) and keeps the label override.
   - Integration (`tests/targets.rs` or `tests/install_first_launch.rs`): the reproduction above as a test (vanilla and forever overrides; `targets -v` rules name; Multi and Fv install from the game-suffix TOC; Gated installs; no `unknown_flavor`).
5. **Docs:** README `:402` and `:1517-1522`: an override on an unreadable client takes that family's current rules; the interface comes from `Config.wtf` when the client has written one, else installs are judged by the family's interface range and `out_of_date` is not reported. Record on omad-vision-8qa (behaviour of overrides, DEC-4 allows it).

No new error or warning codes; `targets` and `status` JSON keep their shape (values become right).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `targets -v --json` on the reproduction shows rules `vanilla` (and `forever` with that override).
- Multi installs from `Multi_Vanilla.toc`, Gated installs, Fv installs from `Fv_Forever.toc` on the overridden era.
- A family override recomputes the interface; on legacy rows `lastAddonVersion` wins; the 1.18.1 custom example has interface 11200 and no `out_of_date` warning on an 11200 addon.
- No `unknown_flavor` for a target whose family an override set; it still fires without an override.
- README and the vision comment updated.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `src/rules.rs` (row choice without a version), `src/app/world.rs` (override recomputation), `src/discover/*` (shared interface helper keeps today's discovery results: the existing matrix tests are the net).
- Integration: the reproduction as a CLI-level test; `tests/discover_matrix.rs` and `tests/discover_custom.rs` adjusted for the moved warning.
- Contract: `tests/contract/` snapshots that contain `unknown_flavor` (if any) re-reviewed.

## Considerations

- The registry and records store no rules row, so no migration; a cached `Target` re-derives its row on load (`src/discover/cache.rs:206-218`), and must re-derive its interface the same way when an override applies (the override runs after the cache, so this holds).
- An override to a family whose row requires a newer client than the real one (e.g. `mainline` on a 9.x client with an unreadable version) gets the newest mainline row. Acceptable: the user chose the family, and the verdict still checks interfaces.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5 adds a custom version rule for 1.16–1.49 clients and may add an interface pin to version rules; the shared interface helper from step 2 is where that pin belongs. Either order works.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5`: Custom 1.12-based clients stamped 1.17/1.18 (Turtle WoW) are read as Classic Era
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.7`: ClientRules fields directive_conditionals, path_variables and game are read by nothing
acceptance_criteria: with no readable version, a family override picks that family's newest row for the install kind (vanilla, forever, mainline, every classic family), not fallback-battlenet; an override recomputes the interface from the new row, and on legacy rows Config.wtf lastAddonVersion wins as discovery does; unknown_flavor is not reported for a target whose family a config override set; the reproduction installs Multi from Multi_Vanilla.toc and the AllowLoadGameType-gated folder on the overridden era; argc gate passes
close_reason: A family override on a client with no readable version now takes that family's current rules row; every override recomputes the interface; unknown_flavor is said after overrides, so it goes quiet once the family is set.

title: Bottles reader misses moved bottles directories and custom-path bottles
description:
## Background

README "Where discovery looks" (`README.md:366`) promises: "Bottles: every bottle, including bottles kept at a custom path, native and Flatpak". Vision §5.2 step 1b lists Bottles among the launcher readers, and the 3.5 comment on omad-vision-8qa records "Bottles (native and Flatpak)".

The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found that custom paths are only half handled. `src/discover/launchers/bottles.rs:14-35` lists the children of `<data>/bottles/bottles` and of the Flatpak's `data/bottles/bottles`, keeps each child that has `drive_c/`, and follows an absolute top-level `Path:` in that child's `bottle.yml` (`custom_path`, `:39-46`). Verification against Bottles upstream shows neither custom-path mechanism matches what Bottles writes.

Bottles 67.4 (bottlesdevs/Bottles tag `67.4`, released 2026-09-07):

- `bottles/backend/globals.py:61-88`: `Paths.base = $XDG_DATA_HOME/bottles` (default `$HOME/.local/share/bottles`; inside the Flatpak `XDG_DATA_HOME` is `$HOME/.var/app/com.usebottles.bottles/data`, and `_get_wine_compatible_base` at `:42-58` may spell it `/var/data/bottles`, which is the same host directory); `Paths.bottles = f"{base}/bottles"`.
- `bottles/backend/managers/data.py`: `DataManager.__p_data = f"{Paths.base}/data.yml"`; `UserDataKeys.CustomBottlesPath = "custom_bottles_path"`.
- `bottles/backend/managers/manager.py:182-201`: when `data.yml` has `custom_bottles_path` naming a writable directory, **`Paths.bottles` becomes that directory** (every bottle lives there instead of `<base>/bottles`); a document-portal path (`/run/user/…/doc/…`) is refused.
- `manager.py:1916-1933` and `:1988-2000`: a bottle created at a custom location lives at `<path>/<name>` with `bottle.yml` `Path: <absolute>` and `Custom_Path: true`, and Bottles writes only a **placeholder** in the bottles directory: `<Paths.bottles>/<name>/placeholder.yml` with `Path: <absolute bottle path>` (no `bottle.yml`, no `drive_c/` there).
- `manager.py:1418-1450` (`check_bottles`): lists `Paths.bottles`; for a child with `placeholder.yml` it reads the real `bottle.yml` at the placeholder's `Path`.
- Both mechanisms are long-standing: `manager.py` of 51.9 already reads `UserDataKeys.CustomBottlesPath`, and `placeholder.yml` appears in both 51.9 and 2022.10.14.

So omaddons misses (1) every bottle when the user moved the bottles directory in Bottles' preferences, and (2) every bottle created at a custom path, because the default directory holds a `placeholder.yml`, and the reader skips a child without `bottle.yml` (`:26-28`). Its own model (an absolute `Path:` in a `bottle.yml` inside the default directory, fixture `fuzz/seeds/bottles/custom-path.yml` and `tests/common_selftest.rs:328`) is not a layout Bottles writes. A missed bottle is invisible unless it happens to be a direct child of `$HOME/Games`.

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment (native Bottles; the Flatpak layout is the same under `$HOME/.var/app/com.usebottles.bottles/data/bottles`):

```bash
ISO=<scratch>/iso-d5; H=$ISO/home; mkdir -p $H/.local/share/bottles/bottles $ISO/proc
run() { env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=$H XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$H/.config \
  XDG_STATE_HOME=$H/.local/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=$H/.cache \
  OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=$ISO/proc target/debug/omaddons "$@"; }
# (1) the bottles directory moved in Bottles' preferences
printf 'custom_bottles_path: %s\n' "$H/Bottles" > $H/.local/share/bottles/data.yml
mkdir -p "$H/Bottles/wow/drive_c/Games/Era/Interface/AddOns"; touch "$H/Bottles/wow/drive_c/Games/Era/Wow.exe"
printf 'Name: wow\nPath: wow\nCustom_Path: false\n' > $H/Bottles/wow/bottle.yml
# (2) one bottle created at a custom path
mkdir -p $H/.local/share/bottles/bottles/wow2
printf 'Path: %s\n' "$H/Other/wow2" > $H/.local/share/bottles/bottles/wow2/placeholder.yml
mkdir -p "$H/Other/wow2/drive_c/Games/Wotlk/Interface/AddOns"; touch "$H/Other/wow2/drive_c/Games/Wotlk/Wow.exe"
printf 'Name: wow2\nPath: %s\nCustom_Path: true\n' "$H/Other/wow2" > $H/Other/wow2/bottle.yml
# (3) control: a bottle in the default directory
mkdir -p "$H/.local/share/bottles/bottles/wow3/drive_c/Games/Ctl/Interface/AddOns"; touch "$H/.local/share/bottles/bottles/wow3/drive_c/Games/Ctl/Wow.exe"
printf 'Name: wow3\nPath: wow3\n' > $H/.local/share/bottles/bottles/wow3/bottle.yml
run targets --json | jq -c '.data.targets[] | {id, found_by}'
```

Expected: three targets (`era`, `wotlk`, `ctl`), each `found_by: launcher:bottles`.

Actual (HEAD 53b54e6): only `{"id":"ctl","found_by":"launcher:bottles"}`.

## Technical Approach

1. `src/discover/launchers/bottles.rs:14-35`, per install (native base `<data>/bottles`, Flatpak base `$HOME/.var/app/com.usebottles.bottles/data/bottles`):
   - bottles directories: `<base>/bottles`, plus `custom_bottles_path` from `<base>/data.yml` when it is absolute after `~` expansion (`expand_home`), is a directory, and is not under `/run/user/*/doc/` (skip with a diagnostic, as Bottles does). Read both: Bottles ignores the default directory once a custom one is set, but scanning it too is bounded and finds bottles left from before the move.
   - for each child (sorted): a prefix when `is_prefix`; `placeholder.yml` with an absolute top-level `Path:` → that path as a prefix (when it exists); `bottle.yml` with an absolute top-level `Path:` → that path (keep today's rule; a bottle under a custom bottles directory may record its absolute path).
   - `Hints::prefix` already de-duplicates. Every prefix keeps `launcher: bottles` and the install's `flatpak` flag.
2. Generalize `custom_path` into `top_level_path(text, key, home) -> Option<PathBuf>` (top-level line, `yaml_value`, `~` expansion, absolute only) used for `custom_bottles_path` and both `Path:` cases; keep `custom_path` as a thin wrapper if the fuzz target or tests name it.
3. Module doc (`:1-4`): the layout above with the upstream files and tag; drop "The keys and the Flatpak location are unverified". The Flatpak location follows from `globals.py` reading `XDG_DATA_HOME`, which Flatpak sets to `$HOME/.var/app/<app-id>/data`.
4. Test builders (`tests/common/launchers.rs:132-158`): `bottles_data(env, install, custom_dir)` writing `data.yml`; `custom_path_bottle(env, install, name, dir)` writing the placeholder and the real bottle (`bottle.yml` with `Custom_Path: true` and the absolute `Path`, plus `drive_c/`), as 67.4 does. Replace the `Some(path)` use of `bottle()` at `tests/common_selftest.rs:328` with the new builder and drop the override parameter if nothing else needs it.
5. Tests: unit tests for `top_level_path` (absolute, `~`, relative ignored, nested `Path:` under `External_Programs` ignored, CRLF); `tests/discover_launchers.rs`: both mechanisms, native and Flatpak, a document-portal `custom_bottles_path` (diagnostic, nothing found), a placeholder naming a missing directory (skipped silently), all with `found_by: launcher:bottles`. Fuzz: `fuzz/fuzz_targets/bottles.rs` also runs `top_level_path` with `custom_bottles_path`; add seeds `fuzz/seeds/bottles/data.yml` and `placeholder.yml` via `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs`, and replace `custom-path.yml` with a real-layout `bottle.yml` (`Custom_Path: true`).
6. README: `:366` stays true; extend it to "every bottle, including a moved bottles directory and bottles created at a custom path, native and Flatpak". `:1779`: drop Bottles from the UNVERIFIED list. Vision comment on omad-vision-8qa: the Bottles layout verified against 67.4 (files above).

Rejected alternatives: parsing `bottle.yml` fully (no YAML dependency, vision §5.2; only top-level keys matter); reading Bottles' gsettings (custom paths are not stored there in 67.4; `data.yml` is the source, `data.py`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The reproduction finds all three clients, `found_by: launcher:bottles`.
- The same holds for the Flatpak base.
- A document-portal `custom_bottles_path` is skipped with a diagnostic.
- Seeds and fuzz target cover `data.yml` and `placeholder.yml`; `argc fuzz bottles --time 600` finds nothing.
- Module doc and README updated; vision comment recorded.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `src/discover/launchers/bottles.rs` (`top_level_path` table, proptest on any text).
- Integration: `tests/discover_launchers.rs` (both mechanisms × native/Flatpak), `tests/common_selftest.rs` (builders), `tests/discover_matrix.rs` unchanged.
- Fuzz: `bottles` with new seeds.

## Considerations

- A `custom_bottles_path` or placeholder may point outside `$HOME` (another disk). Launcher-named prefixes are walked wherever they are today (Lutris and Heroic prefixes too), so this adds no new kind of reach; it stays read-only.
- Bottles' library (`<base>/library.yml`) and `External_Programs` name executables inside bottles; the `drive_c` walk of each launcher prefix already finds those clients, so they are not read.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.3 covers the remaining launcher readers; this bead closes Bottles completely.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.3`: Verify Lutris, Heroic and Steam readers against upstream and close cheap gaps
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.3.5`: Launcher config readers: Lutris, Heroic, Steam, Bottles (native and Flatpak)
acceptance_criteria: the Bottles reader lists bottles under data.yml's custom_bottles_path and follows placeholder.yml Path entries, native and Flatpak, as Bottles 67.4 writes them; document-portal paths are skipped with a diagnostic; fixtures and the bottles fuzz target cover data.yml and placeholder.yml; the module doc cites the upstream files and drops "unverified"; README's UNVERIFIED bullet no longer names Bottles; argc gate passes
close_reason: The Bottles reader follows both custom locations Bottles 67.4 writes: a bottles directory moved in its preferences (data.yml custom_bottles_path) and bottles created at a custom path (placeholder.yml), native and Flatpak.

title: Custom 1.12-based clients stamped 1.17/1.18 (Turtle WoW) are read as Classic Era
description:
## Background

README FAQ (`README.md:1880`): "Server-specific patches are not special-cased: Turtle WoW is a `vanilla-legacy` client." README `:414`: "Turtle WoW and other 1.12.1 servers are plain `vanilla-legacy` clients." Vision §4.2 and §8 mark Turtle's exe version UNVERIFIED; D29 promises private servers "correct rules without code changes".

A custom client's family comes from its exe's `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` (`src/discover/pe.rs`, `src/discover/custom.rs:69-86`) through the version → family table (`src/rules.rs:1020-1038`). Only exactly 1.12 maps to `vanilla-legacy` (`:1025`); any other 1.x below 1.50 falls to the general row `(None, 1, 0..49) → vanilla` (`:1030`), the Battle.net Classic Era family (interface range 11300–14999, multi-TOC, `src/rules.rs:1059-1068`).

Public evidence (2026-10-18) that Turtle WoW's client identifies as 1.17/1.18, not 1.12.1:
- Kelsidavis/WoWee (an open-source client) `Data/expansions/turtle/expansion.json`: Turtle WoW `"version": { "major": 1, "minor": 18, "patch": 1 }, "build": 7272, "worldBuild": 5875`; its README: "Turtle WoW defaults to authentication build 7272. Older compatible servers can use [7234]".
- tortoise-wow/tortoise-wow (a community restoration): "This project targets version 1.18.1 build 7272 … the final client version of Turtle-WoW"; its issue #251 mentions 1.18.0 build 7233 as the largest public download.
- A WRobot forum thread titled "Turtle WoW 1.17.1 client".
- Turtle's own UI addons, extracted from the client (refaim/Turtle-WoW-UI-Source, e.g. `Interface/AddOns/Turtle_General/Turtle_General.toc`), and its community addons (pfUI, a catalog entry: `pfUI.toc` `## Interface: 11200`; pfUI-turtle, pfQuest-turtle) all declare `## Interface: 11200`. So the client's addon interface stays 11200.

None of these is the PE resource itself; whether `Wow.exe`'s `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` carries 1.18.1 or still 1.12.1 needs a real file (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.4). The fix below is correct either way: a 1.12.1 stamp keeps today's rule, a 1.16–1.49 stamp gets the new one.

What happens today with a 1.18.1 stamp (reproduced with a synthetic exe): family `vanilla`, rules row `vanilla`, interface 11801; installing a 1.12 addon (`## Interface: 11200`) is refused with `wrong_flavor` (`interface_not_in_family`). The README's workaround (`[targets.vanilla] family = "vanilla-legacy"`) then installs it but warns `out_of_date` for every addon, because the override keeps the stale interface (that part is omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.3).

## Steps to Reproduce

Build a minimal PE with a version resource (port `tests/common/pe.rs::pe_stub` to a scratch script, or call it from a scratch test) and an isolated client:

```bash
ISO=<scratch>/iso-v3; T=$ISO/home/Games/turtle; mkdir -p $T/Interface/AddOns $T/WTF $T/Data/enUS $ISO/proc
run() { env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=$ISO/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$ISO/home/.config \
  XDG_STATE_HOME=$ISO/home/.local/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=$ISO/home/.cache \
  OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=$ISO/proc target/debug/omaddons "$@"; }
printf 'set realmlist logon.example.invalid\n' > $T/Data/enUS/realmlist.wtf
<write $T/WoW.exe = pe_stub(1, 18, 1, 7272)>
A=<scratch>/addons/Legacy; mkdir -p $A; printf '## Interface: 11200\n## Title: Legacy\nl.lua\n' > $A/Legacy.toc; touch $A/l.lua
run targets -v --json | jq -c '.data.targets[] | {id, family, version, interface, rules: .details.rules}'
run install $A -t vanilla --dry-run --json | jq -c '[.error.details.tried[]?.reason]'
```

Expected: `family: vanilla-legacy`, `interface: 11200`, rules `vanilla-legacy`; the install succeeds with no `out_of_date`.

Actual (HEAD 53b54e6): `{"id":"vanilla","family":"vanilla","version":"1.18.1.7272","interface":11801,"rules":"vanilla"}`; the install is refused: `interface_not_in_family`, `interfaces: [11200]`.

## Technical Approach

1. **Version rule** (`src/rules.rs:1024-1038`): add `(Some(InstallKind::Custom), exactly(1), between(16, 49), Family::VanillaLegacy)` after the 1.12 row. Custom 1.13–1.15 (a Classic Era client copied out of its Battle.net root) and 1.50+ (Forever) keep their rows. Comment it with the evidence and date; no client is special-cased in code (D15/D29): it is a table row.
2. **Interface pin:** `VersionFamilyRule` (`src/rules.rs:388-396`) gains `interface: Option<u32>`, "the client's addon interface when its version stamp does not give it". Set `interface: Some(11_200)` on the new row. The interface is computed in one place (omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.3 introduces a shared helper; if omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5 lands first, add `RulesTable::interface_for_client(&version, kind, &rules)` and use it from `src/discover/custom.rs:83-86` and `src/discover/battlenet.rs:70-74`): the matching version rule's `interface` when set, else `interface_for(version, rules)`; on legacy rows `lastAddonVersion` (`src/discover/custom.rs:87-92`) still wins. Without the pin, 1.18.1 on the `vanilla-legacy` row would compute 11800 (no patch digit), outside the family's 11200–11299 range, and every addon would warn `out_of_date` until the client first writes `Config.wtf`.
   - Rejected: clamping any legacy interface to its family floor (implicit and surprising for a real 1.12.x build); a ClientRules row per server (the row describes loading rules, which are plain 1.12 here; only the version stamp differs); special-casing the exe name (`WoW.exe` is shared with every other private server).
3. **Config:** `[[rules.version_families]]` entries accept `interface` (omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.9 adds it to the known keys if it lands first). README "Rules overrides (advanced)" (`README.md:1529`) says so.
4. **README:** the legacy table (`README.md:406-412`) gains a row: "1.16–1.49 custom builds of the 1.12 client (Turtle WoW 1.17/1.18) | `vanilla-legacy` | `vanilla` | plain TOC, interface 11200"; `:414` and the FAQ (`:1880`): Turtle WoW is a `vanilla-legacy` client whichever version its exe reports. Interface formula paragraph (`:435`): a version rule may pin the interface.
5. **Vision:** comment on omad-vision-8qa: §4.2/§8's "Turtle WoW's exe version is UNVERIFIED" is now handled by data (rule and pin, evidence and date); the remaining real-file check is omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.4.
6. **Tests:** `src/rules.rs` unit: `family_for` on custom 1.12.1, 1.16.0, 1.17.2, 1.18.1, 1.49.0 → `vanilla-legacy`; 1.13.0, 1.15.9 custom → `vanilla`; 1.60.1 → `forever`; Battle.net 1.15.9 unchanged; `interface_for_client` pin; the builtin rules snapshot. Integration (`tests/discover_custom.rs`): `CustomRoot::at(…).version(1, 18, 1, 7272)` and `(1, 17, 2, 7234)` are `vanilla-legacy` with interface 11200, `Config.wtf` `lastAddonVersion "11200"` still applied; `tests/toc_matrix.rs` `cases.toml`: a 1.18.1 custom client loads a plain 11200 TOC and ignores `_Vanilla.toc`. The `catalog_matches_declared_flavors` live probe (README "Live probes") gains a 1.18.1 custom client at the next checkpoint.

Contract (DEC-4, before the freeze): a new optional config key `interface` on version-family rules; changed family for custom 1.16–1.49 clients. No new codes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The reproduction shows `vanilla-legacy`, interface 11200, rules `vanilla-legacy`, and the 11200 addon installs with no `out_of_date`.
- The same for a 1.17.2 stamp; a 1.12.1 stamp unchanged; custom 1.15.9 still `vanilla`; Battle.net clients unchanged (the discovery matrix passes untouched).
- `lastAddonVersion` in `Config.wtf` still overrides on legacy rows.
- `[[rules.version_families]]` with `interface` works from config.
- README, the builtin rules snapshot and the vision comment updated.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `src/rules.rs` (rule order, pin, config override with `interface`), `src/discover/custom.rs` (interface source order).
- Integration: `tests/discover_custom.rs`, `tests/toc_matrix.rs`, `tests/install.rs` (an 11200 addon on a 1.18.1 client).
- Live probe at the next checkpoint (not part of the gate).

## Considerations

- omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.4 (deferred on the owner) confirms the real stamp; if it is 1.12.1, this rule is simply unused, and if it is something outside 1.16–1.49, widen the row.
- The target's default id stays `vanilla` (the family's default id), so `-t vanilla` resolution is unchanged (README "Choosing a target").
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.3 (override recomputes the interface) and this bead touch the same interface computation; whichever lands second reuses the other's helper.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.3`: A family override on a client with no readable version picks the fallback rules
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.9`: Unknown keys under [rules] in config.toml are ignored without a config_unknown_key warning
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.4`: Check a real Turtle WoW Wow.exe stamp and lastAddonVersion against the custom-client rule
acceptance_criteria: custom clients reporting 1.16–1.49 map to vanilla-legacy through a builtin version_families rule; version rules can pin the client's interface (interface = 11200 on that rule, overridable in [[rules.version_families]]); Config.wtf lastAddonVersion still wins on legacy rows; a synthetic Wow.exe stamped 1.18.1.7272 or 1.17.2 is vanilla-legacy with interface 11200 and installs an Interface 11200 addon without out_of_date; 1.12.1 and Battle.net 1.15.x/1.60.x clients are unchanged; README legacy table, FAQ and rules overrides updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: Custom clients stamped 1.16–1.49 (Turtle WoW 1.17/1.18) are vanilla-legacy at interface 11200, via a builtin version-family row with a pinned interface; config rules can pin one too.

title: product.db reader reads an install's uid as its product code
description:
## Background

Discovery's best hint is Battle.net's `product.db` (vision §4.1, §5.2 step 1a; README "Where discovery looks", route 1). When a flavor folder has no `.flavor.info`, the folder's product comes from `product.db` (`src/discover/battlenet.rs:49-53`: `.flavor.info`, then `hints.product_by_folder`, then the products table). The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found that the reader picks the wrong string as the product.

`src/discover/product_db.rs:60-78` (`classify`) collects every printable string of a top-level message depth first and takes the **first** one that looks like a product code (`:65`, `let product = first(is_product_code);`). The Agent's `ProductInstall` message starts with a `uid` (field 1) and only then the `product_code` (field 2). For most products the two are equal, which is why nothing failed so far. For Anniversary they differ: the uid is `wow_classic_anniversary` and the product code is `wow_anniversary`.

Verified on the development machine's real `product.db` (read-only, with a scratch decoder; no contents copied): its top level holds repeated field-1 installs, plus fields 5 (a message), 6 (a varint) and 7 (strings), and no field 2 at the time of reading. Every WoW install has field 1 (uid), field 2 (product code), field 3 (settings: 1 install path, 2 region, 13 the `_flavor_` folder), field 4 (cached state: 1 base state, whose 7 is the version string), field 6 (`wow`, the product family) and field 8. The Anniversary install has uid `wow_classic_anniversary`, product code `wow_anniversary`. The development machine's `<cache>/omaddons/discovery.json` records `product_by_folder["_anniversary_"] = "wow_classic_anniversary"`, a code that no products table row has.

The field numbers match two independent upstream readers:
- overtools/TACTLib `TACTLib/Agent/Protobuf/ProtoDatabase.cs` at commit 129f977 (generated from the Agent's schema): `Database { ProductInstall product_install = 1; InstallHandshake active_installs = 2; ActiveProcess active_processes = 3; ProductConfig product_configs = 4; DownloadSettings download_settings = 5; uint64 version_summary_seqn = 6; string priority_uid_list = 7 }`, `ProductInstall { uid = 1; product_code = 2; settings = 3; cached_product_state = 4; product_operations = 5; product_family = 6; hidden = 7; persistent_json_storage = 8 }`, `UserSettings { install_path = 1; play_region = 2; …; game_subfolder = 13 }`, `CachedProductState { base_product_state = 1; … }`, `BaseProductState { installed = 1; playable = 2; …; current_version_str = 7; … }`, and `InstallHandshake { product = 1; uid = 2; settings = 3 }`.
- lutris/lutris `lutris/util/battlenet/product_db.py` at 3307967 (`uid` 1, `product_code` 2, `settings` 3 with `install_path` 1, `cached_product_state` 4 → `base_product_state` 1 → `current_version_str` 7).

User-visible consequence today: none while Battle.net writes `.flavor.info`, which takes precedence. Without it (a client mid-install, an older layout, or a Battle.net change) the Anniversary target gets product `wow_classic_anniversary`: it loses its game mode (`tbc-anniversary`), `-t wow_anniversary` and `-t tbc-anniversary` fail with `target_not_found` (the second one claiming the client is not on this machine), its kind and exe are guessed instead of read from the product row, and its version comes from `product.db` instead of `.build.info` (the `.build.info` row lookup in `version_for`, `src/discover/battlenet.rs:177-196`, is by product code). A second defect of the same shape: `parse_product_db` (`:49-58`) classifies every top-level length-delimited field, so an `InstallHandshake` (field 2, written while Battle.net installs something; product at 1 and uid at 2, reversed) would also be read as an install.

The only `product.db` fixtures (`tests/fixtures/product_db/retail.db`, `fuzz/seeds/product_db/*.db`) and both builders (`src/discover/product_db.rs` tests `install()` at ~:248-276, `tests/common/product_db.rs:51-72`) write uid equal to the product code, so no test can see the bug.

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment (never the real `HOME`):

```bash
ISO=<scratch>/iso-d1; mkdir -p $ISO/home $ISO/proc
run() { env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=$ISO/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$ISO/home/.config \
  XDG_STATE_HOME=$ISO/home/.local/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=$ISO/home/.cache \
  OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=$ISO/proc target/debug/omaddons "$@"; }
P=$ISO/home/Games/battlenet; R="$P/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft"
mkdir -p "$P/dosdevices" "$P/drive_c/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent" "$R/_anniversary_/Interface/AddOns" "$R/_anniversary_/WTF"
ln -s ../drive_c "$P/dosdevices/c:"; touch "$R/_anniversary_/WoWClassic.exe"     # no .flavor.info
printf 'Branch!STRING:0|Active!DEC:1|Build Key!HEX:16|Tags!STRING:0|Version!STRING:0|KeyRing!HEX:16|Product!STRING:0\nus|1|aa||2.5.6.70006||wow_anniversary\n' > "$R/.build.info"
```

Write a `product.db` in the Agent's layout with a scratch script (Python shown; run it with `-I` from a scratch directory):

```python
import sys
def vi(n):
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        b, n = n & 0x7f, n >> 7
        out.append(b | 0x80 if n else b)
        if not n: return bytes(out)
ld = lambda num, body: vi(num << 3 | 2) + vi(len(body)) + body
s = lambda num, t: ld(num, t.encode())
u = lambda num, n: vi(num << 3) + vi(n)
settings = s(1, "C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft") + s(2, "us") + s(13, "_anniversary_")
state = ld(1, u(1, 1) + u(2, 1) + s(7, "2.5.6.70006"))
install = s(1, "wow_classic_anniversary") + s(2, "wow_anniversary") + ld(3, settings) + ld(4, state) + s(6, "wow")
open(sys.argv[1], "wb").write(ld(1, install) + u(6, 1))
```

```bash
python3 -I mkpdb.py "$P/drive_c/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db"
run targets --rescan --json | jq -c '.data.targets[] | {id, product, modes, found_by}'
run status -t wow_anniversary --json | jq -c '.error.code'
run status -t tbc-anniversary --json | jq -c '.error.message'
```

Expected: `{"id":"anniversary","product":"wow_anniversary","modes":[{"id":"tbc-anniversary",…}],"found_by":"product_db"}`; both `status` calls succeed.

Actual (HEAD 53b54e6): `"product":"wow_classic_anniversary","modes":[]`; `-t wow_anniversary` gives `target_not_found`; `-t tbc-anniversary` gives `target_not_found` with "Burning Crusade Anniversary runs in the Burning Crusade Anniversary client (_anniversary_), which was not found on this machine".

## Technical Approach

Decided: read by field number. The layout is now verified (development machine, TACTLib's generated schema, Lutris's reader), and shape-based extraction cannot tell `uid` from `product_code`.

1. `src/discover/product_db.rs:49-58`: `parse_product_db` takes only top-level **field 1** length-delimited values (`Database.product_install`). Fields 2 (handshakes), 4 (product configs), 5, 6 and 7 are ignored.
2. Replace `classify`/`walk` (`:60-103`) with a field-number reader over the existing wire decoder (`decode_message`, `:156-166`, stays):
   - `product`: field 2, when it passes `is_product_code` (`:112-116`); never field 1;
   - `install_path`: field 3 → field 1, when it passes `is_install_path`;
   - `flavor_folder`: field 3 → field 13, when it passes `is_flavor_folder`;
   - `version`: field 4 → field 1 → field 7, when it passes `is_version`;
   - keep the entry when it has an install path and either a product code starting with `wow`, a field 6 equal to `wow`, or a path containing `world of warcraft` (today's rule, `:66-71`, plus the product family). A missing or malformed sub-field leaves that value `None`; a truncated entry is still dropped (today's `damage_keeps_what_decoded_before_it` behaviour).
   - The shape predicates stay as validators so a garbage field never becomes a product or path.
3. Rewrite the module doc (`:1-9`): the layout, its sources (TACTLib file and commit, Lutris file and commit) and the verification date; drop "unverified". Keep `MAX_DEPTH` only if a recursive helper remains.
4. Tests in `src/discover/product_db.rs`: the `install()` builder (~`:248-276`) takes a separate uid and writes fields 5, 6, 7 and 8 like the Agent; `extraction_ignores_field_numbers_and_depth` is replaced by `the_product_code_is_field_2_not_the_uid` and `handshakes_and_other_top_level_fields_are_not_installs`. Keep `a_wowup_shaped_database`, `the_development_machine_database` (retail.db has uid = code), the damage, varint, depth and proptest cases.
5. `tests/common/product_db.rs:1-5,51-72`: `ProductDb::install_as(uid, code, path, folder, version)`; `install()` keeps uid = code. The header comment states the verified layout.
6. A synthetic multi-product fixture, generated by the builder (no real values): `retail` (`wow`/`wow`, `_retail_`, 12.1.5.70391), `wowf`/`wowf` `_forever_` 1.60.1.70245, `wow_classic`/`wow_classic` `_classic_` 5.5.4.63000, `wow_classic_era`/`wow_classic_era` on `D:\Games\World of Warcraft` `_classic_era_` 1.15.9.65000, `wow_classic_anniversary`/`wow_anniversary` `_anniversary_` 2.5.6.70006, an `agent` install at `C:/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent`, a top-level field-2 handshake (`product` 1 = `wow_classic_titan`, `uid` 2, settings with a WoW path), field 5 `{1: 0, 2: 1000000}`, field 6 varint and three field-7 uid strings. Commit it as `fuzz/seeds/product_db/multi-product.db` through the existing seed writer (`tests/fuzz_seeds.rs`, `OMADDONS_WRITE_SEEDS=1 cargo test --test fuzz_seeds -- --ignored write`) and assert its decode in a unit test (five WoW installs, Anniversary's code `wow_anniversary`, no titan entry).
7. Integration: in `tests/discover_matrix.rs` (or the product.db scenario that already exists there), an Anniversary folder without `.flavor.info`, found through the multi-product database: product `wow_anniversary`, mode `tbc-anniversary`, version from `.build.info`, `found_by: product_db`.
8. README "Known limitations" (`README.md:1779`): drop `product.db` from the UNVERIFIED list. Vision: a comment on omad-vision-8qa recording that the §4.1 "field layout … is UNVERIFIED" note is superseded (verified 2026-10-18; sources as above).

Rejected alternatives:
- Prefer a product-shaped string that the products table knows. Breaks D15: a new product (as `wowf` was on 2026-10-13) would be read through its uid again.
- Take the last product-shaped string. Field 6 (`product_family`, always `wow`) comes after the product code.
- Keep shape extraction but skip field 1. Still guesses: the settings and state messages hold other strings, and the handshake message reverses the order.

No contract change: `ProductDbEntry` is internal, and the cache invalidates itself because each root's cached `hints` are compared on reuse (`src/discover/cache.rs:125-139`) and change with the corrected product.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `parse_product_db` reads only top-level field-1 installs, and per install the product from field 2, the path from 3.1, the folder from 3.13 and the version from 4.1.7.
- The multi-product fixture decodes to five WoW installs with the right codes (`wow_anniversary`, not `wow_classic_anniversary`), the Agent entry and the handshake are not installs.
- An Anniversary folder without `.flavor.info` found through `product.db` has product `wow_anniversary`, game mode `tbc-anniversary`, its `.build.info` version, and answers `-t wow_anniversary` and `-t tbc-anniversary`.
- Truncated and malformed databases still yield what decoded before the damage; the proptests still pass.
- Module docs, `tests/common/product_db.rs` and README no longer call the layout unverified; the vision comment is recorded.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/discover/product_db.rs`): uid ≠ code; handshake and other top-level fields ignored; missing sub-fields; the multi-product fixture; existing damage, varint, depth and proptest cases.
- Integration (`tests/discover_matrix.rs`): Anniversary without `.flavor.info` through `product.db`, with `-t` by product code and by mode.
- Fuzz: `argc fuzz product_db --time 600` with the new seed.

## Considerations

- `.flavor.info` keeps precedence; this changes only the fallback.
- A second install of one product may carry a uid like `<code>_2` (unverified); reading field 2 makes that harmless.
- Do not copy anything from the development machine's real `product.db` into fixtures: install ids, paths, regions and the field-8 string are personal. The committed `retail.db` predates this rule and stays as it is.
- Interacts with omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.3 only through the README UNVERIFIED bullet.

## Related

- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.3.8`: Tolerant product.db protobuf reader and dosdevices drive mapping
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.3`: Verify Lutris, Heroic and Steam readers against upstream and close cheap gaps
acceptance_criteria: product.db installs read the product code from ProductInstall field 2, the install path from settings field 1, the flavor folder from settings field 13 and the version from cached state 1.7; only top-level field 1 entries are installs; a synthetic multi-product fixture with a uid that differs from its product code decodes to the right products; without .flavor.info an Anniversary folder is product wow_anniversary with its game mode; README and the module docs no longer call the layout unverified; argc gate passes
close_reason: product.db is read by field number, the layout verified against a real Agent database, TACTLib and Lutris: only top-level installs, the product from field 2 (never the uid), so Anniversary is wow_anniversary.

title: ClientRules fields directive_conditionals, path_variables and game are read by nothing
description:
## Background

D15 and D29 make client capabilities data: "Client capabilities as data (`ClientRules`)" and "Rows are overridable in config. No client version is special-cased in code" (vision §5.3). README "Rules overrides (advanced)" (`README.md:1528`) lists `game`, `directive_conditionals` and `path_variables` among the fields a `[client_rules.<row>]` patch may set. The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found that three of them change nothing:

- `ClientRules.game` (`src/rules.rs:430`), `directive_conditionals` (`:441`) and `path_variables` (`:442`) are read only by `src/rules.rs` itself (builders, override `apply`/`new_row` at `:850-923`, tests) and by `src/state/config.rs:323-339` (`RULES_FIELDS`). `grep -rn 'directive_conditionals\|path_variables\|\.game\b' src` finds no other reader.
- Conditional directives are evaluated on every non-legacy row because `Toc::dependencies_for` checks `rules.legacy` (`src/toc.rs:482`) and `Toc::title_for` checks `!rules.legacy` (`src/toc.rs:521`), not `directive_conditionals`. omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.1 did this on purpose ("without gating on the flag … so the rules table can be corrected", its Considerations), because the builtin data is wrong: only `mainline` and `mainline-12.0.7` set the flag (`src/rules.rs:1155-1180`), while `modern_row`'s doc says "no directive conditionals" (`:1090-1092`) for every Classic and Forever row.

What the client actually supports (warcraft.wiki.gg `TOC_format`, raw wikitext fetched 2026-10-18, "Patch changes"): Modern 12.0.7 "Added inline directives and variables for addon directives"; Classic Era 1.15.9, Classic Anniversary 2.5.6, Classic Titan Reforged 3.80.2 and Classic Progression (Mists) 5.5.4 each "Includes all Modern changes up to 12.0.7"; Forever 1.60.1 "Includes all Modern changes up to 12.1.5". Earlier builds (Classic Era 1.15.8, Mists 5.5.1 and 5.5.0: up to 11.2.0 or 11.1.7; Cata 4.4.1: up to 11.0.0) lack directive conditionals. Every live client therefore supports them, so today's `rules.legacy` gate happens to give the right answer for the builtin rows, but a user who patches `directive_conditionals` (as README invites) changes nothing, and the data contradicts the client.

`path_variables` describes `[Family]`, `[Game]` and `[TextLocale]` in TOC file lines (Modern 11.1.5). omaddons parses them into `TocFile.path_vars` (`src/toc.rs:293-323`) but never resolves a TOC's file list: the verdict is decided per folder from the loaded TOC, its Interface and its game types (README "How omaddons decides what loads"), and no code reads `Toc.files` outside `src/toc.rs`. `game` is the client's game type name (`standard`, `camelot`, …), which only `[Game]` expansion would need; game-type matching already uses `game_types` plus `family_suffixes` (`client_names`, `src/toc/loaded.rs:445-453`).

## Steps to Reproduce

Code-level trace (the isolated binary shows no difference, because every builtin non-legacy row behaves as if the flag were true):

1. `[client_rules.vanilla]` with `directive_conditionals = false` in `<config>/omaddons/config.toml` is accepted (`src/state/config.rs:315-339`) and applied (`src/rules.rs:885-888`).
2. `Toc::dependencies_for` (`src/toc.rs:480-482`) still takes `self.conditional` because `rules.legacy` is false on the vanilla row, so a `## Dependencies [AllowLoadGameType vanilla]: X` line still makes `X` a requirement on Classic Era.
3. `[client_rules.mainline] path_variables = false` or `game = "other"` has no reader at all.

Unit-level reproduction (no new production code): in a scratch test, patch the builtin vanilla row with `directive_conditionals: false` via `RulesTable::with_overrides` and call `parse_toc(b"## Interface: 11509\n## Dependencies [AllowLoadGameType vanilla]: X\n").dependencies_for(row)`; it returns `required: [X]`.

## Technical Approach

Decided per field:

1. **`directive_conditionals`: wire it.** It is exactly the capability the parser needs, and D29 says it belongs in data.
   - `src/toc.rs:482`: `let conditional = if rules.directive_conditionals { &self.conditional[..] } else { &[] };` and `src/toc.rs:521`: `.filter(|d| rules.directive_conditionals && …)`. Update the doc comments at `:470-479` and `:509-512` (a client without directive conditionals reads such a line's key literally, so no conditional variant applies). `src/toc/loaded.rs:386` (`!rules.legacy && game_type_excluded`) is about the `AllowLoadGameType` directive itself (10.2.7+), not about conditions: leave it.
   - Data (`src/rules.rs:1153-1335`): set `directive_conditionals: true` on `forever`, `vanilla`, `tbc`, `titan`, `mists` and `fallback-battlenet` (an unmapped Battle.net client in 2026 is built on 12.0.7 or later; its rules are already "permissive modern"). Keep `true` on `mainline` and `mainline-12.0.7`; keep `false` on `mainline-10.2.7`, `mainline-9.1`, `wrath`, `cata` (no live product; their last builds predate 12.0.7), the five legacy rows and `fallback-custom`. Rewrite `modern_row`'s doc (`:1090-1092`) and the table doc (`:1141-1152`), citing the wiki's per-client "Includes all Modern changes up to 12.0.7" lines with the fetch date.
   - The classic rows cover whole families (`vanilla` from 1.13.0). This follows the table's documented policy ("these rows describe current clients"); Classic Era 1.15.0–1.15.8 builds are not live. Say so in the doc comment.
2. **`path_variables`: remove it.** Nothing in omaddons resolves TOC file lines, and the folder verdict does not depend on them (omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.2 records the same finding). Remove the field from `ClientRules` (`:442`), `ClientRulesOverride` (`:858`), `apply` (`:889`), `new_row` (`:922`), `modern_row`/`legacy_row` (`:1116`, `:1139`), the test at `:1819`, `RULES_FIELDS` (`src/state/config.rs:334`) and README `:1528`. `TocFile.path_vars` parsing in `src/toc.rs` stays (it is parser output, harmless, and a future file-list check can use it).
3. **`game`: remove it.** No reader; `game_types` is what conditions and `AllowLoadGameType` match. Remove it from the struct (`:430`), override (`:850`, `:878`), `new_row` (`:914`; a new row no longer requires it, so update the doc at `:842-845` and README's "needs every required field" list if it names it), the `modern_row`/`legacy_row`/fallback builders (their `game` parameter), the test at `:1633` (assert `game_types` instead) and `RULES_FIELDS` (`src/state/config.rs:327`).
4. Update `src/snapshots/omaddons__rules__tests__builtin_rules_table.snap` (`cargo insta review`), the discovery cache basis changes with the table (`src/discover/cache.rs:62-71`), so every cache re-parses once after upgrade, as designed (omad-lmk3).
5. Tests: `mainline_rows_follow_client_capabilities` (`src/rules.rs:1605-1626`) gains assertions for every row's flag; a new `dependencies_for` case per row in `src/toc.rs` tests: a conditional dependency counts on vanilla, forever, titan and mists, not on `mainline-10.2.7`, wrath, cata or any legacy row; an override `directive_conditionals = false` on `vanilla` turns it off.

Rejected alternatives:
- Keep `rules.legacy` and document the flag as informational. README and D29 promise the opposite, and an override would still do nothing.
- Wire `path_variables` and `game` by resolving TOC file lists. No verdict depends on files; that is new behaviour (file-existence checks) beyond M1/M2's promise and would need its own design (a doctor-style check is M4).
- Keep the two dead fields "for later". README must describe exactly what exists.

Contract implications (allowed before the M4 freeze, DEC-4): `game` and `path_variables` leave the config `[client_rules.<row>]` surface. A config that still sets them gets `config_unknown_key` once omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.9 lands (today it is silently ignored either way). No error or warning code changes. Record on omad-vision-8qa: §5.3's field list loses `path_variables`, `directive_conditionals` is now read and true for every current client, and the date and source of the capability data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/toc.rs` gates conditional dependencies and titles on `rules.directive_conditionals`.
- Builtin flag values are exactly: true for `mainline`, `mainline-12.0.7`, `forever`, `vanilla`, `tbc`, `titan`, `mists`, `fallback-battlenet`; false for all other rows.
- `[client_rules.vanilla] directive_conditionals = false` makes a `[AllowLoadGameType vanilla]` dependency stop counting on Classic Era.
- `game` and `path_variables` exist nowhere in `ClientRules`, its override, `RULES_FIELDS` or README.
- The builtin rules snapshot is reviewed and updated; the vision comment is recorded.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/rules.rs`): per-row flag table; `new_row` without `game` succeeds; snapshot.
- Unit (`src/toc.rs`): `dependencies_for` and `title_for` per row, plus the override case.
- Integration: `tests/cli_config.rs` keeps accepting the remaining fields; `tests/deps.rs` and `tests/inventory.rs` keep passing unchanged (current clients keep evaluating conditions).

## Considerations

- omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.2 rewrites how conditions are recognized and combined; it reuses this flag as the switch between "inline directives are read" and "the line is read literally". Do omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.7 first; omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.2 depends on it.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.9 makes stale `game`/`path_variables` keys warn; until then they are ignored, which is what they always did.
- No behaviour change on any live client: the flag now says what the `legacy` gate assumed.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.2`: TOC parser misses 12.0.7 inline directives at line end, the form ElvUI ships
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.9`: Unknown keys under [rules] in config.toml are ignored without a config_unknown_key warning
- `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.1`: TOC conditional directives and plain titles
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.4.2`: Product, version-to-family, interface and ClientRules tables in src/rules.rs
acceptance_criteria: dependencies_for and title_for gate conditional directives on rules.directive_conditionals instead of rules.legacy; builtin rows set directive_conditionals true for every current client built on 12.0.7 (mainline 12.0.7+, forever, vanilla, tbc, titan, mists, fallback-battlenet) and false elsewhere; path_variables and game are removed from ClientRules, its override, config RULES_FIELDS and README; an override setting directive_conditionals = false on a row turns conditional dependencies off there; the builtin rules snapshot is updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: dependencies_for and title_for gate conditional variants on rules.directive_conditionals; builtin rows set it true exactly for current clients (mainline 12.0.7+, forever, vanilla, tbc, titan, mists, fallback-battlenet); game and path_variables removed from ClientRules, its override, RULES_FIELDS and README; an override setting it false turns variants off; snapshot reviewed and updated; vision comment added.

title: A client found only while it ran is lost after it exits unless it was registered meanwhile
description:
## Background

README "Where discovery looks" (`README.md:379`), route 7: "The roots of registered targets that no route above reached, while they are still WoW roots. A client found once, for example while it ran, is still found after it exits." The process route (README `:368`) finds a client in a nested prefix such as `$HOME/Games/umu/umu-default` only while it runs (omad-93rc; M2 close comment on omad-vision-8qa: "registered roots that no route reached are a last route, so it stays found after it exits").

The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found that the promise holds only for **registered** clients. `World::load_with` (`src/app/world.rs:72-84`) builds route 7 from `registry.targets` alone, and registration happens only on a first change or `targets add|rename|default` (README "Targets"). A user who runs `omaddons status` (read-only) while the game runs sees the client; after it exits, `status`, `list` and `install -t <it>` no longer find it.

The behaviour is also inconsistent: the discovery cache still holds the process-found root, so `status --cached` (which re-reads cached roots, `src/discover/cache.rs:158-162`) keeps showing it until the next full run rewrites the cache without it (`:248-257`).

And route 7 misreports its origin: a registered root that no other route reached is passed with `DiscoverySource::Scan` (`src/app/world.rs:78-81`, `Origin::Discovered => DiscoverySource::Scan`), so `targets` shows `found_by: scan` for a client the scan never reached (`src/app/targets.rs:243-256`).

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment with a fake `/proc` (debug builds read `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`):

```bash
ISO=<scratch>/iso-d6; H=$ISO/home; mkdir -p $H $ISO/proc/4242
run() { env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=$H XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$H/.config \
  XDG_STATE_HOME=$H/.local/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=$H/.cache \
  OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=$ISO/proc target/debug/omaddons "$@"; }
P=$H/Games/umu/umu-default; C="$P/drive_c/Games/Private/WoW335"
mkdir -p "$C/Interface/AddOns" "$C/WTF"; touch "$C/Wow.exe"
printf 'Wow.exe\n' > $ISO/proc/4242/comm
printf 'C:\\Games\\Private\\WoW335\\Wow.exe\0' > $ISO/proc/4242/cmdline
printf 'WINEPREFIX=%s\0' "$P" > $ISO/proc/4242/environ
run status --json | jq -c '[.data.targets[] | .id]'          # ["wow335"]
run targets --json | jq -c '[.data.targets[] | .found_by]'   # ["process"]
mv $ISO/proc/4242 $ISO/proc-off                              # the client exits
run status --cached --json | jq -c '[.data.targets[] | .id]' # ["wow335"] (from the cache)
run status --json | jq -c '[.data.targets[] | .id]'          # []  <- lost
run status --cached --json | jq -c '[.data.targets[] | .id]' # []
```

Registered variant: with the process present, `run targets default wow335`, then remove the process: `targets --json` shows `found_by: "scan"`.

Expected: after exit, every command still finds `wow335`; `found_by` says how (here: remembered; registered once registered).

## Technical Approach

Decided: remember process-found roots in the discovery cache, a derived file every command may already write (`src/discover/cache.rs:1-7`, `write_cache` `:270-283`), as their own last route. Rejected: narrowing README to registered clients (the process route would then be a "while it runs" curiosity, and `status --cached` would stay inconsistent); registering on discovery (registration writes the registry and `target.json` markers under the lock, which read-only commands never do, vision §5.2 step 7).

1. **New sources** (`src/discover/target.rs:22-38`): `DiscoverySource::Registered` (route 7) and `DiscoverySource::Remembered` (route 8); wire names `registered`, `remembered` in `found_by` (`src/app/targets.rs:106-107`, `:243-256`; `manual` keeps precedence for manual entries).
2. **Route 7 source:** `src/app/world.rs:78-81` passes `Registered` for `Origin::Discovered` (keeps `Manual` for manual).
3. **Route 8:** `DiscoveryInput` gains `remembered_roots: Vec<(PathBuf, String)>` (path, qualifier). `discover_cached` (`src/discover/cache.rs:143-258`) fills it from the previous cache's roots whose `source` is `Process` or `Remembered` and whose path is under `input.home` (a throwaway `HOME` with a shared cache directory must not reach the user's clients; same rule as `process_prefixes`, `src/discover/running.rs:102-114`). `collect()` (`src/discover/mod.rs`, after the registered-roots loop that ends the function) adds them, while still WoW roots, with `DiscoverySource::Remembered` and their recorded qualifier. A root reached by an earlier route is reported by that route, as today (`Candidates::add` keeps the first).
4. **Every mode:** `Full` and `NoScan` already load the cache. `Rescan` (`:150-152`) loads it too, but only to take the remembered roots; it still reuses no parse. A remembered root is forgotten when it stops being a WoW root (it is then dropped like any gone root, `:194-200`) or when the cache file is deleted.
5. **README:** route 7 sentence: "The roots of registered targets (`found_by: registered`) …"; new route 8: "Roots found earlier while a client ran (`found_by: remembered`), kept in `$HOME/.cache/omaddons/discovery.json`, while they are still WoW roots under your home. A client found once while it ran is still found after it exits." `:383`: "`targets --rescan` re-parses every root and reuses no cached parse; remembered roots are still looked at." Document the `found_by` values in the `targets` section (`README.md:1036-1050`).
6. **Contract** (DEC-4, before the M4 freeze): two new `found_by` values; a new route. Record on omad-vision-8qa (§5.2 hints list gains the remembered route; found_by values).

## Acceptance Criteria

- In the reproduction, after the process is gone, `status`, `status --cached`, `list` and `install … -t wow335 --dry-run` find the client, and `targets` reports `found_by: remembered`.
- After `targets default wow335` and exit, `found_by: registered`.
- `targets --rescan` keeps remembered roots.
- Deleting the root makes it disappear; deleting the cache forgets it.
- A different `HOME` with the same `XDG_CACHE_HOME` does not see the remembered root.
- README and the vision comment updated.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/discover/cache.rs`): remembered roots survive `Full`, `Rescan` and `NoScan` runs; are dropped when gone; are filtered by `home`.
- Integration (`tests/running.rs` or `tests/discover_cache.rs` with `tests/common/procfs.rs`'s `FakeProc`): the reproduction above, the registered variant, the rescan case and the throwaway-HOME case.
- Contract: `targets` JSON snapshot (if one pins `found_by`) re-reviewed.

## Considerations

- omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.10 removes `DiscoveryMode::Cached`; do omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.10 first or fold it in, since both edit the mode matches in `src/discover/cache.rs` and `src/app/world.rs:86-89`.
- Provisional ids follow route order (3.6 comment): a remembered root is last, so on a collision it gets the qualified id, which matches its being found last.
- Running detection stays live on every call (vision §5.2 step 8); remembering a root does not make it "running".
- The cache schema (`DiscoveryCache`, `CURRENT` 1.1, `src/discover/cache.rs:56-59`) gains no field: the root's `source` already records `process`. A `Remembered` source value written by a newer binary is unknown to an older one, which ignores a newer-versioned cache anyway (`load_cache`, `:261-266`); bump the schema minor if the serialized enum value would make an older binary reject it.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.10`: Remove DiscoveryMode::Cached, a discovery mode no command selects
- `omad-93rc`: Running-process discovery hints are implemented and tested but never wired into World
acceptance_criteria: roots found through a running process are remembered in the discovery cache and looked at as a last route (under HOME only, while still WoW roots), by every discovery mode including targets --rescan; found_by reports remembered for them and registered for registry roots instead of scan; a read-only status while the client runs is enough for status, list and install -t to find it after it exits; README "Where discovery looks" and the targets found_by doc list the routes; argc gate passes
close_reason: A client found while it ran stays found after it exits, registered or not: process-found roots are remembered in the discovery cache as the last route (found_by remembered), and route 7 reports found_by registered.

title: Unknown keys under [rules] in config.toml are ignored without a config_unknown_key warning
description:
## Background

README "Configuration" (`README.md:1453`): "A broken file fails commands with `state_corrupt` citing line and column, and unknown keys only warn." `config_unknown_key` is the warning (`src/error.rs`, README warnings table).

The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found that the `[rules]` section is exempt. `unknown_keys` (`src/state/config.rs:521-557`) skips it outright (`:526`, `("rules", _) => {}`), and the rules structs (`RulesOverrides`, `ClientRulesOverride`, `Product`, `GameMode`, `VersionFamilyRule`, `NumRange` in `src/rules.rs:294-301`, `:343-370`, `:388-396`, `:826-859`) are `#[serde(default)]` without `deny_unknown_fields`, so a misspelled key is dropped silently. The top-level `[client_rules.<row>]` shorthand is checked (`client_rules.*.*` against `RULES_FIELDS`, `src/state/config.rs:315-339`), but its documented twin `[rules.client_rules.<row>]` (README "Rules overrides (advanced)", `README.md:1528`) is not.

Consequence: a user patching load rules (an advanced, high-stakes edit: it changes what installs where) gets no hint that `prodcuts`, `multi_tocs` or `famly_ranges` did nothing.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
ISO=<scratch>/iso-d7; mkdir -p $ISO/home/.config/omaddons $ISO/proc
run() { env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=$ISO/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$ISO/home/.config \
  XDG_STATE_HOME=$ISO/home/.local/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=$ISO/home/.cache \
  OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=$ISO/proc target/debug/omaddons "$@"; }
cat > $ISO/home/.config/omaddons/config.toml <<'EOF'
[rules]
prodcuts = []

[rules.client_rules.vanilla]
multi_tocs = false

[client_rules.mainline]
comma_interfaces = true

[targets.retail]
labl = "x"
EOF
run status --json | jq -c '[.warnings[]? | select(.code == "config_unknown_key") | .message]'
```

Expected: four `config_unknown_key` warnings (`rules.prodcuts`, `rules.client_rules.vanilla.multi_tocs`, `client_rules.mainline.comma_interfaces`, `targets.retail.labl`).

Actual (HEAD 53b54e6): two, for `client_rules.mainline.comma_interfaces` (did you mean `comma_interface`?) and `targets.retail.labl`; nothing for the two `[rules]` keys.

## Technical Approach

Decided: warn, never fail. README says unknown keys only warn; `deny_unknown_fields` would turn a typo into `state_corrupt` and break every command, which is the opposite of the contract.

1. `src/state/config.rs:524-546`: replace `("rules", _) => {}` with a walk of the `rules` table:
   - top-level keys: `products`, `version_families`, `family_ranges`, `client_rules`;
   - `rules.client_rules.<row>.<field>`: `RULES_FIELDS` (the same list the shorthand uses);
   - each `[[rules.products]]` element: `code`, `folder`, `exe`, `kind`, `default_id`, `modes`; each `modes` element: `id`, `name`, `aliases`; path spelled `rules.products[<i>].<key>` (and `…modes[<j>].<key>`);
   - each `[[rules.version_families]]` element: `install_kind`, `major`, `minor`, `family` (plus `interface` if omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5 lands first); `major`/`minor` tables: `min`, `max`;
   - `rules.family_ranges.<family>` tables: `min`, `max` (the family name itself is a typed key: an unknown one is already a `state_corrupt` deserialize error, keep that).
   A value of the wrong TOML type stays a deserialize error (unchanged).
2. Suggestions: `closest_key` (`:352-395`) only knows `KEYS`. Add a `RULES_KEYS` pattern list (with `*` for row names and `[]` for array indices) used by the `rules` walk and by a `closest_rules_key` with the same edit-distance-2 rule, so `rules.prodcuts` suggests `rules.products`. Keep `RULES_KEYS` out of `KEYS`: `config get/set` (`src/app/config.rs`) must not start accepting `rules.*` paths (array tables are not settable that way).
3. Keep the lists honest: a unit test derives each struct's field names from its `schemars` schema (`schema_for!(Product)` etc. — the structs already derive `JsonSchema`) and asserts they equal the hard-coded lists, so a new field (omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.7 removing `game`/`path_variables`, omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5 adding `interface`) cannot drift.
4. README: Configuration paragraph unchanged (now true); "Rules overrides (advanced)" gains "Unknown keys there warn `config_unknown_key` too." No new code (`config_unknown_key` exists); no vision comment needed beyond noting it in the next contract comment, since behaviour now matches the documented contract.

Rejected: `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` (fails commands); collecting unknown fields through `serde_ignored` (a new dependency for one walk the code already does by hand for the other sections).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The reproduction yields four `config_unknown_key` warnings, the two `[rules]` ones with did-you-mean suggestions (`rules.products`, `rules.client_rules.vanilla.multi_toc`).
- Unknown keys inside `[[rules.products]]`, their `modes`, `[[rules.version_families]]` and range tables warn with indexed paths.
- Valid rules overrides produce no warning; config `get`/`set` refuse `rules.*` as today.
- The schema-derived field-list test passes.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/state/config.rs` tests): each unknown-key location; suggestions; no false positive on every documented field (one table with every field set); schema-derived lists.
- Integration (`tests/cli_config.rs`): the reproduction's warnings through `status --json`.

## Considerations

- After omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.7, configs that still set `game` or `path_variables` start warning: intended (those keys do nothing).
- Warnings are emitted on every command that loads config, as for other sections; no dedup needed beyond today's.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.7`: ClientRules fields directive_conditionals, path_variables and game are read by nothing
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5`: Custom 1.12-based clients stamped 1.17/1.18 (Turtle WoW) are read as Classic Era
acceptance_criteria: every key under [rules] that the rules overrides do not define (top level, [rules.client_rules.<row>] fields, [[rules.products]] and their modes, [[rules.version_families]], NumRange tables) warns config_unknown_key with its dotted path and a did-you-mean suggestion; the known field lists are tested against the structs' JSON schemas; config get/set behaviour is unchanged; argc gate passes
close_reason: Unknown keys anywhere under [rules] warn config_unknown_key with a did-you-mean from the same table, array elements by index; the field lists cannot drift from the structs.

Evidence: unit unknown_keys_under_rules_warn_with_a_suggestion (the bead's four warnings with rules.products and …vanilla.multi_toc suggestions; indexed paths rules.products[0].colour, …modes[0].nmae, version_families[0].famly and .major.mid, family_ranges.vanilla.maks), every_documented_rules_field_is_quiet (every field of every table set, rules.client_rules and the shorthand: no warning), the_rules_field_lists_are_the_structs_fields (each list equals its struct's schema properties); tests/cli_config.rs unknown_keys_under_rules_warn_too (status --json: four warnings with both suggestions; config set rules.products refused). argc gate passes. · found: none
