title: Epic: Test-suite quality and README accuracy
description:
## Background

The milestone checkpoints rest on the test suite and on README as the product contract. The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found:
- checkpoint tests that bail out early report as passed, so a skip reads as a pass (the M2 checkpoint's "9 passed" included a skip);
- speed budgets run in the default gate although `tests/perf.rs` says every budget lives there;
- about 20 race tests order processes with fixed sleeps;
- the real HTTP transport (`src/net/client.rs`) is never exercised by the gate;
- README and doc comments contradict the code in 22 places: stale counts, codes called "reserved" that M2 uses, a stale hero sample, and others.

## Goals

- A checkpoint run cannot mistake a skip for a pass, and the default gate has no timing-dependent flakes.
- README states exactly what the code does at the closing commit.

## Success Criteria

- Every child bead is closed; `argc gate` passes; README numbers and claims match the code.

## Non-Goals

- No README rewrite beyond the listed contradictions; other beads update the README sections their fixes change.

## Considerations

- The README-accuracy bead is the single owner of README's error and warning code tables and their counts. Beads that add a code update the row and the count in the same commit.
acceptance_criteria: every child bead is closed, each with its regression test or recorded evidence; argc gate passes; README.md and the vision bead record each behaviour or contract change

title: Checkpoint tests that bail out early report as passed, so a skip reads as a pass
description:
## Background

Vision §5.12 and D16 make real-machine smoke tests and live probes checkpoint-only checks: "ignored by default, enabled by an environment variable". Each milestone checkpoint then pastes their result into its close reason as evidence. The M2 checkpoint (omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7, vision comment 630) recorded "Real machine: 9 passed". But one of those nine, `keyless_installs_forever`, did nothing: it returns early while the Forever stress-test set is installed. libtest has no "skipped" outcome, so a test that returns early is counted as passed. The close reason only explains this because the agent happened to notice.

The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found the same pattern at every checkpoint-only entry point. All line numbers are at HEAD 53b54e6.

- `tests/real_machine.rs:36-40` `enabled(live)` is false unless `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1`, plus `OMADDONS_LIVE=1` for the eight live tests. Every test starts with `if !enabled(..) { return; }`: lines 338-340, 462-464, 497-499, 624-626, 717-719, 753-755, 797-799, 850-852 and 905-907. A checkpoint run that forgets `OMADDONS_LIVE=1` therefore reports "9 passed", even though eight tests never ran.
- `tests/real_machine.rs:151-162` `skip_if_running` prints `skipped: the <id> client is running` and the test returns, so it also passes. Callers: lines 467, 503, 629, 722, 801 and 854.
- `tests/real_machine.rs:635-642`: `keyless_installs_forever` returns early when the forever client manages any addon. That is the M2 case.
- `tests/live_probes.rs:36-45`: `live()` returns `None` without `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`, and all 16 probes start with `let Some(..) = live() else { return };` (lines 175, 353, 360, 381, 397, 431, 465, 530, 628, 664, 701, 758, 825, 877, 909 and 948). The M2 "16 live probes passed" is therefore only as good as the environment of that one invocation.
- `tests/discover_custom.rs:233-249` `real_custom_client` returns early without `OMADDONS_REAL_CUSTOM_ROOT`.
- `src/net/tests.rs:555-560` `live_github_request` returns early without `OMADDONS_LIVE`.

Consequence: a checkpoint can record "N passed" for checks that never ran. The skips that exist today print only a free-text line, which disappears among the `note()` evidence the real-machine tests write to stderr. "Done is a recorded fact" (the M2 checkpoint bead's own background) is not true for these checks.

## Technical Approach

Decided mechanism: **a skip fails unless the run names it as accepted, and every skip prints one greppable line.**

1. New file `tests/common/checkpoint.rs`, declared in `tests/common/mod.rs`. It is compiled into every test binary, and the module already has `#![allow(dead_code)]`.
   - `pub const ALLOW_SKIP: &str = "OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP";`
   - `pub fn skip_allowed(allow: Option<&str>, test: &str) -> bool` is pure and parses a comma-separated list of exact test names, trimming whitespace. An empty or absent value allows nothing. A name must match exactly, so `keyless_installs` does not allow `keyless_installs_forever`.
   - `pub fn skip(test: &str, reason: &str)` writes `SKIP <test>: <reason>\n` with `writeln!(std::io::stderr(), …)`. That is a direct write, which libtest does not capture, the same way `note()` already writes. It then asserts `skip_allowed(std::env::var(ALLOW_SKIP).ok().as_deref(), test)` with the message `"{test} did not run: {reason}. A checkpoint run must not skip it; to accept this skip, run with OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP={test}"`.
   - `pub fn require(test: &str, vars: &[&str]) -> bool` returns true when every var is exactly `"1"`. Otherwise it calls `skip(test, "<VAR> is not 1")` naming the first missing var, and returns false only when that skip was allowed. Callers write `if !checkpoint::require("keyless_installs_retail", &["OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE", "OMADDONS_LIVE"]) { return; }`.
   - The test name is passed as a literal. Rejected: reading `std::thread::current().name()`, because that depends on how libtest names its threads.
2. `tests/real_machine.rs`:
   - Replace `enabled()` with `checkpoint::require(<name>, …)` at all nine sites.
   - `skip_if_running(test, &target)` calls `checkpoint::skip(test, &format!("the {} client is running; quit it and run again", id))` and returns true.
   - The forever early return becomes `checkpoint::skip("keyless_installs_forever", &format!("the forever client manages {managed} addons (the stress-test set of omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6); undo or remove them to run this test"))`.
   - Update the module doc at lines 1-8: "A test that cannot run prints a SKIP line and fails unless OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP names it".
3. `tests/live_probes.rs`: `live(test: &str)` calls `checkpoint::require(test, &["OMADDONS_LIVE"])`, and each probe passes its own name.
4. `tests/discover_custom.rs::real_custom_client`: when `OMADDONS_REAL_CUSTOM_ROOT` is unset, `checkpoint::skip("real_custom_client", "OMADDONS_REAL_CUSTOM_ROOT is not set")`.
5. `src/net/tests.rs::live_github_request`: this unit test cannot use `tests/common`. Without `OMADDONS_LIVE` it should fail with the same message shape (`panic!` is allowed in tests). The test is `#[ignore]`d and reached only by its explicit filter, so failing is the honest result.
6. Leave these alone and say why in a one-line comment each. They are tools invoked on purpose, not checks:
   - the fixture recorders (`record_*`, which need `OMADDONS_RECORD=1`);
   - the child-process helpers (`child_holder`, `child_prune`, `fsx::sys::tests::child_*`);
   - `write_fuzz_seeds`;
   - `tests/perf.rs` `bench_home` and `live_home`. README's perf command also gains `--skip bench_home --skip live_home`, so the perf summary counts only budgets.
7. README.md, "Milestone checkpoints" (about lines 1838-1851):
   - Show `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1 OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=keyless_installs_forever cargo test --test real_machine -- --ignored --test-threads=1` for as long as the stress-test set stays installed.
   - Add a sentence: "A checkpoint test that cannot run prints `SKIP <test>: <reason>` and fails; `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=<test>[,<test>…]` accepts the named skips, which still print their line. The checkpoint's close reason quotes every SKIP line."
   - Also document the variable in the "Environment variables" note as test-only (it is read only by the test harness, never by the binary).
8. Vision bead: add one comment (test-only, so no contract change). It records the rule above, and the correction "M2 real machine: 8 ran and passed, 1 (`keyless_installs_forever`) skipped by design". It also says the M3 checkpoint bead must quote every SKIP line.

Rejected alternatives:
- A summary file that each test appends PASS/SKIP lines to, read by the checkpoint. It adds concurrent appends and a file nobody reads by default. A failing test is unmissable in libtest's own summary.
- Converting skips into `#[ignore]`. The skip conditions are runtime facts (a running client, installed addons) that `#[ignore]` cannot express.
- nextest-only features. The project's gate is plain `cargo test`.
- Leaving `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE` unset as a silent pass "for safety". Safety comes from checking the variable before anything touches the machine. That stays the first statement of every test, and failing at that point touches nothing.

Contract: none. The change is to the test harness only. The binary never reads `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One helper (`tests/common/checkpoint.rs`) is the only way a checkpoint test returns early. A grep for `return;` right after an env check in those files finds none outside it.
- `cargo test --test real_machine -- --ignored` with no env vars fails all 9 tests. Each prints exactly one `SKIP <name>: OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE is not 1` line, and nothing else runs (the env check is the first statement).
- The same run with `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=<all nine names>` passes all 9, and each prints its SKIP line.
- `OMADDONS_LIVE` unset gives the same behaviour for `cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored` (16 tests).
- `skip_allowed` has gate tests: exact names, comma lists with spaces, empty and absent values, and a prefix that must not match.
- README's checkpoint section and env-var note describe the rule. The vision comment exists.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `tests/common_selftest.rs` gains `skip_allowed_takes_exact_names_only`. Cases: `None`, `Some("")`, `Some("a")` for `a`, `Some("a, b")` for `b`, `Some("keyless_installs")` for `keyless_installs_forever` (false), and `Some("x,,y")`.
- Integration, run by hand when implementing, never in the gate:
  - `cargo test --locked --test real_machine -- --ignored`, with `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE` and `OMADDONS_LIVE` unset, expecting 9 failures and 9 SKIP lines;
  - the same with `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` listing all nine, expecting 9 passes;
  - the same two runs for `tests/live_probes.rs`.
  - **Do not set `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE` or `OMADDONS_LIVE` while implementing**: those runs touch the real home and the network, and belong to the checkpoint.
- The gate itself is unaffected: `cargo test` never runs ignored tests.

## Considerations

- The first statement of every real-machine test must stay the env check. The helper must never be called after anything that reads or writes the real home.
- `skip_if_running` keeps its meaning: a client that is running is a reason not to mutate. A checkpoint that runs while a client is open now fails visibly instead of passing quietly.
- In-test partial skips are by design and stay as they are. Examples: `catalog_matches_declared_flavors` skips catalog entries without a `release.json`, and `outdated_over_the_catalog…` skips non-GitHub refs. They are per-row decisions inside a test that did run, and the probe's printed matrix shows them.
- Interaction with omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2: `tests/perf.rs` stays the home of time budgets. Its own early returns (`bench_home`, `live_home`) are tools and are excluded by the README invocation, not failed.
- omad-wez's post-launch run of `keyless_installs_forever` needs no allow entry once the stress-test set is gone. Mention this in a comment on omad-wez.

## Related

- `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7`: M2 checkpoint verification
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.7.10`: Verify the M1 checkpoints: real-machine smoke, keyless installs, fuzz, probes and README
- `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6`: Confirm omaddons-installed addons load in the real Forever client during the 2026-10-19 stress test
- `omad-wez`: Re-verify Forever keyless installs and launch layout after the 2026-11-04 launch
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2`: Speed budgets run in the default gate although tests/perf.rs says every budget lives there
acceptance_criteria: every early return in tests/real_machine.rs, tests/live_probes.rs, tests/discover_custom.rs::real_custom_client and src/net/tests.rs::live_github_request goes through one skip helper; a skip prints one `SKIP <test>: <reason>` line on stderr and fails unless OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP names that test; an allowed skip passes and still prints its line; the helper's allow-list parsing has gate tests; README's checkpoint section shows the new invocation; a vision comment corrects the M2 real-machine count; argc gate passes
close_reason: A checkpoint test that cannot run now prints a SKIP line and fails unless OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP names it; every checkpoint entry point goes through one helper.

title: Speed budgets run in the default gate although tests/perf.rs says every budget lives there
description:
## Background

`tests/perf.rs:1-4` says: "Time budgets, measured on release builds only … A debug build is several times slower and proves nothing, so each test is ignored. Every budget lives here, and nothing timing-based anywhere else." Vision §5.12 asks that "the lock-hold time is measured", and D16 puts benchmarks among the checkpoint-only checks. Still, the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found wall-clock assertions in the default gate (`cargo test`). They run in a debug build, in parallel with roughly 1,300 other tests, on a machine that other agents share. They passed 3 of 3 runs on an idle machine, and passed once more on 2026-10-18. They remain flake candidates whenever the machine is loaded, for example when another agent is building `target/` or btrfs fsync latency spikes. A flaky gate blocks every code commit (D16).

Each timing assertion at HEAD 53b54e6, classified:

| Site | Assertion | Class | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/engine_concurrency.rs:491-528` `multi_addon_commits_hold_the_lock_under_50_ms` | engine-reported `lock_held_ms` < 50 for four fixture-backed shapes (update of three, install with a dependency, mixed sync, handover) | speed budget (vision §7 M1: "Lock hold time per commit is < 50 ms on fixtures") | keep in the gate as a measurement with a 2,000 ms sanity ceiling and the printed values, renamed `multi_addon_commits_report_their_lock_hold`; the 50 ms budget moves to perf.rs (step 2) |
| `tests/engine_concurrency.rs:531-562` `every_commit_holds_the_lock_under_50_ms` | 20 commits, `lock_held_ms` < 50 | speed budget | moves to perf.rs (step 2) |
| `tests/inventory.rs:412-431` `classes_depth_is_fast` | 500 folders at `Depth::Classes` < 50 ms (debug) / 5 ms (release) | speed budget | timing moves to perf.rs; the gate keeps `counts.unmanaged == 500` and determinism, renamed `classes_depth_counts_500_folders` |
| `tests/discover_cache.rs:318-336` `cached_mode_is_fast` | 10 cached roots < 50 ms (debug) / 5 ms (release) | speed budget | timing moves to perf.rs; the gate keeps `(targets 10, reused 10, scanned false)`, renamed `cached_mode_reuses_every_root_without_scanning` |
| `tests/stage.rs:255-280` `five_thousand_small_files_within_budget` | staging 5,001 files < 5 s | throughput budget | timing moves to perf.rs (release, < 1 s); the gate keeps the 5,001-entry files index, renamed `five_thousand_small_files_are_staged_and_indexed` |
| `tests/fsx_lock.rs:126-149` `a_timeout_reports_locked_with_the_holder` | 190 ms ≤ waited < 2 s for a 200 ms timeout | correctness: the timeout is honoured (not 0, not the 5 s default) | keep. The lower bound cannot fail under load, because `acquire_with_timeout` (`src/fsx/lock.rs:79-111`) only gives up after `started.elapsed() >= timeout`. The upper bound has 10x margin |
| `tests/fsx_lock.rs:150-162` `sigkill_frees_the_lock_at_once` | re-acquire < 500 ms after SIGKILL | correctness (the kernel frees the flock at exit, vision §4.8) expressed as a speed | replace the timing: after `child.wait()`, assert `probe_global(&p) == LockState::Free`, then `GlobalLock::acquire_with_timeout(&p, "update", Duration::ZERO)` succeeds (zero timeout is a single `try_lock`, `src/fsx/lock.rs:100-110`) |
| `tests/targets.rs:333-350` `a_held_lock_times_out_as_locked` | elapsed ≥ 4 s | correctness: the CLI waits out the 5 s lock timeout (README "Exit codes", `locked`) | keep. A lower bound only gets safer under load |
| `tests/running.rs:267-283` `real_proc_within_budget` (already `#[ignore]`) | `detect_running` on the real `/proc` < 2 ms | speed budget, outside perf.rs | moves to perf.rs as an ignored release test (it reads `/proc` only) |
| `src/engine/tx.rs:1257-1261` | `lock_held_ms` < 2,000 | sanity ceiling | keep |
| `src/fsx/prune.rs:637-640` | < 1 s with the lock already held | correctness (it did not wait out the 5 s lock) | keep |
| `src/sources/git_hosts.rs:869-872` | < 10 s against a `sleep 30` child | correctness (the child was killed) | keep |
| `src/fsx/lock.rs:328` | `held_for` < 5 s | sanity | keep |
| `src/net/limit.rs:208-211` | `recv_timeout(100 ms)` is an error while a permit is held | can only pass falsely, never fail falsely | keep |

Waits that rely on sleeps to order processes (`tests/engine_concurrency.rs:259`, `tests/adopt.rs:1158`, `tests/multi_addon.rs:238`, and the in-process ones in `src/engine/tx.rs`) are a separate defect with a separate fix (explicit synchronization). They belong to omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.4, not to this bead.

## Technical Approach

1. **The rule, in `tests/perf.rs`'s header.** Replace "Every budget lives here, and nothing timing-based anywhere else" with: "Every speed budget lives here. Elsewhere, time appears only as a correctness bound with a wide margin: a wait that must last at least its timeout, a sanity ceiling of a second or more, or a killed child that must not run its course. Never as a speed target."
2. **New ignored release-build tests in `tests/perf.rs`**, each `#[ignore = "a release-build budget: cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored"]`, each printing its measurement on stderr (direct `writeln!` like the existing ones):
   - `commits_hold_the_lock_under_50_ms`: the body of `every_commit_holds_the_lock_under_50_ms` (20 `--file` + `--offline` installs through `common::engine::Scene`; these need no HTTP fixtures, so the release binary can run them). Add three multi-folder local shapes: one `install` of three local zips in one transaction, a `remove` of the three, and the `undo` of that remove. Assert `lock_held_ms` < 50 for every commit. The fixture-backed shapes cannot run here, because release builds never replay fixtures.
   - `classes_inventory_of_500_folders_under_5_ms`: median of 21 runs of `inventory(.., Depth::Classes)` over 500 folders < 5 ms. The 5 ms is the `status --cached` budget the gate test's comment already cites.
   - `cached_discovery_of_10_roots_under_5_ms`: median of 21 `DiscoveryMode::Cached` runs < 5 ms.
   - `staging_5001_files_under_1_s`: stage the same 5,001-file archive; < 1 s. The gate test's own message records about 0.3 s in a debug build; release is faster, so 1 s keeps a 3x margin over the debug figure.
   - `detect_running_on_the_real_proc_under_2_ms`: moved from `tests/running.rs:267-283` unchanged (budget from omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.3.10).
3. **Gate tests keep their non-timing assertions** and lose the timing, renamed as in the table, so their names no longer promise speed. `multi_addon_commits_report_their_lock_hold` keeps the presence check for the `lock released: … lock_held_ms N` log line, the stderr print (checkpoint evidence, as H2 used it) and `ms < 2_000`, matching `src/engine/tx.rs:1258`.
4. **`sigkill_frees_the_lock_at_once`** gets the deterministic assertion from the table.
5. **README.md**:
   - Safety model → Concurrency (about line 1352): "Tests assert each commit holds it under 50 ms" becomes "The checkpoint budget is under 50 ms per commit (`tests/perf.rs`, release build); the M1 and M2 checkpoints measured at most 2 ms."
   - Tests table (about line 1831): `tests/engine_concurrency.rs` becomes "Parallel runs, duplicate installs, races between plan and commit, the lock hold of multi-addon commits (measured)". Add a `tests/perf.rs` row: "Time budgets (release build, checkpoint only) and the request-economy checks that run in the gate".
   - Coordinate with omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.5, which rewrites the surrounding Tests paragraph. Whichever lands second rebases on the other.
6. **Checkpoint record**: the next checkpoint runs `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored` (omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.1 adds `--skip bench_home --skip live_home`) and pastes the printed numbers. No vision comment is needed: vision §7's "< 50 ms on fixtures" stands, and only where it is measured changes. Mention it in the close reason.

Rejected alternatives:
- Widening the margins in place (e.g. 50 ms → 500 ms in debug). It still flakes under heavy load and still contradicts perf.rs's rule, and a 500 ms bound proves nothing about a 50 ms budget.
- `#[ignore]`-ing the gate tests where they are. That scatters budgets across files and loses their non-timing assertions from the gate.
- Running perf.rs under the `bench-fixtures` profile so the fixture-backed lock shapes can move too. That changes what every existing release budget measures (debug assertions on).

No contract change: tests only, plus README wording.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `grep -n "elapsed\|Instant::now" tests/*.rs` outside `tests/perf.rs` matches only the kept correctness bounds in the table: `fsx_lock` timeout window, `targets` ≥ 4 s, polling deadlines and `common_selftest` mtime checks.
- The five perf tests exist, are ignored, pass under `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored`, and print their numbers.
- The renamed gate tests keep every non-timing assertion they had.
- `sigkill_frees_the_lock_at_once` contains no duration bound.
- README's Concurrency sentence and Tests table match.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Integration (gate): run the renamed tests under load to show they no longer depend on speed, e.g. `cargo test --locked --test inventory --test discover_cache --test stage --test fsx_lock --test engine_concurrency` while `cargo build --release` runs in another shell.
- Perf (checkpoint): `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored` once, recording the numbers in the close reason.
- Concurrency suite: `tests/engine_concurrency.rs` keeps all of its race tests unchanged here. Their synchronization is omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.4's.

## Considerations

- Release builds ignore `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` and `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`. The moved lock-hold test uses only `--file` and `--offline`, so the release binary reads the real `/proc` (harmless: synthetic targets in a tempdir HOME never match a real process, and the process route only looks under HOME) and makes no request. The existing `status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_a_realistic_memo` already runs this way.
- Do not drop the multi-addon lock measurement from the gate. Its printed numbers were the M2 checkpoint's evidence ("update of three 2 ms, …"). It only stops failing on speed.
- The structural guard behind README's promise that planning and staging take no lock already exists in-process (`src/engine/tx.rs:1397` `the_lock_is_free_while_staging`), but it is sleep-timed. omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.4 makes it deterministic and adds a process-level test: the lock is observed free while a run is paused at `engine.plan.done` and at `engine.stage.synced`. That guard holds whatever the machine's speed, so it, not the 50 ms check, is the correctness net in the gate. This bead does not depend on it, because the 2,000 ms ceiling and the printed values stay meanwhile.
- If a later change adds a timing assertion to a gate test, the perf.rs header is the rule to cite in review.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.4`: Race tests order processes with fixed sleeps; add a pause failpoint and sync explicitly
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.1`: Checkpoint tests that bail out early report as passed, so a skip reads as a pass
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.4`: Engine failure-injection matrix and concurrency tests (M1 checkpoints)
- `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7`: M2 checkpoint verification
acceptance_criteria: no gate test asserts an upper bound on wall-clock time tighter than 1 s except as documented correctness bounds; the five throughput and lock-hold budgets run in tests/perf.rs as ignored release-build tests with their numbers; each gate test keeps its non-timing assertions; sigkill_frees_the_lock_at_once asserts the lock is free without timing; README's lock-hold sentence and suite table say where the budget lives; argc gate passes
close_reason: Every speed budget is a release-build check in tests/perf.rs that prints its numbers; gate tests keep their non-timing assertions and only correctness bounds of a second or more.

title: The real HTTP transport (src/net/client.rs) is never exercised by the gate
description:
## Background

README "Network and privacy" makes promises that rest on the bottom transport, `src/net/client.rs`:
- the allowlist "is checked on every redirect hop". This needs ureq to follow no redirect itself, so that every hop goes back through `Redirecting` and the guard;
- "HTTP proxies are not supported";
- "TLS uses rustls with the bundled Mozilla root store (webpki-roots), not the system store".

Its module doc (`src/net/client.rs:1-3`) states the same: "ureq follows no redirects …, treats no status as an error, and uses no proxy". Vision §5.12 says every network test replays HTTP fixtures "through the `Http` trait, so tests use no network". That is right for the decoders and layers, but it means `UreqTransport` itself is never tested in the gate:
- `UreqTransport::new()` (`src/net/client.rs:15-28`) only runs when a binary run selects the real transport (`src/net/mod.rs:318`). Even then, offline tests are refused by the guard before `send` is called.
- `send` (`:37-68`) and `transport_error` (`:71-78`) run only in `#[ignore]`d live probes (`tests/live_probes.rs`, `src/net/tests.rs:555`).
- The M1 checkpoint (omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.7.10 close reason) measured "src/net/client.rs 0% (the real HTTP transport, exercised only by live probes)". Nothing has changed since.

The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit raised this. Consequence: a ureq upgrade, or an edit to the builder, could make the transport follow redirects, read proxy variables from the environment, turn 404s into errors or drop the User-Agent, and the gate would stay green. A transport that followed redirects would bypass the per-hop allowlist and `Authorization` stripping in `Redirecting`, and README's privacy promise rests on those.

ureq 3.4.2 makes this cheap to test. It exposes the agent's config (`Agent::config()`, with getters `max_redirects`, `http_status_as_error`, `proxy`, `user_agent`, `timeouts`, `tls_config().root_certs()/provider()/disable_verification()/use_sni()`). The transport itself does not enforce https, because the guard does (`src/net/tests.rs` `unlisted_and_non_https_urls_are_refused_before_sending`). So `send` can be driven over plain HTTP on loopback, with the production configuration unchanged.

## Technical Approach

Decided: **unit tests of the agent's configuration, plus `send` against a plain-HTTP loopback server, inside `src/net/client.rs`'s own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.** No TLS server and no new crate.

1. Small refactor in `src/net/client.rs` (no behaviour change):
   - `UreqTransport` gains `api_timeout: Duration` and `download_timeout: Duration`, set by `new()` from `API_READ_TIMEOUT` and `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT`.
   - `send` uses `fn timeout_for(&self, kind: TimeoutKind) -> Duration` instead of the inline match (`:38-41`).
   - Add a `#[cfg(test)]` constructor `with_timeouts(api, download)` that reuses `new()`'s agent. It exists only in this crate's unit-test build, never in a release build or in integration tests. That is the only test-only code, and it widens no seam: no environment variable, no public API.
2. Tests (`src/net/client.rs`):
   - `the_agent_is_configured_as_documented`, from `UreqTransport::new().agent.config()`:
     - `max_redirects() == 0`;
     - `!http_status_as_error()`;
     - `proxy().is_none()`;
     - `user_agent()` is `AutoHeaderValue::Provided(USER_AGENT)`;
     - `timeouts().connect == Some(CONNECT_TIMEOUT)`;
     - `tls_config().provider() == TlsProvider::Rustls`;
     - `matches!(root_certs(), RootCerts::WebPki)`;
     - `!disable_verification()` and `use_sni()`.
   - `timeouts_follow_the_request_kind`: `Api` → `API_READ_TIMEOUT`, `Download` → `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT`.
   - A loopback helper in the test module, using only `std::net`:
     - `serve(responses: Vec<Vec<u8>>) -> (SocketAddr, JoinHandle<Vec<String>>)` binds `127.0.0.1:0` (a kernel-assigned ephemeral port, never a fixed one);
     - for each canned response it accepts one connection, reads the request head up to `\r\n\r\n`, records it, writes the response and closes;
     - it returns the recorded heads;
     - it sets a 5 s accept/read timeout so a broken test cannot hang the gate.
   - `a_redirect_is_returned_not_followed`:
     - server A answers `302` with `Location: http://<server B>/next`;
     - assert `status == 302`, `location()` is B's URL, A saw exactly one request and B saw none (B's listener is non-blocking and checked after the call).
   - `error_statuses_are_responses`: 404 and 503 come back as `Ok(Response)` with those statuses and their bodies.
   - `headers_go_out_and_come_back`:
     - a GET with `req.headers` `accept` and `if-none-match`: the recorded head has `user-agent: <USER_AGENT>` and both headers (names compared case-insensitively);
     - the response's `ETag` and a custom header are returned and the body bytes are equal;
     - a `Method::Head` request is recorded as `HEAD`.
   - `a_stalled_server_times_out_as_network`:
     - a listener that accepts and never writes, with `with_timeouts(200 ms, 200 ms)`;
     - the result is `Err` with `ErrorCode::Network` and `retryable`;
     - the call returns in under 5 s. That is a correctness bound with a 25x margin, allowed under omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2's rule.
   - `a_refused_connection_is_network_and_redacted`:
     - bind a listener, take its port, drop it, then send to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/x?token=SECRET`;
     - the result is `Err(Network)`, retryable, and the message contains `127.0.0.1` but not `SECRET`;
     - this pins `redact` in `transport_error`.
3. Docs: `src/politeness.rs:21` "Read timeout for JSON API calls" becomes "Timeout for a whole JSON API call: DNS, connect, headers and body". The code applies it as ureq's `timeout_global` (`src/net/client.rs:52-55`), and the vision table says only "JSON API calls". The REGISTRY note "JSON API calls" (`src/politeness.rs:96`) stays, so the limits snapshot does not change.
4. Coverage: the M3 checkpoint's `cargo llvm-cov --summary-only` should show `src/net/client.rs` at about 90% lines or more. Record the number in that checkpoint's close reason.

Rejected alternatives:
- **A loopback TLS server with a test CA injected under `cfg(test)`.** It needs rustls's server side as a dev-dependency, committed key material that expires, and a root-certificate injection path. It mostly tests rustls and webpki rather than omaddons. The TLS choices omaddons makes (provider, roots, verification) are pinned by the config test, and real TLS against github.com stays covered by the live probes at checkpoints.
- **A debug-only allowlist exception for `127.0.0.1`**, so the whole stack could hit a local server. README promises the list is "matched exactly". A loopback hole in debug builds is one `cfg` away from shipping, and the per-hop guard is already tested with fake transports (`src/net/tests.rs`).
- **Setting `https_only(true)` on the agent** as defense in depth. The guard already refuses `http://` before sending. This would make the transport untestable over plain loopback. If it is ever wanted, the test then needs the TLS path, so it is not done here.
- **Relying on the live probes alone.** They run at checkpoints only, and the gate is what catches a regression in the commit that causes it.

No contract change: tests plus one doc comment. No dependency change, so `cargo deny` is not triggered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The seven tests above exist in `src/net/client.rs` and pass in the gate, using only loopback.
- `UreqTransport::new()`'s production configuration is unchanged (diff limited to the timeout fields and `timeout_for`).
- No new crate in `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`.
- No `cfg(debug_assertions)` seam and no environment variable added.
- `src/politeness.rs:21`'s doc matches the whole-call semantics.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `src/net/client.rs` tests as listed. Run `cargo test --locked --lib net::client` three times in a row to show they are stable, and once while `cargo build --release` runs.
- Integration: none new. `tests/net_replay.rs` and `src/net/tests.rs` keep covering the layers above the transport.
- Checkpoint: the live probes (`OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored`) remain the real-TLS evidence. Coverage is recorded as in step 4.

## Considerations

- ureq's 3.x getters are public API, so if a ureq upgrade renames one, the test fails at compile time. That is the point.
- The loopback server must answer `Connection: close` and close the socket, so that ureq's connection pool cannot reuse a connection across the tests' canned responses.
- Port 0 binds avoid clashing with anything else on the machine. No fixed port is ever used.
- The stalled-server test costs about 200 ms of gate time, and nothing else waits on the clock.
- Interaction with omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2: the 5 s bound in the stalled-server test is a correctness bound (the timeout fired at all), not a speed budget, so it may stay in the gate under omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2's rule.

## Related

- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.7.10`: Verify the M1 checkpoints: real-machine smoke, keyless installs, fuzz, probes and README
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2`: Speed budgets run in the default gate although tests/perf.rs says every budget lives there
acceptance_criteria: unit tests in src/net/client.rs pin the ureq agent's configuration (no redirects, statuses not errors, no proxy, the User-Agent, the connect timeout, rustls with the webpki roots and verification on) and drive `send` against a plain-HTTP loopback server (a 302 is returned and not followed, 4xx/5xx are responses, headers go out and come back, HEAD sends HEAD, a stalled server times out as retryable `network`, a refused connection is `network` with the query redacted); no release-build seam or new dependency is added; politeness.rs documents API_READ_TIMEOUT as the whole-call timeout it is; argc gate passes
close_reason: The real HTTP transport is tested in the gate: its ureq configuration is pinned and send is driven against a plain-HTTP loopback server.

title: Race tests order processes with fixed sleeps; add a pause failpoint and sync explicitly
description:
## Background

Vision §5.12 requires concurrency tests: "concurrent staging by two processes; a reader during a live swap never recovers; … no lost records". README's Safety model promises: "Planning and staging take no lock … The global lock … is held for the commit window." The tests that prove this need one run to stop at a known step while another acts. Today they rely on timing. A child is armed with `sleep:<ms>` at a failpoint (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs:17-27`, `:96-110`). The test then either sleeps a fixed time itself, or polls for an observable condition and assumes the child's sleep outlasts what it does next.

The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit flagged `tests/engine_concurrency.rs:259`. Re-checking at HEAD 53b54e6 found the same pattern at about twenty sites, in two failure modes:

- **Fixed parent sleeps guess how long planning takes.**
  - `tests/engine_concurrency.rs:254-262` (`a_pin_that_commits_while_an_update_plans_wins`) polls for the planning in-flight lock, which appears when planning *starts*, then sleeps 500 ms hoping run A has read the records. If A is slower, B's pin lands before A plans, and the race under test does not happen.
  - `tests/adopt.rs:1150-1163` (`a_file_changed_between_planning_and_the_lock_is_plan_stale`, 300 ms) is worse. If adopt has not hashed the folder before the parent edits `core.lua`, adopt hashes the edited file, nothing is stale, and `r.expect(1)` fails.
  - `tests/multi_addon.rs:226-241` (`while_planned`, 500 ms) has the same shape and is used by several handover tests.
- **The child's sleep must outlast the parent's next command.** If the parent's action takes longer than the remaining sleep under load, the child wakes, commits first, and the assertions see the other interleaving:
  - `tests/engine_concurrency.rs:58-75` (reader during a live swap, `engine.swapped=sleep:2000`; the reader's `status` must finish inside 2 s);
  - `:106-125` (recovery only under the lock, `engine.lock.acquired=sleep:2000`);
  - `:142-166` `concurrently()` (`engine.stage.synced=sleep:500`, "so they overlap");
  - `:323-341` `pin_races_an_install` (1,500 ms);
  - `:393-401` and `:426-434` (1,500 ms);
  - `tests/fsx_lock.rs:193-205` (`fsx.lock.acquired=sleep:500`; the poll must see `Held` inside 500 ms);
  - `tests/fsx_prune.rs:131-145` (`fsx.prune.deleting=sleep:1000`).
  - The in-process unit tests in `src/engine/tx.rs` use 400–600 ms sleeps with 150 ms parent sleeps, the tightest margins in the suite: `:1397-1424` `the_lock_is_free_while_staging`, `:1429-1478` `a_concurrent_change_is_replanned_once`, `:1748-1790` `edits_survive_concurrent_changes_their_guards_allow`, and the tests starting at `:1792`, `:1808`, `:1832` and `:1930-1960`.
  - Example: in the second half of `a_concurrent_change_is_replanned_once`, if the slow thread has not planned within 150 ms, the `Remove` and the new `Bar/` directory land before it plans. It then fails at plan time with `unmanaged_folder` instead of `plan_stale`, and the assertion fails.

`tests/engine_concurrency.rs:1-4` says its assertions are "on final state, never on interleavings". Several tests do assert an interleaving, though. For example, `a_pin_that_commits_while_an_update_plans_wins` asserts history `["install", "update"]`, "two commits, none by A". All of these passed on idle runs, and they are flake candidates whenever the machine is loaded. A flaky gate blocks every code commit (D16).

## Technical Approach

1. **A `pause` action in `src/fsx/failpoint.rs`** (debug builds only, like every action, DEC-7):
   - Syntax: `<name>=pause[@N]`. `parse_action` (`:83-93`) gains `"pause" => Some(Action::Pause)`.
   - On a hit, with a pause directory configured:
     - create `<dir>/<name>.reached` holding the pid, using `create_new`; if it already exists, overwrite it;
     - poll every 5 ms for `<dir>/<name>.resume`, waiting at most `PAUSE_MAX = 60 s`;
     - then return `Ok(())`.
   - Once `.resume` exists, every later hit of that name passes straight through. That is how a failpoint hit once per target (for example `engine.stage.synced`) pauses only the first time, unless `@N` picks another hit.
   - On timeout it continues, so a broken test never leaves a hung child.
   - The pause directory comes from `OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR` (absolute path) for environment-armed failpoints. For thread-local overrides it comes from a new `pub fn with_spec_in<T>(dir: &Path, spec: &str, f: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> T` (`#[doc(hidden)]`, debug only, beside `with_spec` at `:179`).
   - A `pause` with no directory is ignored, as malformed entries are today (module doc, `:7-8`).
   - The marker files are written with `std::fs` inside `src/fsx/`. That is where the single writer allows writes (`tests/single_writer.rs`), and they are only debug-build test scaffolding. `PAUSE_MAX` is a test-seam constant, not a §5.13 safety limit or a politeness constant, so it stays in `failpoint.rs` with a comment saying so.
   - Update the module doc's syntax line (`:3`) and the action list.
2. **A test helper `tests/common/pause.rs`**, declared in `tests/common/mod.rs`:
   - `Pause::new(&TestEnv)` makes its own directory under the env root, one per child process, so two children can pause at the same name.
   - `.env()` returns `("OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR", dir)`.
   - `.reached(name)` waits up to 30 s for the marker and panics with `"the child never reached {name}"`.
   - `.resume(name)` creates the resume file.
   - For `src/engine/tx.rs` unit tests, add the same three methods to `src/engine/testing.rs` (cfg(test)), so in-process threads use `with_spec_in`.
3. **Convert every site listed in Background.** The pattern is: arm `=pause`, wait `reached`, act, `resume`, wait for the child. Delete every `std::thread::sleep` used for ordering, and every `sleep:` failpoint whose purpose is ordering. Specifics:
   - `concurrently()` pauses both children at `engine.stage.synced`, waits for both to reach it, then resumes both. The overlap is then guaranteed, not hoped for.
   - `a_pin_that_commits_while_an_update_plans_wins` and `while_planned` pause at `engine.plan.done`. There, planning has finished by definition, so the 300 and 500 ms guesses go.
   - `fsx_lock::probe_reports_missing_held_and_free` pauses at `fsx.lock.acquired` and also asserts that the holder is still unwritten (`Held { holder: None }`). Its comment claims that today but does not check it.
   - `fsx_prune::deletion_runs_without_the_global_lock` pauses at `fsx.prune.deleting` and asserts once (victim gone, one trash entry, lock `Free`), without a polling loop.
   - Sleeps that only pace a polling loop while waiting on a real condition (for example `poll()` in `tests/engine_concurrency.rs:21-27`) are fine and stay. They order nothing.
4. **A structural lock guard (new test)**, `tests/engine_concurrency.rs::planning_and_staging_take_no_lock`:
   - On a registered `Scene`, spawn `install … --file v2 --offline` with `engine.plan.done=pause`; wait `reached`; assert `probe_global(&paths) == LockState::Free`; resume.
   - Do the same at `engine.stage.synced`.
   - The run then commits (exit 0, generation + 1).
   - Make `src/engine/tx.rs::the_lock_is_free_while_staging` deterministic the same way.
   - This is README's "Planning and staging take no lock" as a check that holds whatever the machine's speed. omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2 relies on it when it moves the 50 ms budget out of the gate.
5. **Docs**:
   - `tests/engine_concurrency.rs:1-4`: the header becomes "real processes synchronized by `pause` failpoints: each run stops at a named step until the test resumes it, so the interleaving a test names is the one that runs".
   - README "Environment variables" (about line 1546): "Debug builds also read `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD` and `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` for testing. Release builds ignore them."

Rejected alternatives:
- Longer sleeps. They are slower in every run and still only probabilistic.
- Signalling through the child's stderr (a log line at the failpoint). Commands never print outside `src/output/`, and the test would need a reader thread per child.
- Pausing via `SIGSTOP`/`SIGCONT`. The test cannot know where the child stopped.
- Polling an on-disk side effect instead of a marker. There is none at `engine.plan.done` for records-only runs such as `adopt` and `pin`.

No contract change: debug-only seam, no wire field, no error or warning code. Release builds never read either variable (`configured()` is `None` there, `src/fsx/failpoint.rs:117-121`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pause` parses, pauses until resumed, passes through once resumed, honours `@N`, and continues after `PAUSE_MAX`.
- `pause` without a directory is ignored.
- Release builds ignore it.
- Every site in Background uses `reached`/`resume`.
- `grep -rn "thread::sleep" tests/*.rs src/engine/tx.rs` finds only polling-loop pacing, each next to the condition it waits for.
- `grep -rn "=sleep:" tests src` finds none used for ordering. The `failpoint.rs` unit tests of the `sleep` action itself stay.
- `planning_and_staging_take_no_lock` exists and passes.
- README's env-var sentence names `OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR`.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs` tests):
  - `parses_pause` (`pause`, `pause@2`);
  - `pause_waits_for_resume_and_then_passes`, using `with_spec_in` on a thread with a tempdir: reached appears, the thread is still blocked, resume, the thread returns, and a second hit passes at once;
  - `pause_without_a_directory_is_ignored`.
- Integration:
  - every converted test in `tests/engine_concurrency.rs`, `tests/adopt.rs`, `tests/multi_addon.rs`, `tests/fsx_lock.rs` and `tests/fsx_prune.rs`;
  - the new `planning_and_staging_take_no_lock`.
- Load check (by hand, not in the gate): run `cargo test --locked --test engine_concurrency --test adopt --test multi_addon --test fsx_lock --test fsx_prune` and `cargo test --locked --lib engine::tx` three times while a `cargo build --release` runs. All pass.
- Crash suite: `tests/engine_crash.rs` is untouched. It arms `abort`, never `sleep`.

## Considerations

- Wall time drops: the 1.5–2 s sleeps go, so the concurrency suite gets faster.
- A child that never reaches its failpoint (the code path changed) now fails with a precise message instead of a confusing state assertion.
- `@N` with `pause`: marker names do not carry N. Each test pauses at most one hit per name per child, and separate `Pause` directories keep children apart.
- If this is too large for one session, split it: (a) the action, the helper and the integration-test conversions, plus the new structural test; (b) the `src/engine/tx.rs` unit-test conversions. (b) depends on (a).
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2 moves the lock-hold speed budget to `tests/perf.rs`. The structural guard here is what keeps README's lock promise checked in the gate.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2`: Speed budgets run in the default gate although tests/perf.rs says every budget lives there
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.4`: Engine failure-injection matrix and concurrency tests (M1 checkpoints)
- `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7`: M2 checkpoint verification
acceptance_criteria: a debug-only `pause` failpoint action stops at a named point until the test resumes it (marker files in OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR for child processes, a directory passed to with_spec_in in-process); every test listed below waits for "reached" instead of sleeping and resumes explicitly; no test in tests/ or src/ orders two runs with thread::sleep or a sleep: failpoint any more; an integration test shows the global lock free while a run is paused at engine.plan.done and at engine.stage.synced; README's debug env-var sentence names the new variable; argc gate passes
close_reason: Race tests synchronize through a debug-only pause failpoint instead of sleeps; a structural test shows the global lock free while a run is planned and staged.

title: README and doc comments contradict the code in 22 places after M2
description:
## Background

README.md is the product contract, and CLAUDE.md requires that it "describes exactly what exists". The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit listed contradictions between README, doc comments and the code at HEAD 53b54e6. This bead verified each one against the code. Reading README end to end on 2026-10-18 found five more (marked NEW below). Users and agents read README as the specification, so each wrong line misleads someone: an agent told `auth_required` is "reserved" will not handle it, and a user who sets `check_interval_hours = 0` expecting "checks only when the panel opens" gets the 6-hour default.

Evidence came from read-only code reading, `cargo test --locked -- --list`, and isolated synthetic homes (`env -i`, throwaway `HOME`/XDG dirs, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, an empty fake `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`) running the debug binary.

| # | README / doc | Claim | Code at HEAD | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | README:1266 | "Every warning code (26)" | `src/error.rs:240-296` registers 35, and README's own table (1268-1304) lists the same 35 | "(35)". Keep the count: the table under it changes in the same commit as the registry, as the error count (39, correct) does |
| 2 | README:1322, :1829 | "24 snapshots" | `tests/contract/snapshots/` holds 60 (`tests/contract/matrix.rs` makes 60 `assert_json_snapshot!` calls) | No count: "insta snapshots in `tests/contract/snapshots/` pin representative envelopes" |
| 3 | README:1852 | "nine cargo-fuzz targets: archive, bottles, …" | `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` has 16: archive, atom_feed, bbcode_text, bottles, bpsv, desired_toml, heroic, html_text, lutris, product_db, ref_parse, steam_vdf, toc, tukui_addons, wowi_details, wowi_filelist; `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs:17-34` lists the same; each has `fuzz/seeds/<target>/` | "One cargo-fuzz target per parser of untrusted input, in `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` (16 at the M2 checkpoint: <the list>); `argc fuzz-all` runs every file there, and `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs` keeps the list in step with `fuzz/Cargo.toml`." |
| 4 | README:1825 | "760 tests: 464 unit …, 295 integration tests in 46 test binaries, one doctest. 29 proptest properties. 28 are #[ignore]d … live probes, real-machine tests, fixture recorders and child-process helpers" | `cargo test --locked -- --list` at HEAD: 1,333 tests = 699 unit (src/lib.rs) + 633 integration in 72 test binaries + 1 doctest; 45 ignored; 24 `proptest!` blocks with 37 properties. The ignored ones: 16 live probes, 9 real-machine, 5 in `tests/perf.rs` (3 budgets, `bench_home`, `live_home`), 7 fixture recorders, 4 child-process helpers, `write_fuzz_seeds`, `real_custom_client`, `real_proc_within_budget`, `net::tests::live_github_request` | Dated facts that stay true: "At the M2 checkpoint (2026-10-16) there were 1,333 tests: 699 unit tests in `src/`, 633 integration tests in 72 test binaries and one doctest, with 37 proptest properties. `cargo test -- --list` counts today's. 45 are `#[ignore]`d and run only at checkpoints or by hand: live probes, real-machine and real-client checks, time budgets and the bench homes (`tests/perf.rs`), fixture recorders, the fuzz-seed writer and child-process helpers." Rejected: a script-generated count. README is not a build artifact, and a gate check that reads README would make README-only commits gate-relevant, against D16 |
| 5 | README:1833 | `tests/catalog.rs`: "The 19 GitHub and `git:` catalog entries …" | Correct (14 `gh:` + 5 `git:`; `tests/catalog.rs:85,111`). The 2 `tukui:` entries are tested in `tests/sources_tukui.rs:37-38`. The test file's own doc (`tests/catalog.rs:1`) says "Every catalog entry" | README row: append "(the two Tukui entries: `tests/sources_tukui.rs`)". `tests/catalog.rs:1`: "Every GitHub and `git:` catalog entry resolves …" |
| 6 | README:1472-1474, :1503 | `check_interval_hours` "Read; used in milestone 3"; "0 checks only when the panel opens" | Used today. `Config::effective_limits` (`src/state/config.rs:496-501`) sets `default_check_interval`, and `status` reads it (`src/app/status.rs:390-393`) for `updates.stale`, as README:599 says. A value of 0 is filtered out (`.filter(\|h\| *h > 0)`) and keeps the 6-hour default (`src/politeness.rs:36`) | Example comment: "# How old an update check may be before status calls it stale (updates.stale): 1–48 hours; 0 keeps the default of 6." Table: "`status` reports `updates.stale` when the oldest check is older than this (1–48; 0 keeps the default)". Keep `auto_backup` as "Read; used in milestone 3" (true: nothing reads it, `src/app/config.rs:140` only shows its default) |
| 7 | `src/state/config.rs:43`, `:247-251` | field doc "0–48; 0 checks only when the panel opens"; key help "Hours between background update checks" | No background checks exist; see #6 | Field: "Hours before `status` calls an update check stale (`updates.stale`); 0 keeps the default." Help: "Hours before status calls an update check stale" |
| 8 | README:1291 | `credential_file_mode` "reserved for credential files other users can read (no command reads credentials yet)" | Raised by `resolve_credential` (`src/state/config.rs:755`, the warning at `:777-786`) for `{ file = … }` credentials and for the stored token (`src/sources/github_token.rs:112-117`, "through the credential reader, for its file-mode warning") | "a credential file (config.toml's `{ file = … }` credential, or the token `auth github set` stores) is readable by other users; the fix is `chmod 600 <file>`" |
| 9 | README:1257-1258 | `auth_required`, `auth_rejected` "reserved for credentialed sources" | `auth_required` comes from `src/sources/github_token.rs:188-202` (an empty or malformed token), `src/state/config.rs:757-774` (unset `{ env }`, unreadable `{ file }`) and `src/app/auth.rs:237-262` (`--from-gh` without `gh`, or `gh auth token` failing). `auth_rejected` comes from `src/sources/github_token.rs:158-179` (a 401 for the token) and `src/state/config.rs:799-806` (a failed `{ command }` credential). README:1134 already describes the 401 case | `auth_required`: "a GitHub token is configured or stored but cannot be used: an unset `{ env = … }` variable, an unreadable `{ file = … }`, an empty or malformed token, or `auth github --from-gh` without a working `gh`". `auth_rejected`: "GitHub answered 401 to the token (the fix clears or replaces it where it came from), or a `{ command = … }` credential failed" |
| 10 | `src/state/config.rs:38`, `:231-235` | "The target for commands without -t" | Only `install` reads it (`src/app/install.rs:761`); `targets` shows that it wins (`src/app/targets.rs:561`). README:1460, 1498 and 453 are right | Both become "`install`'s target when `-t` is absent: an id, key or any `-t` form" |
| 11 | README:1868 | FAQ: "Adopting existing addons into management is milestone 2." | M2 is done; `adopt` exists (README:985-1034) | "… and even that is undoable. `omaddons adopt` brings them under management exactly as they are, changing only records (see [`adopt`](#adopt))." |
| 12 | README:167 | Design philosophy 5: "a new Classic client or a misdetected private server is a config change, not a release" | `Family` is a closed enum (`src/rules.rs:148-163`); the `release.json` flavor names (`:234-251`, `:167-172`) and family default ids (`:1059-1074`) are code; `[rules] family_ranges` can only re-range existing families. omad-359 (Titan) changed the built-in row, though `[client_rules.titan]` could have patched it | "Each can be patched from `config.toml`: a new product code, a changed version range or load rule for a known family, or a misdetected private server is a config change, not a release. A new family (an expansion line with its own `release.json` flavor) still needs a release, because families are a closed set in code." |
| 13 | README:1422 | Tukui: "responses are never cached (`no-store`)" | The HTTP validator cache never stores them (`src/sources/tukui.rs:90-91`), but the stripped project list (no download links) is kept in the release memo (`DecodedList::memo`, `:71-77`) and reused for 15 minutes and offline (README:646, 1079; `src/resolve/cache.rs:394-398`) | "… responses are never stored by the HTTP cache (`no-store`); the project list, without its download links, is kept in the release memo (15 minutes, and for `--offline`)" |
| 14 | README:1779; `src/discover/product_db.rs:5-6`; vision §4.1 and §8 | product.db's layout "UNVERIFIED" | Verified on the development machine (omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.3.8 comment 108: install path at settings(3).1, flavor folder at settings(3).13, version at cached_state(4).base_state(1).7, matching WowUp; fixture `tests/fixtures/product_db/retail.db`) | **Not fixed here: owned by omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.6**, which reads product.db by field number (fixing the uid/product-code mix-up), rewrites the module doc, drops product.db from README:1779 and adds the vision comment. This bead leaves those lines alone |
| 15 | README:15-25 | Hero `status` block: "Real output from the development machine", forever "0 managed · 12 unmanaged" | The development machine's forever client now has 12 managed folders (the stress-test set, omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6), and `status` now prints adoptable counts and a `Next:` line | Regenerate from a synthetic home with the development machine's layout (recipe below). Caption: "Output from a test home laid out like the development machine: five Battle.net clients in one Proton prefix and a 3.3.5a private-server client in another, found with no configuration." Rejected: re-running on the real machine (real paths, changes daily) and dating the old block (it shows output the binary no longer prints) |
| 16 NEW | README:290-321 | "A whole session … real output from a test home" | Re-run at HEAD in a synthetic home: `history` prints a run column (`01M582ENGR…  01M582ENGQ…  2026-10-18 …`), as README:903 says ("Every line shows its run"); `list` has a (blank) latest column between version and ref | Regenerate the session block with the same commands |
| 17 NEW | README:327, :1164 | `file:$HOME/Downloads/./EraOnly.zip`; JSON `"ref":"file:…/src/./Bar-2.1.0.zip"` | omad-ex35 ("new file: refs carry no . component") removed the `./`: today's message is `file:$HOME/Downloads/EraOnly.zip does not load on retail (Mainline)` and the dry-run ref is `file:<home>/Downloads/Bar-2.1.0.zip` | Drop the `./` component in both examples |
| 18 NEW | README:1672, :1771 | "Wine prefixes are found only as direct children of `$HOME/Games`, as `$HOME/.wine`, or where a launcher config names them"; "Discovery reads only the direct children of `$HOME/Games` as prefixes" | The process route (omad-93rc, `src/discover/running.rs:82-115`, `src/app/world.rs:85-89`) adds a running WoW or Battle.net process's `WINEPREFIX` under `HOME`, and registered roots stay found (README:367, 379) | 1672: "… or where a launcher config names them, and, while a WoW or Battle.net process runs, as that process's `WINEPREFIX` under your home; once registered, such a client stays found after it exits." 1771: "Discovery scans only the direct children of `$HOME/Games` as prefixes (a nested prefix is found through a launcher config or while its client runs), and Lutris …" |
| 19 NEW | README:1779 | Known limitations lists what is UNVERIFIED | Vision §4.8 and §8 also mark Wine's process naming under Proton/umu UNVERIFIED (vision comment 341: "Not verified on real installs: Wine process naming under Proton while the game runs"); running detection depends on it | Add it to the same bullet. omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.6 and omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.3 also edit README:1771 and :1779, so rebase on them. omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.1 removes the note once observed |
| 20 NEW | README:1350 | "Interrupted runs. The next command that commits a change (install, remove or undo) recovers" | Every engine commit recovers first (`src/engine/tx.rs:575`, `src/engine/undo.rs:223`), so `update`, `pin`/`unpin`, `sync`, `adopt` and `copy` do too | **Not fixed here.** omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10 changes which commands recover. Align this sentence with omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10 when it lands, and make sure omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10's README step covers it |
| 21 NEW | README warning table, `stale_check` row (~1293) | "an offline answer came from the release memo, whatever its age; it names the oldest remembered check" | The stored WoWInterface index raises it too, offline or after a failed refresh (`src/sources/wowi/index.rs:174-177`, `:191-194`, `:212-221`) | "an answer came from stored data, not from the source now: offline from the release memo, or from the stored WoWInterface index (offline, or after a failed refresh); it names how old". (Folded in from a parallel draft; omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.12 may change this warning's message, so rebase on it) |
| 22 NEW | Vision §5.5 Retention (pinned bead omad-vision-8qa) | "Blobs referenced by retained transactions, installed records or unexpired plans are pinned" | `src/engine/retention.rs:203-210` pins blobs of installed releases only, which is exactly what README "Retention" promises ("Archives of releases installed on any target are pinned"). Undo never reads blobs (it uses snapshots), and the LRU already evicts retained transactions' blobs last. Pinning them would let heavy setups exceed the 1 GiB cap by far; the only cost today is a re-download on an explicit `install --version <old>` | Code and README stand. Add a comment on omad-vision-8qa recording the departure: "§5.5 Retention: blobs are pinned for installed releases only; undo uses snapshots, so retained transactions need no blob pin (plans are M4)." Verified and decided by the 2026-10-16 audit follow-up, which dropped the code change |

Lines owned by other beads are left untouched here:
- README:1352 and the `tests/engine_concurrency.rs` row at :1831 (omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2);
- the checkpoint commands at :1838-1851 (omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.1);
- README:1350 (omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10);
- the command reference sections that omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.3/omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.4 (CLI) and omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.1/omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.13/omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.8 (sources) may rewrite.

Rebase on whichever lands first.

## Technical Approach

1. Apply each decision in the table to README.md, and to `src/state/config.rs:38,43,231-235,247-251` and `tests/catalog.rs:1`. Doc strings and test docs are code, so the gate runs. No string here is snapshotted (grep found none), and no wire field, code or schema changes.
2. **Synthetic home for #15 and #16.** Build it with a throwaway script outside the repository, never against the real home: `env -i PATH=… HOME=<tmp>/home XDG_*=<tmp>/home/… OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<tmp>/proc target/debug/omaddons …`. Layout:
   - `$HOME/Games/battlenet/` is a prefix (`drive_c/`, `dosdevices/c: -> ../drive_c`) with `drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/`. Its `.build.info` (the 15-column header of `tests/common/trees.rs:59`) has one row per product, with versions 2.5.6.70006 (`wow_anniversary`), 5.5.4.70268 (`wow_classic`), 1.15.9.70003 (`wow_classic_era`), 1.60.1.70245 (`wowf`) and 12.1.5.70391 (`wow`). Each flavor folder has a `.flavor.info`, an empty exe (`WoWClassic.exe`, `Wow.exe`, `WoW.exe`), `Interface/AddOns/` and `WTF/`.
   - `$HOME/Games/wow-335/` is a prefix with `drive_c/WoW/Wow.exe`, a PE stub with file version 3.3.5.12340 and product version 3.3.0.0 (the layout of `tests/common/pe.rs`), `Data/enUS/realmlist.wtf` set to `set realmlist 127.0.0.1`, and 23 `Blizzard_*` folders with `## Interface: 30300` TOCs.
   - Then: `install ./HelloWorld ./Bar-2.1.0.zip -t retail`, plus three hand-placed folders on forever named by catalog entries (`Plater`, `Bartender4`, `DBM-Core`, each with `## Interface: 16001`).
   - At HEAD 53b54e6 `omaddons status` then prints exactly:

     ```text
     anniversary  tbc                                           2.5.6.70006   live  anniversary (battlenet)  0 managed · 0 unmanaged · 0 protected
     classic      mists                                         5.5.4.70268   live  classic (battlenet)      0 managed · 0 unmanaged · 0 protected
     era          Classic Era · Hardcore · Season of Discovery  1.15.9.70003  live  era (battlenet)          0 managed · 0 unmanaged · 0 protected
     forever      forever                                       1.60.1.70245  live  forever (battlenet)      0 managed · 3 unmanaged · 0 protected · 3 adoptable
     retail       mainline                                      12.1.5.70391  live  retail (battlenet)       2 managed · 0 unmanaged · 0 protected
     wotlk        wrath-legacy                                  3.3.5.12340   live  localhost                0 managed · 0 unmanaged · 23 protected
     Next: omaddons adopt -t forever
     ```

     Regenerate at implementation time and paste what the binary prints then.
   - For #16, run the session commands of README:293-320 in a retail + Classic Era home (one unmanaged `OldThing` and one `Blizzard_*` folder on retail), and paste the output with absolute paths shortened to `~`, as the caption says.
3. One vision comment, for #22 (the retention departure). #14's comment is omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.6's. Docs only, no DEC-4 contract change.
4. Run the de-slopify pass on the edited paragraphs only.

Rejected:
- A gate test that diffs README blocks against rendered output. README is not a gate input (D16), and coupling would make README-only commits need the gate.
- Leaving the hero block and dating it. It would show output the binary no longer prints.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Items 1-13, 15-19, 21 and 22 are applied as decided (22 as a comment on omad-vision-8qa). Item 14 is omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.6's and item 20 is omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10's; note both in the close reason.
- README contains no "24 snapshots", "nine cargo-fuzz", "760 tests", "(26)", "reserved for credentialed", "no command reads credentials yet", "Read; used in milestone 3" next to `check_interval_hours`, "0 checks only when the panel opens", "milestone 2." in the FAQ, "found only as direct children", or `./EraOnly.zip`.
- The hero block and the session block are what the binary prints on the synthetic homes.
- `src/state/config.rs` doc and help strings for `default_target` and `check_interval_hours`, and `tests/catalog.rs:1`, match the code.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: none new. The doc strings carry no behaviour. Run `cargo test --locked --lib state::config` to confirm nothing snapshots them.
- Integration: none new. Regenerate the two README blocks from synthetic homes as in step 2, and diff the README text against that output by eye.
- `grep` checks from the Acceptance Criteria.

## Considerations

- Several other beads also edit README: omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.1 (checkpoint commands), omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2 (lock-hold sentence, Tests table), omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10 (Interrupted runs), omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.3/omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.4 (CLI) and omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.1/omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.13/omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.8 (sources). Keep this bead's diff to the lines in the table so rebases are mechanical.
- The hero block must not carry real paths, hostnames, account names or the owner's real addon set. The synthetic home guarantees that.
- `check_interval_hours = 0`: this bead documents today's behaviour (0 keeps the default). Whether 0 should mean something else belongs to the widget in milestone 3. Do not change the code here.
- If omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.1 lands first, #19's bullet should already be gone. Check before adding it.
- decided: this bead is the one owner of every README code-table row (1, 8, 9 and 21). A parallel draft that covered the same rows was folded in here and not filed; its proposed gate test that parses README's code tables is rejected (D16 lets README-only commits skip the gate, so such a test would fail the next code commit for a docs reason). When omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.1 or another fix adds a warning code, that bead updates the row and the count in the same commit, as the error table already does.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.1`: Checkpoint tests that bail out early report as passed, so a skip reads as a pass
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2`: Speed budgets run in the default gate although tests/perf.rs says every budget lives there
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.3`: The real HTTP transport (src/net/client.rs) is never exercised by the gate
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.1`: Observe Proton process names with a client running and pin them in a regression test
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10`: Lock holders outside the engine and no-op change commands never recover pending journals
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.6`: product.db reader reads an install's uid as its product code
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.3`: Verify Lutris, Heroic and Steam readers against upstream and close cheap gaps
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.3`: Failure envelopes and stderr drop every warning the run raised before it failed
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.4`: A JSON flag spelling that fails to parse gets no stdout envelope
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.1`: WoWInterface and Tukui downloads without a usable MD5 install unverified and silently
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.13`: Catalog families filter dependencies and adoption, though documented to restrict nothing
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.8`: Tukui's patch list waives the own-folder-must-load rule that only release.json may waive
- `omad-khsy`: Doc comments and help strings that contradict the code (M1 audit)
- `omad-ex35`: Human output says 1 folders, and file: refs keep a ./ component
- `omad-93rc`: Running-process discovery hints are implemented and tested but never wired into World
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.3.8`: Tolerant product.db protobuf reader and dosdevices drive mapping
acceptance_criteria: every item in the table below is fixed as decided; README counts that go stale are replaced by dated checkpoint facts or by wording without a count; the hero status block and the session sample are regenerated from a synthetic home; the src/state/config.rs doc and help strings and the tests/catalog.rs module doc match the code; lines owned by omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.1, omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.2, omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.10 and omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.6 are left to those beads; argc gate passes

title: Observe Proton process names with a client running and pin them in a regression test
description:
## Background

Running detection decides what the engine may do while a client runs:
- the `safe` policy refuses removing a loaded folder, and refuses every change on legacy clients;
- SavedVariables are never written while the client runs (D33);
- every mutation reports `reload_required` (README "Running clients", vision §5.5, D30).

Since omad-93rc, discovery also uses it: a running WoW or Battle.net process's `WINEPREFIX` is a discovery route (`src/discover/running.rs:82-115`, `src/app/world.rs:85-89`).

The detector (`src/discover/running.rs:1-12`, `:200-250`) looks at the user's own `/proc/<pid>` entries:
- it reads `comm` and matches it against the known exe names, case-insensitively, with or without `.exe`, and with 15-byte truncation (`COMM_MAX`, `:26-27`);
- only for a match does it read `cmdline` (the exe path; a Windows path is mapped through the prefix's `dosdevices`) and `environ` (only `WINEPREFIX`, `:238-240`).

The premise is unverified:
- Vision §4.8: "Wine sets the Unix process name (`/proc/<pid>/comm`, 15-character limit) to the Windows exe basename (UNVERIFIED under Proton/umu)".
- Vision §8: "Wine process naming under Proton/umu is UNVERIFIED".
- The M1 checkpoint (vision comment 341): "Not verified on real installs: Wine process naming under Proton while the game runs (no client was running during the checkpoint)".
- omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.3.10 comment 233: "no Wine or WoW process was running during this session … Next time a client runs, check `cat /proc/*/comm` for its name (never read environ)".

If Proton gives the game's process a loader name (for example `wine64-preloader`), or keeps the Windows exe path in a form the mapper does not resolve, then `status` reports a running client as idle. The `safe` policy then lets a remove of a loaded addon through. An undo's SavedVariables restore runs while the game is open and is overwritten at logout. And the process discovery route never fires. The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit listed this. The development machine's clients run through umu-launcher and GE-Proton in a Battle.net prefix (vision §4.7). The WoW: Forever stress test opens on 2026-10-19 and is the first chance to observe a running client.

## Technical Approach

All steps are read-only on the real machine. Never signal, stop or attach to a process. Never run a mutating omaddons command. Never write under a client directory or the real omaddons state.

1. **Precondition.** List the user's own processes by `comm` only:
   `for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do [ -O "$p" ] && printf '%s\t%s\n' "${p#/proc/}" "$(cat "$p/comm" 2>/dev/null)"; done`
   If no WoW, Battle.net, wine, proton, umu or pressure-vessel process is running, defer again with `--until +1d` and a transition comment.
2. **Record the shapes.** Do this for each own process whose `comm` or first `cmdline` argument mentions `wow`, `battle.net`, `agent.exe`, `wine`, `proton`, `umu`, `pressure-vessel` or `reaper` (case-insensitive). Number the processes P1, P2, …; never record real pids.
   - `comm` exactly, with its byte length (`wc -c` minus the newline), to check the 15-byte cap.
   - `cmdline` as an argv list. Replace the home directory with `$HOME`, the user name in `C:\users\<name>` with `<user>`, and anything else personal with a placeholder.
   - From `environ`, only the `WINEPREFIX` value, with `$HOME` substituted: `tr '\0' '\n' < "$p/environ" | grep '^WINEPREFIX='`. Record only the presence (yes/no) of `STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH`, `PROTONPATH` and `GAMEID`. Never print or store any other variable, because environ can hold tokens.
   - The `basename` of `readlink /proc/<pid>/exe`, and the chain of parent `comm`s up to the first non-Wine ancestor (via the `ppid` field of `/proc/<pid>/stat`).
   - Whether `/proc/<pid>/ns/pid` and `/proc/<pid>/root` differ from `/proc/self`'s. pressure-vessel may run the game in a container whose paths differ from the host's.
   - Which client was played (its target id), and whether the Battle.net launcher ran alongside.
3. **Run detection, read-only.**
   - Build `cargo build --locked --release` from HEAD.
   - Run `env XDG_STATE_HOME=<tmp>/state XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<tmp>/config XDG_CACHE_HOME=<tmp>/cache target/release/omaddons status --json --offline`.
   - The real `HOME` is needed: discovery scans `$HOME/Games`, and the process route looks only under HOME. The throwaway XDG dirs keep the real registry, records and caches untouched; only the throwaway cache is written.
   - Record `[{id, running}]` for every target.
   - Expected: `running: true` on exactly the played client.
     - `WoWClassic.exe` serves the `classic`, `era` and `anniversary` targets in one prefix. If all three show `true`, the exe path was not resolved and the conservative `PrefixOnly` fallback fired (`src/discover/running.rs` module doc). Record that as a defect of exact attribution.
     - If no target shows `true`, detection failed. Find out which step missed: the `comm` match, the `WINEPREFIX` read (absent, relative, or a `pfx` subdirectory), or the `cmdline` path mapping.
4. **Fix or file.**
   - If the miss is confined to name matching or path mapping in `src/discover/running.rs`, fix it here. ejl.3.10's Considerations already decided the shape of such a fix: "extend the matcher to check `cmdline` for known exe names on processes whose `comm` matches a small list of Wine loader names".
   - Anything larger (for example container path translation) gets its own bug bead with `--deps discovered-from:<this>` and the recorded shapes.
   - Do not change what happens when detection is uncertain. That is omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.5's ("detection fails open"). Hand omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.5 the observed facts in a comment.
5. **Regression test.** Add `observed_proton_shapes_map_to_the_played_client` to `tests/running.rs`.
   - Build a `common::procfs::FakeProc` tree reproducing every recorded shape: the `comm` strings, the argv with paths rebuilt under the synthetic `Prefix`, `WINEPREFIX` in the observed form, and loader and launcher processes as non-matching neighbours.
   - Assert `detect_running_in` reports the played client's target with `RunningEvidence::ExePath`, and nothing else.
   - Assert `running_prefixes` returns the prefix.
   - If a `WoWClassic.exe` client was observed, assert the other two `WoWClassic.exe` targets are not running.
   - The fixture holds no real user name, path, pid or environ value.
6. **Docs.**
   - Add a vision comment (do not edit the body): "§4.8/§8: Wine process naming observed under umu/GE-Proton on <date>: <shapes>".
   - `src/discover/running.rs:4` becomes "observed under Proton/umu, <date>".
   - Remove the README Known-limitations note on process naming (added by omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.5 #19), or never add it if omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.5 has not landed.
   - Add a comment on ejl.3.10's successor trail (this bead's close reason is enough).
   - If the Forever client ran, also add a one-line comment on omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6 saying whether `status -t forever` showed it running.

Rejected:
- Asking the owner to paste `ps` output. An agent can read `/proc` directly, and the owner's process list can hold unrelated personal data.
- Recording `environ` wholesale. It can hold secrets, and only `WINEPREFIX` is ever used (`src/discover/running.rs:11-12`).
- Running `status` against the real XDG state. That is not needed for detection and risks touching the real discovery cache.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The close reason holds the recorded shapes per process (placeholders only), the client played, and the `status` running flags per target.
- Either the flags were exactly right, or a fix landed here with its test, or a bug bead exists with the shapes.
- `tests/running.rs` has the regression test, and it passes.
- The vision comment exists.
- `src/discover/running.rs`'s doc and README's limitation note match what was observed.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Integration: `tests/running.rs::observed_proton_shapes_map_to_the_played_client` (fake `/proc`). The existing tests in that file stay green.
- If the matcher changes: unit tests in `src/discover/running.rs` for the new name forms, plus the recorded-reader test (`environ_and_cmdline_only_for_matches`) extended so the new path still reads `environ` only for matches.
- Discovery: if the `WINEPREFIX` form differs (a `pfx` subdirectory, a trailing slash), add a `tests/discover_scan.rs` case for the process route with that form.

## Considerations

- 2026-10-19 likely runs only the Forever client (`Wow.exe`, `_forever_`) and the Battle.net launcher.
  - Record whatever runs. If no `WoWClassic.exe` client was observed, say so in the close reason. The fixture still covers that exe through the same Wine naming mechanism.
  - The 3.3.5a client runs under its own Wine runner in another prefix, so its shape may differ. Record it too if it runs; otherwise list it as unobserved.
- `comm` reflects `prctl(PR_SET_NAME)`, which Wine may set after startup. Sample it again after the client has run for a minute before concluding.
- Do not run the real-machine test suite (`OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) for this. It mutates clients, and a client that is running makes those tests skip anyway (omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.1).
- The `status` run is read-only for client directories. Discovery never writes there (`tests/discover_*` assert "nothing written").

## Related

- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.3.10`: Live running-client detection from /proc
- `omad-93rc`: Running-process discovery hints are implemented and tested but never wired into World
- `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6`: Confirm omaddons-installed addons load in the real Forever client during the 2026-10-19 stress test
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.5`: Running detection fails open: an unreadable /proc makes every client look not running
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.5`: README and doc comments contradict the code in 22 places after M2
acceptance_criteria: while a WoW client runs under umu/Proton, the comm, cmdline and WINEPREFIX shapes of every WoW and Battle.net process are recorded with no personal data; a read-only `omaddons status --json` (real HOME, throwaway XDG dirs) shows `running: true` on exactly the played client's target, or the mismatch is fixed or filed; tests/running.rs gains a fake-/proc regression test built from the observed shapes; vision §4.8/§8 and README's limitation note are updated by comment and edit; argc gate passes
