title: Confirm omaddons-installed addons load in the real retail, Classic and 3.3.5a clients
description:
## Background

README's first line promises that omaddons "installs only the addons each client will actually load". Design philosophy 1 says: "What decides is the TOC file the client would load from each folder … judged by that client's rules row". Every install is checked against `ClientRules` (`src/toc/loaded.rs`, `src/rules.rs`), and the M1/M2 checkpoints proved installs against those rules on real clients (omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7, criterion 12: "9 real-machine tests"; omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.4 for Classic Era, Anniversary and Mists Classic).

No test has observed a real client *loading* an addon omaddons installed. The rules rows are taken from warcraft.wiki.gg and publishers' archives (vision §4.3). A wrong row would install a folder the client ignores, or skip one it would load, and every test would stay green. omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6 checks Forever during the 2026-10-19 stress test. This bead covers the other five clients on the development machine.

The same evidence also answers two open questions:
- vision §4.4: "`AddOns.txt` … the modern format is UNVERIFIED", and "The 'Load out of date AddOns' checkbox resets each patch; where it is stored is UNVERIFIED";
- vision §8 repeats both.

The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit listed this gap.

Evidence the client writes, which an agent can read afterwards (vision §4.4):
- at logout, `/reload` or quit, every *loaded* addon that declares `## SavedVariables` gets `WTF/Account/<account>/SavedVariables/<Folder>.lua`, and `## SavedVariablesPerCharacter` files go under `<account>/<realm>/<character>/SavedVariables/`;
- each character folder has `AddOns.txt` with each addon's enabled state;
- an addon that never loaded gets no SavedVariables file.

## Technical Approach

decided: this bead is filed deferred, not ready. Steps 0 and 1 install addons into five real clients the owner did not ask to change, so they run only once the owner has planned the play sessions (the undefer), and the bead defers itself again after step 1 until the sessions are done. (omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6 could start ready because the owner had asked for the Forever test.)

**Step 0, read-only survey (agent, before installing).**
- Use the release binary built from HEAD, with the real environment, read-only commands only.
- For each target `retail`, `classic`, `era`, `anniversary` and `wotlk`, run `omaddons list -t <id> --json` and `omaddons list -t <id> --unmanaged --json`. Record which candidate addons below are already present, managed or not.
- Check each client is not running (`omaddons status --json`, `running`).

**Step 1, install the known set (agent).**
- Each set is taken from the M2 catalog × declared-flavor matrix (omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7), so each addon installs there as its publisher declares. Each has SavedVariables. The sets include a multi-TOC addon and a multi-flavor archive with skipped modules:

  | Target | Set (first choice) | Fallbacks |
  |---|---|---|
  | `retail` | Bartender4, OmniCC, DBM | Dominos, Masque |
  | `classic` (Mists) | Bartender4, Questie, DBM | OmniCC, Dominos |
  | `era` | Bartender4, Questie, DBM | OmniCC, Dominos |
  | `anniversary` | Bartender4, Questie, DBM | OmniCC, Dominos |
  | `wotlk` | GroupBulletinBoard (`gbb`) | none: the catalog's only `wrath-legacy` entry |

- Skip an addon that is already present on that client (managed or unmanaged) and take the next fallback. Never `--force` and never `adopt`: the owner's own folders stay as they are.
- Per client:
  1. run `omaddons install <set> -t <id> --dry-run --json`;
  2. then `omaddons install <set> -t <id> --json --actor agent --reason "load check (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.2)"`;
  3. record the transaction id, each item's folders (added/skipped) and each folder's TOC `## SavedVariables` / `## SavedVariablesPerCharacter` lines in a bead comment (take the expected file names from those lines; the file is named after the folder).
- Then defer with the text in the frontmatter, phrased as the session needed: "NEEDS OWNER: log in to one character on each of retail, classic, era, anniversary and wotlk, play a minute, and log out normally".

**Step 2, read the evidence (agent, after the undefer).** Read-only, and never write under `WTF/`. For each client:
- List the file names in `WTF/Account/*/SavedVariables/` and `WTF/Account/*/*/*/SavedVariables/` that match the expected `<Folder>.lua` names, each with its mtime compared with the install's time. Print only those names. Refer to the folders as `<account>`, `<realm>` and `<character>`.
- In each `AddOns.txt`, print only the lines for the installed folders. Record the exact line syntax (for example `Bartender4: enabled`), and whether the file has any header or other structure. That answers the modern-format question; describe the structure, not the owner's other addons.
- "Load out of date AddOns":
  - `grep -E '^SET (checkAddonVersion|lastAddonVersion) ' <client>/WTF/Config.wtf`, and the same in `WTF/Account/*/config-cache.wtf`. Print only those lines.
  - Record where `checkAddonVersion` lives and its value.
  - If it is not in either file, record "not located" and leave the vision note UNVERIFIED. Do not ask anyone to toggle it.
- Run `omaddons status -t <id> --json` and record `folders.invalid` and `attention`.
- If a client has no `WTF/` evidence newer than the install (no session yet), defer again with `--until +3d` and a comment. Do not guess.

**Step 3, results.**
- An installed addon whose declared SavedVariables file was written after the install loaded. Record it per client in the close reason.
- An addon without evidence, while another addon on the same client has it, means the client did not load a folder omaddons judged loadable. File a bug bead (`--deps discovered-from:<this>`) with the client, the addon, its folders' TOC names and lines, and the AddOns.txt line. That reopens the rules row in `src/rules.rs`.
- An addon whose AddOns.txt line says `disabled` is inconclusive. Record it as such.
- Add one vision comment for §4.4/§8: the AddOns.txt format, the out-of-date storage (or "not located"), and "TOC-verified installs load on <clients>".

**Step 4, clean up.**
- When the clients are not running, undo the omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.2 transactions by id, newest first: `omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables keep`. The folders go, and the SavedVariables files the session wrote stay untouched (harmless).
- Check `omaddons history` shows the undos, and the unmanaged and managed sets match step 0.

Rejected:
- Leaving the set installed, as omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6 decided for Forever. There the owner asked to test with that client. Here it would add addons the owner did not choose to five clients.
- Undoing with `--saved-variables auto`. That moves aside SavedVariables the session created, which is more change than this check needs.
- Installing a synthetic probe addon instead of real publishers' builds. That would not test the rules rows against the TOC sets publishers actually ship. omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6 uses a probe for the 3.3.5a runtime questions.
- Asking the owner to report what loaded. The client writes the evidence itself.

No contract change. Results that change a rules row follow D15 (data) in their own bug bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The step 1 comment exists, with tx ids, folders and expected SavedVariables files per client.
- The close reason gives each installed addon's evidence per client, with placeholders only.
- The AddOns.txt format and the out-of-date setting's location (or "not located") are recorded in a vision comment.
- Every addon without evidence has a bug bead.
- The omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.2 transactions are undone with `--saved-variables keep`, and each client's folder sets match step 0.

## Test Plan

- Evidence collection only, with `ls`/`stat`/`grep` reads and read-only omaddons commands. No code change is expected.
- If a rules row turns out wrong, the bug bead carries the fix with `tests/toc_matrix.rs` cases built from the observed TOC set, and fixture tests.

## Considerations

- Account, realm and character folder names are personal. They never appear in a comment, close reason or fixture.
- Addons that declare no SavedVariables leave no file. The Battle.net first choices are expected to declare them. Re-check from the TOCs in step 1, and if one does not, take a fallback. `wotlk` has no fallback: if GroupBulletinBoard declares none, its AddOns.txt line is the only evidence. Record that, together with omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6's probe result, which shows load evidence on that client directly.
- The `era` client runs Classic Era, Hardcore and Season of Discovery from one AddOns folder. One session in any of those modes covers it.
- The Battle.net clients share one prefix but have separate `WTF/` trees. Read each client's own.
- A client patch between install and session can make `client_not_launched_since_patch` or `out_of_date` appear. Record it. A build out of date for the client loads only with the checkbox on, and that is exactly the setting step 2 looks for.
- Forever is excluded here (omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6). The 3.3.5a `/reload` and comma-list questions are omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6's.

## Related

- `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6`: Confirm omaddons-installed addons load in the real Forever client during the 2026-10-19 stress test
- `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.4`: Real-machine smoke tests for the Classic Era, Anniversary and Mists Classic clients
- `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7`: M2 checkpoint verification
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6`: Observe whether 3.3.5a loads new addons and TOC changes on /reload, and reads comma lists
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.5`: Verify the 1.12.1, 2.4.3, 4.3.4 and 5.4.8 legacy rows against real client executables
acceptance_criteria: a small known set is installed through omaddons (--actor agent --reason, -t per client) into retail, classic (Mists), era (Classic Era; SoD and Hardcore share it), anniversary and wotlk (3.3.5a), with tx ids and folders recorded; after the owner's play sessions, each installed addon's load evidence (its SavedVariables file written after the install, its AddOns.txt line) is recorded per client with no personal data; the modern AddOns.txt line format and the storage of "Load out of date AddOns" (or "not located") are recorded; any addon without evidence has a bug bead; the test installs are undone with --saved-variables keep; vision comments record the results

comments.text: NEEDS OWNER: one play session per client (retail, Mists Classic, Classic Era, Anniversary, 3.3.5a), scheduled · only the owner can log in to Battle.net and the local 3.3.5a server · confirms that TOC-verified installs actually load, or reopens the rules rows that are wrong; undefer when the sessions are planned, so the test set is installed only shortly before them

title: Verify Lutris, Heroic and Steam readers against upstream and close cheap gaps
description:
## Background

README "Where discovery looks" (`README.md:356-370`) lists the launcher readers: "Lutris: `games/*.yml` under the native config and data directories (prefix and exe); Heroic: every `winePrefix` in `GamesConfig/*.json`, native and Flatpak; Steam: the `compatdata/*/pfx` Proton prefixes of every library in `libraryfolders.vdf`, native and Flatpak … Bottles …". Known limitations (`README.md:1771`, `:1779`) admit "Lutris only from its native install (no Flatpak reader). Steam's `shortcuts.vdf` is not read" and "several upstream file layouts (product.db, Steam and Bottles Flatpak paths) are marked UNVERIFIED in the code".

The M1 checkpoint recorded "Not verified on real installs: … Lutris, Heroic, Bottles and Flatpak layouts (fixtures only)". The development machine has none of these launchers (native Steam only, no WoW in it), so verification has to be against upstream source. The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit carried this as a research-and-fix task; Bottles is done separately (omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.4) and `product.db` too (omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.6).

Initial research (2026-10-18), to be confirmed and extended by the implementer:

- **Lutris v0.5.22** (latest release, 2026-02-25):
  - `lutris/settings.py:21-33`: `CONFIG_DIR = GLib.get_user_config_dir()/lutris`, but when it does not exist `CONFIG_DIR = DATA_DIR` (`get_user_data_dir()/lutris`, "we're deprecating $HOME/.config/lutris"); `GAME_CONFIG_DIR = CONFIG_DIR/games`. omaddons reads both (`src/discover/launchers/lutris.rs:12-31`): correct.
  - Game YAML keys under `game:`: `exe`, `prefix`, `working_dir` (`lutris/runners/wine.py:260-290`). A relative `exe` resolves against the game's `directory` from `pga.db` (`wine.py:704-717` `game_exe`; `lutris/game.py:84`, `:280`), not against `working_dir`/`prefix` as omaddons does (`lutris.rs:66-95`). Without a SQLite reader, keep omaddons' resolution but document the difference; a relative exe that resolves nowhere is already a diagnostic.
  - Flatpak: Flathub app `net.lutris.Lutris` (Lutris itself spawns `flatpak run net.lutris.Lutris`, `lutris/util/steam/shortcut.py:156-157`); inside the sandbox GLib's config and data dirs are `$HOME/.var/app/net.lutris.Lutris/config` and `…/data`, so game files live at `$HOME/.var/app/net.lutris.Lutris/{config,data}/lutris/games/*.yml`.
- **Heroic v2.22.4** (latest, 2026-10-15), `src/backend/constants/paths.ts:8-38`: `appFolder = <appData>/heroic` (Electron's `appData` is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `$HOME/.config`; inside the Flatpak `com.heroicgameslauncher.hgl`, `$HOME/.var/app/com.heroicgameslauncher.hgl/config`), `gamesConfigPath = appFolder/GamesConfig`, `defaultWinePrefixDir = $HOME/Games/Heroic/Prefixes` (with `default` and `shared`), so default prefixes are grandchildren of `$HOME/Games` and are found today only when a `GamesConfig` file names them. Sideloaded apps (how Battle.net or a private-server client is usually added): an electron-store `sideload_apps/library.json` under `userData` (`src/backend/storeManagers/sideload/electronStores.ts`), with `games[].install.executable` (`src/backend/storeManagers/sideload/library.ts:22-40`). The `winePrefix` key omaddons reads (`src/discover/launchers/heroic.rs:39-60`) is the per-game setting (`src/common/types.ts`, `winePrefix: string`); the app settings in `config.json` also carry `defaultWinePrefix` (kept "only for backwards compatibility") and `sharedWinePrefix` in the same file.
- **Steam** (closed source; follow established readers): Lutris's `lutris/util/steam/config.py:14-25` lists the data dirs `$HOME/.steam/debian-installation`, `$HOME/.steam`, `$HOME/.local/share/{steam,Steam}`, `$HOME/snap/steam/common/.local/share/Steam`, `$HOME/.steam/steam`, `$HOME/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/data/{steam,Steam}`; it reads `config/libraryfolders.vdf` (`:196`). omaddons (`src/discover/launchers/steam.rs:19-30`) lacks the Snap root and the lowercase `steam` spellings, and also tries `$HOME/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/.local/share/Steam` (keep it; harmless). Non-Steam shortcuts: `<steam>/userdata/<steamid32>/config/shortcuts.vdf` (`lutris/util/steam/shortcut.py:19-36`), binary VDF with per-shortcut keys `appid` (int32; the `compatdata/<appid>` folder uses its unsigned value), `AppName`, `Exe` (quoted path), `StartDir` (quoted), `LaunchOptions` (`shortcut.py:150-160`).

## Technical Approach

1. **Pin and cite.** For each reader, re-check the facts above at the pinned tags (Lutris `v0.5.22`, Heroic `v2.22.4`; for Steam, Lutris `v0.5.22`'s `lutris/util/steam/` plus one more independent reader of `shortcuts.vdf`, e.g. a well-known shortcut manager's parser, cited by repository, path and commit). Put file, tag and keys in each module doc (`src/discover/launchers/{lutris,heroic,steam}.rs`) and remove "unverified" (`steam.rs:10`).
2. **Lutris Flatpak** (`lutris.rs:12-31`): also read `$HOME/.var/app/net.lutris.Lutris/config/lutris/games` and `…/data/lutris/games`, with `flatpak: true` (the reader currently hard-codes `false`).
3. **Heroic** (`heroic.rs:11-37`): per install (native and Flatpak), also read `sideload_apps/library.json` and keep each `games[].install.executable` as an exe hint when it is a WoW client or launcher (reuse Lutris's `client_exe` test, `lutris.rs:62-80`, moved to `launchers/mod.rs`); add `$HOME/Games/Heroic/Prefixes/*` children that are prefixes as Heroic prefixes (cheap, bounded), and the `defaultWinePrefix`/`sharedWinePrefix` values of `config.json` when present.
4. **Steam** (`steam.rs:19-60`): add the Snap root and the lowercase Flatpak and native `steam` spellings (de-duplicated by canonical path, as now). Add a small tolerant binary-VDF reader for `userdata/*/config/shortcuts.vdf` (types 0x00 map, 0x01 string, 0x02 int32, 0x08 end; bounded by `src/limits.rs` sizes; never panics), yielding each shortcut's `Exe` (unquoted) and `StartDir`; a WoW exe becomes an exe hint (`launcher: steam`), and its `compatdata/<appid>/pfx` is already among the prefixes. New fuzz target `steam_shortcuts` with seeds generated by `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs`.
5. **Fixtures** (`tests/common/launchers.rs`): builders for the new files (Flatpak Lutris games, Heroic `library.json` and the default prefix dir, Snap Steam root, `shortcuts.vdf` writer producing the binary layout); `tests/discover_launchers.rs` scenarios for each, native and Flatpak where applicable; `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs` seed lists.
6. **README:** discovery list (`README.md:362-367`) gains "Flatpak" for Lutris, Heroic sideloaded apps and default prefixes, Steam's Snap install and non-Steam shortcuts; Known limitations `:1771` keeps only "Discovery reads only the direct children of `$HOME/Games` as prefixes" (plus what remains), and `:1779` drops Steam. Record the verification and sources on omad-vision-8qa (§5.2 step 1b).

Rejected: a SQLite dependency to read Lutris's `pga.db` (new crate for an edge case; relative exes are rare and already diagnosed); a general YAML/VDF crate (vision §5.2: small tolerant readers only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the three readers cites its upstream files and pinned versions in the module doc; no "unverified" remains in `src/discover/launchers/` except where a fact could not be confirmed (then say exactly which).
- Flatpak Lutris games, Heroic sideloaded WoW exes and default prefixes, Snap Steam libraries and `shortcuts.vdf` WoW exes are found, with the right `found_by: launcher:<name>`.
- The `steam_shortcuts` fuzz target runs 10 minutes without a crash.
- README lists exactly what is read; the vision comment is recorded.
- `argc gate` passes (and `argc gate --all` if a crate is added: none is planned).

## Test Plan

- Unit: each reader's parsing helpers (new binary VDF reader: maps, nesting, truncation, wrong types, huge lengths).
- Integration: `tests/discover_launchers.rs` (new scenarios), `tests/discover_matrix.rs` unchanged, `tests/common_selftest.rs` for the new builders.

title: Check a real Turtle WoW Wow.exe stamp and lastAddonVersion against the custom-client rule
description:
## Background

Vision §4.2 ("1.12.1, e.g. Turtle WoW … Its exe version is UNVERIFIED") and §8 ("Unverified client details: … Turtle WoW's exe version") leave one fact that only a real file can settle. README's FAQ promises "Turtle WoW is a `vanilla-legacy` client" (`README.md:1880`).

omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5 (filed from the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit) makes that promise hold for every plausible stamp: custom clients reporting 1.16–1.49 map to `vanilla-legacy` with a pinned interface of 11200, and a 1.12.1 stamp keeps the existing rule. Its evidence is indirect: open-source clients and restoration projects describe Turtle's client as 1.18.1 build 7272 (auth build) on world build 5875, and the client's own UI addons declare `## Interface: 11200`. What the `Wow.exe` PE resource actually says (`src/discover/pe.rs` reads `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` file version, then product version) and what the client writes to `WTF/Config.wtf` (`SET lastAddonVersion "…"`, which overrides the interface on legacy rows, `src/discover/custom.rs:87-92`) have not been seen.

## Technical Approach

When the file is available (no code needed to read it):

1. Copy the client's `Wow.exe` and `WTF/Config.wtf` (only these two files, plus an empty `Interface/` folder) into a scratch directory, never touching the real install.
2. Run omaddons in an isolated environment with that directory as an extra root:
   `env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=<scratch>/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<scratch>/home/.config XDG_STATE_HOME=<scratch>/home/.local/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=<scratch>/home/.cache OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<scratch>/proc target/debug/omaddons targets add <scratch>/turtle --name turtle --json`, then `targets -v --json`: record `version`, `family`, `interface`, `details.rules`.
3. Record the file and product versions separately (a PE tool such as `pelite`'s example or any resource viewer), and the `lastAddonVersion` value. Nothing else from the files (no realm, account or path).
4. Compare with omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5's rule:
   - stamp within 1.16–1.49 and interface 11200: close with the values; comment on omad-vision-8qa that §4.2/§8's Turtle note is verified;
   - stamp 1.12.x: close the same way (omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5's rule is unused but harmless);
   - anything else (e.g. a 2.x stamp, or an interface other than 11200): file a follow-up bead with `--deps discovered-from:omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.4` to adjust the version rule or pin, with the values.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Values recorded in the close comment and on the vision bead.
- The isolated run shows `vanilla-legacy`, interface 11200 (or a follow-up bead exists).
- No real path, realm or account data in any bead.

## Test Plan

- None in the gate; the isolated run above is the check. If a follow-up changes the rule, it carries the unit and integration tests.

## Considerations

- Run nothing against the real install; the copy is enough because discovery reads only the exe, `Config.wtf` and `realmlist.wtf`.
- If the owner no longer has a Turtle WoW client, close this bead as not obtainable with that reason; omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5's rule stays, with its indirect evidence documented.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.3`: A family override on a client with no readable version picks the fallback rules
acceptance_criteria: the VS_FIXEDFILEINFO file and product versions of a real Turtle WoW Wow.exe (1.17.x or 1.18.x) and its WTF/Config.wtf lastAddonVersion are recorded (values only, no paths or account data) in this bead's close comment and on omad-vision-8qa; if they fall outside omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.5's 1.16–1.49 rule or the interface is not 11200, a follow-up bead adjusts the rule; omaddons discovers that client as vanilla-legacy with interface 11200 in an isolated environment; argc gate passes if code changes

title: Verify the 1.12.1, 2.4.3, 4.3.4 and 5.4.8 legacy rows against real client executables
description:
## Background

README promises omaddons "identifies private-server clients 1.12.1 to 5.4.8 from their executable's version resource" (Why use omaddons?, and the Private-server clients table at README:404-414). Detection is data (vision §4.2, D15):
- `src/discover/custom.rs:37-50` picks the exe: `wow.exe`, then `wow-64.exe` ("5.4.8 ships both"), then any other `wow*.exe`;
- `src/discover/pe.rs:1-31` reads `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO`, file version first and product version only when the file version is all zeros;
- `src/rules.rs:1024-1038` (`VERSION_FAMILIES`) maps a custom client's major.minor to a legacy family;
- `src/rules.rs:1059-1074` (`FAMILIES`) gives each family its interface range and default id;
- `src/rules.rs:1274-1302` holds the legacy rules rows (plain TOC only, leading Interface number, `version_min` 1.12.0, 2.4.0, 3.3.0, 4.3.0 and 5.4.0);
- `lastAddonVersion` from `WTF/Config.wtf` overrides the computed interface (`src/discover/config_wtf.rs:2-12`, README:435).

Only 3.3.5a has been checked against a real client. The development machine's `Wow.exe` reports file version 3.3.5.12340 and product version 3.3.0.0 (`src/discover/pe.rs:2-5`, `tests/common/pe.rs:27-31`), and the M1 checkpoint saw `wrath-legacy`, interface 30300, label "localhost". The other four generations exist only as synthetic PE stubs whose file and product versions are equal: `tests/common/trees.rs:50-56` `LEGACY_VERSIONS` = 1.12.1.5875, 2.4.3.8606, 4.3.4.15595 and 5.4.8.18414, built by `pe_stub`. If a real executable carries different numbers, for example a zero file version, a product version of 1.12.0.0, a repacked exe with its resource stripped, or a 5.4.8 pack where only `Wow-64.exe` has a version, the client gets family `unknown`. That family accepts only builds for its exact major.minor. It could also get the wrong family. Either way the user sees refusals or wrong-generation installs. Vision §8 also lists "Turtle WoW's exe version" as unverified. The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit listed this gap.

Agents must not download Blizzard client binaries, so the four installs can only come from the owner.

## Technical Approach

When the owner has placed the clients and said where (in the undefer comment), do the following for each client, read-only. Never write in the client directory, and refer to it as `<client>` in every record.

1. **Executables.**
   - List `wow*.exe` names in `<client>` (names only).
   - Read both version pairs of each exe with a read-only PE reader, for example `uvx --with pefile python3 -I <script outside the repo>` printing `FileVersionMS/LS` and `ProductVersionMS/LS`.
   - Record them as `file a.b.c.d, product a.b.c.d`. No hashes and no copies of the binaries.
2. **Client facts.**
   - `grep -E '^SET lastAddonVersion' <client>/WTF/Config.wtf`. Print only this line, because Config.wtf holds account names.
   - The `## Interface:` lines of the client's own `Interface/AddOns/Blizzard_*/*.toc`, if any are on disk.
   - Whether `Data/<locale>/realmlist.wtf` exists, and the label omaddons derives from it. Not the server address itself, unless it is loopback.
   - If the 1.12.1 client is Turtle WoW, say so and record its versions too (vision §8).
3. **Discovery, read-only, in a throwaway environment.**
   - `env -i PATH=… HOME=<tmp>/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<tmp>/config XDG_STATE_HOME=<tmp>/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=<tmp>/cache OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 target/release/omaddons status --json`.
   - `<tmp>/config/omaddons/config.toml` holds `extra_roots = ["<client root>"]`.
   - Record `family`, `interface`, `version`, `label`, `id` and `exe_name` (`-v`), and any warning (`unknown_flavor`, `client_not_launched_since_patch`).
   - Expected: `vanilla-legacy` 11200, `tbc-legacy` 20400, `cata-legacy` 40300 and `mists-legacy` 50400, unless `lastAddonVersion` says otherwise. Default ids `vanilla`, `tbc`, `cata` and `mists`.
4. **Compare and correct.**
   - If a client lands in the wrong family, or in `unknown`, decide from the observed numbers:
     - widen a `VERSION_FAMILIES` row (`src/rules.rs:1024-1038`);
     - change which version `pe.rs` prefers (only if a real exe proves the file version wrong; 3.3.5a must keep working);
     - change the exe order in `custom.rs`.
   - These tables are data (D15), so no contract change. Record any change in a vision comment, and update README:406-412 and 428-432 if a documented number changes.
5. **Regression fixtures.**
   - Replace `LEGACY_VERSIONS` in `tests/common/trees.rs:50-56` with a table of observed `(file, product)` pairs per generation. Use `pe_stub_with(file, product)`, as 3.3.5a already does.
   - Have `tests/discover_matrix.rs` and `tests/discover_custom.rs` assert each observed pair yields its family and interface.
   - For 5.4.8, add the observed exe set (for example both `Wow.exe` and `Wow-64.exe`) to the tree builder.
   - Only version numbers and file names enter the repository.
6. **Record.**
   - Add a vision comment: §4.2 legacy rows verified for <generations> on <date>, each with its versions.
   - Write a close reason listing every observation.
   - Any generation the owner could not supply stays unverified. Say which in the close reason. Do not guess.

Rejected:
- Downloading client binaries or repacks. That is forbidden for agents, and the provenance of a download proves nothing about the owner's clients.
- Committing the exes or their hashes. They are Blizzard binaries, and their hashes identify specific repacks.
- Running discovery against the real HOME. A throwaway HOME with `extra_roots` reaches exactly the client and nothing else.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each supplied client has its observations recorded, with placeholders only.
- Discovery output per client matches the expected family, interface and id, or a rules or code fix landed with its test.
- `tests/common/trees.rs` uses the observed version pairs, and the discovery suites assert them.
- The vision comment exists.
- README's legacy table still matches.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Integration: `tests/discover_matrix.rs` (the legacy rows through the binary) and `tests/discover_custom.rs` (one test per observed generation, built with `pe_stub_with`).
- `tests/toc_matrix.rs` stays as is unless a rules row changes. In that case add the changed row's cases.
- Unit: `src/discover/pe.rs` tests gain a case for any version layout the real exes show (for example file version zero and product version set).

## Considerations

- Interface numbers: legacy rows have `interface_includes_patch: false`, so 1.12.1 computes 11200. If `lastAddonVersion` shows 11201 or the like, that is still inside `vanilla-legacy`'s 11200–11299 range. Record it; no change is needed.
- Two installs of one generation (for example two 3.3.5a servers) are covered by the existing collision ids (`wotlk`, `wotlk@b`). No need to verify that here.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6 covers the running-client behaviour of legacy clients (3.3.5a). This bead is about detection only.

## Related

- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.3.6`: Discovery test matrix over synthetic trees (M1 checkpoint 2)
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.4.4`: TOC load-rule test matrix (M1 checkpoint 3)
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6`: Observe whether 3.3.5a loads new addons and TOC changes on /reload, and reads comma lists
acceptance_criteria: for each of the four legacy clients the owner supplies, the exe names present, both VS_FIXEDFILEINFO versions, lastAddonVersion and the Blizzard TOC Interface lines are recorded with no personal data; read-only discovery in a throwaway HOME (extra_roots pointing at the client) reports the expected family, interface and version, or the src/rules.rs row is corrected; tests/common/trees.rs and the discovery tests use the observed (file, product) version pairs; a vision comment records the result; argc gate passes

title: Observe whether 3.3.5a loads new addons and TOC changes on /reload, and reads comma lists
description:
## Background

The `safe` running policy refuses *every* change on a legacy client while it runs (README "Running clients": "On legacy and unrecognized custom clients, every change is refused"). Code: `src/engine/running.rs:134` (`(RunningPolicy::Safe, false) if rules.legacy => …, "legacy_client"`), with the message "this client needs a restart to pick up any addon change" (`:143`) and `ReloadRequired::Restart` (`:172`). That rests on an unverified premise:
- vision §4.4: "3.3.5a, and legacy clients generally, likely need a full restart for new addons or TOC changes (UNVERIFIED)";
- vision §4.2;
- `src/engine/running.rs:5-7`: "legacy clients (UNVERIFIED) need one for anything".

If 3.3.5a in fact picks up a new addon on `/reload`, the policy refuses changes a player could safely make. If it does not, the restart message is right and only the UNVERIFIED notes go.

The comma-list rule is also unverified. The legacy rules rows have `comma_interface: false` (`src/rules.rs:1134`), so omaddons reads only the leading integer and warns `toc_comma_on_legacy` (`src/toc/loaded.rs:249-258`, `:388-396`). `src/toc.rs:43` says so: "The leading digits, which a client without comma lists reads (unverified)". Vision §8 lists "how legacy clients handle comma Interface lists" as unverified. If the client instead treats `30300, 30400` as unreadable, an addon omaddons installs with a warning would never load.

The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit listed both. Only the owner can run a logged-in 3.3.5a session: the development machine's client talks to a local AzerothCore server that needs the owner's login (vision §4.7).

## Technical Approach

**Probes.** Write three local addons in a scratch directory outside the repository. They carry no personal data, and their SavedVariables hold only timestamps and API results.
- `OmaddonsProbe/OmaddonsProbe.toc`:
  ```
  ## Interface: 30300
  ## Title: omaddons probe
  ## SavedVariables: OmaddonsProbeDB
  a.lua
  ```
  `a.lua`: on `ADDON_LOADED` for `OmaddonsProbe`:
  - append `time()` to `OmaddonsProbeDB.loads`;
  - set `OmaddonsProbeDB.check = GetCVar("checkAddonVersion")`;
  - set `OmaddonsProbeDB.comma = {GetAddOnInfo("OmaddonsProbeComma")}` (name, title, notes, enabled, loadable, reason).
- Version 2 of the same folder adds `b.lua` to the TOC. `b.lua` sets `OmaddonsProbeDB.b = time()`. This is the TOC change.
- `OmaddonsProbeComma/OmaddonsProbeComma.toc`, with `## Interface: 30300, 30400` and `## SavedVariables: OmaddonsProbeCommaDB`. Its Lua sets `OmaddonsProbeCommaDB = {loaded = time()}`.

**Run** (agent; read-only except the omaddons transactions):
1. When picked up, wait for the 3.3.5a client. Poll the user's own `/proc/*/comm` every 30 s for up to 4 h for the `wotlk` target's process (`omaddons status -t wotlk --json` → `running: true`). If it does not appear, defer again with `--until +1d`.
2. Record the client process's start time as wall-clock T0 (field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat` plus `btime` from `/proc/stat`), and keep its pid in a local variable, not in the record.
3. Run `omaddons install ./OmaddonsProbe ./OmaddonsProbeComma -t wotlk --while-running --actor agent --reason "legacy reload check (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6)" --json`. Record tx1, the time T1, and the `toc_comma_on_legacy` warning (expected).
4. Watch `<client>/WTF/Account/*/SavedVariables/OmaddonsProbe.lua` (mtime only) every 30 s while the same pid lives. SavedVariables are written on `/reload`, logout and quit (vision §4.4).
5. After the first write, re-install `./OmaddonsProbe` at version 2 (`b.lua` added to the TOC) the same way. Record tx2 and T2.
6. When the client has exited (or after the third write), read the two probe SavedVariables files and record:
   - the `loads` timestamps;
   - `b`;
   - `check`;
   - the `comma` tuple;
   - `OmaddonsProbeCommaDB.loaded`.
   Refer to the account folder as `<account>`.

**Interpretation:**
- A `loads` entry with T1 < t, written while the process started at T0 was still alive (t before its exit), means **new addons are picked up without a restart** (on `/reload` or relog).
- No such entry, with three reloads done, means **a new addon needs a restart**, as the policy assumes.
- `b` set with T2 < b means **TOC changes are picked up on `/reload`**. `b` absent means they need a restart.
- `OmaddonsProbeCommaDB.loaded` set, and `comma.reason` nil, means the client reads the leading integer (omaddons' rule confirmed).
  - Not loaded, with `comma.reason` `INTERFACE_VERSION` (or similar), means the client rejects comma lists. `toc_comma_on_legacy` should then be a refusal (`wrong_flavor`), not a warning. File that change as a bug bead: it is a contract change, so use DEC-4 with a vision comment and update README's warning table.
  - If `check` is `"0"` (out-of-date addons load anyway), the comma result is inconclusive. Record that, and do not change any CVar.

**Follow-up and docs:**
- If new addons and TOC changes both load on `/reload`, file a task bead (`--deps discovered-from:<this>`): "Allow adds and TOC-preserving replacements on running 3.3.5a under `safe`, with `reload_required: reload`". It changes `src/engine/running.rs:134` for the `wrath-legacy` row only, or for all legacy rows only if omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.5/omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.2 show the same. It is a behaviour change, so README "Running clients" and FAQ "Is it safe to use while WoW is running?" must change and a vision comment is needed (DEC-4, before the M4 freeze).
  - Do not make that change in this bead.
- Update `src/engine/running.rs:5-7` and `src/toc.rs:43` to say what was observed, with the date (doc-only, so the gate runs).
- Add one vision comment for §4.2/§4.4/§8.

**Clean up:** after the client exits, undo tx2 then tx1 by id with `--saved-variables keep`. The probe folders go; their SavedVariables files stay (harmless). Confirm `omaddons list -t wotlk --unmanaged` matches what it showed before.

Rejected:
- Asking the owner to report what the AddOns screen shows. The probes record it themselves, with timestamps that tell restart from reload.
- Reading AddOns.txt for this. It shows the addon list, not whether the running process loaded a file.
- Changing the policy before observing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The close reason gives T0, T1 and T2 as times only, the probe SavedVariables values, and each conclusion: new addon on `/reload` yes/no, TOC change yes/no, comma list read as leading integer / rejected / inconclusive.
- The doc comments in `src/engine/running.rs` and `src/toc.rs` match.
- The vision comment exists.
- The follow-up bead exists when warranted.
- The probes are undone.
- argc gate passes for the doc edits.

## Test Plan

- Evidence collection only. A doc-only code change runs the gate.
- If the comma rule or the policy changes in a follow-up bead, that bead adds `tests/toc_matrix.rs` legacy comma cases and `src/engine/running.rs` table rows (`:265-322`) for the new verdicts.

## Considerations

- `--while-running` is needed because `safe` refuses every legacy change while the client runs. That is the very behaviour under test. SavedVariables are never written by omaddons while the client runs (D33), whatever the flags.
- `time()` is wall-clock in the client's Lua. Wine maps it to the host clock, so it compares directly with T0, T1 and T2 taken from the host.
- The probe must not print in game or touch other addons. It only writes its own SavedVariables.
- If the owner's session has no `/reload` at all, the "new addon" question stays open. Defer again with the same NEEDS OWNER text, rather than concluding "needs restart".
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.5 covers the other legacy generations' detection. Their runtime behaviour is not verified here; record that the result applies to 3.3.5a only.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.2`: Confirm omaddons-installed addons load in the real retail, Classic and 3.3.5a clients
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.5`: Verify the 1.12.1, 2.4.3, 4.3.4 and 5.4.8 legacy rows against real client executables
- `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.6.9`: Running policy and reload_required
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.5`: README and doc comments contradict the code in 22 places after M2
acceptance_criteria: during one running, logged-in 3.3.5a session, probe addons installed through omaddons (--while-running, --actor agent) show from their own SavedVariables whether a new addon and a TOC change load without a client restart, and how the client judges `## Interface: 30300, 30400`; the results and the client's checkAddonVersion are recorded with no personal data; the comment in src/engine/running.rs and src/toc.rs's "(unverified)" note match the observation; a follow-up bead exists if the legacy running policy can be relaxed; the probes are undone afterwards; argc gate passes for any code or doc change

comments.author: GlowingOrchid
comments.text: NEEDS OWNER: a running, logged-in 3.3.5a session on the local server, with /reload typed three times at least five minutes apart · requires the owner's local-server login · may relax the legacy running policy and confirm the comma-list rule

title: Measure keyless coverage of the most popular addons per family; propose catalog entries
description:
## Background

Vision §8 lists a risk: "Keyless coverage of the long tail (e.g. Details! is not on GitHub releases). WoWI, URL/zip installs and optional CF cover the gap."
- README promises "No account, token or API key is needed for anything that works today".
- Its "Use something else when" section tells CurseForge-only users to look elsewhere.
- The catalog holds 21 entries (README "The built-in catalog").

Nobody has measured how much of what players actually use is reachable keylessly. That number decides two things: whether the catalog should grow, and how much M5's opt-in CurseForge support matters. The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit listed this as an unmeasured risk. This is a research task. Nothing in it is code unless a proposal is accepted, and accepted proposals become their own beads.

What omaddons supports keylessly today (README "Sources and refs"):
- catalog names;
- `gh:` releases: the stable path via `release.json` with no REST, or zip assets via the REST fallback, 60 requests an hour without a token;
- `git:` on GitHub, keyless via the commits feed and codeload;
- `wowi:` (WoWInterface, MD5-checked);
- `tukui:` (ElvUI, Tukui);
- `url:` on allowlisted hosts.

`omaddons search` already queries the catalog, the WoWInterface index, the Tukui list and GitHub's repository search, with a per-client hint.

## Technical Approach

Everything runs in a throwaway environment: `env -i PATH=… HOME=<tmp>/home XDG_*=<tmp>/… target/release/omaddons …`. Use the release binary built from HEAD and the real network, but never the real HOME or state. Its `net.log` is the request record.

1. **Popularity lists, dated.**
   - WoWInterface: run `omaddons search details --source wowi` once. That fetches the keyless file list into `<tmp>/cache/omaddons/wowi/index.json` (one `wowi-filelist` request, as README describes). Take the top 100 entries by `downloads` (`src/sources/wowi/index.rs:43`, from `UIDownloadTotal`). Libraries count, because they are dependency targets.
   - CurseForge-only: read one public, non-API popularity listing of WoW addons by total downloads. The curseforge.com website's own listing qualifies if its terms allow reading it; otherwise use another public list and name it. Take the top 50 names that the WoWInterface top list does not already contain. Never call `api.curseforge.com`, never use a key, and record only names, slugs and the linked source repository if the page shows one.
2. **Sources per addon.** For each name, check in this order:
   - the catalog (`omaddons search <name> --source catalog --offline`);
   - Tukui (`--source tukui`);
   - WoWInterface (the index from step 1);
   - GitHub, from the project's own links (a TOC `X-Website`, or the listing's source link) or `omaddons search <name> --source github`.
     - Search is limited to one request per run, 10 a minute without a token; pace the runs.
     - For a GitHub repository, note whether its latest release has `release.json` (keyless stable path) or only zip assets (REST fallback).
   - Record the first source that works and every other source found.
3. **Outcome per family.**
   - Build one synthetic client per live family in the throwaway HOME: `mainline`, `mists`, `vanilla`, `tbc` and `forever`. Use the Battle.net root layout of `tests/common/trees.rs`, the same way `live_probes::catalog_matches_declared_flavors` does. `wrath-legacy` gets a custom client (PE stub, `pe_stub_with`).
   - For each addon's best ref, run `omaddons install <ref> -t <id> --dry-run --json` on each client. Batch several refs per command, because each ref is fetched once per command.
   - Record `installed`, `no_compatible_release` (with `error.details.tried` reasons summarized), or another error code.
   - Dry runs download archives to verify them. The throwaway blob cache keeps each download to one per run.
4. **Politeness.**
   - Stay within omaddons' own limits (6 concurrent, 3 per host, `Retry-After` honoured).
   - Spread GitHub REST use so the 60-an-hour budget is never exhausted. A `rate_limited` answer means wait for `details.reset_at`, not retry.
   - Keep the whole study under about 1,000 requests (count them from `net.log`) and record the total.
5. **Report.** Write it in the close reason, or a comment the close reason links. It is dated and has no personal data.
   - A table: addon × family → source and outcome.
   - Coverage per family: the share of the WoWInterface top 100 and of the CurseForge-only top 50 that install keylessly.
   - The addons with no keyless source at all (CurseForge- or Wago-only), and whether each one's page links a source repository.
   - The request count from `net.log`.
6. **Proposals.**
   - Propose catalog entries for the popular addons whose verified keyless source installs on at least one family and whose name lookups would otherwise be ambiguous or miss.
   - Group them as one follow-up bead per batch of at most 10 (`--deps discovered-from:<this>`).
   - Each follow-up must verify every entry by README "The built-in catalog" rules:
     - against its publisher's `releases/latest` tag, `release.json` and the addon roots inside the zip (GitHub);
     - against the API's list and the zip's folders and TOCs (Tukui);
     - against the TOC's `## Interface` (legacy);
     - plus the live catalog × declared-flavor probe (omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.7).
   - Do not edit `catalog/catalog.toml` in this bead.

Rejected:
- Using the CurseForge API with a personal key. D4 and README say CurseForge is opt-in and arrives in M5, and keys are non-transferable.
- Measuring against the owner's installed addons. That is not public, and it is a sample of one.
- Counting a source as covered without a dry run. Metadata alone is exactly what omaddons refuses to trust (Design philosophy 1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The report exists with the dated lists, the per-addon sources and outcomes, coverage per family, the keyless gaps and the request count.
- Each proposal is a follow-up bead with its verification checklist.
- `net.log` in the throwaway state shows no `api.curseforge.com` request.
- Nothing was written outside the throwaway directories.

## Test Plan

- Research only. No code or test changes in this bead.
- Each follow-up catalog bead carries its own tests: `tests/catalog.rs` gains fixture-backed entries recorded with `OMADDONS_RECORD=1 cargo test --test catalog -- --ignored record`, and the live probe runs at the next checkpoint.

## Considerations

- Popularity lists drift. Date every list, and do not hard-code the result anywhere but the report.
- WoWInterface's compatibility tags lag behind patches, so judge by the dry-run outcome only (README `wowi:` row).
- Some top addons are libraries or Tukui and ElvUI plugins. Report them, but propose catalog entries only for addons a player would install by name.
- Details!, the vision's example, should be one of the first rows. Its outcome on each family answers §8's example directly.
- This feeds M5 planning (CurseForge, Wago). Do not plan M5 here: report the gap and stop.

## Related

- `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7`: M2 checkpoint verification
- `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.7`: Live probe: every catalog addon installs on every client its publisher declares, and only there
acceptance_criteria: a dated report (in the close reason, or a comment linked from it) covers the top 100 WoWInterface addons by downloads and the top 50 CurseForge-only addons from a public non-API popularity list; for each it names the keyless source omaddons supports today (catalog, GitHub release.json, GitHub zip assets, WoWInterface, Tukui, or none) and the dry-run outcome on one synthetic client per live family; it gives coverage per family; catalog additions are proposed as follow-up beads that follow README "The built-in catalog" verification rules; no CurseForge API is used and no real home is touched

title: Epic: M2 — Updates, dependencies, adoption, desired state
description:
## Background

M2 is the second milestone of omaddons (vision bead `omad-vision-8qa`, §7 M2, as amended by the comments added after body revision 2). It was planned on 2026-10-15 against `main` at `e902d36` and decomposed into these beads the same day.

**M1 made omaddons correct.** It finds every WoW client on the machine with no configuration. It verifies every archive against the client's own TOC load rules before writing anything. Every change runs through a journaled, crash-safe, undoable transaction engine behind a strict machine-readable CLI. It works today on the owner's machine against six real clients: retail, Classic Era, Mists Classic, Anniversary, the Forever stress-test client, and a 3.3.5a private-server client.

**M1 did not make omaddons useful day to day:**
- The only way to update is to re-run `install` addon by addon, and nothing says which addons are out of date.
- An addon that needs another addon installs alone and silently fails to load in game.
- Addons already installed by another manager, or by hand, can only be destroyed with `--force`.
- The addon set lives only in state files, so it cannot be described once and reproduced on another machine or after a reinstall.
- Two of the largest keyless ecosystems are missing: WoWInterface (about 8,200 projects) and Tukui (ElvUI).

**When M2 lands:**
1. **`omaddons outdated` and `omaddons update`** keep every client current. Each distinct ref is fetched once per run across all targets. Unchanged GitHub releases cost one request with no REST budget, and a repeat check inside 15 minutes costs nothing. Each distinct archive is downloaded once per run however many clients take it. One `omaddons undo` reverts everything a multi-client update did. `pin`/`unpin` and per-addon channels give control. `status` shows pending update counts offline in under 5 ms, so the M3 widget can paint a badge without touching the network.
2. **Dependencies resolve.** `omaddons install littlewigs` also installs BigWigs in the same transaction, recorded as a dependency of LittleWigs, and undo reverts both together. Optional dependencies are never auto-installed. Removing something another addon needs warns, and dependencies nobody needs any more are reported as orphans.
3. **WoWInterface and Tukui are sources.** `wowi:` refs and pasted WoWInterface links install with MD5 verification. `elvui` installs from Tukui onto every client its TOC supports. Release notes come from GitHub's Atom feed, WoWI's changelog and Tukui's changelog endpoint, so `info --changelog` costs no REST budget.
4. **Existing installs are adopted.** `omaddons adopt` classifies every unmanaged folder: `exact` (byte-identical to the newest release), `identified` (source known from the catalog, TOC ids or WoWInterface, chosen exactly as `install` would choose it, version from the TOC), or `guess`. `adopt --apply` brings the confident ones under management in one undoable transaction per client that writes records only and never touches a folder.
5. **Drift is visible.** `status` compares every managed file to the index written at install, stat-first, re-hashing only what changed. A 5,000-file check stays under 30 ms. Locally modified files are named, and `install <addon> --reinstall` repairs them, from the blob cache with no network when it can.
6. **The addon set becomes a file.** `omaddons export` writes `addons.toml` (per-family and per-target sections). `omaddons sync` makes every client match it, idempotently, with zero network on a no-op re-run. `--locked` reproduces exact versions and `--prune` removes what is no longer listed. `omaddons copy --from era --to anniversary` carries a set across clients where it is compatible.
7. **`omaddons search`** finds addons across the catalog, the local WoWInterface index, Tukui and GitHub, ranked, with per-client compatibility hints and a ready-to-run install command.

None of this weakens an M1 guarantee. Every new mutation (update, adopt, pin, sync, dependency installs, reinstall) runs through the same transaction engine and is undoable. Every new write goes through fsx, every new network request is allowlisted and logged, and every new error carries an executable fix.

**Why this is the right M2.** Each feature removes a manual chore the owner has today. `update`, the most valuable one, comes first, so it lands before WoW: Forever launches on 2026-11-04 and publishers start shipping frequent Forever builds. Adoption and `sync` make omaddons the *sole* authority over the clients, which is the thesis of the whole project. Dependencies and drift close correctness holes that M1's TOC verification cannot see. The engine work M2 needs is also exactly what M3's widget ("Update all", "Undo last") and M4's doctor ("repair" transactions) build on: records-only transactions, multi-addon transactions with dependencies, and multi-target commits. Doing it now removes risk from both later milestones.

**What changes in the vision.** Investigation found four facts the vision bead got wrong or could not know. Each is a recorded decision (decision log comments on this epic):
- Current BugSack declares `!BugGrabber` as an *optional* dependency, and `!BugGrabber` has no official GitHub release. The dependency checkpoint therefore uses LittleWigs → BigWigs, a real required dependency between two catalog addons (M2-D10).
- WoWInterface sends no `ETag` or `Last-Modified`, so conditional requests are impossible and caching relies on `max-age` (M2-D12). Its compatibility tags lag the game by patches, so they never exclude a build; the TOCs decide (M2-D11).
- Tukui download URLs are tokens that expire within seconds, so they are resolved at download time and never stored (M2-D13).
- GitHub's GraphQL batch path needs POST support, body-keyed fixtures and a new decoder, for a small gain once the tag-first probe exists. It moves to M5 with the other account features. `auth github` (the opt-in REST token) stays in M2 (M2-D22).

**Structure.** Eight area epics and 61 leaf beads. The plan sized five tasks as L; each became a small epic whose children are the work (A4, C4, E4, E5, F3).

| Area | Epic id | What it delivers |
|---|---|---|
| A | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1` | Engine and contract foundation: grouped help, multi-target selection, carry-over rules, records-only work and the `pin` kind (A4 epic), the working view and folder handover, the multi-target outcome, MD5, deferred assets and download de-duplication, progress, test helpers, run ids and run-level undo |
| B | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2` | Update checks and updates: the release memo and `ReleaseCache`, the GitHub tag-first probe, candidate facts, the update-status evaluator, `outdated`, `update`, `pin`/`unpin`, `status` counts, `install --reinstall` |
| C | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3` | Dependencies: TOC conditionals, catalog additions, the pure resolver, engine rounds (C4 epic), output, bookkeeping and orphans, index lookups |
| D | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4` | Sources and changelogs: gzip for API responses, the WoWInterface index and source, the Tukui source, HTML/BBCode to text, changelogs |
| E | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5` | Integrity and adoption: index timestamps and the live-folder indexer, the drift detector and its surfaces, identification (E4 epic), the `adopt` command (E5 epic) |
| F | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6` | Desired state: `addons.toml`, `export`, `sync` (F3 epic), `copy` |
| G | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.7` | `search` and `auth github` |
| H | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8` | Checkpoint: contract audit, crash and concurrency, performance, live probes, real machine, README and vision records, the checkpoint itself |

Beads and comments refer to each other by plan key (A1 … H7). The key → id table is the first comment on this epic.

## Goals

- **G-M2-1 Current by default.** Every managed addon on every client can be brought to its newest compatible release with one command, and the tool can say what is out of date without changing anything. Both use the minimum number of requests: one fetch per distinct ref per run, one download per distinct archive per run, a free re-check inside `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` (15 minutes), and no GitHub REST for `release.json` publishers.
- **G-M2-2 Complete installs.** An addon whose loaded TOC requires another project gets that project in the same transaction, from a keyless source, verified like any other install. Nothing the TOC marks optional is ever installed without being asked for.
- **G-M2-3 More keyless sources.** WoWInterface and Tukui install, update and verify like GitHub (MD5 where the source provides one). Their changelogs are readable.
- **G-M2-4 Sole authority.** Folders installed before omaddons, or by another manager, can be brought under management without being replaced, and only on confident identification. The owner can see and repair managed files that changed on disk.
- **G-M2-5 Declarative sets.** The addon set of every client can be exported to one reviewable TOML file, reproduced exactly (`--locked`) or loosely, kept in sync idempotently, and copied between compatible clients.
- **G-M2-6 Findable.** Addons can be searched for across every keyless source, and every result carries an install command.
- **G-M2-7 No regression of M1 guarantees.** Every new mutation is a transaction (journaled, snapshotted, undoable, attributed), every write goes through fsx, every request is allowlisted and logged, every error has a fix, and the JSON contract stays one envelope.

## Success Criteria

The M2 checkpoint. H7 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7`) runs each criterion and records the evidence in its close reason, as M1's checkpoint bead did. These amend the vision's §7 M2 checkpoints; the amendments are recorded decisions.

1. **Update speed and economy.** `update --all` across about 30 managed addons on three targets takes under 2 s warm and under 10 s cold (hyperfine, release build, fixture-backed for repeatability, plus one live run). `net.log` shows each distinct ref fetched once and each distinct asset downloaded once per run. A single `omaddons undo` then reverts every client's transaction from that run.
2. **Zero-REST checks.** A full `outdated` across every `release.json` publisher in the catalog makes zero `api.github.com` requests. A second `outdated` inside 15 minutes makes zero requests of any kind. After the window, an unchanged release costs exactly one `github.com` request per ref. Exhausting REST on beta-channel or non-`release.json` repos returns `rate_limited` with `details.reset_at`.
3. **Dependencies** *(amended: LittleWigs replaces BugSack, M2-D10)*. Installing LittleWigs also installs BigWigs in the same transaction, with BigWigs recorded as `reason: dependency, required_by: ["LittleWigs"]`. Undoing that transaction removes both. `OptionalDeps` never auto-install: BugSack does not pull `!BugGrabber`. `Blizzard_*` dependencies count as satisfied. Removing BigWigs warns `still_required`, and removing LittleWigs reports BigWigs as `orphaned_dependency`.
4. **Adoption fixtures.** Current installs come out `exact`. One-version-behind installs come out `identified` and are replaced by the next `update`. A `guess` is never applied without an explicit folder argument. A `UIDir`-only match with a mismatched Title and Author is never `identified`. No fixture is adopted under the wrong source. Undo of an adopt removes the records and leaves every folder byte-identical.
5. **Drift.** A check over 5,000 managed files takes under 30 ms warm (release build). A touched-but-identical file produces no finding. Modified, deleted and added files are named. `install <addon> --reinstall` repairs drift from the blob cache with no network.
6. **Desired state.** `export` followed by `sync --locked` into an empty target reproduces refs and versions. Re-running `sync` is a no-op with zero network requests. `--prune` removes only unlisted managed addons. Family sections never touch `test` targets.
7. **Tukui.** ElvUI installs from Tukui into retail and Classic targets (and every other family its TOC declares). The download's MD5 is checked against the response `ETag`.
8. **WoWInterface.** A `wowi:` ref and a pasted WoWInterface link both install with MD5 verification. A tampered fixture fails with `hash_mismatch`.
9. **Status.** `status --cached` runs in under 5 ms with update counts populated from the memo, and makes no network I/O.
10. **Changelogs.** `info <gh addon> --changelog` shows release notes from the Atom feed with zero `api.github.com` requests.
11. **Search.** `search` returns ranked hits from the catalog, the WoWI index, Tukui and GitHub, with per-target compatibility hints. `--offline` works from cached indices.
12. **Gate and probes.** `argc gate --all` passes. Every new fuzz target runs 10 minutes without a crash. Live probes pass, including the catalog × declared-flavor matrix extended to Tukui entries. The real-machine suite passes and leaves every AddOns folder as it found it, including the untouched Forever stress-test set. README.md describes exactly what exists.

## Non-Goals

- The Omarchy widget, `errors` (BugGrabber) and `backup`. These are M3. M2 does make sure `status --cached` carries what the widget needs.
- `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, intent inference beyond the existing closest-command fix, the wire-names golden, stored plans (`plan_id`, `apply`) and the `doctor` surface. These are M4; M2's `--dry-run` keeps returning `plan_id: null`. M2 ships **no `doctor` command**: comment D17–D22 on the vision bead put some doctor items in M2, but body revision 2 superseded it and moved the whole doctor surface to M4. M2 does ship the detectors M4 will wrap (the drift detector, and the orphan and missing-dependency checks) as plain library functions with typed results.
- CurseForge and Wago sources, `auth curseforge|wago`, and the GitHub GraphQL batch path (moved to M5, M2-D22). M2 adopts CurseForge-only folders only when the user names a keyless `--ref`.
- Separate addon sets per game mode. Classic Era, Hardcore and Season of Discovery share one AddOns folder, and the game cannot split it.
- Parsing or editing SavedVariables, WeakAuras strings or profiles.
- Background daemons or scheduled checks. The M3 widget schedules `outdated`.
- Downgrades. Neither `update` nor `sync` ever installs an older release unless a version is pinned or locked explicitly, or the user explicitly switches the addon to another channel (`update X --channel stable`).

## Considerations

- **The Forever timeline drives the order.** The WoW: Forever stress test runs from 2026-10-19 and the game launches on 2026-11-04. After launch, publishers will ship Forever builds often, so the update loop (`outdated`, `update`, run-level undo, `status` counts) is delivered first. Delivery waves: (1) update core: A1, A2, A3, A9, A10, A12, A6, B1, B3, B4, B5, B6, B8; (2) engine foundation: A4.x, A5, A7, A8, B2, B7, B9; (3) dependencies and sources: C1–C7, D1–D5; (4) integrity and adoption: E1–E5, plus F1 (a root that E5.2 needs for `--ref`, so it must finish within this wave); (5) desired state, search, auth, changelogs: F2–F4, G1, G2, D6; (6) checkpoint: H1–H7, A11. The waves are an order of completion, not a ban on starting early: every root (A1, A2, A3, A7, A9, A10, A11, A12, B1, C1, C2, C3, D1, D5, E1, F1) can start at once on parallel agents.
- **The Forever stress-test set must stay untouched.** The owner's `forever` client holds 12 managed folders (5 addons) installed by transaction `01M50WBAPCN7YWGFFK8EB48RN8`, left installed on purpose for the load check tracked by `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` (deferred to 2026-10-20). Until that bead closes, no M2 test may remove, update, pin, sync, adopt or undo anything on `forever`. Real-machine tests use the other clients, or read-only commands on `forever` (H5).
- **Critical paths** (weighting size-S as 1 and size-M as 2 over the wired edges; the delivery comment shows the derivation):
  - the longest is the update → sources → adoption chain: B1 → B3 → B4 → B5 → D3 → E5.1 → E5.2 → E5.3 → H1 → H7. Splitting `adopt` made its three parts serial, so E5.x needs an agent early;
  - the engine chain is nearly as long: A3 → A4.1 → A4.2 (and A5) → C4.1 → F3.1 → F3.2 → H2 → H7, with H5 branching off F3.1;
  - E4.1 → E4.2 starts on day one through C1 and must be done before E5.1 needs it.
- **Top risks** (full table in the risks comment): the multi-target commit path has never run outside dry-run probes (A6 tests it with an `error@N` failpoint before B6 lands; A12 makes the run undoable as one); records-only work could regress install/remove semantics in `rejudge` (A4.1 keeps M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites as the regression net; A4.4 adds the record oracle); folder handover between addons (A5 merges it into `Replace` plus `Transfer`, which undo already reverses); a files-index schema bump would lock older binaries out (designed out: optional field, no version bump, E1); dependency resolution could pick the wrong project among 781 shared WoWI folder names (conservative chain, catalog first, M2-D8); adoption under the wrong source (catalog-first precedence M2-D40, `guess` never applied implicitly, exactness by hash, the `older_than_installed` guard M2-D42).
- **Collision hot spots** for parallel agents on one `main`: `src/engine/plan.rs` (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x), `src/app/status.rs` (A2, B8, C6, E3, E5.x), `src/error.rs` (new codes in several beads), `src/engine/undo.rs` (A4.x, A12, E1). Claim with file lists, keep commits small, rebase before each gate run, and treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work.
- **The contract stays additive.** Every new key, code and kind is additive and recorded on the vision bead (DEC-4: contract additions are allowed before the M4 freeze if recorded; M2-D32), with one deliberate type change in non-persisted dry-run output (`PlannedRelease.expected_hash`, A7). Error codes go from 38 to 39 (`desired_state_invalid`). M1 consumers keep working.
- **README is the product contract.** Each bead that ships a user-visible command updates README's "What it does today" and commands table in the same commit or the next one, so README never lags `main` by more than one commit. H6 is the final consistency pass, not the first mention. README's "Status" says M2 is done only at H7.
- **House rules** (every leaf bead repeats them): `argc gate` before code commits (D16, no CI); one writer (`src/fsx/`); commands never print; no `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`; constants in `src/politeness.rs`/`src/limits.rs`; tokio, reqwest, native-tls, openssl and aws-lc are banned; DEC-1 (each command adds its own subcommand, no stubs), DEC-3 (`Serialize + JsonSchema`, `BTreeMap`), DEC-7 (test hooks in debug builds only); public-safe bead text; work on `main`.
- **Placeholders** used in every M2 bead: `<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>` are `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `$XDG_STATE_HOME` and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`, so the app directories are `<config>/omaddons/`, `<state>/omaddons/` and `<cache>/omaddons/`; `<client dir>` is the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`. Code references `file.rs:123` are as of `e902d36`; line numbers drift, symbol names do not.
- **Planning record.** The plan was reviewed three times against the code before decomposition (17, 28 and 22 findings, all folded in). The comments on this epic carry everything the plan held that is not specific to one bead: the key → id table, the decision log M2-D1…M2-D43, the defaults, ground truth as verified on 2026-10-15, the architecture traces, the user workflows, delivery and lanes, risks, rationale and confidence, contract additions and the wire-name glossary, and the files and modules touched.
acceptance_criteria: All eight M2 area epics (A-H) and their children are closed; every M2 checkpoint criterion (update speed and economy, zero-REST checks, LittleWigs to BigWigs dependencies, adoption fixtures, drift, desired state, Tukui, WoWInterface, status --cached under 5 ms, Atom changelogs, search, gate and probes) has recorded evidence in the close reason of H7; argc gate --all passes; the real-machine suite leaves every AddOns folder as it found it, including the untouched Forever stress-test set; README.md describes exactly what exists; the vision bead carries the M2 decomposition, contract additions, constants, departures and M2-done comments
close_reason: All children completed

comments.text:
**Bead key → id map.** Descriptions and comments refer to M2 beads by these plan keys (for example "B4" or "the A4.1 bead"). Five large plan tasks were split into small epics whose children are the work: A4 (A4.1–A4.4), C4 (C4.1–C4.2), E4 (E4.1–E4.2), E5 (E5.1–E5.3), F3 (F3.1–F3.3). "Blocked by" and "Blocks" list the blocking edges as wired in br; epics carry no blocking edges (their children do).

| Key | Id | Type | Pri | Size | Title | Blocked by | Blocks |
