title: Fetch progress as each ref is answered, not after the whole batch
description:
## Background

A9 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.9`) reports `fetch` progress from `plan()` after `ReleaseCache::get` returns, one event per ref whose answer came from a source (`Origin::Fetched`). `sources::fetch_once` calls each source's `fetch` once with its whole batch (sources run in parallel through `run_bounded`), and only returns when every source has answered. So the fetch events arrive in one burst after the network wait. For `install` with a few addons that is fine. For `update` and `outdated` across about 30 GitHub addons, the progress line sits still for the whole fetch and then jumps to 30/30. The M3 widget's progress bar would do the same.

## Technical Approach

- `Source::fetch` (`src/sources/mod.rs`) gains a per-ref completion hook, for example `done: &(dyn Fn(&Wanted) + Sync)`, which each source calls as each wish is answered (github, github_rest, git, url, local, and the test source in `src/sources/mod.rs`).
- `fetch_once` takes the hook and passes it through. `ReleaseCache::get` takes the `ProgressSink` (or holds one, set where `app::engine::Engine` builds the cache), so the `fetch` total is the number of refs actually going to a source.
- Remove the post-hoc loop in `plan()` (`from_sources`), so each ref is reported only once and only from where it is fetched.
- Keep the sink's rules: counted under its lock, monotonic, fixed total, an item once per phase.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the acceptance criteria field.

## Test Plan

- Unit: a fake source answering a 3-ref batch calls the hook three times, and the sink emits fetch 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 in completion order.
- E2E: the existing `a_long_install_reports_progress_only_when_asked` keeps passing; its fetch assertion compares items as a set, because completion order is not deterministic across sources.

## Considerations

- Touches every source. Keep the hook call one line per answered wish.
- `fetch_once` is used directly by tests (`tests/catalog.rs`, `tests/sources_github*.rs`). A no-op hook argument keeps them simple.

## Dependencies

Discovered from A9. Most useful before B5 (`outdated`) and B6 (`update`), but it does not block them: they already emit fetch progress through `plan()`.
acceptance_criteria: During a cold fetch of several refs, fetch progress events arrive as each source answers each ref (not all after the slowest source); each ref fetched from a source is reported exactly once, current is monotonic up to a fixed total equal to the refs sent to sources, memo answers are not reported; fetch_once and every Source::fetch take the completion hook; existing progress tests pass
close_reason: Fetch progress is reported as each ref is answered

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: Source gains fetch_reporting(wanted, http, answered) (default: fetch, then each wish; forwarded through Arc); GithubSource reports each repository as its run_bounded worker answers, GitSource each repository in turn; batch sources (WoWInterface, Tukui, url, local) keep the default. sources::fetch_once_reporting passes the hook (fetch_once is it with a no-op; a disabled source's wishes are not reported). ReleaseCache::with_progress (Engine::cache sets it) grows the fetch phase by the refs it sends to an enabled source and reports each as it answers; the post-hoc loops in plan() (main fetch and dependency rounds), update and outdated are gone. outdated --changelog adds only refs whose changelog was asked but whose metadata came from the memo (grows the phase for them). Unit test sources::each_answered_wish_is_reported_once_and_disabled_sources_never; tests/install a_long_install_reports_progress_only_when_asked compares fetch items as a set (completion order); outdated's refresh progress test (1/5 … 5/5) unchanged. Gate green (1274). Note for the vision record: with --changelog, a changelog request for a ref fetched now is no longer its own progress item (the fetch item is reported when the metadata arrives).

title: Multi-target selection with World::select_many
description:
## Background

`-t` selects targets today only through `resolve_one`, so a selector that matches several clients is an error everywhere. Line numbers below are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

- `discover::registry::resolve(selector, targets, table)` (`src/discover/registry.rs:614-684`) returns **every match of the first precedence step that matches anything**. In order, the steps are: key, id, product code, flavor folder, game mode (`table`'s mode ids and aliases, so `sod` selects the Classic Era client), family, path (install root, client dir or AddOns path). With no match it returns `target_not_found`, naming the missing client for a known mode, with the fix `omaddons targets --rescan` (mode) or `omaddons targets`.
- `resolve_one` (`registry.rs:709-739`) calls `resolve`, and turns more than one match into `target_ambiguous`. The fix is the argv with `-t <first id>`, plus one alternative per other candidate, and `details: {selector, candidates}`.
- `World::select` (`src/app/world.rs:157-167`) uses `resolve_one` for `-t`, else every target sorted by id. Its only caller is `list` (`src/app/list.rs:179`).
- `status` (`src/app/status.rs:217-224`) and `info` (`src/app/info.rs:199-206`) hand-roll "`-t` through `resolve_one`, else every target". `remove` (`src/app/remove.rs:166-179`) and `install`'s defaulting chain (`src/app/install.rs:564-568`) also use `resolve_one`, and should keep doing so.
- Result: `-t vanilla` on a machine with two vanilla clients is `target_ambiguous` for `status`, `list` and `info`. That is right for `install`, which must land on one client, and wrong for `update`, `outdated`, `adopt`, `export` and `sync`, where "all my vanilla clients" is a natural request.

This serves G-M2-1 (bring every client current with one command) and G-M2-5 (export and sync over several clients), and keeps G-M2-7's "never guess the client" rule for single-target commands. It implements **M2-D24**: multi-target commands fan out family, mode and product selectors, while single-target commands keep their ambiguity errors (rejected: changing `resolve_one` globally, which would let `install -t vanilla` pick a client).

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `src/app/world.rs` (`select_many`; retire `select`), `src/app/status.rs`, `src/app/list.rs`, `src/app/info.rs`, `src/discover/registry.rs` (read-only use of `resolve`; doc comments only), tests in `tests/status.rs`, `tests/list.rs`, `tests/install.rs` (or a new `tests/target_selection.rs`).

1. **Add `World::select_many(&self, ctx: &Context) -> Result<Vec<&DiscoveredTarget>>`:**
   - **No `-t`:** every discovered target in `self.resolved.targets`, `live` and `test` alike (today's `select` behaviour), sorted by target id.
   - **With `-t`:** `resolve(selector, &self.resolved.targets, &self.table)`, unchanged. The result is every match of the first precedence step that matches anything, so `-t vanilla` yields every vanilla client and `-t retail` yields the one client with that id. Sort by target id and de-duplicate (by key, else client dir).
   - **No match:** `target_not_found`, with exactly the message, fix and details `resolve_one` produces today. Both go through `resolve`, which builds that error, so return it unchanged.
2. **The precedence it inherits** (first step with any match wins; all its matches are returned):

   | # | Step | Example |
   |---|---|---|
   | 1 | key (ULID) | `-t 01M…` |
   | 2 | id, case-insensitive | `-t retail`, `-t retail@steam` |
   | 3 | product code | `-t wow_classic_era` |
   | 4 | flavor folder | `-t _classic_era_` |
   | 5 | game mode id or alias (selects the client running it) | `-t sod`, `-t hardcore` |
   | 6 | family | `-t vanilla`, `-t mainline` |
   | 7 | path (install root, client dir or AddOns) | `-t <client dir>` |

3. **Switch `status`, `list` and `info` to `select_many`.**
   - `status` keeps listing missing registry entries (client dir gone) only when no `-t` is given, as today (`status.rs:226-229`). It already sorts its targets by id (`status.rs:326`).
   - `info` without `-t` now iterates targets in id order instead of discovery order. Review any snapshot that changes and note it in the close comment.
   - `list` replaces `world.select(ctx)` with `world.select_many(ctx)`.
4. **Single-target commands keep `resolve_one`:**
   - `install`, with its defaulting chain (`-t`, then config `default_target`, then the registry default, then the single compatible live target);
   - `remove` (unchanged M1 semantics);
   - `copy --from/--to` (F4: each side must be one client);
   - `adopt <folder> --ref R` (E5.2: one target, so the ref is unambiguous);
   - `history` and `undo`'s `World::history_key` (`world.rs:139-155`), which also resolves registry entries whose client is gone.
5. **Who will call `select_many`** (later tasks; write the doc comment for them):
   - `outdated` (B5), `update` (B6) and `export` (F2);
   - `sync` (F3.1), as a filter on the file's sections;
   - `adopt` report and `--apply` (E5.1, E5.2);
   - `pin`/`unpin` (B7), filtered to targets where the addon is installed, with or without `-t`;
   - `search` (G1), for its compatibility columns;
   - `status` (B8 adds counts), `list` and `info` (this task).
6. **Retire `World::select`.** After `list` switches, it has no caller. Delete it rather than keep a second "-t or all" selector, and put the "which commands use which" note on `select_many` and on the `resolve_one` call sites. (The plan said to keep it; the code shows `list` is its only caller, so keeping it would leave dead API.)
7. **Missing targets.** Registry entries whose client dir is gone are not in `resolved.targets`, so they are excluded from fan-out, exactly as `select` excludes them today. `status` reports them. `export` (F2) is the one command that also exports missing targets, from their state records; that is F2's business, not this task's.
8. **No wire changes.** No new codes, keys or kinds. Output is byte-identical when `-t` names a single target.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons status -t vanilla` on a tree with two vanilla clients lists both. Today it is `target_ambiguous`. `omaddons list -t vanilla` and `omaddons info <addon> -t vanilla` likewise cover both, and `omaddons list -t mainline` covers every mainline client.
- `omaddons install x -t vanilla` with two vanilla clients is still `target_ambiguous` (exit 3), with one fix per candidate (`fix_argv` plus one `alternatives` entry per other client), and running each fix's argv selects that client.
- `-t sod` resolves through `select_many` to the Classic Era client (mode step), for example `status -t sod`.
- A selector that matches nothing is `target_not_found` with the same message, fix and details as before.
- Output is unchanged when `-t` names a single target, and the existing `status`, `list`, `info`, `install` and `remove` tests pass.
- Results are sorted by target id, with no duplicates.

## Test Plan

- **Unit** (`src/app/world.rs` or `src/discover/registry.rs` tests): `select_many` over a synthetic resolved set: no `-t` gives everything sorted by id; an id gives one; a family gives every member, sorted; a mode gives its host client; a key wins over an id that equals a family name; no match gives `target_not_found`; no duplicates.
- **E2E:** two vanilla clients, built from a `BattlenetRoot` Classic Era product (`Home::new(&["wow_classic_era"])`) plus a `CustomRoot` at a 1.15.x build (family `vanilla`; assert the family through `targets --json` in the setup), as `tests/status.rs:36-45` builds its 3.3.5 custom root. Run `status`, `list` and `info` with `-t vanilla` and check both clients are present. Check `install x -t vanilla` is ambiguous and that each fix's argv runs. Check `status -t sod` on a tree with a Classic Era client.
- A10's `Home::with_custom` helper may not exist yet. Build the custom root directly with `CustomRoot::at(...)`.

## Considerations

- Keep `resolve` unchanged. The precedence rules already make fan-out predictable, and changing them would alter `install`'s errors.
- A test target (PTR, beta) is included when no `-t` is given, as today. Family sections in `sync` exclude test targets by F3.1's own rule, not here.
- `src/app/status.rs` is also edited by B8, C6, E3 and E5.x. Keep this change to the selection lines, so their merges stay small.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:** none (can start immediately).

**Unblocks:**
- B5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.5` (The outdated command): checks every selected target by default, and `-t vanilla` must mean every vanilla client.
- B6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6` (The update command): bare `update` and `update -t <family>` fan out to one transaction per selected target.
- B7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.7` (pin and unpin): selects with `select_many`, then filters to targets where the addon is installed, with or without `-t`.
- B8 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.8` (status update counts, adoptable count, hints and the list latest column): builds on the `status` and `list` selection this task switches, in the same files.
- E5.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.1` (adopt report mode): classifies unmanaged folders on every selected target.
- F2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.2` (The export command): exports the selected targets (default: all).
- F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` (sync core): uses `select_many` as a filter on the file's sections.
- G1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.7.1` (The search command): computes per-target compatibility hints for every selected target.
acceptance_criteria: World::select_many returns every discovered target sorted by id without -t, and with -t every match of the first matching precedence step of discover::registry::resolve (key, id, product, flavor folder, game mode, family, path), sorted by id with no duplicates; status -t vanilla on a tree with two vanilla clients lists both (today target_ambiguous), and list -t vanilla, list -t mainline and info <addon> -t vanilla likewise cover every matching client; install x -t vanilla with two vanilla clients is still target_ambiguous (exit 3) with one fix per candidate, and each fix's argv runs; -t sod resolves to the Classic Era client through select_many; a selector matching nothing is target_not_found with the same message, fix and details as before; output is unchanged when -t names a single target and the existing status, list, info, install and remove tests pass; install, remove, history and undo keep resolve_one; World::select is removed once list no longer calls it
close_reason: World::select_many fans read commands out over every matching client; single-target commands keep resolve_one; argc gate passes

comments.author: GildedLedger
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead, and how it serves M2.** M2's daily-use commands work across clients: `outdated` and `update` check every client, `adopt` classifies every client, and `export` and `sync` describe and reconcile every client. The owner's machine has six clients, and a family, mode or product selector is the natural way to name some of them (`-t sod`, or "update my vanilla clients" on a machine with more than one vanilla client). Today any selector that matches two clients is `target_ambiguous`, so agents would need one command per client. That breaks the "at most two commands per intent" design (vision agent workflows) and multiplies undo work. One small function in `World` that reuses the existing resolver unchanged lets every later multi-target command fan out the same way. The thesis rule that omaddons never guesses which client a single-target change lands on stays intact, because `install`, `remove`, `copy` and `adopt --ref` keep `resolve_one`.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D24: multi-target commands fan out family, mode and product selectors; single-target commands keep their ambiguity errors.** Why: natural phrasing ("update my vanilla clients") without weakening install's "never guess the client" rule. Rejected: changing `resolve_one` globally, which would make `install -t vanilla` silently pick one client, or install onto several in one command and break M1's single-target install contract.
- The fan-out uses `resolve()`'s existing precedence (key, id, product, flavor folder, mode, family, path; the first step with any match wins). A selector that is an id therefore never fans out, and a family fans out only when no id, product, flavor folder or mode has that name. That keeps fan-out predictable without new rules.
- Deciding inside this task: `World::select` goes away rather than staying as dead API. The plan said to keep it for single-target commands, but at `e902d36` none of them call it (`install` and `remove` call `resolve_one` directly), and `list` is its only caller.

**Facts verified during planning** (code at `e902d36`).
- `resolve` returns all matches of the first matching step (`src/discover/registry.rs:614-684`). `resolve_one` wraps it and builds `target_ambiguous` with per-candidate argv fixes (`:709-739`).
- `World::select` (`src/app/world.rs:157-167`) has one caller, `list` (`src/app/list.rs:179`). `status` (`src/app/status.rs:217-224`) and `info` (`src/app/info.rs:199-206`) hand-roll the same "-t or all" logic.
- Missing registry entries are outside `resolved.targets`, so fan-out excludes them for free. `status` lists them separately only without `-t` (`status.rs:226-229`).
- `tests/game_modes.rs` already checks that `sod` resolves to the Classic Era client through `resolve`.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- *Order changes in `info` output without `-t`* (discovery order becomes id order). Mitigation: review the snapshot diff and note it in the close comment. The new order is deterministic, which matches the plan's ordering default: sort by target id, then addon name, then folder key.
- *Collision in `src/app/status.rs`*, which B8, C6, E3 and E5.x also edit. Mitigation: touch only the selection lines, and land early (wave 1).
- Confidence: high. The resolver is unchanged and the new function is a thin wrapper.

title: Record carry-over rules and the extended RequestedChange
description:
## Background

The planner rebuilds an installed addon's record from scratch on every install, and nothing re-applies the user's intent under the lock. Line numbers below are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

- `RequestedChange` (`src/engine/plan.rs:70-90`) is `Install { ref, channel, version, file, name } | Remove { addon } | Reinstall { addon }`. Nothing constructs `Reinstall`. `want()` (`plan.rs:465-504`) resolves it with the record's ref and channel and `version: installed.pinned.then(|| installed.version.clone())`.
- `TargetPlanner::install` builds the record template at `plan.rs:724-745`: `channel = wanted.channel`, `pinned = wanted.version.is_some()`, `reason = Explicit`, `required_by = []`. `build_install` then copies `required_by` from the existing record (`plan.rs:828`). Consequences:
  - a plain `install X` silently **unpins** a pinned X and moves it to the newest release;
  - updating a `reason: dependency` record flips it to `explicit`, which breaks orphan detection (C6);
  - a caller that forgets the recorded channel resets it.
- When the chosen release equals the installed one, the plan returns "unchanged" (`plan.rs:659-667`) even when the *record* should change: `pin X --version <installed>`, a channel switch whose newest release is installed, or promoting a dependency.
- `rejudge` (`plan.rs:411-462`) rebuilds each work under the lock from its plan-time template (`:440-452`). A rule applied only at plan time would undo a `pin` that commits between an update's planning and its lock. A dropped work is `Ok(None)` (consumed at `src/engine/tx.rs:462-478`), with no way to return a warning.

Update (B6), pin (B7), reinstall (B9), dependencies (C4.1), sync (F3.1) and records-only work (A4.1) need one testable set of carry-over rules that also holds under the lock. This serves G-M2-1 (an `update` that is safe to run over everything because it never drops a pin) and G-M2-5 (`sync` converges on pins and channels). It implements **M2-D29** and the record side of **M2-D33** (both inlined below).

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `src/engine/plan.rs`, `src/engine/tx.rs` (`AddonWork` intent, `locked()` warnings), `src/app/install.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs` (`-v` notes), `src/error.rs` (`WarningCode::AddonPinned`; the `ALL.len()` assertion at `:746` goes from 22 to 23), `src/model.rs` (doc comments on `AddonRecord.pinned/channel/reason`), every `RequestedChange::Install` literal (`src/engine/testing.rs:353`, the test at `src/sources/git_hosts.rs:977`, `tests/plan.rs`), and the tests in `tests/plan.rs`, `tests/install.rs` and `tests/engine_concurrency.rs`.

**1. `RequestedChange` becomes** (an internal type; no `Serialize`):

```rust
pub enum RequestedChange {
    Install {
        r#ref: Ref,
        channel: Channel,            // the app resolves: --channel, else recorded, else default_channel, else stable
        channel_explicit: bool,      // NEW: true when --channel (or a desired-state entry) set it
        version: Option<String>,
        file: Option<PathBuf>,
        name: Option<String>,
        pin: PinIntent,              // NEW
        reason: AddonReason,         // NEW: Explicit for user requests, Dependency for resolver output
        reinstall: bool,             // NEW (B9): bypass the "already current" no-op; same release again
    },
    Remove { addon: String },
    Update { addon: String },        // RENAMED from `Reinstall` (it always meant "newest compatible release")
    Edit { addon: String, edit: RecordEdit },   // NEW in A4.1 (records-only changes), not in this task
}
pub enum PinIntent { Keep, Pin, Unpin }
```

`reinstall` exists here and stays `false` until B9 wires `--reinstall`. `channel_explicit` is carried for B6 and F3.1; it changes no behaviour in this task.

**2. Keep the intent on the work.** Add `InstallIntent { channel, channel_explicit, version: Option<String>, pin: PinIntent, reason: AddonReason, reinstall: bool, required_by_add: BTreeSet<String>, required_by_remove: BTreeSet<String> }` and store it on `AddonWork` (`intent: Option<InstallIntent>`, `None` for removes).
- The two `required_by` sets are empty for user requests.
- C4.1 fills `required_by_add` with the requester for dependency installs. It builds those works inside the engine, so `RequestedChange::Install` gets no `required_by` field.
- A4.1 owns folding. It keeps `AddRequiredBy`/`RemoveRequiredBy` edits folded into a `Folders` work in that work's own `edits` list and applies them right after `carry_over`, at plan time and in `rejudge`. The `required_by` result is the table row below either way (existing ∪ additions − removals); these two sets carry only what the planner itself creates, such as C4.1's requesters on a new dependency install.

**3. One function implements the table:** `fn carry_over(existing: Option<&AddonRecord>, intent: &InstallIntent, chosen: &AddonRecord) -> AddonRecord`. `chosen` is the release template that both the plan-time path and `rejudge` hold (ref, version, `version_confidence`, `release_id`, `blob_sha256`, folders). The plan named this parameter `winner: &Winner`, but `rejudge` has no `Winner`. Call `carry_over` inside `build_install` against whatever record `existing` holds at that moment: the snapshot at plan time, the current record under the lock.

| Field | New install | Existing record, user request | Existing record, dependency resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pinned` | `Pin` → true; otherwise false | `Pin` → true; `Unpin` → false; `Keep` → existing value | existing value |
| release chosen | newest eligible, or `version` | when the existing record is **pinned**, the intent is `Keep` and there is no `version`, the change is a no-op with warning `addon_pinned` (fix `omaddons unpin <name> -t <id>`). Otherwise newest eligible, or `version` | the existing record satisfies the dependency; no release change |
| `channel` | as passed | as passed (the app passes the recorded channel unless `--channel` was given) | existing value |
| `reason` | as passed | as passed: `install`, `sync` and `copy` pass `Explicit`, which **promotes** a dependency; `update`, `update --channel` and `pin --version` pass the recorded reason | existing value |
| `required_by` | `[]`, or `[requester]` for dependencies | existing ∪ additions − removals (dependency bookkeeping: additions from folded `AddRequiredBy`, removals from `RemoveRequiredBy` on remove and update) | existing ∪ `[requester]` |
| `name` | catalog name, or derived | existing name (record identity) | existing name |

`required_by` is always sorted and de-duplicated. The other fields keep today's behaviour: `version`, `version_confidence`, `release_id` and `blob_sha256` come from the chosen release, an empty version takes the TOC `## Version` (`plan.rs:829-834`), and `state` is `ok`. For the interim `addon_pinned` fix, see step 6.

**Two further rules complete the table.**
- **A pin intent never moves the release by itself.** `Pin` or `Unpin` with no `version` keeps the installed release and is always a records-only `SetPinned` edit. Only a `version`, or a newer release under `Keep`, changes the release.
- **`reinstall: true` skips the pinned no-op.** Repairing a pinned addon reinstalls its recorded release and keeps the pin. B9 implements the reinstall itself.

**4. Order inside `TargetPlanner::install`:**
1. Find `existing` by ref.
2. **Pinned no-op:** `existing.pinned`, `pin == Keep`, no `version` and `!reinstall` give `Ok(None)` plus `addon_pinned`, before any candidate download.
3. **No-move guards:** `Pin`/`Unpin` without a version, and `reason: Dependency`, against an existing record never select a new release. They go straight to the same-release comparison (step 5). If the record's folders are not all present, they are reported `unchanged` with the `-v` note. Nothing in M2 sends these: B7 and F3.1 send `Edit(SetPinned)`, and C4.1 sends `Edit(AddRequiredBy)` for managed dependencies. These are safety guards.
4. Otherwise select and try candidates as today.
5. The same-release check.
6. `build_install` → `carry_over`.

**5. Record-only differences are changes, not no-ops.** Suppose the chosen release equals the record's (`release_id` equal) and all its folders are present, but the carried-over `pinned`, `channel` or `reason` differ from the record. The change must still record that intent. This is how `pin X --version <installed>`, `update X --channel beta` when the newest beta is installed, and `install <current dependency>` take effect, and how `sync` converges.
- This task **detects** the difference. A4.3 turns it into a records-only `Records` work: kind `pin` if only `pinned` changed, else the request's kind.
- Until A4.3 lands, report the item `unchanged` with a `-v` note naming the fields that would change. Keep the notes in a `#[serde(skip)]` list on `TargetPlan`. `install`'s outcome carries them, and `app::dispatch` logs them at `LogLevel::Debug`, as it logs `lock_held_ms` today (`src/app/mod.rs:124-136`).

**6. Under the lock, and in the app layer.**
- **`rejudge`** rebuilds every install through `build_install`, so `carry_over` sees the current record. It re-checks the pinned no-op first: a record pinned since planning drops the work and adds `addon_pinned`.
  - Give it a return type that carries that warning, for example `enum Rejudged { Planned(PlannedAddon), Dropped { warnings: Vec<Warning> } }`. `locked()` adds those warnings to the target outcome, including when every work drops: the early return at `tx.rs:481-499` already carries `warnings`.
  - A pinned no-op is not a refusal, so it never becomes `plan_stale`.
- **`install`** (`change_for`, `src/app/install.rs:372-386`) passes:
  - `pin: Pin` when `--version` or a release-URL tag (`version_hint`) is given, else `Keep`;
  - `reason: Explicit`;
  - `channel_explicit` exactly when `--channel` was given;
  - `reinstall: false`.

  Channel resolution is unchanged.
- **`want()`** resolves `Update { addon }` to an install with the record's ref, channel and name, `Keep`, the record's reason and **`version: None`**. Drop today's `installed.pinned.then(…)`, so that a pinned record hits the pinned no-op. An addon with no record stays `not_managed`.
- **`addon_pinned`** is a new `WarningCode::AddonPinned`. Its message is `"<name> is pinned at <version> on <target id>; nothing was installed. Pass --version to move it"`. Build it in one constructor that B6 reuses.
  - The table's fix, `omaddons unpin <name> -t <id>`, names a command that B7 adds. The house rule is that a task never emits a fix for a command a later task adds; it emits the nearest existing command instead.
  - Decided: until B7 lands, the fix argv is `omaddons info <name> -t <id>`, which shows the pin and the newest release. B7 switches the constructor to `unpin`.

**Decisions.**
- **M2-D29:** `install X` of a pinned X is a no-op with `addon_pinned`, and `install X --version V` re-pins (`PinIntent::Pin`, today's behaviour). Why: pins protect working setups. Rejected: silently unpinning, as today.
- **M2-D33:** dependency installs use `default_channel`, never the requester's channel. Why: a beta-channel addon should not drag its dependencies onto beta. Rejected: inheriting the channel. Here, the dependency column keeps an existing record's channel; C4.1 passes `default_channel` for new ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `install X` on a pinned X is `unchanged`, with warning `addon_pinned` whose fix carries argv. X's files (tree hash) and record are unchanged.
- `install X --version V` installs V and records `pinned: true`. A later `install X --version W` installs W, still pinned.
- Updating a `reason: dependency` addon through `RequestedChange::Update` keeps `dependency`. An explicit `install` of it at a newer release records `explicit`; at the same release it is the record-only case, `unchanged` with a `-v` note until A4.3.
- `channel` is preserved when the app passes the recorded channel. `install X --channel beta` records `beta`.
- `required_by` survives an update unchanged, sorted and de-duplicated.
- **Concurrency:** a pin that commits between an update's planning and its lock leaves the addon pinned and un-updated. A test synchronises the two processes with a `sleep:` failpoint at `engine.plan.done`.
- Record-only differences are detected and reported `unchanged` with a `-v` note naming the fields.
- `addon_pinned` is registered (`WarningCode::ALL` has 23 entries), and the wire-name test passes.
- The existing install, plan, crash, concurrency and undo tests pass.

## Test Plan

- **Unit:**
  - a table test of `carry_over` covering every cell above (three columns × six rows);
  - both further rules, and `reinstall` on a pinned record;
  - record-only detection for each of `pinned`, `channel` and `reason`.
- **Unit (deterministic rejudge):** with `engine::testing::TxScene`, plan an update, commit a pinned record of that addon, then `rejudge` the planned work. It is dropped with `addon_pinned`.
- **E2E** (`tests/install.rs`):
  - the pinned no-op, comparing tree hash and record before and after;
  - re-pin to W;
  - channel preservation: `install gh:o/foo --file v1.zip --channel beta`, then a newer `--file` install keeps `beta`;
  - an explicit install of a dependency at a newer release.

  Switch fixtures with `home.scenario(...)` (`tests/install.rs:184`).
- **Plan level** (`tests/plan.rs`): write a record with `reason: dependency` through `store`, plan `RequestedChange::Update`, and assert `dependency` is kept.
- **Concurrency** (`tests/engine_concurrency.rs`, `Scene` with `--file` zips and `--offline`). B7's `pin` and B6's `update` do not exist yet, so both sides are installs:
  1. Install Foo from `v1.zip`, unpinned.
  2. Process A runs `install gh:o/foo --file v2.zip` (`Keep`) with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.plan.done=sleep:2000`.
  3. About 500 ms later (A's local-zip planning takes milliseconds), process B runs `install gh:o/foo --file v3.zip --version 3` (`Pin`) to completion.
  4. Assert final state only: Foo is at v3 with `pinned: true`. A's envelope has `tx: null`, the item `unchanged` and the warning `addon_pinned`. History holds two lines.
- **Contract:** `addon_pinned` appears in the envelope's `warnings` and in the stderr NDJSON mirror, with `fix_argv`.

## Considerations

- Install's JSON changes only additively; C5 adds `reason` to its items.
- The same-release no-op still requires every recorded folder to be present (today's rule). A pinned addon with a missing folder:
  - plain `install X` gives the pinned no-op;
  - `install X --version <pinned version>` reinstalls it (same release, folder missing);
  - B9's `--reinstall` will do the same.
- `install X --file new.zip` without `--version` on a pinned X is also the pinned no-op. The rule is uniform.
- Never compute carry-over only at plan time. The concurrency criterion exists because `rejudge` would restore the plan-time record.
- Collision hot spots: `src/engine/plan.rs` (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x) and `src/error.rs` (several tasks). A4.1 makes `rejudge` mode-aware right after this task, so keep the `Rejudged` change small and documented.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:** none (can start immediately).

**Unblocks:**
- A4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1` (Records-only engine work): adds `RequestedChange::Edit`, moves `intent` into its `Folders` work shape, and folds edits into a work by applying them right after this carry-over.
- B6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6` (The update command): needs `Update` resolving with `Keep` and the recorded reason, `channel_explicit`, and `addon_pinned`.
- B7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.7` (pin and unpin): `pin --version V` is `Install { version, pin: Pin, reason: record.reason }`; B7 also upgrades the `addon_pinned` fix to `unpin`.
- B9 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.9` (install --reinstall and installs from the blob cache): wires the `reinstall` field and intent added here into both no-op checks.
- C4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1` (Dependency rounds on install): plans `Install { reason: Dependency, pin: Keep, channel: default_channel }` with `required_by_add`, relying on the dependency column.
- F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` (sync core): passes `Explicit`, `channel_explicit: true` and pin intents, and converges through the record-only rule.

**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead, and how it serves M2.** `update --all` is M2's most-used command, and publishers will ship frequent WoW: Forever builds after its 2026-11-04 launch. Today a plain `install X` silently unpins X, and a dependency becomes `explicit` the first time it is updated. An update path built on that would quietly drop pins and wreck orphan detection, and the owner would stop trusting it. The thesis (omaddons as the sole, safe, undoable authority) needs the user's recorded intent (pin, channel, reason, who requires what) to survive every engine path, including the window between planning and the lock. Writing the rules as one table, implemented by one pure function, makes every cell testable and gives B6, B7, B9, C4.1 and F3.1 a single contract to build on. A3 is a root task on the critical path (A3 → A4.1 → A5 → C4.1 → F3.1).

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D29:** `install X` of a pinned X is a no-op with `addon_pinned`; `install X --version V` re-pins. Why: pins protect working setups. Rejected: silently unpinning, as today. That is M1's behaviour, and it makes every later `update` dangerous.
- **M2-D33:** dependency installs use `default_channel`, never the requester's channel. Why: a beta-channel addon should not drag its dependencies onto beta. Rejected: inheriting the channel. A3 encodes the record side, in the dependency column (existing channel kept). C4.1 passes `default_channel` for new dependency installs.
- **M2-D10's amended "never downgrades" rule** (no downgrade unless pinned, locked, or explicitly switched to another channel) is why `channel_explicit` exists. B6 uses it to skip the downgrade guard on `update X --channel C`. A3 only carries it.
- Review-round fixes folded into this task:
  - the rules re-run under the lock, so a `pin` that commits between an update's planning and its lock is not undone;
  - record-only differences count as changes, which is what lets `sync` converge (review pass 2, "sync convergence");
  - detecting *which* fields differ, so A4.3 can derive kind `pin` when only `pinned` changed (review pass 3, "pin-kind derivation").
- **Decided in this bead (staging).**
  - The `addon_pinned` fix is `omaddons info <name> -t <id>` until B7 adds `unpin`, following the plan's own rule that a task never emits a fix for a command a later task adds. B7 switches the fix to `omaddons unpin <name> -t <id>`.
  - The concurrency test races two installs (`Keep` against `--version`), because `pin` and `update` do not exist yet.
  - The `-v` note for record-only differences is logged by `dispatch`, as `lock_held_ms` is.
  - `carry_over` takes the release template rather than `Winner`, because `rejudge` has no `Winner`.

**Facts verified during planning** (code at `e902d36`).
- Template built at `src/engine/plan.rs:724-745` (`pinned = wanted.version.is_some()`, `reason = Explicit`); `required_by` copied at `:828`.
- Same-release no-op at `plan.rs:659-667`; `rejudge`'s same check at `:428-439`; rebuild from the template at `:440-452`.
- `Reinstall` is constructed nowhere. `want()` passes the pinned version for pinned records (`plan.rs:492`).
- `install` already passes the recorded channel (`src/app/install.rs:372-377`).
- `WarningCode::ALL` has 22 entries, asserted at `src/error.rs:746`.
- `--file` with `--version` pins today (`file_candidate`, `plan.rs:1241-1269`), which makes an offline concurrency test possible with the existing `Scene` helper (`tests/common/engine.rs`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- *Regressing M1 install semantics.* `tests/install.rs:183-208` (a newer release of an unpinned addon updates it) must pass unchanged. M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites are the regression net.
- *Changing `rejudge`'s return type collides with A4.1*, which makes `rejudge` mode-aware. Keep the change small, and land A3 first (A4.1 is blocked by it).
- *A pinned addon with a missing folder is no longer repaired by plain `install X`.* Mitigation: `install X --version <pinned>` repairs it now, and B9's `--reinstall` will. The warning's message says to pass `--version`.
- Confidence: medium-high, the plan's level for engine changes. The rules are pure and table-tested; the risk is in the plumbing under the lock, which the concurrency test covers.

title: Epic: Records-only work, the pin kind, history record and edit ops
description:
## Background

Adoption (E5), `pin`/`unpin` (B7), channel and reason edits, `required_by` bookkeeping (C4, C6), `sync`'s pin edits (F3) and removing an addon whose folders are already gone all change records without touching an AddOns folder. The engine cannot express that today. Line numbers are as of `e902d36`; the symbol names are what matter.
- **`rejudge` drops the work.** Under the global lock, `rejudge` (`src/engine/plan.rs:428-461`) treats a work with a record but no inspected archive as "no longer needed" (`_ if !record.addons.contains_key(..) => Ok(None)`, `:454-459`), or turns it into a remove.
- **History cannot see it.** `history_ops` (`src/engine/tx.rs:716-734`) derives ops only from folder swaps, so a records-only commit writes `ops: []`. Undo cannot reverse it, and conflict detection cannot see it. That is also latent defect 1: a `remove` whose folders were deleted out of band writes `ops: []`, and its undo restores nothing.
- **No kind.** `TxRequest` cannot name a kind, `target_kind` knows only install, update and remove, and `TxKind` has no `pin`.
- **Last work wins.** `next_record` (`tx.rs:661-674`) lets the last work for an addon win, so two works on one addon in one transaction (an update of BigWigs plus a `required_by` edit on it) would roll the record back.
- **Dependency undo breaks.** Undo restores whole records and treats every op as a folder touch (`src/engine/undo.rs:636-647`, `:840-846`), so undoing a requester after its dependency was updated would conflict, or roll the dependency back under its new folders.

Epic A4 makes records-only work a first-class engine transaction: journaled, snapshotted, attributed and undoable like any install (M2-D6). It adds the `pin` kind (M2-D5) and makes `required_by` edits reversible in place (M2-D35). It serves G-M2-7 (every new mutation is a transaction), and through its dependents G-M2-1, G-M2-2, G-M2-4 and G-M2-5.

**Decisions this epic implements:**
- **M2-D5:** pin and unpin are records-only transactions of a new kind `pin`; channel changes ride on `install`/`update --channel`.
  - Why: undoable and attributed, with no extra `channel` command.
  - Rejected: plain state writes (not undoable), and reusing the `adopt` or `update` kinds (misleading history).
- **M2-D6:** records-only work, the per-target working view and folder handover are first-class in the engine. Adopt, pin, dependency bookkeeping, sync and M4's repair all need them, so there is one implementation and one crash matrix. Rejected: ad-hoc state writes per feature.
- **M2-D35:** `required_by` edits are history ops with an `edit` field, reversed in place by undo and ignored by conflict detection, so updating a dependency keeps its requester undoable. Rejected: snapshot restore for every records-only change.

## Goals

- **Records work shape** beside today's `Folders` work, with every `RecordEdit`: `SetPinned`, `SetChannel`, `SetReason`, `AddRequiredBy`, `RemoveRequiredBy`, `Forget`, `Repoint`, `Adopt(AdoptSpec)`.
- **Engine rules.** One work per addon per transaction, edit-specific guards under the lock, `record` history ops, the kind override and `TxKind::Pin`, commit rules and output additions.
- **Reversible `required_by` edits** through `HistoryOp.edit`.
- **Record-only differences** (pin, promote to explicit, channel switch at the installed release) recorded as records-only transactions instead of `unchanged`.
- **Crash and concurrency proof** for the records-only path with a record-based oracle.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:
- **Commit and undo.** A records-only transaction commits with `record` ops and `undo` reverts it, folders untouched; a remove of an addon whose folders are gone records `record` ops and its undo restores the record.
- **Engine rules.** Updating D plus a `required_by` edit on D writes one consistent record. `rejudge` never drops a work whose guard holds; a broken pin guard is `plan_stale` or a no-op. `TxKind::Pin` serialises as `pin`, and `remove` plus `RemoveRequiredBy` is kind `remove`.
- **Dependency undo.** Install R (adding R to D's `required_by`), update D, undo R: R is gone, D keeps its update minus R, no `undo_conflict` is raised, D's files-index entries are byte-identical, and a following `undo <D's update>` succeeds.
- **Record-only differences:**
  - `install X --version <installed>` writes a `pin` transaction;
  - `install <current dependency>` writes an `install`-kind promotion;
  - `install X --channel beta` at the installed beta records `SetChannel`, and a repeat changes nothing.
- **Crash and race.** The records-only matrix crashes at ≥10 failpoints with the record oracle holding; a records-only transaction racing another addon's install commits. Existing crash, concurrency and undo suites pass unchanged.

## Non-Goals

- **Commands.** `pin`/`unpin` (B7), `adopt --apply` and repoint (E5.2) and `sync` (F3.1) build on this epic but are not part of it.
- **The working view.** Folder handover and intra-transaction claims are A5. Until A5, `Records.after` is computed from the snapshot plus works already planned in the target.
- **Dependency resolution.** Emitting `required_by` edits from real installs is C4.1 and C6.
- **Crash ops.** Adopt and mixed-transaction crash ops are H2.
- **Format bumps.** No new journal phase or payload field, and no history or files-index `schema_version` bump (M2-D36).

## Considerations

- **Most delicate change.** Change `rejudge` only with mode-aware arms, keep install and remove byte-identical, and treat M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites as the regression net. The plan rates this area **medium-high** confidence.
- **Undo needs both snapshots.** Records-only transactions still create the state snapshot and an empty SavedVariables manifest, because undo requires both. They never stage, never need a reload, and are allowed while the client runs.
- **Hot spots.** `src/engine/plan.rs` (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x), `src/engine/undo.rs` (A4.x, A12, E1), `src/engine/tx.rs`. Rebase before every gate run.

## How this was split

The plan sized A4 as one L task, reasoning that splitting would leave either a half-supported work kind that `rejudge` drops, or history that undo cannot reverse. The split keeps everything that must land together in A4.1, and peels off only parts that `main` can live without for a while.

- **A4.1** holds the whole core path: the `Records` shape and every edit, folding, guards with mode-aware `rejudge`, `record` history ops, the `Forget` conversion, the kind override and `TxKind::Pin`, commit rules and output. After it lands, every records-only work the engine accepts is planned, guarded, journaled, committed and undone by snapshot restore. No half-supported state exists. A4.1 also adds an in-process `error` failpoint matrix, so `main` has crash evidence for the new path before A4.4.
- **A4.2** isolates `required_by` reversal: `HistoryOp.edit`, in-place inverse, exclusion from undo's `direct` set, `touched` folders and index changes, and stale-name dropping. Between A4.1 and A4.2, `required_by` edits undo by snapshot restore, which is wrong once the dependency is updated later. So nothing outside tests may produce them until A4.2. Their only producers, C4.1 and C6, are blocked on A4.2.
- **A4.3** changes one planning outcome: a record-only difference becomes a `Records` work instead of `unchanged`. Before it lands, `main` reports such requests `unchanged` with a `-v` note, as A3 leaves them. That is less capable but consistent. B7 and F3.1 need the conversion and wait for it.
- **A4.4** is test-only. It adds the cross-process `abort` matrix with the record oracle (`Op::Pin` through a test-only engine-API child, `Op::Forget` through `remove`) and the records-only concurrency race. H2 builds on it.

**Where dependents attach:**
- A5, B7, E5.2 and F3.1 need A4.1;
- C4.1 and C6 need A4.2;
- B7 and F3.1 also need A4.3;
- H2 needs A4.4.

## Children

| Key | Id | Title | Scope in one line | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A4.1 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1` | Records-only engine work: Records mode, RecordEdit, RecordGuard, record history ops, kind override and TxKind::Pin | Work shapes, every `RecordEdit` and `AdoptSpec`, folding, guards, mode-aware `rejudge`, `record` ops, `Forget`, kind rules, commit and output | A3 |
| A4.2 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.2` | Reversible required_by edit ops in history and undo | `HistoryOp.edit`, in-place inverse on undo, exclusions from direct/touched/index/conflicts, stale-name dropping | A4.1 |
| A4.3 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.3` | Record-only differences become records-only transactions (pin, promote to explicit, SetChannel) | Same-release pinned/channel/reason differences become `Records` works at plan time and under the lock | A4.1 |
| A4.4 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.4` | Records-only crash matrix with the record oracle, and records-only concurrency | `Op::Pin`, `Op::Forget`, record oracle, records-only race against an install | A4.1 |

title: Records-only engine work: Records mode, RecordEdit, RecordGuard, record history ops, kind override and TxKind::Pin
description:
## Background

Adoption (E5.2), pin/unpin (B7), channel and reason edits (A4.3, F3.1), `required_by` bookkeeping (C4.1, C6) and removing an addon whose folders are already gone all change records without touching an AddOns folder. The engine cannot express that. Line numbers are as of `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.
- `rejudge` (`src/engine/plan.rs:411-462`) arms: `(Some(template), Some(inspected))` → no-op check or `build_install` (428-453); `_ if !record.addons.contains_key(..) => Ok(None)` (454-459); `_ => planner.remove(..)` (460). A work with a record and no inspected archive is dropped under the lock, or turned into a remove.
- `history_ops` (`src/engine/tx.rs:716-734`) derives ops from `SwapOp`s only, so a swap-less commit writes `ops: []`. Undo and `check_conflicts` (`src/engine/undo.rs:507-555`) read `ops`, so such a commit is not undoable and invisible to conflict detection.
- `next_record` (`tx.rs:654-688`) inserts each work's full record, the last for an addon wins (661-674), and restamps `installed_at` for every work (666).
- `TxRequest` (`tx.rs:84-92`) has no kind; `target_kind` (`plan.rs:538-548`) knows Install, Update and Remove and is recomputed in `locked()` (`tx.rs:480`); `TxKind` (`src/model.rs:408-419`) has no `Pin`.
- **Latent defect 1:** `TargetPlanner::remove` (`plan.rs:861-898`) gets no allowed op for a folder with no live entry (`src/engine/ownership.rs:159-163`). A remove whose folders were all deleted out of band writes `ops: []`, its undo restores nothing, and the gone folders' index entries stay.

Without this, each feature would hand-roll an un-undoable state write, breaking G-M2-7 (every mutation is a transaction) and starving G-M2-4 (adopt without replacing folders), G-M2-5 (sync converges) and G-M2-1 (pins protect updates). First child of epic A4 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4`).

## Technical Approach

Builds on A3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.3`): `Install` carries `channel_explicit`, `pin: PinIntent { Keep, Pin, Unpin }`, `reason`, `reinstall`; `Reinstall` is renamed `Update`; `AddonWork` keeps the intent; `carry_over` runs in `build_install` at plan time (snapshot) and under the lock (current record). Add `RequestedChange::Edit { addon: String, edit: RecordEdit }`.

**1. Work shapes.** `AddonWork { addon, mode }`:
- `Folders { record, blob, inspected, skipped, swap, transfers, degraded, intent: Option<InstallIntent>, edits: Vec<RecordEdit> }`: today's install, update, remove (A3's `intent` moves here from `AddonWork`), plus folded edits.
- `Records { before: Option<AddonRecord>, after: Option<AddonRecord>, edits, index_upserts: Vec<(FolderName, FolderIndex)>, index_removals: Vec<FolderName>, guard: RecordGuard }`: no folder ops, nothing staged.

`edits` is kept because the rules run again under the lock: `rejudge` recomputes `after` by applying `edits` to the **current** record, so a concurrent change to another field survives (`Adopt` keeps the spec's record, `Forget` keeps `None`). Read `w.record`/`w.inspected` through accessors (`stage_all`, `creates_addons_dir`, `src/app/install.rs:795`).

**2. `RecordEdit`:** `SetPinned(bool)`, `SetChannel(Channel)`, `SetReason(AddonReason)` set the field; `AddRequiredBy(String)`/`RemoveRequiredBy(String)` add or remove a name, kept sorted and de-duplicated by `TargetRecord::addon_key`; `Forget` drops a record whose folders are all missing (with a folder present, the item fails `usage`, fix `omaddons remove <name> -t <id>`); `Repoint(Ref)` sets `ref`, clears `release_id` and sets `version_confidence: toc`, so the next `update` installs from the new ref (E5.2); `Adopt(AdoptSpec)` creates a record, `AdoptSpec { record, folders: Vec<(FolderName, FolderIndex)>, stats }` with per-file plan-time `(size, mtime_ns)` (E5.2 fills it via `index_live_folder`). An edit that changes nothing plans no work (unchanged, no transaction). An edit on an unrecorded addon is the item failure `not_managed` (except `Adopt`).

**3. One work per addon per transaction.** Two works for one addon would roll its record back to whichever `next_record` inserts last (an update of BigWigs plus an `AddRequiredBy` on BigWigs). So an edit to an addon that already has a work is folded into it: into a `Folders` work's carry-over (applied after `carry_over`, at plan time and in `rejudge`) or merged into its `Records` work. Folding is order-independent: a `Folders` work planned after a `Records` work for the same addon absorbs its edits and replaces it, change included. `Records.after` comes from the snapshot plus the works already planned in this target; A5 replaces that with the working view, so keep folding in one function A5 can rewire.

**4. `RecordGuard`**, re-checked by `rejudge` under the lock, offline, per edit kind so an unrelated concurrent change does not abort the target:
- `SetPinned`, `SetChannel`, `SetReason`, `Repoint`: still recorded with the same `release_id`.
- `AddRequiredBy`, `RemoveRequiredBy`: still recorded, at any release.
- `Forget`: still recorded, and its folders still absent.
- `Adopt`: every folder still present, unmanaged and not a symlink; a re-listing finds exactly the indexed paths; every file keeps its plan-time `(size, mtime_ns)`; no record has taken the spec's name.

Several folded edits take the strictest guard. Failure rules: **an adopt guard failure is always `plan_stale` (retryable), whatever the generation**, because a file edited between hashing and the lock never bumps it, and dropping the work would lose the request. For edits, a failed guard with the generation changed is `plan_stale` with `details.cause` via `tx::stale()`, as for folder work (cause: an existing code such as `not_managed`; no new code). With the generation unchanged the edit is dropped as no longer needed (only a `Forget` whose folder came back by hand). Give `rejudge` the plan-time generation, or a typed failure `locked()` maps.

**5. History, `rejudge`, `remove`.** `history_ops` also emits one `HistoryOp { op: FolderOp::Record, folder, addon }` per folder (before ∪ after) of every `Records` work. Undo already turns `record` ops into "no swap" (`undo.rs:647`) and restores the addons named in `ops` from the snapshot, which undoes pin, channel, reason, repoint, adopt and forget. `rejudge` becomes mode-aware: `Folders` arms stay byte-identical; `Records` works check the guard, then return the recomputed work or apply the failure rules, and are never dropped or turned into a remove while the guard holds. `TargetPlanner::remove` plans a `Records` work when every recorded folder is absent: `before` = the record, `after: None`, `index_removals` = its folders, guard `Forget`, `Change { kind: Remove, folders.recorded }`, no running policy. That fixes latent defect 1. A partly absent remove stays a `Folders` work (M1 behaviour).

**6. Kind.** `TxRequest.kind: Option<TxKind>` (override), carried into `PlanRequest`. `TxTarget.default_kind: TxKind` (what the app means: install → Install, remove → Remove, update → Update) is copied into `TargetRequest.default_kind`. Both feed `plan()` and the recomputation in `locked()`. Add **`TxKind::Pin`** (wire `pin`, undoable). `target_kind(changes, override, default_kind)`, in order:
1. no changes → no transaction;
2. an override wins: `Adopt` (adopt, repoint), `Pin` (pin, unpin), `Sync`;
3. all changes are `Edit`s that changed only `pinned` → `pin`;
4. all changes are `Edit` or `Adopt` → `default_kind`;
5. in a mix, `Edit`/`Adopt` changes are ignored and today's rule applies: `remove LittleWigs` plus `RemoveRequiredBy` on BigWigs is `remove`.

Undo of any kind is an ordinary `undo`. Update the literals in `src/app/install.rs:406` and `:592` (probe), `src/app/remove.rs:225`, `src/engine/testing.rs:367`, `tests/plan.rs`.

**7. Commit.** The journal already handles zero swap steps: `swap()` still writes `swapped` (`src/engine/swap.rs:338`). A crash while Prepared rolls back nothing, and once Swapped it rolls forward record, index and history idempotently. No new phase or payload field. Records-only transactions still take the state snapshot and write an empty `WTF.manifest.json` (`snapshot_saved_variables` with no folders); undo requires both (`undo.rs:412-414`, `:871-872`), so do not optimise them away. Merge `index_upserts`/`index_removals` into the swap-derived `IndexChanges`, so they ride in the journal payload. `next_record`: a `Records` work inserts `after` (or removes the key), sets `tx_id`, keeps `installed_at`; an `Adopt` (no previous record) takes the commit time; `Folders` works restamp as today. Records-only works skip staging and the running policy, report `reload_required: none`, and commit while the client runs.

**8. Output.** `ChangeKind` gains `Adopt`, `Edit` (wire `adopt`, `edit`). Keep it a `Copy` string enum and add `Change.fields: Vec<EditField>` (wire `fields`: `pinned|channel|reason|required_by|ref`, sorted, omitted when empty) so existing change JSON is byte-identical. Example: `{"addon":"Foo","ref":"gh:o/foo","kind":"edit","fields":["pinned"],"from_version":"1","to_version":"1","folders":{"added":[],"replaced":[],"removed":[],"skipped":[],"recorded":["Foo","FooOld"]}}`. `FolderSummary.recorded: Vec<FolderName>` (folders whose ownership record changed without a swap; sorted, always serialised; update `install.rs` `sorted()`). `src/app/history.rs` `ChangeCounts.recorded` counts `record` ops, shown in the human line when non-zero.

**Why (M2-D6):** done once in the engine, every records-only change is journaled, snapshotted, attributed and undoable, and M4's `repair` gets it free. **Crash safety:** the folder oracle cannot see records-only work. Record oracle: after a crash and recovery, the record holds the edit **iff** `history.jsonl` holds the transaction, the generation matches, and AddOns is byte-identical. A4.4 runs it cross-process (`abort`); this bead in process (`error`).

**Files:** `src/engine/{plan,tx,undo,testing}.rs`, `src/engine/journal.rs` (verify only), `src/model.rs`, `src/state/history.rs` (doc), `src/app/{history,install,remove}.rs`, `tests/plan.rs`, `tests/engine_undo.rs`, snapshots `tests/snapshots/{install__*,plan__plan_dry_run}.snap` and `tests/contract/snapshots/contract__matrix__{history_ok,install_*}.snap`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Edit(SetPinned(true))` via the engine API commits kind `pin` with one `record` op per folder; `undo` unpins it (generation +1); AddOns stays byte-identical.
- `remove Foo` after its folders were deleted out of band commits kind `remove` with `record` ops and drops record and index entries; `undo` restores both.
- Updating D plus `Edit(AddRequiredBy("R"))` on D, in either order, writes one record (new release, R in `required_by`) and one change.
- Guards: a pin still commits after a concurrent install of another addon; a `RemoveRequiredBy` survives a concurrent update of its addon and keeps that release; a concurrent update breaking a pin guard is `plan_stale` (retryable, `details.cause`); a changed adopted file is `plan_stale` even at an unchanged generation.
- `TxKind::Pin` serialises `pin` and is undoable; `target_kind` follows the five rules, including `remove` + `RemoveRequiredBy` → `remove`.
- A no-op edit creates no transaction; records-only transactions report `reload_required: none` and commit while the client runs under `safe`.
- An `error` at each commit-window failpoint leaves the edit present iff its history line exists, folders untouched.
- The existing crash, concurrency and undo suites pass unchanged; install/remove output changes only by `folders.recorded`; reviewed snapshots committed.

## Test Plan

- Unit `plan.rs`: `target_kind` table; `apply_edit` per variant; fold order independence; guard checks and the strictest-guard rule.
- Unit `tx.rs` (`TxScene`): `history_ops` with mixed works; `next_record` with `Records` works; an `error` matrix over `FAILPOINTS` for a pin, modelled on `an_error_at_any_failpoint_leaves_folders_wholly_old_or_wholly_new`; two-thread races with `failpoint::with_spec("engine.plan.done=sleep:400", …)` against a competing `TxScene::run` (pin vs other install; `RemoveRequiredBy` vs update; pin vs update → `plan_stale`).
- Unit `undo.rs`: undo of a pin, a forget, and a hand-built `Adopt` (record and index entries go; folders untouched).
- E2E: `tests/engine_undo.rs` forget-remove then `undo` via the CLI; `tests/plan.rs` dry run showing `kind: "edit"`, `fields`, `folders.recorded`. Unit `app/history.rs`: `recorded` counted.

## Considerations

- Keep install and remove byte-identical; the M1 suites are the regression net. Change `rejudge` only by adding mode-aware arms.
- **`required_by` edits keep M1 snapshot-restore undo until A4.2.** Undoing a requester after its dependency was updated would raise `undo_conflict` or roll the dependency's record back under new folders. Nothing outside tests may produce `AddRequiredBy`/`RemoveRequiredBy` before A4.2; C4.1 and C6 wait for it.
- Command statuses for edits belong to A4.3, B7, E5.2, F3.1. One exception, owned by A6 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.6`): if A6's `src/app/outcome.rs` is already on `main`, map the new kinds in its `build` as A6 specifies (`Adopt` → `adopted`; an `Edit` whose `fields` are only `pinned` → `pinned` or `unpinned` by the new value; any other `Edit` → `edited`), because whichever of A6 and A4.1 lands second adds that mapping. `FolderOp::Record` exists since M1; `HistoryOp` is unchanged here.
- Hot spots: `src/engine/plan.rs` (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x), `src/engine/undo.rs` (A4.x, A12, E1), `src/error.rs`.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.3` (Record carry-over rules and the extended RequestedChange): edits fold into A3's carry-over, and `rejudge` re-applies the intent A3 keeps on `AddonWork`.

Unblocks:
- A4.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.2` (Reversible required_by edit ops): adds `edit` to the `record` ops emitted here.
- A4.3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.3` (Record-only differences become records-only transactions): produces `Records` works, guards and kind rules defined here.
- A4.4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.4` (Records-only crash matrix and concurrency): crashes this commit path.
- A5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.5` (Per-target working view): replaces the view behind `Records.after` and folding, and applies edits to its view.
- B7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.7` (pin and unpin): `Edit(SetPinned)` with the `Pin` override and `TxKind::Pin`.
- E5.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.2` (adopt --apply and repoint): `Adopt(spec)`, `Repoint`, the adopt guard, the `Adopt` override, `folders.recorded`.
- F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` (sync core): `SetPinned` edits in mixed transactions under the `Sync` override.
acceptance_criteria: Edit(SetPinned(true)) through the engine API commits a pin-kind transaction whose history ops are one record op per folder, and undo unpins it with AddOns byte-identical; remove of an addon whose folders were deleted out of band commits kind remove with record ops, dropping the record and its index entries, and undo restores both; an update of D plus Edit(AddRequiredBy) on D in either order writes one record with the new release and the requester; a pin still commits after a concurrent install of another addon, a RemoveRequiredBy survives a concurrent update of its addon and keeps that release, a concurrent update breaking a pin guard is plan_stale (retryable, details.cause), and a changed adopted file is plan_stale even at an unchanged generation; TxKind::Pin serialises pin and is undoable, and target_kind follows the five rules including remove plus RemoveRequiredBy is remove; a no-op edit creates no transaction; records-only transactions report reload_required none and commit while the client runs; an injected error at each commit-window failpoint leaves the edit present iff its history line exists; existing crash, concurrency and undo suites pass unchanged and install/remove output changes only by folders.recorded
close_reason: Records-only work is a first-class engine transaction: journaled, snapshotted, guarded under the lock, history record ops, undoable; argc gate passes

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** Five M2 features (adopt, pin/unpin, channel and reason edits, dependency bookkeeping, sync's pin edits) change records without moving a folder. If each wrote state by hand, those changes would be unjournaled, unsnapshotted and impossible to undo, and the project's thesis would break: omaddons as the sole, safe, undoable authority over every client's addons. This bead makes "a records-only change" a first-class engine transaction, so `undo`, `history`, conflict detection and crash recovery cover it like any install. It also fixes latent defect 1: a remove of an addon whose folders were already gone wrote `ops: []`, and its undo restored nothing.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D6:** records-only work, the per-target working view and folder handover are first-class in the engine. Adopt, pin, dependency bookkeeping, sync and M4's repair all need them, so there is one implementation and one crash matrix. Rejected: ad-hoc state writes per feature.
- **M2-D5:** pin and unpin are records-only transactions of a new kind `pin`; channel changes ride on `install`/`update --channel`. That keeps them undoable and attributed, with no extra `channel` command. Rejected: plain state writes (not undoable), and reusing the `adopt` or `update` kinds (misleading history). This bead adds `TxKind::Pin`; B7 uses it.
- **M2-D35** is staged out to A4.2. Here `required_by` edits produce plain `record` ops with snapshot-restore undo, so nothing outside tests may emit them until A4.2 lands.
- **Review-round fix, pin-kind derivation:** `target_kind` derives `pin` only when every change is an edit of `pinned` alone, and `Edit`/`Adopt` changes are ignored in mixes. That way `remove LittleWigs` plus a `RemoveRequiredBy` on BigWigs stays `remove`.
- **Decided while splitting, recorded here:**
  - `Records` and `Folders` works keep their `edits`, and `rejudge` recomputes `after` from the current record. Otherwise the plan-time copy would overwrite a concurrent change, and "a `RemoveRequiredBy` survives an unrelated update" could not hold.
  - Folded edits take the strictest guard.
  - The edit field list is a sibling `Change.fields`, so `kind` stays a string and existing change JSON is unchanged.
  - An `Adopt` record takes the commit time as `installed_at`, since it has no previous record.
  - An `Adopt` whose name was taken meanwhile fails its guard.
  - An explicit `Forget` with a present folder fails the item with `usage`.
  - An in-process `error` failpoint matrix lands here, so `main` has crash evidence for this path before A4.4's cross-process matrix.

**Facts verified during planning** (at `e902d36`):
- `rejudge`'s arms are at `src/engine/plan.rs:428-461`.
- `history_ops` (`tx.rs:716-734`) uses swaps only.
- `next_record`'s last-wins insert is at `tx.rs:661-674`, and it restamps `installed_at` at `:666`.
- `ownership::check` drops removes of absent folders (`ownership.rs:159-163`).
- The journal works with zero swap steps: `swap()` writes `swapped` at `swap.rs:338`, and roll-forward is idempotent by generation and by history tx id.
- With no folders, `snapshot_saved_variables` writes an empty manifest, which undo requires (`undo.rs:412-414`, `:871-872`).
- Undo maps `record` ops to no swap (`undo.rs:647`) and restores `direct` addons wholesale (`undo.rs:776-815`).
- `stage_all` stages only works with an inspected archive (`tx.rs:377-395`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Regressing install/remove in `rejudge` (medium likelihood, high impact): add mode-aware arms only, and keep M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites unchanged as the regression net.
- A records-only work silently dropped under the lock (the bug this bead removes): covered by the guard tests and the in-process failpoint matrix.
- The plan rates the engine changes (A4, A5, C4, A12) **medium-high** confidence. They touch the most delicate code, and the mitigations are M1's large regression suites plus the new record oracle.

**Siblings.** A4.2 adds `HistoryOp.edit` and edit-aware undo for `required_by`. A4.3 turns record-only differences, which A3 reports as `unchanged`, into the `Records` works defined here. A4.4 adds the cross-process `abort` matrix for `Op::Pin`/`Op::Forget` and the records-only concurrency race. This bead must not emit `edit` fields, change install's item statuses, or convert record-only differences.
