title: Epic: M2 update checks and updates
description:
## Background

M1 made omaddons correct, but not useful day to day. The only way to update is to re-run `install` addon by addon, target by target. Each run fetches again and downloads again: one DBM release installed on three Classic clients is downloaded three times. Nothing says what is out of date. `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` (15 minutes, `src/politeness.rs:34`) is defined but unused. And an unchanged GitHub stable ref costs two fetches on every check (`releases/latest`, then `release.json`, which redirects to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`: three requests on the wire).

This epic delivers the daily-use loop:
- `omaddons outdated` says what is out of date, cheaply and read-only;
- `omaddons update` brings every client current, with one run-level undo;
- `pin`/`unpin` hold a known-good version;
- `status` shows pending update counts offline, so the M3 widget can paint a badge without the network;
- `install --reinstall` repairs an install from the blob cache.

It is the **highest-value epic and first in delivery order**. WoW: Forever launches on 2026-11-04, after a stress test from 2026-10-19, and publishers will ship Forever builds often after launch. Being able to update everything everywhere is the most valuable thing M2 can deliver early. Wave 1 of delivery (the update core) is A1, A2, A3, A9, A10, A12, A6, B1, B3, B4, B5, B6 and B8. B2, B7 and B9 follow in wave 2, alongside the engine foundation.

The design keeps every M1 guarantee:
- the memo is derived data in `<cache>/omaddons/`;
- `status` never writes;
- every update is a journaled, undoable transaction per target;
- every request is allowlisted and logged to `net.log`;
- the TOC check stays the ground truth for compatibility (vision D5).

## Goals

Goal "current by default": every managed addon on every client can be brought to its newest compatible release with one command, and the tool can say what is out of date without changing anything. Both use the minimum number of requests:
- **one fetch per distinct ref per run**, across all targets, dependency rounds and engine runs of a command;
- **one download per distinct archive per run**, however many clients take it (blob facts in the memo here; per-command de-duplication in A8);
- **a free re-check inside `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL`** (15 minutes): `outdated` followed by `update` makes no second round of requests;
- **zero GitHub REST for `release.json` publishers.** After the window, an unchanged GitHub stable ref costs exactly one `github.com` request (the tag-first probe).

And for behaviour:
- One pure evaluator decides "update available" for `outdated`, `update`, `pin` hints, `status` and `list`, so they can never disagree.
- `update` never downgrades on its own, never "updates" an adopted newer build to an older keyless one, and treats a newest release that does not load on a client as `blocked`, not as a failure.
- Pins are respected everywhere and are undoable transactions of the new kind `pin`.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:
- **Economy and speed.** `update --all` across about 30 managed addons on three targets runs under 2 s warm and under 10 s cold (H3 measures, with a release build). `net.log` shows each distinct ref fetched once, and each distinct asset downloaded once once A8 has landed. A single `omaddons undo` then reverts every client's transaction from that run.
- **Zero-REST checks.** A full `outdated` across every `release.json` publisher makes zero `api.github.com` requests. A second `outdated` inside 15 minutes makes zero requests of any kind. After the window, an unchanged release costs exactly one `github.com` request per ref. Exhausting REST on beta-channel or non-`release.json` repos returns `rate_limited` with `details.reset_at`.
- **Status.** `status --cached` runs in under 5 ms with update counts populated from the memo, and makes no network I/O.
- **Repair.** `install <addon> --reinstall` reinstalls the recorded release from the blob cache with no network.
- **Pins and blocks.** `pin` and `unpin` write undoable `pin` transactions. A pinned addon is skipped by `update`. A newer release that fails verification on a client is `skipped/blocked`, and the run is not partial.
- Every request-economy assertion runs in the normal gate from `net.log` counts, not from timing.

## Non-Goals

- Background daemons or scheduled checks. The M3 widget schedules `outdated`.
- The GitHub GraphQL batch path. It moves to M5 (M2-D22); the opt-in REST token is G2.
- Downgrades. Neither `update` nor `sync` installs an older release unless a version is pinned or locked, or the user explicitly switches channel (`update X --channel stable`).
- Treating pending updates as `status` attention (M2-D27). `status --check` is health; `outdated --check` is freshness.
- Changelogs (D6 adds `outdated --changelog`), dependency handling on the update path (C4.2, C6), adopt hints (E5.3), drift (E2, E3), and the WoWI and Tukui sources (D3, D4), which plug into the same memo.
- `update --version`. Exact versions come from `install --version` or `pin --version`.

## Considerations

- **Freshness is per command (M2-D37):**
  - `install` revalidates (probe or fetch), so someone installing now gets now's release;
  - the batch commands and `info` use the 15-minute window;
  - `--refresh` always fetches;
  - `--offline` answers from the memo only, and wins over `--refresh`.
- **No stale fallback for mutating commands.** `outdated` may fall back to a stale memo entry on a network failure. `update`, `install` and `sync` never do, because installing from stale metadata could pick a release the source withdrew.
- **The memo is a cache (M2-D1).** Its absence or corruption never fails a command. Concurrent writers may lose an entry, which costs one request.
- **Real machine.** Tests must never touch the `forever` target's stress-test set (transaction `01M50WBAPCN7YWGFFK8EB48RN8`) before `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` closes. Mutating real-machine tests name `-t` explicitly and undo by tx id.
- **Hints only for existing commands.** Until `adopt` exists, `not_managed` fixes name `install`, and E5.3 upgrades them later.
- **Collision hot spots:** `src/engine/plan.rs` (B3, B9, plus A3, A4.x, A5, A8, C3, C4.x) and `src/app/status.rs` (B8, plus A2, C6, E3, E5.x). Claim with file lists and keep commits small.
- **B6 before A5.** One handover case degrades: an update that drops a folder another addon newly ships fails `ownership_conflict` on the second addon, and a re-run completes it. A5 makes it one transaction.

## Children

| Key | Id | Title | Scope in one line | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.1` | The release memo and ReleaseCache | `<cache>/omaddons/releases.json` and `ReleaseCache` (window, revalidate, refresh, offline), command-wide fetch-once, `install`/`info` wired, `http_validators` registered | — |
| B2 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.2` | GitHub tag-first probe and conditional feeds | `Source::probe` via `releases/latest`, commits feed validators, 304 rate-limit header fix, REST exhaustion test | A10, B1 |
| B3 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.3` | Candidate facts: verdicts and blob hashes in the memo | `Plan.facts`, downloads skip the network for cached `(release_id, asset)`, `loads`/`out_of_date`/`primary_interface` per client | B1 |
| B4 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.4` | The update-status evaluator | pure `evaluate` plus shared `statuses()`: current, update_available, pinned, ahead, blocked, failed, unchecked, static | B1, B3 |
| B5 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.5` | The outdated command: a cheap, read-only update check across targets | `outdated [-t] [--refresh] [--check] [--verify]`, alias `check`, token-frugal listing, writes only the cache | A1, A2, A9, A10, B4 |
| B6 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6` | The update command: multi-target updates with run-level undo | `update [<addon>…] [--all] [-t] [--channel] [--refresh] [--strict]`, alias `upgrade`, one tx per target under one run id, planner-side downgrade guard | A1, A2, A3, A6, A9, A10, B4 |
| B7 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.7` | pin and unpin as records-only pin transactions | `pin [--version]`/`unpin` as records-only `pin`-kind transactions on every target that has the addon | A1, A2, A3, A4.1, A4.3, A6, B1, B4 |
| B8 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.8` | status update counts, adoptable count, hints and the list latest column | `status` `updates` and `adoptable`, `update`/`check_updates` recommendations, `list` latest column, the `--cached` budget | A2, B4, B5, B6 |
| B9 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.9` | install --reinstall and installs from the blob cache | `--reinstall` bypassing both no-op checks, the local-blob candidate, the `reinstall` verb fix | A3, B3 |

B7 waits for A4.1 (records-only work and `TxKind::Pin`) and A4.3 (pinning an installed version becomes a records-only `pin` transaction), not for all of A4.
acceptance_criteria: All nine children are closed; update --all over about 30 addons on three targets is under 2 s warm and 10 s cold, fetches each distinct ref once and downloads each distinct asset once (with A8), and one omaddons undo reverts every client's transaction; a full outdated over release.json publishers makes zero api.github.com requests, a repeat inside 15 minutes makes none at all, and an unchanged GitHub ref after the window costs one github.com request; REST exhaustion returns rate_limited with details.reset_at; status --cached shows update counts in under 5 ms with no network; install --reinstall works from the blob cache offline; pins are undoable pin transactions

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this epic, and why first.** Each M2 feature removes a manual chore. This one removes the most frequent chore: today, updating DBM on three clients means three `install` runs, each fetching and downloading separately. After it, `omaddons update` does one fetch, one download and three transactions, and a single `omaddons undo` reverts all three. `status` shows pending counts offline, so the M3 widget can paint a badge without touching the network. The epic lands first because WoW: Forever launches on 2026-11-04 and publishers will then ship Forever builds often. Being able to update every client before that is the most valuable early delivery. It also serves the thesis, that omaddons is the sole, safe, undoable authority over every client's addons: every update is still a journaled transaction per target under one run id.

**One memo, one evaluator.** `outdated`, `update`, `status` and the M3 widget cannot disagree about what is out of date, because they call the same pure function (B4) over the same data, the release memo (B1) (M2-D1). The alternative was a stored result file. It goes stale the moment `update` commits, and it needs a mutating writer for a read command. The memo is derived data in `<cache>/omaddons/`, so deleting it costs only requests. `status` still never writes, and its counts stay right because they are recomputed from records plus the memo. Economy is a design constraint, not an optimisation: the tag-first probe, the memo window, blob facts and (in A8) per-command download de-duplication make repeated and background checks nearly free, which keeps omaddons polite toward volunteer-run services.

**Decisions this epic applies:**
- **M2-D1:** the memo lives in the cache dir.
- **M2-D2:** the tag-first GitHub probe.
- **M2-D3:** `outdated` is metadata-only by default; `--verify` downloads; every confidence counts; verified failures become `blocked`.
- **M2-D4:** bare `update` means `--all`.
- **M2-D5:** `pin`/`unpin` are records-only transactions of kind `pin`.
- **M2-D17:** updates replace locally modified files with a warning, and undo recovers them.
- **M2-D27:** pending updates are not `status` attention.
- **M2-D28:** download de-duplication plus blob facts.
- **M2-D29:** `install X` of a pinned X is a no-op.
- **M2-D31:** URL, file and directory installs are static.
- **M2-D37:** freshness is per command.
- **M2-D38:** undo works per run.
- **M2-D39:** the `check` and `upgrade` aliases.
- **M2-D41:** a non-loading newest release is `blocked`, not failed.
- **M2-D42:** the downgrade guard for TOC-version adoptions.

Each child bead states the decisions it implements, with the reasons and the rejected alternatives.

**GitHub facts this epic relies on** (verified live on 2026-10-15):
- **`releases/latest`** answers `302 Location: …/releases/tag/<tag>` (confirmed for WeakAuras 5.22.1 and BugSack v12.1.7). Reading the tag from that redirect is the cheap probe: one request, no REST.
- **`release.json`** downloads redirect to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, so a full stable fetch is three requests on the wire. That is why the probe halves the cost of a check, and why a changed tag shows two `net.log` lines for its `release.json` fetch.
- **`releases.atom`** carries the 10 latest releases, with full notes as `<content type="html">`, a weak ETag and `cache-control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate`. It cannot tell prereleases apart, so it is not the probe (M2-D2's rejected alternative). D6 uses it for changelogs.
- **REST limits.** Unauthenticated REST allows 60 requests an hour, and omaddons keeps `GITHUB_REST_RESERVE` (5) in reserve. Only beta/alpha channels and repos without `release.json` need REST.
- **Latent defect 2.** On a 304, the validator cache hands the REST budget the cached 200's rate-limit headers. B2 fixes it.

**Risks.**
- The multi-target commit path has never run in production. A6 tests it with an `error@N` failpoint before B6 lands, and A12 makes the run undoable as one.
- Concurrent memo writers lose entries (by design). That costs one request.
- `status --cached` budget creep: the memo is trimmed and capped, the evaluator is pure CPU, and a precomputed memo `brief` is the designed fallback.
- GitHub's undocumented secondary limits: tag-first probes, the window, a per-host cap of 3 and backoff.

**Confidence:** high. The update path (B1–B6) is a thin layer plus a cache over M1's proven fetch → select → verify → transaction pipeline. The request-economy claims are asserted from `net.log` in fixtures and repeated live at the checkpoint (H4).

title: The release memo and ReleaseCache
description:
## Background

Every command that needs release metadata calls `sources::fetch_once` (`src/sources/mod.rs:179`), and it always goes to the network. Its callers are `plan::plan` (`src/engine/plan.rs:291`, so every engine run) and `info` (`src/app/info.rs:286-299`). `install` without `-t` runs the engine twice: a dry-run compatibility probe (`src/app/install.rs:592-605`), then the real run (`:416`). Each run fetches the same refs again. `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` (15 minutes, `src/politeness.rs:34`) is defined and registered, but nothing reads it.

Nothing remembers what a fetch learned, so `outdated` (B5), `status` counts (B8) and a warm `update` (B6) cannot answer without the network, `outdated` followed by `update` would fetch everything twice, dependency rounds (C4.1), Tukui (D4), adoption (E5.1) and search (G1) have no command-wide fetch-once path, and `info --offline` can only answer `latest: null`.

This bead adds the release memo (a cache file) and `ReleaseCache`, the one entry point for every fetch. It serves the M2 goal "current by default": say what is out of date without changing anything, and bring everything current with one command, at the minimum request cost (one fetch per distinct ref per run, a free re-check inside `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL`). It also serves "no regression of M1 guarantees": the memo is derived data, written through fsx, never locked, never able to fail a command.

Found missing during planning: `CachedMeta` (`src/net/validators.rs:24-37`, kind `http_validators`) implements `Versioned` but has no row in `store::KINDS` (`src/state/store.rs:107-133`), the list of persisted formats that M4's `capabilities` and wire-name golden read. It is the only impl missing. This bead adds its row with the memo's.

Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`). The symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The memo file (`src/state/memo.rs`, new)

The file is `<cache>/omaddons/releases.json`, reached through a new `Paths::release_memo()` in `src/state/paths.rs`. Its kind is `release_memo` and its schema is `1.0`. It gets `impl Versioned` and a `store::KINDS` row.

```json
{
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "entries": {
    "gh:deadlybossmods/deadlybossmods|stable": {
      "wanted": {"ref": "gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods", "channel": "stable"},
      "fetched_at": "2026-10-15T20:01:02Z",
      "probe": "12.1.15",
      "set": { "ref": "gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods", "releases": [ { "release_id": "gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods@12.1.15", "version": "12.1.15", "channel": "stable", "published_at": null, "assets": [ … ], "changelog_url": "…" } ] },
      "known": [{"release_id": "gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods@12.1.14", "published_at": null}],
      "failure": null
    }
  },
  "candidates": [
    {"release_id": "gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods@12.1.15", "asset": "DBM-12.1.15.zip",
     "sha256": "…", "size": 4123456,
     "verdicts": [{"rules": "mainline", "interface": 120105, "loads": true, "at": "…"},
                  {"rules": "mists", "interface": 50504, "loads": true, "at": "…"}]}
  ],
  "tukui_list": {"fetched_at": "…", "entries": [{"id": -2, "slug": "elvui", "name": "ElvUI", "author": "…", "version": "16.00", "patch": ["12.1.0", "5.5.4", "1.15.9", "2.5.6"], "directories": ["ElvUI", "ElvUI_Libraries", "ElvUI_Options"], "last_update": "2026-10-13"}]}
}
```

- **Key:** the `Ref` identity, then `|`, then the channel. Identity lowercases the GitHub owner and repo, as `Ref::eq` does. It is `Ref::identity` (`src/model.rs:643`), which is private today: make it `pub(crate)` and use it. D4 later lowercases Tukui slugs in the same function.
  - Pinned-version fetches (`Wanted.version = Some`) are **not** memoised, neither read nor written. They are rare (`--version`, `sync --locked`) and must see the exact release.
- **`set`:** trimmed to the single newest release eligible for the entry's channel (`resolve::select::newest`, `src/resolve/select.rs:99`). That is all `select` looks at without a pin. `ReleaseSet` already derives `Deserialize` (`src/model.rs:869`).
- **`known`:** up to `MEMO_KNOWN_RELEASES` (new limit, 10) other `{release_id, published_at}` pairs the fetch saw, newest first. B4's downgrade guard uses them to detect `Ahead`.
  - Size: a release with a large `release.json` (DBM's per-interface metadata) is about 3 KB once trimmed, so 100 refs come to about 300 KB.
  - If the `status --cached` budget (B8) is threatened, the fallback is a per-entry `brief`, precomputed at write time: the newest `release_id`, version, date, and the candidate rank per family. Do not build it now.
- **`probe`:** a source-specific cheap-check token: the GitHub stable tag, or the git sha. For sources with no probe cheaper than the fetch itself (WoWI, Tukui, git on other hosts) it is the release id. B1 stores the newest `release_id` for every source. B2 makes GitHub store the tag when it adds the probe. Entries written before that mismatch once, cost one full fetch, and are rewritten with the tag.
- **`failure`:** `{code, message, at}`, stored for **non-retryable** upstream failures only (`not_found`, `ref_invalid`). When a failure is stored, `set` is null.
  - These are terminal states, such as a deleted WoWI project or a repository renamed away. `outdated` and `status` must report them as `failed` with a fix (B4), not as "never checked" forever.
  - Retryable failures (`network`, `http_status` 5xx, `rate_limited`) are **never** stored; the next run simply retries.
  - `source_disabled` is **not** stored, because it is local configuration. The evaluator gets the set of enabled sources instead.
- **`candidates`:** facts learned by downloading. The blob SHA-256 and size of `(release_id, asset filename)` make a second download of the same asset unnecessary in any later run, as long as the blob is still cached. Per-client verdicts say whether that asset loads on a rules row and interface; they come from planning. Define the types here, with every field B3's design needs, so the file format is complete from day one: `CandidateFact { release_id, asset, sha256, size, verdicts: Vec<VerdictFact> }` and `VerdictFact { rules, interface, loads, out_of_date, primary_interface, at }`. `out_of_date` defaults to false and `primary_interface` is optional. B3 produces and consumes them.
- **`tukui_list`:** `{fetched_at, entries: [{id, slug, name, author, version, patch, directories, last_update}]}`, the Tukui index for dependency resolution and search (`patch` and `last_update` feed G1's compatibility hints and recency). It holds version metadata only, never URLs. Define it here (optional, absent by default) and merge it. D4 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.4`) owns the entry type (`TukuiIndex`) and fills it.
- **Bounds:** at most `RELEASE_MEMO_MAX_ENTRIES` entries (new limit in `src/limits.rs`, 4,096, not configurable) and at most as many candidate facts. Past the cap, the write drops the oldest: entries by `fetched_at`, candidate facts by their newest verdict `at`.
- **Writes:** an untracked fsx session, `WriteSession::untracked(Writer::Derived, &scopes, "release-memo")`, as `Validating::store` does (`src/net/validators.rs:79-102`); the Cache scope row admits every writer. Merge on write: load the current file; merge per key (newer `fetched_at` wins; candidate facts union, the newer verdict winning per `(rules, interface)`; `tukui_list` by newer `fetched_at`); cap; encode with `store::encode`; then `Op::WriteFile`, which writes a unique temp file and renames it (`write_atomic`, `src/fsx/sys.rs:136`).
  - Two concurrent writers can still lose one writer's newest entry. That is acceptable for a cache: it costs one extra request later. No lock is taken, which keeps vision D24 intact (the global lock is held only for a commit window).
  - Decided: when the file on disk has a newer schema, skip the write and log it at `-v`, so an older binary never clobbers a newer binary's cache. A corrupt file is replaced.
- **Reads are tolerant.** A missing, corrupt or newer-schema memo is treated as empty. That produces a `-v` log line and no warning, because it is a cache. Map every `store::load` error and `VersionStatus::Newer` to empty. A `fetched_at` in the future (clock skew) is treated as stale.
- **Who writes:** every fetch goes through `ReleaseCache`. `install` and `info` refresh the memo from this bead on; `outdated`, `update`, `sync`, `adopt` and `copy` do so as they land. `status` only reads it (B8).

**Why the cache dir and not state (M2-D1).** The memo is derived data. Deleting it costs only requests, which matches the README's promise that deleting `<cache>/omaddons/` is always safe. The fsx State row does not admit `Writer::Derived` (`Scope::admits`, `src/fsx/scope.rs`). Putting the memo in state would mean either widening that row or giving a read command a mutating writer, and both weaken the scope model.

### 2. `ReleaseCache` (`src/resolve/cache.rs`, new)

```rust
pub struct ReleaseCache<'a> { memo: MemoView, http: &'a dyn Http, registry: &'a SourceRegistry, policy: Freshness }
pub enum Freshness {
    Window(Duration),   // answer fresh entries from the memo (SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL)
    Revalidate,         // never answer from the memo alone: probe (reuse the set if unchanged) or fetch
    Refresh,            // --refresh: always fetch
    OfflineOnly,        // --offline: memo only
}
impl ReleaseCache<'_> {
    /// Fetch-once over the whole run: de-duplicates `wanted` (a run-scoped map, so later calls
    /// never refetch the same Wanted), answers per the freshness policy, probes stale entries whose
    /// source supports it, fetches the rest in bounded parallel, and records the results.
    pub fn get(&self, wanted: &[Wanted]) -> BTreeMap<Wanted, Fetched>;
    pub fn persist(self, facts: &[CandidateFact]) -> Vec<Warning>;   // one memo write per command
}
pub struct Fetched { pub set: Result<ReleaseSet>, pub origin: Origin /* Memo | Probed | Fetched | StaleFallback */, pub fetched_at: Timestamp }
```

The run-scoped map needs interior mutability (`Mutex`). Expose a read view of one entry (`MemoEntryView`: set, known, failure, fetched_at) for B4 and B8.

Rules:
1. **Fresh** (`Window`, and `now − fetched_at < SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL`): answer from the memo with no request (`Origin::Memo`). A stored non-retryable `failure` is also answered from the memo inside the window.
2. **Stale, or `Revalidate`, with a probe:** call `Source::probe`. If the token equals the memo's, reuse the memo set and bump `fetched_at` (`Origin::Probed`, one cheap request). Otherwise do a full fetch. B1 leaves this as a hook; B2 adds `Source::probe` and fills it.
3. **Otherwise:** a full `Source::fetch`, batched per source as `fetch_once` does today (`Origin::Fetched`). `fetch_once` stays public: the cache uses it, and the source tests call it.
4. **Offline** (`--offline` or `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, both already in `Context.offline`):
   - every key is answered from the memo regardless of age (`Origin::StaleFallback`), with one `stale_check` warning naming the oldest `fetched_at` used;
   - keys with no memo entry are `unchecked { reason: offline }` for `outdated` and `status`, and item failures with code `offline` for mutating commands;
   - mutating commands may plan from memo entries while offline, but every archive must then come from the blob cache (memo candidate facts, or a record's `blob_sha256`). An item whose archive is not cached fails `offline`. That is what makes `install --reinstall --offline` and `sync --locked --offline` useful: an offline run can never install anything that is not already on disk.
5. **Network failure on a stale key** (`network`, `http_status` 5xx, `rate_limited`):
   - `outdated` falls back to the memo entry with `Origin::StaleFallback` and a per-item warning, and the run is `partial: true`;
   - mutating commands (`update`, `install`, `sync`) do **not** fall back. They report the failure, because installing from stale metadata could pick a release the source withdrew.

   Decided, so that rule 5 is safe by default: `get` never substitutes a stale entry for a failed fetch on its own. It returns the error. A read-only caller that may fall back asks for the stale entry explicitly, for example `ReleaseCache::stale(&Wanted) -> Option<Fetched>`. B5 uses that; mutating commands never do. `info` keeps its M1 behaviour on a failed fetch (`partial`, `latest: null`, the error mirrored as a warning; `tests/info_netlog.rs:118-151`).

**Freshness per command (M2-D37):**

| Command | Freshness | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `outdated`, `update`, `sync`, `copy`, `adopt`, `search` (Tukui list) | `Window` | `outdated` followed by `update` must be free; these are the batch commands the economy targets are about |
| `install` | `Revalidate` | Someone installing *now* expects *now*'s release. M1's `tests/install.rs:183-208` (switch the fixture to v2, then `install Foo` updates) keeps passing. A GitHub probe still makes an unchanged tag cost one request with no `release.json` refetch |
| `info` | `Window` | Read-only; two `info` calls in a row cost one fetch |
| any command with `--refresh` | `Refresh` | explicit |
| any command with `--offline` | `OfflineOnly` | explicit; `--offline` wins over `--refresh` |

This bead wires `install` and `info`. Each later command picks its row when it lands. Two M1 behaviours change on purpose: `info --offline` answers `latest` from the memo with `stale_check` instead of `latest: null`, and `info` inside the window does not re-fetch.

### 3. Wiring

- `PlanCtx` (`src/engine/plan.rs:93`) and `EngineCtx` (`src/engine/tx.rs:102`) gain `cache: &ReleaseCache`. `plan::plan` calls `ctx.cache.get(&to_fetch)` in place of `fetch_once` and reads `Fetched.set`. Update every construction site: `src/engine/tx.rs` (two `PlanCtx`), `src/app/engine.rs`, `src/engine/testing.rs` and `tests/plan.rs`. `rejudge` under the lock stays offline and never calls the cache.
- `ReleaseCache` borrows the `Http` and `SourceRegistry` that `app::engine::Engine` (`src/app/engine.rs:21`) owns, so it cannot live inside `Engine` without a self-reference. Expose accessors on `Engine`, build the cache in the command, and pass `&ReleaseCache` to `Engine::run`. Keep one cache per command, so that `install`'s probe run and its real run share the run-scoped map and fetch each ref once.
- `info` builds its cache with `Window` (or `Refresh` or `OfflineOnly`) instead of calling `fetch_once`.
- Add `--refresh` to `InstallArgs` (`src/app/install.rs:39`) and `InfoArgs` (`src/app/info.rs:33`), with help text.
- `persist` runs once, after the command's last engine run. Its warnings join the outcome. Its `-v` notes (tolerant loads, skipped writes) go back to the command, and `app::dispatch` logs them with `reporter.log(LogLevel::Debug, …)`, as it does for `status`'s discovery line (`src/app/mod.rs:107-122`).
- New warning code `stale_check` in `src/error.rs` (`warning_codes!`). D2 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.2`) also emits it and neither bead blocks the other, so whichever of B1 and D2 lands first registers it and the other reuses it. Registering it raises the `WarningCode::ALL` count asserted at `src/error.rs:746` by one (22 at `e902d36`; A3 and D2 may already have raised it). The fix is per warning instance: B1's offline answers use the guard's existing text, "run without --offline and with OMADDONS_OFFLINE unset" (`src/net/guard.rs:93-95`); D2's failed-refresh fallback uses its own text.
- New limits `RELEASE_MEMO_MAX_ENTRIES` (4,096) and `MEMO_KNOWN_RELEASES` (10) in `src/limits.rs`. Each needs a `REGISTRY` row and an entry in the `LIMIT_NAMES` test list, and the `limit_registries` snapshot changes (review it).

**Files:** new `src/state/memo.rs`, new `src/resolve/cache.rs`, `src/state/mod.rs`, `src/resolve/mod.rs`, `src/state/paths.rs`, `src/state/store.rs` (`KINDS`), `src/limits.rs`, `src/model.rs` (`Ref::identity` visibility), `src/error.rs`, `src/engine/plan.rs`, `src/engine/tx.rs`, `src/engine/testing.rs`, `src/app/engine.rs`, `src/app/info.rs`, `src/app/install.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs`, `src/sources/mod.rs` (doc comment), `tests/info_netlog.rs`, `tests/plan.rs`, `tests/common/home.rs` (`Home::seed_memo`), new `tests/release_cache.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two `info dbm` calls within 15 minutes make one set of requests (`net.log` count). With `--refresh`, the second call fetches again.
- `install Foo` after the fixture switches to v2 updates, exactly as `tests/install.rs:183-208` expects (`Revalidate`).
- `--offline info dbm` after an earlier fetch answers `latest` from the memo with a `stale_check` warning. With no earlier fetch it answers `latest: null`. Neither makes a request.
- A non-retryable `not_found` is stored as `failure` and answered from the memo inside the window. A `network` error, a 5xx `http_status` or `rate_limited` is never stored.
- A corrupt memo file is ignored without error, and the next fetching command rewrites it valid.
- Two `info` processes writing at the same time leave a valid memo that contains at least one writer's entries.
- The memo never exceeds `RELEASE_MEMO_MAX_ENTRIES` (unit test with a cap override).
- A pinned-version `Wanted` is never read from or written to the memo.
- `install` without `-t` on two live targets fetches each ref once across its probe run and its real run.
- `store::KINDS` lists `release_memo` and `http_validators`.
- The existing `install` tests pass, and `fetch_once` semantics hold within a run.

## Test Plan

- **Unit** (`src/state/memo.rs`, `src/resolve/cache.rs`): merge rules; trimming (newest eligible release, at most 10 `known`); caps through a cap parameter; the freshness decision per policy; key identity (`gh:DBM/X` and `gh:dbm/x` are one key, channels are separate keys); a future `fetched_at` is stale; which failures are stored; the pinned bypass; run-scoped de-duplication with a counting fake `Source`, as in the `src/sources/mod.rs` tests.
- **E2E** (`tests/release_cache.rs`, `tests/info_netlog.rs`): request counts from `net.log` (`tests/common/netlog.rs`: `read_net_log`, `count_host`); the new `Home::seed_memo(entries)` writes `releases.json` with chosen `fetched_at` values (and optional candidate facts, which B4, B5 and B6 tests use to seed `blocked` and `verified` cases), so freshness tests need no clock seam; offline; corrupt-file recovery; two spawned `info` processes (`Home::spawn`); `install`'s fetch count across its two engine runs.
- Update `tests/info_netlog.rs:80-91`: offline `info` now answers from the memo with `stale_check`, and `latest: null` only without an entry.
- SHOULD: a source-scan test, in the style of `tests/single_writer.rs`, asserting that every `impl Versioned for` in `src/` has a `KINDS` row. It would have caught the missing `http_validators` row.

## Considerations

- The memo is a cache. Its absence, corruption or a failed write must never fail a command. Keep it small, because `status --cached` reads it on every widget refresh (B8 budgets that read under 5 ms with realistically sized sets).
- Keep the freshness decision pure (pass `now` in). Rule 5 is a safety rule: a mutating command never installs from stale metadata.
- Collision hot spots: `src/engine/plan.rs` (also edited by A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3 and C4.x) and `tests/common/home.rs` (A10).

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: none (can start immediately).

Unblocks:
- B2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.2` (GitHub tag-first probe and conditional feeds): it fills rule 2's probe hook and the memo's `probe` token, and its tests age entries with `Home::seed_memo`.
- B3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.3` (Candidate facts): it fills the memo's `candidates` slot defined here and reads it through `PlanCtx.cache`.
- B4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.4` (The update-status evaluator): it evaluates records against `MemoEntryView` (set, known, failure, fetched_at).
- B7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.7` (pin and unpin): `pin --version` plans through the cache, and `unpin` says what `update` would install from the memo with no network.
- C4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1` (Dependency rounds on install): each round calls `ReleaseCache::get` with only the new refs, and the run-scoped map keeps fetch-once across rounds.
- D4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.4` (The Tukui source): it fills `tukui_list`, memoises Tukui version metadata and adds the `ReleaseCache::tukui_list()` getter.
- E5.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.1` (adopt report mode): its exactness check fetches identified refs through the cache (`Window`) and reads the Tukui list.
- G1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.7.1` (The search command): it reads the Tukui list from the memo under `Window`.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** Every update feature in M2 rests on one shared record of "what is the newest release of this ref, and when did we learn it". With it, `outdated` followed by `update` costs one round of requests instead of two, a repeat check inside 15 minutes costs nothing, `status --cached` can show update counts with no network, and dependency rounds, adoption and search share one fetch-once path per command. Putting every fetch behind `ReleaseCache` also makes the economy claims checkable from `net.log` in fixtures rather than from timing. The project's thesis is that omaddons is the sole, safe, undoable authority over every client's addons; that is only practical if checking is cheap enough to run often, and polite enough toward volunteer-run upstreams.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D1.** Update-check results live in a release memo in the cache dir, and `status --cached` derives its counts from it with the pure evaluator (B4). `status` still never writes. Why: derived data belongs in the cache, where deleting it is safe, and the State scope does not admit derived writers. Counts stay right after `update` because they are recomputed from records plus the memo. Rejected: an `outdated.json` result file in state, which would need a mutating writer for a read command and goes stale the moment `update` commits.
- **M2-D37.** Freshness is per command: `install` revalidates (probe or fetch); batch commands and `info` use the 15-minute window. Why: installs see *now*'s release, so M1's install-then-update test keeps passing, and `outdated` followed by `update` is free. Rejected: one window for every command, which would make `install` silently install a release up to 15 minutes old.
- **Rule 5:** no stale fallback for mutating commands, because installing from stale metadata could pick a release the source withdrew. To make that the default, `get` never falls back by itself, and read-only callers ask for a stale entry explicitly.
- **Fix folded in:** the missing `http_validators` row in `store::KINDS`, found during planning.
- **Decided while writing this bead:**
  - B1 defines the full `CandidateFact`/`VerdictFact` types and the `tukui_list` slot, so the file format does not change when B3 and D4 land;
  - B1 adds the `MEMO_KNOWN_RELEASES` limit (10), which the plan's contract table lists without naming an owner;
  - a newer-schema memo on disk is never overwritten;
  - `stale_check` is registered by whichever of B1 and D2 lands first (they share it and neither blocks the other), and B1's offline answers reuse the guard's existing offline text fix;
  - the `tukui_list` slot carries the eight fields D4 decodes (including `patch` and `last_update`, which G1 needs), so search adds no field later;
  - `info` keeps M1's behaviour when a fetch fails.

**Facts verified during planning** (code at `e902d36`):
- `fetch_once` (`src/sources/mod.rs:179`) always hits the network. It is called from `plan.rs:291` and `info.rs:296`, and `install` without `-t` plans twice (`install.rs:592-605`, then `:416`).
- `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` is 15 minutes (`politeness.rs:34`), registered and unused.
- The Cache scope admits every writer, while State admits only `Mutating`, `Undo`, `Backup`, `BackupRestore` and `Doctor` (`fsx/scope.rs`).
- `Op::WriteFile` is atomic: it writes a unique temp file and renames it (`fsx/sys.rs:136`).
- `ReleaseSet` derives `Deserialize`.
- `Ref::identity` (`model.rs:643`) is the lowercase identity behind `Eq` and `Ord`.
- `tests/info_netlog.rs:80-91` asserts `latest: null` offline today.
- On GitHub's stable path, an unchanged ref costs two fetches (three requests on the wire, because `release.json` redirects to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Concurrent memo writers lose entries: likely by design, low impact. A lost entry costs one request. Merge-on-write keeps losses small, and tests assert validity, not completeness.
- `status --cached` budget creep: the memo is trimmed to one release per key and capped, and a precomputed per-entry `brief` is designed in as a fallback.
- Changing `PlanCtx`/`EngineCtx` touches every engine test helper. The crash, concurrency and undo suites are the regression net.

The plan rates the update path (B1–B6) **high** confidence: it is a thin layer plus a cache over M1's proven fetch → select → verify → transaction pipeline, and its request economy is asserted from `net.log`.

title: GitHub tag-first probe and conditional feeds
description:
## Background

Even when nothing changed, the GitHub stable path costs two fetches per ref. First, `latest_tag` requests `releases/latest` with manual redirects and reads the tag from the 302 (`src/sources/github.rs:187-247`, purpose `release-latest`). Then `release_json` fetches `releases/download/<tag>/release.json` (`:251-263`, purpose `release-json`), which GitHub redirects to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`. That is three requests on the wire per ref, on every check. The M2 checkpoint wants an unchanged ref, once B1's 15-minute memo window has passed, to cost exactly one `github.com` request and zero REST. B1's `ReleaseCache` leaves a probe hook in its rule 2 ("stale, or `Revalidate`, with a probe"); this bead fills it for GitHub.

Two smaller gaps sit in the same layer:
- **The git source's commits feed never revalidates.** `head()` in `src/sources/git_github.rs:102-130` builds `Request::get(url, "commits-atom")` (`:110`) without `validators`. Every check of a `git:` ref on GitHub therefore downloads the feed again, changed or not.
- **Latent defect 2: a 304 returns the cached 200's headers.** On a 304, `Validating` drops the 304 response and rebuilds one from the stored `meta.headers` (`src/net/validators.rs:123-133`). `GithubRest::send` (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:115-135`) passes that response to `Budget::update`, which then reads stale `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. Only the beta/alpha release-list path uses validators on REST (`list`, `github_rest.rs:137-170`, `req.validators = true` at `:141`), so only it is affected. There, the budget can believe requests remain when they do not, or the reverse.

Goal served: G-M2-1 "current by default". Checking must cost the minimum: a free re-check inside `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL`, then one request per unchanged ref, and no GitHub REST for `release.json` publishers (M2 checkpoint 2, "zero-REST checks").

Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`). The symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

### Trait evolution (`src/sources/mod.rs`, `Source` at `:85`)

The M2 shape of the trait is below. This bead adds `probe`; A8 adds `resolve_asset` and D6 adds `changelog`. Default methods keep every existing source compiling unchanged.

```rust
pub trait Source: Send + Sync {
    fn id(&self) -> SourceId;
    fn fetch(&self, wanted: &[Wanted], http: &dyn Http) -> Vec<Result<ReleaseSet>>;      // unchanged
    /// A cheap freshness token for `wanted`, when cheaper than fetch (GitHub stable: the tag from the 302).
    fn probe(&self, _wanted: &Wanted, _http: &dyn Http) -> Option<Result<String>> { None }   // NEW (B2)
    /// The concrete URL and hash rule of a Deferred asset, fetched immediately before download.
    fn resolve_asset(&self, _key: &str, _http: &dyn Http) -> Result<ResolvedAsset> { Err(internal) } // NEW (A8)
    /// Release notes for releases of `r` newer than `since` (exclusive), newest first, at most `limit`.
    fn changelog(&self, _r: &Ref, _since: Option<&str>, _limit: usize, _http: &dyn Http) -> Option<Result<Changelog>> { None } // NEW (D6)
}
pub struct ResolvedAsset { pub url: String, pub expected_hash: Option<ExpectedHash>,
                           pub hash_from_header: Option<HashFromHeader /* EtagMd5 */>, pub canonical_url: Option<String> }
```

D3 later changes `SourceRegistry::builtin()` to take the source enable flags. B2 does not touch the registry.

### Probes (per source)

- **GitHub stable, unpinned:** the existing `releases/latest` request with manual redirects, returning the tag. It costs one request and no REST.
  - On a match, the memo's set and its `release.json` metadata are reused. This is the "tag-first" economy (M2-D2).
  - On a mismatch, the full fetch costs one `release.json` fetch. Live, that is two `net.log` lines, because of the redirect to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`.
- **git on GitHub:** the commits feed is already a single request. B2 sets `validators = true` on it, so an unchanged branch can come back as a 304 when GitHub sends an ETag. There is no separate probe.
- **WoWI and Tukui** (D3, D4): no probe. Their fetch is already one batched request for every ref.

### `GithubSource::probe` (`src/sources/github.rs`)

- Only `Wanted { channel: Stable, version: None }` gets a probe. Every other wish returns `None`: beta and alpha go through the REST list, which already revalidates, and pinned versions are never memoised.
- The probe calls `latest_tag` (`:187`), which already follows repository renames, and returns `Some(Ok(tag))`. Errors come back as `Some(Err(e))`. `ReleaseCache` handles a probe error exactly like a fetch error for that key: a 404 `not_found` is stored as the entry's failure, and 5xx, `network` or `rate_limited` errors are never stored.
- **A mismatch MUST NOT request `releases/latest` a second time.** Otherwise a changed tag costs four lines instead of three. `GithubSource` keeps each probe's result for the run, `(base, tag)` keyed by ref identity, in a `Mutex<BTreeMap<…>>`; the registry is built per command, so this lives exactly one run. `fetch_one` (`:74`) then uses the remembered pair instead of calling `latest_tag`. Keep `base`: after a rename it points at the new repository.
- **The stored token is the tag.** `release_set` builds `release_id` as `<ref>@<tag>` (`github.rs:289`), and the REST path does the same (`github_rest.rs:247`). Take the tag from the probe when one ran, otherwise derive it from the newest release's id. Entries B1 wrote (whose token is the release id) mismatch once and are rewritten.

### Rule 2 in `ReleaseCache` (`src/resolve/cache.rs`, from B1)

- A probe runs only for a memo entry that has a `set`: a stale entry under `Window`, or any entry under `Revalidate`. A missing entry, or one holding only a stored failure, gets a full fetch. `Refresh` never probes, and `OfflineOnly` never touches the network.
- Probes run in bounded parallel (`net::run_bounded`, `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`) through the same network stack, so `Limited` caps them at 3 per host (`MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST`).
- An equal token reuses the memo set and bumps `fetched_at` (`Origin::Probed`). A different token leads to a full fetch, batched per source (`Origin::Fetched`).

### Commits feed (`src/sources/git_github.rs:110`)

Set `req.validators = true`. `Validating` then sends `If-None-Match` and answers a 304 from `<cache>/omaddons/http/`. It is one request either way, and the stored token for git refs is the sha.

### The 304 fix (`src/net/validators.rs`)

The plan allowed two fixes. Decided: merge in `Validating`. On a 304 for a cached entry, return the cached status and body with the cached headers **overlaid by the 304's own header fields** (a field present in the 304 replaces the stored field of the same name, compared case-insensitively), the way HTTP caches refresh stored headers. `X-RateLimit-*` then come from the 304, `Budget::update` stays unchanged, and the response keeps `CacheState::Revalidated`. Rejected: having `GithubRest` skip `Budget::update` for revalidated responses. It would leave the budget at its previous value rather than the server's current one, and the acceptance below asks for the 304's numbers.

### REST exhaustion (checkpoint test only)

The behaviour already exists in M1. `GithubRest::send` refuses when `Budget::allows()` is false, meaning remaining is at or below `GITHUB_REST_RESERVE` (5, `src/politeness.rs:43`). It then returns `rate_limited` with `details.reset_at` and a text fix naming `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN`. The budget is per run and starts unknown, so the first REST request of a run is always sent, and the refusal applies to the next one (`tests/sources_github_rest.rs:167-218` shows this at the source level). B2 adds the end-to-end checkpoint test through the CLI.

**Files:** `src/sources/mod.rs`, `src/sources/github.rs`, `src/sources/git_github.rs`, `src/net/validators.rs`, `src/resolve/cache.rs`, `src/sources/github_rest.rs` (doc comment only, unless the merge needs more), `tests/release_cache.rs`, `tests/sources_github.rs`, `tests/git_github.rs`, `tests/sources_github_rest.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Install N GitHub stable refs on one target, then re-run `install` of the same refs (`Revalidate`) with every tag unchanged. The re-run makes exactly N `github.com` requests, all with purpose `release-latest`, zero `release-json` fetches, and zero `api.github.com` requests (`net.log`).
- With an aged memo entry (`Home::seed_memo`, `fetched_at` older than 15 minutes) and an unchanged tag, `info <ref>` makes exactly one `github.com` request (`release-latest`) and bumps `fetched_at`, so a second `info` inside the window makes none.
- A changed tag adds exactly one `release.json` fetch for that ref and never a second `releases/latest`. With a fixture that models GitHub's redirect to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` (as the recorded `tests/fixtures/http/github-stable/` scenario does), that fetch is two `net.log` lines. With the synthetic `gh_release` fixture, which serves `release.json` directly, it is one.
- A probe 404 is stored like a fetch 404 (`not_found` failure). A 5xx probe is never stored.
- A second fetch of a `git:` ref on GitHub whose commits feed is unchanged (ETag) is answered through a 304, with `CacheState::Revalidated`, and yields an identical set.
- A 304 on the REST release list computes the budget from the 304's headers. Unit test with crafted headers: the cached 200 says remaining 50, the 304 says 3, so the budget is 3 and the next REST request is refused.
- One command with two beta-channel refs, whose first REST response carries `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 5`, fails the second ref with `rate_limited` and `details.reset_at`. `net.log` shows exactly one `api.github.com` line.
- The existing GitHub, git and REST source tests pass.

## Test Plan

- **Unit, `src/resolve/cache.rs`** (the probe decision table):
  - a fresh entry gets no probe;
  - a stale or `Revalidate` entry with a set gets a probe;
  - an equal token gives `Probed`;
  - a different token gives `Fetched`, with no second `releases/latest`;
  - no entry, or a stored failure, gets a full fetch;
  - `Refresh` fetches;
  - `OfflineOnly` makes no request;
  - a pinned wish is fetched and never memoised.
- **Unit, `src/sources/github.rs`**, with the existing `Canned` fake (`:387-418`): an unpinned stable wish gives the tag; a rename is followed; beta, alpha and pinned wishes give `None`.
- **Unit, `src/net/validators.rs`**, with its `Fake` (`:171-191`): the 304 header merge.
- **E2E with `net.log` counts:**
  - A10's `net_log(home)` counters by host and purpose;
  - A10's `gh_release_v` and `gh_latest`, to re-point `releases/latest` at a new tag without clobbering the old fixtures;
  - `home.scenario(...)` switches between commands, because replay sequences restart in every process (`replay.rs:6-7`);
  - B1's `Home::seed_memo` for aged entries.
- H4 repeats these scenarios live.

## Considerations

- Probes go through the same `Limited` layer, at 3 per host, which also respects GitHub's undocumented secondary limits.
- Do not probe with the Atom feed. It cannot tell prereleases apart, which is why M2-D2 rejected it.
- A probe replaces a fetch only when a memo set exists to reuse. It never adds a request to a cold check, because the full fetch performs the same `releases/latest` request anyway.
- `Budget` is per run. Do not persist it: the server's headers are the authority.
- Collision hot spots:
  - `src/sources/mod.rs` (A8 adds `resolve_asset`, D3 changes `builtin()`, D6 adds `changelog`);
  - `src/sources/github.rs` (D6's Atom content);
  - `src/resolve/cache.rs` (B1, B3, D4).

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A10 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.10` (M2 test helpers): the request-counting tests need its `net_log(home)` counters by host and purpose, and its `gh_release_v`/`gh_latest` fixtures that re-point `releases/latest` at a new tag without clobbering earlier fixtures.
- B1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.1` (The release memo and ReleaseCache): the probe hook in rule 2, the memo's `probe` field, and `Home::seed_memo` for aged entries.

Unblocks:
- H3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.3` (Performance budgets and bench recipes): its request-economy assertions require that, after the window, unchanged tags log exactly N `release-latest` lines and no `release-json`.
- H4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.4` (Live probes for M2): it repeats this economy live, with `outdated` over the whole catalog and an aged memo making exactly one `github.com` request per unchanged GitHub ref.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** Once B1's 15-minute window expires, every check of a GitHub stable ref would otherwise cost the full fetch again: `releases/latest`, then `release.json` and its redirect hop, so three requests on the wire per ref. The tag-first probe cuts an unchanged ref to one `github.com` request with no REST. That is what makes background checks by the M3 widget polite enough to run every few hours. It matters most for the owner after WoW: Forever launches on 2026-11-04, when publishers will ship builds often and `outdated` will run constantly. It keeps omaddons a good citizen toward GitHub's undocumented secondary limits, and it is the mechanism behind the M2 checkpoint "zero-REST checks". The two smaller fixes in this bead are a latent defect and a missed economy in the same validator layer.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D2, tag-first GitHub probe.** A stale entry costs one `releases/latest` request, and `release.json` is fetched only when the tag changed. Why: this halves the cost of a check with zero REST, and the memo holds the metadata for unchanged tags. Rejected:
  - always re-fetching `release.json`, which doubles the cost of every check;
  - the Atom feed, which cannot tell prereleases apart, so a beta tag could look like a new stable release.
- **Latent defect 2** (from the plan's code review): a 304 hands `GithubRest`'s budget the cached 200's rate-limit headers. The plan allowed either fix, as long as it was tested. Decided: merge the 304's header fields over the stored ones in `Validating`, because the acceptance needs the budget to reflect the 304's own numbers. Skipping the budget update would leave it at stale values.
- **Decided while writing this bead:**
  - after a mismatched probe, `GithubSource` reuses the probed `(base, tag)` for the run, so a changed tag never costs a second `releases/latest`;
  - a probe error is handled like a fetch error for that key, so a 404 is stored and a 5xx never is.

**Facts verified** (live on 2026-10-15, and in the code at `e902d36`):
- `releases/latest` answers `302 Location: …/releases/tag/<tag>`. This was confirmed for WeakAuras 5.22.1 and BugSack v12.1.7.
- `release.json` downloads redirect to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, which is on the allowlist (`src/net/allowlist.rs:12`). The recorded `tests/fixtures/http/github-stable/` scenario carries that hop; the synthetic `gh_release` fixture serves `release.json` directly.
- `releases.atom` has a weak ETag and `cache-control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate`, which is why the feed paths use validators.
- `latest_tag` already follows repository renames (`github.rs:187-247`).
- REST quotas:
  - unauthenticated REST allows 60 requests an hour;
  - `GITHUB_REST_RESERVE` is 5;
  - the per-run budget starts unknown, so the first REST request of a run is always sent (`github_rest.rs:115-135`);
  - `rate_limited` carries `details.reset_at`.
- `Validating` drops the 304 and rebuilds the response from `meta.headers` (`validators.rs:123-133`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- GitHub could change how `releases/latest` redirects. `latest_tag` already fails with a clear `http_status` or internal error naming the endpoint, and H4's live probes catch the change at the checkpoint.
- Secondary limits: probes go through the per-host cap of 3 with backoff, and the memo window keeps repeat checks free.
- A wrong token comparison would silently serve stale sets. The probe decision table is unit-tested, and the E2E tests assert on `net.log` lines, not on timing.

Confidence: **high**. The request-economy claims are asserted from `net.log` in fixtures and repeated live by H4.

**done:** the GitHub tag-first probe in the release cache's rule 2, conditional commits feeds for `git:` on GitHub, and the 304 header merge. Also, REST requests are serialized so one command's parallel prerelease fetches share one budget. `argc gate` passes: 1155 tests, 0 failed, ubs 0 critical.

**What landed:**
- **`Source::probe(&self, &Wanted, &dyn Http) -> Option<Result<String>>`** (`src/sources/mod.rs`): default `None`, delegated through the `Arc` impl.
- **`GithubSource::probe`** (`src/sources/github.rs`):
  - Only stable wishes without a version get one. It is `latest_tag` alone: one `releases/latest` request, renames followed, no REST.
  - It returns the token `<ref>@<tag>`, which is the newest release id `release_set` and REST build.
  - `GithubSource.probed: Mutex<BTreeMap<identity, (base, tag)>>` keeps each probe's answer for the run. `fetch_one` takes it (`remove`) instead of asking `releases/latest` again, keeping the renamed base.
  - The new `GithubSource::with_rest` constructor replaces the struct literals, because `probed` is private.
- **`ReleaseCache`** (`src/resolve/cache.rs`):
  - `Decision::Probe` is taken for a remembered entry with a set and a probe token, under `Window` (stale) or `Revalidate`. `Refresh` fetches; `OfflineOnly` answers stale without the network; a stored failure, or nothing remembered, is fetched.
  - `ReleaseCache::probe` runs probes in bounded parallel (`run_bounded`, `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`, through the same stack, so `Limited` applies).
  - An equal token answers `Probed` with the remembered set and bumps `fetched_at` in the learned memo.
  - A probe error is the fetch's: it is remembered exactly when `MemoEntry::of` would remember a fetch error (`not_found`, yes; 5xx or network, no).
  - A different token, or a source without a probe, goes to the batched fetch.
- **`git_github.rs`:** the commits-feed request sets `validators = true`.
- **`Validating`** (`src/net/validators.rs`): on a 304, the cached headers are overlaid by the 304's own (`merge_headers`, names ignoring ASCII case), so `X-RateLimit-*` are the server's current numbers. `CacheState::Revalidated` is kept.
- **`GithubRest`** (`src/sources/github_rest.rs`): a `gate: Mutex<()>` is held across each API request, so the next one sees the budget the last answer left. Parallel fetches previously all passed an unknown budget.
- **`ItemError` details** (`src/app/outcome.rs`): besides within-transaction conflicts, an item error keeps `{reset_at}` from a rate limit.
- **README:** the `outdated` paragraph describes the probe economy and the git 304.

**Tests:**
- **Unit, `resolve::cache`:**
  - The probe decision table: fresh Window is Memo; stale Window is Probe; Revalidate (even fresh) is Probe; a stored failure is Fetch; Refresh is Fetch; Offline is StaleFallback.
  - An equal token gives `Probed` with no fetch and a bumped `fetched_at`, then Memo; Revalidate probes; offline never probes; a moved token is `Fetched`.
  - A probe `not_found` replaces the set with the failure; a network error leaves the set.
- **Unit, `sources::github`:** probe and fetch through a rename ask `releases/latest` once each per URL and fetch from the renamed repository; the token equals the release id. Beta, alpha and pinned wishes get no probe.
- **Unit, `net::validators`:** a 304 refreshes `x-ratelimit-remaining` (50 becomes 3), keeps fields it lacks, and has no duplicate field.
- **`tests/release_cache.rs`:**
  - Re-installing 3 unchanged gh refs is exactly 3 `github.com`/`release-latest` lines.
  - An aged (20 min) entry with an unchanged tag makes `info` do one `release-latest` and bump `fetched_at`; the next `info` makes 0 requests.
  - A moved tag is exactly `release-latest` plus `release-json` (synthetic fixture).
  - A probe 404 stores `not_found` (the next `info` makes no request); a 503 probe leaves `fetched_at` unchanged.
- **`tests/sources_github.rs`:** in-process over the recorded `github-stable` scenario, a WeakAuras entry remembered at an older tag gives `Fetched` 5.22.1 with exactly one `release-latest`, `github.com` 2 lines plus `release-assets` 1 (the redirect), and no REST.
- **`tests/git_github.rs`:** a feed with an ETag, then a 304, gives an identical set and statuses `[200, 304]`.
- **`tests/sources_github_rest.rs`:**
  - A 304 on the release list takes the budget from its own headers (50 then 3), and the next REST request is refused.
  - In one `install --channel beta` of two refs whose first answer says remaining 5, exactly one item fails `rate_limited` with `details.reset_at` and one installs; `net.log` has one `api.github.com` line.
- **`tests/outdated.rs`:** `requests` is now `{fetched 3, probed 2}` (the two unchanged tags are probed) with 3 `release-json` lines; the snapshot `outdated_three_clients` was reviewed.
- The existing GitHub, git and REST source tests pass.

**decided:**
- The probe token is the newest release id `<ref>@<tag>`, the shape `MemoEntry.probe` already stores, rather than the bare tag. Existing memo entries therefore compare as they are, with no rewrite.
- REST API requests of a run are sent one at a time, so the reserve is honoured under parallel fetches.
- Rate-limited item errors keep `details.reset_at` (additive).
- A probe error answers the wish directly; no fetch follows a failed probe.

**Wire names:** no new codes, warnings or constants. `outdated`'s `requests.probed` now counts probes. `data.items[].error.details.reset_at` is new on rate-limited items.

title: Candidate facts: verdicts and blob hashes in the memo
description:
## Background

Planning already downloads, inspects and verifies every candidate it tries (`TargetPlanner::try_candidate`, `src/engine/plan.rs:1018-1093`). Then it forgets what it learned. `download(url, expected)` (`:1121-1150`) skips the network only when the source supplies an expected SHA-256 and that blob is cached (`:1123-1127`). Only GitHub's REST path supplies one (`zip_asset`, `src/sources/github_rest.rs:346-364`). Every `release.json` asset has `expected_hash: None` (`src/sources/github.rs:275`), and so do git, url and local assets. Three later needs depend on the results:

- **`outdated` (B5).** It needs to know whether a newer release has already proved not to load on a client. With that it reports `blocked`, instead of advertising the same update forever.
- **Warm updates (B6) and adoption's exactness check (E5.1).** They need the SHA-256 of an asset that was already downloaded, so they can skip the download.
- **`install --reinstall` (B9) and `sync --locked` (F3.2).** They need the same facts to work offline.

This bead records candidate facts in B1's memo and uses them. It serves the M2 goal "current by default": each distinct archive is downloaded at most once per run, and not at all when an earlier command already cached it. A release that is known not to load on a client stops being advertised as an update.

Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`). The symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

### Candidate facts

- **`Plan` gains `facts: Vec<CandidateFact>`.** Mark it `#[serde(skip)]`: `Plan` (`src/engine/plan.rs:112`) is serialised as dry-run output, and facts are internal. B1 already defines both types in `src/state/memo.rs`; this bead produces and consumes them.

  ```rust
  pub struct CandidateFact { pub release_id: String, pub asset: String, pub sha256: String, pub size: u64,
                             pub verdicts: Vec<VerdictFact> }
  pub struct VerdictFact { pub rules: String, pub interface: u32, pub loads: bool, pub out_of_date: bool,
                           pub primary_interface: Option<u32>, pub at: Timestamp }
  ```

  - `out_of_date` is the verdict's flag.
  - `primary_interface` is the highest in-family interface of the primary folder's loaded TOC.
  - B4's downgrade guard for adopted (TOC-version) records uses both.
- **`download()` changes signature.** It takes the `release_id` and the asset filename as well as the URL and expected hash, so it can look facts up and record them. Today it is `download(url, expected)`. A8 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.8`) needs the same two parameters for its `DownloadMemo` key; whichever of A8 and B3 lands first adds them.
- **Dry runs record facts too.** A dry run downloads anyway, as in M1, so its facts are true.
- **Commands pass facts to `ReleaseCache::persist`.**

### The two uses

- **Downloads skip the network.** Before downloading `(release_id, asset)`, the planner asks the memo for a known `sha256`. If `blobs/<sha256>` exists, it uses that blob.
  - This makes a warm `update` free of downloads, and lets multi-target updates share archives across runs.
  - It also lets `--reinstall` and `sync --locked` work offline when the blob is cached.
  - A fact never replaces the existence check: blob eviction makes facts stale.
- **The update status learns from failures.** If the newest release failed TOC verification on a client (every candidate `loads: false`), `outdated` reports `blocked` for that client instead of advertising the update again (B4).

### Implementation

1. **`download(&self, release_id, asset, url, expected) -> Result<BlobRef>`.** `BlobRef` (`src/engine/blobs.rs:39`) carries `sha256`, `size` and `path`. Steps, in order:
   1. the expected-SHA-256 fast path, as today;
   2. the memo fact for `(release_id, asset)`: `ctx.blobs.get(ctx.scopes, &fact.sha256)` (`blobs.rs:171`); use the blob when it is present;
   3. the network, as today (retry once on `hash_mismatch`). Afterwards, record `sha256` and `size`.

   The order is fixed for later work as well: A8 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.8`) inserts its per-command `DownloadMemo` before the facts lookup, giving `DownloadMemo`, then memo facts and the blob cache, then the network. Keep the facts lookup ahead of any URL resolution, so A8's deferred (Tukui token) assets skip resolution when their blob is cached.
2. **Record a verdict per downloaded candidate.** In `try_candidate`, for `AssetLocation::Url` candidates only, add a `VerdictFact` for `(self.target.rules.name, self.target.interface)` once `verify`, `partition` and `accepts` have run:
   - `loads`: whether the candidate was accepted. A wrong-flavor result (`Ok(Err(reason))`) gives `loads: false`.
   - `out_of_date`: the primary folder's `Verdict::Compatible { out_of_date }` (`src/toc/loaded.rs:266-278`).
   - `primary_interface`: the highest interface of the primary folder's loaded TOC that lies in the target's family range. `judge` computes exactly this as `best` (`src/toc/loaded.rs:354-385`) but does not expose it. Extract it into a shared helper. B4's installed-side reader must compute the installed folder's value with the same function, or the display and the planner would disagree.

   Download errors, unreadable archives and `LocalZip`, `LocalDir` and `GitCheckout` candidates record nothing: none of them has a downloaded `(release_id, asset)` identity.
3. **Merge facts in the plan.** `Plan.facts` gathers every target's facts, merged per `(release_id, asset)`, with the newer `at` winning per `(rules, interface)`. The engine returns the plan inside `TxOutcomes` (`src/engine/tx.rs:141-148`). If planning fails as a whole, its facts are lost; that is acceptable.
4. **Persist once.** Engine-running commands collect the facts from every engine run (`install`'s dry-run probe and its real run) and call `ReleaseCache::persist(&facts)` once. `info` runs no engine and persists an empty slice.
5. **`FactIndex`, for B4.** Provide an index over the memo's facts: the `sha256` for `(release_id, asset)`, and the verdict for `(release_id, asset, rules, interface)`. The planner uses it in step 1.2, and B4's `evaluate(…, facts: &FactIndex, …)` takes it.

Within one command, a fact learned on target 1 does not save target 2's download. That de-duplication is A8's per-command `DownloadMemo` (M2-D28's other half). Facts serve later commands.

**Files:** `src/engine/plan.rs` (`try_candidate`, `download`, `Plan.facts`), `src/toc/loaded.rs` (the `best` helper), `src/state/memo.rs` (`FactIndex`, merge), `src/resolve/cache.rs` (fact lookups through `PlanCtx.cache`), `src/app/install.rs` and `src/app/info.rs` (persist), new tests in `tests/release_cache.rs` and `tests/install.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Install a release, remove it, then install the same release again. The second install makes zero `asset` requests (`net.log`) while the blob is cached.
- With that blob deleted from `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/`, the same sequence downloads the asset again: one `asset` request, and the fact is refreshed.
- A candidate that fails verification on a target leaves `loads: false` for that target's `(rules, interface)` in the memo.
- `out_of_date` and `primary_interface` are recorded from the verdict. A fixture whose TOC lists an older in-family interface records `out_of_date: true` and that interface.
- A `--dry-run` install records facts.
- Facts survive memo merges, and they are capped together with entries (`RELEASE_MEMO_MAX_ENTRIES`).
- Dry-run plan JSON is unchanged: `facts` is not serialised, and `plan__plan_dry_run.snap` does not change because of this bead.

## Test Plan

- **Unit:**
  - fact merging: the union per `(release_id, asset)`, with the newer verdict winning per `(rules, interface)`;
  - the `FactIndex` lookups;
  - the extracted `best` helper against `judge`'s verdicts (in range, out of date, out of family).
- **E2E:**
  - the install, remove, install request count;
  - eviction (delete the blob in the test, then install);
  - a wrong-flavor candidate recorded as `loads: false` (a release whose only asset's TOC declares another family), checked by reading `releases.json`;
  - a dry run recording facts.

  Use `tests/common/netlog.rs` for counting and B1's helpers for the memo.

## Considerations

- A verdict is keyed by the rules row name *and* the interface. A client patch changes the interface, which forces re-verification.
- The blob cache is trusted for integrity, because it is content-addressed. It is not trusted for compatibility: the candidate is still inspected and verified against the current client rules every time.
- Facts are the fast path for MD5-hashed sources (WoWI, Tukui; A7, D3, D4). The existing fast path at `plan.rs:1123` matches only SHA-256 expectations, by design.
- Collision hot spots:
  - `download()` is also changed by A7 (the `ExpectedHash::Md5` match arms, `plan.rs:754` and `blobs.rs:125`), by A8 (`DownloadMemo`, deferred assets) and by B9 (the local-blob candidate);
  - `src/engine/plan.rs` is also edited by A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B9, C3 and C4.x.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- B1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.1` (The release memo and ReleaseCache): the memo's `candidates` slot and the `CandidateFact`/`VerdictFact` types, `PlanCtx.cache` for lookups, and `persist` for writing facts.

Unblocks:
- B4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.4` (The update-status evaluator): `Blocked { verified_not_loading }`, `Blocked { older_than_installed }` and `Verified` confidence all read facts through `FactIndex`, and the installed-side interface reader uses the extracted `best` helper.
- B9 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.9` (install --reinstall and installs from the blob cache): the local-blob candidate takes `release_id` from the fact with a given `sha256`, and a reinstall offline needs the download skip.
- D4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.4` (The Tukui source): a warm Tukui reinstall skips the `tukui-addon` and `asset` requests only through the memo facts.
- E5.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.1` (adopt report mode): the exactness check downloads facts-first and records the verdicts it learns.
- H3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.3` (Performance budgets and bench recipes): its economy assertions ("assets once", a warm `update` with zero downloads) rely on the download skip.
acceptance_criteria: Installing a release, removing it and installing the same release again makes zero asset requests the second time while the blob is cached (net.log); with the blob deleted the asset downloads again once and the fact is refreshed; a candidate that fails verification on a target leaves loads false for that target's (rules, interface) in the memo; out_of_date and primary_interface are recorded from the verdict (an older in-family TOC interface records out_of_date true and that interface); a --dry-run install records facts; facts survive memo merges and are capped together with entries under RELEASE_MEMO_MAX_ENTRIES; a fact never replaces the blob existence check; dry-run plan JSON is unchanged because Plan.facts is serde(skip)
close_reason: Planning records candidate facts in the memo and downloads skip the network when a remembered blob is cached; argc gate passes
