comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** M1 throws away the most expensive thing planning learns: the downloaded archive's hash, and whether it actually loads on each client. Keeping those two facts does two things.
- A warm `update` of DBM on three Classic clients downloads nothing, and `--reinstall` and `sync --locked` can restore from the local cache with no network, which also lets them work offline.
- The update badge stays honest. A newer release that failed TOC verification on a client becomes `blocked` there, after at most one attempt, instead of being offered again on every check.

Both serve the M2 economy goal (each archive at most once per run, and not at all once cached). They also serve the thesis that omaddons is the safe authority: the TOC check remains the ground truth (vision D5), and the facts only remember its answers.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D3.** `outdated` is metadata-only by default, and only `--verify` downloads. Every `UpdateAvailable` confidence counts, and verified failures become `blocked`. Why: background checks must not download every archive that changes, and a single attempt corrects a false positive for good. Rejected:
  - hiding `Unlikely` candidates, which would miss real updates;
  - always downloading, which is wasteful.

  This bead supplies the facts that make "verified failures become blocked" possible.
- **M2-D28.** Per-command download de-duplication, plus blob facts in the memo. Why: each distinct archive is downloaded once per command, and not at all when it is already cached. Rejected: re-downloading per target, as today. This bead is the cross-command half (facts). A8's `DownloadMemo` is the within-command half.
- **Decided while writing this bead:**
  - `primary_interface` comes from a helper extracted from `judge` (its `best` value), so B4's installed-side reader computes the same number;
  - facts are recorded only for downloaded (`Url`) candidates;
  - B3 provides the `FactIndex` that B4 consumes.

**Facts verified in the code** (`e902d36`):
- `try_candidate` (`plan.rs:1018`) downloads, inspects, verifies and partitions every candidate, and keeps nothing but the winner.
- `download` (`plan.rs:1121`) skips the network only for expected SHA-256 hashes (`:1123`).
- Only the REST path's `zip_asset` (`github_rest.rs:346`) supplies a hash; `release_set` sets `expected_hash: None` (`github.rs:275`). So every `release.json` asset is downloaded again by every target and every run today.
- `BlobRef` has `sha256`, `size` and `path`, and `BlobCache::get` checks that the blob exists.
- `judge` (`toc/loaded.rs:333-401`) computes the best in-family interface and the out-of-date flag.
- `TxOutcomes` returns the plan to the command.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- A stale fact after blob eviction: a fact never replaces the existence check.
- A client patch: verdicts are keyed by the rules row *and* the interface, so a patch forces re-verification.
- Wrong bytes from a fact: a fact is written only after the blob cache has hashed a download, and blobs are content-addressed, so the bytes are right by construction. The candidate is still verified against the current client every time.
- Collisions in `download()` with A7, A8 and B9. Coordinate through claims, and keep this bead's change narrow (signature, lookup, record).

Confidence: **high**. It reuses M1's proven download, inspect and verify path; the change is recording its results.

title: The update-status evaluator
description:
## Background

Four places must agree exactly on what "update available" means: `outdated` (B5), `update` (B6), the `pin`/`unpin` hints (B7) and `status` counts with the `list` latest column (B8). Today nothing computes it. `info` derives `latest` ad hoc (`src/app/info.rs:302-330`), and the planner's only notion of "current" is its no-op check by `release_id` (`src/engine/plan.rs:659-667`). If each command derived its own answer, the badge, the check and the update would drift apart.

The answer is one pure function over the record, the memo entry, the candidate facts and the target. It runs in `status --cached` on every widget refresh, so it must be pure CPU. Being pure also makes every edge case table-testable: pins, channel switches, blocked releases, static refs, identified adoptions, downgrades and upstreams that disappeared.

Goals served:
- "Current by default": say what is out of date without changing anything, at no network cost once the memo is warm.
- "Sole authority": an adopted build newer than the keyless release is never "updated" to an older one.
- "No regression": `update` never downgrades on its own.

Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`). The symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

### The evaluator (`src/resolve/updates.rs`, new; add it to `src/resolve/mod.rs`)

```rust
pub fn evaluate(record: &AddonRecord, entry: Option<&MemoEntryView>, facts: &FactIndex, target: &Target,
                installed_primary_interface: Option<u32>, source_enabled: bool) -> UpdateStatus;
pub enum UpdateStatus {
    Current { latest: ReleaseBrief },
    UpdateAvailable { latest: ReleaseBrief, confidence: Confidence },
    Pinned { latest: Option<ReleaseBrief> },
    Ahead { latest: ReleaseBrief },                            // installed is newer than the newest eligible
    Blocked { latest: ReleaseBrief, reason: BlockedReason },   // newest release is known not to suit this client
    Failed { error: ErrorBody },                               // a stored non-retryable failure (gone upstream)
    Unchecked { reason: UncheckedReason },
    Static,                                                    // nothing to check
}
pub enum Confidence { Verified, Declared, Likely, Unlikely }
pub enum BlockedReason { VerifiedNotLoading, OlderThanInstalled }
pub enum UncheckedReason { NeverChecked, SourceDisabled, Offline, NoEligibleRelease }
pub struct ReleaseBrief { pub version: String, pub release_id: String, pub published_at: Option<Timestamp>, pub channel: Channel }
```

`source_enabled` is the "enabled-source set passed in by the caller" that step 2 needs, reduced to one record (`statuses()` below takes the set itself). `MemoEntryView` comes from B1; `FactIndex` comes from B3.

**Wire names** are snake_case:
- statuses: `current`, `update_available`, `pinned`, `ahead`, `blocked`, `failed`, `unchecked`, `static`;
- confidence: `verified`, `declared`, `likely`, `unlikely`;
- reasons: `verified_not_loading`, `older_than_installed`, `never_checked`, `source_disabled`, `offline`, `no_eligible_release`.

Every type derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. B5's `outdated` items carry these as the keys `status`, `confidence`, `blocked_reason`, `unchecked_reason` and `error`, with `latest` as `{version, release_id, published_at, channel}`. Serialising `UpdateStatus` internally tagged by `status`, with the reason fields named `blocked_reason` and `unchecked_reason`, lets B5 flatten it directly.

### Algorithm, in order

1. **`Static`:**
   - `file:`, `url:` and directory installs (M2-D31);
   - any record whose `release_id` contains `@sha256:` or `@dir:`, whatever its ref. A `gh:` ref installed with `--file` gets `<ref>@sha256:<hex>` (`file_candidate`, `plan.rs:1241-1269`, through `local_identity`, `:1292-1307`, which yields `sha256:<hex>` for a zip and `dir:<ulid>` for a directory). Without this rule such a record would show as an update forever.
2. **No usable memo entry:**
   - the ref's source is disabled (`source_enabled == false`) → `Unchecked { source_disabled }`;
   - no entry → `Unchecked { never_checked }`. Under `--offline` the caller maps a missing entry to `Unchecked { offline }`;
   - a stored `failure` → `Failed`. For `not_found`, the item carries the fix `omaddons remove <name> -t <id>`. The design adds the alternative `omaddons adopt <folder> --ref <new ref> -t <id>`, but `adopt` does not exist yet, and no task may emit a fix naming a command a later task adds. So this bead emits the remove fix only, and the adopt alternative waits for E5.3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.3`). Decided: the other storable code, `ref_invalid`, gets the same remove fix, because the record's ref cannot be fetched either way.
3. `selection = select(set, target, record.channel, None)` (`src/resolve/select.rs:45`). With no candidates (`EmptyReason::NoEligibleRelease` or `NoAssets`), the result is `Unchecked { no_eligible_release }`.
4. **Same release:** if the first candidate's `release_id` equals `record.release_id`, the result is `Current`.
5. **Pinned:** if `record.pinned`, the result is `Pinned`, with the latest release attached.
6. **Downgrade guard.** `update` never downgrades on its own.
   - If both `published_at` values are known (the installed one comes from the entry's `set` or `known`, matched by `record.release_id`), an installed release newer than the latest gives `Ahead`.
   - If the dates are unknown but both version strings parse as dotted numerics (an optional leading `v`; trailing non-numeric parts ignored), an installed version greater than the latest gives `Ahead`.
   - Only when neither comparison is possible does evaluation continue as updatable. On GitHub, a stable tag that differs from the installed one almost always means newer.
   - Note: the GitHub `release.json` path sets `published_at: None` (`src/sources/github.rs:292`), so for most GitHub records the version comparator does the work. `12.1.15` parses; `Plater-v662` and `bundle/v12.2.0+v1.0.7` do not.
7. **Facts:**
   - If every candidate of that release has `loads: false` for this target's `(rules.name, interface)`, the result is `Blocked { verified_not_loading }`. A candidate with no fact for this target does not count as failing.
   - For records with `version_confidence: toc` (identified adoptions), the result is `Blocked { older_than_installed }` if a fact says the candidate is `out_of_date` on this client, or if its `primary_interface` is lower than `installed_primary_interface` (the installed primary folder's highest in-family interface, read from the TOC at status time). Use the fact of the first candidate, in selection order, that has a `loads: true` fact for this target. This keeps an adopted, newer, CurseForge-sourced build from being "updated" to an older keyless one.
   - **Planning enforces the same guard when no fact exists yet.** That happens after `adopt --no-verify`, after memo eviction, or when upstream publishes a newer release. For `toc`-confidence records the `Update` intent carries `installed_primary_interface`, and `try_candidate` rejects a candidate that verifies `out_of_date` or has a lower primary interface. It records the fact, and the item becomes `skipped` with `skip_reason: blocked`. The evaluator's guard is the display side; the planner's guard is the safety side. B6 implements the planner side.
8. **Otherwise `UpdateAvailable`**, with a confidence:
   - `Verified` when a fact says a candidate loads on this target;
   - `Declared` when the best candidate's rank is `MetadataInterface` or `MetadataFlavor`;
   - `Likely` for `NameHint` and `Unannotated` (WoWI, Tukui single assets, git);
   - `Unlikely` for the mismatch tiers (`NameHintMismatch`, `MetadataMismatch`).

   For `version_confidence: toc` records without a fact, the confidence is capped at `Likely`. Records adopted at the `identified` tier have `release_id: None`. They are `UpdateAvailable` whenever a release exists and no guard applies, which is what makes "identified, then replaced by the next update" work.

**Why every confidence counts as an update (M2-D3, M2-D41).** A count that hid `Unlikely` would mislead the other way, by never offering an update that might work. The self-correcting loop is better: `update` tries the candidate, verification refuses it, the fact is recorded, and from then on it is `Blocked`. The badge stays honest after at most one attempt, and that attempt is a skip, not a failure.

**Where it runs.** `status --cached` runs this evaluator over the memo. That is pure CPU, well under 1 ms for hundreds of records, so update counts cost no network (M2-D1). Reading `installed_primary_interface` needs one TOC read per `toc`-confidence record. Those records are few, and `status` reads at most one TOC per record, within its 5 ms budget.

### Shared helpers (same module)

- **`statuses(records, memo, facts, targets, enabled: &BTreeSet<SourceId>, read_primary_interface) -> Vec<(target, addon, UpdateStatus)>`.** It is used by `outdated`, `update`, `status`, `list` and `unpin`'s hint, and none of them may duplicate its logic.
  - For each target and record, it looks up the memo entry by `(record.ref, record.channel)`.
  - It derives each record's `source_enabled` from `enabled`, the caller's enabled-source set. Until D3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.3`) lands, callers pass every source id `SourceRegistry::builtin()` registers (`github`, `git`, `url`, `local`). D3 adds `SourceConfigView` (from `sources.<id>.enabled`); from then on callers build the set from that view, so `status` and `list`, which build no registry, get the same answer as `outdated`.
  - It calls `read_primary_interface` only for `version_confidence: toc` records.
  - It sorts the output by target id, then addon name (case-insensitive).
- **Production `read_primary_interface`.** It reads the record's primary folder's loaded TOC with the target's rules (`loaded_toc`, `src/toc/loaded.rs`) and returns the highest in-family interface. Use the helper B3 extracts from `judge`, so the display side and the planner side compute the same number. This reader is the module's only I/O; keep it separate from `evaluate`.

**Files:** new `src/resolve/updates.rs`, `src/resolve/mod.rs`, insta snapshots under `src/snapshots/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

A table test covers each status, reason and confidence, including:
- a pinned record with a newer release (`pinned`);
- an identified adoption (`release_id: None`) with and without facts (`update_available`, confidence capped at `likely` without a fact);
- an installed beta newer than the newest stable after a channel switch, with dates (`ahead`), with comparable versions (`ahead`), and with neither (`update_available`);
- every candidate `loads: false` (`blocked`, `verified_not_loading`);
- a `toc` record whose candidate has a lower `primary_interface`, or `out_of_date: true` (`blocked`, `older_than_installed`);
- a release with mismatch-tier candidates only (`unlikely`);
- `file:`, `url:`, directory and `gh:…@sha256:` records (`static`);
- a missing memo entry (`never_checked`), a disabled source (`source_disabled`), and an empty selection (`no_eligible_release`);
- a stored `not_found` failure (`failed`, with fix argv `omaddons remove <name> -t <id>`).

Also:
- `statuses()` returns results sorted by target id, then addon name, and calls `read_primary_interface` only for `toc`-confidence records.
- `evaluate` performs no I/O and reads no clock.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests only, since the evaluator is pure. Build records, memo entry views, a `FactIndex` and targets in code.
- Snapshot the JSON of one example per variant (insta, reviewed).
- Unit-test the dotted-numeric comparator on its own: `v12.1.15` against `12.1.14`, `12.1.14-beta` against `12.1.14`, and non-parsing strings.

## Considerations

- Keep it pure: no I/O and no clock. B8 passes `now` where staleness matters; the evaluator itself has none.
- Order matters. A pinned record whose installed release is the newest is `Current`, not `Pinned`. The downgrade guard runs after the pin check.
- It must stay fast, because `status --cached` runs it per record. If B8's budget test is threatened, the designed fallback is a per-entry `brief` precomputed in the memo (B1), not changes here.
- `Failed` is built from the memo's `{code, message}`, plus the fix this bead adds. `ErrorBody` derives `Serialize` and `JsonSchema` only, which is all output needs.
- B6 owns the planner-side guard and the `channel_explicit` bypass (an explicit `update X --channel C` installs the newest release of C even if it is older). The evaluator never sees that intent.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- B1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.1` (The release memo and ReleaseCache): `MemoEntryView` (trimmed set, `known`, `failure`, `fetched_at`) is the evaluator's input.
- B3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.3` (Candidate facts): `FactIndex` and the verdict facts behind `blocked`, `verified` and `older_than_installed`, plus the shared in-family interface helper.

Unblocks:
- B5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.5` (The outdated command): `outdated` is `statuses()` plus rendering.
- B6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6` (The update command): `update` computes statuses through the same `statuses()` and turns `UpdateAvailable` into `Update` requests.
- B7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.7` (pin and unpin): `unpin` reports what `update` would install, from the memo and the evaluator with no network.
- B8 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.8` (status update counts and the list latest column): `status` counts and `list`'s `latest.status` use these statuses and names.
acceptance_criteria: A pure table test covers every status, reason and confidence: a pinned record with a newer release is pinned; an identified adoption (release_id None) is update_available with and without facts, capped at likely without one; an installed beta newer than the newest stable after a channel switch is ahead by dates, ahead by comparable dotted versions, and update_available when neither comparison is possible; every candidate loads false gives blocked verified_not_loading; a toc record whose candidate is out_of_date or has a lower primary_interface gives blocked older_than_installed; a mismatch-tier-only release is unlikely; file:, url:, directory and gh:…@sha256: records are static; a missing memo entry is never_checked, a disabled source source_disabled and an empty selection no_eligible_release; a stored not_found is failed with fix argv omaddons remove <name> -t <id>; statuses() sorts by target id then addon name and reads the installed primary interface only for toc-confidence records; evaluate does no I/O and reads no clock; one JSON snapshot per variant is reviewed
close_reason: Pure update-status evaluator and the shared statuses() helper, table-tested; argc gate passes

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** "One memo, one evaluator" is the architectural core of the update work. `outdated`, `update`, `pin`, `status` and the M3 widget cannot disagree about what is out of date, because they all call this one pure function over the same memo. The alternative, a stored result file, goes stale the moment `update` commits. For the owner this means three things: the badge count matches what `update` will do; a pin is respected everywhere; and an addon adopted from another distribution is never silently downgraded. That last one supports the project's thesis: omaddons can be the sole authority over every client's addons only if it never makes a working setup worse on its own.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D3.** Every `UpdateAvailable` confidence counts as an update, and verified failures become `blocked`. Why: one attempt corrects a false positive for good, and a count that hides `Unlikely` would miss real updates. Rejected:
  - hiding `Unlikely`;
  - always downloading to verify, which is wasteful for background checks.
- **M2-D31.** `url:`, `file:`, directory, `@sha256:` and `@dir:` installs are `static` and are not update-checked, while `git:` refs are checked through their rev. Why: a URL's release id is the URL itself, so there is nothing to compare, and a git ref has a moving head. Rejected: re-downloading URLs to compare hashes.
- **M2-D42.** Identified (TOC-version) adoptions are protected from downgrades by comparing the candidate's primary interface and its `out_of_date` flag with the installed TOC. Why: an adopted newer build from another distribution must not be "updated" to an older keyless one. Rejected: trusting `release_id: None` to mean "anything is newer".
- **M2-D41** (consistency): a newest release that does not load on a client is skipped (`blocked`), not failed, so `--strict` stays meaningful and runs with WeakAuras on retail are not permanently partial.
- **Review-round fix folded in:** the plan's third review pass added the **planning-time `older_than_installed` guard**. The evaluator is the display side. B6's planner rejects an `out_of_date` or lower-interface candidate for `toc` records even when no fact exists yet (after `adopt --no-verify`, after memo eviction, or with a newer upstream release), records the fact, and skips the item as `blocked`.
- **Decided while writing this bead:**
  - `evaluate` takes `source_enabled`, which the design passes in as the caller's enabled-source set;
  - the `not_found` adopt alternative waits for E5.3, because no task may emit a fix for a command a later task adds;
  - `ref_invalid` failures get the same remove fix;
  - the installed-interface reader shares B3's helper extracted from `judge`.

**Facts verified in the code** (`e902d36`):
- `select` (`resolve/select.rs:45`) considers only the newest eligible release. Its tiers are `MetadataInterface`, `MetadataFlavor`, `NameHint`, `Unannotated`, `NameHintMismatch` and `MetadataMismatch`.
- `newest` (`:99`) orders by `published_at` only when every eligible release has a date.
- The GitHub `release.json` path leaves `published_at: None` (`sources/github.rs:292`), so the dotted-version comparator carries the downgrade guard for most GitHub records.
- `--file` installs get `<ref>@sha256:<hex>` and directories get `<ref>@dir:<ulid>` (`engine/plan.rs:1252`, `:1292-1307`).
- `AddonRecord` (`model.rs:528`) already has `pinned`, `channel`, `version_confidence` and an optional `release_id`.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- A wrong "newer" judgement on unparsable tags (`Plater-v662`). On GitHub a differing stable tag almost always means newer, and the guard steps aside only when it cannot compare.
- Budget creep in `status --cached`: the evaluator is pure CPU, well under 1 ms for hundreds of records, and a precomputed memo `brief` is the designed fallback.
- An adoption whose installed TOC has no readable in-family interface. `installed_primary_interface` is then `None` and only the `out_of_date` fact can block. That is a conservative miss, and the planner-side guard still verifies before installing.

The plan rates the update path **high** confidence; the evaluator is pure and fully table-tested.

Tests: table tests for every status, reason and confidence (pinned, pinned-at-newest current, identified adoption likely/verified, ahead by dates/versions and update_available when neither, blocked both reasons, unlikely, static x5, never_checked, source_disabled, no_eligible_release, failed with argv), comparator cases, statuses ordering and selective TOC reads, and the reviewed snapshot src/resolve/snapshots/omaddons__resolve__updates__tests__update_statuses.snap. New wire names: status current|update_available|pinned|ahead|blocked|failed|unchecked|static (internally tagged 'status'), confidence verified|declared|likely|unlikely, blocked_reason verified_not_loading|older_than_installed, unchecked_reason never_checked|source_disabled|offline|no_eligible_release, latest {version, release_id, published_at, channel}. Decided: (1) the entry input is state::memo::MemoEntry (the bead's MemoEntryView); statuses() takes an entry lookup closure so outdated/update can pass ReleaseCache::entry and status --cached the loaded memo; (2) when both dates are known they decide, and versions are compared only when a date is missing; (3) dotted() reads numbers up to the first non-numeric suffix (12.1.14-beta == 12.1.14); (4) unchecked offline is produced by callers, never by evaluate. found: none

title: The outdated command: a cheap, read-only update check across targets
description:
## Background

Today the only way to learn whether an addon is out of date is to re-run `install` for it, target by target. Nothing reports pending updates:

- `info <addon>` makes one metadata fetch per call through `fetch_once` (`src/sources/mod.rs:179`) and shows the newest release of one addon. It never compares against several clients.
- `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` (15 min, `src/politeness.rs:34`) is documented as "`outdated` reuses the last per-source result inside this window unless `--refresh`", but no command uses it. B1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.1`) adds the release memo and `ReleaseCache` that do.
- `World::select` (`src/app/world.rs:159`) resolves `-t` with `resolve_one`, so `-t vanilla` on a machine with two vanilla clients is `target_ambiguous`. A2 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.2`) adds `World::select_many`.
- `status` (`src/app/status.rs`) recommends nothing about updates.

This bead adds `omaddons outdated`: a read-only check of every managed addon on every client, cheap enough for the M3 widget to run every few hours. It serves the M2 goal "current by default": every managed addon on every client can be brought to its newest compatible release with one command, and the tool can say what is out of date without changing anything, using the minimum number of requests (one fetch per distinct ref per run, a free re-check inside the 15-minute window, no GitHub REST for `release.json` publishers).

Without it, the owner has to reinstall to discover updates, B8's `check_updates` recommendation in `status` would name a command that does not exist, and D3, D6, E5.2, H3 and H4 have no command to assert against. Line numbers in this bead are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

### Command surface

`omaddons outdated [-t T] [--refresh] [--check] [--verify]`, plus the global flags (`--offline`, `--json`, `-v`, `--progress`).

- New module `src/app/outdated.rs` with `OutdatedArgs { refresh: bool, check: bool, verify: bool }` and an `Outdated` variant in `cli::Command` (`src/cli.rs`) with `visible_alias = "check"` (M2-D39: `check` is a likely first guess that falls outside the Levenshtein-2 suggestion range, so the alias is pulled forward from M4's intent inference). Add the `command_name` and `dispatch` arms in `src/app/mod.rs`.
- Add `outdated` to the **Look** group of A1's command group registry (A1 turns `COMMANDS` in `src/app/mod.rs:25` into `{name, group}` rows) in the same commit as the clap variant. Bare help must stay under 30 lines.
- **`--changelog` is not added here.** D6 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.6`) adds the flag together with its behaviour. Vision rule DEC-1: a command or flag lands only with its behaviour, never as a stub.

### Flow

1. `World::load()`, then `select_many` (A2). With no `-t` it returns every discovered target, live and test. With `-t` it returns every match of the first precedence step that matches anything (key, id, product, flavor folder, mode, family, path), so `-t vanilla` yields every vanilla client. Results are sorted by target id. Registered targets whose client dir is gone are excluded. An empty result is `target_not_found` with the fixes `resolve_one` produces.
2. Load the record of each selected target (`world.records()`, `src/app/world.rs:108`). Unregistered targets have no records and contribute no items.
3. Collect the distinct `Wanted { ref: record.ref, channel: record.channel, version: None }` across all targets and call `ReleaseCache::get` once.
   - Pinned records are included with `version: None`: the point is to learn the newest release so the output can say "pinned (latest X)".
   - Static records are never fetched (M2-D31: a URL's or local file's release id is the URL or content hash itself, so there is nothing upstream to compare, and re-downloading to compare hashes was rejected): `file:` and `url:` refs, directory installs, and any record whose `release_id` contains `@sha256:` or `@dir:` (a `gh:` ref installed with `--file` gets `<ref>@sha256:<hex>`, `src/engine/plan.rs:1252`).
   - Freshness: `Freshness::Window(SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL)` by default, `Refresh` with `--refresh`, `OfflineOnly` with `--offline` or `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`. `--offline` wins over `--refresh`.
4. Evaluate every record with B4's shared `statuses(records, memo, facts, targets, enabled, read_primary_interface)` helper, never a copy of its logic. `enabled` is the set of source ids the command's `SourceRegistry` registers (D3 later derives it from `sources.<id>.enabled`). The `read_primary_interface` callback reads the installed primary folder's loaded TOC and returns its highest in-family interface. It is called only for `version_confidence: toc` records (identified adoptions), at most one TOC read per such record.
5. With `--verify`, verify candidates (below), then re-evaluate those items against the new facts.
6. `ReleaseCache::persist(facts)` once: one memo write per command.
7. Build data, warnings, `commands` and `partial`, and render.

### Update statuses (B4's evaluator, `src/resolve/updates.rs`)

`evaluate(record, entry, facts, target, installed_primary_interface, source_enabled) -> UpdateStatus`. Wire names are snake_case:

| Status | Meaning | Extra fields |
|---|---|---|
| `current` | the newest eligible release is the installed one | `latest` |
| `update_available` | a newer eligible release exists | `latest`, `confidence` |
| `pinned` | the record is pinned and the newest eligible release differs | `latest` |
| `ahead` | the installed release is newer than the newest eligible one (after a channel switch) | `latest` |
| `blocked` | the newest release is known not to suit this client | `latest`, `blocked_reason` |
| `failed` | a stored non-retryable upstream failure (`not_found`, `ref_invalid`: a deleted project, a renamed-away repo) | `error` |
| `unchecked` | nothing to evaluate against | `unchecked_reason` |
| `static` | nothing to check (`file:`, `url:`, directory, `@sha256:`/`@dir:` ids) | |

- Confidence: `verified` (a fact says a candidate loads on this target), `declared` (rank `MetadataInterface` or `MetadataFlavor`), `likely` (`NameHint`, `Unannotated`: WoWI, Tukui single assets, git), `unlikely` (the mismatch tiers). For `toc`-confidence records without a fact it is capped at `likely`.
- Blocked reasons: `verified_not_loading` (every candidate of that release has `loads: false` for this target's rules row and interface), `older_than_installed` (for `toc`-confidence records, the candidate is `out_of_date` here or its primary interface is lower than the installed one).
- Unchecked reasons: `never_checked` (no memo entry), `source_disabled` (from the enabled-source set the caller passes), `offline` (no memo entry under `--offline`), `no_eligible_release` (`select` gives no candidate on the record's channel).
- Order: static, then no usable entry (`source_disabled`, `never_checked`, stored failure → `failed`), then `select(set, target, record.channel, None)`, then same release → `current`, then pinned → `pinned`, then the downgrade guard (`published_at` dates, else dotted-numeric versions with optional leading `v`) → `ahead`, then facts → `blocked`, else `update_available`.
- A stored `not_found` carries fix `omaddons remove <name> -t <id>` (B4 builds it).

### Output

**Default listing is token-frugal.** Items appear only when actionable or noteworthy: `update_available`, `blocked`, `ahead`, `failed`, and `pinned` (whose latest differs from the installed release). `-v` lists every item, including `current`, `static` and `unchecked`. `summary` always counts every status. Targets are sorted by id, items by name ignoring case.

**JSON** (keys binding, values illustrative):

```json
{"ok":true,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"outdated","exit_code":0,"partial":false,
 "data":{"checked_at":"2026-10-15T20:01:02Z","requests":{"fetched":3,"probed":1,"reused":11},
  "targets":[{"target":{"id":"retail","key":"01M…"},"items":[
    {"name":"DBM","ref":"gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods","channel":"stable","pinned":false,
     "installed":{"version":"12.1.14","release_id":"gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods@12.1.14"},
     "latest":{"version":"12.1.15","release_id":"gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods@12.1.15","published_at":null,"channel":"stable"},
     "status":"update_available","confidence":"declared","blocked_reason":null,"unchecked_reason":null,"error":null}]}],
  "summary":{"update_available":3,"current":11,"pinned":1,"ahead":0,"blocked":0,"failed":0,"unchecked":0,"static":0}},
 "warnings":[],"commands":[{"action":"update","command":"omaddons update","argv":["omaddons","update"],"destructive":false}],
 "meta":{"elapsed_ms":212,"offline":false}}
```

- `requests` counts distinct `Wanted`s by `ReleaseCache` origin: `fetched` (`Origin::Fetched`), `probed` (`Origin::Probed`), `reused` (`Origin::Memo` and `Origin::StaleFallback`).
- `checked_at` (decided here): the oldest `fetched_at` among the memo entries this run evaluated against, `null` when nothing was checked.
- `latest` is `{version, release_id, published_at, channel}` (B4's `ReleaseBrief`), `null` for `unchecked`, `failed` and `static`.
- A `blocked` item sets `blocked_reason`, an `unchecked` item sets `unchecked_reason`, a `failed` item sets `error` (`code, message, fix, fix_argv`).
- Every struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3).

**Human output:**

```
$ omaddons outdated
retail (12.1.5, mainline)
  DBM          12.1.14      → 12.1.15       gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods
  Plater       Plater-v661  → Plater-v662   gh:Tercioo/Plater-Nameplates
classic (5.5.4, mists)
  DBM          12.1.14      → 12.1.15
forever (1.60.1, forever)
  Questie      bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6   pinned (latest bundle/v12.2.0+v1.0.7)
3 updates on 2 clients · 1 pinned · checked just now (4 requests, 11 reused)
Run `omaddons update` to install them.
```

The ref column appears on a ref's first line only. The summary line counts updates, pinned, blocked and failed items, the age of `checked_at`, and requests made (`fetched + probed`) versus reused.

**`commands`:** when any item is `update_available`, one hint: `omaddons update`, or `omaddons update -t <id>` when only one target has updates (action `update`, `destructive: false`). Nothing else. E5.3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.3`) later adds `adopt -t <id>` for targets with zero records and adoptable folders; this bead MUST NOT, because a hint never names a command that does not exist yet.

### `--check`

Exit 6 (`check_failed`, `ok: false`, `data` kept) when any item is `update_available`, through `Outcome::assertion_failure` (`src/output/mod.rs`). A partial run with updates also exits 6: `--check` wins, because an assertion failed. No updates: exit 0 (or the partial run's normal exit 0 with `partial: true`).

### `--verify`

For each `update_available` item whose confidence is below `verified`, download and verify the candidate exactly as install planning would, without staging and without the global lock: one dry-run engine run (`dry_run: true`) with one target request per target, each change the item's update request (`RequestedChange::Update { addon }`, named `Reinstall` until A3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.3`) renames it; once B6 adds `installed_primary_interface` to it, fill that field with the same reader `statuses()` uses, so the planning-time guard applies to `--verify` too). Planning holds its in-flight lock under `<state>/omaddons/inflight/` and releases it. B3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.3`) records the verdicts as candidate facts (dry runs included) and warms the blob cache, so a following `update` downloads nothing. Re-evaluate those items with the new facts, so the same run shows `verified` or `blocked`. A download failure during `--verify` leaves the item's status as it was, is mirrored as a warning, and makes the run partial. Other planning refusals (ownership, a running client) do not change the item's status and are logged under `-v`.

Off by default (M2-D3): `outdated` is metadata-only so background checks never download every archive that changes. Every `update_available` confidence counts as an update, `unlikely` included, because hiding it would miss real updates; the loop self-corrects instead: `update` (or `--verify`) tries the candidate, verification refuses it, the fact is recorded, and from then on it is `blocked`.

### Offline, stale data and failures

- **Offline:** every key is answered from the memo regardless of age (`Origin::StaleFallback`) with one `stale_check` warning (B1) naming the oldest `fetched_at` used. Keys without an entry are `unchecked` with reason `offline`.
- **Retryable fetch failure** (`network`, 5xx `http_status`, `rate_limited`) on a ref with a memo entry: evaluate against the stale entry and add a per-item warning. `ReleaseCache::get` never substitutes a stale entry by itself (B1's rule 5), so `outdated`, as a read-only caller, asks for it explicitly with `ReleaseCache::stale(&Wanted) -> Option<Fetched>` (`Origin::StaleFallback`). Without an entry: the item is `failed` with that error (`retryable: true`). Either way the failure is mirrored into `warnings` (M1's convention: the warning's code is the item's error code, with its fix) and the run is `partial: true`.
- Retryable failures are never stored in the memo; the next run retries.

### Writes

Only the memo and other files under `<cache>/omaddons/` (blob cache and HTTP validators with `--verify`), `net.log` (`<state>/omaddons/net.log`), and, with `--verify`, the in-flight lock under `<state>/omaddons/inflight/`. It never takes the global lock and never writes records, history or any client directory.

### Progress

Emit A9 progress events: phase `fetch` per ref, and `download`/`verify` per candidate under `--verify`, at most one event per item per phase.

**Files:** new `src/app/outdated.rs`; `src/cli.rs` (`Outdated` variant, alias); `src/app/mod.rs` (group row, `command_name`, `dispatch`); new `tests/outdated.rs`; `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (rows); new snapshots under `tests/snapshots/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a three-target fixture with five addons where two refs changed, `outdated` lists exactly the expected items with the right statuses, and `net.log` shows each distinct ref fetched once (at most one `release-latest` line per distinct GitHub ref).
- A second run within 15 minutes makes zero requests (`net.log` unchanged) and prints the same data apart from `meta` and `requests`.
- `--check` exits 6 with `data` populated when updates exist, 0 otherwise, and 6 when updates exist and the run is partial.
- `--offline` with a populated memo prints results plus a `stale_check` warning. With an empty memo, items are `unchecked` with reason `offline`.
- It writes nothing except under `<cache>/omaddons/`, to `net.log`, and to `<state>/omaddons/inflight/` (with `--verify` only). A test snapshots the state dir before and after, excluding those paths.
- `--verify` downloads only update candidates whose confidence is below `verified`, and records facts.
- `omaddons check` behaves as `omaddons outdated`.
- Static records make no request. Pinned records with a newer release are listed as `pinned` with `latest`.
- `commands` holds exactly one `update` hint when any update is available, with `-t <id>` when only one target has updates.
- A retryable fetch failure makes the item `failed` (no memo entry) or stale-evaluated with a warning (memo entry), and `partial: true`.
- `--changelog` is not accepted (D6 adds it).
- Bare help stays under 30 lines with `outdated` in the Look group.

## Test Plan

- **E2E** in new `tests/outdated.rs`, with HTTP replay fixtures and A10's helpers: `Home::installed_behind(base, (old_tag, old_assets), (new_tag, new_assets), targets)` across retail, era and classic; a pinned addon; `blocked` via a candidate fact seeded with B1's `Home::seed_memo` (entries plus candidate facts); a static `file:` install; a stored `not_found` (seeded memo failure) reported `failed` with the remove fix; `--offline` with and without a memo; `--refresh` refetching inside the window; `--verify` downloading only below-`verified` candidates; the `check` alias.
- **Request economy** from `net.log` only, never from timing: A10's `net_log(home)` counters by host and purpose; `release-latest` at most once per distinct ref; zero lines on the warm re-run; zero `api.github.com` lines for `release.json` publishers on stable (`assert_no_github_rest`, `tests/common/netlog.rs`).
- **Writes:** hash the state dir before and after, excluding `net.log` and `inflight/`.
- **Contract:** success and failure rows in `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (one envelope on stdout, NDJSON on stderr, exit codes 0, 2, 3, 6).
- **Determinism:** two runs inside the window are byte-identical apart from `meta`.
- **Snapshots:** JSON and human output for the three-target fixture (reviewed, not blindly accepted).

## Considerations

- Count requests from `net.log` in tests, never from timing.
- Fixture response sequences restart in every CLI process (`src/net/replay.rs`); multi-command scenarios switch fixture sets with `home.scenario(...)`.
- `outdated` never falls back to a mutating path. `update` (B6, `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6`) shares `statuses()`, so the two can never disagree about what is out of date.
- The `failed` item's `adopt` alternative (`omaddons adopt <folder> --ref <new ref> -t <id>`) is added by E5.3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.3`) in B4's evaluator, once `adopt` exists; until then B4 emits the remove fix only.
- Unchecked items are hidden by default; the human summary still says how many there are, so an offline run with an empty memo is not silent.
- Collision hot spots: `src/cli.rs` and `src/app/mod.rs` are edited by every command bead (B6, B7, E5.1, F2, F3.1, F4, G1, G2). Keep the arms small and rebase before each gate run.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.1` (Grouped bare help with a command group registry): `outdated` joins the Look group; without the grouped layout a new command breaks the 30-line bare-help test.
- A2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.2` (Multi-target selection with World::select_many): the default scope is every target, and `-t vanilla` must fan out instead of failing `target_ambiguous`.
- A9 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.9` (Progress plumbing for long commands): a cold check across many refs takes seconds; `Context` carries no progress sink until A9.
- A10 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.10` (M2 test helpers): the E2E tests need `installed_behind`, release sequences and the `net.log` counters by purpose.
- B4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.4` (The update-status evaluator): `outdated` is a thin layer over `statuses()`; B4 in turn brings B1's memo and `ReleaseCache` and B3's facts.

Unblocks:
- B8 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.8` (status update counts, adoptable count, hints and the list latest column): its `check_updates` recommendation runs `omaddons outdated`, which must exist.
- D3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.3` (The WoWInterface source): its acceptance asserts `outdated` statuses (`failed`, `current`, `update_available/likely`) for `wowi:` refs.
- D6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.6` (Changelogs): adds `outdated --changelog` to this command.
- E5.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.2` (adopt --apply …): its acceptance checks `outdated` after adopting (`update_available`, `blocked/older_than_installed`).
- H1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` (Contract conformance audit): audits this command's rows and determinism.
- H3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.3` (Performance budgets and bench recipes): benchmarks warm and cold `outdated`.
- H4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.4` (Live probes): runs `outdated` over the whole catalog live for the zero-REST and one-request-per-ref checks.
- H6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` (README, help text and vision-bead records): documents the command, alias and wire names.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** `outdated` answers the owner's most frequent question, "is anything out of date?", across all six clients in one command, without changing anything. It is the read side of the update loop that M2 delivers first, before WoW: Forever launches on 2026-11-04 and publishers start shipping frequent builds. It is also what the M3 widget schedules in the background, so its cost matters: one request per distinct ref after the 15-minute window, zero inside it, zero GitHub REST for `release.json` publishers. Keeping it read-only (cache, `net.log` and the in-flight lock only) keeps the project's thesis intact: only transactions change addons.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D3: metadata-only by default; `--verify` downloads.** Background checks must not download every archive that changes. Every `update_available` confidence counts, including `unlikely`, because hiding it would miss real updates; a verified failure becomes `blocked` after at most one attempt, so the count self-corrects. Rejected: hiding `unlikely` (misses updates), always downloading (wasteful).
- **M2-D39: the `check` alias, pulled forward from M4.** It is a likely first guess and falls outside the Levenshtein-2 suggestion range of `outdated`. Rejected: waiting for M4's intent inference.
- **M2-D31: static records are not checked.** A URL's release id is the URL itself, so there is nothing to compare; `@sha256:`/`@dir:` ids come from `--file` installs. Rejected: re-downloading URLs to compare hashes.
- **M2-D37: batch commands use the 15-minute window.** `outdated` followed by `update` must be free. Rejected: one freshness policy for every command (installs revalidate).
- **M2-D27 (context):** pending updates are not `status` attention. `outdated --check` is the freshness check and `status --check` stays a health check, so neither is permanently red.
- **DEC-1:** `--changelog` waits for D6, which implements it; no flag lands before its behaviour.
- **Staging decisions made while writing this bead:** `checked_at` is the oldest `fetched_at` among entries the run used; a retryable failure with no memo entry yields `status: failed` with `retryable: true`; `--verify` is one dry-run engine run whose planning failures other than verification do not change statuses.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` is 15 min (`src/politeness.rs:34`) and unused today; `info` calls `fetch_once` (`src/sources/mod.rs:179`) every time.
- `release-latest`, `release-json` and `asset` are the existing `net.log` purposes (`src/sources/github.rs:192,257`, `src/engine/plan.rs:1132`); `tests/common/netlog.rs` already has `read_net_log`, `count_host` and `assert_no_github_rest`.
- `Outcome::assertion_failure` is the existing `--check`/`--strict` hook (`src/output/mod.rs`).
- GitHub `releases/latest` answers `302 Location: …/releases/tag/<tag>` (verified live on 2026-10-15 for WeakAuras 5.22.1 and BugSack v12.1.7), which is what B2's one-request probe relies on.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Request-economy regressions are invisible in timing tests; every economy claim is asserted from `net.log` counts.
- A memo concurrency loss costs one extra request, never a wrong answer (B1's merge-on-write).
- `--verify` downloads; it is opt-in and shares the blob cache with `update`, so the download is never wasted.
- Confidence for the update path (B1 to B6) is **high**: a thin layer over M1's proven fetch, select and verify pipeline plus a cache.

title: The update command: multi-target updates with run-level undo
description:
## Background

Updating today means re-running `install` per addon, per target. The pieces exist but nothing connects them:

- `RequestedChange::Reinstall { addon }` (`src/engine/plan.rs:86-89`, doc "Update in M1: install the newest compatible release of an installed addon") is never constructed. Its `want()` arm (`plan.rs:485-501`) resolves it to an install of the record's ref and channel. A3 renames it `Update`.
- `build_install` labels a change to an installed addon `ChangeKind::Update` (`plan.rs:822-826`), and `target_kind` makes any transaction containing one kind `update` (`plan.rs:538-548`).
- `install` builds a single `TxTarget` and renders `outcomes.first()`; the multi-target commit path has never run outside dry-run probes (A6 adds the shared outcome and its test).
- `TargetPlanner::install` rebuilds the record from scratch (`plan.rs:724-733`: `pinned = wanted.version.is_some()`, `reason = Explicit`), so an update path built on it would silently unpin addons and promote dependencies. A3's carry-over rules fix that.
- An `ownership_conflict` fix appends `--force` to the argv (`src/engine/ownership.rs:261-265`). For `update` that would be `omaddons update … --force`, which does not exist.

This bead adds `omaddons update`, the most-used command of the milestone. It serves the M2 goal "current by default": every managed addon on every client is brought to its newest compatible release with one command, one fetch per distinct ref and one download per distinct archive per run, and one `omaddons undo` reverts the whole run. Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

### What the owner sees

```
$ omaddons update
retail: updated 2 addons (tx 01M5…)
  DBM          12.1.14 → 12.1.15
  Plater       Plater-v661 → Plater-v662
classic: updated 1 addon (tx 01M5…)  — /reload in game
  DBM          12.1.14 → 12.1.15
forever: nothing to update (Questie is pinned)
Undo all of it with: omaddons undo
```

Underneath: bare `update` means `--all` (M2-D4, a departure from the vision, which required `--all`: the first command an agent or a person guesses should work, every comparable tool behaves this way, and run-level undo makes it safe; `--all` stays accepted); one fetch per ref, from the memo when fresh; one download per distinct asset (DBM's zip is shared by retail and classic, and A8's (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.8`) per-command download memo fetches it once); one transaction per target, committed in turn under one run id (A12, `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.12`); a failure on one target does not roll back another; per-item failures make the run `partial`; a newer release that does not load on a client is `skipped` (`blocked`), not failed. `classic` was running, so `running_policy = safe` allowed the replace and the outcome says `/reload`. `omaddons undo` reverts the whole run, both transactions in reverse order (M2-D38: history lines carry a run id and bare `undo` reverts the most recent run, so "undo what I just did" after a multi-client update is one command); `omaddons undo <tx>` still reverts one client.

### Command surface

`omaddons update [<addon>…] [--all] [-t T] [--channel C] [--refresh] [--strict] [--dry-run]` (`-t` and `--dry-run` are existing global flags). C4.2 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.2`) adds `--no-deps`.

- New `src/app/update.rs` with `UpdateArgs { addons: Vec<String>, all: bool, channel: Option<String>, refresh: bool, strict: bool }`; `channel` uses the same `value_parser = ["stable", "beta", "alpha"]` as install. `Update` variant in `cli::Command` with `visible_alias = "upgrade"` (M2-D39: a likely first guess outside the Levenshtein-2 suggestion range, pulled forward from M4); `command_name` and `dispatch` arms; `update` in the **Change** group of A1's registry, in the same commit.
- **No `--reinstall`** (that is B9's `install --reinstall`, `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.9`), **no `--force`** (taking over another addon's folder is a deliberate act), **no `--version`**.
- **`help update`** renders clap's long help (`for_command` in `src/app/help.rs` calls `render_long_help()`), so the subcommand's `long_about`/`after_help` says: exact versions come from `omaddons install <addon> --version V` (which pins) or `omaddons pin <addon> --version V`.

**Usage errors** (exit 2):
- `--all` together with names: fix argv is the argv without `--all` (make `without_flag`, `src/cli.rs:502`, `pub(crate)`).
- `--channel` without names: fix `omaddons update <addon> --channel <C>`. `<addon>` is a placeholder, so this is a text fix listed in `TEXT_FIXES` (`tests/contract/main.rs`), following M1's `omaddons targets add <path>`.
- `update … --version V`: clap reports an unknown argument and `usage_error` (`src/cli.rs:324`) finds no flag within Levenshtein 2. Add a special case: subcommand `update` plus unknown `--version` gives fix argv `omaddons install <same args> --version V` and, once B7's (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.7`) `pin` exists, the alternative `omaddons pin <addon> --version V`. Whichever of B6 and B7 lands second adds the `pin` alternative (a hint never names a command that does not exist yet).

### Name matching

Named addons restrict the run to those names, on the targets where they are installed.
- A name matches a record's name case-insensitively, or a catalog name or alias (`Catalog::by_name`, `src/resolve/catalog.rs`) whose ref equals a recorded ref by `Ref` identity. B7's `pin`/`unpin` match names the same way; whichever of B6 and B7 lands second moves the matcher into one shared function used by both.
- A name installed on no selected target is an item failure `not_managed` with fix `omaddons install <name>`. Decided: it is reported once, as a failed item under the first selected target (by id), with a message naming the targets checked, and mirrored into `warnings`. When every name is unknown, the command fails with the first name's error (exit 3), as M1 install does when every item fails. Once `adopt` exists, E5.3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.3`) changes the fix to `omaddons adopt <folder> --ref <ref> -t <id>` when an unmanaged folder of that name exists.

### Flow

1. `World::load()`, `select_many` (A2; no `-t` means every target, family/mode/product selectors fan out), then records.
2. Compute update statuses exactly as `outdated` does, through B4's shared `statuses()` helper, never duplicated: one `ReleaseCache::get` over the distinct `Wanted { ref, record.channel, None }` of non-static records, freshness `Window(SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL)` (15 min), `Refresh` with `--refresh`, `OfflineOnly` with `--offline` (`--offline` wins).
3. Classify each record in scope:

| Status | Item |
|---|---|
| `update_available` | planned as `RequestedChange::Update { addon, installed_primary_interface }` |
| `current` | `unchanged` (hidden unless `-v`, counted in `summary`) |
| `pinned` | `skipped`, `skip_reason: pinned`; a **named** pinned addon also adds warning `addon_pinned` through A3's shared constructor (fix argv A3's interim `omaddons info <name> -t <id>` until B7 switches the constructor to `omaddons unpin <name> -t <id>`) |
| `ahead` | `skipped`, `ahead` |
| `blocked` | `skipped`, `blocked` |
| `static` | `skipped`, `static` |
| `unchecked` | `skipped`, `unchecked` |
| `failed` (stored) | `failed` with the stored error |

4. **`--channel C`** on named addons: they skip the evaluator and are planned as `Install { ref: record.ref, channel: C, channel_explicit: true, version: None, pin: Keep, reason: record.reason, reinstall: false, name: Some(record.name) }`. Because the user explicitly switched, the downgrade guard does not apply, and the newest release of the new channel is installed even if it is older. Decided: when C equals the recorded channel, the item goes through the normal status path (no switch, guard applies). A switch whose newest release is already installed is a records-only `SetChannel` edit once A4.3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.3`) lands; until then A3 reports it `unchanged` with a `-v` note. A pinned addon under `--channel` hits A3's pinned no-op (`unchanged` plus `addon_pinned`).
5. Build one `TxRequest` with a fresh run id (A12) and one `TxTarget` per target that has planned items. `TxTarget.default_kind` (added by A4.1, `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1`, and copied into `TargetRequest.default_kind`) is `Update` for this command; whichever of B6 and A4.1 lands second sets it. No kind override.
6. `want()` resolves `Update` to `Install { ref, channel: record.channel, version: None, pin: Keep, reason: record.reason }`. Do not keep M1's `version: installed.pinned.then(...)` (`plan.rs:492`): pinned records are skipped before planning, and a record pinned since planning hits A3's pinned no-op under the lock (`Ok(None)` plus `addon_pinned`). `carry_over` (A3) runs inside `build_install`, so pins, channels, reasons and `required_by` survive.
7. `engine.run(&req)`: targets commit sequentially in key order, each its own transaction.
8. Map outcomes through A6's `build`, merge the evaluator items into each target's item list (sorted by name ignoring case), and include selected targets without work (`tx: null`).
9. `ReleaseCache::persist(plan.facts)` once (facts include dry runs), then render.

### A candidate that fails verification is not a failure (M2-D41)

When the newest release turns out not to load on this client during planning, the item is `skipped` with `skip_reason: blocked`, B3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.3`) records the `loads: false` facts, and the run does **not** become partial. The next `outdated` shows it `blocked`. Why: it is information, not a failure, consistent with `copy` skipping builds a client lacks, and it keeps `--strict` meaningful; failing the item would make every run with WeakAuras on retail partial. Map to `blocked`: `wrong_flavor`, and `no_compatible_release` whose `details.tried` lists candidates (the "no candidate loads on this client" path, `plan.rs:708`). An empty selection ("no release on this channel", `plan.rs:653`) stays a failure.

**Planning-time downgrade guard for identified adoptions** (M2-D42: an adopted newer build from another distribution must never be "updated" to an older keyless one, so `release_id: None` is not trusted as "anything is newer"). For `version_confidence: toc` records, the app fills `installed_primary_interface` (a new `Option<u32>` field on `RequestedChange::Update`) from the installed primary folder's loaded TOC, using the same reader as `statuses()`. `try_candidate` rejects a candidate that verifies `Compatible { out_of_date: true }` on this client, or whose primary folder's highest in-family interface is lower, records the fact, and the item becomes `skipped/blocked`. The evaluator's guard is the display side; this is the safety side for when no fact exists yet (after `adopt --no-verify`, memo eviction or a newer upstream release).

### Output (A6's shared multi-target outcome, `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.6`)

Item `status` values are `installed`, `updated`, `removed`, `adopted`, `pinned`, `unpinned`, `edited`, `unchanged`, `skipped`, `failed`. This command produces `updated`, `unchanged`, `skipped` and `failed`. `skip_reason` (null unless skipped) is one of `pinned`, `ahead`, `blocked`, `static`, `unchecked`, `already_installed`, `no_build_for_target`, `local_source`, `duplicate`; this command uses the first five. `summary` buckets: `changed`, `unchanged`, `skipped`, `failed`.

```json
{"command":"update","partial":false,
 "data":{"dry_run":false,"run":"01M…","targets":[
   {"target":{"id":"forever","key":"01M…"},"tx":null,"kind":null,"no_section":false,
    "items":[{"request":"Questie","name":"Questie","ref":"gh:Questie/Questie","status":"skipped","skip_reason":"pinned",
              "from_version":"bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6","to_version":null,"error":null}],
    "reload_required":"none","atomic_swap":null,"creates_addons_dir":false,"error":null},
   {"target":{"id":"retail","key":"01M…"},"tx":"01M…","kind":"update","no_section":false,
    "items":[{"request":"DBM","name":"DBM","ref":"gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods","status":"updated","skip_reason":null,"reason":"explicit",
              "from_version":"12.1.14","to_version":"12.1.15",
              "folders":{"added":[],"replaced":["DBM-Core","DBM-GUI"],"removed":[],"skipped":[],"recorded":[]},"required_by":[],"error":null}],
    "reload_required":"none","atomic_swap":true,"creates_addons_dir":false,"error":null}],
  "summary":{"targets":2,"changed":1,"unchanged":11,"skipped":1,"failed":0}},
 "commands":[{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo 01M…","argv":["omaddons","undo","01M…"],"destructive":false}]}
```

- `commands`: `undo --run <run>` (action `undo_run`) first when more than one transaction committed, then one `undo <tx>` per transaction.
- `--dry-run`: per-target plans with `tx: null`; `data.dry_run: true`.
- `partial`: any failed item or target-level error (for example `locked` at commit). `--strict` turns partial success into exit 6 (`check_failed`, data kept).

### Ownership, running clients, drift, dependencies

- **Ownership:** an `ownership_conflict` during update (a new release ships a folder another addon owns) is an item failure whose fix is rewritten to `omaddons install <name> --force -t <id>`; the existing alternative `omaddons remove <owner>` stays. Decided: a non-symlink `unmanaged_folder` refusal gets the same rewrite, because the engine's fix would otherwise be `update … --force`.
- **Running clients** reuse `running::evaluate` unchanged: a running modern client under `safe` gets the update with `reload_required: reload`; a running legacy client under `safe` fails every item on that target with `game_running`; the other targets commit.
- **Drift (M2-D17):** updates replace locally modified files; users expect `update` to update, the transaction snapshot keeps the edits for at least 24 h, and refusing would make `update --all` fragile. E3 adds the `local_changes_replaced` warning with an undo fix; `update` never refuses because of drift.
- **Dependencies:** C4.2 makes a new release that adds a required dependency install it in the same transaction, and adds `--no-deps`.
- **No stale fallback:** a retryable fetch failure on a stale key is an item failure; mutating commands never install from stale metadata.
- **Progress:** A9 events for fetch, download, verify and per-target commit.

### Before A5 lands, one handover case degrades

When one addon's new release drops a folder that another addon's new release adds in the same run, the second fails `ownership_conflict` (clear, not retryable), the first commits, and re-running `update` completes the handover. A5 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.5`) later merges the pair into one `Replace` plus a handover transfer in a single transaction.

**Files:** new `src/app/update.rs`; `src/cli.rs` (variant, alias, `usage_error` special case, `without_flag` visibility); `src/app/mod.rs`; `src/engine/plan.rs` (`Update` resolution in `want()`, `installed_primary_interface`, the guard in `try_candidate`); new `tests/update.rs`; `tests/contract/matrix.rs`; `tests/contract/main.rs` (`TEXT_FIXES`); snapshots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Three targets, five addons, two refs changed: two transactions commit (targets with work only), items are `updated` with from and to versions, and `commands` holds `undo --run <run>` first. `omaddons undo` then reverts both.
- `net.log`: each distinct ref is fetched at most once. Each distinct asset is downloaded once once A8 has landed; until then this bead asserts refs only (H3 asserts both).
- Bare `update` produces the same data as `update --all`. `omaddons upgrade` works.
- A pinned addon is untouched and reported `skipped/pinned`. A named pinned addon adds `addon_pinned`.
- `update dbm --channel beta` records `channel: beta` and installs the newest beta. When the newest beta is already installed, the item is `unchanged` with a `-v` note until A4.3 lands (A4.3's own acceptance covers the `SetChannel` edit).
- A newer release that fails verification on one target is `skipped/blocked` with `partial: false`, and the next `outdated` shows `blocked`. The same holds for a `toc`-confidence record whose candidate fails the planning-time guard; the folder is untouched and the fact recorded.
- `--strict` with one genuinely failing item (a network error) exits 6; without `--strict`, exit 0 with `partial: true`.
- Running clients (fake proc): a running modern client under `safe` gets the update with `reload_required: reload`; a running legacy client under `safe` fails every item on that target with `game_running`; the other targets commit.
- Undoing one target's transaction restores it byte-for-byte without touching the others.
- `--all` with names, `--channel` without names, and `--version` are `usage` errors with the fixes above. A name installed nowhere is `not_managed` with fix `omaddons install <name>`.
- An `ownership_conflict` item's `fix_argv` is `omaddons install <name> --force -t <id>`.
- `help update` mentions `install --version` and `pin --version`; bare help stays under 30 lines with `update` in the Change group.

## Test Plan

- **E2E** in new `tests/update.rs` with replay fixtures and A10's `Home::installed_behind(base, (old_tag, old_assets), (new_tag, new_assets), targets)` across retail, era and classic: the main three-target scenario then `undo`; bare versus `--all` equality; the `upgrade` alias; pinned (bare and named); `--channel beta` (fixture with a beta release); a wrong-flavor newest release on one target (`skipped/blocked`, then `outdated` shows `blocked`); a `toc`-confidence record written directly with A10's state helpers for the planning-time guard; a network failure with and without `--strict`; running clients via `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` (`tests/common/procfs.rs`); per-target undo byte-for-byte (tree hashes); usage errors; `--dry-run` snapshot.
- **Request economy:** A10's `net_log(home)` counts by purpose (`release-latest` per distinct ref, `asset` per distinct asset once A8 exists).
- **Contract:** success and failure rows in `tests/contract/matrix.rs`; the new text fix in `TEXT_FIXES`.
- H2 adds the crash case for a multi-addon update.

## Considerations

- `install X` on a newer release still updates (M1's idempotency rule); `update` is the recommended way.
- A record whose upstream is gone (stored `not_found`) makes every bare `update` partial until it is removed; that is intended, and its fix says how.
- Unchanged items are omitted by default; agents read `summary` and pass `-v` for the full list.
- Collision hot spots: `src/engine/plan.rs` is edited by A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3 and C4.x; keep the `want()` and `try_candidate` changes small and rebase before each gate run. `src/cli.rs` and `src/app/mod.rs` are touched by every command bead.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.1` (Grouped bare help with a command group registry): `update` joins the Change group without breaking the 30-line bare help.
- A2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.2` (Multi-target selection with World::select_many): bare `update` covers every target and `-t vanilla` fans out.
- A3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.3` (Record carry-over rules and the extended RequestedChange): the `Update` variant, `PinIntent`, `channel_explicit` and `carry_over`, without which updates would unpin addons and promote dependencies.
- A6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.6` (Shared multi-target outcome and multi-target commit coverage): the data shape, renderer, undo commands and the tested multi-target commit path (A6 brings A12's run ids).
- A9 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.9` (Progress plumbing): a cold update takes seconds.
- A10 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.10` (M2 test helpers): `installed_behind`, release sequences, state and `net.log` readers.
- B4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.4` (The update-status evaluator): `statuses()` decides what to update, shared with `outdated`.

Unblocks:
- B8 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.8` (status update counts…): its `update` recommendation must name a command that exists.
- C4.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.2` (Dependencies on the update path…): adds `--no-deps` to `UpdateArgs` and dependency rounds on update.
- C6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.6` (Dependency bookkeeping on update and remove): `RemoveRequiredBy` edits when a requester's new release drops a dependency.
- E3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.3` (Drift in status, list and info): its acceptance runs `update` over a modified addon (`local_changes_replaced`).
- E5.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.2` (adopt --apply …): identified adoptions are replaced by the next `update`.
- H1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` (Contract conformance audit): audits the rows and fixes.
- H2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.2` (Crash and concurrency coverage): adds `UpdateMany` and update-versus-install races.
- H3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.3` (Performance budgets): benchmarks `update --all` warm and cold.
- H5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.5` (Real-machine smoke tests): `update X -t era` then undo.
- H6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` (README, help text and vision-bead records): documents the command, alias and departures.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** Today updating DBM on three clients means three `install` runs, each fetching and downloading separately. After this bead it is `omaddons update`: one fetch, one download, one transaction per client, and one `omaddons undo` reverts all of it. It is the most valuable M2 deliverable and lands in the first wave, before WoW: Forever launches on 2026-11-04. Every change still runs through the journaled, undoable transaction engine, which keeps the thesis true: omaddons is the sole, safe, undoable authority over every client's addons. It is also exactly what the M3 widget's "Update all" and "Undo last" call.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D4 (departs from the vision): bare `update` equals `update --all`.** Vision D17 says the first command an agent guesses should work; every comparable tool behaves this way, and run-level undo makes it safe. `--all` stays. Rejected: requiring `--all`, the vision's literal form.
- **M2-D17: updates replace locally modified files**, with `local_changes_replaced` (E3) and undo recovering them from the snapshot (kept at least 24 h). Users expect `update` to update; refusing would make `update --all` fragile. Rejected: refusing until `--force`.
- **M2-D39: `upgrade` alias pulled forward from M4.** A likely first guess outside the Levenshtein-2 range. Rejected: waiting for M4 intent inference.
- **M2-D41: a newest release that does not load on a client is `skipped/blocked`, not failed.** It is information, consistent with `copy` (M2-D30), and keeps `--strict` meaningful. Rejected: failing the item, which would make every run with WeakAuras on retail partial.
- **M2-D42: identified adoptions are protected from downgrades** by comparing the candidate's primary interface and `out_of_date` flag with the installed TOC, enforced at planning time too (a review-round fix: the evaluator alone is only the display side). Rejected: trusting `release_id: None` as "anything is newer".
- **M2-D38 (context):** history lines carry a run id; bare `undo` reverts the most recent run. Rejected: reverting one client out of three.
- **Review-round fixes folded in:** the carry-over rules re-run under the lock (A3), so a `pin` committing between this update's planning and its lock is not undone; the pre-A5 handover degradation is explicit; `update` has no stale-memo fallback on network failure.
- **Decisions made while writing this bead:** an unknown name is one failed item under the first selected target (all unknown: command error); `--channel` equal to the recorded channel is a normal update; `unmanaged_folder` fixes are rewritten like `ownership_conflict` fixes; the `--channel`-without-names fix is a text fix because `<addon>` is a placeholder; the `pin` alternative for `--version`, and moving the name matcher into one function shared with `pin`/`unpin`, are done by whichever of B6/B7 lands second; a named pinned addon's `addon_pinned` carries A3's interim `info` fix until B7 switches it to `unpin`.

**Facts verified during planning.** `RequestedChange::Reinstall` exists unused (`src/engine/plan.rs:86-89`) and its `want()` arm resolves to the record's ref and channel (`plan.rs:485-501`); `target_kind` returns `update` when any change is an update (`plan.rs:538-548`); the record is rebuilt with `pinned = wanted.version.is_some()` and `reason = Explicit` (`plan.rs:724-733`); `ownership::check` builds the `ownership_conflict` fix by appending `--force` to argv (`src/engine/ownership.rs:261-265`); the verification-failure and empty-selection paths of `no_compatible_release` are distinguishable (`plan.rs:653` versus `plan.rs:708`, `details.tried`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- The multi-target commit path had never run in production; A6 adds its engine test before this bead, A12 makes the run undoable as one, and H2 adds a crash case. Each target stays its own transaction, so a failure is contained.
- Silent unpinning: prevented by A3's carry-over and the pinned no-op under the lock.
- Plan confidence for the update path (B1 to B6) is **high**: a thin layer over M1's fetch, select, verify and transaction pipeline.
