comments.text:
**done:** `identify` groups candidate folders into addons with tiers, the winning ref, evidence and alternatives (M2-D40). `argc gate` passes: 1076 tests, 0 failed, ubs 0 critical.

**What landed (`src/resolve/adopt.rs`):**
- **Types:**
  - `Tier`: `exact`, `identified`, `guess`, `cf_only`, `unknown`.
  - `GroupClaim { ref: Option<Ref>, strength, evidence, name }`.
  - `Group { folders, primary, tier, claim: Option<GroupClaim>, alternatives, unloaded_folders }`.
  - All `Serialize + JsonSchema` in wire order. `identify` never yields `exact` and leaves `unloaded_folders` empty; both are E5.1's.
- **`identify(candidates, lookups) -> Vec<Group>`:**
  - Candidates are keyed (the first of a duplicate key is kept).
  - Every rank 1–6 claim becomes a proposal covering its folders that are present.
  - **Rank rounds 1..=6:**
    - A proposal is valid while its source is unassigned at the round's start, or assigned to the same ref.
    - Each still-unassigned folder covered by valid proposals goes to the first ref in tie order. Several refs make it contested, and the rest are remembered as tied.
    - A round's assignments are all computed before any is applied.
  - **Grouping:**
    - Ref groups are the folders assigned to one ref.
    - Each still-unassigned folder with only rank-7 claims seeds its own `cf_only` group.
  - **Joining:**
    - An evidence-less folder joins a group when it requires a member, or a member requires it (`TocSummary.dependencies`, ignoring case), and both share a name prefix of at least `GROUP_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS` (3).
    - It repeats until nothing joins, so chains join.
    - The chosen group is the strongest winning rank, then ref, then primary key. Joiners inherit the group's claim.
    - The remaining evidence-less folders form `unknown` groups by connected components of the same relation.
- **Per ref group:**
  - Strength is the weakest of the members' best own rank for the ref; with no such member, it is the assigning rank.
  - Tier is `guess` when any member is contested or no member has its own evidence. Otherwise `catalog`, `toc_id` and `corroborated` give `identified`, and `name_only` gives `guess`.
  - Alternatives are the tied refs first, then the members' own rank ≤ 5 claims naming another ref, by (rank, ref). They are de-duplicated, never the group's ref, and capped at `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES`.
  - Evidence is each member's own evidence at its best rank, plus the alternatives' claims.
  - Name is the best own claim's, else the assigning proposal's.
  - Primary is `primary_folder(ref, folders, name)`.
- **Tie order** is a total-order tuple key: coverage first, then ref class in identity order (gh, tukui, wowi), then:
  - for WoWI: `UIName` equal to the folder, then downloads, then `date_ms`;
  - for GitHub: the catalog name equal to the folder;
  - then the ref.
- Groups are sorted by primary key, and folders by key.
- **`src/engine/plan.rs`:** `primary_by_shape(folders)` is extracted from `primary_folder`, which calls it after its hint and repo-name checks, with no behaviour change. `cf_only` and `unknown` groups use it.
- **`ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES = 3`** in `src/limits.rs`, with a `REGISTRY` row (not configurable) and a `LIMIT_NAMES` entry. The snapshot was reviewed: one row added. `GROUP_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS = 3` is documented in `adopt.rs`.

**Fixtures:** `tests/fixtures/adopt/sets.toml` holds every set in one file, as `[<set>.<Folder>] toc = …`, written into the client by the test:
- `dbm`: the catalog's 8 folders, `DBM-Core` with `X-Website: https://deadlybossmods.com`, the others requiring `DBM-Core`;
- `dbm_strays`: `DBM-Extra`, and `XYZ-Thing` requiring `DBM-Core`;
- `bigwigs`: 4 folders, `X-WoWI-ID: 5086`;
- `elvui`: 3 folders, Tukui −2 and the project folders;
- `bugsack`: WoWI 5995, Curse 6273, Wago `rkGrrgGy`, OptionalDeps;
- `details`: the coloured title, and `Details_DataStorage`.

Real ids are the bead's verified ones; the rest are synthetic. I chose one TOML file over 20 `.toc` files for reviewability.

**Tests:**
- **`tests/adopt_identify.rs` (11, plus a 64-case proptest):** each case writes the folders into a synthetic retail client, reads them through `inventory(Depth::Full)` and `CandidateFolder::from_entry`, then calls `identify`. The lookups are the builtin catalog or fakes; the WoWI fake sanitises dirs with `sanitize_dirs`. Every case runs `check`:
  - each candidate is in exactly one group, with no folder twice;
  - nothing is `exact` and `unloaded_folders` is empty;
  - alternatives are ≤ 3 and never the group's ref;
  - refs are only `gh:`, `wowi:` or `tukui:`;
  - the group's ref is named by some evidence for one of its folders;
  - the claim's presence matches the tier;
  - the result is identical reversed and rotated.
- **Cases:**
  - BigWigs: `identified` `gh:BigWigsMods/BigWigs`, `catalog`, evidence `[catalog_folder, toc_wowi_id]`, alternatives `[wowi:5086]`, 4 folders, primary `BigWigs`.
  - `X-WoWI-ID` only gives `wowi:777` (`toc_id`). `X-Website` GitHub gives `gh:o/r`. `deadlybossmods.com` gives `unknown`, never `url:`.
  - ElvUI: one `tukui:elvui` group of 3 folders, `toc_id`; with a catalog entry it is `catalog`.
  - DBM: one 8-folder `identified` group, primary `DBM-Core`. With the strays, `DBM-Extra` joins (9 folders, still `identified`) and `XYZ-Thing` is `unknown`.
  - A unique `UIDir` with a matching coloured title, or the author only, is `identified` (`corroborated`). With both mismatched it is a `guess` (`name_only`).
  - A catalog alias only gives a `guess`. `X-Curse-Project-ID` only gives `cf_only` with a null ref. No evidence gives `unknown` with no claim.
  - Two catalog entries on one folder: a `guess` with the other in alternatives. Two WoWI projects sharing `Details`: the one covering more present folders wins, as a `guess` with the other in alternatives.
  - BugSack with a catalog entry: `identified` `gh:funkydude/BugSack`, alternatives `[wowi:5995]`, no cf evidence.
  - Five projects listing one folder: 3 alternatives.
  - All sets together: each addon in its group. Details is a `guess` because `Details_DataStorage`'s own `UIDir` match is not corroborated: the weakest member decides (rule 4).
- **The proptest:** random subsets of every fixture folder, in seeded random order, with a WoWI index that includes a contested project.
- **Unit (`resolve::adopt`, 2 new):**
  - the prefix rule (`DBM`, `BigWigs`, `UI_` rejected);
  - a discarded proposal: `Lib` is the catalog's, so its Tukui project-folder proposal, which also lists evidence-less `Mod`, is discarded. `Mod` stays `unknown`, and `Lib` lists `tukui:elvui` as an alternative.

**decided** (as the bead lists):
- rank-based rounds, with proposals discarded once their source goes elsewhere;
- a group without own evidence for its ref is a `guess`;
- `unknown` folders group by components, and `cf_only` folders are one group each;
- `name_only` disagreements appear only as ties;
- coverage comes first in tie order;
- `Tier::Exact` lives here but is never produced;
- E4.2 owns `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES`;
- `primary_by_shape` is extracted.

Also:
- The tie key orders ref classes in identity order, so mixed-class ties (for example a catalog name match against a WoWI dir match at rank 6) resolve as ref identity does. The GitHub catalog-name rule applies within the GitHub class.
- When joining, a group's "winning rank" is its members' best assignment rank (7 for `cf_only`).

**Wire names:**
- `Tier`: `exact`, `identified`, `guess`, `cf_only`, `unknown`.
- `Group` keys: `folders`, `primary`, `tier`, `claim` (`ref`, `strength`, `evidence`, `name`), `alternatives`, `unloaded_folders`.

**Constants:** `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES` (3, new).

title: Epic: The adopt command
description:
## Background

The owner arrives with folders installed by hand or by another addon manager, and M1 can only replace them. `install` refuses such a folder with `unmanaged_folder`, whose fix (`unmanaged_fix`, `src/engine/ownership.rs:358`, "rerun with `--force` until `adopt` exists (M2)") overwrites it with a fresh download. `status` can only point at `list -t <id> --unmanaged` (`src/app/status.rs:393-399`). `TxKind::Adopt` (`src/model.rs:413`) exists but is never produced. Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

This epic delivers `omaddons adopt`. It classifies every unmanaged folder and brings the confident ones under management (updates, drift checks, undo) without changing a byte under AddOns. It serves M2 goal G-M2-4, "Sole authority": folders installed before omaddons, or by another manager, come under management without being replaced, and only on confident identification. That is what makes omaddons the sole, safe, undoable authority over a client.

The identification rules are pure and belong to the split epic E4 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.4`). E4.1 collects per-folder evidence in the precedence M2-D40 fixed so that adoption picks the source `install` would: catalog folder index, `X-Tukui-ProjectID`, an `X-Website` GitHub/WoWInterface/Tukui link, `X-WoWI-ID`, a WoWInterface `UIDir` match corroborated by Title or Author, then a name match. E4.2 groups folders into addons with a tier. This epic is the command around them: inventory, lookups, downloads and hashing, the exactness check, the records-only `adopt` transactions, and hints in other commands.

```
$ omaddons adopt -t retail
retail: checking 14 identified addons against their newest releases (≈ 63 MB, 9 already cached)
retail: 41 unmanaged folders → 17 addons
  exact       DBM (8 folders)        gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods  12.1.15
  identified  BugSack                gh:funkydude/BugSack (catalog)    v12.1.6 (from TOC; update available)
  guess       Details (7 folders)    wowi:23056 (name only)            — not applied; choose with --ref (or wowi:25068)
  cf_only     TradeSkillMaster (2)   X-Curse-Project-ID only           — CurseForge arrives in M5; pass --ref
Apply exact + identified: omaddons adopt --apply -t retail
$ omaddons adopt --apply -t retail
retail: adopted 14 addons (31 folders), tx 01M5… — no folder was changed
```

## Goals

- A read-only report grouping every unmanaged folder into addons with a tier (`exact`, `identified`, `guess`, `cf_only`, `unknown`), evidence, alternatives and unloaded folders, writing nothing outside `<cache>/omaddons/`, `net.log` and `<state>/omaddons/inflight/`.
- An objective `exact` tier: the folders are byte-identical (per-file SHA-256) to the newest release's verified install set for this client (M2-D18).
- `--apply`, `<folder>…`, `--ref R` and re-pointing: one records-only transaction of kind `adopt` per target, all sharing one run id, writing records, index entries and history `record` ops, with no stage and no swap. Undo removes the records and leaves every folder byte-identical.
- Adopted addons update like installed ones, but a newer build adopted from another distribution is never downgraded (M2-D42: compare the candidate's primary interface and `out_of_date` verdict with the installed TOC; B4 and B6 implement it, E5.2 proves it end to end).
- Hints that today say `install`, `--force` or `list --unmanaged` offer `adopt` where it is the right next step, with an argv that runs.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:
- Fixture installs identical to the release come out `exact` (recorded with `release_id`, `version_confidence: release`); one version behind comes out `identified` (`toc`) and the next `update` replaces it.
- A `guess` is never applied without an explicit folder argument, and a guess with alternatives needs `--ref`.
- A WoWInterface `UIDir`-only match whose Title and Author both disagree is never `identified`.
- No fixture is adopted under a source other than its winning evidence. BigWigs, whose TOC carries `## X-WoWI-ID: 5086`, adopts as the catalog's `gh:` ref.
- `adopt --apply` changes no file under AddOns (tree hashes equal before and after). `undo` removes the records, and the folders stay byte-identical.
- A folder modified between `adopt --apply`'s planning and its lock fails with `plan_stale` (retryable).
- `status` recommends `adopt -t <id>` only when `adoptable > 0`, and `install X` onto an unmanaged `X` fails with the fix argv `omaddons adopt X --ref <ref> -t <id>`, which then succeeds.

## Non-Goals

- CurseForge and Wago adoption. Fingerprint matching and `auth curseforge` are M5. A CurseForge-only folder is reported `cf_only` and can be adopted only with an explicit keyless `--ref` (M2-D18).
- Changing, moving or deleting any folder. Adoption never stages, swaps or prunes. Leftover modules stay unmanaged.
- `adopt --force`, or adopting `Blizzard_*`, symlinked (`linked`), invalid or case-duplicate folders.
- Detecting two targets that share one AddOns directory through a symlink (adopt would double-manage it): a known limitation, filed for the M4 doctor (`target-addons-shared`) by H6.

## Considerations

- Adoption is heuristic. Conservatism bounds the damage of a wrong call to "a record that `undo` or `adopt <folder> --ref R` corrects": catalog-first precedence, `guess` never applied implicitly, exactness by hash, and the planning-time downgrade guard. Planning rated adoption confidence medium-high for this reason.
- Adoption never calls the write-oriented `ownership::check`; it reads inventory classes directly.
- Report mode may use the network, as a command whose job is to look upstream: always through `ReleaseCache` (`Window` freshness) and the WoWI index's max-age.
- Real-machine tests (H5) run report mode only, with `--no-verify`; `forever` stays read-only while `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` is open.
- Collision hot spots: `src/app/status.rs` (A2, B8, C6, E3, E5.x), `src/engine/plan.rs`, `src/error.rs`.

## Children

| Key | Id | Title | Scope in one line | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E5.1 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.1` | adopt report mode: classify unmanaged folders and verify exactness | `adopt [-t T] [--no-verify] [--refresh]`: inventory, lookups, `identify`, exactness check, report data, progress | A1, A2, A9, A10, B1, B3, D2, D3, D4, E1, E4.2 |
| E5.2 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.2` | adopt --apply, named folders, --ref and repoint as records-only adopt transactions | `--apply`, `<folder>…`, `--ref`, repoint; the adopt transaction; report-mode `commands` | A4.1, A6, B5, B6, E5.1, F1 |
| E5.3 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.3` | Adopt hints and fixes across status, outdated, update, pin, remove, install and dependencies | `adopt` recommendations and fixes in other commands, the ownership fix, C4's dependency hint | B7, B8, C4.1, E5.2 |

## How this was split

Planning sized `adopt` as one large (L) task, because its report, apply, named-folder, `--ref` and repoint modes share one pipeline (identify, then verify exactness, then plan records-only transactions) and each mode is thin over it. The split keeps that pipeline whole in one subtask and layers the rest on top:

- **E5.1** builds the pipeline and the read-only report: full-depth inventory, candidates, lookups, `identify`, the exactness check with its up-front download announcement, `unloaded_folders`, the offline and `--no-verify` rules, candidate facts, report data and progress. Its subcommand has only the report flags (`--no-verify`, `--refresh`; `-t` is global). Its `commands` stay empty and its human output names no `--apply` or `--ref`, because those do not exist yet (DEC-1: no flag before its behaviour; and M2's rule that a task never hints at a command a later task adds). After E5.1, `main` has a complete read-only `adopt`.
- **E5.2** adds the mutating modes over the same pipeline: `--apply`, `<folder>…`, `--ref` (resolved through F1's `src/app/resolve_args.rs`) and re-pointing; the adopt transaction (spec, record fields, naming, guard to `plan_stale`, commit with no stage or swap, undo); item failures with fixes; A6 output; and the report-mode `commands`, whose argv now runs. Other commands still emit their earlier hints (`install`, `--force`, `list --unmanaged`), which are valid, so nothing is half-supported.
- **E5.3** rewires hints in other commands: `status`, `outdated`, `update`, `pin`, `remove`, the engine's `unmanaged_folder` fix and C4.1's dependency hint. It edits those commands' code, so they must exist first. That is why it waits for B7 (`pin`), B8 (`status` `adoptable`), C4.1 (the dependency hint) and E5.2.

Dependents attach to the subtask that provides what they need: H5 (real-machine smoke tests) runs report mode only and waits for E5.1; H2 (crash and concurrency) needs the adopt transaction and waits for E5.2; H1 (contract audit) and H6 (docs and vision records) need every hint and wait for E5.3.
acceptance_criteria: E5.1, E5.2 and E5.3 are closed; fixture installs identical to the release adopt as exact with release_id and version_confidence release, and one-version-behind installs adopt as identified (toc) and are replaced by the next update; a guess is never applied without an explicit folder argument; a UIDir-only match with mismatched Title and Author is never identified; no fixture is adopted under a source other than its winning evidence (BigWigs with X-WoWI-ID adopts as the catalog gh: ref); adopt --apply changes no file under AddOns and undo removes the records with folders byte-identical; a folder modified between planning and lock gives plan_stale; status recommends adopt only when adoptable > 0; install onto an unmanaged folder offers an adopt --ref fix whose argv succeeds
close_reason: All children completed

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this epic, and how it serves M2.** Adoption is one of the two features (with `sync`) that make omaddons the *sole* authority over a client, which is the project's thesis. Without it, a migrating user's only path is `install --force`, which destroys and re-downloads every folder. With it, existing folders come under management (updates, drift, undo) without a byte changing, and only on confident identification (goal G-M2-4). Every adopt is a journaled, snapshotted, undoable records-only transaction, so no M1 guarantee weakens (G-M2-7).

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D18 (departs from the vision).** CurseForge-only folders are reported `cf_only` with a `--ref` fix, not "adoptable, fix `auth curseforge set`", because `auth curseforge` arrives in M5 and a fix must name a command that exists. `exact` needs per-file SHA-256 equality with the newest release's verified install set. Rejected: fingerprinting (CurseForge's method, M5) and matching version strings, which cannot prove the bytes are the release's.
- **M2-D40.** Evidence precedence is catalog, then `X-Tukui-ProjectID`, then `X-Website` (only GitHub, WoWInterface or Tukui links), then `X-WoWI-ID`, then corroborated WoWInterface `UIDir`, then name. Reason: adopt must pick the source `install` would, or the next `update` swaps the user's build for another distribution; real TOCs carry several ids (BigWigs `X-WoWI-ID: 5086`, Bartender4 `11190`, both curated `gh:` catalog entries). Rejected: TOC ids first, which would adopt catalog addons under WoWInterface.
- **M2-D42.** Identified (TOC-version) adoptions are protected from downgrades by comparing the candidate's primary interface and its `out_of_date` flag with the installed TOC. Rejected: trusting `release_id: None` as "anything is newer", which would "update" an adopted newer CurseForge build to an older keyless one.
- **M2-D6.** Records-only work is first-class in the engine (A4.1), so adopt needs no hand-rolled state write. Rejected: ad-hoc state writes per feature, which would not be journaled or undoable.
- **Review-round fixes folded in.** Wrong-source adoption (second review) produced the catalog-first precedence and the `X-Website` host limit. The planning-time `older_than_installed` guard (third review) covers adoptions made with `--no-verify` or after memo eviction, where no fact exists yet.

**Facts verified during planning.** `src/engine/ownership.rs:358` (`unmanaged_fix`) appends `--force` and says it waits for `adopt`; `src/app/status.rs:393-399` emits `list_unmanaged`; `src/app/remove.rs:396-402` gives `not_managed` the fix `list --unmanaged`; `TxKind::Adopt` (`src/model.rs:413`) and `FolderOp::Record` exist unused (all as of `e902d36`). Live facts (2026-10-15): BugSack's TOC carries `X-WoWI-ID: 5995`, `X-Curse-Project-ID: 6273` and `X-Wago-ID`; the WoWInterface filelist has 781 folder names shared by several projects; Details! (`wowi:23056`) is a stale 2020 upload; the ElvUI zip carries `X-Tukui-ProjectID: -2` and `X-Tukui-ProjectFolders`.

**Risks and mitigations.** Adoption under the wrong source, or an "update" that replaces an adopted newer build with an older one: low likelihood after M2-D40 and M2-D42, high impact. Mitigations: catalog-first precedence, the `X-Website` host limit, Title/Author corroboration, `guess` never applied implicitly, the exactness hash, the downgrade guard, `adopt --ref` re-pointing and undo. Two targets sharing one AddOns directory through a symlink would be double-managed; documented as a known limitation and filed for the M4 doctor by H6. Planning rated adoption medium-high confidence: heuristic by nature, but conservatism bounds a wrong call to a record that undo or `--ref` corrects.

**Why the split.** One pipeline, three subtasks: E5.1 builds it read-only, E5.2 adds the transactions, E5.3 rewires other commands' hints once those commands exist. Each leaves `main` consistent.

title: adopt report mode: classify unmanaged folders and verify exactness
description:
## Background

`omaddons adopt` brings folders installed by hand or by another manager under management without changing them. This bead builds the shared pipeline (identify, then verify exactness) as a read-only **report mode**; E5.2 adds the mutating modes, E5.3 the hints elsewhere.

Nothing classifies unmanaged folders today. `inventory(target, record, table, depth)` (`src/inventory.rs:114`) sorts entries into `FolderClass::{Protected, Managed, Linked, Unmanaged, Invalid}`, flags `case_duplicate`, and at `Depth::Full` reads each loaded TOC into `TocSummary` (`src/inventory.rs:84`, widened by C1). Inspection yields `InspectedFile { rel_path, size, sha256 }` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:93`) and the files index `FileEntry { path, size, mtime_ns, sha256 }` (`src/state/files_index.rs:43`), so released and on-disk bytes compare file by file. Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); symbol names are what matter.

Without this, E5.2 has nothing to plan from and H5 cannot check adoption on real clients. It serves G-M2-4, "Sole authority": existing folders come under management only on confident identification, shown first.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** new `src/app/adopt.rs`; `src/cli.rs`; `src/app/mod.rs` (`COMMANDS` group Change, dispatch); `src/app/help.rs`; `src/engine/plan.rs` (a candidate entry without ownership); new `tests/adopt.rs`; `tests/common/` (extract a fixture zip into `AddOns/` with no record); `tests/contract/matrix.rs`; snapshots.

**Surface.** `omaddons adopt [-t T] [--no-verify] [--refresh]`, `AdoptArgs { no_verify, refresh }` (`-t`, `--offline`, `--progress` are global; global `--dry-run` is ignored). Folders, `--apply` and `--ref` come with their behaviour in E5.2 (DEC-1: no stubs). Targets: `World::select_many` (A2), fanning out family, mode and product selectors (M2-D24).

**Step 1, candidates.** `world.records()`, then `inventory(.., Depth::Full)`. Candidates via E4.1's `CandidateFolder::from_entry` (class `Unmanaged`, valid name, not `case_duplicate`; `toc: None` when no TOC loads here).

**Step 2, lookups and `identify`.** `Catalog::load`; the Tukui list via `ReleaseCache::tukui_list()` (D4); the WoWI index via `WowiIndex::load_or_refresh` (D2). Disabled sources (`{source, reason: "disabled"}`) and a missing WoWI index (`{source: "wowi", reason: "no_index"}`) go in `data.sources_skipped`; a stale index raises `stale_check`. Then `resolve::adopt::identify(&candidates, &lookups) -> Vec<Group>` (E4.2, never fetches). What it does:
- Evidence, strongest first (M2-D40), `wire → strength`: family-filtered catalog `by_folder`, whose `folders` give the group (`catalog_folder` → `catalog`); `X-Tukui-ProjectID` via the Tukui list or built-in −1→`tukui`, −2→`elvui`, folders from `X-Tukui-ProjectFolders` (`toc_tukui_id` → `toc_id`); `X-Website` only as `gh:<owner>/<repo>`, a WoWI `info<id>` or a Tukui link, never `url:` (`toc_website` → `toc_id`); `X-WoWI-ID` (`toc_wowi_id` → `toc_id`); a unique WoWI `UIDir` match with Title ≈ `UIName` or Author ≈ `UIAuthorName` (`wowi_dir_corroborated` → `corroborated`); an uncorroborated `UIDir` match (`wowi_dir`) or a name equal to a catalog name/alias or `UIName` (`name_match`) → `name_only`; only Curse/Wago ids (`toc_curse_id`, `toc_wago_id` → `cf_only`).
- Grouping: evidence proposes `(ref, folder set)` over present unmanaged folders; the strongest claim wins a folder, equal strength makes a `guess` with the rest in `alternatives`; a disagreeing TOC id is listed, never chosen; an evidence-less folder joins a group listing it, or one it requires (or is required by) sharing a name prefix (to the first `-`/`_`, ≥ 3 chars). Tier = weakest own claim among members (joiners inherit): `catalog`/`toc_id`/`corroborated` → `identified`, `name_only` → `guess`, `cf_only` → `cf_only`, none → `unknown`.
- `Group { folders, primary, tier, claim: Option<GroupClaim { ref, strength, evidence, name }>, alternatives, unloaded_folders }`; `Tier` has `Exact`, but `identify` never yields it and leaves `unloaded_folders` empty; this bead fills both.

**Step 2b, leftovers (decided here).** A group whose claim ref equals (by `Ref` identity) a ref recorded on this target is a leftover module of a managed addon; adopting it would give one ref two records. Drop it and list its folders in `failed` as `already_managed` (new), matching B8's `adoptable`.

**Step 3, exact versus identified.** For each `identified` group whose source is enabled and reachable (online, or offline with a memo entry and cached blob), unless `--no-verify`:
1. `ReleaseCache::get` (B1), `Wanted { ref, channel: default_channel or stable, version: None }`; `Window` (15 min), `Refresh` with `--refresh` (also the WoWI index), `OfflineOnly` with `--offline`; each ref once per run.
2. `select`, download (facts and blob cache first; A8's `DownloadMemo`), inspect, verify, partition, `accepts`: install planning minus ownership. B5's `--verify` runs a full dry-run plan whose ownership check would refuse unmanaged folders, so expose a planner entry running `try_candidate` without ownership, running policy, stage or lock, returning the winner's folders, files and skip list.
3. `index_live_folder(path, &limits)` (E1) per present folder: streaming, no symlink following, bounded by `ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES` (20,000) and `ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED` (1 GiB). Keep the indexes for E5.2. An inner symlink → `failed` `unindexable`, a limit hit → `limit_exceeded`; that group is then not verified, never a crash.
4. `unloaded_folders`: present folders the archive contains but `partition` skips here (a retail-only module on Classic). Reported, never adopted.
5. **`exact`** iff the install set equals present folders minus `unloaded_folders` (by key) **and** each folder's archive `(rel_path, sha256)` set equals its on-disk `(path, sha256)` set. Then version and `release_id` from the release, `version_confidence: release`, `blob_sha256` set, `reason: null`.
6. Else **`identified`**: version from the primary folder's `## Version` (`@project-version@` or empty → `"unknown"`), `version_confidence: toc`, `release_id: null`, `reason` `files_differ`, `folder_set_differs`, `not_verified` (`--no-verify`, disabled source, member in `failed`), `not_verified_offline`, or `source_error` (fetch, select, download or verify failed, or nothing loads here; cause at `-v`).
- Retryable failures (`network`, `rate_limited`, 5xx, `download_failed`) are also mirrored as item warnings with `partial: true`; one group never fails the command.
- Facts (blob hash, size, verdicts with `loads`, `out_of_date`, `primary_interface`) go to `ReleaseCache::persist` once (B3). M2-D42's guard reads them: an identified adoption is never "updated" to a candidate that is `out_of_date` here or has a lower primary interface than the installed TOC.

**Announcement.** Before downloading, `data.verify = {groups, downloads, bytes}` (groups to check, distinct uncached assets of their top candidates, summed known `Asset.size`; `null` under `--no-verify`), plus a `download` progress event with `current: 0` (A9's wire shape: `{"event":"progress","phase","message","current","total"}`). Human output opens `checking 14 identified addons against their newest releases (≈ 63 MB, 9 already cached)`.

**Data** (keys binding; every group carries every key, null or empty when not applicable):

```json
"data":{"verify":{"groups":14,"downloads":5,"bytes":63000000},"targets":[{"target":{"id":"retail","key":"01M…"},"unmanaged":41,
  "groups":[
   {"folders":["DBM-Core","DBM-GUI","…"],"primary":"DBM-Core","tier":"exact","strength":"catalog","ref":"gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods","name":"DBM",
    "version":"12.1.15","version_confidence":"release","evidence":["catalog_folder"],"alternatives":[],"unloaded_folders":[],"reason":null},
   {"folders":["BigWigs","BigWigs_Core","…"],"tier":"identified","strength":"catalog","ref":"gh:BigWigsMods/BigWigs","version":"v427.6","version_confidence":"toc",
    "evidence":["catalog_folder","toc_wowi_id"],"alternatives":["wowi:5086"],"reason":"files_differ"},
   {"folders":["TradeSkillMaster"],"tier":"cf_only","strength":"cf_only","ref":null,"evidence":["toc_curse_id"]}],
  "failed":[{"folder":"LinkedLibs","reason":"unindexable"}]}],
 "sources_skipped":[]}
```

- `unmanaged` = `counts.unmanaged`; `target.key` null when unregistered. `name`: `GroupClaim.name` (catalog, Tukui or WoWI name), else primary folder.
- Order (decided): targets by id; groups by tier (`exact` first), name, primary key; folders by key.
- `commands` stays empty; the human output omits "Apply …" and "--ref" notes until E5.2 makes them runnable.

**Progress (A9):** `fetch` per ref, `download` per asset, `verify` per group. **Writes:** only `<cache>/omaddons/`, `net.log`, `<state>/omaddons/inflight/`; no lock, records, history, game files or registration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `adopt` is in the Change help group; `--no-verify`, `--refresh`, `-t` work; `--apply`, folders and `--ref` are still usage errors.
- Folders identical to the release's install set → `exact` (`release`); one version behind → `identified` (`toc`, TOC version, `files_differ`).
- BigWigs with `X-WoWI-ID: 5086` → the catalog `gh:` ref, evidence `["catalog_folder","toc_wowi_id"]`, `wowi:5086` in `alternatives`; no fixture is reported under a source other than its winning evidence.
- A `UIDir`-only match with mismatched Title **and** Author is never `identified`; a CurseForge-only folder is `cf_only`.
- A retail-only module on Classic is in `unloaded_folders` and does not prevent `exact`.
- An inner symlink → `failed` `unindexable`, group `not_verified`; a folder of an already-recorded ref → `failed` `already_managed`.
- `--no-verify`: no `asset` requests, `verify: null`, `not_verified`. `--offline`: `exact` only with memo entry and cached blob, else `not_verified_offline`, no request.
- A second run downloads nothing. `-t vanilla` reports both vanilla clients. A disabled WoWI source is in `sources_skipped`.
- Nothing is written outside `<cache>/omaddons/`, `net.log`, `<state>/omaddons/inflight/`; AddOns trees are unchanged.
- Progress events are monotonic; `commands` is empty; repeat runs are byte-identical apart from `meta`.

## Test Plan

- E2E `tests/adopt.rs`: A10 helpers, D2/D3/D4 fixture builders, E4.2's TOC sets (`tests/fixtures/adopt/`), the extract helper; one test per criterion with `net.log` counts.
- Unit: exactness (equal, differing file, extra file, missing folder, unloaded folder), reasons, `verify`, ordering. Contract rows; snapshots.

## Considerations

- Never call the write-oriented `ownership::check`; keep `identify` pure.
- Paths compare exactly; only the winning candidate is compared (nolib → `files_differ`).
- New wire names for the close comment: `already_managed`, `unindexable`, `limit_exceeded`, the five reasons, `verify`, `unmanaged`, `groups`, `failed`, `sources_skipped`.
- Collision hot spot: `src/engine/plan.rs` (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x).

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.1` (Grouped help): `adopt` joins the Change group.
- A2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.2` (select_many): fan-out over targets.
- A9 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.9` (Progress plumbing): the progress events.
- A10 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.10` (Test helpers): fixtures and readers.
- B1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.1` (ReleaseCache): freshness, fetch-once, offline.
- B3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.3` (Candidate facts): facts-first downloads; facts M2-D42 reads.
- D2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.2` (WoWI index): `UIDir` evidence.
- D3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.3` (WoWI source): verifying `wowi:` groups with MD5 downloads.
- D4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.4` (Tukui source): verifying `tukui:` groups, `tukui_list()`, deferred assets (A8).
- E1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.1` (Live-folder indexer): `index_live_folder`.
- E4.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.4.2` (Adoption grouping): `identify` and `Group`.

Unblocks:
- E5.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.2` (adopt --apply and friends): plans from these groups and indexes.
- H5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.5` (Real-machine smoke tests): runs report mode with `--no-verify`.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** A migrating user's first question is "what do I already have, and can omaddons take it over without breaking it?". Report mode answers that, read-only, with an objective `exact` tier and an honest `identified`/`guess`/`cf_only`/`unknown` for the rest. It is also the shared pipeline: E5.2's `--apply` re-runs exactly these steps before planning, so a report and an apply can never disagree on identification. This serves G-M2-4 (sole authority, only on confident identification) and keeps G-M2-7 (no M1 regression): nothing is written outside the cache, `net.log` and the in-flight lock directory.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D40, evidence precedence.** Catalog, then `X-Tukui-ProjectID`, then `X-Website` (GitHub, WoWInterface or Tukui links only), then `X-WoWI-ID`, then corroborated WoWInterface `UIDir`, then name. Why: adoption must pick the source `install` would, or the next `update` replaces the user's build with another distribution. Rejected: TOC ids first, which adopts curated catalog addons under WoWInterface.
- **M2-D18 (departs from the vision).** `exact` requires per-file SHA-256 equality with the newest release's verified install set for this client; CurseForge-only folders are `cf_only` with a `--ref` fix (E5.2) because `auth curseforge` is M5. Rejected: fingerprinting (CurseForge's method, M5) and comparing version strings, which proves nothing about the bytes.
- **M2-D42.** The facts this bead records (`out_of_date`, `primary_interface`) let `outdated`/`update` refuse to "update" an identified adoption to an older keyless build. Rejected: treating `release_id: None` as "anything is newer".
- **M2-D37, per-command freshness.** `adopt` uses the 15-minute `Window`, like the other batch commands, so a report followed by `--apply` costs no second fetch. Rejected: revalidating every ref like `install`, which doubles requests for no gain.
- **M2-D24.** `adopt` fans out family, mode and product selectors (`-t vanilla` means every vanilla client). Rejected: changing `resolve_one` globally.
- **Review-round fixes folded in.** Wrong-source adoption (second review) produced the catalog-first precedence and the `X-Website` host limit; the third review added the planning-time `older_than_installed` guard that depends on the facts recorded here.

**Decisions made while writing this bead (record them in the close comment).**
- *Leftovers of managed addons.* A group whose ref is already recorded on the target is listed in `failed` as `already_managed` instead of being offered. Otherwise `--apply` would create a second record for one ref (for example for a module left unmanaged as unloaded on an earlier run), which breaks `update`'s duplicate handling, `export` and `sync`. This matches B8's `adoptable`, which already excludes such folders.
- *`unloaded_folders`* are folders the winning archive contains but `partition` skips for this client. A folder absent from the archive makes the group `folder_set_differs`.
- *A member that cannot be indexed* (inner symlink, limit) leaves its group `identified` with `not_verified`; retryable source failures set `partial: true`; the group order is tier, then name.
- *A candidate entry without ownership.* B5's `--verify` is a full dry-run plan, whose ownership check refuses unmanaged folders, so this bead exposes `try_candidate` behind a planner entry that skips ownership and the running policy.

**Facts verified during planning.** `inventory()` (`src/inventory.rs:114`) and `TocSummary` (`:84`, fields `file, title, version, author, interfaces, x_ids`); `InspectedFile { rel_path, size, sha256 }` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:93`); `FileEntry { path, size, mtime_ns, sha256 }` (`src/state/files_index.rs:43`); the SHA-256-only blob fast path at `src/engine/plan.rs:1123`, which is why memo candidate facts serve the MD5 sources; `ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES` = 20,000 and `ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED` = 1 GiB (`src/limits.rs`). All as of `e902d36`. Live (2026-10-15): BigWigs and Bartender4 TOCs on the owner's `forever` client carry `X-WoWI-ID` 5086 and 11190 although both are `gh:` catalog entries; BugSack carries `X-WoWI-ID: 5995` and `X-Curse-Project-ID: 6273`; Details! (`wowi:23056`) is a stale 2020 project; 781 WoWInterface folder names are shared by several projects.

**Risks and mitigations.** Downloads can be large (the example run checks about 63 MB): announced up front, de-duplicated per command, skipped entirely with facts and cached blobs, and avoidable with `--no-verify`. A wrong identification only reports here; nothing is written. Confidence for adoption overall is medium-high (heuristic, but conservative).

**Relation to siblings.** E5.1 must not add `--apply`, folder arguments, `--ref` or any `commands`/human hint that names them; E5.2 adds those together with their behaviour and reuses this bead's groups and folder indexes so each folder is hashed once per command. E5.3 then changes other commands' hints.

comments.text:
**done:** `omaddons adopt [-t T] [--no-verify] [--refresh]` in report mode: identify unmanaged folders, then check identified groups against their newest release, file by file. `argc gate` passes: 1089 tests, 0 failed, ubs 0 critical.

**What landed:**
- **`src/app/adopt.rs`** (new): `AdoptArgs { no_verify, refresh }`, `run`, `AdoptOutcome` (command `adopt`, `commands` always empty), and human rendering. The announcement line opens the output, then per target a heading, group lines and failed folders.
  1. **Targets:** `World::select_many`, with each target's inventory at `Depth::Full`. Candidates come from `CandidateFolder::from_entry`.
  2. **Lookups:**
     - the catalog via `Catalog::load` (its warnings join the outcome);
     - the Tukui list via `ReleaseCache::tukui_list()`; a failure goes to `sources_skipped` as offline, rate-limited or `no_index`, and the built-in ids still work;
     - the WoWI index via `WowiIndex::load_or_refresh` with `IndexPolicy::from(freshness)`, so `--refresh` refreshes it too; its warnings (`stale_check`) and `skipped()` are kept;
     - each of github, wowi and tukui that is off is listed as `{source, reason: disabled}`.
     - The adapters `TukuiLookup` and `WowiLookup` (normalised `UIName`s computed once) feed `identify`.
  3. **Leftovers:** a group whose claim ref is recorded on the target is dropped, and its folders are listed in `failed` as `already_managed`.
  4. **Exactness, unless `--no-verify`:**
     - Only identified groups whose source is on are checked. Offline without a memo entry they are `not_verified_offline`, with no request.
     - Each present folder is indexed with `index_live_folder` under the engine's archive limits; a failure goes to `failed` as `unindexable` or `limit_exceeded`, and the group stays `not_verified`.
     - The distinct wishes (default channel, no pin) are fetched once through `ReleaseCache::get`, with `fetch` progress.
     - The verify plan: `groups`; `downloads`, the distinct top candidates not in the blob cache (facts or a declared SHA-256 whose blob exists); `bytes`, their known `size`. It is announced as a `download` progress event at `current: 0`.
     - `Engine::check_releases` runs, with `verify` progress per group.
     - The pure `exactness` compares folder sets (present minus the release's skipped, which become `unloaded_folders`) and, per folder, `(rel_path, sha256)` against `(path, sha256)`. Equal gives `exact`, with the release's version and `release_id`.
     - Otherwise the reason is `folder_set_differs`, `files_differ`, or `source_error` (refused, or failed to fetch or read), or `not_verified_offline` for an offline error. Retryable failures are mirrored as item warnings with `partial: true`.
     - Facts are written once through `cache.remember`.
  5. **Group fields:** the version is the release's for `exact`; otherwise the primary folder's `## Version` (`@project-version@` or empty gives `unknown`) with `version_confidence: toc`. The name is the claim's, else the primary folder.
  6. **Ordering:** targets by id; groups by tier (`exact` first), then name ignoring case, then primary key; failed folders by name, de-duplicated.
- **Engine, the verify-only entry:**
  - `plan::check_release(ctx, target, wanted, set, name_hint, &mut CheckNotes) -> Result<Checked>` runs `select`, then each candidate through the planner's `try_candidate` (download, inspect, verify, partition, `accepts`) with no ownership, policy, staging, lock or dependencies.
  - It returns `Checked::Loads(ReleaseCheck { release_id, version, install, skipped, blob_sha256 })`, or `Checked::Refused(why)`, or `Err` when nothing could even be read.
  - `tx::check_releases(&[CheckJob], &EngineCtx) -> CheckedReleases` builds the plan context once, with an in-flight lock that is cleaned up and the command's download memo.
  - `app::engine::Engine` gains `check_releases`, `http`, `archive_limits` and `default_channel`.
- **`ProgressSink::announce(phase, total, message)`:** one `current: 0` event before a phase's items.
- **CLI:** the `Adopt` subcommand. `COMMANDS` has `adopt` in Change after `unpin` (the planned layout), plus the name mapping and dispatch (`-v` notes). `--apply`, folder arguments and `--ref` remain usage errors, because they are not defined until E5.2.
- **README:**
  - the status line and the "What works today" row;
  - a new `### adopt` section: evidence order, the tier table, reasons, failed folders, writes;
  - the limitations row, the ownership note, and `adopt` in both progress-command lists.
- **Snapshots:** `cli_skeleton__bare_help_human` and `cli_skeleton__bare_help_json` (adopt in Change) and the new `contract__matrix__adopt_ok`, all reviewed.

**Tests:**
- **`tests/adopt.rs` (10):**
  - The release's exact files are `exact`: `release`, `v2`, `release_id gh:o/foo@v2`, `unmanaged 2`, `verify.groups 1`, `commands []`. v1 files on disk are `identified`, `v1`, `toc`, `files_differ`.
  - BigWigs with `X-WoWI-ID 5086`: the catalog `gh:` ref, evidence `[catalog_folder, toc_wowi_id]`, alternatives `[wowi:5086]`, `not_verified`, no asset request.
  - An uncorroborated `UIDir` match is a `guess`. A Curse id alone is `cf_only` with a null ref.
  - A retail-only module on Classic is `exact` with `unloaded_folders [Foo_Retail]`.
  - An inner symlink gives `failed [Foo unindexable]` and `not_verified`, with no download. A catalog-listed leftover of an installed `gh:o/foo` is `already_managed`, with no group.
  - `--no-verify` makes no asset request and gives `verify: null`. The first full run downloads once; the second makes no asset or `release-latest` request and reports `downloads: 0`.
  - Offline with nothing remembered is `not_verified_offline`, with no asset request. After one online run, offline is `exact` with no request at all.
  - `-t vanilla` reports both vanilla clients. A disabled wowi is in `sources_skipped`.
  - State is unchanged (except `net.log` and inflight), the AddOns tree is unchanged, and no in-flight lock is left. Progress is monotonic per phase, with the download announcement at 0. Repeat runs are identical without `meta`.
  - `--apply`, a folder argument and `--ref` are usage errors (exit 2).
- **Unit (`app::adopt`):** `exactness` (equal, a changed file, an extra released file, a folder only on disk, a folder only in the release, an unloaded folder) and `megabytes`.
- **Contract:** the `adopt` row, with the snapshot `adopt_ok` (an `exact` group, target key `null` while unregistered), `--no-verify`, and `--apply` as a usage error.

**decided:**
- A failed Tukui list is skipped with `offline`, `rate_limited` or `no_index` (its index), and the built-in Tukui ids still identify.
- Only the identified groups' folders are indexed: the indexes are kept per group for E5.2.
- `release_id` is part of every group (null unless `exact`). It is additive; the spec text names it for `exact`.
- Groups that are not identified carry `reason: null` and the TOC version.
- A disagreeing lookup that fails (the list or the index unreachable) is a `-v` note plus `sources_skipped`, never a failure.
- The verify plan counts a group as cached when its top candidate's blob is in the cache. `bytes` sums the declared asset sizes, so it is 0 when a source declares none (GitHub `release.json`).

**Wire names:**
- the command `adopt` and the flags `--no-verify`, `--refresh`;
- the data keys `verify {groups, downloads, bytes}`, `targets[] {target, unmanaged, groups, failed}` and `sources_skipped`;
- the group keys `folders`, `primary`, `tier`, `strength`, `ref`, `name`, `version`, `version_confidence`, `release_id`, `evidence`, `alternatives`, `unloaded_folders` and `reason`;
- the reasons `files_differ`, `folder_set_differs`, `not_verified`, `not_verified_offline` and `source_error`;
- the failed reasons `already_managed`, `unindexable` and `limit_exceeded`.

No new error codes and no constants.

title: adopt --apply, named folders, --ref and repoint as records-only adopt transactions
description:
## Background

E5.1 reports what every unmanaged folder is, but nothing acts on it: the owner's only path is still `install --force`, which overwrites the folders. `TxKind::Adopt` (`src/model.rs:413`) has never been produced. A4.1 makes records-only work first-class in the engine (`RecordEdit::{Adopt(AdoptSpec), Repoint(Ref)}`, per-kind `RecordGuard`, `TxRequest.kind`, history `record` ops, `ChangeKind::{Adopt, Edit}`, `FolderSummary.recorded`). This bead turns E5.1's groups into one records-only `adopt` transaction per target, adds named folders, `--ref` and re-pointing, and emits the report's runnable `commands`. Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); symbol names are what matter.

It serves G-M2-4 ("Sole authority": existing folders come under management without being replaced) and G-M2-7 (every mutation is a journaled, undoable transaction).

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `src/app/adopt.rs`; `src/cli.rs` (`AdoptArgs` gains `folders`, `apply`, `ref`); `src/error.rs` (warning `adopt_name_changed`); `tests/adopt.rs`; `tests/contract/matrix.rs`, `tests/contract/main.rs` (`TEXT_FIXES`); snapshots.

**Surface.** `omaddons adopt [<folder>…] [-t T] [--apply] [--ref R] [--no-verify] [--refresh] [--dry-run]`, `AdoptArgs { folders: Vec<String>, apply: bool, r#ref: Option<String>, no_verify, refresh }`.
- **Report** (no folders, no `--apply`): E5.1's mode, now with `commands` (below).
- **`--apply`**: adopts every `exact` and `identified` group on the selected targets (`select_many`). Never a `guess`, `cf_only` or `unknown`.
- **`<folder>…`**: adopts the groups containing these folders, at any tier from `guess` up. A `guess` with non-empty `alternatives` requires `--ref`.
- **`--ref R`**: exactly one folder (else `usage`) and one target: `-t` through `resolve_one`, or without `-t` the only target that has the folder (several → `target_ambiguous`, one `-t <id>` fix each). R accepts every form `install` accepts, catalog names included, through F1's `src/app/resolve_args.rs` (today `parse_ref`, `src/app/install.rs:497`).
  - **Unmanaged** folder: R overrides identification for its group (just the folder when unknown); E5.1's exactness check runs against R unless `--no-verify`.
  - **Managed** folder: `RecordEdit::Repoint(R)` on the owning record, `release_id` cleared, `version_confidence: toc`, so the next `update` installs from R. Kind `adopt`, `ChangeKind::Edit` `fields: ["ref"]`, item `edited`; R equal to the recorded ref is `unchanged`. This corrects a wrong adoption or a moved repo without uninstalling.
- Decided: `--apply` with folder arguments is `usage` (fix argv without `--apply`), as `update` treats `--all` with names. `--dry-run` returns the plan (`tx: null`).

**Pipeline steps 4 to 7**, after E5.1's steps 1 to 3 in the same command (a folder modified before `--apply` is simply re-classified):
4. Choose the mode's groups. A `--ref` R already recorded on the target fails the item (E5.1's `already_managed` rule: one ref, one record).
5. `index_live_folder` per chosen folder (E1), reusing step 3's indexes. A failure (inner symlink, over `ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES` 20,000 or `ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED` 1 GiB) fails that group's item, never the command.
6. `RequestedChange::Edit { addon: <record name>, edit: RecordEdit::Adopt(spec) }` per group, or `Edit { addon, edit: Repoint(R) }`.
7. `TxRequest { kind: Some(TxKind::Adopt), run, … }`, one `TxTarget` (`default_kind: Adopt`) per target with changes, via `app::engine::Engine`. One run id (A12), so bare `omaddons undo` reverts every target's adoption.

**`AdoptSpec`** (A4.1's type), computed lock-free at plan time: the record, `index_live_folder` per folder, each file's `(size, mtime_ns)`.
- Record: `ref` (claim or R); `version`, `version_confidence`, `release_id`, `blob_sha256` from E5.1 (`exact`: the release's; `identified`: TOC version, `toc`, none, none); `channel: default_channel`; `pinned: false`; `reason: explicit`; `required_by: []`; `folders`: present minus `unloaded_folders`; `state: ok`. `installed_at` and `tx_id` come at commit.
- Name: `GroupClaim.name` (catalog, else Tukui, else sanitised WoWI `UIName`), else primary folder. If another record already has it, record `<name> (<primary folder>)` with warning `adopt_name_changed` (new; decided fix argv `omaddons list -t <id>`).
- **Under the lock** A4.1's Adopt guard re-checks each folder: present, unmanaged, not a symlink, a re-listing finds exactly the indexed paths, every file keeps its `(size, mtime_ns)`; and no record has taken the spec's name. **Any difference is `plan_stale` (retryable), whether or not the generation changed**: a file edited after hashing never bumps the generation, so dropping the work would silently lose the request.
- `Repoint`'s guard: still recorded with the same `release_id`; on failure `plan_stale` (`details.cause`) if the generation changed, else dropped as no longer needed.
- **Commit** (A4.1): records, index upserts, one history `record` op per folder; no stage, no swap, `reload_required: none`; the state snapshot and an empty SavedVariables manifest are still made. Allowed while the client runs: `running::evaluate` sees no folder operation.
- **Undo** removes the records and index entries, folders untouched. A later `update` of the addon makes undoing the adopt an `undo_conflict`, as for any later transaction on those folders. Repoint undo restores the record from the snapshot.

**Item failures** (decided, existing codes):

| Folder | Code | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| not present on the selected targets | `not_found` | `omaddons list [-t <id>] --unmanaged` |
| `unknown` | `not_found` | text: `omaddons adopt <folder> --ref <ref> -t <id>` (fill in the ref) |
| `cf_only` | `source_disabled` (CurseForge and Wago arrive in M5) | the same `--ref` text |
| `guess` with alternatives, no `--ref` | `ref_ambiguous` | argv of the first `adopt_with_ref`, the others as `alternatives` |
| `already_managed`, or R already recorded | `ownership_conflict` (`details.owner`) | text: remove the leftover yourself, or pass the ref it belongs to |
| `Protected` | `protected_folder` | `omaddons list -t <id> --protected` |
| `Linked`, `Invalid` | `unmanaged_folder` (`details.class`) | `omaddons list -t <id> --unmanaged` |
| unindexable or over a limit | the indexer's error | `omaddons list -t <id> --unmanaged` |

A named folder that is already managed, without `--ref`, is `unchanged`. Every failure is an item (`status: failed`) and makes the run `partial`.

**Report-mode `commands`** (added here; each `CommandHint` carries argv):
- `adopt`: `omaddons adopt --apply` when any group is `exact` or `identified`, with `-t <id>` when one target has such groups, else the user's own `-t` if given (decided: the hint never widens the scope).
- `adopt_folder`: `omaddons adopt <primary folder> -t <id>`, one per `guess` without alternatives.
- `adopt_with_ref`: `omaddons adopt <primary folder> --ref <r> -t <id>` per guess with alternatives: the group's ref first (decided: it is a valid choice too), then each alternative, at most E4.2's `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES` (3) in total.
- Human notes: `— not applied; choose with --ref (or wowi:25068)`, `— CurseForge arrives in M5; pass --ref`, `Apply exact + identified: omaddons adopt --apply -t retail`.

**Output** (A6's multi-target shape): item status `adopted` (folders in `folders.recorded`), `edited`, `unchanged` or `failed`; `request` is the folder typed, or the primary folder under `--apply`; per target `tx`, `kind: "adopt"`, `reload_required: "none"`; `commands`: `undo --run <run>` first when more than one transaction committed, then `undo <tx>` each. Human: `retail: adopted 14 addons (31 folders), tx 01M5… — no folder was changed`. Progress adds the `commit` phase.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `adopt --apply` records every `exact` group with `release_id`, `version_confidence: release`, `blob_sha256`, and every `identified` group with the TOC version, `toc`, `release_id: null`; it never applies a `guess`.
- `adopt --apply` changes no file under AddOns (tree hashes equal); history has `record` ops and kind `adopt`; `reload_required: none`; it commits while a legacy client runs under `safe` (fake `/proc`).
- `undo` removes the records and index entries and leaves every folder byte-identical; across three targets one bare `undo` reverts all three.
- After adopting a one-version-behind install, `outdated` shows `update_available` and `update` replaces it with the release, after which the record is `release`-confidence.
- An adopted folder whose TOC interface is newer than the keyless release's: `outdated` shows `blocked`/`older_than_installed` and `update` leaves it alone. After `adopt --apply --no-verify` (no facts), `update` downloads the candidate, the planner's guard rejects it, the item is `skipped`/`blocked`, the folder is untouched and the fact is recorded.
- `adopt <folder>` applies a guess without alternatives; with alternatives it fails `ref_ambiguous` until `--ref` is given.
- `--ref` resolves catalog names exactly as `install` does. `--ref gh:o/x Foo` on unmanaged Foo adopts it under that ref (identified, TOC version); on a managed folder it re-points the record (kind `adopt`, undoable).
- BigWigs with `X-WoWI-ID` adopts as the catalog's `gh:` ref; no fixture is adopted under a source other than its winning evidence; a `UIDir`-only match with mismatched Title and Author is never applied by `--apply`.
- A CurseForge-only folder named on the command line fails `source_disabled` with the `--ref` text fix.
- A file modified between planning and the lock (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.plan.done=sleep:<ms>`) gives `plan_stale` (retryable) and records nothing for that group.
- A name clash records `<name> (<primary folder>)` with `adopt_name_changed`; a `Blizzard_*` folder is refused with nothing written.
- Report `commands` hold `adopt`, `adopt_folder` and `adopt_with_ref` per the rules, and each argv runs successfully.
- `--apply --dry-run` shows the plan (`tx: null`), commits nothing.

## Test Plan

- E2E `tests/adopt.rs` with E5.1's fixtures and extract helper, A10's `installed_behind` and state readers, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` for the running client; cross-process `plan_stale` with `engine.plan.done=sleep:`, editing a file during the sleep.
- Undo: one target, three targets with bare `undo`, the later-update `undo_conflict`, repoint. Outdated/update integration for identified, blocked and `--no-verify`.
- Contract rows (success and failure per mode), `TEXT_FIXES` for the `--ref` text fix, snapshots. H2 adds the crash matrix and the adopt-versus-install race.

## Considerations

- Never call the write-oriented `ownership::check`; never stage, swap or prune. Hash outside the lock (vision D24: the lock covers only the commit window).
- Real-machine adoption is H5's, report mode only.
- New wire names for the close comment: `adopt_name_changed`, status `adopted`, actions `adopt`, `adopt_folder`, `adopt_with_ref`.
- Collision hot spot: `src/error.rs` (new codes from several beads); rebase before the gate.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1` (Records-only engine work): `Adopt`/`Repoint` edits, `AdoptSpec`, guards, `TxRequest.kind`, `record` ops.

Unblocks:
- E5.3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.3` (Adopt hints elsewhere): its hints run `adopt <folder> [--ref R]`.
- H2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.2` (Crash and concurrency): the `Adopt` crash op and the adopt-versus-install race.

comments.author: GildedLedger
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** This is where adoption becomes real: the owner's existing folders come under management (updates, drift checks, undo) without a byte changing, through the same journaled, snapshotted, attributed transaction engine as every other mutation. "No folder was changed" and a one-command undo are what let a cautious user try it. It serves G-M2-4 and keeps G-M2-7: adopt is a transaction, not a hand-rolled state write. `--ref` and re-pointing make a wrong identification cheap to correct, which is what keeps a heuristic feature safe.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D6.** Records-only work is first-class in the engine (A4.1), so `adopt` writes records, index entries and `record` history ops through the normal commit. Rejected: an ad-hoc state write, which would not be journaled, snapshotted or undoable, and would make "every mutation is a transaction" false.
- **M2-D18 (departs from the vision).** A CurseForge-only folder is `cf_only` with a `--ref` fix rather than "adoptable, fix `auth curseforge set`" (M5). Rejected: fingerprinting (M5) and version-string matching.
- **M2-D40.** `--apply` adopts under the winning evidence only, which puts the catalog first; a disagreeing TOC id becomes an alternative. Rejected: TOC ids first.
- **M2-D42.** An identified record (`release_id: None`, `version_confidence: toc`) is updatable, but `update` refuses a candidate that is `out_of_date` on the client or has a lower primary interface than the installed TOC. B4 and B6 implement it; this bead's acceptance proves it end to end, including after `--no-verify`. Rejected: trusting `release_id: None` as "anything is newer".
- **M2-D38.** One run id across the per-target transactions, so bare `undo` reverts the whole adoption. Rejected: reverting only the last transaction (one client out of several).
- **The adopt guard always fails `plan_stale`.** A file edited between hashing and the lock never bumps the generation, so the edit-style rule ("drop when the generation is unchanged") would silently lose the request. A retryable error makes the user or agent re-run, and the re-run re-classifies the folder.
- **Review-round fixes folded in.** The planning-time `older_than_installed` guard (third review) is exercised here after `--no-verify`; adoption source precedence (second review) is exercised by the BigWigs criterion.

**Decisions made while writing this bead (record them in the close comment).**
- `--apply` together with folder arguments is `usage`, mirroring `update --all` with names.
- `adopt_with_ref` offers the guess's own ref first, then the alternatives, capped at `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES` (3) in total. Offering only the alternatives would leave an agent no runnable way to accept the guess's own ref, since `adopt <folder>` refuses a guess with alternatives.
- The `adopt` command hint keeps the user's `-t` selector when several targets qualify, so it never widens the scope.
- Item failures reuse existing codes (`not_found`, `source_disabled`, `ref_ambiguous`, `ownership_conflict`, `protected_folder`, `unmanaged_folder`), following M2's rule to prefer an existing code with a precise message, fix and details.
- A `--ref` naming a ref already recorded on the target fails, extending E5.1's `already_managed` rule: one ref never gets two records.
- `adopt_name_changed` gets the fix argv `omaddons list -t <id>`, and a named folder that is already managed (without `--ref`) is `unchanged`.

**Relied on from A4.1.** The Adopt guard also requires that no record has taken the spec's name under the lock; records are keyed by name (`TargetRecord::addon_key`), so without it a concurrent install under the same name would be overwritten.

**Facts verified during planning.** `TxKind::Adopt` exists unused (`src/model.rs:413`); `FolderOp::Record` exists in `src/state/history.rs`; the install argument resolver is `parse_ref` (`src/app/install.rs:497`), which F1 moves to `src/app/resolve_args.rs`; the failpoint `engine.plan.done` and the `sleep:<ms>` grammar exist (`src/engine/tx.rs` `FAILPOINTS`, `src/fsx/failpoint.rs`); records are keyed by addon name (`TargetRecord::addon_key`). All as of `e902d36`.

**Risks and mitigations.** Wrong-source adoption: catalog-first, `guess` never applied implicitly, exactness by hash, `--ref` re-pointing and undo. A concurrent `install` touching an adopted folder: the guard turns it into `plan_stale`, and H2 tests the race. Two targets sharing one AddOns directory would be double-managed: a documented limitation for the M4 doctor. Confidence: medium-high.

**Relation to siblings.** E5.1 provides the pipeline, groups and folder indexes; this bead must not re-hash a folder E5.1 already hashed in the same command. E5.3 then changes other commands' hints to point here; this bead does not touch `status`, `outdated`, `update`, `pin`, `remove` or the engine's ownership fix.

- **`src/app/outcome.rs`:** the adopt header reads `retail: adopted 2 addons (3 folders), tx 01M5…… — no folder was changed`. `ItemError.details` is documented for adopt items.
- **`src/error.rs`:** the warning `adopt_name_changed` (fix: `omaddons list -t <id>`); the warning count test is now 27.
- **CLI:** the `adopt` about line changed. `-v` dispatch logs lock hold times. The help snapshot `cli_skeleton__bare_help_json` was reviewed.

**Tests:**

The AddOns tree is unchanged, history has kind `adopt` with only `record` ops, and the index holds the three folders. `undo` forgets records and index entries, leaving folders byte-identical.
  - **Three clients:** one bare `undo` reverts all three, with `undo_run` first among the commands.

  - **Behind:** a one-version-behind adoption gives `outdated` `update_available` v2, then `update` gives `updated` and `release` confidence.

  - **Guesses and report commands:** report commands are `adopt_with_ref` ×2 (wowi:100 and wowi:200) and `adopt_folder`. `--apply` writes nothing. A guess with rivals named alone fails `ref_ambiguous`, with `fix_argv` and `alternatives` equal to those commands. Each command then runs: adopted, edited (re-pointed), adopted.
  - **`--ref`:** the catalog name `foo` adopts MyFoo as `gh:o/foo` with TOC m1, and `gh:o/x` on Zed is identified with z1. A ref on a managed folder gives `edited` with kind `adopt`, null `release_id` and `toc`. The same ref, or the folder alone, is `unchanged`. A ref another addon records fails `ownership_conflict` with `details.owner`. `undo` restores the ref.

Two failures give `details.items` with 2 entries, and nothing is written.
  - **Name clash:** recorded as `Foo (FooTwo)`, with the warning and its fix argv.
  - **`plan_stale`:** cross-process, with `engine.plan.done=sleep:2000` and `core.lua` edited during the sleep. The result is `plan_stale` with `retryable: true`, and nothing is recorded.
  - **`--apply --dry-run`:** `tx: null`, `dry_run: true`, the item `adopted`, and no state written.
  - **Usage:** `--apply Foo` is usage with fix `adopt Foo`; `--ref` without exactly one folder is usage. On two clients, `--ref` is `target_ambiguous` with fix `-t classic` and one alternative, and the fix runs.
  - **BigWigs:** `--apply` records `gh:BigWigsMods/BigWigs` with its four folders.
  - **Human output:** checked for the hint line, both group notes and the adopt header.
- **Contract:** `--apply Foo` and `--ref` alone are usage errors.
  - `adopt Mystery` fails `not_found` with the text fix (`TEXT_FIXES` gains `omaddons adopt --ref <ref>`), snapshot `adopt_unknown_folder`.
  - `adopt --apply` gets snapshot `adopt_apply`.
  - The re-point is `edited`.
  - `adopt_ok` now carries the `adopt` command.
  - All reviewed.

**decided:**
- A named folder on none of the selected clients fails `not_found` on each one. If it is on some, it is adopted there and nothing is said about the others.
- In the adopting modes, only the groups being adopted are checked, never every identified group. A failed check does not make the run partial: the group is still adopted as identified, and the warning stays.
- `--apply` lists no items for leftovers. They stay in the report's `failed` and are not failures of `--apply`.
- With `--ref R` (R not recorded), a leftover folder's group is adopted under R. An unknown group is cut down to the folder named, while other groups keep their folders.
- An item failure decided before the engine keeps its `details` (`folder`, plus `owner`, `class` or `refs`). When it is the run's only item, the command fails with that error itself, alternatives included.
- A folder in a case-duplicate pair fails `unmanaged_folder` with class `unmanaged`.
- `plan_stale` from the guard fails that client's whole transaction (the engine commits per client), so nothing is recorded there.
- Adopt transactions run with `no_deps` (records only).
- `--dry-run` in report mode changes nothing, as before.
- The human header is "adopted N addons (M folders), tx …… — no folder was changed"; a dry run says "would be adopted …".

**Wire names:**
- the flags `--apply`, `--ref` and the positional `FOLDER`;
- the warning `adopt_name_changed`;
- the item status `adopted`, now produced;
- the command actions `adopt`, `adopt_folder` and `adopt_with_ref`;
- the item error `details` keys `folder`, `owner`, `class` (`linked`, `invalid`, `unmanaged`) and `refs`;
- `target_ambiguous` `details` `{folder, candidates}` for `--ref`.

No new error codes and no constants.
